item.title: Aaron Coleman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641083949277 Aaron Coleman gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650682810589 [] surat india Explore Aaron Coleman's multi-disciplinary art confronting US race and class histories through printmaking, sculpture, and installation. Discover works in major collections. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“A pull quote that runs over three lines and tells the user more about the artist and their work.”"}]}]} {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aaron Coleman is a multi-disciplinary artist and associate professor at the Herron School of Art and Design. With an MFA from Northern Illinois University, his work in printmaking, sculpture, and installation has gained international recognition, featuring in collections like the Janet Turner Print Museum and the National Library of France. Coleman's art is deeply rooted in exploring social themes, particularly the intricate and pervasive histories of race and class in the United States. \\n \\nThrough a multi-media approach, Coleman reworks and re-contextualizes everyday objects and found imagery to confront uncomfortable truths and hidden narratives of racism and classism. His practice engages a critical analysis of authoritarian systems—religion, science, and anthropology—that upholds racial and class-based oppression. \\n \\nHis prints and mixed media pieces are known for their dynamic integration of comic book aesthetics, stained glass motifs, children's book illustrations, and offensive caricatures, crafted into powerful social commentaries. His installations offer new narratives by juxtaposing unexpected objects such as picket fences, gym flooring, textiles, and reinterpreted racist memorabilia. Through these constructions, Coleman challenges viewers to confront the enduring impact of systemic power and control in modern society."}]}]}

item.title: Aaron Samuel Mulenga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084113117 Aaron Samuel Mulenga gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640191676637 [] Discover Aaron Samuel Mulenga, a Zambian multimedia artist (b. 1990) exploring identity, power, and re-imagined religious iconography. His art challenges Eurocentric narratives, incorporating Zambian cultural symbols to foster inclusive dialogue on African spirituality. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aaron Samuel Mulenga, born in1990 in Lusaka, Zambia, is a multimedia artist currently pursuing a Master's degree at Rhode University. His work delves into themes of identity, power, mobility, and reinterpretation of religious iconography, particularly Christianity. By re-imagining biblical figures and stories to be more inclusive of people of colour, Mulenga challenges the dominant Euro-centric narrative often associated with such imagery. \\nHis art incorporates symbols rooted in Zambian cultural heritage, drawing inspiration from practices like the distinctive body markings of the Bemba people, used for self-identification. Mulenga's exploration began when he recognized the under-representation of Black people in Christian imagery, prompting him to engage in a broader dialogue about spirituality in Africa through his art. \\n \\nAaron Samuel Mulenga , born 1990 at Lusaka, Zambia is a multimedia artist and at present a Master's candidate at Rhodes University. His work explores themes of identity, power, mobility, and the reimagination of religious iconography - in particular - Christianity. By reimagining images that depict biblical characters or stories in a way that is more inclusive of people of colour, his intention is to destabilize the Eurocentric narrative that is prevalent in such images. \\n Mulenga’s work contains symbols that speak to Zambian cultural heritage and draws on practices such as the unique body markings used by the Bemba people (amongst other cultural groups in the country) as a tool to identify themselves. He was drawn to this enquiry when he realized that there was a lack of representation of black people in the images of Christianity he was engaging with, leading him to join the conversation of spirituality in Africa through the work he produces."}]}]}

item.title: Abdias Ngateu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084309725 Abdias Ngateu 2226 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640191709405 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013447590109","gid://shopify/Product/9014039478493"] Discover Abdias Ngateu (b. 1990, Cameroon), a painter known for witty, colorful social commentary through animal characters. His art humorously highlights Cameroonian life, transport chaos, and issues like corruption, gaining international acclaim. [16571,23179] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdias Ngateu (b. 1990, Douala, Cameroon) is a painter celebrated for his witty social commentary on life in his home country. Through colorful, humorous paintings featuring animal characters, Ngateu sheds light on the everyday struggles of Cameroonians, particularly focusing on the country's chaotic transportation system. His works, while playful, offer deeper insights into issues such as corruption, infrastructure deficiencies, and the resilience of ordinary citizens. \\n \\nNgateu’s artistic journey began at the age of 14, when he studied graphic and decorative arts, later earning a degree in sociology from the University of Douala. His background in sociology deeply informs his art, allowing him to add layers of meaning to his vibrant, detailed works. Beyond the comical animal figures, he includes witty details like slogans on vehicles (“Free Wifi on Board,” “Air-conditioned Taxi”), which challenge viewers to confront the realities behind the humor. \\n \\nOver the years, Ngateu’s talent has gained recognition both locally and internationally. He received accolades such as the Goethe Institute's \"Discovery\" Award in 2015 and third prize in the \"Young Hopes 2017\" National Contest. His work has been showcased at prestigious events, including the DAK'ART Biennale of Contemporary African Art, and his pieces have sold at respected auctions like ArtCurial. Since 2018, Ngateu has been represented by the Out of Africa Gallery, and his career continues to flourish as his unique blend of humor and social critique resonates with global audiences. \\n \\nAnd, as one of his famous taxi slogans warns: “YOU SLEEP, YOUR LIFE SLEEPS!”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013447590109 gid://shopify/Product/9014039478493

Specializing in handcrafted leather goods, we are celebrated for exquisite craftsmanship, timeless design, and creating beautiful pieces built to last. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdon Mkopi, born in 1997 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, is the founder and creative force behind Abdon Studio, a Cape Town-based known for it's handcrafted leather goods. Established in 2016, Abdon Studio is a reflection of Mkopi's passion for craftsmanship and timeless design. After arriving in Cape Town, driven by a desire to master the art of leather-work and build a new life, Mkopi founded the studio with the goal of creating pieces that are not only beautiful but built to last. His meticulous attention to detail and dedication to excellence shine through in every product. \\nAbdon Mkopi ,born 1997 at Dar es Salaam, Tanzania is the founder of Abdon Studio, a Cape Town-based brand known for its handcrafted leather goods. Established in 2016, Abdon Studio reflects Mkopi's passion for both exquisite craftsmanship and timeless design. \\nDriven by a desire to master the art of leatherwork and build a new life, Mkopi founded Abdon Studio after arriving in Cape Town from Tanzania. His commitment to excellence ensures each piece is not only beautiful but built to last. Visit Abdon Studio at 196 Victoria Road, Woodstock."}]}]}

[19224,19236,19228,19229,19230,19231,19232,19233,19234,19235] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdulla Omer Hamza (b. in Sudan) is a visual artist who delves into social and cultural complexities of his homeland. Through his art, Omer strives to \"reshape and bring colour back to life\" in the aftermath of war, envisioning a future marked by peace and inclusivity in Sudan. \\n \\nBorn in Sudan, visual artist Abdullah Omer delves into his homeland's social and cultural landscape. His recent 2024 series powerfully confronts the displacement and violence currently plaguing Sudan, a direct response to the devastating conflict that erupted in April 2023. While this context deeply informs his practice, Omer's work extends beyond current events. \\nHe strives to capture the rich tapestry of Sudanese culture and society, depicting the relationships born from its diversity and the geographical variations within the country. Ultimately, his artistic vision seeks to \"reshape and bring color back to life\" in the aftermath of war and displacement, working towards a more inclusive and peaceful Sudan."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013883273437 gid://shopify/Product/9013884059869 gid://shopify/Product/9013884977373 gid://shopify/Product/9013885796573 gid://shopify/Product/9013886681309 gid://shopify/Product/9013887467741 gid://shopify/Product/9013888418013 gid://shopify/Product/9013889171677 gid://shopify/Product/9013890056413 gid://shopify/Product/9013890777309 gid://shopify/Product/9014032302301 gid://shopify/Product/9014041641181 gid://shopify/Product/9014065955037 gid://shopify/Product/9014065987805 gid://shopify/Product/9014066053341 gid://shopify/Product/9014067593437 gid://shopify/Product/9014067626205 gid://shopify/Product/9014067724509 gid://shopify/Product/9014067757277 gid://shopify/Product/9133223936221 gid://shopify/Product/9133223968989

His work spans photography, videography, and mixed media installations, blending science and spirituality. Exhibited internationally, Salaam's art bridges the physical and the ethereal. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdus Salaam (b. 1989, Cape Town) is a self-taught artist whose multidisciplinary practice spans photography, videography, and mixed media installations. His decade in Los Angeles greatly influenced his artistic journey, which reignited upon his return to Cape Town. Salaam’s work bridges science and spirituality, focusing on minimalism and philosophy to create profound meanings within each medium. \\nSalaam's diverse practice includes both traditional tools, such as 8x10 photography and oil/acrylic painting, and unconventional materials like clay, glass, and stone. Through his installations, he blurs the lines between the physical and the ethereal, exploring the essence of form and meaning. \\nHe has exhibited at prestigious venues like AVA, Smit Studios, and Gallery MOMO, and his work is part of numerous private collections, earning him recognition both locally and internationally."}]}]}

item.title: Abe Mathabe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641084932317 Abe Mathabe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650684973277 [] Discover Abe Mathabe, a South African artist whose creative journey began in Pimville, Soweto. From crafting childhood toys from discarded materials to training at Artist Proof Studios and travelling internationally, his work reflects a unique blend of local influences and global experiences. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abe Mathabe, born in Pimville, an informal settlement near Soweto, South Africa, this artist is the fourth of eight siblings. From childhood, art was a constant presence in their life. Growing up with limited resources sparked their creativity, leading them to craft toys from clay, paper, sticks, and discarded materials. Their talent was first recognized in grade four when a teacher commissioned their first artwork, earning them 20 cents – a proud moment that marked the start of their artistic career. \\nThough they explored dance and music, art ultimately became their passion. Through the support of a sponsor, they qualified as a graphic designer at the Johannesburg Art Foundation and continued to refine their skills at Artist Proof Studios in Newtown, Johannesburg, where they studied for three more years. \\nTheir artistic journey extended beyond the classroom, with travel experiences in Cardiff, Wales; Burnie, Tasmania; and Amsterdam, enriching their creative outlook. Today, their work reflects a blend of local influences and global experiences. \\nImage Credit: Giovanni Piesco."}]}]}

item.title: Abiola Olabamiji
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085096157 Abiola Olabamiji 2148 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640192135389 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013419966685","gid://shopify/Product/9013420032221"] Discover Abiola Olabamiji, a contemporary artist from Nigeria. His work portrays the resilience of African men through unique palm fronds patterns and vibrant colors, inspired by Yoruba philosophy and modern expressions. [15237,15238] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abiola Olabamiji (b. 1992, Ibadan, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist. Inspired by the works of Chuck Close, Abiola embarked on his professional art career in 2021, after exploring various creative mediums. His work focuses on inner hardships and resilience of African men, expressed through his signature use of palm fronds patterns and intricate texture. His subjects, depicted in bold hues of black, brown, purple, and green reflect the contemporary life and aspirations of the African man. \\nAbiola primarily works with oil and acrylic on canvas, crafting portraits that evoke the strength, dignity, and stability of Black culture. He draws inspiration from Yoruba philosophy, aiming to bring its significance into the modern Renaissance through his art. According to Abiola, the texture of palm fronds symbolizes the resilience of African life, akin to the palm tree's endurance against powerful storms. His subjects' firm gazes encourages viewers to contemplates their own life journeys, offering multiple interpretations. \\nAbiola's work has evolved from large-scale neo-expressionist paintings to a more experimental and innovative approach. Growing up as a neglected child in Nigeria, his love for art began in elementary school, where he found a solace in creating. Watching a neighbour's artistic talents bring joy to his community sparked his creative path, which he continues to pursue with passion and dedication today."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013419966685 gid://shopify/Product/9013420032221

item.title: Ablade Glover
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085292765 Ablade Glover 1809 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640192233693 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013366751453","gid://shopify/Product/9013366849757","gid://shopify/Product/9013366882525","gid://shopify/Product/9013366948061","gid://shopify/Product/9013367013597","gid://shopify/Product/9014113566941","gid://shopify/Product/9014113665245","gid://shopify/Product/9014113730781","gid://shopify/Product/9014114386141","gid://shopify/Product/9014114418909","gid://shopify/Product/9014114484445","gid://shopify/Product/9014114517213"] Discover Professor Ablade Glover (b. 1934, Ghana), a luminary of modern African art. Explore his vibrant oil paintings depicting Ghanaian life, urban scenes, and the resilience of African women. Educator and founder of Artist Alliance Gallery. [12206,25120,25121,12209,12208,25122,25099,25119,25098,12194,12207,25097] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Professor Ablade Glover, born in 1934 in Accra, Ghana, is one of the most significant figures in modern African art. A celebrated painter, educator, and advocate for African culture, Glover’s vibrant, textured oil paintings are renowned for their depiction of bustling street markets, urban life, and the resilience of African women. His work stands as a powerful expression of Ghana's socio-cultural and political transformations during the 20th and 21st centuries. \\n \\nGrowing up under British colonial rule, Glover’s early life coincided with Ghana's movement towards independence, which deeply influenced his artistic practice. After beginning his education at the College of Art at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) in Kumasi, Glover was awarded a government scholarship to study textile design at London’s School of Art and Design. When he returned to Ghana, the factory where he was meant to work had not yet been built, allowing him to explore his passion for painting. He later earned another scholarship, personally authorized by Ghana’s first president, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, to study Art Education at Newcastle University. Further studies took him to the United States, where he completed a master's degree at Kent State University and earned his doctorate at Ohio University in 1974. \\n \\nUpon returning to Ghana, Glover joined the faculty at KNUST, where he taught for over two decades, eventually becoming Department Head and Dean of the College of Art. Glover was instrumental in shaping Ghana’s modern art scene through his dedication to education and mentorship. After retiring in 1994, he turned to full-time painting and founded the Artist Alliance Gallery in Accra in 1993. This gallery has become a major institution for promoting African contemporary art, showcasing the work of emerging artists from across the continent. \\n \\nGlover’s art is characterized by his dynamic use of color and thick layers of oil paint, applied with palette knives in a \"wet-on-wet\" technique. His paintings, which often require the viewer to step back to fully appreciate their intricate textures, are grouped into categories such as \"Market,\" \"People,\" \"Townscapes,\" and \"Celebrations.\" Glover’s signature approach vividly captures the chaos and energy of Ghanaian life, especially the Makola Market in Accra, which serves as a recurring theme in his work. His respect for women, especially those who sustain Ghana’s informal economy, is a central motif, as seen in his \"Profiles\" series, where women are portrayed with elegance and courage. Through his work, Glover elevates women as symbols of strength and resilience, reclaiming their power from the colonial exploitation of the past. \\nHis contribution to art extends beyond the canvas, as he has played a vital role in bringing international attention to both traditional and contemporary African art. Glover's works are housed in prestigious collections worldwide, including the Imperial Palace of Japan, UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, and Chicago's O'Hare International Airport. He has exhibited extensively in West Africa, Europe, the USA, and Japan, and has received numerous accolades, including the Flagstar Award, the Ghana Order of the Volta, and the Millennium Excellence Award. \\n \\nThroughout his long and distinguished career, Glover’s passion for Ghana, its people, and its culture remains the driving force behind his artistic journey. His paintings are not only a testament to his love for his country but also a powerful celebration of the people who form its backbone, particularly the women of Ghana. Glover's legacy as both an artist and educator continues to inspire future generations of African artists."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013366751453 gid://shopify/Product/9013366849757 gid://shopify/Product/9013366882525 gid://shopify/Product/9013366948061 gid://shopify/Product/9013367013597 gid://shopify/Product/9014113566941 gid://shopify/Product/9014113665245 gid://shopify/Product/9014113730781 gid://shopify/Product/9014114386141 gid://shopify/Product/9014114418909 gid://shopify/Product/9014114484445 gid://shopify/Product/9014114517213

item.title: Abongile Sidzumo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085358301 Abongile Sidzumo 1295 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650685759709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013331329245","gid://shopify/Product/9013331362013"] Discover Abongile Sidzumo, an award-winning South African artist who uses leather offcuts and repurposed materials to explore themes of healing, coexistence, and memory in post-apartheid South Africa. His work offers a powerful commentary on trauma and restoration. [9018,9019] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abongile Sidzumo, born in 1996 in Cape Town, is an emerging South African artist recognized for his use of leather offcuts and repurposed materials to create thought-provoking works that examine humanity, coexistence, and our connection with nature. A graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Arts (2019), Sidzumo draws inspiration from personal memories, spaces he has inhabited, and the daily lives of marginalized communities. His practice is rooted in the idea of healing trauma, specifically reflecting on the experiences of black communities during and after apartheid in South Africa. \\nSidzumo’s work delves into the symbolic meaning of leather, a material often associated with luxury, wealth, and power. Through his meticulous process of re-stitching and weaving, he encourages viewers to rethink the value of repurposed materials. His practice becomes a metaphor for the healing and restoration of black communities, focusing on the continuous journey of recovery in post-apartheid South Africa. \\n \\n \\nSidzumo works with leather offcuts and repurposed materials to create works that reflect and interrogate humanity, the way we co-exist and our relationship with nature; he re- visits memories and connects them to spaces he has lived in as well as the everyday life of marginalised communities. \\nLeather is often associated with luxury, wealth and power. Through his process of res- tichting and weaving this precious material, Sidzumo is proposing that we start thinking about repurposed materials, connecting it and his process of stitching to notions of heal- ing trauma that has been inflicted on black communities during apartheid, in a sense, his practice also functions as a manner of interrogating the continuous healing of black communities in post-apartheid South Africa. \\nIn 2020, Sidzumo was awarded the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize, which led to his solo exhibition at the Everard Read Gallery in Johannesburg. His work was also featured in \"We’ve come to take you home,\" an exhibition of newly acquired works by the University of Cape Town. The same year, he was a runner-up for the Cassirer Welz Award, hosted by Strauss & Co auctioneers. Sidzumo has participated in several group exhibitions, including \"A Cloud\" and \"The Oasis\" in 2021, curated by Studio Nxumalo Contemporary. His most recent recognition includes the Gerald Sekoto Award as part of the Absa L’Atelier 2021. He continues to live and work in Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013331329245 gid://shopify/Product/9013331362013

item.title: Abushariaa Ahmed
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641085685981 Abushariaa Ahmed gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650686480605 [] Discover the work of Abushariaa Ahmed, a Sudanese artist based in Kampala, Uganda. Influenced by the iconic Khartoum School, his art blends modernism with rich Sudanese traditions and is featured in prestigious international collections, including the World Bank. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abushariaa Ahmed graduated from Sudan University’s College of Fine and Applied Arts in 1990. After leaving Sudan in the mid-90s, he lived in Kenya for several years and later spent time in Cologne, Germany. Since 2000, Ahmed has resided in Kampala, Uganda, where he continues to work as a full-time artist. \\nHis artistic style is heavily influenced by the pioneers of Sudan's contemporary art movement, such as Ibrahim el Salahi and Rashid Diab. These artists were key figures in the 1960s Khartoum School, a modernist movement that combined Western influences with Sudan's rich cultural traditions, creating a distinctive style known as Sudanawiyya, reflecting the country’s diverse heritage. \\nAhmed’s work has been exhibited widely in East Africa, as well as internationally in Canada, the US, Germany, Denmark, Monaco, and the UK. His art is featured in numerous private and public collections worldwide, including the African Museum of Art in Seoul, South Korea, and the World Bank collection in Washington, DC, USA. He continues to push boundaries, contributing to the global appreciation of Sudanese modern art. \\n"}]}]}

She holds a BA and BA Honours in Fine Arts from the University of Witswatersrand. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ada-Ruth Kellow (b. 1957, Bremen, Germany) is a figurative painter residing and working in Johannesburg, South Africa. Her subject matter lies in the uncomfortable and the unspeakable, aligning with Susan Sontag's view that “we can’t be haunted enough”. Kellow continues the tradition of social critique painting, following in the footsteps of artists such as Goya, Gericault, Munch, and Golub. \\nIn her work of realistic rendering, Kellow uses metaphors and symbols, incorporating ornamental patterns that provide a sense of consolation. Through her art, she invites viewers to trace the unfolding narrative, blending confrontation with moments of humour. \\nKellow obtained her BA in Fine Arts from the University of Witswatersrand and completed her BA Honours with distinction in 2022. She has taken classes in painting at Hermann Niebuhr Studio, Johannesburg, and life drawing at Freie Kunstakademie Frankfurt, Germany. She also attended the Pentiment International Summer Academy for Art & Design in Hamburg, Germany. \\nKellow has participated in several group exhibitions in South Africa, with a solo exhibition at Gordart Gallery in Johannesburg in 2022. In 2024, she was among the top 40 Finalists for the Rust-en-Vrede Portrait Award and attended the Blue Cactus Art Residency in Barcelona, Spain."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014033645789 gid://shopify/Product/9014033711325 gid://shopify/Product/9014033776861 gid://shopify/Product/9014033809629 gid://shopify/Product/9014033875165 gid://shopify/Product/9014033940701 gid://shopify/Product/9014041477341 gid://shopify/Product/9014057468125 gid://shopify/Product/9014057500893 gid://shopify/Product/9014057926877 gid://shopify/Product/9014057959645 gid://shopify/Product/9014057992413 gid://shopify/Product/9014058057949 gid://shopify/Product/9132523028701 gid://shopify/Product/9132523356381 gid://shopify/Product/9132523389149 gid://shopify/Product/9132523421917 gid://shopify/Product/9132523454685 gid://shopify/Product/9132523487453 gid://shopify/Product/9132523585757 gid://shopify/Product/9133212532957 gid://shopify/Product/9133212598493 gid://shopify/Product/9133213581533 gid://shopify/Product/9133230883037 gid://shopify/Product/9133230915805 gid://shopify/Product/9133230948573 gid://shopify/Product/9133230981341 gid://shopify/Product/9134146945245 gid://shopify/Product/9134148714717 gid://shopify/Product/9134148747485 gid://shopify/Product/9134148813021 gid://shopify/Product/9134148845789

[22673,22550] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Addie Mak is an exceptionally talented self-taught artist hailing from Lagos, Nigeria. His artworks are a fascinating reflection of his innermost emotions, expressed through a vivid array of colours and compelling imagery. He began his artistic journey at the College of the Arts (COTA), where he honed his skills, and later advanced his studies at the University of Namibia (UNAM). \\n \\nIlovu’s artistic journey extends beyond the studio, as he actively participates in the vibrant art scene. He has exhibited in numerous group shows, showcasing his diverse talents, and his artistic vision has been presented in solo exhibitions at prestigious venues such as the Franco Namibian Cultural Centre and The Project Room Namibia. \\n \\nHis commitment to artistic development is further demonstrated through his involvement in workshops, including the Tulipamwe workshop in 2011, the Baker’s Bay artists’ retreat in 2022, and a Moleskine workshop led by renowned curator Simon Nyami in Zimbabwe in 2021. [19176,19177] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nigerian photographer Adedolapo Salako embarked on her artistic journey at the age of 25 in 2022, fueled by a passion for self-portraiture and fashion photography. However, her artistic vision soon expanded as she became captivated by the vibrant streets of Lagos, where she now excels in street photography and reportage. \\nAdedolapo's lens acts as a powerful storyteller, documenting the diverse communities that inhabit Lagos. Through her work, she captures their resilience, determination, and the captivating energy that pulsates through the city's street life. Each photograph serves to illuminate the rich tapestry of humanity that thrives in Lagos, providing an intimate glimpse into the lives of its inhabitants. \\n \\nSalako's mission is to amplify the voices of these communities, shedding light on their experiences and stories. Her work not only showcases the beauty and complexity of urban life but also invites viewers to appreciate the depth of human connection found within the bustling streets of Lagos. Through her compelling photography, Adedolapo Salako continues to forge a meaningful narrative that celebrates the spirit of the city and its people."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013856075997 gid://shopify/Product/9013856108765

item.title: Adejoke Tugbiyele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641086570717 Adejoke Tugbiyele gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640192823517 [] Discover the work of Adejoke Tugbiyele, a multi-award-winning Nigerian-American artist and activist. Her sculptures and performances explore race, gender, and sexuality and are held in collections like the Brooklyn Museum and the Smithsonian. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adejoke Tugbiyele is a multi-award-winning, Nigerian-American artist and activist whose work powerfully interrogates the intersections of race, gender, sexuality, and religion. A U.S. Fulbright Scholar, she has received numerous prestigious accolades, including the Grand Prix Leridon, the Joan Mitchell Painters and Sculptors Grant, and recognition as one of the '100 Leading Global Thinkers' in 2015. \\n \\nTugbiyele’s practice spans intricate 2D and 3D works and immersive performance art. Using diverse materials such as wire, natural fibers, bronze, and wood, she creates figurative sculptures that explore the body, spirituality, and the potential for self-love. Her art challenges established norms by examining how history, culture, and religion shape identity and perception. \\n \\nHer influential work is housed in esteemed public and private collections worldwide, including The Brooklyn Museum, the Smithsonian Institution's National Museum of African Art, and the Leslie-Lohman Museum of Gay and Lesbian Art. An alumna of the New Jersey Institute of Technology and the Maryland Institute College of Art, Tugbiyele is a sought-after panelist and contributor to global dialogues on art and social change."}]}]}

item.title: Adele Van Heerden
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641086832861 Adele Van Heerden gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193282269 [] Discover Adele van Heerden, a Cape Town-based painter (b. 1989) known for her work in pastel and gouache on drafting film. Her art explores light, reflection, and the relationship between urban landscapes and natural environments, inspired by personal experience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adele van Heerden (b. 1989) is a painter living and working in Cape Town, South Africa. Her artistic practice is characterized by her use of pastel, pencil, and gouache on drafting film, and it is deeply informed by her experiences of specific sites and places. Van Heerden's recent body of work, titled \"Mirror,\" focuses on the careful observation and study of surface, light, reflection, and fluidity, revealing her interest in the relationships between built environments and natural landscapes. \\n \\nIn her artist statement, Van Heerden expresses her interest in the relationships between built environments, natural landscapes, design, and abstraction versus figuration. She aims to capture moments and give shape to experiences, focusing on urban landscapes, waterscapes, and interior spaces. Recently, her work has expanded into a visual exploration of the interplay between water and light, drawing inspiration from her experiences as a swimmer. Water, which refracts and reflects light, serves as a significant theme in her practice. \\n \\nThe autobiographical component of her work reflects an abstracted narration that she translates through her experiences. This exploration began when she was diagnosed with a hip condition that required surgery and extensive rehabilitation, making swimming an embodied experience that facilitates sensory revelations. Through her art, Adele van Heerden continues to connect deeply with the environments she inhabits and portrays. \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Adeolu Osibodu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641086963933 Adeolu Osibodu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650688446685 [] Meet Adeolu Osibodu (b. 1997), an award-winning Nigerian photographer and photo artist. Discover his expressive, self-taught visual storytelling, featured by CNN and Adobe, and exhibited internationally in France, Germany, and the UAE. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adeolu Osibodu, born in 1997 in Lagos, Nigeria, is a self-taught photographer and photo artist who has carved a unique niche in the world of visual storytelling. He was drawn to photography because it allows him to express himself without the need for words, stating, “the idea of photography caught my eye because I didn't have to say anything to express myself. In other words, I never have to explain myself.” This philosophy underscores his approach to art. \\n \\nOsibodu's work has gained international attention, being exhibited in prestigious locations across France, Germany, and the UAE. In 2017, he achieved significant recognition by winning the Eyeem Portraitist Award in Berlin for an image from his impactful project \"Losing Amos.\" His work has also been featured and acknowledged by notable publications and platforms, including Ignant, Adobe Photoshop, Gup Magazine, Flickr, Blur Magazine, Kwerfeldein, and CNN. \\n \\nOsibodu’s artistic practice is driven by a keen observation of the world around him. He expresses, “I’m inspired by everything I see, hear, and feel,” reflecting his holistic approach to photography as a medium for capturing the essence of life. Through his lens, he documents moments and emotions, often finding clarity and understanding in the reflections of his captured images. This commitment to visual storytelling continues to resonate in his work as he explores the intersections of personal experience and broader societal themes."}]}]}

item.title: Adesola Yusuf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641089061085 Adesola Yusuf gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193315037 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013370454237","gid://shopify/Product/9013393031389","gid://shopify/Product/9013393588445","gid://shopify/Product/9013393719517","gid://shopify/Product/9013393752285","gid://shopify/Product/9013393785053"] Discover Abdulrahman Adesola Yusuf (Arclight) (b. 1997), a multidimensional artist exploring connection through liminal processes. His portraits blend abstraction and recognition, embodying "optimistic nihilism" and examining reality through emotive figures. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Abdulrahman Adesola Yusuf (Arclight) (b.1997) is a multidimensional artist deeply fascinated by connection, whose philosophy of creation centers the process rather than the destination. For Adesola, the true meaning of art lies in the labour of creation—an iterative journey of overthinking minute details and embracing the art of collage, layering materials through trail and error, and learning from irrevocable mistakes. His creative process is heavily rooted in the liminal. \\n \\nAdesola focuses on painting the intricate interplay of colour, form, and human expression to create silhouettes that teeter between abstraction and recognition. These figures are both present and elusive, reflecting his profound fascination with the transient nature of identity and the fluidity of the human form. He describes his compelling portraits as embodying \"optimistic nihilism\". \\nThrough his work, Adesola deconstructs his perception of the experiences that shape his world, revealing the subtle threads of connection between transcendent ideas and economic conditions. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013370454237, gid://shopify/Product/9013393031389, gid://shopify/Product/9013393588445, gid://shopify/Product/9013393719517, gid://shopify/Product/9013393752285, gid://shopify/Product/9013393785053,

item.title: Adilson De Oliveira
item.description: Adilson De Oliveira 2816 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193577181 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014055043293"] Discover Adilson De Oliveira, Johannesburg artist (The Magolide Collective). Explore multi-disciplinary works using XR, AI, and printmaking to probe Luso-African identity, decoloniality, and tech's role in art. [23693] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adilson de Oliveira (b. 1998 in Bez Valley, Johannesburg), is a multidisciplinary artist, self-taught animator, and cultural practitioner. He holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the University if Witwatersrand. De Oliveira initially worked as a printmaker, producing screen-prints for artist across Southern Africa, but grew disillusioned with the technical aspects of executing others' visions. This led him t explore technology as a creative assistant and collaborator. \\n \\nIn 2019, alongside Mzoxolo 'X' Mayongo, he co-founded 'The Magolide Collective'. De Oliveira's artistic practice has since evolved into what he terms a practice of deception, utilizing technology to challenge 'Western Art' historical narratives and aiming to create PC-generated work indistinguishable from physical objects. Employing drawing, video, printmaking, and particularly XR (Extended Reality) and AI as crucial tools for decoloniality, his work investigates and documents the metropolitan myths, legends, and socio-political realities of Johannesburg's Lusophonic (Luso-African) communities. \\n \\nAs of early 2025, De Oliveira continues to push technological boundaries in art and is a creative partner with the innovative AI video platform, Runway AI."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014055043293

item.title: Adia Mahlalela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641091223773 Adia Mahlalela gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193544413 [] Discover Adia Mahlalela, a South African art photographer celebrating raw African beauty. Her work challenges global beauty standards, empowering self-acceptance and showcasing diverse African culture and women. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adia Mahlalela, a South African art photographer, was born in Gauteng and raised in the serene, natural landscape of Emangweni, Mpumalanga. Her upbringing fostered a deep connection to nature and a profound love for African environments and cultures, instilling in her an appreciation for the inherent beauty in all things. \\n \\nMahlalela's art photography is a vibrant testament to this philosophy: embracing African beauty in its raw, unfiltered glory. She actively challenges conventional global beauty standards that often deem individuals as \"ugly\" or \"insufficient\", instead redefining beauty through an inclusive lens. \\n \\n \\nAdia firmly believes that beauty is an universal connector in a diverse world. Through her powerful work, she aims to illustrate that Africans are magnificent works of art themselves, deeply rooted in a rich cultural heritage. By featuring individuals of diverse shapes and sizes, her photography champions self-acceptance and highlights that true perfection comes from embracing one's authentic self, free from external opinions. \\nPhotography serves as a vital platform for Mahlalela, allowing her to be a voice for the voiceless and enabling viewers to see Africans and their beauty through a fresh perspective. Her work passionately embraces Africanism, African culture, and history, with a particular focus on empowering African women to embrace and celebrate themselves as genuine works of art."}]}]}

item.title: Adrian Fortuin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641092075741 Adrian Fortuin 1777 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640194330845 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013363998941","gid://shopify/Product/9013364064477","gid://shopify/Product/9013364130013"] Discover Adrian Fortuin (b. 1994, Johannesburg), an artist exploring intuition, identity, and abstraction through layered paintings and diverse media. Recipient of Wits Young Artist Award. [11946,11944,11945] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adrian Fortuin (b. 1994) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work deeply investigates the intersection of intuition, intersubjectivity, identity, image-making, and abstraction. With a primarily conceptual approach, Fortuin's choice of media is diverse, allowing him to explore the limits of representation and the enduring legacies of identity and experience tied to family, ancestry, community, and broader society. \\nFortuin's art is powerfully shaped by the emancipatory potential of abstraction. He graduated from Wits School of Arts with a Bachelor of Fine Art, where he was honoured with both the Wits Young Artist Award and the Martienssen Prize in 2019. Since then, his practice has evolved from a performative, lens-based approach to a trans-media engagement with painting and drawing. His paintings are distinctively characterized by an obsessive process of revision, where new layers of paint are applied over existing ones. This sedimentation transforms the painted surface into an archive of thought and gestures, serving as a potent metaphor of how personal historical trances endure in the present. \\nInfluenced by South African artist Tracey Rose (his former advisor) and Moshekwa Langa, as well as Daisuke Yokota, Fortuin also draws from expressionist tendencies within African modernisms and postmodernisms. His work has been featured in group exhibitions across Johannesburg, Cape Town, Kampala, and the touring African platform Boda Boda Lounge. He recently completed a residency at the David Krut Print Workshop in Johannesburg, continuing to expand his artistic exploration."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013363998941 gid://shopify/Product/9013364064477 gid://shopify/Product/9013364130013

item.title: Adolf Tega
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641091748061 Adolf Tega gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640193806557 [] Discover Adolf Tega (b. 1985, Harare), a contemporary Zimbabwean artist based in South Africa. Explore his journey from the National Gallery of Zimbabwe to solo exhibitions and prestigious collections like Spier and UCT. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adolf Tega (b. 1985, Harare, Zimbabwe) began his artistic journey at the young age of ten, inspired by his artist uncle and brother. He honed his skills at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe, where he also had his inaugural group exhibition. In 2008, Tega moved to South Africa, joining the Good Hope Art Studios to further develop his practice. \\n \\nTega quickly made his mark in the South African art scene. He held his first solo exhibition at AVA Gallery in Cape Town in 2012, followed by a second at World Art in 2014. His distinctive work is now featured in several prominent institutional and private collections, including those of Spier and the University of Cape Town. More recently, Tega was selected for the Nando’s Creative Exchange 2020, which culminated in an exhibition at the Basha Uhuru Freedom Festival, further cementing his growing recognition."}]}]}

item.title: Adrian Kohler
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641093222621 Adrian Kohler 2492 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195182813 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015754461"] Discover Adrian Kohler, co-founder of Handspring Puppet Company and a world-leading puppetry expert. His acclaimed puppets, blending artistry and engineering, are exhibited internationally and held in major collections. [22394] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adrian Kohler (b. 1957) is widely recognized as one of the word's foremost experts in puppetry, serving as the esteemed Co-founder and Artistic Director of the renowned Handspring Puppet Company. \\n \\nKohler's foundation passion for creating moving figures was nurtured from a young age; his mother; an amateur puppeteer, alongside his father, a yacht builder and cabinetmaker, instilled in him a deep understanding of woodwork and kinetic artistry. He further honed his artistic skills, earning a BA in Fine Art from the University of Cape Town. His early career included significant stints at The Space Theatre in Cape Town, the city's sole non-racial venue at the time, and a year in the U.K. at the Canon Hills Arts Centre and Weld Community Arts Centre in Birmingham. Kohler then dedicated three years to running the National Popular Theatre Program in Botswana. \\n \\nHis groundbreaking puppets for Handspring Puppet Company have garnered widespread international acclaim and extensive exhibition. Kohler has been honored with a solo retrospective at the National Gallery in South Africa, and selections of his works have been showcased at prestigious venues globally, including The Barbican Art Gallery in London and The Museum for African Art in New York. His exceptional puppets are part of significant public and private collections, notably including the Constitutional Court in South Africa, the Munich Stadt Museum in Germany, and the Old Mutual Art Collection. \\nIn recognition of his profound contributions to the arts, Kohler received the Michaelis Prize, a lifetime achievement award from Tshwane University in 2006, and an honorary doctorate in literature from the University of Cape Town in 2012. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014015754461

With a distinctive approach, Migadde employs diverse techniques, from intricate magazine collages to experimental painting with alcohol. \\nThrough his unique artistic lens, Migadde vividly depicts the nuances of daily life, exploring rich emotional landscapes, and bringing to light aspects he believes are often overlooked within his community and broader society. She holds both a Bachelor of Fine Art Painting (Honours, 2008) and a Master’s in Fine Art Painting (2014) from the esteemed Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST). \\n \\nAmiteye's artistic practice centers on her keen interest in exploring colors within figurative painting. item.title: Adrian Owen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641093714141 Adrian Owen 1352 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195313885 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013375434973"] Discover Adrian Owen (b. 1974), a self-taught South African artist specializing in fine art, portraiture, and illustration. Known for his distinctive charcoal dry brush technique, his work aims to reveal innate human beauty. [12872] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Adrian Owen (b. 1974) is a self-taught artist based in Kommetjie, near Cape Town, renowned for his expertise in fine art, portraiture, and illustration. His distinctive style of portraiture began to emerge in the 1990s as a young man sketching in London's Leicester and Trafalgar Squares. \\nThis early period included annual appearances on The Royal Mile at The Edinburgh International Arts Festival, a tradition he continued upon his return to South Africa by participating annually at the Grahamstown National Arts Festival. A pivotal trip to Chiang Mai in 2007 introduced him to the dry brush technique, which he skillfully adopted to expand his mastery in the disciplined art of charcoal drawing. \\nBeyond his fine arts pursuits, Adrian freelances commercially as an illustrator, contributing to the publishing, advertising, film, and television industries. Throughout his career, private portrait commissions and works exploring his unique interpretations of the human form have remained a staple, finding homes and private collections across the globe. His compelling work has been exhibited in notable galleries throughout South Africa. \\n \\nAdrian believes his purpose as an artist, in a world often overwhelmed by polarization and conflicting information, is “to remind people of our innate beauty through the pursuit and depiction of it”. \\nIn 2020, his work was featured in the SHE and Drawn In exhibitions at RK Contemporary in Riebeek Kasteel, and he also held a solo exhibition during Open Studios Kommetjie. \\nAdrian currently lives and works in Kommetjie near Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013375434973

item.title: Again Chokuwamba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641094926557 Again Chokuwamba gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195674333 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013418885341"] Discover Again Chokuwamba (b. 2000, Zimbabwe), a Best Emerging Artist 2023 award-winner. His art explores community complexities, social issues, and human unity through daily life inspirations and personal introspection. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hailing from Harare, Zimbabwe, Again Chokuwamba (b. 2000) is a rising contemporary artist whose compelling work delves into the intricate complexities of his community. After gaining local recognition through group exhibitions, his impactful solo project at First Floor Gallery Harare propelled him into the spotlight. His growing international acclaim was further solidified when he was awarded the prestigious Best Emerging Artist prize at the Zimbabwe Visual Art Awards 2023. \\nChokuwamba's artistic journey is deeply rooted in a desire to challenge societal misconceptions surrounding artists and to utilize his canvas as a powerful platform for expressing and highlighting the social issues faced by his community. Drawing inspiration from everyday scenes, human interactions, body language, music, and the use of mirrors, his artwork profoundly reflects the dynamics of human existence. \\n \\nDriven by the conviction that communities bear a responsibility to shape daily life, Chokuwamba commits to extensive research exploring the concept of human unity. His acute social awareness and focus on personal interactions provide the narrative bedrock for his broader artistic exploration. Through his work, he poses thought-provoking questions about the meaning we assign to everyday actions and their far-reaching impact on both ourselves and the collective good. \\n \\nChokuwamba openly acknowledges his own sensitivity and emotions, revealing that this body of work is integral to his personal healing process from societal pressures and past experiences. He finds solace and growth in solitude, recognizing its power for peace. His artistic exploration stems from a sense of alienation within his own environment, where misunderstanding can lead to negativity. Chokuwamba consistently emphasizes the interconnectedness of thought, feeling, and behavior, prompting viewers to contemplate their own contributions to the world. His artistic journey is a profound introspection, a continuous search for meaning amidst the multifaceted complexities of human experience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013418885341

item.title: Agnes Waruguru
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641095450845 Agnes Waruguru 2231 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640195707101 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013842477277"] Discover the work of Agnes Waruguru, a Kenyan contemporary artist exploring identity and home through multi-sensory painting, installation, and textile art. [18430] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Agnes Waruguru (b.1994) is Kenyan whose work delves into the intimate realms of everyday life, home and personal histories. Through a dedicated and repetitive practice of material experimentation, she create multi-sensory experiences that transform painting, drawing, printmaking, and needlework into immersive installations. \\nWaruguru’s art is deeply connected to her surrounding, yet it weaves in multiple histories and identities, inviting viewers into meticulously crafted environments. By engaging the senses with elements like scent, organic materials, light, and water, she constructs spaces that suspend time, encouraging moments of care, slowness, and contemplation. \\nA graduate of the Savannah College of Art and Design (BFA), Waruguru has gained significant international recognition. She has participated in the inaugural Stellenbosch Triennale (2020) and completed a prestigious residency at the Rijksakademie in Amsterdam (2021-2023). Her work has been exhibited across the globe, in Kenya, South Africa, France and the United States. Following her first solo show, 'Small things to Consider', at Circle Art Gallery in 2020, she was nominated for the esteemed Volkskrant Beeldende Kunst Prijs in 2022. Waruguru continues to live and work in Amsterdam, Netherlands."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013842477277

item.title: Aida Muluneh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641096564957 Aida Muluneh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640196264157 [] Explore the work of Aïda Muluneh, a leading Ethiopian photographer and cultural advocate whose powerful art addresses identity, history, and justice. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aïda Muluneh is a globally celebrated photographer and cultural entrepreneur whose work explores complex narratives of identity, history, and social justice through a distinctly vibrant and graphic lens. After an itinerant childhood in Yemen and England, she settled in Canada before graduating from Howard University in Washington D.C. with a degree in film. She began her career as a photojournalist for The Washington Post, a foundation that honed her powerful storytelling abilities. \\nMuluneh's art has been exhibited in leading institutions across the world, and her photographs are held in the permanent collections of the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), the Smithsonian's National Museum of African Art, and the RISD Museum, among others. A decorated artist, she is the recipient of the European Union Prize at the Rencontres Africaines de la Photographie (2007) and The Royal Photographic Society Curatorship Award (2020).A leading voice in global photography, Muluneh has served as a juror for the World Press Photo Contest and became the first Black woman to co-curate the Nobel Peace Prize exhibition in 2019. She is the founder and director of the Addis Foto Fest (AFF), the first international photography festival in East Africa. Through her company DESTA For Africa, she continues to curate exhibitions, foster education, and build cultural infrastructure from her base in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia."}]}]}

Fall is passionate about photography's narrative power and works to inspire audiences by demonstrating how, through photography, one can transform the world. As both an African woman and a graduate in African language and studies, Fall embraces the responsibility of representing her culture, continent, heritage and community. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Aimee Lindeque
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641097056477 Aimee Lindeque gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640196296925 [] Discover the intricate and imaginative art of Aimee Lindeque, a South African artist whose dense, doodle-like works explore the visual overload of the modern age. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Drawing inspiration from the relentless visual onslaught of the modern information age, South African artist Aimee Lindeque creates intricate and imaginative works in a unique eclectic style. She describes her process as an \"intuitive auto-pilot\", allowing her subconscious to guide the flow of images, textures, and ideas directly onto the canvas. This results in densely populated, doodle-like compositions that capture a sense of organized chaos. \\nA graduate of University of Cape Town's Michaelis School of Fine Art, Lindeque's art invites viewers to get lost in its detailed worlds, rewarding closer inspection with hidden narratives and whimsical discoveries, echoing the experience of navigating our own saturated realities."}]}]}

[18915,18931,16575,18932,18933,16574,18934] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ajarb Bernard Ategwa (b. 1988) is a self-taught Cameroonian visual artist who has risen to international prominence from his home base in Douala, Cameroon. His artistic journey began in 1998 with illustrations on plywood, but his perspective was transformed in 2001 after witnessing the work of artists like Hako Hankson, which inspired him to explore new dimensions of painting. \\nAtegwa's work is an intimate reflection of the bustling street life of Douala. He captures the \"plural, hard-working, noisy and eclectic\" energy of the city, yet his focus is on the moments of quiet respite found within the urban chaos. In a style influenced by Pop Art and the colour profusion of Jackson Pollock, he depicts characters in moments of pause—a \"ceasefire\" that creates a pocket of poetry amidst the disorder. \\nRepresented by leading galleries such as Jack Bell Gallery (London), Peres Projects (Berlin), and Fredric Snitzer Gallery (Miami), Ategwa's work has been showcased at prestigious international art fairs including Art Basel, FIAC, and Frieze. His paintings are held in notable public collections, including the Pérez Art Museum Miami (PAMM), the Chazen Museum of Art, and the Zuzeum Art Centre."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013447622877 gid://shopify/Product/9013447688413 gid://shopify/Product/9013849129181 gid://shopify/Product/9013849424093 gid://shopify/Product/9013849489629 gid://shopify/Product/9013849522397 gid://shopify/Product/9013849587933

[14486,14484,14485] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Akilah Watts (b. 1996) is a Barbadian artist whose multidisciplinary work explores identity, cultural heritage, and the nuanced realities of her island home. After receiving her BFA in 2017, she quickly gained international exposure, participating in the Prizm Art Fair in Miami that same year. Watts has since built a significant exhibition record both locally in Barbados and internationally in cities like New York and San Francisco, including a notable exhibition at the World Trade Centre. \\n \\nHer practice is deeply personal, with distinct bodies of work that delve into her relationship with natural hair and her Caribbean roots. In another prominent series, Moments From My Island Home, she thoughtfully navigates the space between the idyllic, postcard image of Barbados and the authentic, lived experience. Watts has been featured in numerous publications and online platforms such as Artsy, Artnet, and Art-LeadHER, marking her as a compelling voice in contemporary Caribbean art. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013404074205 gid://shopify/Product/9013404106973 gid://shopify/Product/9013404139741

item.title: Akintunde Disu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098399965 Akintunde Disu 2511 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640197279965 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013941698781","gid://shopify/Product/9013941731549","gid://shopify/Product/9013941764317","gid://shopify/Product/9013941797085","gid://shopify/Product/9013941829853","gid://shopify/Product/9013941862621"] Explore the work of Akintunde Disu, a Nigerian mixed-media artist and screen printer whose layered art delves into personal and Nigerian history. [19996,19999,19994,19995,19993,19998] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Akintunde Disu is a distinguished Nigerian mixed-media artist and screen printer whose work intricately navigate his personal history and the broader history of Nigeria. First gaining prominence as a runner-up in the 1986 BP National Portrait competition, Disu has built a career defined by intellectual depth and technical skill. \\n \\nHis artistic language is a rich tapestry woven from diverse influences, including Surrealism, Pop Art, and the masterful printmaking of fellow Nigerian artist Bruce Onobrakpeya, alongside Islamic and classic European art traditions. \\n \\nThrough the deliberate process of screen printing and layering, Disu creates immersive \"conversations on canvas,\" inviting viewers to look beyond the surface and uncover underlying narratives. His art, which often employs repetition and motif reminiscent of tribal art, serves as a tangible exploration of history and identity. Disu has exhibited extensively both in Nigeria and internationally, with notable shows at the National Museum in Lagos, a solo exhibition at the Didi Museum, and participation in exhibitions in the United Kingdom. He continues to challenge perceptions and create sensational, original work that dialogues with the very essence and fluidity of art. \\n \\n Disu draws inspiration from various sources including Surrealism, the Pop-art movement, and notably, the Nigerian print master Bruce Onobrakpeya. \\n \\nHis notable exhibitions span both national and international stages, showcasing his depth and versatility. Highlights include participation in the Society of Nigerian Artists group exhibition at the National Museum in Onikan, Lagos, a solo exhibition at Didi Museum in Lagos in November 2014, and contributions to group shows such as Pecha Kucha at the Goethe Institute in Lagos, and \"What is the Point?\" at the Federation of British Artists' Threadneedle Space, Mall Gallery, in the United Kingdom. \\n \\nDisu is committed to creating immersive art that serves as a conversation on canvas, offering fresh perspectives on the essence of art. He leverages screen printing to delve into the history of his people, aiming to create a magical, tangible experience. His work is a testament to the power of collaboration and the liberating effect of intentional methodology. Through layering, Disu invites audiences to look beyond the surface, challenging them to uncover the underlying narratives. \\n \\nHe masters his craft by engaging with significant, substantive subjects and cites a broad array of influences from Islamic and tribal art to classic landscape artists like Turner and environmental artists like Christo and Jeanne-Claude. His art speaks a language of repetition and motif inherent in tribal art, while also drawing contemporary influences from artists such as Rene Magritte, Salvador Dali, Sol Lewitt, and Andy Warhol. Disu's art is not only a reflection of his rich heritage and diverse influences but also a dialogue on the democratization and fluidity of art, emphasizing its originality and sensational impact."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013941698781 gid://shopify/Product/9013941731549 gid://shopify/Product/9013941764317 gid://shopify/Product/9013941797085 gid://shopify/Product/9013941829853 gid://shopify/Product/9013941862621

item.title: Akshar Maganbeharie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098531037 Akshar Maganbeharie 1874 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640197345501 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014025486557"] Discover the art of Akshar Maganbeharie, a South African artist using pop culture icons to critique capitalism, colonialism, and identity in his vibrant work. [22784,22783,22785] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Akshar Maganbeharie is a Cape Town-based, multi-disciplinary artist whose work offers a sharp and witty critique of contemporary culture.A 2017 Fine Art graduate from the University of the Witwatersrand, Maganbeharie moves fluidly between painting, drawing, and installation to explore how identity is shaped by pop culture and social media. \\nCiting Britney Spears, Starbucks, and Kylie Jenner as primary inspirations, he employs a semi-abstract, impressionistic style that appears carefree on the surface. However, beneath this veneer of \"unserious\" subject matter lies a pointed commentary on complex issues such as cultural imperialism, neo-colonialism, and capitalism. As a member of the Kutti Collective, a group of South African Indian artists, and selected as one of Design Indaba's Emerging Creatives in 2022, Maganbeharie has established himself as a significant voice. His works, held in private collections locally and internationally, challenge viewers to reconsider the profound impact of popular culture on the modern world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014025453789 gid://shopify/Product/9014025486557

item.title: Alastair Campbell
item.description: Alastair Campbell 1484 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640198328541 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013335195869"] Alastair Campbell is a Cape Town artist known for his detailed graphite drawings and live projection visuals for music events like Afterlife. [9125,9124] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alastair Campbell is a Cape Town-based artist whose work uniquely bridges the gap between meticulous traditional drawing and cutting-edge performance. Originally from Johannesburg, he studied Motion Graphics in Melbourne, Australia, which laid the foundation for his dual artistic practices. As a studio artist, Campbell is renowned for his hyper-realistic graphite drawings. These detailed studies, often inspired by the intricate forms and textures of nature, showcase his exceptional technical skill and patient observation. \\nIn parallel, Campbell is a highly sought-after VJ and live visual artist. He performs globally, creating and mixing projection-mapped visuals for major electronic music events and festivals, most notably for the internationally acclaimed Afterlife series. This dynamic aspect of his work contrasts with the quiet solitude of his drawing practice, yet both are united by a strong sense of composition, light, and atmospheric depth. This duality makes him a fascinating figure in the contemporary art and music scenes."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013335163101 gid://shopify/Product/9013335195869

item.title: Al Luke
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641106198749 Al Luke gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640198295773 [] Discover the abstract art of Al Luke, a Cape Town-based artist and designer. Explore his expressive paintings, murals, and collaborative work with Mrs + Mr Luke. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Al Luke (b. 1981) is a Cape Town-based artist known for his expressive abstract style that blurs the lines between street art and the gallery space. With a background in graphic design and a long career in advertising, Luke channels his creative energy into paintings and murals characterized by bold, intuitive line-work and a dynamic use of colour. Using markers and spray paint as his primary tools, he explores the limitless and evolving nature of abstraction. \\nSince dedicating more time to his personal art practice around 2017, Luke has become a prominent figure in the South African contemporary art scene. He has exhibited extensively in solo and group shows, including at the Turbine Art Fair and WORLDART gallery. Beyond his individual work, he is one half of the acclaimed artist duo Mrs + Mr Luke, a collaboration with his wife, Faatimah Mohamed-Luke. Together, they create vibrant, layered artworks that celebrate connection and human emotion. Luke is also a co-founder of the creative studio Black Koelewijn, further cementing his role as a multifaceted creative force."}]}]}

His practice is centered on what he terms ‘the architecture of time and the poetics and politics of place,’ seeking to illuminate the 'space between moments.' His work has been featured at major art fairs, including multiple editions of the Investec Cape Town Art Fair. \\nBeyond his personal practice, Whitton is a key figure in the Cape Town art scene as the director of These Four Walls gallery, where he curates and presents the work of other contemporary artists. item.title: Albert Adams
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641098957021 Albert Adams gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640198557917 [] Discover the art of Albert Adams, a South African modernist artist renowned for his bold depictions of human cruelty and violence. Known for the triptych South Africa 1959, Adams' work explores themes of oppression and identity with expressive figures and intricate textures. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Albert Adams (1929-2006) was a South African modernist artist known for his impactful work addressing themes of human cruelty, violence, and oppression. Born in Cape Town, Adams displayed exceptional artistic talent from a young age, which was nurtured by supportive teachers. Despite being denied entry to the Michaelis School of Fine Art due to apartheid-era racial segregation, Adams pursued his passion for art through part-time classes and teacher training. \\nAdams' artistic journey led him to the Slade School of Fine Art in London, where he honed his skills from 1953 to 1957. His time in Europe was marked by further studies in Germany and Austria, including master classes with the expressionist painter Oskar Kokoschka. These experiences profoundly influenced his style, characterized by bold color palettes, multi-layered textures, and expressive, contorted figures. \\nOne of Adams' most significant works is the triptych South Africa 1959, housed in the Johannesburg Art Gallery. This piece is often compared to Picasso’s Guernica for its raw depiction of the horrors of violence and oppression. Adams' work is deeply reflective of his personal experiences and political stance, making his art a powerful commentary on the social issues of his time. \\nAfter the Sharpeville Massacre in 1960, Adams settled in London, where he continued to create and exhibit his work. His art remained focused on confronting human cruelty, often depicting menacing figures that evoke a sense of unease and introspection. Adams also produced a series of self-portraits that explored his African-Indian heritage and identity. \\nAdams' legacy includes numerous solo exhibitions and retrospectives, such as the Albert Adams: Journey on a Tight Rope exhibition in 2008 and Bonds of Memory in 2016. His works, donated to the Iziko South African National Gallery, continue to inspire and challenge viewers with their emotional depth and artistic mastery."}]}]}

Inspired by John Singer Sargent, his work captures moments of intrigue and emotion. [19024,15267,12356,12362,12358,15268,15269,12361,12368,12357,12367,12366,12359,12365,12364,15270,15272,12360,19022,15271] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aldo Balding (b. 1960) is a celebrated English artist known for his evocative and narrative-driven figurative paintings. After beginning his career as an illustrator in London, he transitioned to become a full-time artist based in the South of France. A pivotal moment in his youth—an encounter with the work of John Singer Sargent—ignited his artistic direction. \\nBalding was captivated by Sargent's ability to create a stunning illusion of reality with loose, expressive brushwork that resolves into realism only from a distance. This principle remains central to Balding's own technique. He masterfully balances detailed realism with painterly strokes, creating contemporary scenes rich with atmosphere and intrigue. Unity of colour is paramount in his work, lending harmony and balance to his compositions. More than just a technician, Balding is a storyteller who uses body language, light, and the arrangement of figures to create a sense of anticipation, inviting viewers to interpret the unspoken narratives within each piece."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013368357085 gid://shopify/Product/9013368389853 gid://shopify/Product/9013368455389 gid://shopify/Product/9013368520925 gid://shopify/Product/9013368586461 gid://shopify/Product/9013368619229 gid://shopify/Product/9013368717533 gid://shopify/Product/9013368815837 gid://shopify/Product/9013368881373 gid://shopify/Product/9013368946909 gid://shopify/Product/9013369143517 gid://shopify/Product/9013369241821 gid://shopify/Product/9013420556509 gid://shopify/Product/9013420589277 gid://shopify/Product/9013420622045 gid://shopify/Product/9013420687581 gid://shopify/Product/9013420753117 gid://shopify/Product/9013420785885 gid://shopify/Product/9013851226333 gid://shopify/Product/9013851750621 gid://shopify/Product/9013851783389 gid://shopify/Product/9013851848925

item.title: Alejandra Arevalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641099153629 Alejandra Arevalo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640198623453 [] Explore the impactful photography of Alejandra Arévalo Martínez, a Colombian visual storyteller. Her work addresses themes of territory, gender, and identity through innovative, research-driven projects. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alejandra Arévalo Martinez (Bogotá, Colombia) is a visual storyteller and photographer, currently based in Dortmund, Germany. She holds a BA in Visual Communication from Bauhaus Universität-Weimar and is pursuing an MA in Photographic Studies at Fachhochschule Dortmund. Alejandra's work is deeply focused on themes of territory, gender, and identity, using photography to convey stories that resonate with contemporary society. \\nIn her artistic practice, Alejandra explores the intersections between photography, memory, and identity. Her work exists in the tension between personal experiences and collective memory, often through the lens of photographic archives, material traces, and everyday objects. Alejandra uses photography as a tool to penetrate and make visible both inner and outer worlds, questioning how visual narratives are constructed and their influence on our understanding of identity. \\nShe approaches photographic techniques playfully and experimentally, combining analog and digital methods to create new layers of meaning. Her work is strongly rooted in research and engagement with theoretical approaches from history, philosophy, and art history, flowing into projects that often have a dialogical character. Alejandra also engages with the concept of participatory art, creating spaces where viewers are actively involved in interpreting and transforming stories. \\nOne notable project is her photobook \"A Cloud Above Me,\" which focuses on paternal absence in Latin America. Supported by the Bauhaus University Women’s Development Fund and the Stibet Scholarship for International Students, the book has been nominated for several prestigious awards, including the German Photo Book Award (2021), Encontros da Imagem (2021, Portugal), and Photolux Festival (2022, Italy). \\nAlejandra's projects have been shortlisted for Encontros da Imagem (Portugal), Belfast Foto Festival (Ireland), and BarTur Fotos (Great Britain). Her work has received support from DAAD, the Women’s Fund at Bauhaus University, and the Rosa Luxemburg Stiftung. She has been recognized with awards such as Talents 36 by C/O Berlin, the Young Art Prize La Rioja 2020, and the Kunstpreis Fotografie Berlin Brandenburg Lotto 2016."}]}]}

item.title: Aleruchi Kinika
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641099251933 Aleruchi Kinika 2952 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640200163549 ["gid://shopify/Product/9133230555357","gid://shopify/Product/9133233144029","gid://shopify/Product/9133234225373","gid://shopify/Product/9133234323677"] Discover Aleruchi Kinika, a Nigerian conceptual photographer and writer based in Port Harcourt. Her emotive series like Blue Hour and Wrappers of Rivers explore memory, melancholy, feminine identity, and cultural heritage. [25478,25477,25476,25475] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Aleruchi Kinika (b.1997) is a visual artist living in Port Harcourt, Nigeria. Her mediums include photography, writing and pen on paper drawing. She started photography in order to preserve her culture and understand her identity. Her works explore individual storytelling through an intersection of surrealism and chiaroscuro. She aims to express deep seated emotions and cultural values through storytelling in effective and exciting ways. \\nKinika’s work also highlights femininity, beauty and fashion and is deeply inspired by cinema and baroque techniques which involves the play of light and shadows to further dramatize her subjects and drive her story. item.description: Alessandro Iovino gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640200884445 [] Discover the work of an Italian artist Alessandro Iovino focused on seeing the beauty of the everyday by challenging habit and rediscovering the familiar with new eyes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alessandro Iovino (b. Their practice is rooted in the ideas of stepping away from the familiar—be it people, places, or daily routines—in order to return and perceive them with renewed clarity and appreciation. [17922] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alet Swarts is a Pretoria-based artist whose work captures the fleeting, internal moments of becoming conscious of a new understanding. His work has been featured in notable solo exhibitions, showcasing his unique position at the intersection of two distinct, yet complementary, creative fields."}]}]}

item.title: Alex Nkuna
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641103446237 Alex Nkuna gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640202129629 [] Discover the powerful prints of Alex Nkuna, a South African artist from Giyani exploring themes of community, labour, and rural life. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alex Nkuna (b. 1990) is a South African artist from Thomo Village, Giyani, whose work serves as a powerful reflection of Limpopo home. After being introduced to visual arts in high school, he honed his craft at the acclaimed Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, which he joined in 2016, specializing in printmaking. \\n \\nSince completing his training, Nkuna has established himself as a significant emerging artist. His work, primarily in linocut and etching, moves beyond simple representation to explore the socio-economic landscape of Giyani, focusing focusing on themes of community, labour, migration, and the impact of zama zama (illegal mining) on the region. His detailed and narrative-driven prints have gained national recognition, leading to his selection as a finalist for the prestigious Sasol New Signatures competition. He continues to exhibit his work, offering a nuanced and personal perspective on the complexities of rural life in contemporary South Africa."}]}]}
