Holding a Master of Fine Arts from the University of Johannesburg, Pienaar draws on her personal history—growing up on a small farm in the Western Cape—to inform her practice. \\nShe works predominantly with leather, a medium deeply familiar to her through her father, a skilled leather craftsman. With a background shaped by living and working in the historically charged cities of Berlin (1995-2005) and Johannesburg (since 2006), Opper's work exploits the overlaps and slippages between art and architecture to destabilize the politics of both fields. \\nHis methodology is guided by a concept he terms \"Undoing Architecture.\" This approach allows him to cut through the conventional tendencies of both disciplines to give expression to the difficult, suppressed, and marginalized aspects of everyday life. In it, he proposed a progressive and inclusive reinterpretation of the former seat of the German monarchy, a vision that stands in stark contrast to the \"regressive, Disneyfied\" copy eventually built on the site. \\nBy working in this less-defined zone between fields, Opper produces artistic responses—often through a mode of institutional critique—that challenge the status quo of current material, spatial, social, and cultural phenomena. item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641099972829 Alexandra Karakashian 1836 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640202752221 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013371011293"] Discover the work of Alexandra Karakashian, a South African artist who uses used engine oil and salt to explore themes of exile, migration, and ecology. [12418,12419] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexandra Karakashian (b. 1988, Johannesburg) is a South African artist based in Cape Town whose practice is a investigation of exile, migration, and ecological precarity. Drawing from her own personal and family history, her work gives form to the complex emotional and political states of displacement and the loss of land. \\nProcess and materiality are central to Karakashian's work. She is renowned for her use of unconventional and symbolic materials, primarily used engine oil and salt, as a medium for her large-scale, abstract painting and installations. These materials directly engage in ecological discussions, referencing the threatening instability of our environment, the unethical seizing of dwindling natural resources on the African continent, and the subtle processes of collapse. Through these visceral, often monochromatic landscapes, she explores notions of individual and collective mourning, creating powerful lamentations for those who have been \"unhomed.\" \\nHer work has been exhibited globally and is held in significant public and private collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, the Spier Collection, and the Luciano Benetton Collection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013370945757 gid://shopify/Product/9013371011293

[15576,15706,14025,15575] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexandra Naledi Holtman is a Cape Town-based interdisciplinary artist and a graduate of the University of Cape Town's Michaelis School of Fine Art. Her practice, which often incorporates sound, sculpture, and interactive installation, is a thoughtful investigation into the nature of communication, connection, and perception. \\nDrawing on both academic theory and playful, tangible experiences, Holtman's work explores how we relate to one another across space and technology. A key example is her interactive sound installation based on Roy Ascott's concept of \"telematics.\" In this piece, she uses lo-fi materials like parabolic receivers and cup-and-string telephones to create an intimate, private communication channel between two people. item.title: Alexandre Kyungu
item.description: Alexandre Kyungu [] Discover the work of Alexandre Kyungu Mwilambwe, a contemporary Congolese artist who explores themes of migration, identity, and borders through a unique blend of cartography and scarification in his paintings, sculptures, and installations. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexandre Kyungu Mwilambwe, born in Kinshasa, D.R. Congo, in 1992, is a contemporary artist who continues to live and work in his vibrant home city. A graduate of the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, he is a significant figure in the local art scene, having co-founded the artist group Vision Total (vi.to) and maintaining an active collaboration with the renowned Kin Art Studio (KAS). \\n \\nKyungu's artistic practice is a profound exploration of the imaginary space between cartography and the human body. Working across a versatile range of media that includes painting, drawing, sculpture, and installation, he delves into critical themes of migration, identity, borders, and the spaces we occupy. His work centers on the parallels between the structured lines of urban maps and the personal, cultural marks of body scarification. \\n \\nA central motif in his work is the \"door,\" which he views as a powerful symbol of openness, encounter, and discovery in our increasingly globalized society. Through what he terms a \"cartographic essay,\" Kyungu deconstructs and fuses maps from different cities with the patterns of scarification. This process is a deliberate act to erase political borders, question notions of identity tied to place, and forge a new, unified territory within the imaginative realm of his art. \\n \\nIn his series, \"The shadow of the city,\" Kyungu specifically addresses areas of conflict. He creates compelling works by superimposing an inverted silhouette onto maps of countries and regions marked by turmoil. The body silhouette is itself scarified with the traditional African symbol nzoloko and marked with colourful geolocation icons, directly linking the human form to specific, contested locations on the global map. \\n \\nKyungu's powerful and distinct vision has earned him international recognition through numerous exhibitions and residencies. In 2020 alone, he was featured in several group shows, including \"Art Off-Screen\" curated by Eileen Jeng Lynch at Wavehill, New York; the \"Africa Art Auction\" by Calabar Gallery in New York; \"Doors, Eyes and Marks tribal\" at AKKA Project Gallery in Dubai; and \"trajectory\" at Five Myles gallery in Brooklyn. That same year, he participated in the \"transition\" themed International Biennale of Congo, organized by KinArtStudio in Kinshasa. In 2019, his work was presented at the AKAA Paris art fair by Gallery Angalia. \\n \\nHis development has been further enriched by prestigious artist residencies, including Art OMI in New York (2019), the Bag Factory in Johannesburg (2019), Atelier Mondial in Basel, Switzerland (2018), and the Bloc des Artistes in Cosenza, Italy (2018), with his Swiss and South African residencies organized by Pro Helvetia."}]}]}

item.title: Alexia Vogel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641100136669 Alexia Vogel gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640202850525 [] Explore the immersive, dreamlike paintings of Alexia Vogel, whose work uses lush tactility and a blend of abstraction and figuration to capture the sublime nature of nostalgia, fantasy, and wanderlust. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"With a lush tactility and heady mystique, the painted worlds of Alexia Vogel translate the amoebic, sublime nature of nostalgia, fantasy and wanderlust into vast, immersive canvases and vivid works on paper. Her imagined paradises disavow the logic of time in order to reach a space and state more felt than perceived—spaces of sustained reverie and suspended sensation. \\nVogel's creative process is guided by instinct and spontaneity, allowing the physical properties of the paint and its autonomous movement across the surface to direct the outcome. Within her work, moments of lucidity dissolve into states of dreamy meditation as she intuitively shifts between abstraction and figuration. Her more recent work sees notions of journey, passage and transition attaining more emphasis, while the artist continues to explore extremes of scale and further degrees of abstraction."}]}]}

item.title: Alexis Peskine
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641100660957 Alexis Peskine gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640202948829 [] Discover the powerful and innovative work of Alexis Peskine, a contemporary artist who creates stunning, three-dimensional portraits by hammering thousands of nails into wooden planks. Explore themes of identity, resilience, and the 'Black Experience' through his unique and internationally acclaimed art. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alexis Peskine (b. 1979, Paris) is a Franco-Brazilian artist whose work explores the complexities of the 'Black Experience'. His own multicultural heritage—with a Jewish grandfather who survived a concentration camp and an Afro-Brazilian grandfather from Salvador, Bahia—deeply informs his thematic focus on identity, struggle, and transcendence. \\nPeskine holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Howard University and a Master of Arts from the Maryland Institute College of Art (MICA), and is a recipient of the prestigious Fulbright Scholarship. He is renowned for his unique and impactful technique of creating large-scale portraits by driving nails of various sizes into wooden planks. Each nail functions as a brushstroke, hammered at different depths to create a three-dimensional, textured surface. \\nFor Preskine, the nail is a powerful symbol, representing both the pain and persecution faced by the African diaspora, as well as their incredible strength and resilience. His work specifically pays tribute to the perilous journey undertaken by migrants crossing the see from North Africa to Europe. \\nHis art has been exhibited globally across the United States, Europe, Africa, South America, and the Caribbean, and featured in major international exhibitions such as the Dakar Biennale, Addis Foto Fest, and Pulse New York. Peskine's compelling creations have garnered significant international attention, with features in prominent publications like The New York Time, La Monde and O Correio da Bahaia. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Alexis Preller
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641100726493 Alexis Preller gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640203047133 [] Explore the work of Alexis Preller, a major South African artist who fused inspiration from ancient cultures with the vibrant traditions of Africa, including Ndebele geometric art. Discover his unique artistic journey from iconic African figures to universal, abstract themes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Pretoria, Alexis Preller was a pioneering South African artist who forged a unique and independent artistic path. He began his formal training at the Westminster School of Art in London, but his distinct style was primarily shaped by his extensive travels and voracious reading. Preller immersed himself in a wide array of artistic traditions, drawing inspiration from Egyptian, ancient Greek, Etruscan, early Renaissance, and particularly, the rich cultural heritage of southern and central Africa. \\nRejecting both traditional European conventions and mainstream Modernism, Preller was dedicated to creating an art form that was deeply rooted in his own time and place. In the late 1940s and early 1950s, he frequently visited Ndebele settlements near Pretoria. These visits had a profound impact on his work, which began to feature the striking imagery of ‘Mapogga’ (Ndebele) women in their distinctive traditional attire and the vibrant geometric murals adorning their homesteads. \\nIn his later years, Preller's focus expanded from the local and African to the universal. Influenced by a growing interest in space exploration and discovery, his work evolved, becoming progressively more abstract and celestial in nature."}]}]}

item.title: Alf Kumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104036061 Alf Kumalo 1563 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640204357853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013344993501","gid://shopify/Product/9013345026269"] Explore the life and work of Alf Kumalo, one of South Africa's most important photographers. Discover his iconic images that captured the key moments and figures of the anti-apartheid struggle, earning him international recognition and a lasting legacy in documentary photojournalism. [9815,9814] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alf Kumalo (1930-2012) was one of South Africa's most important and internationally recognised photographer, celebrated for his front-row documentation of the nation's liberation history. Born in Utrecht, KwaZulu-Natal, Kumalo moved to Johannesburg as a young boy and, though largely self-taught, embarked on an extraordinary career that placed him at the heart of pivotal moments in the struggle against apartheid. \\n \\nThroughout his career, Kumalo demonstrated a unique ability to gain access to iconic figures, capturing both the tragic and joyous turning points of his time. He began his professional journey in the 1950s with Bantu World and Golden City Post, later freelancing for the influential Drum magazine in the 1960s and the Sunday Times in the 1970s, before joining The Star in the 1980s. \\n \\nHis powerful images were not only central to South African media but also gained global attention, appearing in leading international newspapers such as The Observer, The New York Times, and The Sunday Independent. His work was also prominently exhibited at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City. \\n \\nKumalo authored several significant books, including Mandela: Echoes of an Era and his photographic memoir, Through My Lens. In recognition of his immense contribution to photojournalism and the documentation of South African history, he was awarded the Presidential Order of Ikhamanga in Silver in 2004 and the Nat Nakasa Award for Media Integrity in 2005."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013344993501 gid://shopify/Product/9013345026269

item.title: Alfred Thoba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641103544541 Alfred Thoba 1010 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640214778077 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014062645469","gid://shopify/Product/9014062809309"] Discover the powerful work of Alfred Thoba, a key figure in South Africa's resistance art movement. Explore his politically charged paintings that document the struggles of apartheid and the social challenges of post-apartheid life in Johannesburg's townships. [23901,23899] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alfred Thoba (b. 1951, Johannesburg) is a prominent self-taught artist who is renowned for his politically charged and socially conscious artworks. As an active member of the resistance art movement during apartheid, Thoba used his paintbrush as a powerful tool for protest. His work not only condemned the violence of the state but also unflinchingly depicted the internal conflicts and societal damage inflicted upon the Black population by the oppressive system. \\n \\n \\nIn the post-apartheid era, Thoba’s focus shifted but his profound connection to the struggles of his community remained. He became deeply moved by the plight of people in Black townships, exploring the complex effects of urbanization and Westernization on traditional values. His canvases often feature narratives of survival, highlighting the harsh realities faced by children forced into stealing, prostitution, and violence on the streets. Drawing inspiration from human relationships, personal suffering, and current events sourced from newspaper articles, Thoba frequently accompanies his finished paintings with a handwritten letter, adding another layer of narrative to his visual commentary. \\nThoba’s significant contributions to South African art have been recognized both critically and commercially. His seminal piece, 1976 Riots, set a world record for the artist in June 2012, selling for R913,480 at a Strauss & Co auction. This was followed by another major sale in May 2013, with Fruits of Life achieving R818,496. In 2018, the Wits Art Museum hosted a major retrospective of his work titled Alfred Thoba: A Step Becomes a Statement, solidifying his status as a key figure in South African art history. He continues to live and work in his hometown of Johannesburg. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014062645469 gid://shopify/Product/9014062809309

[25365,25362,25363] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alia (b. 2002) is an emerging South African artist whose practice centres on creating large-scale installations and ambient sound collages. Her work navigates the complex interplay between decay and sustenance, exploring themes of material agency and an ethics of care. Drawing from her own familial histories, she seeks to re-member and engage with ancestral experiences of death, labour, and grief. Through the specific lens of practiced Cape Muslim rituals, Alia critically investigates the enduring structures and agendas of 'postapartheid' and 'postcolonial' South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9132522143965

item.title: Alice Mann
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104101597 Alice Mann gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640216219869 [] Alice Mann is an award-winning South African photographic artist (b. 1991) known for her intimate, long-term, and collaborative portrait essays. Discover her acclaimed series 'Drummies,' celebrated with the prestigious Taylor Wessing Photographic Portrait Prize. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alice Mann (b. 1991) is a South African photographic artist whose work is defined by intimate, long-term portraiture essays. Central to her practice is the concept of picture-making as a collaborative act, where she aims to create nuanced and empowering representations of her subjects. \\nMann's distinctive vision has earned her extensive international recognition. Her work has been showcased in numerous prestigious venues and events, including Red Hook Labs, Unseen Photo Fair, The National Portrait Gallery, Addis Foto Fest, and the International Centre of Photography. Her photographs are also a feature at major art fairs like 1:54 London and Paris Photo Fair. Both her personal projects and commissioned assignments have been featured in world-renowned publications such as The Guardian, The New Yorker, The New York Times Magazine, and National Geographic. \\n \\nHer acclaimed series, ‘Drummies,’ which thoughtfully explores the world of all-female drum majorette teams in South Africa, has garnered multiple awards. These include the Lensculture Emerging Photographer Prize (2018), the PHMuseum Women’s ‘New Generation’ Prize (2018), and the Grand Prix at the 34th Hyères International Festival of Fashion and Photography (2019). In a remarkable achievement, four images from the series were awarded first place at the prestigious Taylor Wessing Photographic Portrait Prize in 2018. This celebrated body of work was the subject of her first solo exhibition at the Kunsthal Rotterdam in late 2021, which coincided with the release of her first monograph, ‘Drummies,’ published with GOST Books."}]}]}

item.title: Alice Smeets
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104199901 Alice Smeets gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640216776925 [] Discover the work of Alice Smeets, a Belgian artist and photographer. Explore her award-winning documentary series on Haiti and her celebrated Ghetto Tarot project, a unique collaboration with Haitian artists that re-imagines the traditional tarot deck. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alice Smeets (1978) is a multi-disciplinary Belgium artist and documentary photographer known for per profound engagement with Haiti. After studying photography in Liége, she embarked on her first trip to the country, where she began her career assisting the renowned Magnum Photos photographer, Phillip Jones Griffiths. \\nSmeets gained significant international acclaim in 2008 when she received the UNICEF Photo of the Year Award for an image from her powerful series, \"Growing up in Haiti\". This recognition was followed by her first major solo exhibition in 2009 at the Ludwig Forum for International art in Aachen, Germany, cementing her role as a traveling documentary photographer. \\n \\nInspired by the creativity and resilience of the Haitian people, Smeets initiated her celebrated photographic project, the Ghetto Tarot. In collaboration with the Haitian artist collective Atis Rezistans, she created a new artistic interpretation of the traditional Rider-Waite tarot deck, staging the scenes within the vibrant context of a Port-au-Prince ghetto. This project exemplifies her unique approach of blending documentary practice with conceptual art and collaboration."}]}]}

item.title: Alice Marcelino
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104167133 Alice Marcelino gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640216449245 [] Discover the work of Alice Marcelino, a portrait and documentary photographer exploring identity and subcultures. See her internationally exhibited images and learn about her passion for teaching the next generation of photographers. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alice Marcelino is a portrait and documentary photographer whose work delves into the personal stories of individuals. She holds a degree in Photography from the University of East London, and her creative journey began with experimentation in various art forms, including dance and theatre. Before launching her own career, she honed her skills by assisting established photographers in Lisbon and Paris. \\nMarcelino's photography is distinguished by its exploration of identity, subcultures, and their significance in a globalized world. Her images reflect a deep and special interest in capturing the unique narratives of her subjects. Her work has been showcased in exhibitions across Macau, Portugal, and the UK, and has been featured in both print and online publications in London and internationally. \\nIn addition to her practice as an artist, Alice is a passionate documentary photography tutor. She is dedicated to sharing her enthusiasm for the medium and focuses on encouraging her students to discover and express their own unique creative voices."}]}]}

item.title: Alison Elizabeth Baker
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104396509 Alison Elizabeth Baker gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640216842461 [] Alison Elizabeth Baker (b. 1956) is a Zimbabwean artist and anti-poaching game ranger based in Victoria Falls. Her award-winning work uses site-specific materials like mud and bone to explore themes of conservation, nature, and environmental resilience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alison Elizabeth Baker, born on 17th April 1956 in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, has spent a lifetime immersed in art and nature. Surrounded by artists from a young age, she explored European galleries and the cave paintings of the Matopos, developing an early passion for painting, drawing, and horseback riding. Her foundational training in life drawing began under Alec Lambeth at the Bulawayo School of Art, providing invaluable early experience. \\nAlthough her father forbade her from attending art school, Alison pursued academic studies, earning a degree in History and History of Art from the University of Cape Town and later completing postgraduate qualifications in the UK. Her professional career has been diverse, spanning roles with the Zimbabwe Parks and Wildlife Authority, teaching art at the secondary school level, and serving as an Exhibitions Designer at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe. \\nCurrently based in Victoria Falls, Alison combines her work as an artist with her role as a game ranger, where she leads her own anti-poaching unit. This direct connection to wildlife informs her art, which often explores themes of environmental destruction, human responsibility, and the resilience of nature. Her use of site-specific materials—mud, sand, shell, and bone—creates a visceral connection to the landscapes she seeks to protect, while her work grapples with the cycles of decay, reconstruction, and survival of the planet. \\nAlison has participated in numerous exhibitions, including group shows at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe and the National Gallery of Bulawayo. Her recent solo exhibition A Book That Cannot be Read (2022-2023) at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe, curated by Fadzai Muchena, won the NAMA Arts Award for Exhibition of the Year in 2023. Her artistic legacy reflects both a deep commitment to environmental advocacy and an exploration of the intersection between history, art, and nature."}]}]}

item.title: Alison Kearney
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641104593117 Alison Kearney gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640216973533 [] Explore the work of Alison Kearney, a Johannesburg-based artist, researcher, and educator challenging Western art discourses. Discover her performance-based art, research on African art, and commitment to decolonizing art history through her work and teaching at the Wits Art Museum. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alison Kearney is a Johannesburg based artist, researcher and arts educator whose multi-disciplinary work is dedicated to exploring and challenging the very foundations of how art is understood. Her research praxis involves both creating art and theorizing it, with a specific focus on decolonizing inherited Western discourses. \\n \\nAs an artist, Kearney critically engages with the institutions and conventions of the art world. Her artworks have been shown in numerous group exhibitions locally and abroad, with a notable solo exhibition, ‘Offerings,’ held at The Goodman Gallery in Johannesburg in 2008. Since 2022, she has been developing a new body of work titled “The Museum Under Erasure,” which uses performativity and parody to interrogate how cultural value is determined and to challenge institutional authority. These public performances actively explore the audience's role in the creative process and the making of meaning in conceptual art. \\nAs a researcher and writer, Kearney is committed to theorizing modernist and contemporary African artworks in ways that break from Western epistemologies. She seeks to make explicit how both making and theorizing art can be forms of research, contributing to the decolonization of art history through unorthodox approaches to writing. This integrated philosophy underpins her work as an educator, both in her university teaching and in her public engagement with diverse audiences at the Wits Art Museum."}]}]}

[23406,23407] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alka Dass (b. 1992, KwaZulu-Natal) is a South African contemporary artist whose practice centres on the exploration of identity, memory, and folklore. After studying Fine Art at the Durban University of Technology, she/they received the prestigious Young Female Residency Award from The Bag Factory and 'Project Space' in Johannesburg in 2017. This recognition marked a significant step in their career, leading to the accomplishment of three international residencies and two solo exhibitions. \\n \\nWorking across diverse mediums including thread, cyanotypes, collage, and sculpture, Dass delves into personal and collective histories by drawing from archival family photographs, anecdotes, and dreamwork. A central tenet of her/their practice is the re-contextualization of techniques often dismissed as 'ladies' handicrafts.' By elevating these methods, Dass intentionally challenges and disregards the conventional hierarchies within contemporary fine art, creating a deeply personal and subversive visual language."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014044197085 gid://shopify/Product/9014044229853 gid://shopify/Product/9132522897629 gid://shopify/Product/9133227180253 gid://shopify/Product/9133227344093 gid://shopify/Product/9133227409629 gid://shopify/Product/9133227475165 gid://shopify/Product/9133227540701

His work captures issues of inequality, conflict, and resilience. Buy prints and books online to experience his powerful visual storytelling. [22167,22165,22161,22162,22166,22168,22169,22164,22163] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alon Skuy is a distinguished photojournalist born in Johannesburg, South Africa, and currently based in Miami, Florida. After studying photography at The Market Photo Workship, Skuy embarked on a career that lead him to become the Chief Photographer for the Sunday Times and The Times in South Africa. His work focuses on issues of inequality, conflict, resilience, and life on the fringes of society. \\nSkuy's career is defined by his depth and range as a news and documentary photographer. He is especially noted for his coverage of the 2012 Marikana Massacre, the most lethal use of force by South African security forces against civilians since the Sharpeville Massacre of 1960. His long-term work includes documenting xenophobic violence and intimate portrayals of subcultures. \\nHe has received numerous accolades, including recognition from the World Press Photo Foundation and multiple awards from the Picture of the Year International (POYI). Notably, he won first place in the News category of the POYI awards in 2015 for his work on the unrest at the Marikana Mine, and was awarded Photographer of the Year, Local in POYI in 2020. Skuy has also been honored with 9 Standard Bank Sikuvile Awards and multiple Vodacom Journalist of the Year Awards in photography. \\nIn addition to his photojournalistic achievements, Skuy was awarded the Ruth First Fellowship for Photojournalism at the University of the Witwatersrand for his photographic essay \"Living Inside A Bridge\" (2008). He has mentored young photographers and conducted workshops in collaboration with World Press Photo. \\nHis work has been featured in public collections and he has published notable books, including [BR]OTHER (2021), which received an Award of Excellence at the 80th Pictures of the Year International Awards, and MARiKANA 2012/2022, commemorating a decade since the Marikana Massacre."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014011199709 gid://shopify/Product/9014011232477 gid://shopify/Product/9014011265245 gid://shopify/Product/9014011298013 gid://shopify/Product/9014011330781 gid://shopify/Product/9014011363549 gid://shopify/Product/9014011396317 gid://shopify/Product/9014011461853

Since its inception around 2010, Alphabet Zoo has dedicated itself to fostering and exposing Johannesburg's zine culture to both local and international audiences. \\nOperating for approximately 15 years (as of 2010), the platform actively engages the community through practical printmaking and zine-making workshops. It focuses on the creation and distribution of zines and is committed to continuously expanding its dedicated zine library. \\nCollaboration is central to Alphabet Zoo's ethos; over the years; it has invited partnerships with a diverse range of creatives including \\nartists, illustrators, photographers, publishers, and designers. Explore her unique sculptures that blend figurative and abstract forms and delve into a career that combines artistic production with academic research on South African art history. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amalie von Maltitz is a distinguished South African sculptor whose work thoughtfully navigates the space between figuration and abstraction. Her art explores profound themes of form, identity, and transformation, reflecting a career deeply rooted in both artistic creation and intellectual inquiry. \\nVon Maltitz laid the foundation for her career at the prestigious Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, graduating in 1962. She further honed her craft in Germany at the Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Stuttgart. Her extensive career is marked not only by decades of artistic production but also by significant contributions as an educator and curator. She held positions at the Rand Afrikaans University (now the University of Johannesburg), where she also earned a Master of Arts in History of Art with distinction. \\nHer sculptural language is characterized by a modernist simplification of form, combined with a nuanced sensitivity to gesture and material. Von Maltitz has exhibited extensively in both solo and group exhibitions since the 1970s, including shows alongside other notable South African artists like Deborah Bell. Her academic pursuits include important contributions to the documentation of South African art history, notably through her work on a publication about the sculptor Edoardo Villa. \\nAdding a unique dimension to her creative practice, von Maltitz is also a licensed commercial pilot and aviation advocate, embodying a rare blend of artistic sensibility and technical precision."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014101344477 gid://shopify/Product/9014101410013 gid://shopify/Product/9014102491357 gid://shopify/Product/9014102655197 gid://shopify/Product/9014104228061 gid://shopify/Product/9014104424669 gid://shopify/Product/9014104457437 gid://shopify/Product/9014104490205

Unconstrained by a single medium, she expresses her ideas through sculpture, painting, and mixed media artworks. \\nHer art serves as a visual exploration of relationships and their broader impact on society. This intimate process gives her work a deeply personal yet universally relatable quality, offering insight into the human condition as seen through her eyes."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013405450461 gid://shopify/Product/9013405515997 gid://shopify/Product/9013419278557 gid://shopify/Product/9013419344093 gid://shopify/Product/9013948547293 gid://shopify/Product/9013948645597 gid://shopify/Product/9013948678365 gid://shopify/Product/9013948809437

item.title: Amber Alcock
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107017949 Amber Alcock gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640225067229 [] Discover the surrealist art of Amber Alcock, a graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art and recipient of the Simon Gerson and Judy Steinberg awards. Her paintings challenge apathy by exploring themes of care, the human-animal connection, and ecological consciousness through a unique blend of fantasy and unsettling beauty. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Surrealist painter Amber Alcock, a 2022 graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art, is redefining the narrative of 'care' through her evocative and unsettling artworks. An award-winning artist, Alcock received both the prestigious Simon Gerson and Judy Steinberg awards for her distinctive painting style upon her graduation. \\nIn a world often marked by apathy, Alcock’s work champions the concepts of fragility, tenderness, and conscientiousness as potent tools of preservation. Her surreal compositions are a battleground where horror and charm, humour and menace, awareness and ignorance converge. Through these juxtapositions, she aims to provoke a \"new wariness and awareness\" in the viewer. \\nAlcock's art delves into the complex and often fraught relationship between humanity, nature, and the animal kingdom. Drawing inspiration from art history and her own sense of personal power and helplessness, she uses the lens of fantasy and surrealism to cast a light on pressing ethical, personal, humanitarian, and ecological concerns. Her work does not seek to provide answers but rather to make evident the profound consequences of a collective lack of genuine care. \\n\"Alcock is fascinated by the inexplicably large galaxy of relational modes, transfused mythologies and histories that govern our attending of the relationship between humanity, the animal and nature,\" states a release about her work. Her paintings serve as a visual exploration of these intricate dynamics, prompting a re-evaluation of our place within the natural world. \\n"}]}]}

[14461,14465,14466,14467,14083,14084,14085,14086] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist Amira Shariff (b. 1999) utilizes photography as her primary medium to navigate the complexities of identity and connection in the contemporary world. Currently completing her degree in strategic brand communications at Vega, Shariff seamlessly merges her artistic pursuits with her professional roles as an art director, set designer, strategist, and cultural curator, where she serves as an art director and creative strategist for an agency and events. \\nShariff's formal photographic education began at the renowned Market Photo Workshop in 2019, followed by her involvement with the Through the Lens Collective in 2020. Her distinct approach to photography, which often involves layering images to create evocative and questioning narratives, has gained significant recognition. Her work has been showcased at prominent platforms including the FNB Art Fair (2022), the Through The Lens Collective Portrait Show (2020), and the Advanced Student Show at Berman Contemporary (2021). \\nInspired by her late uncle, Abdul Shariff, her photographic journey began at the age of thirteen. Today, her practice is a deeply personal exploration of her relationship with herself and the world around her. She poetically investigates how the very elements that are meant to connect individuals can also be the source of their disconnection, inviting viewers to question their own perceptions and the realities presented before them."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013399322845 gid://shopify/Product/9013399355613 gid://shopify/Product/9013399421149 gid://shopify/Product/9013399486685 gid://shopify/Product/9013403255005 gid://shopify/Product/9013403418845 gid://shopify/Product/9013403451613 gid://shopify/Product/9013403549917

item.title: Amy Ayanda Lester
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107607773 Amy Ayanda Lester 2493 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640226148573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013939568861","gid://shopify/Product/9013939962077","gid://shopify/Product/9013940420829","gid://shopify/Product/9013940945117","gid://shopify/Product/9013941567709","gid://shopify/Product/9014041772253","gid://shopify/Product/9014041805021"] Discover the work of Amy Ayanda Lester, a Cape Town-based artist with an Honours degree from Michaelis School of Fine Art. Her abstract art engages with themes of memory, loss, and the South African landscape, particularly fynbos and proteas, influenced by her family's history with Apartheid forced removals. [19813,19989,19853,23325,23328,19876] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Ayanda Lester (b.1992) is a Cape Town-based artist and musician whose vibrant, abstract works explore the intricate relationship between memory, loss, and the striking natural beauty of the South African landscape. A graduate of The Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, where she earned an Honours degree in Painting, Lester's work is deeply inspired by her surroundings, particularly the region's unique flora, colours, and people. \\nHer art, which spans paintings, prints, and collaborative vessels, often features iconic elements like proteas, fynbos, and the silhouette of Table Mountain. These motifs are not merely decorative but are imbued with personal and historical weight, stemming from her family's profound connection to the land and the trauma of their forced removal from their flower farm during Apartheid. This poignant contradiction—between the land's stunning beauty and the painful memories it holds—reverberates through her work. \\nLester's style is characterized by a loose, wandering quality, guided by an intuitive and spontaneous use of colour. She describes her application of colour as being dedicated to a specific feeling or moment, capturing its immediate, abstract, and playful essence. \\nThroughout her career, Lester has been a notable participant in numerous group exhibitions and has exhibited independently. In March 2024, she collaborated with printmaker Roxy Kaczmarek at the prestigious David Krut Workshop. Her recent projects also include a series of vessels with Natasha Human and a new body of nine original works on canvas prepared for a solo presentation at the Latitudes Art Fair in May 2024."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013939568861 gid://shopify/Product/9013939962077 gid://shopify/Product/9013940420829 gid://shopify/Product/9013940945117 gid://shopify/Product/9013941567709 gid://shopify/Product/9014041772253 gid://shopify/Product/9014041805021

Explore art that champions the freedom of being unapologetically oneself. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy-Lee Tak is a self-taught artist who, in her five years as a professional painter, has developed a distinct and resonant visual language. Working primarily with gouache, ink, and acrylic on paper, her art is a gentle yet powerful exploration of unapologetic rest, comfort, and the profound freedom found in accepting one's own skin. \\nHer paintings serve as intimate portraits of tranquility and self-possession. Each piece mirrors the artist's own aspirations for a life characterized by softness, self-love, and ease. Through her depictions of serene figures in moments of quiet contemplation and unabashed repose, Tak invites viewers to consider their own relationships with rest and self-acceptance in a world that often demands constant performance. Her work is a testament to the quiet strength found in vulnerability and the radical act of being at peace with oneself."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013992521949

item.title: Amy-Leigh Braaf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107280093 Amy-Leigh Braaf gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650693001437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013385461981","gid://shopify/Product/9013385724125","gid://shopify/Product/9013385756893","gid://shopify/Product/9013393522909","gid://shopify/Product/9013842149597","gid://shopify/Product/9013842182365","gid://shopify/Product/9013842215133","gid://shopify/Product/9013992325341","gid://shopify/Product/9014054912221"] Discover the work of Hakopike (Amy-Leigh Braaf), a South African painter and illustrator exploring mixed heritage and identity. Through vibrant art, she tells the untold stories of her Indonesian, Japanese, and Cape Malay ancestors in post-Apartheid South Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hakopike, the professional name of Johannesburg-born artist Amy-Leigh Braaf, is a South African painter, illustrator, and photographer with eight years of professional experience. Specializing in vibrant acrylic paintings and digital pieces, Hakopike embarks on a deeply personal exploration of her mixed heritage, drawing from travels and ancestral ties to Indonesia, Japan, and South Africa. \\nBorn into the complexities of post-Apartheid South Africa, Braaf was confronted with labels from a young age. This experience ignited a profound interest in the oral histories and ancestry within her family, leading her to question the nature of history documented primarily through storytelling. This inquiry became the catalyst for her powerful series, \"Celestial Deities.\" Through this body of work, she channels and explores the lives of \"those who came before,\" giving form to the ancestors who gifted her a rich and diverse lineage. \\nAfter learning of her great-grandmother's Indonesian and Japanese roots, combined with her \"Cape Malay\" heritage, Braaf began to investigate the meaning of being racially ambiguous in South Africa. Her art seeks to showcase the unique mixed culture of Coloured people in the nation, celebrating everything from local culinary traditions to the psychological resilience developed in response to the trauma of Apartheid. \\nThrough a compelling use of symbolism, vibrant colour, and narrative, \"Celestial Deities\" depicts characters that fuse her knowledge of the past with the reality of their descendants today. Hakopike's work aims to illuminate the rich, untold stories of those who were denied a voice, bringing their powerful histories to the forefront."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013385461981 gid://shopify/Product/9013385724125 gid://shopify/Product/9013385756893 gid://shopify/Product/9013393522909 gid://shopify/Product/9013842149597 gid://shopify/Product/9013842182365 gid://shopify/Product/9013842215133 gid://shopify/Product/9013992325341 gid://shopify/Product/9014054912221

item.title: Amy Lin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641107804381 Amy Lin gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640226377949 [] Discover the work of Amy Lin, an American artist creating intricate, hand-cut paper and pencil drawing/sculpture hybrids. Her art explores themes of the outsider and perception, and has been exhibited internationally in New York, Tokyo, and Houston. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Lin is an American artist currently living and working in London, following a recent relocation from Pretoria, South Africa. With a distinguished career spanning multiple continents, Lin has held fifteen solo exhibitions in major art hubs including New York City, Tokyo, and Houston. Her work has been critically acclaimed in publications such as the Washington Post and American Contemporary Art magazine and has been featured in the prestigious New American Paintings. \\nAt the core of Lin's artistic practice is an exploration of the outsider's perspective in society. She creates intricate drawing/sculpture hybrids that challenge the viewer's perception. In these works, detailed drawings are deliberately obscured by layers of meticulously hand-cut paper. This layering compels the viewer to physically engage with the piece, moving around it and peering through openings to catch glimpses of the hidden artwork beneath. As Lin explains, \"just as with any outsider, the viewer can’t fully understand or see the whole picture and can only infer what is happening beneath, based on the tiny glimpses that are visible from the surface.\" \\nIn an era dominated by technology, Lin's choice of medium is a deliberate counterbalance. While her precise and intricate forms are often mistaken for being digitally produced or laser-cut, she relies on the most fundamental tools: a pencil and a knife. This \"analog\" process is organic and intuitive, developing in a stream-of-consciousness where each hand-drawn mark informs the next. For Lin, these hand-made \"imperfections\" are a metaphor for humanity itself, reflecting the unique differences that make each individual beautiful. \\nLin's significant contributions to the art world have been recognized through numerous accolades, including the John Anson Kittredge Grant, the D.C. Commission for the Arts and Humanities Grant, and the Strauss Fellowship Grant. Her international presence has been further solidified through artist residencies in Tokyo and Singapore, which provided opportunities for engagement with art professionals and collectors across Asia, enriching and informing her unique practice."}]}]}

item.title: Amy Rusch
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108295901 Amy Rusch 1737 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640226443485 ["gid://shopify/Product/9132522602717","gid://shopify/Product/9133224001757","gid://shopify/Product/9133224067293","gid://shopify/Product/9133224100061","gid://shopify/Product/9133224198365","gid://shopify/Product/9133233045725"] Discover the work of Amy Rusch, a South African interdisciplinary artist who uses stitched thread on found plastic bags to explore themes of deep time, archaeology, and sensory experience. Her unique mark-making bridges contemporary culture with elemental time. [25459,25458,25460,25455,25456,25457] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Rusch is an artist working across disciplines and mediums. She’s been exploring a vibrational expression of mark-making, using stitched thread into layers of found plastic bags. \\n”Cutting, stitching, heating, pulling, binding, gathering, layering – these practices demand their own rhythm, by turns slow and meticulous then quick, fast interventions. The motions enacted in making provide a retrospective link to the embodied experiences, transmuted in the process. The machine stitching into plastic is not about replicating an experience, an object, or anything formally understood. The process is about sitting with the remnants of man-made materials; human time in contrast to the elemental and deep time.” \\nRecent exhibitions include presentations at the Investec Cape Town Art Fair 2025 and FNB Art Joburg 2024 with Suburbia Contemporary. Amy presented a solo body of work with SMAC gallery in 2022 titled Seeing with a Listening Ear, a culmination of 3 years of making. She exhibited at the Norval Foundation as part of the Norval Sovereign African Art Prize 2023 finalists exhibition. She has shown work at the Pretoria Art Museum, Iziko South African National Gallery as well as the Zeitz MOCAA. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9132522602717 gid://shopify/Product/9133224001757 gid://shopify/Product/9133224067293 gid://shopify/Product/9133224100061 gid://shopify/Product/9133224198365 gid://shopify/Product/9133233045725

Learn about her work in art education, her collaborations, and her artistic focus on intimacy, love, and healing. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Amy Simons is an artist and art facilitator based in Cape Town, South Africa. Since 2012, she has worked as a creative arts educator, collaborating with various organizations and educational institutions. In 2015, she completed her BA in Social Science at UCT and an intensive ASTAR art facilitator training course. \\nCurrently, Amy teaches art part-time at South Peninsula High School and collaborates with Indoni Dance Academy and The Astar Project on a youth development interdisciplinary art program. She designs and facilitates art processes for self-development and organizational growth, using art as a tool for social engagement and personal growth. \\nAmy's artistic work focuses on intimacy, love, and healing. She uses watery materials to express themes of love, loss, intimacy, and sexuality. She has participated in various exhibitions, including \"Spaces // A Constellation of Visual Stories,\" an exhibition she helped curate, market, and conceptualize."}]}]}

item.title: Ana Yaki Machava
item.description: Ana Yaki Machava 1956 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650693755101 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013389656285","gid://shopify/Product/9013389689053","gid://shopify/Product/9013389787357","gid://shopify/Product/9013389820125"] Explore the work of Ana Yaki Machava, a Mozambican painter and photographer who investigates themes of Black labor and dignity. Discover how she uses a spiritual channeling process involving "Dicuemba" to create powerful self-portraits and paintings. [13683,13682,13685,13684] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ana Yaki Machava is a Mozambican artist whose work in painting and photography confronts the complex questions of labor and the often-invisible work performed by Black bodies in global societies. Her powerful paintings invite critical reflection on the position of Black labor in relation to other races and social structures worldwide. \\nWhile acknowledging the lens of Afro-pessimism that often influences such depictions, Machava actively counters it by channeling a spirit she refers to as Dicuemba. This spiritual process is central to her practice, serving as a powerful method to restore and assert the dignity of the Black body. The channeling is not merely a theme but an active, integral part of her creation. \\nThis spiritual engagement is most evident in her self-portraits and collage images, which are produced concurrently with her paintings. Machava clarifies that these pieces are not representations of the channeling process, but rather the tangible artifacts of the process itself—a direct communion with Dicuemba. Through this unique methodology, her work transcends simple critique, becoming a restorative and dignifying act. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013389656285 gid://shopify/Product/9013389689053 gid://shopify/Product/9013389787357 gid://shopify/Product/9013389820125

[25402,25404,11421] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anastasia Pather s a Johannesburg-based artist distinguished by her unique practice of finger painting. Her work is a dynamic exploration of value, rejection, and production, delving into the intricate connections between surface, gender, and perceived worth. Pather masterfully employs ambiguity and innuendo, creating layered narratives that invite deeper contemplation. \\nHer paintings navigate the complex and often overlapping territories of exoticism, eroticism, and history. Through this lens, Pather examines her own-conflicted feelings surrounding culture, inheritance, and love. The tactile and immediate nature of finger painting allows for a direct and visceral expression of these multifaceted themes, resulting in works that are as intellectually provocative as they are visually compelling. She challenges viewers to confront their own preconceptions and explore the subtle nuances that define our understanding of identity and relationships."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013359247581 gid://shopify/Product/9133212270813 gid://shopify/Product/9133215842525

item.title: Ande Magoso
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108721885 Ande Magoso gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640227000541 [] Discover the work of Ande Magoso, a South African fine artist based in Durban. His paintings explore duality and cultural identity by merging human figures with goat and sheep features, reflecting his mixed Zulu-Xhosa heritage and the broader theme of societal contrasts. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ande Magoso (b. 1997) is a Durban-based fine artist whose work explores duality and identity, shaped by his personal history. Born in Kokstad to a Zulu father and a Xhosa mother, Magoso's upbringing in the predominantly Zulu community of Kwa-Ngcolosi, KwaZulu-Natal, placed him at the intersection of two powerful cultures. This experience of speaking a blend of isiZulu and isiXhosa, and navigating the nuances between the two, became a foundational influence on his artistic practice. \\nIn his artist statement, Magoso explains that his work is deeply influenced by the \"paired up elements within my identity,\" which include his mixed cultural background, his multilingualism, being a twin, and belonging to a religious family that also practices ancestral traditions. The very landscape of his youth—a village with dams, unchartered forests, and rolling hills—provides the rich and earthy color palette for his creations. \\nMagoso powerfully expresses the concept of duality by fusing human figures with the features of goats and sheep. This choice is symbolic and deeply rooted in his heritage: goats are central to Zulu rituals, while sheep are significant in Xhosa traditions. Through these hybrid figures, his art becomes a reflective space to interrogate the relationships between these contrasting components within himself, extending the conversation to broader societal dualities and contrasting ideas. \\n"}]}]}

Her collections are inspired by dance, joy, and finding art in the everyday. [13901,16656,10740,21601,12974,21602] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andiswa Bhungane is a Johannesburg-based mixed media artist whose work is a vibrant celebration of life's euphoric pleasures. Despite holding a Bachelor of Commerce from the Univ. of KwaZulu-Natal, her creative path was inevitable. Born in KwaZulu-Natal to a family of creatives—her mother a dressmaker and pastry chef, and her sister an event planner and restaurateur—Andiswa's love for art was nurtured from a young age, allowing her to hone the distinctive skills she employs today. \\nIn her practice, Andiswa masterfully combines luxurious and tactile materials, including resin, plaster, oil paint, acrylic, and various forms of gold. She launched her art career just two years ago, making an immediate impact with two collections: “Tempt the fates once more” and “Darling, might we dance?” Inspired by the liberating feeling of dance, these works capture moments of simple, profound joy. This theme of movement and celebration continued into her latest collection, “Invitation to the dance,” which features dynamic 3D sculpted pieces on canvas, beaming with rich colour and texture. \\nGuided by her personal motto, \"Find art in the everyday,\" Andiswa's work translates the energy of social connection and personal delight into tangible, opulent forms. Her art is an invitation to embrace the sentiment expressed by Agnes De Mille: “To dance is to be out of yourself, larger, more beautiful, more powerful…this is power. It is glory on Earth and it is yours for thetaking.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013353054429 gid://shopify/Product/9013376286941 gid://shopify/Product/9013394899165 gid://shopify/Product/9013449490653 gid://shopify/Product/9013844050141 gid://shopify/Product/9014000222429 gid://shopify/Product/9014000255197

item.title: Andrae Green
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641108852957 Andrae Green gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650696179933 [] Discover the work of Andrae Green, a Jamaican painter based in the US. His art explores Caribbean hybridity, collective consciousness, and fractured identity through vibrant, chaotic compositions. An alumnus of the New York Academy of Art, his work has been shown at the Beijing Biennale and the Louvre. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrae Green is a Jamaican painter whose work delves into the nuances of a collective consciousness shaped by memory, mythology, and the complexities of hybrid identity. Currently living and working in Western Massachusetts, Green’s art is a vibrant and chaotic exploration of his Caribbean heritage, which he describes as \"a hybridization of both European and West African cultures... a little of Europe, a little of African and a lot in between.\" \\nBorn in Kingston, Jamaica, Green is a graduate of the Edna Manley School for the Visual and Performing Arts. He was later awarded a full scholarship to pursue his MFA in Painting at the New York Academy of Art. His career is marked by significant international recognition, including representing Jamaica at the 2012 Beijing Biennale and being selected for the American delegation at the 2013 Salon de Société Nationale des Beaux-Arts at the Carrousel du Louvre in Paris. His work has been exhibited in the US, Jamaica, Canada, China, and France, and is held in numerous private collections. In a career highlight, his piece “Acquiescence I” was acquired by the National Museum of China in 2017. \\nDrawing inspiration from Cuban scholar Antonio Benitez Rojo’s concept of the Caribbean as a \"chaotic system,\" Green uses the physical act of painting to merge these diverging worlds and give order to their chaos. He describes his process as an \"active trance,\" where figures emerge on the canvas dancing, struggling, and playing—simultaneously connected and disconnected from themselves. \\nThese figures embody the \"disjointed collaged patchwork\" of his own hybridized identity. They speak to a contemporary world where history, identity, and fantasy are interchangeable, and reality itself can be reinvented. Through his art, Green explores the \"slippages that occur when the self and the space that it occupied is fractured and then put back together.\""}]}]}

item.title: Andre Clement
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109606621 Andre Clement gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650696442077 [] Explore the work of André S Clements, a South African artist who balances traditional painting and drawing with contemporary technology. Discover his portfolio, exhibition history, and his role as host of Life Drawing Randburg. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"André S Clements (b. 1973, Pretoria) is a South African artist whose practice is defined by the integration of diverse contexts and modalities. He navigates the space between time-honoured, atelier-based disciplines and the possibilities afforded by contemporary technology. This approach allows him to create work that is both grounded in tradition and dynamically engaged with the present. \\nHis identity is multifaceted—a husband, father, artist, developer, occasional activist, programmer, photographer, and facilitator—and these varied roles inform his artistic perspective. Based in Johannesburg, Clements has exhibited his work both locally and internationally, including shows in Johannesburg and Bordeaux, France. His art is held in numerous private and corporate collections in South Africa and abroad. His practice has also been featured in multiple arts and culture publications, with a recent appearance in Herri 7. \\nBeyond his personal practice, Clements is an active member of the local art community. He contributes to the foundational discipline of observational drawing by hosting Life Drawing Randburg, providing a space for other artists to hone their skills. This commitment to both personal creation and community engagement underscores his holistic approach to a life in the arts."}]}]}

item.title: André Rose
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641110032605 André Rose gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640228180189 [] Discover the work of André Rose, a South African artist, photographer, and wordsmith who explores social issues, urban life, and marginalized communities. His art is featured in the National Art Bank and has been shortlisted for major awards. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"André Rose is a South African wordsmith, painter, and photographer whose work serves as a poignant commentary on social inequity in contemporary society. His practice is deeply engaged with the urban environment, exploring how these spaces are utilized and how they profoundly influence the lives of their inhabitants. Rose is particularly drawn to the underbelly of the city, focusing his creative lens on marginalized people and communities living on the fringes. \\nHe views the city as a dynamic stage where the lives of its citizens unfold like a performance. Through his photography, he captures candid moments from this ongoing play, reflecting the intricate interactions between the \"actors,\" their peers, and the spaces they occupy. Whether through words, paint, or photography, his art consistently gives voice to pressing social issues and challenges viewers to see the unseen. \\nRose's compelling work has gained significant recognition. He was the runner-up in the prestigious Phatshoane Henney New Breed Art Competition in 2017 and has been shortlisted for other major awards, including the Sasol New Signatures (2018, 2019) and the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Award (2018). His art is held in the corporate collection of Phatshoane Henney Attorneys and the National Art Bank, in addition to various private collections."}]}]}

item.title: Andre Stead
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109704925 Andre Stead 733 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650696868061 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013325824221","gid://shopify/Product/9013403844829","gid://shopify/Product/9013403910365","gid://shopify/Product/9013403975901","gid://shopify/Product/9013404008669","gid://shopify/Product/9014016311517"] Discover the work of Andre Stead, a celebrated South African sculptor based in Cape Town. Explore his elegant, figurative sculptures in bronze, metal, and carbon fibre that question perception and beauty. Exhibiting at Christopher Møller Art Gallery. [14476,14474,14478] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andre Stead is a celebrated Cape Town-based sculptor renowned for his passionate exploration of the human form. With a style that often evokes the elegance and beauty of Art Deco, Stead masterfully works across a diverse range of materials—from traditional bronze and metals to modern plastics and carbon fibre—to create works of exceptional quality and expressive power. \\nHis artistic journey began at a young age, leading him to study painting and graphics at the prestigious Pro Arte School of Arts in Pretoria (1989–1993). After relocating to Cape Town in 1994, he honed his technical prowess through dedicated training in various disciplines. He studied metalworking under John Allesandri and gained invaluable hands-on experience at the Doyle Art Foundry and later at the Bronze Age Art Foundry, where he became proficient in every stage of the lost-wax casting process. \\nIn 2010, Stead embarked on his significant 'Anamorphic' series, which debuted with the solo exhibition 'Evolution' at IS Art Gallery in Franschhoek in 2011. This series became a cornerstone of his practice, influencing subsequent major bodies of work such as 'Illumination' (2012) at Christopher Møller Art Gallery and 'Elemental Man' at Knysna Fine Art. \\nOne of his most notable public works is the 'Flight of the Swallows' sculptural installation (2011), a prominent commission by Laurence Graff for the Indochine restaurant at the Delaire Graff Estate in Stellenbosch. Stead's extensive, first-hand experience with a multitude of materials and sculpture processes allows him to question the nature of human perception and the expression of beauty, grounded in his belief that humanity is intrinsically part of nature, not separate from it. He continues to exhibit his work at the Christopher Møller Art Gallery in Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013325824221 gid://shopify/Product/9013403844829 gid://shopify/Product/9013403910365 gid://shopify/Product/9013403975901 gid://shopify/Product/9013404008669 gid://shopify/Product/9014016311517

Rats appear regularly in her work as markers of how globalized systems dictate ethics, rendering them permissible collateral damage. \\n \\nTitles like 'Soil Erosion - the Musical' and 'Battle Hymn of the Crop Sprayers' delve into the disconnect in domestic consumption and Burgener's own conflicted culpability. [20815,20816,20817,22909,22910,22911,15024] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Munnik (b. 1943) is a distinguished South African Post-war & Contemporary artist celebrated for his masterfully executed and often surreal compositions. Working primarily as a painter and printmaker, particularly in the medium of etching, Munnik's art delves into complex allegorical narratives that explore themes of power, social commentary, and the absurdities of the human condition. item.title: Andrew Ntshabele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109147869 Andrew Ntshabele gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650700472541 [] Discover the work of Andrew Ntshabele, a contemporary South African artist based in Johannesburg. His mixed-media paintings of collage and acrylic explore themes of urbanisation, pollution, and the socio-economic realities of the inner city. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Ntshabele (b. 1986) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work serves as a powerful social commentary on the contemporary urban experience in South Africa. Living and working in the inner city, Ntshabele's art is a direct reflection of his environment, capturing the daily realities of its residents amidst the pressures of rapid urbanisation and its consequences. \\nOriginally from the rural town of Moruleng in the North West Province, Ntshabele moved to Johannesburg at the age of four and has since witnessed the city's profound physical, socio-economic, and political transformations in the post-Apartheid era. He holds a BTech degree in painting from the University of Johannesburg (2013). This academic grounding, combined with his lived experience, informs his investigation into the root causes of urban decay and the challenges faced by its inhabitants. \\nNtshabele’s distinct mixed-media technique—a fusion of collage and acrylic paint—mirrors the layered and complex environment he depicts. Using photographs taken during his travels around the city as a starting point, his work often focuses on the pervasive issues of pollution and poverty. Through his art, he explores the socio-economic predicament of many Black South Africans, offering a poignant and critical look at the promises and challenges of life in a post-colonial metropolis."}]}]}

[24684,24685,24683,24687,24681,24688,24686,24680,24678,24682,24679,24689] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Mogridge is a full-time South African fine artist specializing in ceramics and painting, whose work is characterized by an intuitive process and a dose of acerbic humour. This diverse professional background informs his current practice, which eschews strict planning in favour of imagination and the unexpected. Today, his work is exhibited in some of the most respected art galleries in the country. \\nMogridge’s art explores themes of power dynamics and what he terms \"the farce of authority.\" He embraces the absurd, inviting chance and \"unhappy accidents\" into his creative process. Working with figurative and literal archetypes on highly activated surfaces, he adds further layers of risk and uncertainty to his work. Ultimately, Mogridge invites viewers to relax and engage with his pieces on an immediate level, enjoying their wit and humour without the pressure of searching for a deeper, prescribed meaning."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014099312861 gid://shopify/Product/9014099345629 gid://shopify/Product/9014099378397 gid://shopify/Product/9014099411165 gid://shopify/Product/9014099443933 gid://shopify/Product/9014099476701 gid://shopify/Product/9014099509469 gid://shopify/Product/9014099575005 gid://shopify/Product/9014099607773 gid://shopify/Product/9014099640541 gid://shopify/Product/9014099673309 gid://shopify/Product/9014099706077

Explore his unique style that combines graphic elements with expressive mark-making. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Sutherland is a contemporary artist whose work is driven by a profound sense of wanderlust and the rich narratives that emerge from human encounters with the natural world. His paintings are a celebration of landscape, rendered in dynamic planes that skillfully combine graphic and illustrative sensibilities with expressive, painterly mark-making. This unique fusion creates a visual language that is both bold and deeply felt. \\nSutherland's adventurous spirit is not only evident in his thematic focus but also in his versatile approach to materials. He has a long history of experimenting with a wide array of media, including watercolours, brush pens, acrylics, charcoal, ink, spray paint, and collage, which he applies to surfaces ranging from canvas and paper to wood and walls. This material curiosity underscores his identity as an intrepid explorer in both life and art. \\nEducated at The Ruth Prowse School of Art in Cape Town, Sutherland further honed his skills working as an assistant to a local abstract painter. Through frequent travel and adventure, he continuously gathers inspiration, ensuring his work remains a fresh and authentic reflection of his explorations."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013440413917

item.title: Andrew Salgado
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109246173 Andrew Salgado gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640227262685 [] Discover the work of Andrew Salgado, a critically acclaimed Canadian contemporary figurative painter based in the UK. Explore his bold, expressive portraits that have gained international recognition and success at auction. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Salgado (b. 1982) is a Canadian artist based in London, widely regarded as one of the United Kingdom's leading contemporary figurative painters. Since graduating with an MA in Fine Art from the Chelsea College of Art in 2009, Salgado has achieved remarkable international success, defined by a series of over 16 sold-out solo exhibitions in major art capitals including London, New York, Tokyo, Cape Town, and Basel. \\nSalgado's work is celebrated for its bold, gestural, and often large-scale approach to portraiture, exploring complex themes of identity, sexuality, and memory through a vibrant and aggressive use of colour and texture. In 2017, he became the youngest artist to be honoured with a survey exhibition at The Canadian High Commission in London, a testament to his significant impact on the contemporary art scene. \\nHis rising prominence is further evidenced by extensive press coverage in publications like GQ, The Evening Standard, Artsy, and The Independent, as well as his strong performance in the secondary market. Since 2019, his works have consistently outperformed estimates at major auction houses, including Strauss & Co in South Africa and Phillips in New York. \\nA dedicated philanthropist, Salgado has raised over £135,000 for the Terrence Higgins Trust since 2014. His paintings are held in prestigious private and public collections worldwide, including the Oketa Collection, the Royal Bank of Canada Collection, the Government of Canada, and the collection of the Jordanian Royal Family."}]}]}

item.title: Andrew Tshabangu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109278941 Andrew Tshabangu [] Discover the work of Andrew Tshabangu, a leading South African photographer. Explore his poignant black-and-white images capturing themes of spirituality, community, and urban life, and learn about his major retrospective, "Footprints." {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Tshabangu (b. 1966, Dube, Soweto) is one of South Africa's most significant contemporary photographers, renowned for his evocative black-and-white images that explore themes of spirituality, community, and everyday life in post-Apartheid South Africa. His work occupies a unique space between social documentary and a quieter, more poetic mode of seeing, capturing the rhythms and realities of urban and rural existence. \\nFor decades, Tshabangu has focused his lens on the intimate rituals and transient moments that define the human experience, particularly within Black communities. His subjects often include Zion Christian Church (ZCC) worshippers, the vibrant street life of Johannesburg, and the quiet dignity of individuals navigating their environments. Through his masterful use of light and shadow, he creates images that are both timeless and deeply rooted in a specific social context. \\nHis significant contribution to South African photography was celebrated in the large-scale retrospective exhibition, \"Footprints,\" held at the Standard Bank Gallery in 2017. The critically acclaimed show, which surveyed over two decades of his work, was accompanied by a major book publication, solidifying his status as a pivotal figure in the nation's photographic canon. Tshabangu continues to live and work in Johannesburg, documenting the ever-shifting spiritual and social landscapes of his country. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Andrew Verster
item.description: Andrew Verster gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650701947101 [] Discover the legacy of Andrew Verster (1937 – 2020), one of South Africa's most important contemporary artists. Explore his vibrant paintings, drawings, and designs that celebrate colour, mythology, and the human form. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Andrew Verster (1937 – 2020) was one of South Africa's most versatile and celebrated artists, known for his vibrant and sensuous explorations of colour, form, and pattern across a remarkable range of media. Over a career spanning more than five decades, he established himself as a masterful painter, drawer, printmaker, textile and set designer, leaving an indelible mark on the cultural landscape, particularly in his adopted home of Durban. \\nEducated in the United Kingdom, Verster obtained a National Diploma in Design from the Camberwell College of Art (1959) and an Art Teacher’s Diploma from Reading University (1960). He returned to South Africa and became an influential Fine Arts lecturer at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and the Durban University of Technology. In 1976, he committed himself to being a full-time artist, a move that heralded an intensely productive period of creation and exhibition. \\nVerster's work often celebrates the human figure, mythology, and the lush, subtropical environment of Durban. He was renowned for his fluid use of line and a bold, often joyous, colour palette. His practice extended beyond the canvas to include acclaimed set and costume designs for theatre and opera, as well as large-scale public commissions. \\nIn recognition of his immense contribution to the arts, the Durban University of Technology (DUT) awarded Verster with an honorary doctorate in 2009. His work is held in major public and private collections across South Africa and internationally, cementing his legacy as a pivotal figure in South African contemporary art."}]}]}
