item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641202962653 Charles Nkosi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640313147613 [] Explore the impactful works of Charles Nkosi, a South African artist whose art delves into Black theology, existentialism, and the experiences of Black South Africans during apartheid. Known for his linocuts and collages, Nkosi's pieces offer profound insights into the struggles and resilience of Black communities. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Charles Nkosi is a renowned South African artist whose work powerfully explores themes of Black theology, existentialism, and the lived experiences of Black South Africans during apartheid. Known for his striking linocuts, collages, and paintings, Nkosi's art reflects the struggles, resilience, and cultural identity of township communities. His contributions have left a significant mark on South African contemporary art and its discourse on social justice."}]}]}

item.title: Charles Steroid Mamorobela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203388637 Charles Steroid Mamorobela 848 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640313180381 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013295284445","gid://shopify/Product/9013295317213","gid://shopify/Product/9013295382749"] Explore the impactful mixed media artworks of Charles Steroid Mamorobela, an award-winning contemporary South African artist known for his bold urban art that reflects the dynamic realities of Johannesburg. [4330,4332,4331] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Charles 'Steroid’ Mamorobela is an independent visual artist and a graphic designer; born in Limpopo and later relocated to Alberton, Johannesburg in 1994. \\nMamorobela holds a diploma in Fine Arts from the University of Johannesburg. His work varies in mediums, as he strives to employ all traditional fine art making processes including drawing, painting, sculpting, printmaking and digital art and design. \\nHis fine art studies have enhanced the development of his visual work from creating exquisite figures and landscapes to conceptualizing and creating dialogue through use of imagery, colour, and texture. Mamorobela's career reached a new level when he had the privilege of being one of the 2019 RMB talent unlocked artists that exhibited at the Turbine Art Fair, which gave him an insight for what it takes to be a part of an enormous and important visual art event. In the same year, Mamorobela won the Ekurhuleni prize at the 2019 Thami Mnyele art awards. \\nArtist Statement \\nMy artworks speak about the lives, issues, struggles and journeys of the people of Johannesburg; focussing on current issues in different parts of the city and how these different sections of the city connect to each other, or worse, how they've been neglected by government and service delivery. \\nJohannesburg, a busy city, is filled with crime, poverty, fraud and corruption on the one side and - on the other side - new opportunities; creating both pain and happiness. The paintings I create consist of highly textured abstract backgrounds interpreting the dirty streets of our current society but still highlighting the beauty of the city we call home. \\nThe imagery used in my artworks is inspired by the architecture, people and culture that interact with one another in this dystopian landscape. My art is a form of storytelling, of documenting moments in time using my influences, breaking news (current affairs) or things I see on a daily basis to direct the subject matter and mediums I use in my work."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013295284445 gid://shopify/Product/9013295317213 gid://shopify/Product/9013295382749

item.title: Chelsea Selvan
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203618013 Chelsea Selvan 1738 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640313409757 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359870173","gid://shopify/Product/9013366063325","gid://shopify/Product/9013849161949","gid://shopify/Product/9013849686237","gid://shopify/Product/9013849719005","gid://shopify/Product/9013849751773","gid://shopify/Product/9013849817309","gid://shopify/Product/9013849882845","gid://shopify/Product/9013849915613","gid://shopify/Product/9013849981149","gid://shopify/Product/9013850013917","gid://shopify/Product/9013850112221","gid://shopify/Product/9013943173341","gid://shopify/Product/9014010609885","gid://shopify/Product/9014010642653","gid://shopify/Product/9014010675421","gid://shopify/Product/9014010708189","gid://shopify/Product/9014010806493","gid://shopify/Product/9014010839261","gid://shopify/Product/9014010872029","gid://shopify/Product/9014010904797","gid://shopify/Product/9014010937565","gid://shopify/Product/9014010970333","gid://shopify/Product/9014011035869"] Discover the intricate mixed-media art of Chelsea Selvan, a South African artist and curator. Her work explores the fugitive nature of memory through dynamic collages and printmaking. Buy original art online and experience her unique visual storytelling. [22118,18945,18939,18937,22144,22119,22128,22117,18941,22125,22116,22133,20105,11443,18938,22126,18917,22127,18935,18936,18940,12165,18943,12160,18942] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chelsea Selvan (b.1997, Johannesburg, South Africa) holds a BA Fine Arts, with distinction, from the University of the Witwatersrand. She currently heads up the Editorial, Marketing and Social Media department for Latitudes Online and the RMB Latitudes Art Fair. \\nHer previous work experience at the Johannesburg Art Gallery, William Kentridge’s the Centre for the Less Good Idea, and the Wits Art Museum inculcated a keen interest in the way various genres and mediums of art and performance can intersect in gallery and museum spaces. \\nSelvan is driven by art and its ability to evoke emotion, challenge perspectives and spark dialogue. \\nInspired by intangible feelings and tangible objects Chelsea Selvan’s work explores the fugitive nature of memory, through seemingly abstract means. Her printmaking engages fluid colour fields, some carefully graded others painterly in their rendering. These are used as a backdrop to her dynamic compositions of calligraphic mark making and floating geometric forms. \\nThese configurations are a tentative notation of her fleeting thoughts and an echo of architectural spaces that have imprinted themselves in her mental and emotional fabric. \\nSelvan was the 2022 recipient of the prestigious ABSA L’Atelier award, and had her first solo exhibition with Gallery 2 in August 2024."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013359870173 gid://shopify/Product/9013366063325 gid://shopify/Product/9013849161949 gid://shopify/Product/9013849686237 gid://shopify/Product/9013849719005 gid://shopify/Product/9013849751773 gid://shopify/Product/9013849817309 gid://shopify/Product/9013849882845 gid://shopify/Product/9013849915613 gid://shopify/Product/9013849981149 gid://shopify/Product/9013850013917 gid://shopify/Product/9013850112221 gid://shopify/Product/9013943173341 gid://shopify/Product/9014010609885 gid://shopify/Product/9014010642653 gid://shopify/Product/9014010675421 gid://shopify/Product/9014010708189 gid://shopify/Product/9014010806493 gid://shopify/Product/9014010839261 gid://shopify/Product/9014010872029 gid://shopify/Product/9014010904797 gid://shopify/Product/9014010937565 gid://shopify/Product/9014010970333 gid://shopify/Product/9014011035869

item.title: Chelsea Young
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641205453021 Chelsea Young 2210 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640313966813 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014115795165","gid://shopify/Product/9014115827933","gid://shopify/Product/9014115893469"] Chelsea, an artist based in Botswana, blends textiles and oil paintings, inspired by her travels and natural surroundings. Explore her intuitive, experiential artworks that reflect the beauty and essence of human existence. [25148,25150,25149] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chelsea Young’s paintings are internal responses to natural environments, an attempt to recreate the stillness and gentle essence found in nature and, in turn, within each human \\nbeing. \\nThrough painting, she seeks to access a peaceful and balanced world, removed from the noise and excessiveness that have become characteristic of modern life. \\nYoung is deeply inspired by the interplay between stillness and movement in the natural world. She is drawn to the quiet yet dynamic energy that surrounds all living things, constantly seeking the harmony that exists within this balance. Before beginning a painting, she experiences a deep compulsion, a yearning to create a space of gentleness and calm. \\nThis space reflects the fleeting moments of tranquillity she encounters in nature, moments that seem to call to her until she finally picks up a brush and translates them onto the canvas. \\nOnce a painting is complete, it takes on a life of its own, evoking in her a longing to step inside that world once more. This ongoing tension, the pursuit of rediscovering that internal space, only to be compelled to explore it further, drives her creative process. Her work becomes an exploration of peace, a journey she considers an honour to undertake. \\nBorn in one of Africa’s fifty-four unique nations, Young feels humbled by her deep connection to the continent. She has lived and created in spaces near the Masai Mara, the Okavango \\nDelta, Table Mountain, and the Kruger National Park. These wilderness areas, along with the people who coexist within them, are central to her creative practice. As she continues to \\ntravel across the continent with curiosity, she seeks to uncover the gentle omnipresence that exists beneath its bold, vibrant, and dynamic landscapes. \\nYoung’s paintings serve as allies in bringing light to the world, offering a reminder of perfect stillness and the innate human ability to access a state of rest and unity. Within Africa’s vast natural wilderness, she finds a stillness that mirrors the quietude within each individual. This is the whisper of her paintings—a calling for peace."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014115795165 gid://shopify/Product/9014115827933 gid://shopify/Product/9014115893469

item.title: Chéri Samba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641213972701 Chéri Samba gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640322584797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013875245277","gid://shopify/Product/9013875998941","gid://shopify/Product/9013876818141","gid://shopify/Product/9013878554845","gid://shopify/Product/9013880979677"] Discover Chéri Samba (b.?1956, DR Congo), a Kinshasa?based painter?journalist renowned for his vibrant mixed-media “bubble paintings” combining text and imagery to critique social, political, and cultural life. Featured at Venice Biennale, Centre Pompidou, MoMA, and Musée Maillol. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1956 in Kinto M'Vuila, DRC, Chéri Samba currently resides and works in Kinshasa, DRC. \\nChéri Samba arrived in Kinshasa in 1972. A self-taught artist, he initially earned a living as a signboard painter and a comic strip illustrator for the magazine \"Bilenge Info\" before establishing his own studio in 1975. Much like many Kinshasa painters of his time, including Pierre Bodo, Moke, and Chéri Cherin, he drew inspiration from everyday life and addressed political, social, and economic issues in his artworks. To distinguish himself from his peers, he incorporated self-portraits into his works and added text in the form of commentary. He quickly gained popularity among the Kinshasa audience and could sustain himself through his art. \\n \\nHis paintings are always executed in a rich, vibrant, contrasting, and often glittering color palette, as if to downplay the seriousness of the subject matter. Regardless of his message, Chéri Samba aims to invite viewers into his paintings without apprehension: \"When I start a painting, I define the subject, the idea, the message, even the title. The image is clear in my mind, even the colors... I precisely draw the subject in pencil down to the details, directly on the canvas, without any preliminary sketches. I allow myself up to three versions of the same painting, but with slight differences.\" \\n \\nIn 1975, he created his first self-portrait, and by 1985, he decided to make himself a regular subject of his paintings so that both his name and his face would be recognizable. Noticing that viewers often glance briefly at paintings as they pass by, Chéri Samba also incorporates text or commentary within his canvases. The writing thus captures attention and allows for a better appreciation and understanding of the work. The artist refers to this style as the \"Samba-esque signature.\" For him, art knows no boundaries. The themes he tackles are universal: he portrays current events, customs, sexuality, illness, social inequalities, corruption, and more. \\nChéri Samba is credited with originating the term \"Popular Painting,\" which he defines as \"painting that emerges from the people and speaks to the people.\" \\nChéri Samba has been the subject of several solo exhibitions, including \"Chéri Samba, the Popular Painter of Zaire\" at the Provinciaal Museum voor Moderne Kunst in Ostend and the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London in 1990-1991. \"Chéri Samba\" at the Übersee Museum in Bremen in 1997, and \"J'aime Chéri Samba\" at the Fondation Cartier for Contemporary Art in 2004. \\nHe has also participated in numerous group exhibitions, including \"Art Everywhere\" at the Academy of Fine Arts - CIAF in Kinshasa in 1978. \"Magician of the Earth\" at the Centre Georges Pompidou and the Grande Halle de la Villette in Paris in 1989, which introduced him to the European audience. \"Africa Explorer 20th Century African Art\" at the Museum for African Art and the New Museum of Contemporary Art in New York in 1991. \"Painting on the Move\" at the Kunsthalle Basel in 2002, \"100% Africa\" at the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao in 2006, and \"Beauté Congo 1926 - 2015 Congo Kitoko\" at the Fondation Cartier for Contemporary Art in 2015. \\nFrom October 17, 2023 till April 7th, 2024 at the Maillol Museum, Paris Chéri Samba Will have his first retrospective exhibition “Chéri Samba dans la collection Jean Pigozzi” covering 40 years of creation. It presents over 50 paintings that take the viewer on a journey through several \"Samba-esque\" themes: self-portraiture as a central element of his art, Congo and Africa, geopolitics and the environment, art history, and finally, the theme of women, which introduces an unprecedented dialogue with Maillol's work in the museum. All the works gathered for this occasion come from the Jean Pigozzi collection, the world's largest collection of contemporary African art, which has been contributing to the recognition of sub-Saharan African artists on the international stage for over thirty years."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013875245277 gid://shopify/Product/9013875998941 gid://shopify/Product/9013876818141 gid://shopify/Product/9013878554845 gid://shopify/Product/9013880979677

item.title: Cheriese Dilrajh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641205518557 Cheriese Dilrajh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640314196189 [] Discover Cheriese Dilrajh, Durban-born artist whose multimedia practice (video, installation, textiles) explores migration, multiculturalism, and Indian Ocean histories. BA Wits, MA Goldsmiths. Solo show FNB Art Joburg 2024. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in the coastal town of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa (1997), Cheriese Dilrajh is an artist, writer, and researcher who believes in the Indian Ocean as a world of possibilities shared between African and Indian lands. She enjoys the way the sunset appears to be a Sahara of hues in-between the colour spectrum of pink and blues, and thinks about radical daydreaming under non-linear time. Her formal education is a BA Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, and has recently completed an MA in Art and Politics at Goldsmiths, although her more legitimate knowledge comes from the streets. While exploring migration, belonging, decoloniality, and radical occupation, Dilrajh’s interests extend into alternative ways of invoking the political through cross-disciplinary modes of thinking."}]}]}

His work combines modern influences with storytelling, psychology, and mythology, featured in top art fairs and exhibitions. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chevy Noir (b. 1997, Johannesburg, South Africa), is a contemporary expressionist artist whose work spans painting, printmaking, and animation. A graduate of the University of Johannesburg with a National Diploma in Financial Services Operations (2018). Noir initially pursued a career in the transport industry before redirecting his focus to the arts. In 2023, he completed his third year of printmaking at Artist Proof Studios and is currently finishing his fourth year. \\nNoir’s work engages with a variety of themes, drawing inspiration from contemporary art, storytelling, psychology, philosophy, and mythology. His visual narratives captivate audiences by blending modern influences with rich, symbolic representations. Noir’s artistic journey includes notable exhibitions such as Johannesburg Open Studios at Constitutional Hill and Transwerk (2022), Play Braamfontein (2023), and group shows like “On Common Ground” (2022), “Tales of Our City” (2023), and “Where You Are” (2024). His work has also been featured in prestigious art fairs such as the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, RMB Latitudes Art Fair, and FNB Art Fair (2024) with Artist Proof Studios."}]}]}

item.title: Chiderah Bosah
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641205813469 Chiderah Bosah 2631 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640315408605 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014002647261","gid://shopify/Product/9014002712797"] Discover Chiderah Bosah (b.?2000, Nigeria), a self-taught portrait artist whose expressive oil paintings reflect resilience, identity, and inner dialogue. His work has been exhibited internationally, including a solo show at Gallery?1957 Accra and participation in 1–54 (NY/Paris). [21666,21668] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chiderah Bosah, a Nigerian artist born in 2000, explores the intricate dialogues of the human spirit through his contemporary portraits. His artworks captures the essence of humanity by depicting powerful expressions that reveal the inner self. Bosah's work is defined by a profound exploration of identity and self-reflection, with his portraits often portraying individuals in moments of deep introspection. Through subtle body language and facial expressions, he conveys emotions and thoughts, creating an intimate connection between the viewer and the subject. \\n \\nBosah's unique style emphasizes rich colours and his signature brushwork, which imparts a soft, nuanced texture to his pieces. He frequently uses broad lines to accentuate the human form, particularly highlighting the vulnerability and transparency of his subjects' faces. His sophisticated colour palette, often muted and carefully selected, enhances the emotional depth of each portrait, drawing viewers into the narrative and inviting them to engage with the subject's inner world. \\n \\nThrough his art, Bosah encourages reflection on the complexities of identity, inviting viewers to find connections between his subjects and their own lives. His thoughtful compositions and attention to detail offer a mirror to the universal journey of self-discovery, showcasing the beauty and complexity of the human experience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014002647261 gid://shopify/Product/9014002712797

[25445,25429] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chigozie Obi (b. 1997) is a multidimensional artist whose practice engages various materials to narrate stories influenced by personal and societal encounters. These themes are not only reflective of her personal journey but also serve as a bridge to connect with others who share similar experiences. \\nObi obtained a bachelors degree of Visual Arts from the Creative Arts department, University of Lagos in 2017. Her work has been featured in several exhibitions and fairs, which include, ‘1-54 Marrakech’, Morocco (2025), ‘In Stillness of Being’, Yenwa Gallery, Lagos, Nigeria (2024), ‘Celebrating Identities’, AG18 Gallery, Vienna, Austria (2024), ‘Young Talents: Polymathic Nature’, C+N Gallery CANEPANERI, Genoa, Italy (2023), ‘Future Fair’, New York (2023), ‘Unity’, Vollery Gallery, Dubai (2022), 'Intersections’, Gallery Affinity, Lagos, Nigeria (2021). She won the Access Bank 'Art X Prize’ (2021), is one of the winners of The Future Awards Prize For Art (2021) and was a residency artist at Gasworks, London (April - June 2022)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9133216465117 gid://shopify/Product/9133234847965

item.title: Chinwe Chigbu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641206993117 Chinwe Chigbu 581 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640316391645 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013284667613","gid://shopify/Product/9013284700381"] Chinwe Chigbu is a contemporary visual artist from Nigeria, using photography and performance to explore identity, culture, and social issues. Her work challenges societal norms and advocates for the liberation of black women and marginalized communities. [3251] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chinwe Chigbu (b.1994) is an emerging contemporary visual artist from Nigeria, recognized for her innovative use of photography and performance art. Through experimentation with print methods, Chigbu brings her conceptual ideas to life, exploring themes of identity politics, the black female body, and the nuances of contemporary society and culture. \\nHer work is driven by deep emotional engagement, utilizing her own body and everyday objects to convey complex realities and illusions. Drawing on memories and nostalgia, she experiments with movement, light, shadows, contrast, and texture, creating pieces rooted in empathy, love, and a commitment to human rights. Chigbu advocates for the liberation of the black community, particularly black women, and intersectional groups, seeking to challenge societal limitations through her art. \\nRejecting socio-cultural constraints, Chigbu rewrites her own truth, constructing unique and thought-provoking situations that invite viewers to confront their own perceptions and reconsider what is known, what exists, and what could be. Her work features a subtle pseudo-minimalist style that addresses a range of subjects in multi-layered, corporeal ways. \\nHer meticulously planned pieces resonate with imagery from the boundless imagination, blending abstraction and deconstruction. This approach shifts meanings and invites multifaceted interpretations that hover between reality and illusion. Chigbu draws inspiration from nature, history, popular culture, and her environment, using art as a potent medium to challenge preconceived notions and address pressing societal issues. Her work celebrates individuality, humanism, womanism, black identity, and culture."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013284667613 gid://shopify/Product/9013284700381

item.title: Chipika Simanwe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641207058653 Chipika Simanwe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640316817629 [] Discover Chipika Simanwe, a Lusaka-born abstract painter whose soft yet vivid narrative works reflect Zambian social life. Trained in computer graphics, award-winning (2020), and known for engaging solo shows like Red Handed Too. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chipika Simanwe is a visual fictionist. His work tells stories that only images best describes. Stories that defy words by turning things into fantasy. He is a culture custodian who pokes fun at the very idea of curating culture. He throws jets of liquid at the viewer. As some of the paint lands on the canvas, he begins to dialogue with you, but does not seem to be talking to you, as he is yelling at you. His work provides food for thought though some of thr offering might look toxic, and taste acidic. \\nHis work has been exhibited in the USA, Spain, UK, and South Africa to mention a few. An award winning artist, he recently won best two-dimensional artist at the 2020 Zambia Vistula Arts Council Awards. \\n“As an artist, I am sympathetic with the challenges society is currently facing and through my work I attempt to show these moments through a variety of angles that capture everyday Zambian life.”"}]}]}

She is trained as a printmaker and regularly works in painting and drawing as well as narrative forms of writing, audio and video. \\nShe holds a BFA from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, Cape Town (2011), an MFA from The Glasgow School of Art (2017) and was awarded a yearlong fellowship at the Glasgow Sculpture Studios in 2018. She has exhibited and curated locally and internationally and is currently working on her third collection of very short stories. \\nShe lives in Johannesburg, where she develops collaborative curatorial projects under the name 'gallery, gallery' and writes for artists, alongside her own artistic practice. She also recently co-founded 'wherewithall' along with Kundai Moyo and Amy Watson, which is an online database of equipment, practical knowledge and research into independent curatorial practices in South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013330116829 gid://shopify/Product/9013337555165 gid://shopify/Product/9013353742557 gid://shopify/Product/9013353808093 gid://shopify/Product/9013353873629 gid://shopify/Product/9013353939165 gid://shopify/Product/9013354037469 gid://shopify/Product/9013354135773

[22930,22931,22932,22929] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chris Denovan (b. 1983, Cape Town, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist known for his surreal, expressive paintings and sketches that explore the interplay between strength and vulnerability. As a Queer man, Denovan navigates the world from a multitude of perspectives, incorporating themes of non-toxic masculinity, nature, love, and companionship into his work. practice seeks to heal and overcome feelings of fear and marginalization. \\nDenovan's work often depicts groups of characters in playful, carefree environments, emphasizing the harmony between human figures and nature. His art delves into the intricate balance between opposing forces such as order and chaos, pleasure and danger, love and war. His creations are infused with classical Greek aesthetics, offering a modern take on figuration and portraiture. Through transparent and solid textures, he captures both the robust strength and delicate vulnerability of his characters, blending strong masculine figures with elements of cubism and abstraction. \\nRepresented by 99 Loop Gallery in Cape Town, SOTA Gallery Online, and Ebony Curated in Franschhoek, Denovan continues to create art that challenges preconceptions and celebrates diversity. His work offers a platform for healing and unity, inviting viewers to explore the complexities of human experience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013331198173 gid://shopify/Product/9014030762205 gid://shopify/Product/9014030794973 gid://shopify/Product/9014030827741 gid://shopify/Product/9014030860509 gid://shopify/Product/9014030893277

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641212235997 Chris Kriek gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640317604061 [] Discover Chris Kriek, a Cape Town-based artist specializing in layered charcoal drawings, oil paintings, and collage-inspired works. Drawing on analogue photography and VHS stills, he reconstructs personal and found memories through evocative mixed-media. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chris Kriek has always had a keen interest in art and design but it was only recently that he decided to pursue a full-time art career. He works in many different mediums (including sculpture and ceramics) but his preferred ones include charcoal drawing and oil painting. \\nKriek’s inspiration comes from memories and records of his own and found analogue photography as well as film stills from VHS home and documentary movies. He says that he explores the way we construct and recall memories through the use of collage, layered drawing and oil painting. Often using found ephemera and discarded snapshots as a starting point to reinterpret-edit-erase-re-imagine memories. His style ranges between the figurative and the abstract. \\nHe obtained a BA Fine Arts (Applied Graphics) in 2005 from the University of Stellenbosch (Cape Town), specialising in analogue art photography. Kriek’s work experience is varied; graphic designer, illustrator, art director, running businesses and part-time lecturer in design and drawing (College of Cape Town). Kriek lives and works in Cape Town."}]}]}

item.title: Christiaan Conradie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641210630365 Christiaan Conradie 694 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640318423261 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013352792285","gid://shopify/Product/9013353021661","gid://shopify/Product/9013957689565","gid://shopify/Product/9013957787869","gid://shopify/Product/9013957918941","gid://shopify/Product/9013958017245","gid://shopify/Product/9013958148317","gid://shopify/Product/9013958279389"] Explore Christiaan Conradie (b.?1984, Cape Town), an acclaimed painter who captures expressive portraits of elderly men with vibrant mixed-media textures. Inspired by Rembrandt, Rubens, and Mexican rituals, his work has shown globally in solo and group exhibitions. [10656,20578,20573,20574] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Christiaan Conradie experiences and focuses on concrete spheres within the arts. He draws inspiration from the age-old pictorial techniques of Rubens and Rembrandt while borrowing from Cy Twombly’s abstraction and conceptual art. His pieces are interestingly diverse and multiple but they all share a common, unique denominator. There is no other Conradie. Inspired by the loose, fast and dynamic brushstrokes of Rubens, he picks up on the carnal and dionysian exuberance of the bodies, turning paint into an ode to the human body. As Rembrandt, he isolates living bodies to better capture them, and thus creating a disruption with his time. By doing so, he depicts a transfigured, almost overly alive human body and creates an intimate space of reflection within our complex world. Evident too are echoes from the works of Twombly through the superposition of multiple layers and textures, which resembles a calligraphic, covert staining of the working surface. \\nConradie establishes a concrete dialogue between his favourite artists. He considers his work as a space where the opposite reunite. As he put an extreme patience and precision into the crafting of his works, he invites us to thoroughly examine his human characters and to enjoy the rational, measured side of his works. He paints these figures in silent and immovable spaces, calling for reflection. Yet, these impacting, hyper-realistic figures appear as dismembered, uncomplete, textured and sensitively rendered. Conradie points out the limits of the human body and its weaknesses. Through thorough research and painting, he re-creates personalities that embody time and flesh, bodies that are fragmented and dismembered and yet retain a vivid expression. His subjects are infinite beings that address the issue of age and death. Conradie plays with (a) temporality and frees his pieces from any contextualization whatsoever. \\nHowever, time is ‘felt’: it weighs. While the painted bodies, skin and objects highlight the weight of time, time comes to life through colours and textures. Conradie have clear views on what he wants to achieve and doesn’t rest until he finds the materials that he needs to awaken the emotions he likes. His art is thought as a bridge that unites two opposite worlds that, put together, convey vitality, reason and sensitivity. He uses oil, watercolour, objects and lights amongst other materials. He uses them as devices that allow him to transit between two worlds: the rational and the intuitive. It is precisely in these in-betweens where Christiaan’s creation takes place. His subjects are surrounded by unique, peculiar aesthetics. The paint breaks free from the linear and rational world through its own plasticity, textures and uncertain forms as well as through its irregularities and intensity, transporting one into the world of emotions. Dichotomous spaces are the essence of Conradie’s paintings. \\nAged subjects, with folkloric components, serenity and violence, order and chaos, rationality and insanity, hope and despair, Christiaan plays a game of contradictions that yields a deep sense of vitality, supported by genuine and majestic aesthetic impressions. Christiaan is currently working on a series of works that result from his recent extended stay in Mexico. After living there for a little more than three years, he’s been drawing inspiration from the harsh confrontation of different realities he witnessed. Mexico captured his imagination aesthetically as much as it did emotionally. A new space came to life, both floral and bloody, both spiritual and down-to-earth. Conradie’s current proposal aims at finding a new meaning in the symbols, fragments and sensations of his Mexican stay while intending to adapt them into his work. Thanks to a spontaneous, seamless integration of Mexico into his art, Conradie provides us with powerful, brand new aesthetics and spaces."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013352792285 gid://shopify/Product/9013353021661 gid://shopify/Product/9013957689565 gid://shopify/Product/9013957787869 gid://shopify/Product/9013957918941 gid://shopify/Product/9013958017245 gid://shopify/Product/9013958148317 gid://shopify/Product/9013958279389

item.title: Christiaan Diedericks
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641211023581 Christiaan Diedericks 431 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640318390493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013288861917"] Explore Christiaan Diedericks (b.?1965), an acclaimed South African printmaker known for his conceptual, political monotypes and etchings. Awarded international residencies and prizes, his works are held in major museum collections globally. [3658] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"In my work, time and space appear to dissolve, and an air of conflict erupts. This is often a direct result of a personal aim to calm and disturb at the same time - drawing parallels between the two extremes of utopia and dystopia. There is always a secondary narrative in my work. The primary narrative has symbolic authority and aesthetic promise, although the mysterious secondary narrative exists in order to provoke thought in the viewer.\" \\nChristiaan Diedericks is a multi-award winning visual artist who is considered by many to be one of the finest print makers to have emanated from South Africa. \\nChristiaan has completed over 50 international residencies and has participated in more than 30 international Biennales. \\nHe has developed a strong and loyal global collector’s base who resonate with his artwork and his voice which speaks against social, political and economic injustice. His works grace numerous important museum, corporate and private collections, including MOMA (The Museum of Modern Art in New York), Ampersand Foundation, Cité Internationale des Arts (Paris, France) and the Museum of Contemporary Art (Auvergne, France). Christiaan graduated Fine Arts Cum Laude at the North West University (NWU) and went on to complete his Masters in Fine Art at the University of Pretoria in 2000. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013288861917

item.title: Chuma Adam
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641212924125 Chuma Adam gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640319635677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013464563933","gid://shopify/Product/9013835595997","gid://shopify/Product/9013926133981","gid://shopify/Product/9013926232285","gid://shopify/Product/9013945106653","gid://shopify/Product/9013945172189","gid://shopify/Product/9013945303261","gid://shopify/Product/9013987999965","gid://shopify/Product/9013988065501","gid://shopify/Product/9013988163805","gid://shopify/Product/9013988196573","gid://shopify/Product/9013988262109","gid://shopify/Product/9013988360413","gid://shopify/Product/9014007464157","gid://shopify/Product/9014047703261","gid://shopify/Product/9014047867101","gid://shopify/Product/9014047899869"] Discover Chuma Adam (b.?2001, Johannesburg), a multidisciplinary artist whose earth-toned textures blend soil, umbaco, acrylic, drawing, and print to explore Black identity, visibility, and self?actualisation through Glissant?inspired opacity and abstraction. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chuma Adam (b. 2001) is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, currently completing her Fine Arts degree at the University of Witwatersrand. Her practice spans painting, printmaking, textiles, sculpture, and drawing, with her work deeply influenced by Édouard Glissant’s theory of opacity from Poetics of Relation. Adam's art challenges notions of visibility and self-actualization within the context of Blackness and womanhood, exploring the complexities of identity through abstraction. \\n \\nHer process is heavily informed by her research into Pan-African philosophers and thinkers, and she often incorporates materials like sand and soil from her mother's home into her earth-toned paintings. This tactile element, combined with repetitive mark-making, serves a form of documentation and reflection on the nuanced emotional landscape of Blackness. Chuma's work evokes a sense of vulnerability and introspection, offering immersive visual experiences that speak to the intangible and evolving aspects of identity. \\n Chuma takes into great consideration her research which is led by prolifics. Chuma mainly works through these thoughts, emotions, and conceptual processes through the abstraction of the intangible complexities of navigating one’s self. In trying to disassemble the complexities of her Blackness and womanhood, Chuma introduces texture to her paintings by mixing sand and soil from her mother’s home into her earth-toned paintings and through repetitive mark making which functions as a form of documentation of her cosmic quest. Chuma does this in an attempt to excavate a multiplex of complex feelings, and ideologies surrounding Blackness and womanhood while paying homage to the genesis of African art. Chuma maintains and contains these intense feelings with her emotive, and sometimes controlled brushstrokes within these familiar and organic shapes, creating an immersive and introspective viewing experience. \\nChuma has completed and graduated with a Honours degree in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (2024) and was shortlisted for the WITS Young Artist Award (2022, 2023)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013464563933 gid://shopify/Product/9013835595997 gid://shopify/Product/9013926133981 gid://shopify/Product/9013926232285 gid://shopify/Product/9013945106653 gid://shopify/Product/9013945172189 gid://shopify/Product/9013945303261 gid://shopify/Product/9013987999965 gid://shopify/Product/9013988065501 gid://shopify/Product/9013988163805 gid://shopify/Product/9013988196573 gid://shopify/Product/9013988262109 gid://shopify/Product/9013988360413 gid://shopify/Product/9014007464157 gid://shopify/Product/9014047703261 gid://shopify/Product/9014047867101 gid://shopify/Product/9014047899869

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641211777245 Christine Nyatho 2583 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640319242461 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013981905117","gid://shopify/Product/9013981937885"] Discover Christine Nyatho (b.?1993, Kampala), a Ugandan mixed-media artist working with barkcloth, fabric, raffia, and acrylic. Her solo show "Kafunda Mama" (Amasaka Gallery) celebrates resilient women and lunar symbolism through textures of healing and power. [21049,21050] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Christine Nyatho, born in 1993 in Kampala, Uganda, is a mixed media artist dedicated to reviving indigenous art-making practices through the innovative use of locally sourced organic materials. She uses bark cloth, discarded paper, fabric, raffia, and acrylic on linen to create evocative, multidimensional artworks. Nyatho’s work draws inspiration from celestial bodies, particularly the moon and its subtle yet significant influence on human behavior. This fascination with the cosmos is mirrored in her artistic exploration of themes related to natural cycles. By weaving together these elements, Nyatho’s art becomes a meditation on the interconnections between the heavens, the earth, and the human experience. Through her mixed media practice, Nyatho seeks to connect contemporary audiences with the rich heritage of indigenous art forms while reflecting on universal themes of growth, change, and harmony. Her work serves as both a tribute to traditional craftsmanship and a contemporary exploration of the forces that shape our lives."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013981905117 gid://shopify/Product/9013981937885

item.title: Christine Dixie
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641211744477 Christine Dixie 1781 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640319045853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013431730397","gid://shopify/Product/9013850177757"] Explore Christine Dixie (b.?1966), a South African printmaker, installation artist, and academic known for multidisciplinary works like The Binding, To Be King, and Even in the Long Descent, exhibited internationally and collected by major institutions including Smithsonian. [15907,15908,18946] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Christine Dixie is an established South African artist, who has regularly exhibited in that country, the US and Europe. She is primarily a printmaker, but her art also finds expression through films or elaborate installations. \\nHer work challenges the ways gender roles have been historically conditioned by society, myths, and image-making. The manifestation of the colonial history that haunts the town of Makhanda in South Africa, has compelled her preoccupation with Europe’s legacy in Africa. Her practice and aesthetic rely on archival imagery and in-depth research. \\nHer work is included in national and international collections including The New York Public Library, The Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, The Standard Bank Gallery, The Johannesburg Art gallery, The Durban Art Gallery, the Iziko National Museum of South Africa, and the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Museum of Art. \\nInternational group shows include Earth Matters: Earth as Material and Metaphor curated by Dr. Karen Milbourne (2007) and The Divine Comedy: Heaven, Purgatory and Hell Revisited by Contemporary African Artists curated by Simon Njami (2012), both of which opened at the Smithsonian Museum of African Art. Her installation To Be King was part of the Personal Structures exhibited at Palazzo Bembo in Venice (2017) and was shown at the International Festival at the Coronet Cinema in London and the Kaunas in Art Festival in Lithuania (2018) and the Iwalewahaus, Bayreuth, Germany (2022). \\nRecent exhibitions include, @ Bathurst St., Makhanda at the Gallery of the SARChi chair at the University of Johannesburg, (2022). Blueprint for the DisOrder of Things, Wits Art Museum (2022) and The Astronomer, the Princess and The Order of Things , Graham Contemporary (2022)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013431730397 gid://shopify/Product/9013850177757

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641212956893 Chumisa Fihla gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640319701213 [] Explore the work of Chumisa Fihla, a South African sculptor known for his mixed-media sculptures that address themes of identity, migration, and cultural transformation. Discover his exhibitions and artistic journey. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Chumisa Fihla is a young South African artist from Masiphumelele, Cape Town. He is currently an artist in residence at the Centre for Humanities Research at the University of the Western Cape (UWC). \\nA few words from Fihla as to why he is pursuing a career as an artist: \\n“I am the kind of person that likes to work creatively and with my own hands. I grew up in a family that has artistic skills and is creative, but none of my siblings have ever been able to go further with their careers. I want to bring a change in my family and community. The other reason I want to study art is the fact that you can share your emotions, experiences, thoughts. I like that in the art world you get to make strong relationships and meet people who have different ideas and are willing to share.” \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Ciara Talisa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214333149 Ciara Talisa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640322912477 [] Discover Ciara Talisa Pillay, a South African mixed-media artist featured at Latitudes Gallery’s RMB Latitudes Art Fair 2025. Her introspective photo-print series Shame me, Shape me?I explores vulnerability through transformative self-portraiture. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ciara Talisa (b.1999) is a queer, Indian artist from Durban, KwaZulu Natal who is currently based in Johannesburg. Her creative practice revolves around the omission of queer sexual education for queer youth in South Africa, the portrayal of queer bodies in pornography, and the narratives surrounding queer Indian bodies and identities through an exploration of historical Indian erotic art in the modern age. She thus creates counternarratives emerging from historical metanarratives regarding erotic art and pornography on the the themes of sex, identities, and sexuality in the spheres of pre- and post-colonialism that further create conversations around current sexual education systems within South Africa and globally."}]}]}

[17123,9449,9448,6869,14690,4333,17117,14688,14686,13376,13377,13378,17133,17124,6877,4334,7093,13375,17122,17120,18648,17625,17623,17629,17627,17622,6876,6873,17118,16072,5956,5957,17125,6874,6871,7095,25504,25505,8571,9411,17121,14684,14685,18025,9390,9391,6878,7092,14687,6870,8400,6875,17126,8144,6872,11474,16071,497,14691,14689,16273,7094,17119,17132] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cinthia Sifa Mulanga (b. 1997, Lubumbashi, DRC) s a contemporary artist known for her poignant explorations of the Black female experience through painting and collage. Raised in South Africa, Mulanga's practice is rooted in her diverse cultural experiences. Trained as a printmaker at Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, she later gravitated towards painting and collage, mediums that have come to define her artistic journey. \\nMulanga's art focuses on the representation of Black women, engaging with various personas and emotions to highlight the complexities of female identity. Her multi-perspectival portraits juxtapose multiple women within architectural spaces, creating open conversations about beauty and identity. By incorporating painted or collaged artworks within her compositions, Mulanga challenges the absence of Black female subjects in Western painting and critiques the representation of women by male artists. \\nHer visual references often draw from popular culture and the history of Western art, recontextualizing these elements to pay tribute to other artists and explore aspirational lifestyles. Mulanga's work has been showcased in numerous exhibitions, including her solo show \"In The Becoming\" at Goodman Gallery in Johannesburg (2022) and group exhibitions at Bill Brady Gallery in Miami and The Artroom Gallery in Johannesburg. \\nMulanga has also received several accolades, including recognition from the Normal Sovereign African Art Prize (2023) and the British Fashion Council’s New Wave Creatives. She has collaborated with prominent brands like Gucci, reimagining the iconic Diana Tote Bag. Mulanga continues to live and work in Johannesburg."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013275754717, gid://shopify/Product/9013295513821, gid://shopify/Product/9013295612125, item.title: Claire Lichtenstein
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214464221 Claire Lichtenstein 2544 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640323010781 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014100426973","gid://shopify/Product/9014100459741","gid://shopify/Product/9014100492509","gid://shopify/Product/9014100525277","gid://shopify/Product/9014100558045","gid://shopify/Product/9014100590813","gid://shopify/Product/9014100623581","gid://shopify/Product/9014100689117","gid://shopify/Product/9014100754653","gid://shopify/Product/9014100787421"] Discover Claire Lichtenstein (b.?1984), a South African abstract painter based in Wilderness. Known for her tactile, emotionally resonant works—oil on canvas, watercolor paper, and pearlescent Perspex—featured in exhibitions such as Canvases in Bloom (2023) and (e)mersion (2025). [24727,24720,24724,24721,24725,24723,24726,24722] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Claire Lichtenstein, born in 1984 in Somerset West, is a contemporary abstract South African painter, whose work reflects her profound engagement with the self, the natural world, and the creative process. In 2011, Lichtenstein first started studying painting, and made the decision in 2014 to commit fully to her artistic career. \\nIn addition to her artistic pursuits, Lichtenstein cherishes the transformative journey of motherhood, which has brought its own set of challenges and joys. Balancing the roles of being a mother and an artist, she finds inspiration and fulfilment in both aspects of her life. \\nIn 2023, Lichtenstein and her family embarked on a momentous move, relocating to Wilderness, where they now live in her grandparents' cherished old house, where the artist initially found refuge from childhood trauma. This transformative relocation has had a profound impact on her artistic practice, shaping her approach to painting in significant ways. The immersive experience of being surrounded by the familiar, held by nature's embrace, has provided a nurturing environment for her creative exploration, evident in her latest works. \\nThrough her pieces, Lichtenstein explores the profound connection between nature, the human psyche, and the creative process, translated into the sensuous language of images. Her process is an intricate dance of shadows and light, employing vibrant hues and directional brushwork to construct luminous compositions. Each stroke and mark is an intentional decision, exploring the delicate balance between tension and harmony. \\nLichtenstein draws inspiration from the richness of nature's colours and references the opulent imagery of the Old Masters. With these images and atmosphere in mind, Lichtenstein applies the paint with a formalist’s approach, creating works that exude sultriness, evocation, and romance, inviting viewers into a world where the sensuous and the psychological intertwine. \\nIn her artistic exploration, Lichtenstein embraces the concept of the painting as a sanctuary – a safe space where she delves into her emotions, memories, and inner landscapes. Her childhood experiences and the profound connection she formed with nature during that time have shaped her understanding of the visceral language of the natural world, which she eloquently translates onto her canvases. The interplay of foreground and background, the excavation of hidden layers, and the sense of wandering and wonder are all threads woven into her art. \\nLichtenstein's paintings embody dualities and ambiguity, capturing the contrast between light and dark, chaos and order, openness and closure. Through her work, she invites viewers to fully engage their senses—to explore the unseen and the visible. With a deep appreciation for the transformative quality of creativity, Lichtenstein's paintings serve as windows into her psyche and soul, providing avenues for herself and the viewer to connect with the inherent power and resonance of natural imagery, fostering contemplation, introspection, and a deeper understanding of the human experience. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014100426973 gid://shopify/Product/9014100459741 gid://shopify/Product/9014100492509 gid://shopify/Product/9014100525277 gid://shopify/Product/9014100558045 gid://shopify/Product/9014100590813 gid://shopify/Product/9014100623581 gid://shopify/Product/9014100689117 gid://shopify/Product/9014100754653 gid://shopify/Product/9014100787421

The collective was founded by six graduates from Rhodes University, a school with a rich printmaking tradition, during a class reunion exhibition in 2016. Inspired to create together again, they began exhibiting as The Printing Girls. In 2017, they expanded to include more female printmakers, forming the collective's current iteration. \\nTPG's main focus remains to provide a platform for South African women printmakers to share ideas, network, and exhibit their work together."}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214890205 Claude Chandler 1461 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640323600605 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013331722461","gid://shopify/Product/9013331755229","gid://shopify/Product/9013331853533"] Explore Claude Chandler (b.?1989, Durban), a Cape Town–based artist who transforms portraiture through text-stamped layering techniques. Diploma from DUT, international solo exhibitions, murals, podcast host, and finalist in major awards including SPI and Sasol. [4487,4488,9044,9046,9045] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"In a world now molded by social and online media, everything has become digitized. In its primal core all internet information and imagery is nothing more than 1’s and 0’s (binary code), this transformation factors to the basis for my body of work. As a child I was fascinated with computers, especially the ability to ‘Hack’. \\nTo me this meant that a world could be manipulated and transformed with creativity... Hackers challenge and change the system to make them work differently, to make them better. A ‘Hacker’ then could actually be applied to any field... I describe myself as a ‘Portrait Hacker’."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013331722461 gid://shopify/Product/9013331755229 gid://shopify/Product/9013331853533

item.title: Claudette Schreuders
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214824669 Claudette Schreuders 273 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640323666141 Explore Claudette Schreuders (b.?1973), a Cape Town?based sculptor known for carved, painted wooden figures that examine African identity in post?apartheid South Africa. Her work is held by MoMA, MET, Smithsonian, and she carved the Nobel Square monuments. [349,348,350] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Claudette Schreuders creates carved and painted wooden figures that reflect the ambiguities of the search for an 'African' identity in the post-apartheid 21st century. The domain of woodcarving is a contested one for a white, Afrikaans woman, and the subtractive process of carving offers a certain lack of control that she enjoys. Schreuders' sculptures demonstrate a convergence of African and European influences from the blolo and colon figures of West Africa to medieval church sculpture, Spanish portraiture and Egyptian woodcarving. Their stocky bodies, solid stance and staring eyes 'own' space in a very particular way, partly indebted to the shape of the block of wood from which they emerge. Narrative and storytelling are fundamental to the reading of her figures, which is why Claudette Schreuders opts to show small bodies of work as sculptural installations, after which the figures are available to be bought individually."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013274509533 gid://shopify/Product/9013274542301 gid://shopify/Product/9013274575069

item.title: Claudia Gurwitz
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214955741 Claudia Gurwitz gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640323895517 [] Discover Claudia Gurwitz, a Cape Town–based painter and yoga instructor whose vibrant, detailed plant paintings explore nature’s sacred geometry and resilience. Known for solo shows like Plant, Rooted, Burst, Interrupted, and Adaptation. Featured in major South African and international collections. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Claudia Gurwitz was born in Cape Town. She is a yoga teacher & contemporary artist. Claudia attended Herzlia High School where she discovered her love of art under the tutelage of Jill Joubert. Following school, Claudia explored various mediums, studying ceramics at Barbara Jackson’s studio, mosaic with Lisa Finberg and printmaking at Ruth Prowse. \\nAfter completing 2 years towards a BAFA at Michaelis, UCT in 1996, Claudia left the University to do her Yoga teacher’s training and completed national certifications in various holistic disciplines. Among several other exotic destinations, Claudia has made 2 trips to India to expose herself to, and explore the roots of the yoga discipline and its founding culture. Since 1997 Claudia has run her own established yoga centres in Oranjezicht, Cape Town, and Riebeek Kasteel, in the Swartland. \\nAfter her 9 year journey into the healing arts, Claudia returned to painting and a three-year mentorship under Julia Teale at Spencer Street Studio. \\nClaudia has embraced working as a professional artist since 2007, adopting Riebeek Kasteel as her hometown. In 2016-2020 she participated alongside the other established local Riebeek artists in the annual collaborative art event, Solo Studios. Claudia’s work features in collections such as Old Mutual, Spier Estate, University of Cape Town, Countess Antonia Labia Hardres-Williams, Hout Bay Manor and Nando’s UK. In 2019 Claudia returned to Cape Town where she now lives and creates."}]}]}
