item.title: Claudie Titty Dimbeng
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215021277 Claudie Titty Dimbeng 2132 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640324321501 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013434843357","gid://shopify/Product/9013434908893","gid://shopify/Product/9013438021853"] Discover Claudie Titty Dimbeng (b.?1968), a Paris?based Ivorian–French painter who innovated Mixed Art Relief—a textured fusion of tapa, raffia, oil, and acrylic. Her work, rooted in Vohou?Vohou, addresses African spirituality, women's empowerment, migration, and racial justice, exhibited globally since 2002. [16034,16121,16035] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The artist Claudie Titty Dimbeng, aka Dimbeng (1968) is a Paris-based, painter of Mixed Art Relief, a vector of transcultural dialogue. \\nDimbeng draws her inspiration from African spirituality, the place and role of women in society, the human impact on the planet, and she also deals with major current events, such as the death of African migrants in the Mediterranean, the murder of George Floyd or the Covid 19 pandemic. \\nBorn in Abidjan from an Ivorian father and a French Ivorian mother, she lived in Germany and Austria before moving to Paris where she studied Interior design at the Ecole Supérieure des Arts Modernes, (School of Modern Art) from 1987 to 1991. \\nSince she decided to dedicate herself to painting in 1999, Dimbeng’s works were exhibited notably at the Quai Branly Museum in 2011 and at UNESCO headquarters where she represented the Ivory Coast in 2012. She exhibited her work for the first time in her home country in 2013 with her “Back to the Future” series at the Arts Pluriels Gallery in Abidjan. She further exhibited at the Sandnes Kino Kino Kultur Hus in Norway in 2015, at the Vilnius City Hall in Lithuania, at the Egg Art Studio Gallery in New Delhi, India in 2016, and FNB Joburg Art fair online in 2020. Her works are part of private collections in Europe, particularly in France, Lithuania and Austria, in Africa, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and South Africa, as well as in Canada and India. Dimbeng is a member of the International Association of Arts, IAA, a UNESCO partner. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013434843357 gid://shopify/Product/9013434908893 gid://shopify/Product/9013438021853

item.title: Clement Mohale
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215054045 Clement Mohale 1334 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640324419805 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013317664989", "gid://shopify/Product/9013331460317", "gid://shopify/Product/9013341192413", "gid://shopify/Product/9013345911005", "gid://shopify/Product/9013346009309", "gid://shopify/Product/9013354266845", "gid://shopify/Product/9013354332381", "gid://shopify/Product/9013366816989", "gid://shopify/Product/9013417083101", "gid://shopify/Product/9013993996509", "gid://shopify/Product/9013994029277", "gid://shopify/Product/9013994062045", "gid://shopify/Product/9013994881245", "gid://shopify/Product/9013994946781", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004252893", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004285661", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004318429", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004351197", "gid://shopify/Product/9014004383965", "gid://shopify/Product/9014124904669"] Discover the bold and vibrant art of Clement Mohale, a contemporary South African artist. His mixed-media works explore themes of identity, inner struggle, and socio-political issues. Buy original art online and experience his powerful visual storytelling. [21406,21405,21767,21766,21763,21764,21765,12196,9965,9964,21375,21376,10908,7400,21377,9515,15087,23250,9025,10909,12249] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Clement Mohale (b. 1994, Bela-Bela, Limpopo) is a contemporary South African artist whose passion for art began in childhood. Mentored by the late Ernest Ditshego at The African Art Center, Clement developed foundational skills in the arts. In 2007, he won the Manager's Choice Award in the Cashbuild Art At HeArt Community Competition, marking the start of his journey as an artist. \\nClement's work is bold, vibrant, and deeply emotive, inspired by the daily lived experiences that shape the human condition. His mixed-media creations delve into themes such as childhood memories, identity, inner struggle, and socio-political and economic issues like poverty, homelessness, and limited access to education. Children often take center stage in his art, symbolizing hope and resilience. \\nHis style is characterized by the use of flat and impasto oil and acrylic paints, exploiting color and strong light to create rhythmic movement. His subject matter is predominantly painted in monochrome, with series of blues capturing fleeting gestures or expressions. Clement’s compositions juxtapose his subjects against brilliant and pure colors, creating a powerful visual impact. \\nClement's work has been featured in numerous exhibitions and special projects, including his solo exhibition 'The creative adult is the one who survived' at NWU Gallery and the group exhibition 'Shattered ceilings' presented by The Pencil Club. He has been a finalist in significant art competitions and projects, including The Lockdown Collection Portfolio and The Green Recovery Portfolio project. His artwork has gained international recognition, with collections in the U.S., Switzerland, Germany, France, England, and beyond. \\nIn 2021, Clement obtained a certificate of Contemporary Art Practice with CAP Institute and completed a printmaking course at Artist Proof Studio in Houghton, Johannesburg. His vision extends beyond the canvas, striving to illuminate how socio-political and economic issues impact individuals, prompting viewers to reflect on their own roles in creating a more equitable world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013317664989 gid://shopify/Product/9013331460317 gid://shopify/Product/9013341192413 gid://shopify/Product/9013345911005 gid://shopify/Product/9013346009309 gid://shopify/Product/9013354266845 gid://shopify/Product/9013354332381 gid://shopify/Product/9013366816989 gid://shopify/Product/9013417083101 gid://shopify/Product/9013993996509 gid://shopify/Product/9013994029277 gid://shopify/Product/9013994062045 gid://shopify/Product/9013994881245 gid://shopify/Product/9013994946781 gid://shopify/Product/9014004252893 gid://shopify/Product/9014004285661 gid://shopify/Product/9014004318429 gid://shopify/Product/9014004351197 gid://shopify/Product/9014004383965 gid://shopify/Product/9014040166621 gid://shopify/Product/9014124904669

item.title: Clint Strydom
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215086813 Clint Strydom gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640324845789 [] Discover Clint Strydom (b.?1973), a South African photographer whose powerful visual narratives capture urban energy, rural serenity, and untold histories. Known for Big City Life, Hidden Shadows & Silent Voices, and collaborations with Aston?Martin, FIFA, and The Melrose Gallery. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Clint Strydom is a talented South African photographer, lens-based artist and photo essayist with a profound gift for capturing humanity. His lens-based artistry unravels the hidden perspectives of the overlooked or forgotten in society, resulting in work that is timeless, measured and still. His self-taught technical flair and experimental signature style has created visual narratives whose timeless profundity permeates political, private and commercial spaces. \\nIn his quest to re-balance historical narratives, Strydom found himself drawn towards one of his defining bodies of work: `Hidden Shadows and Silent Voices of Prison Number 4’. This collection was captured inside the historic and notorious `Number Four’ prison at Constitution Hill. The series was created to communicate the great injustice and inhumanity of conditions in this infamous prison that was the home to the likes of Nelson Mandela, Mahatma Gandhi, Robert Sobukwe and Oliver Tambo, amongst numerous others. \\nHis experimental signature style has also resulted in collaborations with the likes of Aston Martin International, FIFA, the Mexican Football Hall of Fame and others. As appreciation for the success accorded him in his career, Strydom elected to invest in other artists of African descent. In 2016, the photographer opened The Melrose Gallery, in Melrose Arch, Johannesburg creating one of the few artist owned galleries in South Africa. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Clive Sithole
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215414493 Clive Sithole gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640326156509 [] Discover Clive Sithole, award-winning South African ceramic artist whose pit-fired vessels and hand-built ceramics reflect Zulu heritage, storytelling, and spirituality. Explore his traditional and contemporary African pottery. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Clive Sithole (b. 1971, Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa) Clive Sithole’s vision as an artist explores landscapes and vessels of containment, expanding our notions of inclusion, belonging and exile. \\nThe work is rooted in a deep physicality that emerges from nature; supportive and powerful. Born in Soweto in 1971, Sithole has honed his career though a life-long practice of extending traditional notions of form and function through his dedication to ceramics, making and clay. In 1978, Sithole moved to Lesotho for a year as an 8-year-old child, where he learned to make animals from river clay, and spent much time taking care of the cattle that would later become a dominant theme and symbolic imagery in his art. Sithole moved to Durban in his twenties and began his career as a practicing ceramic artist at the BAT Centre in 1997. \\nFascinated by the work of Nesta Nala, Molelekoa Simon Masilo and Bonnie Ntshalintshali, Sithole soon developed his own distinct style that catapulted him into the realm of award-winning and internationally recognised artist and teacher. The domination of land that permeates Sithole’s current work stems from the forced exile imposed on South Africa’s people by the colonial and apartheid system. For Sithole, land is about what people have access to, and what they are denied. A strong feminine energy inhabits the work, a tribute to his sisters, his mother, and the predominantly female support and nurturing he has experienced during his career development. \\nSithole sees the land as distinctly feminine, and the Goddess imagery that runs through the exhibition works is emphasised by the symbolic veneration of the cow as a symbol of nourishment, and the ancestors that continue to watch over us. Sithole received a post-graduate diploma in fine art cum laude through the University of KwaZulu-Natal, Pietermaritzburg, in 2006. \\nHe has exhibited in the United States, Tokyo, London, Mexico and China, and his work appears in collections the likes of the Smithsonian, Windsor Castle and the Royal Collection Trust. Sithole draws his inspiration from people who make, and the routines and repetitive movement of people’s hands in the process of creation, from hair plaiting to basket weaving. \\nSithole’s vision looks away from machines, screens and contemporary technology to a more fundamental and emotionally-rooted question. From a landscape of texture and shadow, layers are peeled away by Sithole’s work. Kumnyama Kubomvu: This Land is Ours calls us to attention and asks what it is that our hands have made of the land we inhabit. \\nSithole is currently based at his studio at the Phansi Museum in Durban, where he works and mentors younger creatives. \\nWritten by Kirsten Miller"}]}]}

item.title: Clive van den Berg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215906013 Clive van den Berg gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640328155357 [] Explore Clive van den Berg (b.?1956, Zambia), a Johannesburg-based artist whose multidisciplinary work—painting, sculpture, print—interweaves landscape, memory, queer identity, and public heritage. Notable shows include Fugitive Marks, Landscape Echoes, and a Wits retrospective Porous. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Clive van den Berg (b. 1956, Zambia) is an artist, curator and designer, who works on his own and in collaboration with colleagues in a collective called trace, whose primary activities are the development of public projects. He has had several solo exhibitions in South Africa, and his work is regularly exhibited abroad. His public projects have included the artworks for landmark Northern Cape Legislature and, since he has joined the trace team, museum projects for the Nelson Mandela Foundation, Constitution Hill, Freedom Park, the Workers Museum, The Holocaust and Genocide Centre and many other projects. \\nVan den Berg has much experience working on large-scale institutional projects with teams representing diverse constituencies: urban planners and policy makers, architects, landscape designers, museum curators, historians, community liaison officials and representatives of local and national governments. In the Northern Cape, for example, where he worked with the Luis Ferreira da Silva architects, he pioneered a new strategy for integrating forms of the local landscape and indigenous aesthetics into the overall building design, while also training local artisans as part of a skills transference project aimed at long-term sustainability. The result is a world-renowned and uniquely South African state edifice: a monument to the people of the Northern Cape."}]}]}

item.title: Cloudia Rivett-Carnac
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641216233693 Cloudia Rivett-Carnac gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640328974557 [] Explore Cloudia Rivett?Carnac, a Johannesburg-based master printmaker and founder of Chocolate Ink Studio. Pioneering non-toxic screen-printing, she collaborates with top artists like Kentridge, Sibande, and Makamo and teaches workshops across lino?cut, intaglio, and drypoint. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here’s the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang. In 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University which has always had a strong history of printmaking. During a class reunion exhibition in 2016 they inspired each other to create in print again and began to exhibit as The Printing Girls. The following year they decided to invite new female printmakers to join up, and TPG in its current incarnation began to materialise. But the main focus has never changed - to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network and exhibit together. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Cobus Haupt
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641216889053 Cobus Haupt 1188 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640329302237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013309440221", "gid://shopify/Product/9013309571293"] Discover Cobus Haupt (b.?1976), a Pretoria-based bronze sculptor who celebrates the art of casting through tactile, figurative works. Known for intentional imperfections that highlight process and human fragility, award-winning and featured in public commissions and heritage collections. [6046,6048,6044,6042] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cobus Haupt is an established bronze sculptor who draws on history, popular culture and tradition to produce artworks that are visually interesting, tactile and playful. The process and method of bronze casting informs Haupt’s work both formally and conceptually. \\nHaupt has a tendency to include cracks, flaws and unresolved imperfections which bear witness to the casting process and catalogues the tactile history of the bronze technique itself. At the same time, these fissures also comment on Haupt’s rendering of the human figure. Human beings are understood as unique, fragile and remarkable due to their so-called imperfections, flaws and scars. These human ‘defects’ and ‘deformities’ bear, as in the case of the bronze casting process, witness to their engagement with life. Due to the importance of the process, Haupt undertakes all the aspects of the sculpting process himself from the mould making to the casting. \\nHaupt’s artistic process commences with live models from which he creates figurative sculptures that portray the naturalistic qualities of the model while harnessing the expressive qualities of the medium. Once the sculptures are cast in wax, various sections or parts are removed and combined with other figures and/or objects. These assemblages juxtapose various concepts to allow for new meaning and creation. Apart from the use of the human figure, Haupt also includes found objects such as traditional African figurative sculptures, broken pieces of ceramic cutlery or childhood remnants like Lego or Mecano. Haupt’s work also relies on an autobiographical element as he draws inspiration from that which surrounds him such as his family and objects from his past."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013309440221 gid://shopify/Product/9013309472989 gid://shopify/Product/9013309538525 gid://shopify/Product/9013309571293

item.title: Cobus van Bosch
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641217118429 Cobus van Bosch gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640329826525 [] Cobus van Bosch, South African painter, Prince Albert artist, oil portraiture, Boer War portraits, Forgotten Freedom Fighters, Quarantine series, emotional realist painting, Klein Karoo Kanna Prize, South African history art, pandemic paintings {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cobus van Bosch, born in Cape Town in 1962, is a painter of the human condition in southern Africa, past and present. Where he previously surveyed southern Africa's documented history, he now investigates more universal aspects of the human condition (such as paternalism and male power). \\nHe mainly paints in oil on canvas in a figurative style, with an emphasis on texture and brushwork in order to achieve emotionally charged content. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Coex'ae Qgam (Dada)
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641217183965 Coex'ae Qgam (Dada) gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331071709 [] Discover Coex’ae Qgam, known as Dada (1934–2008), a self-taught San artist from Botswana whose bold lithographs and drawings narrate San folklore, identity, and cultural resilience. Key works include Qauqaua and the 1999 Trickster Suite, exhibited globally and featured in major collections. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"oex'ae Qgam (Dada) 1934 - 2008 was an artist from Ghanzi, Botswana. She attended just three months of primary school, later working as a child minder and domestic help. Qgam had an extensive knowledge of her people's traditions, story telling and healing practices. Her first exposure to textile art was in Namibia, when an employer taught her needlework and embroidery. Fluent in five African languages Qgam joined The Kuru Art Project in 1990 as a translator. Having had difficulty in explaining techniques verbally, she started illustrating them herself and so created her first paintings. \\n \\nQgam's compositions are informal and she worked in a direct, clear way. Her use of colour was bright and bold which is in contrast to the monochrome surroundings of the Kalahari where she lived. \\n \\nShe contributed images to the artists' book Qauqaua and was also the principal author of the book."}]}]}

item.title: Colbert Mashile
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641217806557 Colbert Mashile 511 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331104477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015033565"] Discover the evocative art of Colbert Mashile, a South African artist born in 1972 in Bushbuckridge. His work explores cultural norms, power, and identity, blending personal experiences with universal themes. [22370] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Colbert Mashile (b. 1972, Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga) draws deeply from his cultural heritage and personal experiences. Influenced by powerful customs and rituals such as circumcision, Mashile turned to art for refuge and healing. His work often delves into complex narratives surrounding cultural norms, home, power, language, the natural landscape, and human-animal connections \\n \\nRaised in a family of teacher, Mashile was expected to follow a similar path. However, his curiosity about art during his studies in Tshwane led him to the Johannesburg Art Foundation and ultimately to a Fine Arts degree from the University of the Witwatersrand. His unique ability to tap into universal psychological archetypes, intertwined with his African identity, has brought him national and international recognition. \\nMashile's work is characterized by mystical figures, phallic images, pods, everyday objects, and organic shapes, reflecting his connection to the earth. His use of colours and form conveys a profound understanding of the land and its people. Through his symbols and icons, Mashile communicates the truths of South African society with remarkable clarity and insight."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014015033565

item.title: Colijn Strydom
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641218527453 Colijn Strydom 895 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331170013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013297742045","gid://shopify/Product/9013297873117","gid://shopify/Product/9013300855005","gid://shopify/Product/9013300887773","gid://shopify/Product/9013300920541","gid://shopify/Product/9013367898333","gid://shopify/Product/9013375566045","gid://shopify/Product/9013470527709","gid://shopify/Product/9013470691549"] Discover Colijn Strydom (b.?1979), Cape Town–based visual artist working across drawing, painting, performance, and photography. His work explores Afrikaner masculinity, folklore, irony, nature and Modernist themes with recurring series like Bacchae of Buitenkant and Oedipus. Exhibited widely throughout South Africa and internationally. [17904,12894,12289,4813,4814,4815,4363,4365] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Colijn Strydom is a visual artist living and working in Cape Town. He studied Fine Art at the University of Pretoria and completed his MA (Visual Arts) at Stellenbosch University in 2008. He works primarily in the fields of drawing and painting. \\n He has exhibited throughout South Africa, with his latest solo exhibition being at 99 Loop Gallery in Cape Town. He has taught at Stellenbosch University, the Ruth Prowse School of Art and has been a guest lecturer at the Michaelis School of Art. \\n Strydom’s subject matter is diverse and draws from literature, history and popular culture. Despite this eclecticism, there is throughout his work an interrogation and dialogue with his own masculine Afrikaner identity. Strydom likes to use humour and irony. The realm where spirituality and politics intersect interests him, as well as drawing and painting as subjects in themselves."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013297742045 gid://shopify/Product/9013297873117 gid://shopify/Product/9013300855005 gid://shopify/Product/9013300887773 gid://shopify/Product/9013300920541 gid://shopify/Product/9013367898333 gid://shopify/Product/9013375566045 gid://shopify/Product/9013470527709 gid://shopify/Product/9013470691549

item.title: Collaborative Poetics
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641220067549 Collaborative Poetics gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331235549 [] Collaborative Poetics is a research methodology that merges spoken-word poetry, social science, and community participation to co-create arts-based narratives. Based at the University of Brighton and McGill, CP explores lived experiences around discrimination and resilience through poetic autoethnography and collective storytelling. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Between January 10-12, 2020, 13 womxn came together at lalela. place of listening. These womxn answered an open invitation to join A Retreat in Collaborative Poetics* facilitated by Refilwe Nkomo, Kathy Engel and Maia Marie. The invitation was to spend time with the question: When we listen to the land what do we hear? And to work with this question collaboratively – in a lyrical process of experiencing the making and living of poetry as something shared, interconnected and generative.The featured warrior womxn who make up this offering in the form of Collaborative Poetics - Conversations with Lalela: \\nAnna Sango, Annika Slabbert, Athambile Masola , Faith Itumeleng Thobejane, Itumeleng Moeketsi, Kathy Engel, Kundai Moyo, Lali Tshikalange, Lenka Vrablikova, Maia Marie, Molemo Moiloa Gapare, Natalia Flores Garrido, Refilwe Nkomo \\nThis conversation is part of an ongoing project “Does the land tell the story if we listen?”, with lalela. a place of listening and manifested in collaboration with many beings. It is an invitation into listening to and with the land as a starting point for how we dream and act in the world, for ourselves and each other."}]}]}

item.title: Colleen Winter
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641220100317 Colleen Winter gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331268317 [] Explore Colleen Winter (b. 1956, Johannesburg), a South African artist and MTech graduate whose work in mixed-media drawing and sculpture uses found materials and textiles to probe themes of transience, alchemy, materiality, and life cycles. Exhibitions at Gallery 2 in Johannesburg. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Colleen Winter describes herself simply as a \"maker\" — someone whose artistic practice is deeply process-driven and intuitive. Working in drawing (mixed media) and sculpture, she employs found materials, textiles, and paper to explore themes of transience, alchemy, materiality, self-reflection, and the cycles of life. Her art is an ongoing journey of grappling with inner and outer worlds—transforming them through a tactile, embodied creative process. \\nShe has exhibited solo shows at Gallery 2, Johannesburg, including Matterings/Mutterings (2023) and Umpteen Impossible Things Before Breakfast (2024)."}]}]}

item.title: Collen Maswanganyi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641220329693 Collen Maswanganyi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331333853 [] Discover Collen Maswanganyi (b.?1977, Limpopo), a third-generation South African sculptor who hand-carves painted corkwood and leadwood figures blending tradition and modernity. Award-winning works featured at Absa L’Atelier, Turbine Art Fair, NIROX Carving X workshop, and Kalashnikovv Gallery’s Revival exhibition. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Collen was born in 17 January 1977 in a rural village called Noblehoek near Giyani Limpopo Province, South Africa. He comes from an artistic family. His father is a well-known sculptor. \\nHis father, Johannes Maswanganyi, has participated in a number of exhibitions locally and internationally. He has two wives, his mother Annah makes beadworks, his other wife, Esther Maswanganyi, makes beads, clay-pots and embroidery and has exhibited in a number of exhibitions. His younger sister's and brothers are learning the skills mentioned above. His father was taught by his father, Piet Maswanganyi. \\nHe started school at Haaka primary school in 1983. He passed his matric at two different schools namely Ndengeza high school in 1995 and N'wamavimbi high school in 1996. He did a Fine Arts Diploma at the Technicon Witwatersrand from 1996 to 1999. \\nAfter obtaining his diploma he worked as an full-time artist. \\nJust like his father, he works with wood. He paints most of his sculptures. He sometimes make life size sculptures. \"My art is about the old and the new. I look at life generally where I make sculptures dressed in African and modern ways. I look at technological development. My mostly popular works involve people or couples speaking on phones or people dressed modestly.\" \\nHis works are collected by private people, corporates, museums and galleries. His aim is to exhibit internationally just like his father and other sculptors from his region like Jackson Hlungwani, Noria Mabase and others."}]}]}

item.title: Collin Cole
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641220624605 Collin Cole gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640331694301 [] Explore Collin Cole (b.?1960, Johannesburg), a printmaker and multidisciplinary artist whose work reinterprets historical imagery through etching, monoprint, and collage. Founder of Blue Door Print Studio, educator with over 140 exhibitions and renowned collaborations with Dina Kroon. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Collin Cole, master printmaker with over 30 years experience. He graduated from Natal Technikon with a National Diploma in Fine Art and later obtained a Masters Degree in Fine Art/Printmaking from Rhodes University. \\nCollin was a university lecturer for 16 years and has taught various printmaking techniques including Serigraphy, Intaglio, Relief printing and Off-set Lithography at Rhodes University and The University of North West. \\nIn January 2003, Collin established a private teaching facility, the Blue Door Print Studio at St Ninian’s Church, Parktown North, to teach and give students the opportunity to learn professional printmaking. In May 2017 he moved and opened his new studio in Melville/Richmond, Johannesburg in an old beautiful church built in 1902."}]}]}

item.title: Conrad Bo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641221148893 Conrad Bo 530 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640332284125 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013286731997"] Explore Conrad Bo (b.?1972), a Johannesburg-based South African artist who founded the Superstroke art movement. His textured, expressive paintings and conceptual styles—Superblur and Hybridpointillism—address history, identity, and social issues through bold strokes and symbolic imagery. [3465,3466,3467,3468] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Conrad Bo paints in the style of “Superstroke” and attempts to communicate his views on social issues, historical events and avant garde art theory. \\nInnovation in contemporary art is Conrad Bo’s main objective and he strives to achieve this by using manifesto driven art. He executes his Superstroke paintings by using expressive, even violent brushstrokes, symbols, writing and dripping, to comment on issues of life, history, decoration, morality, and identity. \\nPlus signs (+) feature in nearly all of his paintings and is a sign of the Superstroke, an indication of an increase, by the addition of. The plus sign is a positive sign, a sign of hope, the sum is more than its parts, a ranking on the higher end of a designated scale, a favourable condition or factor and in some instances a sign of peace, and a sign of help. The use of the + (plus) is also used to differentiate Superstroke paintings from other art movements such as Expressionism, Abstract Expressionism and Neo-Expressionism. The 2008 manifesto of the Superstroke Art Movement is the cornerstone of most of the art produced by Conrad Bo and other members of the Superstroke Art Movement. \\nMost of Conrad Bo’s childhood was spent growing up in Witbank also known as eMalahleni, an African town about 150km from Johannesburg. He started drawing and painting from an early age. He experimented with a style called Generalism from 2003 until 2008, when he felt that it (Generalism) came to the end of its innovative cycle. \\nThe art concept and style called Superstroke was founded by Bo in 2008 and became an internationally known Art Movement with members in different countries. The Superstroke art produced by Conrad Bo features expressive, even violent brush, pencil and pen strokes, in accordance with the Superstroke Art Movement manifesto. There is also a heavy emphasis on texture in Superstroke as these paintings are sometimes described as the opposite of Superflat (A Japanese art movement conceived by Takashi Murakami). Another important inspiration in the art of Conrad Bo are 2 books namely: In Pursuit of the Unknown, 17 Equations that Changed the World, by Ian Steward and 5 Equations that changed the world: The Power and Poetry of Mathematics by Michael Guillen. Conrad Bo uses the mathematical equations, and also the concept of Superblur to create some of the most complex and difficult to understand paintings in the world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013286633693 gid://shopify/Product/9013286666461 gid://shopify/Product/9013286699229 gid://shopify/Product/9013286731997

item.title: Conrad Botes
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223114973 Conrad Botes 297 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640333725917 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013293809885", "gid://shopify/Product/9013293842653", "gid://shopify/Product/9013365932253", "gid://shopify/Product/9013365997789", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008709341", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008774877", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008840413", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008873181", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008938717", "gid://shopify/Product/9014009037021", "gid://shopify/Product/9014009069789", "gid://shopify/Product/9014011068637", "gid://shopify/Product/9014011101405", "gid://shopify/Product/9014011134173", "gid://shopify/Product/9014054879453"] Discover the provocative art of Conrad Botes, a South African visual artist and co-founder of Bitterkomix. His work spans monoprints, silkscreens, lithographs, and paintings, reflecting on contemporary society through Post-Pop aesthetics. Buy original art online and experience his powerful visual commentary. [22147,4288,4286,12142,12141,4292,4289,22057,4287,4293,4291,22145,23689,22146,22056,22064,22059,22060,22062,22063] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Conrad Botes (b. 1969, Western Cape, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary visual artist and a pivotal figure in the South African Post-Pop movement. Growing up in a Department of Water Affairs prefab house on the edge of the Theewaterskloof Dam, his unique upbringing has deeply influenced his artistic vision. His father, a local schoolteacher, and the colorful characters of his childhood world have shaped his ability to critically examine and satirize Afrikaanerdom and South African culture. \\nTogether with Anton Kannemeyer, Botes co-founded Bitterkomix, a provocative publication that challenges societal norms through its rude, cutting humour. Bitterkomix has become a national institution and was notably the first publication banned in post-apartheid South Africa. \\nBotes' artistic practice extends beyond comics to include monoprints, silkscreens, lithographs, and other works on paper. His art often features atavistic males and females, including the 'tortured soul' and the femme fatale, mocking conventional notions of individualism and humanism. He uses Post-Pop's preference for 'sugary infantilism' to reflect on contemporary society where religion is irreverent, violence is desirable, and sadism is institutionalized. His work merges pastoral elements with contemporary realities: flowers as wounds, birds as harbingers of doom, and detached hands symbolizing creativity. \\nBotes' paintings are more personal, inviting viewers to formulate their own interpretations and emotional responses. His work has been described as giving a bittersweet edge to Post-Pop sentimentality, creating a powerful visual commentary on modern existential crises."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013293809885 gid://shopify/Product/9013293842653 gid://shopify/Product/9013293908189 gid://shopify/Product/9013294006493 gid://shopify/Product/9013294039261 gid://shopify/Product/9013294072029 gid://shopify/Product/9013294137565 gid://shopify/Product/9013294170333 gid://shopify/Product/9013365932253 gid://shopify/Product/9013365997789 gid://shopify/Product/9014008709341 gid://shopify/Product/9014008774877 gid://shopify/Product/9014008840413 gid://shopify/Product/9014008873181 gid://shopify/Product/9014008938717 gid://shopify/Product/9014009037021 gid://shopify/Product/9014009069789 gid://shopify/Product/9014011068637 gid://shopify/Product/9014011101405 gid://shopify/Product/9014011134173 gid://shopify/Product/9014054879453

item.title: Coral Bijoux
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223311581 Coral Bijoux gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640333824221 [] Explore Coral Bijoux—a multi?disciplinary South African artist and educator whose installations, sculptural works, photo?montages, and drawings document life in a transitioning society. With a background in gender studies and education, her auto?ethnographic practice uses layered materials—wood, clay, plastic, animation—to evoke memory, metaphor, and material alchemy. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Coral Bijoux, a South African artist, makes visible the work that she has engaged with for many years: observing, challenging and documenting life in a transitioning world; amidst political and social upheavals, quiet moments and life experiences. \\nAn auto-ethnographic focus draws near her ideas and concepts through a visual language which is fecund with metaphor and symbol, textured surfaces echoing layered meanings. Her artwork, curatorial practice and projects centre on these experiences and observations using predominantly installation, sculptural forms, drawings, photo-montages and paintings. \\nAs an artist, she is mostly self-taught. She has a teacher’s qualification, 33 years experience in education and art related fields; an Honours degree in Gender Studies (summa cum laude) and is working on an interdisciplinary Masters in Art Degree at the Drama and Theatre Department, UKZN. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Craig Cameron-Mackintosh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223606493 Craig Cameron-Mackintosh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640333889757 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014084894941","gid://shopify/Product/9014084927709","gid://shopify/Product/9014084960477"] Discover Craig Cameron?Mackintosh (b.?1987), a Cape Town–based painter whose cinematic oil portraits in silhouette and evolving abstract landscapes blend filmmaking techniques with emotive ambiguity. Winner of the Sanlam Portrait Award, exhibited in Cape Town, Chicago, Berlin, and Russia. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Craig Cameron-Mackintosh is a painter and filmmaker best known for his oil portraits of models and friends in silhouette. Growing up in White River, Mpumalanga, an environment that inspired many great South African artists, including Keith Alexander and Esias Bosch, Cameron-Mackintosh displayed prodigious talent for drawing from an early age, despite not having studied fine art. His move to Cape Town in 2007 to study filmmaking at AFDA deeply influenced his artistic career, not only lending a sense of cinema and story to his subject matter but also informing his technique. \\nTaking visual cues and references from photography, Cameron-Mackintosh explores the cinematic effects of light and shade, reworking the traditional silhouette motif and pushing the two extremes to trick the eye, creating different ways of seeing the same things. In a reversal of the typical order of artistic practice, his large, highly rendered silhouette paintings inform his smaller, looser works. \\n“What light reveals on one plane, it equally masks and distorts on the opposite. When the subject is backlit, the effect is almost like a photo negative – details are removed, rendering the age, facial features, and even skin colour of the subjects ambiguous. With a quick setting adjustment, the subject is overexposed and blown out with a soft focus. I enjoy this duality of the same scene. These near life-size figures stare out into an unknown landscape, with the graduated blue canvases as their windows.\"- Craig Cameron-Mackintosh. \\nEvolving his artistic practice, Cameron-Mackintosh's newer works move beyond direct figuration, embracing a more intuitive and fluid approach. His continued embrace of a photographic aesthetic manifests in a new format, exploring the essence of presence when detached from the figure through altered perspectives, inviting viewers to engage with what is unseen beyond the frame. In this evolution, Cameron-Mackintosh continues to utilise his background in filmmaking, playing with light and shade to create a duality that challenges perceptions, unlocking novel ways of experiencing familiar scenes by intentionally obscuring details to leave room for ambiguity. \\nSince becoming a full-time artist in 2015, Cameron-Mackintosh has showcased both locally and internationally, including esteemed art fairs such as the Investec Cape Town Art Fair and EXPO Chicago. In 2019, his work earned him first place at the Sanlam Portrait Award. Cameron-Mackintosh continues to be based in Cape Town, exhibiting his work in solo and group exhibitions."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014084894941 gid://shopify/Product/9014084927709 gid://shopify/Product/9014084960477

item.title: Cristiano Mangovo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225277661 Cristiano Mangovo 2405 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640333955293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013852045533","gid://shopify/Product/9013852078301"] Discover the vibrant works of Cristiano Mangovo, an Angolan artist blending surrealism and expressionism. Based between Lisbon and Cabinda, his art explores themes of identity, ecology, human rights, and social activism through painting, sculpture, and performance. [19044,19045] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cristiano Mangovo grew up as a refugee in the Democratic Republic of Congo and spent most of his professional career in Angola's turbulent society. As a result, the Angolan phrase \"Winkeba e Nkeba bu Nkaka\" (\"Protect yourselves and protect others too\") has naturally become the central theme of his artwork. With a strong activist slant, his work often appeals to the need to protect weaker people from the stronger, calling for more balanced societies with improved human conditions for all. \\nMangovo developed various styles and symbolisms over the years, but always with a distinct surrealist twist. His work has also been dominated by an expressionistic style, characterised by the deformed characters without a complete real-life form that dominates in his paintings and collages. \\nMangovo holds a Bachelor's Degree in Fine Art from the Ecole des Beaux-Arts in Kinshasa (DRC), having additional urban scenography and performance training. He received early recognition for his work, earning his first solo show in 2013 by the Foundation of Art and Culture in Luanda, which toured Art BAI. In 2014, he was awarded the Mirella Antognoli Prize by the Italian Embassy and Alliance Française, as well as the prestigious Angolan ENSA Art Prize in 2018. Since then, he has exhibited in solo and group exhibitions worldwide. In 2017, his work was recognized in his home country with a solo retrospective exhibition and installation “Riches of Africa”."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013852045533 gid://shopify/Product/9013852078301

item.title: Dada Khanyisa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641227440349 Dada Khanyisa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640335757533 [] Discover artworks by Dada Khanyisa, a leading contemporary South African artist known for layered storytelling and bold visual language. Shop original art and limited editions online at Latitudes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dada Khanyisa was born in Umzimkhulu in 1991 and lives in Cape Town. They completed a Bachelor of Fine Art degree at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, in 2016, after studying Traditional and Digital Animation at the National Electronic Media Institute of South Africa. \\nMost recently, the artist’s first institutional exhibition, Cape Town, took place at the Johannesburg Art Gallery in 2024. Previous solo shows include Good Feelings, Stevenson, Johannesburg (2020) and Bambi’phone, Stevenson, Cape Town (2018). They have participated in group shows including Growing Out? Growing Up? Contemporary Art Collecting in the Baltics at the at Zuzeum Art Centre, Riga, Latvia (2022); SKIN+MASKS, Kavi Gupta, Chicago, USA (2022); 021 - 2021, Stevenson, Amsterdam, the Netherlands (2021); My whole body changed into something else, Stevenson, Cape Town (2021); HI-STORYTELLING at Sfeir-Semler, Hamburg (2021); Mixed Company at Norval Foundation, Cape Town (2021); Heroes: Principles of African Greatness at the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington, DC (2019); 9 More Weeks and Both, and at Stevenson, Johannesburg (2018); among others at galleries across the country. \n\nIn 2017 Khanyisa produced Afropolitan Tea Party, a mural at Constitution Hill, Johannesburg, commissioned to give the historic site contemporary appeal. \\nKhanyisa was the recipient of the 2022 FNB Art Prize, as well as the Simon Gerson Prize at UCT in 2016. As a merit winner at the SA Taxi Art Awards in 2015, their work featured on 10 taxis traversing the main roads of South Africa. They completed a residency at the Cité internationale des arts in Paris in 2022 and participated in a Fountainhead Residency in Miami in 2018."}]}]}

item.title: Daëna Ladéesse
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641249493213 Daëna Ladéesse gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640373440733 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013926723805"] Explore the work of Daëna Ladéesse, a Franco?Vietnamese Afro?Caribbean artist whose painting and performance engage trans?generational migration, spirituality, and healing. Exhibited at Rele?Gallery (London), Efi??Gallery (Dubai), and Frieze No.?9 Cork Street. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Daëna Ladéesse is a multidisciplinary artist born in Paris to a Franco- Vietnamese father and an Afro-Caribbean and Indian mother and grew up between Paris and Saint-Claude, Guadeloupe. \\nShe channels the divine feminine force and transcribes it in the form of painting and performance. Inter- generational handover is a key concept in her work. “ I believe that we are made of mostly non-us elements, such as water, earth, fire and air. But we also are made of ethereal matter, our descendants and ancestors. My work intend to convey the migrations, exoduses, movements of all the people that came before me as well as after. For me we are connectors between time and place. My work is an ode to trans-generational growth.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013926723805

Discover and collect art online with Latitudes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dale Lawrence lives in Cape Town and works as a solo artist and as part of the creative studio and artist collective Hoick, which he co-founded. \\nHis practice marries painstaking application and wry humour through a range of media including painting, monotype, linocut, sculpture, installation and performance, frequently blurring lines between them."}]}]}

item.title: Dale Washkansky
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641227800797 Dale Washkansky gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640336642269 [] Discover the compelling works of Dale Washkansky, a Cape Town-based artist whose photography, sculpture, and mixed media art delve into themes of Jewish identity, post-memory, and the visualization of conflict zones like Gaza. His exhibitions, including Watching the Sky Fall and Mime, challenge perceptions of history and representation. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dale Washkansky, born 1980 in Cape Town, South Africa, is currently a PhD candidate at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town (UCT) where he also completed his MFA (2010) and BA (FA) (2006). \\nHis solo shows include: Knowing and Un-Knowing: The Affective Relations of Images (2023) at the Michaelis Gallery, Ra Ra Ra (2016) at Youngblood Gallery, Mime (2013) at Commune 1 Gallery and A Space Between (2011) which was exhibited at the AVA Gallery and then re-shown at the Cape Town Holocaust and Genocide Centre. Washkansky has participated in several group exhibitions, most recently Vital Signs (2024) at the Michaelis Gallery, Offcuts (2024) at the AVA Gallery, Interlude (2012) at 196 Victoria Rd, Nano 1.3 (2019) and Nano 1.2 (2018) at the Barnard Gallery. Washkansky has collaborated on several curatorial projects including: Death Speaks (2015) at 6 Spin St. with Suzanne Duncan and Alice Toich, Swallow My Pride (2010) at Blank Projects with Margaret Stone, Lizza Littlewort and William Martin. \\nHe was also co-curator with Dr Siona O’Connell for an exhibition at !Kwa ttu San Cultural Centre (2008). In 2010 Washkansky was employed as the co-curator, with Dr. O’Connell, at the Centre for African Studies (CAS) at UCT. Several shows were put on during this time the most prominent Shared Legacies: the Alfred Duggan Cronin and Edward S. Curtis Photographs, which was then exhibited at Kimberly and Grahamstown. In 2012 Washkansky was employed at the Centre for Curating the Archive (CCA) at UCT where he co-curated the exhibition Spring Queen: The Staging of the Glittering Proletariat with Project Director Dr. O’Connell. The exhibition was shown at the Iziko Bertram House Annex Gallery and the District 6 Homecoming Centre."}]}]}

item.title: Dale Yudelman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641227833565 Dale Yudelman 2962 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640336740573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9133231341789"] Explore the photographic journey of Dale Yudelman, from daily life under democracy to conceptual narratives like Reality Bytes and Joburg Man. Winner of the inaugural Ernest Cole Award, his images blend journalistic clarity and poetic storytelling—available on Latitudes Online. [25506] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dale Yudelman (b. 1958) grew up in Johannesburg and began photographing at a young age under the tutelage of his father. His career in photography has led him through two eras of South African history as well as across several continents. He was barely out of his teens in 1979 when he started working as a staff photographer for The Star Newspaper. In 1986 he moved to London and then Los Angeles, working freelance for various newspapers and magazines. Returning to a newly democratic South Africa in 1996, he began collaborating with artist Arlene Amaler-Raviv. Together they produced three major exhibitions and a number of commissions – their final show, ‘Livestock’ was exhibited at the 8th Havana Biennale in Cuba. \\nYudelman then ventured into uncharted territory drawing on his photojournalism background and a growing interest in digital technology. The resulting series, titled ‘Reality Bytes’, aimed to reclaim and freeze the emotional content of daily experience rather than merely regurgitating actual events. A number of projects followed, most notably a series titled ‘I am…’, a portrayal of the ongoing plight of refugees in South Africa. For his series titled 'Life under Democracy' he won the inaugural Ernest Cole Award in 2012 - the country’s most prestigious prize for social documentary photography. \\nYudelman’s work is a consequence of a studied eye, brokered over more than forty years of incessant image making. Enthralled with the many aspects, nuances and dimensions of reality – his images are a manifestation of how modern photography is able to escape the bounds of the ‘record’ - creating an authentic and evocative account of recent times. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9133231341789

[17569,6257,17570,17571,383,9982,9983] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dan Halter’s artistic practice is informed entirely by his position as a Zimbabwean living in South Africa. His work confronts his sense of a dislocated national identity, human migration and the dark humour of present realities in Southern Africa. Halter employs everyday materials familiar in Zimbabwe and South Africa, adopting local popular visual strategies as a way to engage with the politics of the history of oppression in Southern Africa that continues today. Halter’s work often exploits the notions of craft and curio within a conceptual fine art context. \\nDan Halter was born in Zimbabwe in 1977. In addition to five solo exhibitions, Halter has participated in numerous group shows including US at the South African National Gallery, curated by Simon Njami, Zeitgenössiche Fotokunst aus Südafrika at the Neuer Berliner Kunstverein (NBK), 2009 Havana Biennale and Earth Matters at the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art in Washington DC. He has completed four international residencies, in Zürich, Rio de Janeiro, Scotland and Turin. Recent exhibitions include the 7th Triennial of Contemporary Textile Arts of Tournai, Belgium and Dan Halter / Mappa Del Mondo at the Nassauischer Kunstverein in Wiesbaden Germany. \\nHalter’s also work appears in a number of collections including, The South African National Gallery, UNISA (University of South Africa), University of Cape Town, Scheryn Collection, Artphilein Collection, Pigozzi Collection, SAFFCA Collection, Round About Collection, and the prestigious Rennie Collection. \\nDan Halter lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013275525341 gid://shopify/Product/9013310652637 gid://shopify/Product/9013346304221 gid://shopify/Product/9013346336989 gid://shopify/Product/9013466398941 gid://shopify/Product/9013466431709 gid://shopify/Product/9013466497245

[9047] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Daniel Levi (b. 1973 – Johannesburg, SA) graduated with honours in painting from Michaelis School of Fine Art at UCT in Cape Town (1996). He was raised in Johannesburg in a liberal home by parents who exposed him to politics, psychology, philosophy and the arts from an early age. He currently lives and works in Cape Town. \\nLevi has a background in creative design and his experience of the visual arts, multi-media and post-production supported his transition into directing. Daniel was featured in the Saatchi and Saatchi’s young directors showcase and won best new director at Kinsale. Daniel has directed campaigns for clients such as VW, HSBC, X-Box, Mercedes, Nike and Playstation. Daniel’s music videos for Massive Attack, LFO, The Concretes and Plan B often come up on many all-time best lists. In May 2004 LFO Freak won the prestigious Music Video Production Association Award (MVPA) for Directorial Debut. After taking a couple of years off to focus on his other artistic endeavours; painting, photography and design, he is now back in the director’s chair and his branded content film Henry made in collaboration with Ogilvy & Mather and IBM received critical acclaim and debuted at the Vancouver Film Festival in the short film category even though it was made for a brand. \\n \\nSelected Solo & Duo Exhibitions \\n \\n2019 Please Accept My Resignation – Kalashnikovv Gallery, Johannesburg, RSA \\n2011 Nature Ends – WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town, RSA \\n2006 C.A.Wertheim & Daniel Levi – Galerie Lutz, Delft, NLD \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions & Projects \\n \\n2020 Asymmetrical Identities – 131 A Gallery, Cape Town, RSA \\n2019 New Space – 131 A Gallery, Cape Town, RSA \\n2018 Re-group – Gallery 96, Cape Town, RSA \\n2014 Universum Achterhoek fase 3 – Espace Enny, Laag-Keppe, NLD \\n2013 drinnen binnen buiten draussen – Galerie Roy, Zülpich, GER \\n2013 drinnen binnen buiten draußen – Kersgallery, Amsterdam, NLD \\n2013 Pas Op De Plaats – Kersgallery, Amsterdam, NLD \\n2012 Kompost – Galerie Roy, Zülpich, GER \\n2012 Making Faces: Exploring Contemporary Practice Through Portraiture – WHATIFTHEWORLD, \\n Cape Town, RSA \\n2011 Iene Ambar Daniel Levi – Galerie Eewal, Amsterdam, NLD \\n2009 SPECIMEN – Galerie Lutz, Delft, NLD \\n \\nArt Fairs & Festivals \\nInvestec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, RSA (2019 - 2020) \\nRMB Turbine Art Fair, Johannesburg, RSA (2019)"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013331886301

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641232093405 Daniel Nartey 2632 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640339362013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014002843869"] Discover captivating acrylic and oil paintings by Daniel?Tetteh Nartey, a Ghanaian pop?surrealist artist whose work explores human identity, societal movement, and emotional duality through symbolic bodies and line?traced faces. Shop original artworks and limited editions via Latitudes Online. [21674] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Daniel Tetteh Nartey, a Ghanaian painter and graduate of the prestigious Ghannata College of Arts & Design, stands alongside celebrated artists like Amoako Boafo and Otis Kwaku in his artistic journey. For Nartey, art is a path to self-actualization, with his work continually evolving in tandem with life experiences and personal interpretations. His canvas serves a reflective space, where he visualizes the mental state during moments of transcendence. \\n \\nNartey's paintings are inspired by both the deliberate and accidental actions in daily life, capturing the awkward and satirical elements of human behavior that often elude clear definition. This is particularly evident in his portrayal of figures, where facial expressions and emotions are notably absent. Instead, Nartey uses a distinctive line technique on the faces, representing movement and change, and leaving room for viewers to interpret each piece for themselves. \\n \\nIn his work, Nartey delves into the complexities of human thoughts and emotions, likening life to a pendulum that swings between the polarities of love and hate. The intertwined lines of his figures' faces reflect this back-and-forth, symbolizing the volatile emotional states we all experience. His art suggests that emotional evolution is key to our survival, with the hope that future generations will inherit more of our strengths and fewer of our weaknesses. Nartey's pieces evoke contemplation of the silences surrounding uncomfortable truths, encouraging growth and understanding in an ever-changing world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014002843869

item.title: Daniel Santangelo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641233076445 Daniel Santangelo 2520 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640339656925 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013945860317"] Explore the evocative mixed-media works of Daniel Santangelo, a London-based artist of Ethiopian-Eritrean and Italian heritage. His paintings delve into themes of ancestry, identity, and mythology, blending abstraction with figuration. Available for purchase at Latitudes Online. [20175] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Daniel Santangelo (b. 2004) lives and works in London, UK. \\nBorn to Italian and Ethiopian-Eritrean parents, Daniel Santangelo’s mixed media works explore his ancestry and identity through a mythological lens. His figures explore spaceless, timeless alternative universes - interacting with delicate marks, script, and objects in spiritual and evocative ways. Santangelo looks to distill the Ethiopian-Eritrean experience into objects or behaviours which permeate the surface of his paintings, sitting somewhere between object, abstraction and figuration. In many ways these metaphysical environments are simply reflective of the black ancestral experience - referencing the cultural ties that bind continental Africans and those of the African Diaspora. \\nPortals transport the viewer to a world where both abstract and figurative elements appear in harmony; mankind and animal in symbiosis. Shimmering, sparkling stars are scattered across the surface, referencing humanity’s longstanding interest in the symbolism and secrets held in the night sky and the cosmos beyond. In places, Santangelo’s seemingly ambiguous shapes reference Fidel (traditional Ethiopian/Eritrean script), and his interest in cross cultural mythological representations is evident throughout. Tropes of both Western and Eastern religious painting and mythology feature, as well as a chiaroscuro- esque use of directional light which radiates into and out of both objects and people. These surreal, dramatic dreamscapes strike an interesting balance between peace and power that is somewhat reminiscent of Afrofuturist aesthetics. The sketchy feel of these works helps the surface and ground to breathe, with chaotic brushstrokes and visible pencil sketches hinting at the energy contained within the human mind and hand. \\nSantangelo will graduate from Central Saint Martins with their BFA in 2025. He has been featured by Tate Collective, and has upcoming solo and group shows with Chilli, London. Santangelo is represented by Chilli."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013945860317

[20154,20157,20155,20156] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Daniel Solomon (b. 1987, Cape Town, South Africa) is an artist whose work draws from a deep connection to history, the human experiences, and the delicate balance of our environment and society. With a self-taught artistic practice and an education background in psychology, Daniel expresses themes through a variety of painting media, including oil, acrylic, and gouache. \\nHis artistic journey began with the raw energy of graffiti and street art during his adolescence, exploring urban narratives and the wastelands of industrialised society. Over time, this exploration evolved to include broader narratives that delve into the interactions between past and present, individual and collective angst, and the intricate relationships between humanity and the natural world. \\nDaniel's work is rooted in the rich tradition of figurative painting, using the time-honoured craft of painstaking realism, yet indelibly influenced by the information age. He makes ample use of digital media and tools to create his work. \\nThrough his art, Daniel seeks to investigate our place in time, examining the jumping-off point between analogue and digital reality. He invites viewers to contemplate the hard questions of existence and the fragility of our shared world. \\nDaniels \\nwork is connected to the rich tradition of figurative painting, using the time-honoured craft of painstaking realism, yet indelibly influenced by the information-age; making ample use of digital media and tools to create work. \\n \\nThrough his art, Daniel seeks to investigate our place in time; the jumping-off point between analog and digital reality. \\n \\nInviting viewers to contemplate the hard questions of \\nexistence and the fragility of our shared world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013945467101 gid://shopify/Product/9013945499869 gid://shopify/Product/9013945532637 gid://shopify/Product/9013945565405

item.title: Danielle Clough
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641229668573 Danielle Clough gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640340148445 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013992227037"] Discover vibrant embroidery and fiber artworks by Danielle Clough, a Cape Town-based contemporary artist known for stitching bold pop culture and botanical motifs onto unconventional surfaces—think vintage tennis rackets, chain-link fences, and upcycled objects. Shop original and limited-edition pieces online at Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rumour has it that Adam and Eve had been wandering around in their birthday suits for quite a while before they realised that a bit of modesty might be in order. So, they grabbed a few fig leaves (and possibly a sharp twig), started sewing, and inadvertently set in motion a chain of events that rippled through the strands of time and brought you, dear reader, to this very website at this exact moment. \\nThe threads that link the ancient and the modern are an excellent starting point to describe the work of Cape Town based artist, Danielle Clough (Yes, there are two sewing references in that one sentence and no, we do not think it is overkill). Danielle’s colourful, delicate embroidery celebrates the joining of the old with the new in a wistful and playful manner that is thoroughly modern in approach, yet nostalgic at heart. She utilises a craft that is perceived as archaic but takes inspiration from current pop culture icons and the timeless beauty of nature. Her choice of materials also reflects this fascination with time and her vibrant picture-scapes are just as likely to adorn a vintage tennis racquet as they are a rusty chain link fence or a brand-new pair of Gucci sneakers. \\nThis anachronistic approach to art is reflected in Danielle’s previous medium of choice, live visuals. As a VJ (which is not what you think) she repurposed old video footage to create experimental audio reactive visuals for live music events. Using the stage name Fiancé Knowles, Danielle has performed with fellow South African artists such as Haezer, PH Fat, and Hugh Masekela as well as several internationals acts including the Allah Las, Mick Jenkins, Cid Rim, Soulection, The Black Lips and Black Sun Empire. Her work graced the screens at some of the best music events in South Africa like Rocking the Daisies, Grietfest, Synergy, CTEMF, and NuWorld Fest. \\nDanielle learned the ins and outs of creative expression at The Red and Yellow School where she studied art direction and graphic design. She then began her career as an artist in the fields of visual art, digital design, and the making of bright fluffy things. \\nWhen she is not poking sharp objects into other objects Danielle enjoys expanding her artistic horizons and has hosted a show on Assembly Radio, created custom book covers, and worked as contributing photographer to several local and international publications. She has also stepped into the realm of education with online classes and real-world workshops to help aspiring embroiderers learn and appreciate the craft. Danielle spends her free time biking around Cape Town or enjoying an evening drink from the sunroom of her seaside home. \\nFor Danielle, her creative goal is to express the best of human emotion through art, and for each and every stitch to mark the passing of time spent with love and care. If her work evokes the slightest bit of happiness in you, then her intention has been achieved, and her gratitude is intertwined with your joy in a tapestry so radiant that all the colours in the galaxy could not do it justice. \\n \\nSew far sew good."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013992227037

item.title: Danielle Hewlett
item.description:
gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641229701341 Danielle Hewlett 1489 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640340476125 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013338636509"] Explore the expressive portraiture of Danielle Hewlett, a South African artist known for her bold, gestural paintings that delve into human identity and emotion. Discover original artworks available for purchase at Latitudes Online. [9246] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":""All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players."

"}]}]} {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"For artist Danielle, the creative path was not so much a choice as it was a calling that she has felt since the tender age of eight. She considers herself exceptionally fortunate to have grown up in an environment steeped in creativity, where her ambition to become a painter was not only accepted but actively encouraged. Her childhood was a world surrounded by art and inspired by the work of professional artists, most notably her uncle, the acclaimed painter Alexis Preller, whose influence provided a formative backdrop to her own developing vision. After formally honing her craft at the Surrey Institute of Art and Design, Danielle has now been a practicing artist for twelve years, building a career upon this rich and supportive foundation.

The primary muse for Danielle’s work is found in the vast tapestry of human experience. “I am hugely inspired by everyday people and their stories,” she shares, “and I want to tell those stories in paint.” She is driven by a desire to be a visual narrator, capturing the quiet dramas and unspoken truths of the individuals she meets. Her art seeks to translate personal histories into a universal language of colour and form.

This journey from person to portrait follows an intimate and intuitive process. "Normally I will start with inviting a subject into my studio for a photo session and getting to know them," she explains. This initial meeting is a crucial dialogue, allowing for a genuine connection to form. "Then I spend a good while with the images," a period of quiet contemplation where she studies the nuances of expression and posture, searching for the emotional core of the story she wants to tell. "I move quite quickly to getting the work onto the canvas, normally starting quite messy on a canvas that is splashed with paint." This energetic, almost chaotic foundation of abstract colour is where the discovery begins. "From there," she says, "I begin to find the story I am trying to uncover.” With each layer and brushstroke, the portrait is excavated from the background, as if Danielle is not merely painting a subject, but revealing a truth that was already waiting on the canvas."}]},{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013338636509

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641229963485 Danielle Smith gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640340738269 [] Explore the detailed oil and acrylic wildlife and landscape paintings by Danielle “Danie” Smith, a self-taught artist based in Calgary, Alberta. Shop original and commissioned artworks at Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Danielle Smith started out with a simple yet adventurous life in Harare, Zimbabwe. Due to Zimbabwean politics she moved to Cape Town, South Africa in 2000 where she finished her schooling. She attended the University of Cape Town for 3 years studying Film and Social Anthropology. \\nAfter this she lived in London for two years where personal creative endeavours took a bit of a standstill, but developed as a person: a young girl from Africa in a very new fast exciting world. New thoughts, new friends and new insights of life. \\nBack in Cape Town she worked in Film Production which as exciting as it was did not allow for any time for creativity. At the age of 26 she sold her belongings and bought a ticket to Palma de Mallorca and started a new career working on Super-yachts as a stewardess and chef. \\nHer travels and life experience are influential in her work as symbols of renewal, starting over and constant change. Her paintings are enriched with multiple layers, similar to the stages and phases in life that are in constant flux. Now that she has grounded herself with her family she has everything she needs in order to live the creative life she has always wanted."}]}]}

item.title: Danny Myburgh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641234157789 Danny Myburgh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640341295325 [] Explore the striking works of Danny Myburgh, a Johannesburg-based artist renowned for evocative charcoal drawings of shipping containers, wrecked vessels, and harbour motifs etched on antique maritime charts and photos. Discover original works online at Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I have created art since I was a young child. I find that it is the way that I express my thoughts best. I am not bound by rules, conventions and logic and I am able to express things that are impossible or difficult to verbalise. I have worked as an art therapist and an art teacher and have seen the incredible power of art operate at a subconscious and unconscious level which simply transcends verbal, language, cultural, moral, political values. It functions at a pure, honest, visceral level which is undeniably true. \\n \\nMost of our memories are created before we are 6 years of age. They form the foundation of our neural networks. And by implication, they are the basis of who we become. Unfortunately we can remember barely a handful of these memories even with the help of visual or aural prompts. We are more capable of remembering and understanding a complex occurrence which happened yesterday. And yet our early childhood memories are more influential and more important. \\n \\nWe have very little insight into what motivates us to behave in specific ways in certain situations. Without conscious introspection and mindfulness, we do not understand or have insight into how our early lived experiences affect the rest of our lives. They create the lens through which we experience the world. \\n \\nIn recent times the science of epigenetics (inherited memories) has advanced greatly. Scientists have found tags on our DNA which transfer memories from one generation to another. However the tags need to be activated and this process has yet to be understood. \\nWe do know, that we can inherit memories from our ancestors of things, places, people and events which we have not personally experienced. \\n \\nI am interested in how memories affect our lives. How our perception of these memories changes over time and how this changes the way we live our lives. \\n \\nWhen we are psychologically healthy, we feel contained. In other words, we feel safe as opposed to vulnerable; secure in the belief that the world is at best benign, and at the worst not all bad; mostly in control of ourselves and to a lesser extent our environment; robust enough to be able to deal with some adversity; positive, in that we are prepared to take some risks in order to live our lives to the full; and most importantly, that we have agency and choices to direct our lives. It is therefore very important that we understand ourselves well. And that means we must understand why we do things in certain ways. \\n \\n"}]}]}

Currently featured at Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1979, Mzayiya currently holds a studio space at The Fugitive Art Studios at the New Centre, Selby, Johannesburg. Former artist in residency and a National Research Foundation (NRF) fellow at Factory of the Arts (FOA), a project of the Centre for Humanities Research (CHR) at University of Western Cape (UWC), an artist in residence and board member at Greatmore Artist Studios in Cape Town and Bag Factory in Newtown, Johannesburg. Dathini Mzayiya enrolled at the Community Arts Project (CAP) in Woodstock, Cape Town 2001, where he studied Advanced Programme in Visual Art. Since then, he has been an artist in residencies and exhibited his work nationally and internationally, notably at Art Besel Miami Fair, United States of America, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Scotland, Netherlands, Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Uganda and Tanzania. \\nIn his work, Mzayiya employs mixed mediums ranging from painting, charcoal drawing, animation, sound, video installation, interdisciplinary collaborations and performances. Mzayiya is a founding member of various art organisations and institutions including Factory of the Arts, a Flagship project of the Centre for Humanities Research at University of Western Cape (UWC); Visual Arts Network of South Africa (VANSA); Africa South Arts Initiative (ASAI), City Skin, a public art and public space design firm and Gugulective Artist Collective."}]}]}

Available at Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"David \"Daut\" Makala is an artist born in Lusaka, Zambia and the founder of Studio225 in Chilenje Market. Under the mentorship of Stary Mwaba, he completed an apprenticeship at Evelyn Hone College with Alex Nkazi in drawing and painting (2010-2012). In 2015 he was selected for the Asiko' Art School Residency in Mozambique, organised by Olabisi Silva. That same year, he attended the Insaka International Art Workshop Residency in Livingstone, Zambia. \\n \\nMakala is known for his versatility with materials manifesting in sculpture, painting, printmaking, digital art and performance. He considers his studio practice a research space where thoughts and ideas gather, resulting in his multimedia art. For Makala, the processes involved in production also allow for significant interrogation of themes such as identity politics, the black body and mapping. His works are part of the Lechwe Trust and Chaminuka Lodge Collections. He has participated in numerous exhibitions, residences and art fairs, such as the FNB Johannesburg Fair in 2019,Art Central. and The Congo Biennal 2022."}]}]}
