His oeuvre is currently dominated by portraiture expressed in varying stylized and realistic executions. His range is not limited to portraiture exclusively nonetheless. \\nThe image he produces captures the intricacies of the human emotive, experience, a moment of time is frozen in all its complexities. His interpretations always convey a deeper meaning, through nuance. \\nGrant’s work is represented in corporate and private collections around the globe. \\nWe take pride in being an exclusive touching point with his work and welcome the opportunity to aid in reselling his artwork on your behalf in the future, as an added service."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013333360861 gid://shopify/Product/9013334409437 gid://shopify/Product/9013334966493

item.title: Grace Nyahangare
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641347764445 Grace Nyahangare 2538 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640561594589 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013947334877","gid://shopify/Product/9013947400413","gid://shopify/Product/9013947564253"] Grace Nyahangare [20294,20290,20288] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born 1996 Harare, Zimbabwe \\nLives and works in Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\nGrace Nyahangare is a young painter, who is building up her practice on a foundation of printmaking and photography, which inform both the technical and intellectual elements of her work. Her dreamlike, surreal and dynamically passionate canvases are the result of passing through numerous metamorphoses starting as observations and photographs which are then made into monotypes which then acquire a new environment on canvases in which paint is also transformed through interaction with printers ink to yield a poignancy and otherworldliness. In her early twenties Grace spent three years living and working in the UAE, which has impacted both her aesthetic and ideas about self as a person but also as a woman and now as a young mother. Detachment, reflection and recomposition are synergistic with the ideas that Grace has been working with from the earliest stages of her evolution as an artist, and trying to find whole in a space of cultural and relationship otherness. Grace joined First Floor Gallery Harare in 2023, after completing a three month residency in 2022 she had her first solo in 2023 titled 'Hatikanganwe Asi Tinopora'."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013947334877 gid://shopify/Product/9013947400413 gid://shopify/Product/9013947564253

item.title: Greg Marinovich
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641349599453 Greg Marinovich gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640562413789 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Greg Marinovich is a highly regarded photojournalist, filmmaker and author who distinguished himself photographing the fatal conflicts that preceded the first democratic elections in South Africa in 1994. He was awarded the Pulitzer Prize for Spot News Photography in 1991 for a series of photographs of African National Congress supporters murdering a man they suspected of being an Inkatha Freedom Party spy. \\n \\nMarinovich co-authored a non-fiction book The Bang-Bang Club: Snapshots from a Hidden War (Basic Books, 2000) with João Silva that took readers beyond the photographs, giving context to that tumultuous time as well as many personal stories of those involved. He won the Sunday Times Alan Paton Award in 2017 for Murder at Small Koppie: The real story of the Marikana Massacre, an investigative account of the events leading up to the killing of 34 striking miners in South Africa on 16 August 2012. His book Shots from the Edge: A Journalist's Encounters with Conflict and Resilience, in which he documents his experiences covering war and conflict throughout Africa and the world, was published in 2019 (Penguin Randomhouse). \\n \\nIn 2009, Marinovich was the recipient of the Nat Nakasa award for courageous journalism; and from 2013-14 was a Nieman Fellow at Harvard University. \\n \\nFRISBEE: An African National Congress aligned Self Defence Unit member plays frisbee next to blankets on a line and a severely cut tree at a braai at a safehouse in Thokoza township, South Africa, 1995. \\n \\n“This Self Defence Unit was under the command of Bonga Nkosi and had some of the youngest child soldiers among their fighters in the most contested section of the so called 'Dead Zone' between the Inkatha Freedom Party controlled migrant workers hostels and some surrounding houses and the ANC aligned residential suburbs.” \\n \\nThis is the first public showing of this image, shot as part of Marinovich’s work on the child soldiers at the front lines during the end of apartheid."}]}]}

item.title: Greta McMahon
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641350451421 Greta McMahon gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640563101917 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Greta McMahon (1970 - ) \\n \\nBorn in Wellington, South Africa, Greta completed a National Diploma in Theatre Technology at the Technicon of Pretoria in (1990) and a BA Fine Arts at the Michealis School of Fine Art, UCT (1996). Since then she has participated in numerous group and six solo exhibitions in South Africa and abroad in Ireland and Holland, and in 2005 she was an ABSA Atelier Awards Finalist. \\n \\nGreta uses a variety of media and techniques such as painting, collage, drawing and clay; all the time attempting to integrate aspects of our somewhat polarized existence into an experience of wholeness, awareness and openness. Through her art, she honors and explores mythology, archetypes, dream language symbols, magical realism and an array of polarities such as darkness/light, masculine/feminine, conscious/subconscious, above/below and life/death. \\n \\nArtworks by Greta have been included in the corporate collections of Hollard, Nando’s and Spier, as well as private collections in South Africa, Holland, Norway, the United State of America, the United Kingdom, UAE and Ireland."}]}]}

item.title: Gretchen van der Byl

Explore her figurative work addressing covert violence and the tension in painting-as-window versus surface. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Gretchen van der Byl trained as a painter at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, where she now teaches painting and drawing part-time. Her practice is largely figurative, focusing on covert violence—both in disguised forms unfolding before us and implied through ambiguous spaces. item.title: Gregg Price
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641349435613 Gregg Price 887 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640562970845 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013338374365","gid://shopify/Product/9013338407133"] [9227,9226] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“Perhaps the same bird echoed through both of us yesterday, separate, in the evening.” \\n- Rilke \\n \\nBirds of paradise, Celtic symbols and our new Lockdown reality set amidst the mystical beauty of the Karoo, is the unlikely alchemy that has inspired the artist Gregg Price’s latest solo \\n \\nexhibition: Paradise and the Plague. \\n \\nPrice draws in response to unfolding events in his life. Images, words and symbols are an interpretive language which bridge the space, between his inner and outer worlds. \\n \\nHe chooses to play on the edges of chance and his drawings are an authentic expression of the moment in which he is often surprised by what they reveal. \\n \\n“I do not wish the artwork to be engaged within a literal way. For me, there is no definitive meaning; no clear solution, no resolve, no singular interpretation for each piece. I enjoy both meaning or the lack of it to play lightly through the images.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013338374365 gid://shopify/Product/9013338407133

item.title: Guido van Besouw
item.description: Guido van Besouw gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640563429597 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Guido van Besouw entered the art world when the opportunity arose in 1977 aged 26 to serve as an apprentice under Anton Voorveld an established stained glass artist at the time. \\n \\nIn 1980 Guido launched his career as a full time glass artist, by creating a set of windows and skylights for the Royal Hotel grill room in Durban. In 1984 Guido was invited to group Glass art exhibition at the NSA gallery where he saw blown glass by Shirley Cloete, David Reade and Barry Thompson’s, and was fascinated by the potential of this creative medium. \\n \\nTen years later in 1994 he started in earnest to research the possibility of blowing glass and exploring the potential of making his own glass for stained glass windows. By 1996 he had built a furnace acquired kilns and most of the tools needed to blow glass. Early in 1997 Guido started making glass, teaching himself and developing his skills along the way. \\n \\nToday, Guido van Besouw is recognized as one of the leading glass blowers in South Africa and has mastered the art of hand blown glass. He was awarded the 2003 SA Elle Deco International Design Award for tabletop glass. Guido has been working with glass for thirty years and understands the medium and its potential, and has a unique ability to balance and match colour. He draws his inspiration from nature and his years of experience in creating stained glass windows. \\n \\nHe works from his studio set amongst the green hills of Assagay, Kwa-Zulu Natal, close to The Valley of a Thousand Hills. Fire and sand combine to make liquid glass which Guido then transforms into individual art pieces. Three days later the glass emerges from the annealing kiln in all its beauty, reflecting the colours of fire, sky, earth and water. \\n \\nSome of his commissions have decorated Cape Town, Johannesburg, Durban and Luanda International Airports, The Blue Waters Hotel and The Royal Hotel in Durban. Many pieces have been presented as official diplomatic gifts by various South African dignitaries. His work can also be found decorating many game lodges in and around Southern Africa. There are over 400 stained glass windows that he has designed and made in churches, schools, country clubs, civic buildings and private homes around South Africa."}]}]}

item.title: Guy Du Toit
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641351205085 Guy Du Toit 2521 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640563495133 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014071918813","gid://shopify/Product/9014072017117","gid://shopify/Product/9014076244189"] Guy Du Toit [24109,24181,24111] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“My objects come from my immediate environment, selected for their non-heroic, open-ended meaning. Bells, for instance, may refer either to slavery or liberty. My overriding concern is that of reality and illusion; the fusing of Western and African realities is somehow reflected in this ambiguity.” \\n \\n \\nGuy du Toit uses a wide range of media in his sculptures, including bronze, stone, wood and steel, and draws in pen, ink and charcoal. He has exhibited extensively, both locally and internationally, and has been consistently supported by private and public collectors, institutions, academics and fellow artists. \\n \\nHonoured with several awards, he curates and adjudicates exhibitions and lectures at a number of institutions, including Pelmama Academy in Soweto, Pretoria University, Johannesburg and Pretoria Technicons, and the Johannesburg School of Art, Ballet, Drama and Music. He gives workshops throughout South Africa and has been involved in community projects, seminars and symposia. \\n \\nThe past few years have increasingly been spent on private and public commissions and in working closely with artists and businesses, especially those involved in design, communications, architecture, advertising and entertainment. Guy currently teaches part-time at the University of Pretoria and works full-time from his new home and studio in Zwavelpoort. \\n \\nGuy du Toit’s apparent irreverence can obfuscate the fact that he is undoubtedly one of South Africa’s most accomplished sculptors. “Liberated” (as he says) by the advent of democracy in South Africa from having to concern himself and his art with the notions of identity, he has happily turned his attention to “less provincial” pursuits like revelling in form, concept and media for their own sakes. Du Toit uses the unexpected juxtaposition of bronze casts of universal, everyday found (and made-to-look-found) objects to invite his audience to invent dialogue themselves."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014071918813 gid://shopify/Product/9014072017117 gid://shopify/Product/9014076244189

item.title: Guy Thesen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641351925981 Guy Thesen gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640563593437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014061498589","gid://shopify/Product/9014061695197"] Guy Thesen is a South African artist based in Knysna, known for his unique blend of figurative and abstract art. Drawing inspiration from Hergé, Matisse, and San rock art, his work has been featured in numerous exhibitions at Knysna Fine Art. \n {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Guy Thesen (b. 1961, Knysna) is a South African artist known for his distinctive style and creative versatility. He earned a Diploma in Graphic Design from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town (1983–1986) and began his career as a designer at Americom before moving to Neil Napper and Associates in Johannesburg. During this period, he contributed to high-profile projects, including the design of Ngala Lodges in Timbavati and Buffalo Valley Bushlodges in Knysna. \\n \\nFrom 1992 to 1995, Thesen taught art at Oakhill School in Knysna before fully dedicating himself to a career in fine art in 2004. Drawing inspiration from artists such as Hergé, Henri Matisse, Paul Gauguin, and the rich tradition of South African San rock art, his work blends elements of figurative and abstract styles. Thesen’s art has been showcased in various solo and group exhibitions, primarily through Knysna Fine Art under the curation of Trent Read. He continues to live and work in Knysna, where he creates his art from his home studio. \\n \\nWebsite: www.guythesen.co.za \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014061498589 gid://shopify/Product/9014061695197

item.title: Guy Tillim
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641352548573 Guy Tillim gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640563888349 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Guy Tillim was born in Johannesburg in 1962. After completing a B.Comm at the University of Cape Town in 1983, Tillim joined Afrapix, a collective of South African photographers, in 1986, and since then has seen his work widely published. His involvement with Afrapix continued until 1990, alongside positions with foreign media groups, such as Reuters (1986 - 88) and Agence France Presse (1993-94). He received the Mondi Award (South Africa) for photojournalism in 1998 for his essay of images entitled: Congo River - journey from Kinsangani to Kinshasa. \\n \\nHis work has been included in many exhibitions of South African art and photography, both at home and internationally. \\n \\nHis assignment work takes him to diverse environments with the common theme of war, destruction, torment, hope, and beauty. Tillim has the capacity to access the remoteness of the human condition and continues to be a visual spokesperson for communities in his immediate surroundings and Cape Town home base. Tillim spends much of his time out of the country on foreign assignments and self-motivated projects."}]}]}

item.title: Hamid Nii Nortey
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641354285277 Hamid Nii Nortey 1829 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640564052189 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013377892573","gid://shopify/Product/9013377990877","gid://shopify/Product/9013378089181","gid://shopify/Product/9013382873309","gid://shopify/Product/9013382906077","gid://shopify/Product/9013383004381","gid://shopify/Product/9013383397597","gid://shopify/Product/9013383528669","gid://shopify/Product/9013383561437","gid://shopify/Product/9013383594205","gid://shopify/Product/9013383725277","gid://shopify/Product/9013383790813"] [13535,13086,13528,13088,13529,13536,13089,13533,13532,13530,13531,13534] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"No artist has truly captured the essence of modern gender representation through the African lens more poignantly than the self-taught artist, Hamid Nii Nortey. \\n \\nHis story begins in the bustling country of Ghana where he was born and raised in a traditional Ga ethnic multigenerational home. The multigenerational nature of his upbringing, especially rooted in strong Black female characters, has had the most profound impact on his life – deeply defining both his art and his identity. \\n \\nFrom his inspiring ‘The Beautiful Ones Are Not Yet Born’ group exhibition in 2012 to his breathtaking ‘Beauty in Diversity’ solo series in 2020, Nortey has created a plethora of pieces depicting compelling figurative portrait paintings that redefine gender and sexuality in the most disruptive and thought-provoking way. \\n \\nUltimately, Nortey’s paintings ignite an intriguing dialogue between the subject’s message and the viewer, as he aims to capture the soul, substance and heritage of the human spirit. He also uses his art as an opportunity to lend the world a glance into the lives of people whose stories are yet to be told, all while triggering emotions of pride, honour and humour - it’s a culmination of the stories of his life that words simply cannot explain. \\n \\nCOUNTRY • GHANA"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013377892573 gid://shopify/Product/9013377990877 gid://shopify/Product/9013378089181 gid://shopify/Product/9013382873309 gid://shopify/Product/9013382906077 gid://shopify/Product/9013383004381 gid://shopify/Product/9013383397597 gid://shopify/Product/9013383528669 gid://shopify/Product/9013383561437 gid://shopify/Product/9013383594205 gid://shopify/Product/9013383725277 gid://shopify/Product/9013383790813

Grappling with the psyche, physicality and metaphysics around these experiences. item.title: Hannah-Rose Fleishman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641358807261 Hannah-Rose Fleishman gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640568213725 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hannah-Rose Fleishman is a South African artist based in Cape Town. She graduated with distinction from the Michaelis School of Fine Art in 2022, majoring in photography and sculpture. Her work revolves around the conceptual idea of falling, an inquiry that she believes is also an inquiry into the state of being. Fleishman engages with an ongoing investigation into the human desire to be human. Into the belly-aching pain of being. Into the silliness of asking questions to the internet void to try and crack the code. Questions we all ask. Uncertainties of how to be. How do I walk, kiss, fall in a way that seems as if I have needed no help? Fleishman’s work, being process and research based, spans various mediums with a focus on new media and installation art. Digitality becomes a predominant focus area in her work, explored as space that allows for the reorganizing of spatial ordering. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Hannah Macfarlane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641359528157 Hannah Macfarlane 1142 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640568148189 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013309898973"] [5937] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hannah Macfarlane is a multidisciplinary artist, the core of her practice being sculpture and printmaking. Currently focusing on the tactile realm of wet felting, Macfarlane explores intimacy and vulnerability through the application of unusual materials and processes of art-making, her performance art acting as a gesture of self-care. Cultivating a tender sense of self in uncertain times and learning to sit comfortably with discomfort is her primary goal. \\nMacfarlane uses her art practice as a means of processing, healing and learning as she engages with her chosen material, currently creating sculpted forms by combining hand-dyed fabric, stitching and wet felting by continuously rubbing wool with soap and warm water. Resulting in visceral manifestations, upon closer inspection one is made to think of their own fragile body as Macfarlane threads and weaves these materials together. \\nRecently graduated from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, she currently lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. Macfarlane has recently been a participating artist in the ArtistLab development programme with Latitudes Online, in collaboration with artist Mandy Johnston and mentored by Bonolo Kavula."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013308489949 gid://shopify/Product/9013309898973

Discover her solo shows, awards, and collections housing her work. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hanneke Benadé earned her BA in Fine Arts from the University of Pretoria in 1993 and lectured part-time until 1998. She has exhibited extensively, including at the Joburg Biennale and London Art Fair. Her first solo exhibition, \"Local Girls,\" was in 1996 at Gallery on Tyrone, Johannesburg. After moving to Cape Town, she presented \"Passage\" at Chelsea gallery in Darling, \"The Gift\" at US Gallery in Stellenbosch, and \"Once More, Wants More\" at Scukan Gallery in Pretoria. \\nShe exhibits at the Everard Reads and 'Stage' was her most recent solo exhibition at the Read Gallery in Cape Town. \\nBenade continues to exhibit at Everard Read, with her most recent solo show, \"Stage,\" at Read Gallery in Cape Town. She has received several awards, including Merit Awards at the ABSA Atelier (1995/96) and a Brett Kebble Award (2003). In 2008, she received two Kanna-Awards at the Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees in Oudtshoorn. Her works are included in collections at the Universities of Stellenbosch, Pretoria, Free State, and Johannesburg, as well as at Spier Holdings, Rand Merchant Bank, SAB, Hollard House, Pretoria Art Museum, Gauteng Provincial Government, British American Tobacco Company, Sanlam, Sasol, Telkom, and ABSA."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014014869725 gid://shopify/Product/9014014902493 gid://shopify/Product/9014014935261 gid://shopify/Product/9014031089885

item.title: Hannelie Coetzee
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641361297629 Hannelie Coetzee 580 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640569786589 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013284602077"] [3250] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hannelie Coetzee (b. 1971) is a Johannesburg-based visual artist. Coetzee works in her practice to grow an audience that appreciates art whilst contributing to systems change. She received a BTech degree in social documentary photography from the Vaal University for Technology in 1994. \\n \\nShe followed it up with an Advanced Diploma in Fine Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits) whilst working in the Fine Arts Department (1996-1997). She studied Social Entrepreneurship at the Gordon Institute for Business Science (GIBS), The University of Pretoria’s Business School in Johannesburg on a Rand Merchant Bank Grant in 2013. She was invited to do a Master of Science Degree (MSc) as an artist in the Wits Animal, Plants and Environmental Science School in 2019. She will be reading with an abductive approach to hone science as a medium in artworks that connect people. \\n \\nCoetzee uses natural materials, unlikely partnerships and industry waste to build site-specific artworks. Her artworks are sometimes permanent, but often ephemeral. Research into the material and the context of the site is fundamental to her process and inspires her conceptually. Coetzee’s two-dimensional murals, three-dimensional sculptures and photographs engage partners and viewers to challenge their perspectives, often through immersive experiences such as walking. Coetzee’s artworks integrate science and culture to encourage empathy for and engagement with nature. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013284602077

item.title: Hedwig Barry
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641361854685 Hedwig Barry 449 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640572178653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359083741","gid://shopify/Product/9013360165085","gid://shopify/Product/9013839102173","gid://shopify/Product/9013839167709","gid://shopify/Product/9013986558173","gid://shopify/Product/9013986689245","gid://shopify/Product/9014006612189","gid://shopify/Product/9014007431389"] [11417,21163,21164,18247,21988,18246,21957] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\\n \\nHedwig Barry (b.1969, Bloemfontein) is an artist working at the intersection of the visual arts, arts education, and research. Her drawings, paintings, and sculptures are grounded in a rich conceptual terrain that articulates a feminist politics of love and desire in artistic practice, and in society at large. Probing the metaphor of “grounding”, and of “groundlessness”, Barry’s work explores the grounds we walk on and live in. She asks how we teach and learn, how and whom we include, and what we make along the way. \\n \\nA long career as an educator, facilitator, producer, and collaborator, across artistic disciplines, has led her to a dedicated studio practice embedded in the processes of drawing, painting, sculpting, and writing. In 2020 Barry graduated cum laude from the MA Fine Arts programme at the Wits School of Arts in Johannesburg, with a project titled “Pedagogies, Desires and Practices, the perplexing spaces of teaching and learning”. Also in 2020, through a collaboration between Wits and BMW, she was commissioned by BMW to create two large-scale outdoor interventions for the BMW campus in Midrand, South Africa. Both commissions - the “Crumple” and “Love Letter for Lost Travellers” were completed in early 2021. These and other current works are about the interface of the personal and the public, the emotional and the intellectual, and the bodies, grounds, materials, desires, and gestures which give meaning to these relationships. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013359083741 gid://shopify/Product/9013360165085 gid://shopify/Product/9013839102173 gid://shopify/Product/9013839167709 gid://shopify/Product/9013986558173 gid://shopify/Product/9013986689245 gid://shopify/Product/9014006612189 gid://shopify/Product/9014007431389

item.title: Helen Lotter
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641366311133 Helen Lotter gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640574144733 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here’s the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang. In 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University which has always had a strong history of printmaking. During a class reunion exhibition in 2016 they inspired each other to create in print again and began to exhibit as The Printing Girls. The following year they decided to invite new female printmakers to join up, and TPG in its current incarnation began to materialise. But the main focus has never changed - to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network and exhibit together."}]}]}

item.title: Helena Hugo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641365721309 Helena Hugo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640574406877 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Showcasing underappreciated individuals for the past two decades, Hugo has been exploring the theme of South African labourers, people who, despite their outstanding economic contribution, are often overlooked by society. By portraying them in such formality, she encourages viewers to reconsider their status and importance. Hugo has always been interested in realist portraits that unveil a deeper understanding of people’s character. \\nImmersing herself in the setting Hugo takes photos of her chosen location, finding models within the area. She uses these photographs as reference material to initially sketch out a rough drawing with charcoal. Only after this first conceptualisation of the future artwork, she starts the process of drawing with pastel, giving her portraits a smooth texture. Colour, although carefully considered as part of the presentation of her work, becomes secondary to her emphasis on technical accuracy, strong draughtsmanship and detail in line and texture. \\nHelena Hugo has accumulated recognition around the world, her work displayed in both corporate and private collections. She has participated in numerous solo and group shows, some of which where she was a finalist includes: the BP Portrait Award, the Sasol New Signatures Competition, Johannesburg and Absa L'Atelier Competition, South Africa."}]}]}

item.title: Helen Sebidi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641371160797 Helen Sebidi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640574275805 [] Explore the works of Helen Sebidi, a South African visual artist dedicated to mythologies, ancestry, and traditional value systems. Inspired by her grandmother and mentored by John Keonakeefe Mohl, Sebidi continues to teach and inspire from her studio in Parktown, Johannesburg. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Helen Sebidi was born in Marapyane near Hammanskraal in Northern Transvaal (now Gauteng and Limpopo). Growing up with her grandmother, a traditional wall and floor painter who taught Sebidi the importance of channeling spirit into the world through hard work, commitment to herself, her community and through creativity, whether through cooking, weaving, beading, drawing or painting. \\n \\nConsequently, from a young child, Sebidi developed a lasting love for creative pursuits, particularly drawing and painting and the designs of traditional arts and craft. As a young adult Sebidi worked as a domestic worker, but soon discovered she had a talent for painting. Her employer had taken up painting, and after Sebidi expressed an interest in it, she received her first set of oil paints. She then sought out formal lessons and ended up being taught and mentored by John Keonakeefe Mohl in the early 1970s. Sebidi returned to Marapyane in 1975 to look after her grandmother who later passed in 1981. It was around this time she trained at the Katlehong Arts Centre to improve her clay, moulding and sculpture techniques. Mmakgabo Mapula Helen Sebidi resides in Parktown, Johannesburg, where she works in her studio and, in her spare time, continues to teach and inspire. Sebidi’s practice is dedicated to mythologies, ancestry and traditional value systems"}]}]}

item.title: Hendrick Kgosana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641372340445 Hendrick Kgosana gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640574537949 [] [12809,12900,12810,12899,12821] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hendrick Kgosana was born in the town of Mokopane, Ga Mokaba Village in Limpopo Province. At a young age, Kgosana took a journey to Johannesburg, where most of his education was completed. He studied fine art at the Central Johannesburg College, Crown Mines Campus between 2010 and 2011. During 2013 and 2014, Hendrick furthered his studies at the Artist Proof Studio, where he developed further his knowledge of fine art. In between pursuing his talent of fine art, between 2016 and 2021, Kgosana volunteered at the Braamfontein-based Little Artists’ School, which offers art classes to previously disadvantaged and rehabilitated street children. \\n \\nKgosana’s work focuses on the movement of people in South African townships, as well as village landscapes. He believes that in human beings lies a spiritual connection to God and tries to capture the movement of religion in his works: people belonging to various church groups either singing, dancing to moropa (drums) or in groups on their way to or from church."}]}]}

item.title: Hemali Khoosal
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641372078301 Hemali Khoosal 1128 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640574472413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013360099549","gid://shopify/Product/9013436842205","gid://shopify/Product/9013436874973","gid://shopify/Product/9013846671581","gid://shopify/Product/9133222068445"] [18760,11159,16078,11451,16079] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hemali Khoosal is a socially engaged artist and researcher. She is a Fine Arts graduate of Wits School of Art, in her home city, Johannesburg. Khoosal also completed part of her Honours on exchange in the Scenography department at Haute École Des Arts du Rhin, Strasbourg. The artist enjoys exploring how humans perceive themselves in relation to others. Her art is collaboratively oriented and draws from conversations and interactions with people. As a multidisciplinary artist, each mode allows a different approach to her interests in gesture; language; migration; and intergenerationally inherited and overlooked forms of knowledge. \\nGesture is explored as a channel of communication and an everyday metaphoric language. As things are spoken and gestured into being, Hemali grasps at fragments of what passes her by. Her video installations, paintings, and prints carry disorienting distortions, nostalgic visions, and rhythmic hands in motion. Through cross-sharing stories - especially underrepresented ones - she hopes her video work may hold space for people to find common ground in their seemingly disconnected experiences and internal worlds. \\nMost recently, Khoosal was awarded a three-month residency at The Spinnerei, in Leipzig, Germany, by The Centre for The Less Good Idea & David Krut Projects. Prior to that, she was awarded the Sam Nhlengethwa Young Womxn Award from the Bag Factory, where she had a one-year residency, and a two-person exhibition: In Passing. She graduated with distinction from Wits School of Art; was runner-up for the Wits Young Artist Award; and received the Giovanna Milner Award. She was also the winner of the Emerging Artist’s Portraiture Development Programme, a finalist for Sasol New Signatures, a nominee for the Video Art Awards in Italy, and a recipient of the International Spoleto Award. Additionally, she has work in collections including the Centro Luigi di Sarro; the Jack Ginsberg Collection; and Keleketla! Library."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013360099549 gid://shopify/Product/9013436842205 gid://shopify/Product/9013436874973 gid://shopify/Product/9013846671581 gid://shopify/Product/9133222068445

item.title: Henk Serfontein
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641374306525 Henk Serfontein 665 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640575127773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013837234397","gid://shopify/Product/9133212565725","gid://shopify/Product/9133229768925"] [18158] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Henk Serfontein is an award-winning artist who came to prominence with his hyperreal paintings of nightscapes, featuring the marginal, transitory spaces of South Africa. \\n \\nThroughout the past decade, Serfontein’s abstracts explored similar themes and psychological spaces, questioning the space between European tradition and adventurous, unrestrained African aesthetic as he excavates his own identity: not quite African, not quite European. A deep, enduring attachment to the landscape pervades as an intersection of identity, culture and history. \\n \\nSerfontein’s recent Maputo Abstracts series relies heavily on confrontative colour as invoked by the ubiquitous capulanas (popular wax-printed cloths). His geometric compositions echo the art deco lines of the Mozambican city’s buildings and ceramics. \\n \\nSerfontein drew on his design sensibility in the creation of the 10m2 mosaic commissioned for Nando’s Soho, produced in collaboration with Spier Arts Academy. Inspired by Matisse, Serfontein created this composition by cutting out replicas of his own existing artworks and rearranging them within highly irregular dimensions in a format reminiscent of landscape. Intrinsic to the concept is the relevance of the mosaic materials: included is stone endemic to South Africa, thus literally bringing the landscape to European soil, hence materialising the act of cultural export and intersection. \\n \\nHenk Serfontein holds a degree in Fine Art (cum laude) from the Tshwane University of Technology (1997) and studied at the Cite Internationale des Arts in Paris, France (1997-1999). He has lectured art at tertiary level, adjudicated national art competitions and is an accomplished curator of exhibitions. \\n \\nSELECTED EXHIBITIONS: \\n \\n2020 \\n \\nA Walking Shadow, Everard Read, Franschhoek, South Africa \\n \\n \\n \\n2019 \\nWinter Collection, Everard Read, Franschhoek, South Africa \\n \\n2018 \\nSpring Exhibition, Everard Read, Franschhoek, South Africa \\n \\n2011 \\nUrban Tension, Solo Exhibition, Galeria Alex Telese, Barcelona, Spain. \\n \\n2009 \\nTravelling the Margins, Solo Exhibition, Ilse French Fine Art Consultancy, Johannesburg \\n \\n2002 \\nMemorabilia, Solo Exhibition, Everard Read Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\n1997 \\nLabyrinthe de mémoire et mythe, Solo Exhibition, Cité Internationale des Arts, Paris, France \\n \\n1996 \\nLabyrinth of Remains, Solo Exhibition, Karen McKerron Art Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n1995 \\nHenk Serfontein: Winner of The Reginald Turvey Painting Competition, Karen McKerron Art Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\nPUBLIC COLLECTIONS: \\n \\nABSA Banking Group, GENCOR, SASOL, Rand Merchant Bank, Pretoria Art Museum, Tswane University, British American Tobacco, Webber Wentzel, SPIER, Nando's United Kingdom. Private collections in South Africa, London, New York, Chicago, Berlin, Tokyo, Ireland, Amsterdam and Paris. \\n \\nAWARDS: \\n \\n2011 \\nOfficial invited resident artist at the Piramidon Centre of Contemporary Art, Barcelona Spain. \\n \\n2010 \\n Finalist in the International Guasch Coranty Painting Award, Barcelona, Spain. \\n \\n1996 \\nOfficial representative of South Africa at the Sixth International Cairo Biennale, Egypt with fellow artists Trevor Makhoba, Keith Dietrich and Gordon Froud. \\n \\n1995 \\n Winner of the SASOL New Signatures Art Competition. \\n \\n1994 \\nMerit Award, ABSA Atelier Art Competition. Winner of The Reginald Turvey Painting Competition. \\n \\n1992 \\nWinner of the Dr. I.F. Anderson award for most outstanding final year student, Tswane University. \\nPresented with Silver Rectors Medal for outstanding academic achievement, Tswane University."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013837234397 gid://shopify/Product/9133212565725 gid://shopify/Product/9133229768925

Her practice seeks \\nto intersect the use of mark making, sound, voice, performance and the visual. \\nShe has exhibited in various group shows including Turbine Art Fair, The National \\nArts Festival, MTN UJ Continuing Conversations, top ten Emerging Artist Portrait \\nAward (2018), top 100 Sasol New Signatures (2019) and Top 20 Thami Mnyele Fine Art \\nAwards (2019) and The Centre for the Less Good Idea’s Long Minute Series 1 (2020). \\nRecently, she participated in the Creative Practices Residency in Bloemfontein, which \\nis funded by the Vrystaat Kunstefees and a group exhibition at the Voortrekker \\nMonument as part of Aardklop Festival. \\nShe also co-curated the exhibition a short philosophy on medium showing at AVA \\nGallery in Cape Town until 25th November, 2021. \\nHenrietta holds a degree in English Literature and an honours degree in \\nCommunications Management"}]}]}

item.title: Henry 'Mzili' Mujunga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641378861277 Henry 'Mzili' Mujunga gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640575488221 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Henry ’Mzili’ Mujunga’s portraits feature numerous, seemingly disparate objects brought together into a single frame. They are set in intimate spaces where highly personal interactions take place - often combining several such spaces into one - with titles that the describe the interactions within the paintings themselves, and at the same time allude to external associations. Mzili’s gathering of objects, spaces, and the existing associations with these objects mimics the processes of identity-making that he observes in his native Uganda. Individuals often rely on their outward appearance, their possessions, even their environments (and their interactions within them) to communicate their own vision of themselves. At the same time these very things are looked upon by others to identify those around them. Through these information-packed autobiographical compositions, Mzili offers a glimpse into his personal history and present. In addition, they become, for the viewer, a point of departure from which to begin building an understanding of identity in present-day urban Kampala. \\n \\nRenowned as a painter and printmaker, intermingles traditional visual forms, African art histories and modern techniques and approaches to art making. Over the course of a career spanning more than two decades he has been an advocate of what he refers to as ‘indigenous expressionism’. In 2003, Mzili was a winner of the Royal Overseas League (ROSL) Art Scholarship. He has exhibited extensively in galleries in Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Nigeria, Togo, Benin, Burkina Faso, Mali, Ghana, the UK, Germany, France and The Netherlands. Mzili is a cofounder of Kampala Arts Trust."}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641381056733 Hickmatu Leigh 1822 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640575750365 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013420294365","gid://shopify/Product/9013420392669"] [15261,15262] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hickmatu Leigh (1997) is a Sierra Leonean artist based in Freetown. She recently completed her BSc in Public Health at the Njala University in Sierra Leone and is currently doing her masters in social and behavioral health sciences. Her work is centred around Sierra Leonean women, sharing their stories, and supporting systems that bring their bodies what they need— fundamental human rights. My photo series are almost always of Sierra Leonean women just as they are— multidimensional, polymaths, modern, traditional, soft, powerful, and boundless— forever evolving to supersede local and global stereotypes of “their limits”."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013420294365 gid://shopify/Product/9013420392669

item.title: Hlelo Molefe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641384005853 Hlelo Molefe 2681 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640576241885 [] Explore the captivating works of Hlelo Molefe, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through bold compositions and expressive textures, Molefe’s art delves into themes of culture, identity, and storytelling, creating visually striking and thought-provoking pieces. [22411] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hlelo Molelfe explore the theme of migration of the people of Africa in his work. He has migrated from one African country to another, in search of political and economic stability. The portraits of the people in his work are all immigrants living in Johannesburg. \\nThey are people from different African countries who have encountered the same situations as Hlelo Molefe has. Their portraits break up into pieces and shapes scattered and disrupting the image, similar to the scattered people of the African content. The pieces of shapes resemble pieces of a puzzle or a map. Hlelo Molefe attempt to make the pieces fit together in his works, to make a solid and stable space and place. The fragments are symbolic of the Diasporas of the people of Africa. We are all trying to adapt, fit in and blend into our new environment."}]}]}

item.title: Hlengiwe Dube
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641385218269 Hlengiwe Dube gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640576667869 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hlengiwe Dube is a South African artist who specializes in beadwork and telephone wire baskets and a field worker who travels into rural areas to train remote artists. Dube was born in New Hanover in 1974 and moved to the Valley of a Thousand Hills, KwaZulu-Natal at the age of nine. \\nAs a child she watched her grandmother doing beadwork but was told she was “too young” to try. Instead, she decided to do it in secret. As she wanted to bead as well as her grandmother she worked hard and soon her grandmother was very impressed and proud. of her. The first beaded item she sold was a Zulu Love Letter at the age of twelve. The buyer was the African Art Centre and this piece now resides in their permanent collection at the Killie Campbell Museum in Durban, South Africa. Her vast knowledge of Zulu beading history and technique is drawn from her extensive experience and travels meeting with women throughout KwaZulu-Natal, and from working with her mother and grandmother in her early years. \\nOne of the great resources of Zulu beading history and technique, Dube generously shares her knowledge with students, museum staff and collectors. Dube is gifted as an educator - matched by her talent as a contemporary artist. She is the author of Zulu Beadwork – Talk with Beads recounting the history of beaded messages and has one many awards including : Woman of the year 2000 under Art and Culture sponsored by SABC3 and Checkers, Cosmopolitan Mover 2001 Finalist, Mayor’s Award 2000: Achievement in Business, Sunday Tribune Award 2002, Amafa Heritage Award 2012 and Living Legends 2012. Dube has exhibited beadwork and wirework all over South Africa, in Australia, Germany, USA, France and Brazil, and has taught beading workshops all over the world."}]}]}

item.title: Hoek Swaratlhe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641395867869 Hoek Swaratlhe 2508 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640579813597 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013940322525","gid://shopify/Product/9014016704733","gid://shopify/Product/9014110159069","gid://shopify/Product/9014115434717","gid://shopify/Product/9014115500253"] [22423,24995,19869,25140,20136,25142] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hoek Swaratlhe is a South African photographer and visual based in Soweto, Johannesburg. His themes centre around his community, its urban culture and the history that informs its socio-political landscape. Swaratlhe ‘s career began in commercial photography, he has worked with Johann Barnard, Francois Booyens and others. He was head of Photography at Basement in The Arts and Sound Visual, a recording label. He spent two- years as artist in resident in the Kopanong Art Studio Residency Program at Pretoria Arts Museum from 2015 and completed the Advanced Program in Photography (APP) in 2018. He has photographed for the Market Theatre Foundation, Lampost and Netflix. \\nSwaratlhe recently won the 1st prize in the 3rd annual Umsizi Nopende Award (2024) and had his first solo exhibition 4Dladla (2022) as part of the Media and Advocacy Photography Mentorship. Group exhibitions include In Process (2022) as part of The Incubator Mentorship Program at The Market Photo Workshop, the FUJIFILM showcase ‘Take Ten’ in 2022. He is a member of Occupying the Gallery; the project aims to transform gallery spaces into makeshift open studios for mentorship and artistic development and was a part of the group exhibition ‘Bazobuya’ 2024 curated by Lawrence Lemaoana, at the KZNSA Gallery in Durban, South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013940322525 gid://shopify/Product/9014016704733 gid://shopify/Product/9014110159069 gid://shopify/Product/9014115434717 gid://shopify/Product/9014115500253

She had study graphic design in college then she took her design experience and applied to her paintings, creating her work with bright colors by design style. Hlobile has fascinated by creating beautiful art works and how the world is represented through the eyes of others. \\n \\nHlobile is not into creating something realistic but she enjoy's playing around with painting using bright colors and express her feelings with colors, by her using bright colors she believes that color heals a broken soul and have hope. item.title: Hugo Naudé
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641396785373 Hugo Naudé gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640580042973 [] Discover the life and work of Hugo Naudé, South Africa’s first professional artist. Trained in Europe, he developed a distinctive Cape Impressionist style, capturing the vibrant landscapes of Southern Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hugo Naudé (1869–1941) was a South African painter and one of the country's first professional artists. Born in Worcester, Western Cape, Naudé trained at the Slade School of Fine Art in London and the Kunst Akademie in Munich. Influenced by the Barbizon School in France, he developed a unique Cape Impressionist style, capturing the vivid landscapes of Southern Africa with bold colors and dynamic compositions. \\nHis works often depicted the Namaqualand wildflowers, the Drakensberg mountains, and coastal scenes. Naudé's commitment to plein air painting and his adaptation of European techniques to the African landscape left a lasting impact on South African art. His home in Worcester, known as the Hugo Naudé House, is preserved as a museum and art center, celebrating his contributions to the country's artistic heritage."}]}]}

item.title: Hussein Salim
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641399046365 Hussein Salim 291 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640581714141 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013309964509", "gid://shopify/Product/9013309997277", "gid://shopify/Product/9013310030045", "gid://shopify/Product/9013310095581", "gid://shopify/Product/9013310128349", "gid://shopify/Product/9013314584797", "gid://shopify/Product/9013321302237", "gid://shopify/Product/9013321433309", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324611805", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324677341", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324808413", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324873949", "gid://shopify/Product/9013326610653"] [5601,7193,6426,6425,6427,6428,7194,6430,6431,5605,5606,5607,6438,6086,6437,6436,6435,5602,5603,5604,6424,4294,4295,7191,5685,6087,6088,6089,6090,6091] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As a result of a tumultuous political and economical period in Sudan, which also brought about disputes of its historical context, Hussein Salim spent a number of years as a refugee in various countries including Egypt and South Africa. Following his artistic training at Khartoum University, he attained his Master’s degree in art at the University of Kwa-Zulu Natal, Pietermaritzburg. \\nHe has exhibited extensively overseas along with acclaimed local galleries, such as Johans Borman and Bonisa Private Gallery. It was during this time that Salim and his family embarked on both an emotional and awakening return back to his homeland, Sudan. Inspired by its diversity and diasporic, multicultural communal structure, his body of work celebrates this through the extensive layering of symbols, rich colours and vivid forms. \\nFollowing the example of graciousness, humility and resilience of the Sudanese, Salim has worked closely with NGO’s such as African Angels and Buccaneers Outreach program, which focus on the sustenance and uplifting of children and schools in marginalized communities with proceeds of his artwork sales being donated to various outreach schemes."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013294203101 gid://shopify/Product/9013294235869 gid://shopify/Product/9013307015389 gid://shopify/Product/9013307048157 gid://shopify/Product/9013307080925 gid://shopify/Product/9013307146461 gid://shopify/Product/9013307179229 gid://shopify/Product/9013307211997 gid://shopify/Product/9013307277533 gid://shopify/Product/9013307310301 gid://shopify/Product/9013309964509 gid://shopify/Product/9013309997277 gid://shopify/Product/9013310030045 gid://shopify/Product/9013310062813 gid://shopify/Product/9013310095581 gid://shopify/Product/9013310128349 gid://shopify/Product/9013311471837 gid://shopify/Product/9013311537373 gid://shopify/Product/9013311635677 gid://shopify/Product/9013311701213 gid://shopify/Product/9013311733981 gid://shopify/Product/9013312159965 gid://shopify/Product/9013312258269 gid://shopify/Product/9013312389341 gid://shopify/Product/9013312454877 gid://shopify/Product/9013312553181 gid://shopify/Product/9013312618717 gid://shopify/Product/9013314584797 gid://shopify/Product/9013314683101 gid://shopify/Product/9013314781405 gid://shopify/Product/9013321302237 gid://shopify/Product/9013321433309 gid://shopify/Product/9013324611805 gid://shopify/Product/9013324677341 gid://shopify/Product/9013324808413 gid://shopify/Product/9013324873949 gid://shopify/Product/9013326610653

item.title: Ian Garrett
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641409761501 Ian Garrett gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640587022557 [] Discover the exquisite ceramic art of Ian Garrett, a South African master ceramicist known for his hybrid vessels that blend traditional techniques with contemporary aesthetics. His work is showcased in prestigious public collections worldwide. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ian Garrett (b. 1971) is a South African master ceramicist from the Eastern Cape. His artistic journey reflects his lifelong passion for the ancient craft of hand-building, burnishing, and pit-firing ceramics. Garrett's work, deeply informed by archaic traditions, features nuanced, hybrid vessels that are both timeless and contemporary. \\nHis pieces are characterized by original forms and highly refined surfaces, with glossy burnished areas juxtaposed against intricate swathes of matte-textured linear motifs. These lines, resembling fingerprints, cartographic contours, or magnetic force fields, seem to reveal hidden energies within the clay. \\nGarrett's academic background includes a BFA in sculpture from Rhodes University and an MFA in Ceramics from the University of Kwa-Zulu Natal, where he graduated cum laude. His work is featured in public collections such as the South African National Gallery in Cape Town, the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Art Gallery in Gqeberha, the Pretoria Art Museum, the Die Neue Sammlung Design Museum in Munich, and the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art in Washington D.C."}]}]}

His career so far has been dedicated to exploring the experiences of black people by painting black Portraits as a means of telling individual stories and exploring cultural heritage by merging his Portraits with painted backgrounds of traditional African (Ankara) fabric print designs. \\n \\nHe is keenly observant of how rich the tones, textures and forms of black people are irrespective of their age or origins, and thus offers the viewer intricate details to appreciate in his portraits. His work has been exhibited by international art galleries and in international art fairs such as the Investec Art Fair, South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013348696285 gid://shopify/Product/9013348761821 gid://shopify/Product/9013399584989 gid://shopify/Product/9013400404189 gid://shopify/Product/9013400436957 gid://shopify/Product/9013400568029

The self taught artist is fascinated by the close examination of ordinary objects and placing them in an unusual context. While his subjects are diverse, Banja is repeatedly drawn to portraits and the everyday encounters his subjects find themselves in. In his Struggles series, the artist depicts the habituous hustles of his peers, as he states “I try to express the everyday tussles I witness, the stories I have are never ending”. Ian Banja is creating worlds within worlds through painting small windows as clues into his inner psyche. His upbeat street style paired with detailed technical and aesthetic consideration offers a glimpse into the future of the everyday inhabitants of Kenya."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013329002717 gid://shopify/Product/9013338865885 gid://shopify/Product/9013338898653

item.title: Ibrahim Khatab
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641413464285 Ibrahim Khatab gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640594264285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013325332701", "gid://shopify/Product/9013325463773", "gid://shopify/Product/9013326708957", "gid://shopify/Product/9013326872797", "gid://shopify/Product/9013327003869"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ibrahim Khatab was born in Cairo 1984, works as a co-teacher at Cairo University. He works across the mediums of painting, video art and installation. \\nKhatab has been practicing since his youth – when he was 12 years old, he created billboards on cloths and walls that were put up in the streets of Cairo. This experience at the beginning of his practice continues to influence his work and ignited his passion for the Arabic calligraphy which can consistently be seen reflected in his works. Since 2007, his work has been presented frequently in group shows and solo exhibitions. He has garnered notable recognition locally, exhibiting across various art centres and galleries in Cairo, but has seen impressive exposure abroad, having exhibited widely – from Sweden to Cape Town to Oman. \\nHe has regularly participated in the annual Youth Salon, Cairo, and has also led many workshops in Visual Arts Center, Oman; Fine Arts Association, Doha; and Sharjah Children Biennial (2013). He has been awarded various prizes for his work and in 2018, obtained his PhD from Cairo University. Khatab is currently resident in Cairo, Egypt and represented by Eclectica Contemporary in Southern Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013325332701 gid://shopify/Product/9013325463773 gid://shopify/Product/9013326708957 gid://shopify/Product/9013326807261 gid://shopify/Product/9013326872797 gid://shopify/Product/9013327003869

item.title: Idzila
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641416052957 Idzila gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640595673309 [] Discover Idzila's art, capturing African identity through reclaimed narratives and collective expression, symbolizing resilience against colonial erasure. Through printmaking, Idzila reclaims stolen stories, confronting the invisibility of Black artists in the art world. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As Idzila, their work captures the collective essence of African identity, shattered by colonial violence yet resilient through its people. African art's community-focused narrative has been twisted into erasure, leaving Black artists uncredited and dehumanized. Using African masks as a central motif, they symbolize presence and absence, hidden identities yet forcefully declared. Once sacred masks now sit in foreign museums, nameless and severed from their origins. \\n \\nThrough printmaking, Idzila reclaims these stolen stories, layering exploitation histories with acts of defiance, re-inscribing what was lost. Their art interrogates African art theft, systemic abuse of people of color, and the invisibility of Black bodies in the art world and beyond. \\nIdzila is a reflection, a mirror to history, reminding us that while they are one, they speak for many. Their art seeks revelation—of buried truths, silenced stories, and the forced anonymity of Black artists. Yet, truth endures. Through collective expression, we remember, reclaim, and resist."}]}]}

Telling us that he loves to tell stories that “reflect the passion and undying resilience of Nigerians to defy the odds and dream”, his work is a powerful means of rejecting and challenging stereotypes unjustly placed upon him and his fellow Nigerian citizens - itsnicethat.com"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013338931421

item.title: Ilan Godfrey
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641418477789 Ilan Godfrey 1537 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640596426973 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013271068893", "gid://shopify/Product/9013271101661", "gid://shopify/Product/9013271167197", "gid://shopify/Product/9013271462109", "gid://shopify/Product/9013271494877", "gid://shopify/Product/9013271527645", "gid://shopify/Product/9132521816285", "gid://shopify/Product/9132521849053", "gid://shopify/Product/9132521881821", "gid://shopify/Product/9132521947357", "gid://shopify/Product/9132521980125", "gid://shopify/Product/9133210960093", "gid://shopify/Product/9133211025629", "gid://shopify/Product/9133215416541", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221085405", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221150941", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221183709", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221249245", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221282013", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221380317", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221445853", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221478621", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221511389", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221544157", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221576925", "gid://shopify/Product/9133221675229", "gid://shopify/Product/9133222035677", "gid://shopify/Product/9133225214173"] [10857,10855,10856,10850,10861,10862,10848,10852,10853,10851,10849,10846,10847,10854,10843,10844,10863,10860,10864,10865,10845,10858,10859,10866,9654,9651,9646,9652,9649,9648,9653,9650,9647] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ilan Godfrey is a South African visual artist documenting the diverse social, political, economic and environmental currents that shape contemporary South Africa, giving viewers a broader, and at the same time, more deeply personal understanding of the country they live in but seldom truly gets to grips with. \\nFor eleven years he worked between Johannesburg and London before returning to South Africa in 2011 to focus on several long-term projects. One of which would evolve into the ‘Legacy of the Mine’. An unflinching series of images set out to expose the unwanted and perhaps under-explored legacy confronting South Africa’s land and people by giving agency to those whose lives and livelihoods have been destroyed by mining processes and the long-term environmental ramifications. \\nThis resulted in Ilan receiving the Ernest Cole Award in 2012. Legacy of the Mine (Jacana, 2013) was published as his first monograph and was launched in conjunction with solo exhibitions across South Africa. \\nIn 2016 he continued to explore South Africa’s extractive sector by collaborating with the Open Society Foundation to produce the seminal work, ‘The Platinum Belt’. This multifaceted project incorporates narrative sound, extensive writings and a geotagged online platform accessible to a global audience and in particular the local communities directly impacted by the platinum extractive sector. \\nIlan’s work has been recognized by numerous photography awards and grants here at home and abroad and exhibited in prestigious galleries and museums worldwide, including the National Portrait Gallery (London, UK), Iziko South African National Gallery (Cape Town, SA), Wits Art Museum (Johannesburg, SA), Musée du quai Branly (Paris, France), Everard Read Gallery (Johannesburg, SA) and most recently at the Völklinger Hütte World Heritage Site (Völklingen, Germany). Works from Ilan’s oeuvre are held in private and public collections globally. \\nHis writing and photographic documentation on issues related to mining, the South African landscape and its people have been cited in various research papers and his photographs are regularly published in a broad range of leading international publications including , The New Yorker, Le Monde Magazine, ZEIT Magazine, The Sunday Times Magazine, Guardian Weekend magazine and the Financial Times Magazine. Aside from his editorial work he collaborates with nstitutions and organizations worldwide, working on commissions for global brands. \\nHe holds a BA (Hons) degree in Photography from the University of Westminster in London, England and was awarded the David Faddy Scholarship to continue his studies, receiving an MA degree in Photojournalism"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013271068893 gid://shopify/Product/9013271101661 gid://shopify/Product/9013271167197 gid://shopify/Product/9013271298269 gid://shopify/Product/9013271396573 gid://shopify/Product/9013271462109 gid://shopify/Product/9013271494877 gid://shopify/Product/9013271527645 gid://shopify/Product/9132521816285 gid://shopify/Product/9132521849053 gid://shopify/Product/9132521881821 gid://shopify/Product/9132521947357 gid://shopify/Product/9132521980125 gid://shopify/Product/9133210960093 gid://shopify/Product/9133211025629 gid://shopify/Product/9133215416541 gid://shopify/Product/9133221085405 gid://shopify/Product/9133221150941 gid://shopify/Product/9133221183709 gid://shopify/Product/9133221249245 gid://shopify/Product/9133221282013 gid://shopify/Product/9133221380317 gid://shopify/Product/9133221445853 gid://shopify/Product/9133221478621 gid://shopify/Product/9133221511389 gid://shopify/Product/9133221544157 gid://shopify/Product/9133221576925 gid://shopify/Product/9133221675229 gid://shopify/Product/9133222035677 gid://shopify/Product/9133225214173

item.title: Ilana Seati
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641418150109 Ilana Seati gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640596558045 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ilana Seati is an established South African contemporary artist who creates figurative and abstract works that explore concepts of truth and fantasy. Seati was born in Israel and moved to South Africa in the eighties, where she continued her studies at the Bill Ainsley Johannesburg Art Foundation. \\nSeati only started focusing on her art career and exhibiting regularly after 2000. She has steadily built up her name in the South African art market, working with various galleries and showcasing many successful exhibitions, regularly selling out, one of them being the FNB Art Fair 2017.Her works have been collected by South Africa's top art investors, as well as international collectors and galleries in Europe and the US. \\nSeati paints mainly with oil and acrylic on canvas and Fabriano, but uses various other media such as charcoal, inktense, and has even produced sculptures and installation art. \\n'The manipulation of the human body has no specific connection to the real or fantasy world. What is real or fantasy is in the eye of the beholder. I use the form of the human body to communicate with the viewer. My art is a tool I use to express how I see the world and the uncertainty it represents. Through this communication, if it makes you feel something, can it possibly be a reality?' ~ Ilana Seati"}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641419002077 Ilene Bothma 871 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640596754653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014025847005","gid://shopify/Product/9014025879773"] Discover the work of Ilené Bothma, a South African artist known for her intimate explorations of family and the role of the mother. Bothma holds multiple degrees in Fine Art and has exhibited both locally and internationally. [22795,22796] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ilené Bothma (b. 1981, Port-Elizabeth) is a South African artist who holds a BA in Fine Art (with distinction) and an MA in Fine Art from Stellenbosch University, as well as second MA in Fine Art (with distinction) from Northumbria University in Newcastle-upon-Tyne, United Kingdom. Bothma's academic background has significantly influenced her artistic journey, providing a rich foundation and a diverse perspective on contemporary art practices. \\nBothma started exhibiting as a student and has consistently participated in group exhibitions since 2000, both locally and internationally. She has held six solo exhibitions and has been a finalist in competitions such as the Sasol New Signatures Competition, the Vuleka Art Competition, and the 2016 Barclays L’Atelier. \\nHer solo exhibition, Weird Marriage, at the AVA gallery, was praised by the Mail and Guardian as “a beautifully intimate exhibition about the culture of family” (17 May 2013). The role of the mother and the domestic sphere are significant themes in her art practice. \\nBothma lives and works in Cape Town with her husband and two children."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014025847005 gid://shopify/Product/9014025879773

item.title: Ilya Rabinovich
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641425752285 Ilya Rabinovich 2784 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640597704925 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014045835485","gid://shopify/Product/9014045868253","gid://shopify/Product/9014045966557","gid://shopify/Product/9014045999325","gid://shopify/Product/9014046032093","gid://shopify/Product/9014046097629","gid://shopify/Product/9014046130397","gid://shopify/Product/9014046163165"] Discover the works of Ilya Rabinovich, a typological photographer known for his Museutopia project, which examines ethnography and history museums in Moldova and Israel. With a detached documentary style, Rabinovich's photography explores the impact of historical narratives on contemporary identities. Exhibited internationally, Rabinovich also specializes in commissioned art documentation. [23451,23454,23448,23450,23449,23453,23455,23452] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ilya Rabinovich (b. 1965 in Kisheniev Moldova, U.S.S.R) is a distinguished typological photographer. Immigrating to Israel with his family in 1973, he earned his BFA in photography from the Bezalel Art and Design Academy in Jerusalem in 1994. From 1998 to 1999, Rabinovich was a participant in the prestigious Rijksakademie in Amsterdam and has resided there since. His work focuses on contextual and photographic research of ethnography and history museums, especially through his Museutopia project. \\n \\nThe first part of Museutopia was shot in Moldova, with the current focus on Israeli ethnography museums. His detached documentary style scrutinizes how historical narratives influence contemporary identities, exploring the formation of individual and collective memories, and the strategies employed by institutions to confront and reinterpret their contentious pasts to project a revered national identity. \\nRabinovich's works have been exhibited internationally in museums, galleries, and art centers. He also undertakes commissioned photography projects, specializing in documenting the art world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014045835485 gid://shopify/Product/9014045868253 gid://shopify/Product/9014045966557 gid://shopify/Product/9014045999325 gid://shopify/Product/9014046032093 gid://shopify/Product/9014046097629 gid://shopify/Product/9014046130397 gid://shopify/Product/9014046163165

item.title: Ilze Wessels
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641426735325 Ilze Wessels [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"My work founded itself in advocating for digital agency, as a result of lock down I was able to \\ntest these practices, where dreamy statements of a virtual space to realise place was made into \\nonline art activations and building worlds together across the globe. Wondering how might we \\n‘realise’ together when there is no togetherness remains the question? For architects the concept \\nof world building is not foreign, we do it daily, whether within the frameworks of softwares and \\nscreen or within the theoretical paragraphs of visionary paragraphs, the task remains building \\nyet with materials coming to exist to navigate and form this unfamiliar context. Introducing \\npeople through technology to the world of virtual prototype becomes method, validated by \\ncollaborations with African Reclaimers Organisation, The Goethe Institute, The Makers Valley \\nCollective within spatial contextual prototypes allowed for pivots towards The British Council and \\nD.A.A.D ‘s virtual space needs to establish connections and sustain alignments within a separated \\nplanetary bio-political world. \\nI currently run my own practice ‘is Sound Architecture and work within different educational \\ninstitutions, on-lining youth to Technologies of Architectural Design, Construction and Theory \\nof History and Interior Design. Research into Architectural Dialogue and Sound Practices via \\nCultural Networks with collaborators including iSUPPORT MUSIC, DINTHO OBJECTS, DRIP STUDIOS \\nand WOMBANIFEST continue work-shopping formats of incubation learning spaces for future \\nArchitects, Artists and Activists in this complex Post-pandemic planetary paradigm."}]}]}

item.title: Imile Wepener
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641427259613 Imile Wepener gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640597901533 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Imile Wepener is an artist and illustrator from Johannesburg, South Africa. \\n \\n \\n \\nImile earned a BA Honours in Visual Communication (specializing in Illustration) in 2015 from The Open Window Institute in Pretoria (one of his Honours projects even nabbing him a Loerie Award in 2016). While in High School, Imile was the apprentice of South African master puppeteer Toby van Eck, and added the skill of puppetry to his repertoire that also includes sculpture, animation and painting. \\n \\n? \\n \\nHe currently mostly works as a freelance illustrator, having created commercial illustrations for Standard Bank; Exclusive Books; PUMA; Motherland Coffee; Scholastic; Karen Zoid; Bouwer Bosch; Desmond and the Tutus; Shortstraw; Donna Magazine and many others, for which he was ranked #17th best illustrator in South Africa by the Loerie Awards and as one of 50 of the best Emerging Creatives by the Design Indaba."}]}]}

item.title: Immy Mali
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641428701405 Immy Mali 1939 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640597999837 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013393916125","gid://shopify/Product/9013394407645","gid://shopify/Product/9013394473181","gid://shopify/Product/9013394538717","gid://shopify/Product/9013394604253"] [13836,13837,13821,13839,13838] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Anderu Immaculate Mali a.k.a Immy Mali lives and works in Kampala Uganda. Using a variety of media including, text, video, sound, sculpture, installation, animation, her work attempts to unpack the complexities and entanglements of memory and existence in a neo/postcolonial Uganda. Notions of presence and absence, personal memories of childhood growing up in Uganda juxtaposed with current personal and collective experiences of existence in shifting spaces and places also influence her work. Her ongoing project Letters to my childhood (2017-present) accords her the duality to engage with her past and present simultaneously. \\nShe is a co-founder of Iraa-the granary an experimental artist’s kitchen geared towards exploring the possibility of creating archival/memory systems of artists’ work that is relevant to the African context. In 2013, she obtained her BA in Industrial and Fine Arts from Margaret Trowell School of Industrial and Fine arts, Makerere University, Kampala. She is an alumnus of the Rijksakademie van Beeldende Kunsten in Amsterdam, Netherlands (2018-2019). She has participated in exhibitions, residencies and workshops online and in various countries including Kenya, Netherlands, India, Ethiopia, Denmark, Germany, USA, South Africa, Mozambique, Angola, and Uganda. Her work has been published in art magazines including the Africa arts journal 2019. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013393916125 gid://shopify/Product/9013394407645 gid://shopify/Product/9013394473181 gid://shopify/Product/9013394538717 gid://shopify/Product/9013394604253

item.title: Inayah Essack
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641429782749 Inayah Essack gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640598196445 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Inayah Essack is an artist based in Cape Town, specialising primarily in charcoal drawing and with a penchant for collage and image manipulation. She received a Bachelor of Architectural Studies degree from the University of Cape Town and subsequently completed an internship at a local women-run practice centred on the empowerment of marginalised communities. Essack celebrates the intersection of a spatial practitioner in training and artist, mediating lived spatial experience and visual representation. This duality is highlighted through studies celebrating the human figure inhabiting and creating space, where bodies in harmony and conflict represent manifestations of internal dialogue. Through this she asks questions about perception, representation and spatial presence."}]}]}
