item.title: Ingrid Nuss
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641430634717 Ingrid Nuss 2785 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640598327517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014063562973","gid://shopify/Product/9014063595741","gid://shopify/Product/9014063628509"] ngrid Nuss is a South African visual artist whose work is deeply inspired by the natural beauty of the Garden Route. Drawing from her travels and interests in biology, philosophy, and spirituality, she expresses her innermost emotions through her artwork. [23930,23928,23929] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ingrid Nuss is a visual artist based in Wilderness, South Africa, often referred to as the ‘Heart of the Garden Route’. Her deep connection with nature was nurtured through family camping trips along the Cape and Namibia coasts, which sparked her lifelong love for the natural world and fueled her creative passions. From a young age, Ingrid was captivated by drawing and painting the things she loved, eventually honing her skills at the Jack Meyer Art Centre during her school years. \\n \\nIngrid graduated with distinction from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town (UCT) in 2007. Following her studies, Ingrid traveled extensively, working for one of the world's largest privately-owned art auction houses. Her travels took her to iconic locations such as New York, California, Hawaii, Alaska, and across much of the East and South, experiences that greatly influenced her perspectives and beliefs. Upon returning to South Africa, Ingrid found herself inspired by the Garden Route’s stunning landscape—its lush forests, untouched coastline, and towering mountains became her primary subject matter. \\nHer work is further informed by a fascination with biology, patterns, science, philosophy, and spirituality, which converge in her art to express her innermost emotions. Through her creations, Ingrid communicates her connection to the world around her and her own personal journey."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014063562973 gid://shopify/Product/9014063595741 gid://shopify/Product/9014063628509

item.title: Ingrid Uys
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641430700253 Ingrid Uys 1574 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640598425821 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013937504477","gid://shopify/Product/9013937537245"] [19672,19668] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ingrid E Uys was born in 1985 in Ermelo, Mpumalanga, and currently lives in Johannesburg with her husband and three children. Growing up in small towns like Ermelo, Kroonstad, Clarens, and Harrismith, she spent most of her childhood days painting and drawing the world around her. Her exposure to nature, open spaces, different places and people nurtured a curiosity in the world around her, and making drawings and paintings have always been a way to collect those moments and memories, expressing herself and her thoughts. After years of art classes in different studios in different towns, Ingrid Uys completed her BA Fine Art Degree in 2007 at the University of Pretoria, specializing in oil painting under the tutorage of Diane Victor, Philip Badenhorst, and Rina Stutzer. Ingrid had her first solo exhibition in 2016 at Halifax Art Gallery in Johannesburg, with Diane Victor as the opening speaker. Following with a number of solo and duo exhibitions at The White River Gallery. She has been part of numerous group exhibitions since then at various spaces, introduced at Turbine Art Fair 2018 with the White River Gallery, and rep-resented there every year since. Ingrid has donated work to be auctioned at charity exhibitions for the likes of Surgeons for Little Lives, and Goldi-locks and the Bear Foundation. Her work is currently part of numerous international collections of note, private and corporate.Ingrid Uys has become known for her detailed paintings and drawings depicting birds in flight. This series of work has developed significantly since her first solo exhibition with Halifax Art, “This Fleeting Forever”. Her fascination with Fleeting Time, Fragility and Impermanence is still a major theme in her work, and her recent collections have become more focused on the Hummingbird species as a metaphor for “Capturing Moments”.Hummingbirds are highly sensitive to stimuli in their visual fields, responding to even minimal motion in any direction by reorienting themselves in mid flight. Hummingbirds’ visual sensitivity allows them to precisely hover in place while in complex and dynamic natural environment. This gives an illusion of a moment frozen in time, and the artist depicts this unique characteristic and ability in her work to explore the fragility of time. The Hummingbird also represents the artist in this way: responding to the changes in our visual world, redirecting ourselves to focus and hover and explore and express.Uys urges the viewer to think about the great importance and fragile nature of time, to experience the present, and notice the delicate beauty of the impermanent world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013937504477 gid://shopify/Product/9013937537245

item.title: Irma Stern
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641431421149 Irma Stern gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640598851805 [] Irma Stern {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"After studying in Germany in the 1910s, Irma Stern was a true pioneer of modernist Expressionism in South Africa. Initially derided for her innovative style, she gained widespread recognition after the Empire Exhibition of 1936. She travelled extensively throughout Africa, searching for exotic models to paint. Her golden period is bookended by her visits to Zanzibar (in 1939 and again in 1945). She published two travelogues, Congo (1945) and Zanzibar (1948). In the 1950s and 60s she gained international recognition, participating in numerous Venice Biennales and receiving the Guggenheim Award in 1961. Stern’s joyous use of bright, expressive colour is particularly evident in her many still-life paintings."}]}]}

item.title: Isaac Ntwayagae Chibua
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641433977053 Isaac Ntwayagae Chibua 1937 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640599638237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013387493597", "gid://shopify/Product/9013387657437"] [13615,13614,13613] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Serowe, Botswana, Isaac Ntwayagae Chibua is a semi-realist, abstract and figurative painter, and sculptor. He holds an Associate Degree in Fine Art from the Limkokwing University of Creative Technology with distinction. He is currently a 3rd year Bachelor of Education student in Art and Design at the University of Botswana. He has an honorary Diploma in sculpture from Changchun International Sculpture Symposium, Changchun, China. Chibua spent most of his career as a self–taught and full-time artist. \\n \\nHe incorporates a lot of texture in his work to convey messages and bring richness to his art practice. He tackles a range of social issues and different life experiences. Rusty found materials are prevalent in his work to symbolise and make commentary on the scars of life, from emotional to socio-economic conditions. In his sculptural work he works with recycled materials from scrap yards, both a metaphor for society as he sees it, and also as his contribution towards an environmentally conscious practice. Color is one of the important elements for Chibua when making artwork, meant to break the dullness of his artworks; art after all is therapy, and color contributes to that. He currently feels something in the direction his art practice is about to take a spiritual artistic compass and seems to be proposing a new narrative. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013387493597 gid://shopify/Product/9013387657437 gid://shopify/Product/9013387821277

item.title: Isabella Chydenius
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641435484381 Isabella Chydenius gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640600293597 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Isabella Chydenius (b.1988) is a Finnish interdisciplinary artist based in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nChydenius is currently studying a Master of Fine Art degree at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. Her research-based work focuses on investigating societal structures of femininity, gender and safety/violence. She is interested in the behavioural social constructs behind what constitutes as feminine and masculine in contemporary patriarchal time. \\nHer interdisciplinary conceptual work combines technologies such as light, sound, videography and interactive animation to create experiential installations. She also works with more traditional mediums like textiles, thread, clay, painting and found objects which she uses to form sculptural installations or audience activated compositions."}]}]}

item.title: Isaac Zavale
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641434566877 Isaac Zavale 499 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640599867613 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013286961373","gid://shopify/Product/9013286994141"] [3523,3522] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Isaac Zavale (b. 1987) is a Mozambican fine artist, muralist and co-founder of Prints on Paper Studio. He graduated from Artist Proof Studio and currently lives and works in Johannesburg. \\nZavale has been curating his own group shows and printmaking workshops since 2011. From 2013 Isaac has been working hand in hand with his at partner at Alphabet Zoo Collective, Minenkulu Ngoyi, running zine and printmaking projects throughout the country. His background in mural painting and signwriting is evident in his recent bodies of work, mostly consisting of inner-city landscapes that depict honest and sometimes naive representations of Johannesburg street scenes. \\nZavale has participated in numerous group exhibitions locally and internationally. In 2015 he and Minenkulu Ngoyi were invited to be guest lecturers for 3rd-year students for alternative printmaking, zine-making and bookbinding courses at the University of Witwatersrand. Zavale's work is about the social and political issues in Johannesburg and Africa seen through the lens of a Mozambican immigrant."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013286961373 gid://shopify/Product/9013286994141

item.title: Isabella Maake
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641438925021 Isabella Maake 2564 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640601768157 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013979545821","gid://shopify/Product/9013979611357","gid://shopify/Product/9013979676893","gid://shopify/Product/9013979709661","gid://shopify/Product/9013979742429","gid://shopify/Product/9013979775197","gid://shopify/Product/9013979873501","gid://shopify/Product/9013979971805","gid://shopify/Product/9013980037341","gid://shopify/Product/9013980102877","gid://shopify/Product/9013980233949","gid://shopify/Product/9013981216989","gid://shopify/Product/9013981249757","gid://shopify/Product/9014106849501"] [21039,21015,21017,21014,21027,21019,21021,21022,21026,21016,21023,21024,21038] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Isabella Maake is a contemporary visual artist from South Africa. Living with profound hearing loss from a young age, she has used art as a medium of expression and dreamed of becoming a full-time artist.After completing her undergraduate degree in Graphic Design, she went on to work as a graphic journalist for Media24, where she won several Standard Bank Sikuvile Journalism Awards, including Upcoming/Rising Star of the Year in 2017 and Graphic Journalist of the Year in 2020. \\n \\nIsabella's art is deeply personal and explores themes of identity, dualism, and vulnerability– mostly depicted through portraiture and figurative art. As an artist who is deaf, she draws inspiration from the conceptual state of ‘in-betweenness’ and the possibilities that can exist between two contradictory things such as, black and white; past and present; hearing and deaf; and so on. Her subjects are usually people, as she believes each person contains an entire universe and is fascinated by the stories that lie within. As a multidisciplinary artist working primarily in paint, Isabella is driven by the desire to push the boundaries of traditional art forms by experimenting with different mediums and techniques which include painting, photography, sculpture, and interactive sound installations. She hopes to spotlight the beauty of human complexity and the interconnections we can forge despite perceived barriers. \\n \\nIsabella's artworks have been exhibited in group exhibitions at the 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair in London, and in her hometown of Polokwane, South Africa. In 2023, she was selected as a recipient of the prestigious Chevening leadership scholarship and is currently pursuing her master’s degree in Fine Art in Oxford, England."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013979545821 gid://shopify/Product/9013979611357 gid://shopify/Product/9013979676893 gid://shopify/Product/9013979709661 gid://shopify/Product/9013979742429 gid://shopify/Product/9013979775197 gid://shopify/Product/9013979873501 gid://shopify/Product/9013979971805 gid://shopify/Product/9013980037341 gid://shopify/Product/9013980102877 gid://shopify/Product/9013980233949 gid://shopify/Product/9013981216989 gid://shopify/Product/9013981249757 gid://shopify/Product/9014106849501

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641447182557 Jabulani Dhlamini gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640603406557 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jabulani Dhlamini (b. 1983, Free State, South Africa) lives and works in Johannesburg. Dhlamini majored in documentary photography at the Vaal University of Technology, graduating in 2010. \\nHe is an alumni fellow of the Edward Ruiz Mentorship programme and the Market Photo Workshop in Johannesburg. His work focuses on his upbringing while also reflecting on various communities within contemporary South Africa. \\nDhlamini’s approach is meditative and subtly provokes a closer look at what lies on the edges through an exploration of personal and collective memory. item.title: Jacki McInnes

With a BA(FA) from UNISA and an MFA from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, McInnes has received numerous accolades and is featured in collections both in South Africa and abroad. She currently resides in Cape Town and works between Cape Town and Johannesburg. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jacki McInnes (b. 1966) is a South African artist, arts writer, and curator. She earned her BA(FA) with distinction from UNISA in 2001 where she also received the UNISA Fine Art Faculty Medal. She completed an MFA at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, UCT in 2004 and is currently a PhD candidate (Creative Research) at the Wits School of the Arts, University of Witwatersrand. McInnes resides in Cape Town and works between Cape Town and Johannesburg. \\n \\nMcInnes has received numerous accolades, including the Mixed Media category prize at the M-Web New Signatures Competition in 2000, a National Arts Council scholarship in 2003, and the Pro Helvetia Arts Council of Switzerland Artist’s Residency program in 2004. She won the Sacatar-Spier Contemporary Fellowship Award in 2010. In 2011, McInnes, in collaboration with filmmaker Peter Goldsmid, was a finalist in the inaugural Johannesburg GoodPitch² Documentary Film-making Competition. She also received the Kunstraum Sylt Artist’s Residency award in 2012. Her work is featured in various public and private collections, both in South Africa and internationally. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Jaco Benade
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641452458205 Jaco Benade 990 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640605602013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013362884829"] Explore the evocative paintings of South African artist Jaco Benade, known for his sensitive portraits and intricate landscapes. His artworks blend Classical and Contemporary styles, capturing nostalgia and the richness of human experiences. Buy original art online, available now. [11743] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jaco Benade (b. 1964, South Africa) is a distinguished artist renowned for his sensitive portraits and landscapes studies, which has been creating since 1996. His works are highly sought-after, not only for their visual beauty but also for their artistic finesse. Benade's painting often evoke a sense of nostalgia, portraying individuals he knew, emotions he experienced, and possessions he cherished. \\nThrough radiant portraits and intricate tapestries of flowers and broken objects, Benade masterfully captures the diversity and complexity of human experiences, blending randomness and richness within his artisty \\nBenade's artistic journey explores the intersection between Classical and Contemporary art. He skillfully combines classical techniques with modern composition and subject matter, resulting in works that often convey a disjointed nostalgia or melancholy. His art ventures into the shadows of life, with a touch of restraint, leaving space for the viewer's imagination. \\nJaco Benade's work has been showcased in numerous solo exhibitions and has been featured in key galleries and museums such as the Pretoria Arts Association. His works have been offered at auction multiple times, with realized prices ranging from 20 USD to 2,394 USD. The record price for his artwork was achieved in 2022 at Strauss & Co., Cape Town, for Red String Head with a Hat. \\nOperating from his studio, Benade continues to produce works that reflect his passion for art and his dedication to capturing the essence of human experience through his unique artistic vision."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013362884829

item.title: Jaco Sieberhagen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641454194909 Jaco Sieberhagen gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640606650589 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jaco Sieberhagen is well established within the South African art industry and is currently based in Onrus. He holds a BA degree from the University of Port Elizabeth, a BTh from the University of Stellenbosch and was an occasional student in sculpture under Prof. Jos Nell at Rhodes University. Sieberhagen has taken part in numerous local and international exhibitions and has had 15 solo exhibitions. \\n \\nMonumental sculptures of the artist are in sculpture parks and office buildings as far afield as England, India, China, Australia, Switzerland, Holland and Taiwan, but he has also done large works in SA for Hollards Head Offices in Johannesburg, Cape Gate Head Offices in Vanderbijlpark , Q-square in Worcester, Jan Marais Nature Reserve, Stellenbosch and Leeu Collection in Franschhoek to name but a few. \\n \\nFurthermore his works are in private collection all over the world and has already been incorporated in 28 corporate collections, including The South African Constitutional Court, Development Bank of South Africa, University of Stellenbosch, Cell-C, Sasol, RMB and Sanlam."}]}]}

item.title: Jaco Boëttger
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641453048029 Jaco Boëttger gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640605667549 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jaco Boëttger is a Change Management, Leadership and Organisation Development consultant, with 3 decades of experience. His main focus is on helping organisations and individuals to manage change, optimize the opportunities it presents, and make it work for them. He worked in approximately 28 countries and his “Preparing for Tomorrow” intervention on Future Fitness has been implemented in 40+ countries around the globe. He is the author of five books. His latest book “The Engagement Alphabet” is all about boundaries and taking control of one’s life. \\n \\nHis latest endeavour is to explore the opportunities and possibilities that a crisis can trigger. He uses art as an analogy and example of how we can creatively fill the space opened by a catastrophic event. His own journey is utilised to illustrate that we can choose to use a crisis to reinvent ourselves and to rediscover our latent creative energy...to realign who we are with what we do. He works from the Kouebokkeveld in The Ceres Karoo where he uses material from the local environment to create his Karoo Creatures."}]}]}

item.title: Jaco Van Schalkwyk
item.description: Jaco Van Schalkwyk 1816 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640607600861 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014138372317","gid://shopify/Product/9014138437853","gid://shopify/Product/9014138470621","gid://shopify/Product/9014138798301","gid://shopify/Product/9014139224285"] Discover Jaco van Schalkwyk, a South African artist (b. 1981) challenging notions of paradise through symbolic landscapes. His work, addressing climate change and nature's abuse, is found in prominent collections and has been shown globally. [25263,25264,25265,25266,25262,25255] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Benoni, South Africa, in 1981, Jaco van Schalkwyk grew up within the unique environment of the Latter Rain Mission International headquarters. He holds a BA degree in Historical Studies from UNISA and currently lives in Randburg. \\nSince his acclaimed 2015 solo exhibition, \"Eden,\" at the Barnard Gallery in Cape Town, Van Schalkwyk's artistic focus has centered on the symbolism of forests, islands, and the concept of the exotic. Moving beyond superficial beauty, he challenges the Western notion of \"Utopia\" or \"Paradise\" being found solely in pristine landscapes or \"the other.\" His contemporary vistas, reminiscent of Romantic landscape painting, use metaphor and symbolism to imbue moral significance into the cycles of growth and decomposition in nature. Through his work, Van Schalkwyk addresses pressing issues such as human abuse of the natural world and the escalating threat of climate change, revealing how the very nature once celebrated as a refuge is now neglected and endangered. \\nVan Schalkwyk's work has been showcased in numerous exhibitions both in South Africa and internationally. His art is represented in several prominent collections, including the Reserve Bank of South Africa, Absa Bank, RMB, the University of Pretoria, the University of Johannesburg, the Pretoria Art Museum, and the Ellerman Collection. The Barnard Gallery has successfully hosted five of his solo exhibitions: \"Just a matter of Time\" (2012), \"I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things\" (2013), \"Eden\" (2015), \"-arium\" (2017), and \"Smoke and Mirrors\" (2021). His work was also featured in the 2019 three-person exhibition \"A Land I Name Yesterday.\" Additionally, the Barnard Gallery presented his solo projects \"Arcadia\" at the 2016 FNB Joburg Art Fair and \"Nemora\" at the 2018 Volta Art Fair in Basel, Switzerland. \\n \\nHis talent has been recognized with significant accolades, including the Sylt Foundation Artist residency at the 2013 Absa L’Atelier Art Competition. Since then, he has participated in several international projects facilitated by the Foundation. In 2015, the University of Johannesburg selected him to represent South Africa at the 6th International Beijing Biennale in China, where his work was part of the \"20 – Art in the time of Democracy\" group exhibition."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014138372317 gid://shopify/Product/9014138437853 gid://shopify/Product/9014138470621 gid://shopify/Product/9014138798301 gid://shopify/Product/9014139224285

item.title: Jacob Hendrik Pierneef
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641451606237 Jacob Hendrik Pierneef gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640607699165 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jacob Hendrik Pierneef, born on the Highveld in 1886, is perhaps South Africa’s most iconic landscape painter. Having developed an unmistakable and economical aesthetic during the first half of the twentieth century, his pictures, whether described as startlingly beautiful, willingly experimental, nostalgic, or gently monumental, are familiar to generations of South Africans. Enormously prolific, the artist was equally comfortable working in oils, gouache, watercolour and casein, while the prints he produced, both linocuts and etchings, remain as influential as they are collectable. \\n \\nIt goes without saying that Pierneef has attracted attention from eminent art historians and critics; thanks to the emotive charge of his pictures, and the historical context in which they were produced, his career has been widely discussed in socio-political terms too. A recent, major retrospective at the Standard Bank Gallery – curated by Strauss & Co’s Wilhelm van Rensburg – has shed a new light on the artist’s imagination, range and decorative appeal, and sealed his position as one of the country’s masters."}]}]}

item.title: Jake Aikman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641454915805 Jake Aikman 1590 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640608649437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013352300765"] [10491] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jake Aikman was born in London in 1978 and lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. He obtained his Masters of Fine Arts in 2008 from the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, after completing his Bachelor of Fine Arts in 2005. Aikman had his first solo exhibition This Must Be The Place in 2006. Since then, he has presented five solo exhibitions including Echoes in 2009, Proximity in 2011, and At the Quiet Limit in 2013 at SMAC Gallery. His solo exhibition ConfiniVelati/Veiled Boundaries was presented in 2014 in Rome following a residency in Trevignano Romano in Italy, which was facilitated by the Centro Luigi Di Sarro. \\nIn 2009, Aikman exhibited in L’Anima Del Acqua: The Spirit of Water an exhibition presented as part of the 53rd Venice Biennale. He was also an invited artist for the 4th Beijing International Art Biennale and exhibited in Paralleli, an official exhibition to the 2nd Sabbioneta Biennale in 2010, and the Olympic Fine Arts exhibition Creative Cities Collection that was held at the Barbican Centre in London in 2012. \\nJake Aikman presented Vestiges a solo show with Suburbia Contemporary in Granada, Spain in May 2018. In the following two years, Aikman participated in the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, South Africa, and Future Fair New York, New York, USA both in 2020, a solo presentation at Arte Fiera Bologna, Italy in 2019, as well as Art Verona also in 2019 and The Others Art Fair, Turin, Italy in 2018, all with Suburbia Contemporary."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013352300765

item.title: Jake Michael Singer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641456062685 Jake Michael Singer 427 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640608714973 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014058549469"] [23789] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jake Michael Singer (b.1991, Cape Town) is a South African multidisciplinary artist renowned for his mastery in sculpture, photography, and works on paper. He earned his Bachelor of Fine Arts from Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town in 2013, after expanding his artistic knowledge Central Saint Martins, London in 2012. Since then Singer's dynamic practice has spanned various media, showcasing his exceptional skill and conceptual depth. \\n \\nSinger's work, often exploring themes of identity, materiality, and human experience, has been featured in major global art fairs, solo exhibitions across Europe, America, and Africa, and more than 60 group shows. His prominent public sculpture, Dawn Chorus, is displayed at the iconic W+A building in Johannesburg, while his monumental installation And All Birds Flew With a Harsh Scream (Marmara) was part of the Materiality exhibition at the Iziko South African National Gallery. His works are housed in collections both locally and internationally, and he has received notable recognition through grants, residencies, and exhibitions. \\n \\nHighlighted Shows \\n \\n2019: In Murmurs, THK Gallery, Cape Town \\n2019: Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, Matter Gallery \\n2018: But A Storm Is Blowing From Paradise, Matter Gallery, Toronto \\n2017: Pale Stability, Punt WG, Amsterdam \\n2017: RGB Sky, Hazard Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2017: Nest Collective and Jake Michael Singer, Matter Gallery, Toronto \\n2017: No Longer and Not Yet, 50 Golbourne Gallery: Lagos X Johannesburg with Olalekan Jeyifous, London \\n2016: Catastrophes, Hazard Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2013: Vestiges of Development, Michaelis Grad Show, Cape Town \\n \\n \\nGroup Shows \\n \\n2020: Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town \\n2020: Matereality, Iziko South African National Gallery, Cape Town \\n2020: Between the Lines, THK Gallery, Cape Town \\n 2019: The Main Complaint, Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town \\n2019: Contemporary Istanbul art fair, THK Gallery, Istanbul \\n2019: Also Known As Africa (AKAA) art fair, THK Gallery, Paris \\n2019: Cologne Fine Art & Design, THK Gallery, Cologne \\n2018: Kampala Biennale curated by Simon Njami Kampala \\n2018: Triptych, Matter Gallery, Toronto \\n2018: Talking To Dear Ears, Absa Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2017: AKAA, Also Known As Africa, Art Intelligence, Paris \\n2017: Occupy I, Fried Contemporary, Pretoria \\n2017: Urban Axis, Another Antipodes, Perth \\n2017: Cape Town Art Fair, Hazard Gallery, Cape Town \\n2017: A Flagrant Arcade, Art Africa Fair, Cape Town \\n2017: Whats In It For You? No End Gallery, Johannesburg \\n 2016: I Never Read, Alma Martha, Basel \\n2016: Suba Biennale, Dak’art Off, Dakar \\n2016: Also Known As Africa (AKAA) art fair, Paris, Hazard Gallery \\n2016: FNB Joburg Art Fair, Johannesburg \\n2016: False Idols, Twilsharpe Studios, Johannesburg \\n2016: Young Art Virtuoso, August House, Johannesburg \\n2016: Turbine Art Fair, No End Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2016: Actresses, an adaption of Chekov’s Seagull, Grahamstown Arts Festival \\n2016: August House, Hazard Gallery, Johannesburg \\n 2015: Arte Lima, Psh Projects, Lima \\n2015: Nirox Sculpture Fair, Cradle of Humankind \\n2015:Grid Cape Town Biennale, Cape Town \\n2015:Transitions at the Post Office, Johannesburg \\n2015: Public Sculpture, Arts on Main, curated by Parts and Labour, Johannesburg \\n2015:Africa Future Now, Hazard Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2014: Electron Salon, LACDA, Los Angeles \\n2014: Morphos Sustainable Empires, Venice \\n2014: Emerge Art Fair, Washington DC \\n2014: Play, Nirox Sculpture Park, Cradle of Humankind \\n2014: Fete, an Art Show, curated by Martha Collective, Johannesburg \\n2014: Nirox Sculpture, Cradle of Humankind \\n2014: Cubicle, Infecting the City, Cape Town \\n2014: Greatest Hits, Industrial Harvest, Ava Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\n2013: Two Weeks Notice, Cape Town \\n2014: Platform 18-28, Infecting the City, Cape Town \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014058549469

item.title: Jakinda Mshindi Boya
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641458749661 Jakinda Mshindi Boya gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609009885 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"My practice explores the historical underrepresentation and misrepresentation of black people in contemporary art as well as popular culture. I seek to portray the many facets of the black experience, normalizing a nuanced perception of blackness in contrast to the often stereotypical/one dimensional perceptions promoted in the media. I use my own life experiences as a black man born and raised in Johannesburg to represent my perception of blackness, its complexity and its beauty. As a result, the current phase of my work primarily focuses on black men. I explore my ideas through the centuries old practice of portraiture, focusing on individuals and exploring how these nuanced identities are often expressed through the way they dress, the hairstyles they choose etc. Through these choices I believe people form the \"characters\" they want to be in life and thus my style is largely based on stylized character based portraits. I'm inspired by the idea that in reality we are all \"performing\" who we are through the various roles that we play in life and we become identifiable through the way we choose to express ourselves. So much so that in some cases we create a sort of uniform that classes us amongst our peers. I have recently explored these uniform motifs through football jerseys and how football is a form of escapism for black people. This idea of escapism is also tied in with spirituality and how certain football players are viewed as \"godly\". These football jerseys then become a symbol of one imagining themselves as this godly/hero figure, rising above challenges (as black people often have to do more than any other race). Through these motifs and symbols I aim to express multiple sides of blackness, touching on black masculinity, black joy, struggle and resilience. My medium of choice is oil on canvas, subverting its white male dominated history and using it as a trojan horse to tell black stories in white spaces. My style is deliberately \"unacademic\" in an attempt to create a more pop culture influenced style that is more identifiable with the average black person. I don't want my work to be \"over-intellectualized\", as the art world often feels, because that then because a form of alienating those who are not part of the formal institutions and more often than not those people are black.?"}]}]}

item.title: Jamal Nxedlana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641459273949 Jamal Nxedlana gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609042653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013949595869","gid://shopify/Product/9013949628637","gid://shopify/Product/9013949694173","gid://shopify/Product/9013949726941","gid://shopify/Product/9013949792477","gid://shopify/Product/9013949825245","gid://shopify/Product/9013949858013"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jamal Nxedlana (b. 1985 Durban, South Africa; lives Johannesburg, South Africa) is an artist and cultural worker. His practice explores how the Black figure is materially and symbolically embodied and embraced; and themes related to subcultures, consumerism, and racialized and gendered identity expressions in postcolonial contexts. Specifically, he is concerned with fashion as a domain of intellectual and cultural inquiry, explored through individual and collective cultural identities in the Johannesburg metropolis as they intersect with geopolitical practices, technologies and infrastructural logistics. He has exhibited internationally in galleries, institutions, and independent spaces. Recent exhibitions include SPECTRUM (2023), his second solo exhibition at No Man’s Art Gallery in Amsterdam; Orlando (2022) curated by Tilda Swinton at the Fotomuseum Winterthur, Switzerland; and The New Black Vanguard (2019) curated by Antwaun Sargent at Aperture Gallery in New York. \\n \\nAs a cultural worker, Nxedlana has founded numerous influential independent organisations in Johannesburg where he was based for 14 years before moving to Switzerland. Key among these is Bubblegum Club, a digital platform and culture agency showcasing innovative new work and creating opportunities for emerging cultural workers. He is also a founding member of CUSS Group, a Johannesburg-based collective that has been exploring the hybrid culture of post-colonial South Africa since 2011. CUSS has shown in major institutions including Kunsthall Trondheim Norway (2023), Moderna Museet Stockholm (2019); de Young Museum (2017) and Berlin Biennale (2016)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013949595869 gid://shopify/Product/9013949628637 gid://shopify/Product/9013949694173 gid://shopify/Product/9013949726941 gid://shopify/Product/9013949792477 gid://shopify/Product/9013949825245 gid://shopify/Product/9013949858013

item.title: James De Villiers
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641460420829 James De Villiers 1688 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609108189 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355708637","gid://shopify/Product/9013376090333"] [12951,11144] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"James de Villiers, based in Johannesburg, is a mainly self-taught artist having undergone periods of art studies at Unisa and the Free State Technicon in the 1970s. He has a background as a retail display artist, advertising, magazine, book and graphic designer, illustrator, theatrical props maker, DJ, electronic music experimentalist and newspaper infographic artist. \\n \\nDuring this time, he was also an active fine artist and ran several of his own experimental galleries. In 2014 de Villiers started doing his own art on a full-time basis. He works with realism and abstraction creating mixed media drawings, oil and acrylic paintings and silkscreened artworks. His works are in many collections in South Africa and abroad. \\n \\nDe Villier's work is a meditation on the state of nature, its decay and regeneration, ecology and \"making the invisible forces of nature visible\". He is equally inspired by the growth and decay of plants in a garden and the discoveries of the James Webb Telescope and the Large Hadron Collider. His art is greatly inspired by William Blake: \\n \\n\"To see a World in a Grain of Sand \\nAnd a Heaven in a Wild Flower, \\nHold Infinity in the palm of your hand \\nAnd Eternity in an hour.\""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013355708637 gid://shopify/Product/9013376090333

item.title: James Thomas
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641460748509 James Thomas 2832 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609435869 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014057566429"] Discover James Thomas, a Johannesburg artist whose mixed-media works reflect urban dualities through found materials, expressive text, and bold color. Explore his solo and group exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [23756] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"James Thomas (b.1996) is a visual artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. He works in a range of mediums - oil paint, acrylic, pastel and charcoal on canvas and found objects salvaged from the street .The artist has spent intimate time as a skateboarder on the streets of the inner-city since the age of eleven. This gave him a unique and nuanced view of the visual, socio-political and ambient landscape of the metropolis. An interest in documenting his experiences in the city developed into an obsession as he began to work in various downtown clubs and bars. What began as writing, became drawing and eventually gave way to large-scale paintings. \\nThrough these experiences Thomas has created art with a journalistic approach. He captures, anecdotally and personally, what it means to live in Johannesburg in the 21st century. The work draws from the nature of city: Organized chaos. Words are scrawled on the canvas as if a store front or bus stop. The colours are harsh and monochromatic and then colourful and vibrant. The harsh dualities present in the city are emphasized by contrasting elements of abstraction and realism. The compositions are at odds with one another and in a state of harmony simultaneously."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014057566429

item.title: James Webb
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641461960925 James Webb gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609632477 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"James Webb (b. 1975) is based in Cape Town, South Africa. \\n \\nOne of the most unique collaborations in this portfolio is Webb’s print You, the Collector, editioned by Genevieve Wood – who also worked with Cameron Platter on his edition for ArtThrob. Webb’s practice is characterised by a ‘strategic conceptualism’ that rarely involves the production of an actual art object. His sensibility is one that seeks to engage site and audience with both the tangible and intangible, seen and unseen, and this print – although an object – is no exception. \\n \\nYou, the Collector is a rarely seen paper multiple produced in the path of Hurricane Irene at Dieu Donné Papermill in Hells Kitchen, New York City. Embedded in the paper is a traditional relief watermark in Cochin font produced on a Timothy Moore wove papermaking mould, in archival cotton and Philippine Abaca fibre, with titanium white pigment. \\n \\nThe watermark reads: ONCE ALL MULTIPLES IN THIS EDITION HAVE BEEN DESTROYED BY FIRE, EACH COLLECTOR WILL BE RELIEVED OF A SINGLE PAINFUL MEMORY. EXHIBITION OR STORAGE WILL BRING GRAVE MISFORTUNE TO YOU, THE COLLECTOR. \\n \\nThe edition was signed by the artist on the full moon of September in Cape Town when the moon was in the House of Pisces."}]}]}

item.title: James Delaney
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641459765469 James Delaney 1410 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640609239261 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013405548765","gid://shopify/Product/9013405614301","gid://shopify/Product/9013405647069","gid://shopify/Product/9013405712605","gid://shopify/Product/9013405745373","gid://shopify/Product/9014114779357"] [14584,14588,14585,25125,14586,14587] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"JAMES DELANEY (1971 -) \\n \\nJames Delaney is a contemporary painter, printmaker and sculptor. He’s best known for his laser-cut metal sculptures. His artmaking process has led him to study Johannesburg’s history, architecture and public art and this often serves as an inspiration for his work. “My work deals with relationships between people and nature and the history surrounding us. I’m interested in reference to the things which were here before us – often unnoticed by most – and those that will outlast us.” \\n \\nBorn in Cape Town, Delaney currently works from a studio in Victoria Yards, near downtown Johannesburg, South Africa. He studied at the University of Cape Town. Delaney was one of the winners of the 2018 SAIA Award for Sustainable Architecture and Innovation. In 2019, he won a BASA (Business Arts South Africa) Award for his sculptures installed in The Wilds – a previously neglected park which he is rehabilitating. Delaney has participated in over 20 solo and group exhibitions in South Africa and abroad. His most recent group exhibition being held in 2020 at Galerie Osenat, Paris. Delaney’s work is included in several local and international collections."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013405548765 gid://shopify/Product/9013405614301 gid://shopify/Product/9013405647069 gid://shopify/Product/9013405712605 gid://shopify/Product/9013405745373 gid://shopify/Product/9014114779357

item.title: Jamil Parasol
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641462288605 Jamil Parasol gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640610943197 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jamil Osmar Ramos (Parasol) is an Angolan curator, artist and game developer who graduated from LISAA University, one of the best video game development schools in France. With his unique approach to art, great creativity and knowledge, he worked with and for various artists and galleries in Luanda. He also teaches people to develop their artistic skills beyond technique, curates exhibitions like Hypnosis by Jahmek contemporary arts and was a fellow in the Arak fellowship program. He works on the artistic growth of Angola, by helping artists and creating works of art about the Self and the Being, deconstructing different aspects of modern societies, especially Angolan, challenging the observer to meditate and question his own existence, while using found objects and recycling as a way to tell stories and bring awareness on the global environmental damage we are currently causing. Now, he is working as a curator at This Is Not A White Cube Art Gallery in Luanda. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Jan-Henri Booyens
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641462419677 Jan-Henri Booyens gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640615268573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013367996637","gid://shopify/Product/9013368127709"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Johannesburg in 1980, Jan-Henri Booyens lives and works in Cape Town. He studied at the Durban Institute of Technology and the Gerrit Rietveld Academie voor Beeldende Kunsten in Amsterdam, and has taught in the Visual Arts Department at the University of Stellenbosch. Booyens was one-third of the infamous artist collective Avant Car Guard and his work is part of numerous collections, including the Cartier Foundation for Contemporary Art in Paris. \\n \\nBooyens' work is often described in terms of a struggle between the representational and abstract, the rational and chaotic. His affinity and critical engagement with Modernism is coupled with his relationship to the South African landscape, both physical and social, manifesting in an intuitive, texture-rich layering of oil paint on canvas and a bold use of colour and line."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013367996637 gid://shopify/Product/9013368127709

item.title: Jan Maanda Tshikhuthula
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641475657949 Jan Maanda Tshikhuthula 860 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640611664093 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013407809757","gid://shopify/Product/9013407842525","gid://shopify/Product/9013408104669"] [14697,14698,14699] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jan Maanda Tshikhuthula was born in Tzaneen, but he spent school holidays in Venda when he was young. Most mornings he would wake up early to go and collect water. This was an activity that brought him a lot of joy. The journey to the water took him and his family through the forest and the richness and beauty of the landscape was exciting to him as a boy. Too young to be able to think about the people who lived there permanently - he had no way of knowing what a struggle fetching water was for them. For him, the young child, fetching water was such a common part of the life he knew then he couldn’t see anything unusual about it. \\n \\nNow, living as an adult in Johannesburg, water is a big issue. People across the country cry about water shortages, and we know there are more shortages coming, reminding him of the people back in Limpopo. Their struggle with water today is the same as it has always been, since before he was born. In those areas, people have been crying about water, and facing the struggle of water, all their lives. \\n \\nThe windmills in this body of work depict the movement of people in the Venda and Limpopo areas when they go to collect water. The work shows the physical effort and struggle of the distances involved, but it also offers a sweet and kind mood. This is a reflection of the happy water memories of his youth. \\nThe water journeys of his memories are not reality. In reality, people in these areas really struggle with water. This struggle is depicted in his work, in one way or another. Some pieces, for example, show old water tanks in the process of physically breaking down. These images reflect a reality in rural areas where traditional water transport systems are breaking, and have been breaking for years, while little concern or pity is shown by society. \\nThe loss is real and it doesn’t only concern the water and the people. The the work calls for all South Africans to work harder to protect the water resources we still have. We need to protect what we have right now because we have already lost too much. \\n \\nEXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2020: Lufuno solo exhibition, Lizamore & Associates \\n2019: Venda solo exhibition, Lizamore & Associates \\n2018: Everard Reed Franschoek group exhibition \\n2017: Knysna Fine Arts 20 year celebration (Cape Town) \\n2017: 35 Years Exhibition, Lizamore & Associates (Johannesburg) \\n2017: Turbine Art fair (Johannesburg) \\n2017: Rotary Art fair (Johannesburg) \\n2017: Muta solo exhibition, Lizamore & Associates \\n2016: Rotary Art fair (Johannesburg) \\n2016: Turbine Artfair (Johannesburg) \\n2015: Gibbs Print Fair (Johannesburg) \\n2015: The Power of the Paper (50 years of printmaking in Australia, Canada and South Africa Group Show) \\n2015: Madi a Thavha Wood Sculpture Group exhibition (Venda) \\n2014: I remember my grandfather (Gallery 2 Johannesburg) \\n2013: ABSA L’sAtelier Finalists’ (ABSA Gallery) \\n2013: Freedom (Two man show with Carla Frank, Johannesburg) \\n2012: David Brow Gallery (Johannesburg) \\n2011: Landscapes Revisited (Two-man show with Mongezi Mcaphaii) \\n2011: Unity Gallery (collaboration with Senzo Shabangu) \\n2010: Artist’s Open Studio (Drill Hall, Johannesburg) \\n2010: Artist Proof Studio 3rd year Exhibition (Johannesburg) \\n2010: Kate Miller Photography Gallery (Johannesburg) \\n2009: Craft Yarano sculpture (Pretoria) \\n2009: Artist Proof Studio Gallery with Pony Pedro (Johannesburg) \\n2007: Fried Contemporary Art Gallery (Pretoria) \\n \\nAWARDS \\n \\n2013: ABSA L,Atelier Finalists’ Top 10 \\n2010: Artist Proof Studio, Student of the year \\n2006 / 2007: Vembe District Art Awards (1st & 2nd place) \\n2005: Mapungubwe Building Up Art competition (1st prize) \\n2004: Munghana Lonene FM Art Competition (1st prize) \\n \\nWORKSHOPS & PROJECTS \\n \\n2012 - 2015: Project (collaboration with William Kentridge) \\n2011 - 2014: Facilitated TB, Bilharzia and Aids awareness workshop with Kim Berman in Makuya (Venda) \\n2010 - 2017: Facilitated a book binding, drawing and painting workshop (Limpopo) \\n2008 - 2009: Vhutsila Vhutibiwi pottery workshop at Noria Mabasa (Venda). \\n2007: Bag Factory Artist Residency (Johannesburg) \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013407809757 gid://shopify/Product/9013407842525 gid://shopify/Product/9013408104669

item.title: Jan Neethling
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641476051165 Jan Neethling 2007 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640612090077 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013946384605","gid://shopify/Product/9013946417373"] [20232] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jan Neethling has, over the years, made a name for himself as a distinguished artist. For some fifty years he has creatively collaborated with one of South Africa’s foremost artists, Robert Hodgins. Until recently, Jan was largely unknown outside of Johannesburg. This, was partly due to his own modest and introvert nature, as well as to the generous attitude with which he unconditionally welcomed and supported each and every success Robert Hodgins achieved with is art. There is no doubt, however, that from the moment they met, Robert became Jan’s mentor and muse. \\n \\nJan Neethling’s surprisingly animated figures dominate his canvasses. He is an accomplished painter of life on the move, and even the occasional landscape or still-life he produces will seem as much concerned with the human absence, as they might with a table leg, objects in a room, trees or the lie of the land. They display the same brushstrokes and sense of living presence that we see in the figurative pictures. \\n \\nIt has always seemed that he has been distinguished by two characteristics in his approach to image-making: he is a wide-eyed and impressionable recorder of human activity, but also a skilled and formal technician, hardworking and disciplined in his approach to his materials and subjects. \\n \\nNeethling grew up in a close and cultured family. Due to his father’s diplomatic career he learned early to observe and react to a new green land when they lived in Canada in the first few years following World War II. He cites this exposure at an impressionable young age as fostering his first wanting to draw and paint, and he later excelled in art at school back in South Africa. His high school and arts college education encouraged the figurative element of his work and instilled the discipline ways of the period: specialist teachers taught different media, it was required to learn a solid foundation in each, as well as develop rigorous standards in the preparation of materials, surfaces, and the techniques required before evolving a personal style. He acquired skills not only in painting, sculpture and drawing but also in graphic processes including silkscreen, then very much a new way of working. He made acquaintance who provided access to a social context of arts, literature and music, and also developed his interest in photography. All this provided the basis for experimenting with combinations of medium, becoming open to new processes, and being willing to use his own photographs, and the images of popular culture, as the basis of his paintings. \\n \\nWhile he has painted and exhibited since the 1970’s, this was mainly in collaboration with, or alongside his lifelong friend and mentor, the late Robert Hodgins, and only in more recent years has Neethling painted regularly and exhibited consistently for himself. There are many who believe this career was long overdue for a steeper trajectory. Long self-effacing and modest in promoting his own work, he has frequently been seen as self-sacrificing in his stalwart support for Hodgins’ career. \\n \\nYet the artist himself sees the long development as having been necessary, a steady evolution of his main cast of characters in what we like to call his “theatre of life”. It is true that he and Hodgins actually inspired one another, and that each learned from the other as their years of working together went by. He ventures that he has only recently found and exercised his own artistic voice but that his was always strongly encouraged by Hodgins."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013946384605 gid://shopify/Product/9013946417373

item.title: Jana Aspeling
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641464058077 Jana Aspeling gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640616251613 [] Discover the expressive and thought-provoking works of Jana Aspeling, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Known for her dynamic compositions and unique visual language, Aspeling explores themes of identity, emotion, and abstraction through bold forms and textures. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jana Aspeling was born in 1979 in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\nHer creative journey has traversed multiple disciplines before settling into the world of fine arts.? \\nJana’s formal education in art began at the University of Stellenbosch, where she initially studied graphic design. However, finding the constraints of graphic design limiting, she shifted her focus to fine arts, a move that allowed her to explore a broader spectrum of creativity. During her studies, she specialised in printmaking and painting, disciplines that deeply resonated with her and honed her skills in colour and composition. \\n After university, Jana pursued a career outside the traditional art world, spending nearly two decades in the hairdressing industry. Here, she not only mastered the art of colour and form through her work as a master colourist and salon owner but also deepened her understanding of the human form and psyche. This experience enriched her artistic perspective, particularly in portraying the essence of femininity. \\nJana’s art is characterised by its vibrant colour palettes and intricate textures, often exploring themes of beauty and the complexities of everyday life. Her work frequently features flora and fauna motifs , embedding subtle symbols and narratives that invite viewers to look beyond the surface. The interplay of natural elements and human emotion in her art creates a compelling dialogue between the viewer and the artwork. \\nIn 2021, Jana returned full-time to her first passion—painting—following a transformative period during the lockdown. This shift marked a prolific phase in her career, during which she produced several acclaimed series, including \"Birds and Blooms,\" which reflect both personal growth and artistic evolution. Her works have been exhibited both locally and internationally, resonating with audiences for their depth and authenticity. \\nToday, Jana continues to live and work in Johannesburg, drawing inspiration from her surroundings and personal experiences. She is dedicated to exploring new techniques and subjects, continually pushing the boundaries of her artistic expression. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Jana Kolodziej
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641466056925 Jana Kolodziej gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640616677597 [] Discover the work of Jana Kolodziej, an artist inspired by the natural world, known for her intuitive printmaking process and transformative exploration of themes. Based in Cape Town, South Africa, with roots in East Germany. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Drawing inspiration from the natural world, Jana Kolodziej enjoys deconstructing and playing with images to capture their essence. Through this process, the image transforms into an idea, leading to the development of a theme. \\nFor Jana, the process of printmaking is unpredictable, shaped by numerous factors that influence the final outcome. She finds this unpredictability liberating, as it encourages letting go of expectations. In this way, creating a print becomes a journey of discovery rather than a predetermined act. \\nJana also appreciates the physicality of printmaking, embracing the marks left by the medium and tools while working intuitively to find the right rhythm. Born in East Germany, she studied Fine Art at the Kunsthochschule Berlin-Weißensee, graduating with a degree in Fine Art and Sculpture. After completing her studies, Jana relocated to Cape Town, South Africa."}]}]}

item.title: Jana Visser
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641470841053 Jana Visser 2565 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640617562333 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013982200029","gid://shopify/Product/9013982265565","gid://shopify/Product/9013982429405","gid://shopify/Product/9013982494941","gid://shopify/Product/9013982560477","gid://shopify/Product/9013982593245","gid://shopify/Product/9013982658781","gid://shopify/Product/9013982822621","gid://shopify/Product/9013982920925","gid://shopify/Product/9013983019229"] [21058,21059,21060,21057,21062,21063,21064,21066,21061,21065] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jana Visser is a textile artist and handweaver originally from Stellenbosch, South Africa. In 2019 she completed her Bachelor studies in Fine Art at Stellenbosch University. In 2021 she obtained a Bachelor’s Diploma in Textile Design from LUCA School of Arts in Ghent, Belgium. In the following year she completed her Master’s in Textile Design also at LUCA School of Arts for which she received a Magna Cum Laude. Her master's thesis titled, \"an emptiness that breathes\" was nominated for a Thesis Prize as well as the prestigious Dirk Lauwaert Award. \\nHer work has been exhibited in multiple galleries and institutions in both South Africa and Belgium, including the Design Museum in Ghent, and forms part of private collections in South Africa, Belgium, France and Germany. Recent exhibitions include Verweven/Entrelacés at Schönfeld Gallery, Zomer Salon at Kunsthal Ghent, and I try to imagine how your texture felt like at St. Peter’s Church of Ypres. In October 2022, some of her textile works were on display during Dutch Design Week in Eindhoven, the Netherlands. Her work titled “in the almost” was shortlisted for the LOEWE Foundation Craft Prize of 2023. In May 2024, Visser had her first solo exhibition titled, Breathing Matter, at Queens Brussels Gallery in Brussels, Belgium. \\nCaptivated by weaving as both an art-making method and its conceptual capabilities, Visser seeks a logic of reciprocity and becoming through the framework of her weaving practice. Grounding her practice in an openness \\nto uncertainty, she navigates between controlling method and media, whilst considering relationships between matter, time and space. She views this as a source of meaning-making, and a means to explore the viability of sensory perception and embodied experience. Her methods are slow – requiring patience and time in order to grasp both their material and symbolic potency. There is a desire to know more about the self, the value of rhythm and gesture, and how thread may serve as a conduit for accessing a dimension beyond the tangible. \\nHer interest lies in the relation between weaving, breathing and thinking. The inwards-outwards passage of breath provides a symbolic reflection on weaving gestures, which also depend on constant rhythms and the entanglement of seemingly binary forces; the outwards giving horizontal weft and the inwards receiving vertical warp."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013982200029 gid://shopify/Product/9013982265565 gid://shopify/Product/9013982429405 gid://shopify/Product/9013982494941 gid://shopify/Product/9013982560477 gid://shopify/Product/9013982593245 gid://shopify/Product/9013982658781 gid://shopify/Product/9013982822621 gid://shopify/Product/9013982920925 gid://shopify/Product/9013983019229

item.title: Janine Allen-Spies
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641473790173 Janine Allen-Spies gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640619823325 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Prof Janine Allen-Spies obtained her BA (1992), MA (1995), and PhD (2017) degrees in Fine Arts at the University of the Free State. She works as an artist, image philosopher, and associate professor in Fine Arts at the UFS. \\n \\nAs a visual artist, Prof Allen-Spies (also known as ‘The Brusher’) has won several competitions and is the first artist in the country to be selected for the prestigious international UNESCO-Aschberg Residencies for Artists Programme, of which only two artists from the African continent (in all categories including drama, dance, and theatre arts) were elected. Other notable awards include the International Free State Arts Festival and an Audience Award at the esteemed Spier Contemporary Biennale, Cape Town (2010). In 2017, her PhD exhibition: The Visionary Brusher Game received the ABSA Visual Arts Award. Among other various experimental techniques she employs in her work, she also uses digital pinhole photography. In 2020, her digital work was included in the Smithsonian Lockdown series. Allen’s work is held in collections, including the Luciana Benneton Collection (Venice Biennale), and Modern Art Projects."}]}]}
