item.title: John K Cobra / Roland Gunst
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641523925213 John K Cobra / Roland Gunst gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640642760925 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Roland Gunst, a.k.a. John K Cobra, (* 1977) is a conceptual artist, filmmaker and musician of Belgian-Congolese (D.R.C.) descent, living in Flanders and South Africa. From an autobiographical perspective, he experiments with the potential of hybrid identity and Afro-European stories, inspired by the concept of Afropeanism, in response to conflicts and tensions between black Africa and the white West. Afropeanism is an attitude that values hybridism, transculturality and transnationality. It examines these issues through the prism of the history of African-European relations since the birth of men in Africa and their migration around the world. Gunst researches similarities in concepts and forms in the material and immaterial culture that have been developed separately in Europe and Africa, but point to the common origin and human experience of Europeans and Africans. Gunst uses these spaces of similarity, what Prof. Cecil Fromont called \"spaces of correlation\" to blend European and African cultures to create a new, transcultural tradition. Among his sources of inspiration are the intercultural exchange between Europe and Africa since 1500 that has shaped both continents; the Congolese-Portuguese creolisation of religion, art and political structures in the Kingdom of Kongo from 1500 and the transcultural character of the Congolese conception of identity. \\nGunst creates disruptive hybrid concepts and forms to reflect on the boundaries that define identity, culture, human condition and history. He is inspired by African and European art history, anthropology, psychology, philosophy and mythology. \\nHis journey in developing strategies for body and identity liberation and for emancipation from the monocultural, ethnic and nationalist identity discourse in Europe has evolved in 4 major phases since 2009. Phase 1 investigated extreme assimilation by developing a therapeutic procedure (including the use of a white face mask) to guarantee the assimilation of Flemish people of foreign descent into white Flemish society. Phase 2 transformed the weapons of white nationalism and radicalism via white, Flemish, cultural symbols such as the Flemish flag and the founding myth of the Flemish nation. He imagines the Congolese colonisation of Flanders and the forced application of the current assimilation policy of the government to the Flemish, to reconnect Flemish people with Afropeanism and to strive for the construction of an Afropean community in Flanders. Phase 3 was the transformation of the Flemish identity into a plurality of identities by means of a transformation ritual, based on Flemish and Congolese cultural traditions, in which Lady Flandria, an allegory of the Flemish identity, transforms into a hybrid creature with Afro-European facial scarifications. Phase 4 examines different types of the persona of African Sacred Clowns and European court jesters who are fluid beings with a fluid gender, ethnic, cultural and national identity that transcends all notions of identities."}]}]}

item.title: John Koenakeefe Mohl
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641522614493 John Koenakeefe Mohl gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640644104413 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"‘Mohl’ is a simplification for the sake of Europeans of the Tswana surname Motlhakangna.1 As a child, Mohl used to draw with ‘pepa’ on rocks and animal hides. He also modelled objects of clay. His father carved pestles and chairs. At school in Dinokana and later Mafikeng, Koenakeefe (little crocodile) was often reprimanded and punished because of his insatiable urge to draw during classes. Mohl’s father was convinced that he was wasting his time at school and withdrew him to herd the goats. However, the Reverend Hale of the London Mission Society, who noticed the young boy’s talent, convinced his father to allow him to spend time drawing and to attend Tigerskloof Training School. There he attained a teacher’s diploma and subsequently left for Namibia to work on the docks at Lüderitz in order to study art with a French woman artist, Mary du Pont. She gave him a sound foundation in preparing canvases and applying art materials. Hale and other friends of the London Mission Society and Lutheran Church later sent him to continue his art studies at the Academy in Düsseldorf. He returned to Cape Town and in 1936 painted Kgosi Tshekedi Khama’s portrait, which was shown on the Empire Exhibition. In 1943 he won an Academy award for painting.? Mohl established an art school, White Studio, in the backyard of his home in Annadale Street, Sophiatown in 1944. In 1948 he was commissioned by the then Bechuanaland government to paint places of historic importance in the territory and between 1953 and 1954 he painted Moeng College and King Khama’s Memorial Stone for Kgosi Tshekedi Khama. Mohl was a founder member of Artists under the Sun in 1960 and he served on the committee of this organization until his death. After the demolition of Sophiatown, Mohl moved to Soweto where he eventually settled in Moroka in the mid-1970s and held exhibitions of his paintings in his garden. He played a leading role in the affairs of the St Francis Anglican Church which was close to his home in Moroka and also painted a panel of the Crucifixion for the church. He also gave art lessons at the Madibane and Orlando High Schools in Soweto. In 1972 Mohl founded the Moroka Sympathising Friends Scheme which he also chaired. Lybro Nyelele, Credo Mutwa, Helen Sebidi and his wife Puseletso Mohl also studied art with him. Mohl’s art records the changes that took place in southern Africa during the 20th century. It is a testimony of life as he experienced and observed it from Dinokana to Johannesburg. He painted rural and urban life with equal devotion. The stretches of open, unpolluted space in his landscapes are in stark contrast to the grey smoky air of his Witwatersrand scenes. While he shows the idyllic side of life in the countryside in his farming scenes, the devastating veld-fires raging at night expose the counterpart. His paintings of miners on their way to or from work express the plight of the faceless, dehumanised worker.?"}]}]}

item.title: John Kramer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641523237085 John Kramer 2249 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640648560861 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013456863453","gid://shopify/Product/9013456961757","gid://shopify/Product/9013456994525","gid://shopify/Product/9013457060061","gid://shopify/Product/9013471969501","gid://shopify/Product/9013837070557","gid://shopify/Product/9013837103325","gid://shopify/Product/9014035644637","gid://shopify/Product/9014035677405","gid://shopify/Product/9014035742941","gid://shopify/Product/9014035808477"] [23052,16930,18100,23051,23053,16918,17966,18099,16925,23050,16924] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"John Kramer is a South African artist whose oil paintings capture the essence of the small town in the Western Cape, Karoo and beyond. Born in Worcester, Cape Province, in 1946, Kramer developed a deep appreciation for the region's unassuming houses, quirky shop-fronts, and nostalgic corner cafes. His artistic journey began in the early 1970s when he started photographing these structures, fearing their eventual disappearance. These images became the foundation for his realistic oil and acrylic paintings, which have since become highly regarded and collected world wide. \\nKramer received formal art education at the Hugo Naude Art Centre in Worcester and later pursued a Diploma in Fine Art at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, majoring in painting. He is a winner of the Michaelis prize. In 1969 he joined the Van Zijl and Robinson advertising agency, as a junior finished artist, learning a new set of skills. In 1970 he joined the South African Museum as a designer, working on a diverse number of exhibitions ranging from Wonders of Nature to the Whale Well, ultimately rising to the position of Head of Exhibitions. In April 2002 he took early retirement from the Iziko Museums to pursue a full time painting career. \\nCurrently residing in the Gardens suburb, Cape Town, he continues to captivate audiences with his solo exhibitions, showcasing his realistic paintings that capture the essence of the South African small town. A theme that he has pursued for over fifty years. \\nThroughout his career, Kramer has participated in numerous group exhibitions, leaving an indelible mark on the South African art scene. His work has been featured in prestigious events such as the Cape Town Biennial, Cape Town Triennial, and various exhibitions at renowned galleries like the South African National Gallery. He has had work shown in the Netherlands and Belgium. His work is in a number of private and public collections. \\nJohn Kramer's realistic paintings transport viewers to a bygone era, preserving the essence of small-town life in South Africa. With his meticulous attention to detail and unwavering passion for his craft, Kramer continues to make a significant contribution to the South African art landscape. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013456863453 gid://shopify/Product/9013456961757 gid://shopify/Product/9013456994525 gid://shopify/Product/9013457060061 gid://shopify/Product/9013471969501 gid://shopify/Product/9013837070557 gid://shopify/Product/9013837103325 gid://shopify/Product/9014035644637 gid://shopify/Product/9014035677405 gid://shopify/Product/9014035742941 gid://shopify/Product/9014035808477

item.title: John Meyer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641526677725 John Meyer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640649117917 [] Explore the work of South African artist John Meyer, known for his hyper-real paintings and Sequential Narratives series—emotive, imagined scenes that explore human relationships and memory. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"John Meyer studied at the Johannesburg Technical College’s School of Art before beginning his career in advertising and working as a freelance illustrator. A lifelong advocate of representational painting, Meyer is known for his meticulous technique and cinematic compositions that blur the line between memory and imagination. His hyper-real yet fictional scenes—archetypal moments rather than literal depictions—inviting viewers into a space of both familiarity and narrative ambiguity. \\nIn recent years, Meyer has developed his Sequential Narratives series, a body of work that delves into the intricacies of human relationships. These paintings unfold as interconnected scenes, capturing different facets of a single emotional event from multiple perspectives."}]}]}

item.title: John Madu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641526087901 John Madu 542 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640649019613 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013285093597"] [3299,3300] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"John Madu (born in 1983) is a Nigerian multi-disciplinary artist born in Lagos, best known for his figurative symbolic style of paintings, usually along the lines of the complexity of identity, social behavior and the effects of cultural globalization on individualism. His work can be described as eclectic because of how he derives ideas, from a various range of influences and sources based on popular culture, African history, art history. and personal experiences. symbolism is usually evident in his work, with reoccurring iconography such as books, apples, and other recognizable items which convey a certain meaning in art, and act as metaphors to a subject. \\n \\nJohn’s source of inspiration is from a variety of places, but can be narrowed down to a few things that inspire a major part of his art works, which could be current situations affecting society, be it political, social or just banal everyday life issues. Giving him opportunities and reason to record the history of his time, with the aid of resource materials such as magazines, books, social media, news and even real time situations. He believes the best kind of art is a reaction to certain issues of interest and divulging information to educate and also entertain. “As much as I believe in the beauty of art in itself, I stand with the theory of ‘’significant form” and the aesthetic is experienced when the work of art stimulates an emotion, intellect and imagination. The aesthetics in viewing a work of art should be judged based on the feature of the artwork in itself, and not just based on preferences and personal experiences. The artist however should not be the sole judge of his or her work, as seen that in no other field of human activity where this would be possible”. \\n \\nSELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n2020 | Tokyo Art Fair \\n2020 | Shanghai Art Fair \\n2019 | “Seeing Sounds”,Copeland Gallery, London (House of African Art) \\n2019 | “Next Wave: The Power of Authenticity and Self-Validation”, Hoxton Arches \\nGallery, London \\n2018 | “Identity Tones”, One Artspace Gallery, Manhattan, New York \\n2018 | “Forestation”, Didi Museum, Victoria Island Lagos \\n2018 | “Sao and the Muse”, Saocafe, Lagos \\n2017 | “Artyrama”, Artyrama Gallery, Victoria Island, Lagos \\n2017 | “Its Not Furniture”, Omenka Gallery, Lagos \\n2016 | “Sunrise”, Moor House, London \\n2016 | “Platform”, ArtTwentyOne Gallery Victoria Island, Lagos \\n2016 | “Only The Brave 2”, DIESEL Showroom. Lagos \\n2013 | “Indigenes”, Hamilton Prokleen Centre, Ontario, Canada \\n2008 | “Art Expo Nigeria”, Nkem Gallery, Lagos \\n \\nSOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n2018 | “Identity Tones”, by Bombay Sapphire, Lagos \\n2017 | “Only The Brave 1” Diesel Flagship Store, Victoria Island, Lagos \\n2016 | “An Obscure Fashion for Affection”, Terra Kulture, Lagos \\n2015 | “Morphogenesis”, Didi Museum, Lagos"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013285093597 gid://shopify/Product/9013285126365

item.title: John-Michael Metelerkamp
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641511276765 John-Michael Metelerkamp gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640652591325 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013299740893", "gid://shopify/Product/9013299773661", "gid://shopify/Product/9013299871965", "gid://shopify/Product/9013299970269", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300134109", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300166877", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300199645", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300232413", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300265181", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300297949", "gid://shopify/Product/9013300330717", "gid://shopify/Product/9013315436765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013315502301", "gid://shopify/Product/9013345747165", "gid://shopify/Product/9013345878237", "gid://shopify/Product/9013379989725", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380022493", "gid://shopify/Product/9013380841693", "gid://shopify/Product/9013836120285"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"I believe that my job as an artist is to simplify the complexities of my life. Or at least my experience of it. The sense of overstimulation I feel and a propensity for chaos lingers around every corner of my psyche. That tension between chaos and order is a primary informer of the work I strive to make. Translating what I feel and see into a visual language is about focusing on something that I find interesting. And I may not be able to pin down the exactness of my curiosity; but I feel the need to challenge these thoughts and feelings and show myself what it looks like in a visual sense, with paint. \\n \\nExperimentation is a huge part of my process. I try not to think until I am standing in front of the canvas, paintbrush in hand. Forcing thought opens up possibilities of a journey through the painting. Colours dictate colours and forms dictate forms. \\n \\nGeorge Condo said “Don’t step back until you think you have something to look at’’. I adopt this practice. I get close to the painting. I want to be in the painting.\" John-Michael Metelerkamp is now based in Cape Town, South Africa, where he recently relocated to from Knysna. \\n \\nSelect Exhibitions \\n2020 \\n‘Notcurnes’, Solo, Deepest Darkest, Cape Town \\n‘A Subtle Skill’, Knysna Fine Art, Knysna, South Africa \\n‘A Winter Pallette’. item.title: John Newdigate
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641530904797 John Newdigate 2778 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640650592477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014043181277"] Explore the art of John Newdigate, one of South Africa's most celebrated ceramicists. Discover his hand-built porcelain vessels and unique painting techniques inspired by contemporary issues and natural landscapes. [23383] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"John Newdigate (b. 1968) is one of South Africa’s most celebrated ceramicists and artists. Living in the mountainous Overberg region of the Western Cape, Newdigate records contemporary issues alongside the physical landscapes, plants, and animals he encounters. An exuberant colorist, Newdigate specializes in painting hand-built, porcelain vessels using a unique technique inspired by precise and spontaneous mark-making. \\nNewdigate's signature process involves hand-painting multiple layers of underglaze pigment, reserving certain areas with a wax resist, and then removing surrounding pigments. This process is repeated multiple times, resulting in complex, translucent, and radiant imagery with a mix of sharp and blurred lines that provide depth and perspective. \\n \\nRecurring themes in his work include plants and animals used to make wry commentary on human emotions and interactions. Recently, Newdigate has ventured into creating three-dimensional renditions of his painted imagery, using fiber-reinforced polymer cement layered over a wooden and PU framework, then adorned with oil paints. This exploration, free from the constraints of ceramics, has sparked a wave of fresh creativity and concepts. \\nNewdigate’s work is part of several public collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, the William Humphreys Public Art Gallery, and the South African Cultural History Museum."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014043181277

Known for their thought-provoking works, Newdigate and Garrett merge their unique styles to create art that explores themes of human nature, social issues, and contemporary life. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"For both artists, this collaboration is more than a creative process; it is a conversation. Newdigate and Garrett work in tandem, constantly responding to each other’s visions, materials, and techniques. item.title: John Roome
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641534607581 John Roome gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640651772125 [] John Roome {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"John Roome obtained a Master’s Degree in Fine Art from Rhodes University in 1975 and a Doctor Technologiae: Design from Cape Peninsular University of Technology in 2014. \\n \\n \\n \\nRoome retired from full time lecturing in 2016. He was senior lecturer in Fine Art at Durban University of Technology where he taught drawing, printmaking, papermaking, painting, art theory, and assisted in the co-ordination of the Fine Art Programme. Roome is still extensively involved in the Masters in Fine Art Programme as a supervisor and co-supervisor. He has successfully supervised numerous Masters Students in Fine Arts and other related programmes over the last ten years. \\n \\n? \\n \\nRoome’s own research interests are focused around Creative Practice Based Research Methodologies and Creative Drawing Research. \\n \\n? \\n \\nRoome has held 12 solo exhibitions and participated in numerous group exhibitions in a career that spans 40 years. His creative work includes a variety of media such as painting, printmaking, hand papermaking, drawing, digital drawing and animation. He has works in a number of Public Art Collections including the Durban Art Gallery. \\n \\n? \\n \\nIn addition to his creative outputs, Roome has published a number of papers related to his doctoral research (Creative Applications of Basic Computer Software: A Practice-Led Exploration of Visual Art and Design Thinking Through Drawing and Animation)."}]}]}

item.title: Jonathan Freemantle
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641540800733 Jonathan Freemantle gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640654983389 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born: 1978 Cape Town, South Africa. Lives and works: Edinburgh, Scotland. \\nAt 17, Freemantle was selected as one of five students from around the world to study at St Oswald’s Academy in London, where he completed an intensive, five-year apprenticeship in traditional drawing, painting, sculpture and geometry. These principles continue to inform his rigorous approach to painting and art practice. Founded on an intimate understanding of painting and art history, his work explores the relationship between his body, time and the earth, each of which serve as materials and as inspiration. \\nUsing a variety of media including egg tempera, mountain rocks and ochre in his paintings, he situates the body as an organic presence at one with the landscape, at the same time integrating the landscape physically in the human act of painting. In an age damned as Anthropocene, Freemantle uses his passionate and visceral canvases to consciously and resolutely make the case for redemption and forgiveness of the human – and as a male, of the man – on the planet. \\nFreemantle has been exhibiting internationally since 2007, with group and solo exhibitions in London, Cape Town, Amsterdam, Johannesburg and Edinburgh, including a major commission by The Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg. In addition to an expansive studio practice, Freemantle has been working as an educator, in 2002 setting up the painting department of The Art Academy in London and writing ‘Anatomy made simple for Artists’ published by Arcturus (UK) in 2004. He has also curated numerous exhibitions in the context of Edinburgh International Fashion Festival, which he co-founded in 2012, and as co-director of Hazard Gallery, which he co-founded and ran in Johannesburg from 2015 to 2019. \\nHaving returned to Edinburgh in 2019, Freemantle has focused on full time studio practice. His work is represented in collections worldwide including SAB Miller, Nirox Foundation and the private collection of HRH King Charles III."}]}]}

item.title: Jonathan Silverman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641541751005 Jonathan Silverman gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640655605981 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"JONATHAN SILVERMAN (1981 -) \\n \\nJonathan Silverman is a visual artist who works primarily in painting, digital painting and video. “The theme which ties the imagery in my current work together is of fragmented landscapes, lived through or collected. In my practice, I distil images of our natural environment into fragmented landscapes, exploring the space between the physical and virtual. From my personal encounter with the natural world as a potentially alienating space, I am interested in the question of whether our digital lives are divorcing us ever further from the environment and in what ways this detachment is at once natural and dehumanizing.” \\n \\n?Silverman (born in Manchester, UK) grew up in Israel and then spent time in Italy, graduating with a BFA from the Academy of Fine Arts in Florence (2006). Moving to London, Silverman was awarded the Elizabeth Greenshields Grant in 2009 and in 2010 and graduated with a Post-Graduate Diploma in Drawing from the Royal Drawing School (2011). He has participated in numerous group exhibitions locally and abroad. His most recent will be Salto in Altro, Palazzo Monti, Brescia, Italy in 2021. His last solo exhibition was Steep Bend, Light Step, 99 Loop Gallery, Cape Town (2021). Silverman has been awarded two residencies in India and Italy and has taught and lectured in art. He currently lives and works between South Africa and the UK. Artworks of his are included in various collections around the globe."}]}]}

item.title: Joni Brenner
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641543880925 Joni Brenner gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640656195805 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Joni Brenner is the first artist that has brought a human skull into the studio. It graced the working space with its presence and focused our minds on what is important and what is not. The brains in our skulls were set thinking about the skull on the table, this is reminiscent of the message in Masaccio’s great early Renaissance fresco of the Holy Trinity which includes the inscription: \"IO FU[I] G[I]A QUEL CHE VOI S[I]ETE E QUEL CH['] I[O] SONO VO[I] A[N]C[OR] SARETE\" (I once was what you are and what I am you also will be). \\nBrenner was born in Zimbabwe. She has an MA(FA) degree from the University of the Witwatersrand where she is also a lecturer in History of Art at the Wits School of Arts. \\nBrenner has been practicing professionally as an artist since 1996 and has held solo exhibitions in Johannesburg and London. Her work is in several public and private collections. Brenner’s work is primarily concerned with portraiture but not in the traditional rendering of the physical likeness of an individual. Her work investigates commemoration, life and death and her technique bridges abstraction and realism. \\n\"These lithographs show three different views of a skull. The term ‘articulated’, in relation to a skeleton, indicates that all the bones have been hinged together in the same relative position to each other, as they were when the person was alive—the individual parts made coherent. More generally articulated refers to something clearly defined, or to something said very clearly, so that each word or syllable can be heard. \\nIn these works, fluid broad areas are overlaid with tighter more prominent defining marks to articulate the form, capturing the complex range of solid and intricate sections that make up the skull. \\nMy skull work, since 2012 —mostly rendered in watercolour, but also in clay, bronze and oils—has revisited the same particular skull over and again in a repetitive practice of close looking and re-looking. This focused practice amounts to a meditation on life and living, its transience and fragility, on presence and absence, rather than on a skull as a symbol of danger or anything ghoulish.\" Joni Brenner, 2017"}]}]}

item.title: Jono Dry
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641544241373 Jono Dry 1769 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640656392413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013363278045","gid://shopify/Product/9013363802333","gid://shopify/Product/9013363867869"] [11940,11942,11861] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Based in Cape Town, South Africa and entirely self taught, South African artist Jono Dry has worked for the last thirteen years on creating a practice centred around his large-scale hyperrealist graphite works. \\n \\nThe luxury of time runs strongly through Jono’s practice as an artist ~ with a single hyperrealist graphite drawing taking about 2 months to complete, with up to 200 hours of drawing. Dry then produces a series of limited edition Giclée prints from these original works. \\n \\nExhibiting locally and internationaly, Dry has devoted his practice to pushing the medium of graphite. With perfection as a fundamental aspect of hyperrealism ~ a sense of sleek precision is kept at the core of his practice. \\n \\nUsing rich visuals and storytelling, the video documentation of the pieces reaffirm the work’s sense of time and its power to move."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013363278045 gid://shopify/Product/9013363802333 gid://shopify/Product/9013363867869

item.title: Jordan Anthony
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641545191645 Jordan Anthony gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640656621789 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Operating between Cape Town and Durban, Jordan Anthony (b. 1999) is a film photographer, curator, and arts writer who grew up in KwaZulu Natal and graduated from the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg with a Bachelor of Art in Fine Arts. During her studies, she explored subjects in archaeology and psychology, including themes such as healing, dreams, and intuitive creation in her art practice. Anthony has since collaborated with various professionals in the local art industry, including the KZNSA Gallery in Durban (with Strauss & Co.) and Turbine Art Fair (via overheard in the gallery). Her interests also extend into philosophy, memory, and prehistory."}]}]}

item.title: José Vermeij
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641549484253 José Vermeij gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640663535837 [] Explore the art of Jose Vermeij, a talented artist celebrated for her evocative creations that blend emotion, technique, and storytelling. Discover her unique perspective and artistic journey. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"José is an independent artist from the Netherlands, who joined The Printing Girls in 2020 when she lived in South Africa. She studied printmaking at Academie voor Schone Kunsten Arendonk, Belgium and got hooked. \\nOn moving to South Africa, she found a printing studio to work from, but was able to buy her own press since then. Her love of photography and working in layers defines most of her print work. With cyanotype and collagraphs being her favourite print techniques, she often combines them into mixed media pieces. As a citizen of the world her work includes themes related to global warming, but also dives into social issues like the housing crisis and subjects related to her personal life."}]}]}

item.title: Joseph (Cheri Cherin) Kinkonda
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641545847005 Joseph (Cheri Cherin) Kinkonda gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640661078237 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Joseph Kinkonda, called Chéri Cherin, was born on February 16th, 1955 in Kinshasa (Democratic Republic Congo, formerly called Zaire). He studied at the Academie des Beaux Arts in Kinshasa under the Austrian ceramics-artist Peter Weihs. During this time Chéri Cherin started to paint posters in his residential-quarter Ndjili.Chéri Chérin at his studio in Kinshasa \\n \\nChérin created murals on the walls of bars, barbershops and small boutiques. Impressive pictures of daily life but also with very serious contents. \\n \\nToday Cherin is one of the best known painters in Kinshasa and a teacher to many young talented artists."}]}]}

item.title: Josephine Ghesa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641545552093 Josephine Ghesa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640662520029 [] Explore the captivating works of Josephine Ghesa, a Lesotho-born South African artist celebrated for her unique zoomorphic sculptures that blend traditional Sotho narratives with contemporary ceramic artistry. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Josephine Ghesa (b. 1958, Lesotho) is a celebrated South African ceramic artist known for her distinctive zoomorphic sculptures that merge traditional Sotho narratives with contemporary ceramic techniques. Raised by her grandmother in Lesotho, Ghesa learned pottery at an early age. \\n In 1990, she joined the Ardmore Ceramic Studio in KwaZulu-Natal, where she developed her unique style. Her works often depict mythical creatures and figures, reflecting her rich cultural heritage and spiritual beliefs. Ghesa's pieces are characterized by their vibrant colors, intricate textures, and imaginative forms, making her one of the most recognized artists in the South African ceramic art scene."}]}]}

item.title: Joseph Ntensibe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641548009693 Joseph Ntensibe 1895 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640662421725 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013933506781"] Discover Joseph Ntensibe, a Ugandan artist born in 1953, whose work addresses deforestation through luminous, dreamlike forest scenes. His rare large-scale canvases from the ‘Disappearing Forest’ series highlight Uganda's environmental loss. [19428] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Joseph Ntensibe (b. 1953, Uganda) has dedicated his life to addressing the diminishing forests of his youth. The Uganda of his childhood has changed dramatically due to rampant deforestation caused by mining, war, drought, urbanization, and a lack of awareness about the value of forests. In the past twenty years, Uganda has lost over 1 million hectares of virgin forest cover—almost 30% of the country’s total land. \\nAlthough Ntensibe is a highly collectible artist, his large-scale canvases are rare in the contemporary art market. The opportunity to collaborate with and showcase his extraordinary piece from the celebrated 'Disappearing Forest' series is a great privilege. Ntsensibe's dreamlike forest scenes shimmer with hidden sources of light, creating multicoloured sensory feasts. His work has been likened to that of Cezanne and Klimt for its luminosity, but many believe this artist-activist's work stands in a league of its own. The ever-changing landscapes in the series serve as a profound and poignant timeline of Uganda’s loss. In recent years, critics have noted how glimpses of sky and shafts of light, previously unheard of in true equatorial rain-forests, have appeared in Ntensibe’s forestscapes. While undeniably beautiful, these depictions evoke a sense of witnessing a living tragedy."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013933506781

item.title: Joshua Miles
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641548271837 Joshua Miles gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640662683869 [] Joshua Miles {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Joshua Miles was born in the Western Cape in South Africa in 1967. After early schooling in Swellendam he completed high school in the northern suburbs of Cape Town. He then went on to study at the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town where he received the Michaelis prize for best student in his final year. \\n \\nJoshua is one of those rare artists who has managed to make a living solely from his art. He spent many years painting with oils on canvas but his passion has always been with reduction block printmaking. His influences in printmaking started at a young age watching his aunt Elsa Miles, artist and art historian, doing woodcuts and then later studying under Cecil Scotness at UCT. \\n \\nJoshua is a landscape artist and is inspired by the play of light on the landscape which leads him to explore his local areas. He is always hunting for qualities flight that evoke emotion, this is often the softer light that brings out the in-between tones and greys most would miss. He is also inspired by the impressionists style of loose mark making and by the Japanese tradition of printmaking both of which are evident in his work. \\n \\nAfter finishing at UCT Joshua moved to Hermanus where he met his Scottish wife Angela. They have been married more than 20 years and they have over the years lived and worked between South Africa and Scotland. They work together in the business of selling Joshua's art"}]}]}

A 25 year career as a professional and private chef brings a wealth of world travel and experience to his views on the world. \\nLooking for new artistic outlets quickly lead to a passion for fine photography and the photographic arts. \\nJosh documents life in modern Johannesburg and the fast paced changes in its neighborhoods demographics"}]}]}

item.title: Jozua Gerrard
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641550794973 Jozua Gerrard gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640664027357 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jozua Gerrard (b. 2001) is a young creative who lives and works in Cape Town. \\n \\nHe enjoys painting and sculpture and his work generally reflects on his personal experiences in dealing with depression, anxiety and his journey in discovering his sexual identity."}]}]}

item.title: JOY ADEBOYE
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641549648093 JOY ADEBOYE gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640603046109 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014111043805","gid://shopify/Product/9014111109341","gid://shopify/Product/9014111142109","gid://shopify/Product/9014111207645","gid://shopify/Product/9014111273181"] Joy Adeboye is a Nigerian contemporary artist based in Lagos, known for her expressive watercolor works exploring femininity, spirituality, identity, and self-perception through poetic visual storytelling. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Joy Adeboye (b.1998, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist who lives and works in Lagos,Nigeria. She received her BA (2019) in literature from the Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile Ife. \\nJoy Adeboye’s use of watercolor as her primary medium has been described as both bold and deeply inspiring. She is carving her own path within the \\ncontemporary revival of this technique; a medium with a history that stretches back to the origins of art itself and that only a few contemporary artists have \\nreinterpreted as a means of navigating the ambiguous space between reality, the fantastic, and political utopia. \\nAdeboye’s practice extends this lineage while shaping a language of her own. In her previous works; she explored a more mystical interplay of color and form, \\nfor her solo project in Tommorows Today she has produced a new body of work that delves into the intimate realm of desire, religion and sexuality. \\nSometimes appearing as collages of different papers or as a single piece, these watercolor paintings evoke both the delicacy of petals and the softness of flesh, while avoiding explicit representation. They seem to wander through the inner self.. both physically and mentally, through a language of form and color that remains open, shifting and poetic. Following a very well received solo presentation at FNBartjoburg 2024 adeboye was invited to feature in the Tommorrows Today section at Investec cape town art fair this year. \\nRecent Projects: \"Chaos & the 8th year\" FNBartJoburg 2024. \"The vanguard\" AMG Projects, March 2024, Lagos, Nigeria. \\nSocial media: @joyadejolaadeboye"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014111043805 gid://shopify/Product/9014111109341 gid://shopify/Product/9014111142109 gid://shopify/Product/9014111207645 gid://shopify/Product/9014111273181

item.title: Josie Grindrod
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641549320413 Josie Grindrod gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640662847709 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Josephine Grindrod was born in Durban, South Africa in 1963. She lives and works in Cape Town.Grindrod holds an MA in Visual Studies from the University of Stellenbosch, writing her dissertation onArt and the Imaginary realm of Psychoanalysis (2006). She has also studied at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, completing Discourse of Art I –III (2014), an Advanced Diploma in Painting (1987), and a BA Fine Arts degree (1984).Grindrod has attended annual residencies and workshops with artist/teachers Rosenclaire in South Africa and Italy (2022 –2009) and participated in Tupelo Triangle Arts Workshops, Nyanga (2017) and Woodstock (2007).Grindrod has held four solo shows, the most recent of which was Gesturing Objects, AVA, Cape Town (2018), and has participated in numerous group shows, the most recent of which The Ripple Effect, is currently on view at the AVA, Cape Town. Her work is held in local and international private collections and by the University of Cape Town.Recent collaborative projects have included production of Under Cover of Darkness; an exhibition focused on the history of women in servitude, Iziko Slave Lodge, Cape Town (2021-2018) and the establishment of ZERO, an artist-run exhibition space in central Cape Town focused on climate change and creative exchange (2022)."}]}]}

item.title: JP Meyer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641554399453 JP Meyer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640603242717 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013332476125", "gid://shopify/Product/9013332541661", "gid://shopify/Product/9013332607197"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The initiation processes we experience throughout life are normally etched in our memory as milestones: sometimes pleasant, sometimes painful. Like pieces in a puzzle, Meyer highlights specific initiation processes and rituals in the lives of young boys and men which find expression later on in life: life on the playground, military service or simple acceptance within a new circle of friends. It is a process that is both welcoming and unsettling in its departure from comfort zones. \\n \\nIn contrast to the notion of transitional processes as a necessary part of life, Meyer’s body of work highlights the tension between youthful innocence – individuality even – and the brutal transition towards a uniform group identity. One cannot help but lament the loss of innocence that is suffered during each ritual; like youthful feet being forced into rigid wooden clogs to impose uniformity. Meyer’s work is however not entirely a tale of social suppression. \\n \\nHe sits comfortably with the fact that individuals form part of groups, and that transitional phases such as “religious christening and catechism, the shaping of a toddler to become a scholar, the initiation of a child into adulthood, first sexual encounters, marriage, even student initiations all signify processes towards membership of a new subculture, gang, group or organization”."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013332476125 gid://shopify/Product/9013332541661 gid://shopify/Product/9013332607197 gid://shopify/Product/9013414166749

In 2018, he started working in painting, finding this medium more expansive and thus more suitable for exploring the themes around his upbringing and experiences as a person of mixed race and heritage (termed “coloured”) in apartheid and post-apartheid South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013378613469 gid://shopify/Product/9013378646237 gid://shopify/Product/9013378908381 gid://shopify/Product/9013378941149 gid://shopify/Product/9013379170525 gid://shopify/Product/9013379563741 gid://shopify/Product/9013379924189 gid://shopify/Product/9013379956957 gid://shopify/Product/9013380907229 gid://shopify/Product/9013380972765 gid://shopify/Product/9013381038301 gid://shopify/Product/9013381103837 gid://shopify/Product/9013381136605 gid://shopify/Product/9013381202141

item.title: Judith Mason
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641556889821 Judith Mason 563 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640664518877 ["gid://shopify/Product/9133231407325"] [25533] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Judith Mason (1938 - 2016) was a painter and graphic artist of symbolic and mythological landscapes, figures and portraits. Mason worked primarily in oils and pencil but also incorporated various graphic media and found objects into her work as well as having made a number of artists' books. \\n \\nJudith Mason drew and painted in reaction to her world: political events, books that she read, snippets of history or poetry which caught her eye, or the experience of particular people or animals. \\n \\nShe taught art at the Scuola Lorenzo de Medici in Florence (Italy), the Michaelis School of Fine Art (UCT), at the University of the Witwatersrand and privately. Her work is represented in South African national art collections and museums and internationally in private and public collections including the Museum of Modern Art, New York; Yale University, The Bodleian Library at the University of Oxford and the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington DC. \\n \\nMason's most well known public commission is The Man Who Sang and the Woman Who Kept Silent aka The Blue Dress (1998) at The Constitutional Court in Johannesburg, South Africa. Justice Albie Sachs considers the piece to be \"one of the great pieces of art in the world of the late 20th century.\""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9133231407325

item.title: Judy Woodborne
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641558036701 Judy Woodborne 339 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640664781021 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014140207325","gid://shopify/Product/9014140698845"] Explore the art of Judy Woodborne, an award-winning artist and printmaker (MFA UCT). Discover her experimental prints and paintings, held in international collections like the Smithsonian, and her significant contributions as a festival artist and curator. [25268,25269,25267] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Judy Woodborne is an acclaimed artist and printmaker with a distinguished career marked by innovation and international recognition. She earned her Master of Fine Arts Degree with Distinction from the University of Cape Town (UCT) in 1993. The body of work from her MFA received critical acclaim and is held in significant collections, including the Smithsonian Collection of African Art (USA) and the Sanlam Corporate Collection (SA). \\n \\nWoodborne's artistic prowess was highlighted when she was selected as the ABSA Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees Festival Artist in 2007, for which she produced \"The Garden of Eden,\" a unique series of paintings on gold leaf. Her curatorial talents are evident in \"The Exquisite Corpse,\" a portfolio of 16 etchings she curated and published, which was selected for the Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees 2009 and later exhibited by the Norval Foundation. She also served as a guest curator for the Woordfees in 2018 and 2019. \\n \\nInternationally recognized, Woodborne has participated in numerous International Print Biennales, and her work is represented in various international public collections and museums. Her experimental approach to printmaking was showcased at the Salzburg Summer Festival, Austria, in 2015, and further explored in her series of experimental print constructions, \"The Anatomy of the World,\" exhibited at Lizamore Gallery in 2018. \\n \\nHer excellence in printmaking was affirmed in 2019 when she was awarded the S.C. Bes Romania S.R.L. prize at the International Contemporary Engraving Biennial, Romania, for her engraving \"The Weaver.\" Most recently, her work was selected for the \"Summer 2020\" exhibition curated by the International Print Centre in New York, USA."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014140207325 gid://shopify/Product/9014140698845

item.title: Julio Rizhi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641558888669 Julio Rizhi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640665010397 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"After several years of study at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe visual art studio, Julio decided to pursue his own experimental practice, while based at the Chinembiri studios with several of Zimbabwe's leading new-generation artists such as Gresham Tapiwa Nyaude, Moffat Takadiwa and Wycliffe Mundopa. Rizhi’s works like him a deeply embedded in the life of the city building connections between consumption and its outcomes, through the socio-ethical prism of contemporary Zimbabwe. \\n \\nHis dystopic and dysmorphic constructions speak to environmental decay and the social cost of high-density living such as youth unemployment and addiction. Darkly humoured, Rizhi uses the seductively bright colours of the discarded plastics he melts to construct his sculptures, as a metaphor for the broken promises of a better future advertised but never delivered. \\n \\n2020: Chakafukidza solo exhibition, ?First Floor Gallery Harare, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2020: ARCOLisboa Online, First Floor Gallery Harare, artsy.net \\n \\n2020: ?Cape Town Art Fair, First Floor Gallery Harare, Cape Town, South Africa? \\n \\n2019: Welcome Home, Group Show, MACAAL Gallery, Marrakesh, Morocco \\n \\n2018: Next Level, First Floor Gallery Harare, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2018: Cape Town Art Fair, First Floor Gallery Harare, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\n2017: Art Africa Art Fair, First Floor Gallery Harare, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\n2017: AKAA Paris, First Floor Gallery Harare, Paris, France \\n \\n2017: Another Antipodes/urban axis touring exhibition of Southern African contemporary art, PS Art Space, Freemantle, Australia \\n \\n2017: Mushonga/Medicine, solo exhibition, First Floor Gallery Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2016: THAT Art Fair, First Floor Gallery Harare, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\n2016: 'I am because you are', First Floor Gallery Harare, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n?2016: FNB Joburg Art Fair, First Floor Gallery Harare, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\n2016: Mushonga/Medicine Solo Exhibition, First Floor Gallery, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2015: FNB Joburg Art Fair – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\n2015: Harare Block Party at First Floor Gallery Harare, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2015: Kuyaruka; Coming of Age at First Floor Gallery Harare, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2014: Annual Exhibition at National Gallery of Zimbabwe, Harare, Zimbabwe \\n \\n2014: Final Year Show at National Gallery of Zimbabwe, Harare, Zimbabwe"}]}]}

item.title: Jürgen Schadeberg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641564033245 Jürgen Schadeberg gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640667599069 [] Explore the life and work of Jürgen Schadeberg (1931–2020), the German-born photojournalist who captured pivotal moments in South Africa’s history, including apartheid resistance, township culture, and portraits of Nelson Mandela and Miriam Makeba. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Jürgen Schadeberg (1931–2020) was a German-born South African photographer whose iconic images helped define the visual legacy of Drum magazine and the Sophiatown Renaissance. Arriving in South Africa in 1950, Schadeberg became Drum’s chief photographer and picture editor, mentoring a generation of Black photographers including Bob Gosani, Ernest Cole, and Alf Kumalo. \\nHis camera documented a vibrant yet politically fraught era—capturing figures such as Nelson Mandela, Miriam Makeba, Hugh Masekela, and Dolly Rathebe in moments of both defiance and joy. Schadeberg’s work offers a poignant visual record of apartheid-era South Africa, distinguished by its empathy, elegance, and historical insight."}]}]}

Her work includes jewellery, painting, and poignant portraits addressing social issues, earning recognition in various exhibitions and competitions. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Juria le Roux (b. 1968, Zimbabwe) spent her childhood on a cattle and maize farm near Rusape. She has lived in South Africa since 1976. In 1986, she obtained a B.A. Creative Arts Degree in Jewellery Design and Manufacture from the University of Stellenbosch. The following year, she founded Amulet, a co-operative workshop in Cape Town. Since 1986, Juria has participated in numerous solo and group jewellery and painting exhibitions. \\nIn 1993, she was awarded second prize in the De Beers Diamonds Today competition for her brooch \"Adam, Eve and the Tree of Knowledge\". Juria spent eight years abroad in Belgium and the USA, returning to South Africa to continue creating special commission jewellery pieces for private clients while exploring her love for painting under Pieter Vermaak's tutorship, Her solo exhibition \"Elegie/Reeksmoord\" (US Art Gallery, Stellenbosch 2011 and Absa KKNK, Oudtshoorn 2012), featuring 50 portraits of murder victims in South Africa, garnered widespread interest. Her works have been selected for the Sanlam Portrait Award \"TOP 40\" collection in 2015, 2017, and 2019 for pieces such as \"Joey Mashiya – Local Hero\" (2015), \"Kitchen Tea\" (2017), and \"Inheritance\" (2019). Juria resides on Langverwagt farm near Kuils River."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013837005021 gid://shopify/Product/9013839724765 gid://shopify/Product/9013996781789 gid://shopify/Product/9013996814557 gid://shopify/Product/9013996912861 gid://shopify/Product/9013996945629 gid://shopify/Product/9013996978397 gid://shopify/Product/9013997011165 gid://shopify/Product/9013997043933 gid://shopify/Product/9013997076701 gid://shopify/Product/9013997109469 gid://shopify/Product/9013997142237 gid://shopify/Product/9013997207773 gid://shopify/Product/9013997240541 gid://shopify/Product/9013997306077 gid://shopify/Product/9013997404381 gid://shopify/Product/9014036496605 gid://shopify/Product/9014036529373 gid://shopify/Product/9014036594909 gid://shopify/Product/9014117368029 gid://shopify/Product/9014117433565

item.title: Justice Mathonsi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641560461533 Justice Mathonsi 331 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640665731293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014058418397"] Discover the powerful printmaking of South African artist Justice Mathonsi. Explore large-scale lino reduction portraits celebrating women, Tsonga heritage, and family history. [23785] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Justice Mathonsi (b. 1987, Soweto), raised in Ribugwani, Limpopo from 1990, is a Johannesburg-based South African artist and printmaker. After completing high school and briefly studying Architecture at Intec College in 2011, he found his calling in printmaking, enrolling at the prestigious Artist Proof Studio in 2012. There, he specialized in the intricate technique of lino reduction. \\nCurrently working as a full-time artist, Mathonsi focuses on creating compelling, large-scale portraits, primarily of the significant women within his life and community. His detailed works serve to emphasize their importance and acknowledge their often-overlooked roles in society, particularly in raising children. The lines and textures in his portraits capture elements of time, age, history, and accumulated knowledge. Through his distinct mark-making and the incorporation of patterns referencing his Tsonga roots, Mathonsi elevates these humble women, creating a powerful visual record of his family tree and heritage while prompting viewers to recognize their profound contributions."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014058418397

item.title: Justice Mukheli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641561215197 Justice Mukheli 614 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640665927901 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013850865885", "gid://shopify/Product/9013850996957", "gid://shopify/Product/9013945696477", "gid://shopify/Product/9013945729245"] [20168,3166,3167,20170,3168,18986,18992] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"In his work, Mukheli is interested in capturing children in their moment of quietness. This interest was born out of his own retrospection, having grown up in the township of Soweto, Johannesburg. He had several character defining moments as a young boy and was constantly faced with statements such as, “Do not cry, you are a man and men don’t cry!”, “Don’t be week”, “Fix your face”, “Why are you sad”. He created his works from a place of attempting to capture some of the feelings and emotions that he was told not to express. These images became an index of spaces of possibility. To Mukheli, there is a golden thread that runs through each subject’s captivating gaze, glowing skin and uninhibited interaction with his lens. This thread points towards an answer, a solution or a guide book. He feels that he can be vulnerable openly as a man with no shame, and through these subjects he is reclaiming the emotions that he had to hold in as a young boy who was stopped from crying, being sad, or vulnerable, because “Boys don’t cry”. \\n \\nGroup Exhibition \\n \\n2019 An Estoteric Voyage Through Ecstasy , Redd Gallery, Chaniá, Greece . \\n \\nSolo Exhibition \\n \\n2018 Through Their Eyes , Daville Baille Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\nArt Fairs \\n \\n2019 Also Known as Africa , Art Fair, Paris, represented by Dyman Gallery. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013283422429 gid://shopify/Product/9013283487965 gid://shopify/Product/9013283520733 gid://shopify/Product/9013850865885 gid://shopify/Product/9013850996957 gid://shopify/Product/9013945696477 gid://shopify/Product/9013945729245

item.title: Justin Southey
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641563640029 Justin Southey 1573 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640667533533 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013381693661","gid://shopify/Product/9013381726429","gid://shopify/Product/9013410758877"] [13382,13384,14764] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Justin Southey's practice explores notions of landscapes and fantastical worlds that serve as metaphors for more unquantifiable emotional and spiritual spaces. \\n \\nActing like ephermal mirages, the artist's ambition is to explore and capture the intertwining and transcendent quality of the unseen. Capturing momentary feelings in a visual form, these investigations are both deeply personal and also often made in response to his immediate environment \\n \\nWith playful bold swathes of colour, texture and exuberant mark making, there is a push and pull the viewer experiences, directing the eye and stimulating the senses. \\n \\nThese ‘landscapes’ reveal melodious harmony and an overall narrative, and upon closer inspection investigating smaller worlds unfold, that invite the viewer to dream and imagine the atmosphere of physical space."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013381693661 gid://shopify/Product/9013381726429 gid://shopify/Product/9013410758877

item.title: Kabelo Kim Modise
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641564852445 Kabelo Kim Modise gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640667861213 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Visual artist, painter and printmaker, Kabelo Kim Modise was born in Francistown in Botswana and was schooled and studied further there. He taught at schools in Botswana, and then spend four years at the Botswana National Museum & Art Gallery in Gaborone. \\n \\nWhen Kabelo moved to Namibia, he studied for a diploma in visual arts at the University of Namibia, and he's currently undertaking a Batchelor of Visual Arts(BVA) through the University of South Africa(UNISA). For the past ten years, he has been lecturing textile design and printmaking at the College of the Arts in Windhoek/ Namibia. \\n \\nKabelo has always been inspired by Pop Art, and that influence is keenly felt in his works. Ever since he committed himself to his art, he's had numerous exhibitions and workshops in Namibia, Botswana, South Africa and internationally. He participated in several residencies outside of Namibia and for many years helped to organise the Namibian Tulipamwe International Artist Workshop. \\n \\nKabelo's signature works are his linocut prints. His style is quite unique as he bases his art online and rhythm. Hundreds of fine parallel lines resembling contour lines of a map reveal at closer observation objects and faces."}]}]}

item.title: Kaelik Dullaart

Growing up with photographer parents inspired Dullaart to pursue his own studies in photography at the Market Photo Workshop. His exposure to the medium has been an integral part of how he deals with imagery and composition in his creative process. \\n \\nDullaart is currently obsessed with drawings, predominantly working with pen on paper, however continues to explore multiple mediums such as handmade skateboard decks and self-publishes zines. Kaelik zooms into his interest in human behaviour, which is largely shaped by internal dialogues and prevalent expressions. It is Dullaart’s hope to build connections with his audience, both intellectual and emotional. \\n \\nDullaart’s work has been shown in group shows including “The Cat Show”, David Krut Projects, Joburg Art Fringe 2018, and has recently exhibited works with the Peanut Noir collective, at Through The Lens (TTLC), Victoria yards. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014055141597 gid://shopify/Product/9014055174365 gid://shopify/Product/9014055207133 gid://shopify/Product/9014055305437

item.title: Kaelo Molefe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641568162013 Kaelo Molefe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640668942557 [] Explore the thought-provoking artworks of Kaelo Molefe, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Molefe’s work delves into themes of identity, culture, and abstract expression, using striking visuals and intricate details to tell compelling stories. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kaelo Molefe (b. 1990) is an artist, independent researcher, and medical doctor based in Johannesburg. His multidisciplinary creative practice draws from his experience in clinical medicine and a deep interest in the socioeconomic histories of the Global South and historiographies of \"otherness\". \\nMolefe's work explores how power structures, representation, and concepts of normality are influenced by historical processes that have produced and institutionalized 'difference'. \\nThrough writing, mixed media, collage, and moving images, Molefe explores these socio-historical dynamics, offering a nuanced critique of how identities and powers are shaped by history. His artistic inquiry focuses on the intersection of health, politics, and the human condition, investigating the complexities of societal norms and the bureaucratization of marginalized identities. \\n \\nMolefe has exhibited at prestigious platfroms such as FNB Art Joburg (2023) and Turbine Art Fair (2022) in Johannesburg. His first solo exhibition, Other Schematics (2023), was held at Kalashnikovv Gallery in Johannesburg. He has also participated in group exhibitions, including Keystone at Kalashnikovv Gallery (2024) and Fresh Voices at Guns & Rain Gallery (2023). \\n \\nWith his unique blend of medical knowledge and artistic inquiry, Kaelo Molefe continues to challenge conventional narratives and broaden the discourse on identity and representation in contemporary art."}]}]}

item.title: Kagiso Diale
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641568489693 Kagiso Diale 2679 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640668975325 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014015885533","gid://shopify/Product/9014094495965","gid://shopify/Product/9014122447069"] Explore the powerful works of Kagiso Diale, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through striking compositions and a distinctive artistic voice, Diale’s work delves into themes of identity, culture, and social narratives, offering a compelling visual experience. [22398,25199,24545] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kagiso Diale was born at the end of Apartheid South Africa in 1994, on the 4th of July, and became part of the first “Born Free” generation in the country. \\nHe grew up and attended school in the township of Soweto, where his family still resides today. Despite being brought up in the ideology of a rainbow nation during his first eighteen years, Kagiso only became exposed to different races and backgrounds in his years at the University of the Witwatersrand, where he first studied mechanical engineering before he alternatively went on to obtain a Degree in the Bachelor of Architectural Studies. \\nHe uses his insights and experiences of the broader frame work of the South African tapestry to spark his creative thinking. In addition, he is informed by his experiences of growing up in a single parent household, living with his mother, his two sisters and his two brothers. He has a unique perspective at times almost that of an outsider looking in. His work explores and reflects on themes such as spirituality, violence, class differences, township architecture and history, and cultural identity in modern South Africa. He uses these themes to form an honest understanding of what makes up the idea of home. Kagiso uses mediums such as watercolour, charcoal and ink, and until recently, by printmaking through etching with Artist Proof Studio, to depict his works. He also explores his ideas and skills through digital art, illustrations, short films and animation. Once described by his lecturer as a “rough and untidy creative that yearns for clean work”, Kagiso tries not to soften the tone of each piece he creates, but to rather let it carry its story vehemently so."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014015885533 gid://shopify/Product/9014094495965 gid://shopify/Product/9014122447069

item.title: Kagiso Gundane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641569636573 Kagiso Gundane gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640669335773 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kagiso Gundane is a multidisciplinary visual artist, born and raised in the North West Province, South Africa. \\nBorn into a family of three, he is the oldest and only male among his siblings. Gundane has been fascinated and enthusiastic about art from a young age, and as a result pursued a visual arts degree at the University of Johannesburg. \\nHe works in a variety of art mediums, including; printmaking, drawing, sculpture and installations. Growing up among African traditional healers in his community, his subject matter is centered around African spirituality and cultural sensitivity in a post-colonial space. As a person with a spiritual gift, Gundane is more involved in his work to express his ideas and interpretations at a close and intimate level."}]}]}

item.title: Kagiso Patrick Mautloa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641570488541 Kagiso Patrick Mautloa 515 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640669401309 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013846933725", "gid://shopify/Product/9013846999261", "gid://shopify/Product/9014116778205", "gid://shopify/Product/9014116810973", "gid://shopify/Product/9014116876509", "gid://shopify/Product/9133222625501", "gid://shopify/Product/9133228949725", "gid://shopify/Product/9133229637853"] [25308,25168,25170,25169,18791,23886,18789] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kagiso Patrick Mautloa studied art at Rorke’s Drift Art Centre, KwaZulu Natal and at the Mofolo Art Centre in Soweto. He has participated in Thupelo and Triangle workshops, held numerous solo and group exhibitions, and has work in a number of important public collections across South Africa. \\n \\nHis work studies the street life around him and his studio at the Bag Factory (Fordsburg Artists Studios) in downtown Johannesburg. The women roasting mielies (corn) over coal-fired tin braziers on street corners, the wholesalers and hawkers selling cheap imports from the Far East, the street traders who eke out a living with a few items on a small board near the busy intersections. Working with figurative elements, abstract textures and multiple colour overlays, the work exploits the potential of lithography. Mautloa has made innovative use of drawing materials for these prints, using found objects as stencils through which to spray tusche and toner. Textures are an important part of Mautloa’s work, as he works he notices the mundane surfaces around him and will sometimes use these in his work. \\n \\nUnexpected things like the rough surface of a well-used cutting board, or a worn-out cotton rag, hold a new fascination and beauty for him. Delicate drawing and seemingly random splatter, entice the viewer and challenge one to look at the world in a new way. Kagiso Patrick Mautloa is an artist whose work eludes a neat definition, as he is as comfortable in his abstract work as he is in the more figurative imagery. Most of his work is in oils and acrylic but he has also included found objects and collage in his two dimensional work and has also done a number of installations as well as doing photographic work."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013846933725 gid://shopify/Product/9013846999261 gid://shopify/Product/9014116778205 gid://shopify/Product/9014116810973 gid://shopify/Product/9014116876509 gid://shopify/Product/9133222625501 gid://shopify/Product/9133228949725 gid://shopify/Product/9133229048029 gid://shopify/Product/9133229211869 gid://shopify/Product/9133229637853 gid://shopify/Product/9133229703389

item.title: Kaleab Abate
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641577500893 Kaleab Abate 2394 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640670613725 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013849358557","gid://shopify/Product/9013850538205","gid://shopify/Product/9013920891101","gid://shopify/Product/9013922988253","gid://shopify/Product/9013923676381","gid://shopify/Product/9013924233437","gid://shopify/Product/9013924298973","gid://shopify/Product/9013924397277","gid://shopify/Product/9013942059229"] [19280,18974,19294,19295,19291,19285] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kaleab Abate was born in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia in 1998, where he also currently lives and works. In 2021, he graduated from the renowned Ale School of Fine Arts and Design, Addis Ababa, with a focus on printmaking. He has shown at Art on Paper Brussels, 1-54 London, INVESTEC Cape Town Art Fair and African Galleries Now x Artsy, and has completed a 3-month residency at Silhouette Projects in Kampala. He was part of the group exhibition Eastern Voices: Contemporary Art from East Africa at Addis Fine Art, London (2023) and Form and Fantasy at Afriart Gallery, Kampala (2024). \\n \\nEmploying various printmaking techniques, different materials, charcoal drawing, among others, allows Ethiopian artist Kaleab Abate (*1998) to experiment with different layers in his works on paper and canvas. Beginning with a portrait in which he focuses on emotions and expression rather than the likeness of his subject, he then allows the material and printmaking patterns to guide his compositions intuitively. \\n \\nHe allows bodily shapes to fragment and deform into layers, some rich, others delicate, half-transparent, or patterned, adding his distinct surreal twist. Abate’s layering technique becomes a process to imagine and visualize the complex depths of the stories that may live within the bodies he depicts. \\n \\nAbate’s composition is loaded with unexpected forms and textures, the majority of which are unrealistic. Figures are distorted, shapes are erratic, and color options are limited. The vast majority of events are unreal. This daring fantasy piques the artist’s interest. His creations, however, have a considerable amount of realism. This is why he regards his works as “fantasized realities”. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013849358557 gid://shopify/Product/9013850538205 gid://shopify/Product/9013920891101 gid://shopify/Product/9013922988253 gid://shopify/Product/9013923676381 gid://shopify/Product/9013924233437 gid://shopify/Product/9013924298973 gid://shopify/Product/9013924397277 gid://shopify/Product/9013942059229

item.title: Kalenga Nkonge
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641577861341 Kalenga Nkonge gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650723606749 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kalenga (aka bonkoti) Nkonge’s images are captured digitally and during long extensive walks \\nthat he takes around Lusaka. In his current body of work the images are predominantly taken in \\nLusaka’s markets, busy residential areas, and wherever inspiration shows itself. When he’s \\nshooting in busy areas he likes to capture people in their element, preferring to “shoot from the \\nhip”, allowing him to be both participant and observer of a moment. There are equally special \\nmoments on his adventures where he gets to interact with the people he meets and he’s \\nafforded the opportunity of taking portraits. There usually isn't a predefined idea of what he will \\ncapture, which he sees as a plus in his process, as he likes to be surprised by the compositions, \\ncolours, and stories that the space will present. Kalenga’s photography work centres, as its \\nsubject, the ordinary Zambian and the everyday Zambian experience. The documentary style of \\nhis photography is mixed with equal portions of grit, humour, and colour."}]}]}

item.title: Kamal El Feky
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641579663581 Kamal El Feky gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640671006941 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014013755613"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Artist Kamal Al-Feki was born in 1984, earned a Bachelor Degree in fine arts 2006 Sculpture Department field, fine art college, Helwan University with honours. He has been an active member of the Syndicate of Fine Artists in Cairo, joined the (academia d’Egitto) in Rome, Italy (2016) and participated in many exhibitions and international cultural figures inside Egypt and abroad from 2007 to now. \\n \\nEl Feki’s sculptures is an attempt to capture the familiar yet foreign concept of waiting. The artist evokes the viewer to become content with the uncomfortable pause that his weighted figures narrate in their ageless suspension. The sculptures presents the futile, yet adventurous journey of becoming and the perpetuating cycles of human desire that accompany that role. Kamal’s Sculptures illustrates human life cycles as a concrete plexus of events and desires. They draw us into a state of stillness, anticipation and entraps the viewer in a dormant state of reflection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013307703517 gid://shopify/Product/9013307769053 gid://shopify/Product/9013314978013 gid://shopify/Product/9014013755613

item.title: Kaloki Nyamai
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641579008221 Kaloki Nyamai gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640670777565 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kaloki Nyamai, born in 1985 in Kitui, Kenya, lives and works in Nairobi. His first inspirations were his mother, who worked in fashion, and his grand-mother, who was a musician. It is his mother who first taught him how to draw and his grand-mother who would recount the stories history books do not tell. Drawing heavily on the stories of the Kamba people he was told by his grand-mother, Nyamai – a multidisciplinary artist who studied interior design, film and taught art classes before dedicating himself to his craft – explores how history and identity are intertwined. His works are multimedia and characterized by rich layers, offering fragments to be pieced together slowly. The lengthy, searching process employed in the making of the works is mirrored in the experience of viewing them. His work as been presented in fairs and exhibitions in Africa and Europe. In 2018, he participated in the third edition of the Kampala Biennale, curated by Simon Njami, with a monumental installation. \\nHis painting practice entwines material investigation with a wide-reaching exploration of subject matter. Grounded in hidden narratives, uneasy stories of identity, environment and memory, offering fragments to be pieced together slowly. The lengthy, searching process employed in the making of the works is mirrored in the experience of viewing them. In early works the artist documented the slum settlement that he grew up in. These charcoal pieces are intended to capture a space in flux, to preserve an impression of these fragile sites. But they were also about adding complexity to widely held perceptions of such environments. His work has developed a lot since these pieces, Kaloki’s subject remains closely connected. Nyamai explores the parallels between the past and the present through richly-layered, multimedia works. Drawing heavily on the stories of the Kamba people, the works explore how history and identity are intertwined and how this has informed the identities of people living in present day, post-colonial Kenya. \\n'I think of my work as an open, multilayered conversation through which I question identity and how the tensions between past, present and future affect the way we are perceived and perceive ourselves to be. By layering and experimenting with different mediums, people, animals and abstract forms are revealed, working as symbols that help us look beyond the History we are taught in school, to the rich, often contradictory history made up of the stories of our ancestors shared directly, generation after generation, that took place before and without colonialism. It is only within and through these stories that we can begin the process of layering and texturing the flat identities provided to us by an education burdened by colonialism and its legacy.' - Kaloki Nyamai"}]}]}

[23581,23438,23433,23435,23431,23436,23434,23437,23432,23582] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kamogelo \"Monox\" Litheko, originally from Parys in the Free State, is a self-taught artist whose work explores grief, love, and manhood through a Black lens. His creative journey began in photography and graphic design, but in 2021, he transitioned to painting as a way to express himself more freely. This shift allowed him to move beyond digital constraints, embracing the raw, instinctive nature of painting to tell deeply personal stories. \\nInfluenced by skate culture, fashion, street art, and photography, Monox’s work is a reflection of his experiences navigating identity, emotion, and personal growth. His pieces embody a sense of imperfection, using layered textures and bold compositions to capture the complexities of the human experience. For him, painting is not just about creating image ,it is a therapeutic process, helping him make sense of the world and manage the stresses of city life while immersing himself within the culture to draw inspiration for his stories. \\nThrough his art, Monox invites viewers into an intimate exploration of vulnerability and resilience in an attempt to reframe his perspective of the South African black experience. His evolving body of work continues to shape contemporary African art, offering a raw and honest perspective that speaks to both personal and collective experiences. Each piece stands as a testament to self-discovery and the power of visual storytelling. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014045212893 gid://shopify/Product/9014045245661 gid://shopify/Product/9014045278429 gid://shopify/Product/9014045343965 gid://shopify/Product/9014045409501 gid://shopify/Product/9014045442269 gid://shopify/Product/9014045540573 gid://shopify/Product/9014050619613 gid://shopify/Product/9014050652381
