He lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nHe is currently in his final year, completing a BA Fine Art degree at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (UCT). He received a Diploma in Fine Art at Ruth Prowse School of Art in 2019 where he also won the Ruth Prowse Award for his body of work An Exhaustive Catalogue of Texts Dealing with the Orient which explored Edward Said’s concept of Orientalism using Said’s eponymous book (1978) as the source material. \\nIn 2021 Bineshtarigh was awarded a Creative Knowledge Resources (CKR) Fellowship: CKR is an interdisciplinary project by the National Research Foundation & UCT studying socially engaged artistic practices in Africa and its diaspora. \\nBineshtarigh works in a variety of media, most notably painting and video. His conceptual concerns range from language, (mis)communication as well as the practice of writing and transliteration \\n \\nIn 2021 Bineshtarigh was awarded a Creative Knowledge Resources (CKR) Fellowship: CKR is an interdisciplinary project by the National Research Foundation UCT studying socially engaged artistic practices in Africa and its diaspora. Bineshtarigh works in a variety of media, most notably painting and video. His conceptual concerns range from language, (mis)communication as well as the practice of writing and transliteration."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013315567837

item.title: Kamohelo Blessing Rooi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641583956189 Kamohelo Blessing Rooi 2230 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640672121053 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014085157085","gid://shopify/Product/9014085189853","gid://shopify/Product/9014085222621","gid://shopify/Product/9014085320925","gid://shopify/Product/9014085353693","gid://shopify/Product/9014085386461","gid://shopify/Product/9014085419229","gid://shopify/Product/9014085451997","gid://shopify/Product/9014085550301","gid://shopify/Product/9014085583069","gid://shopify/Product/9014103245021"] [24377,24375,24376,24378,24379,24380,24381,24785,24373,24374,24382] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kamohelo Blessing Rooi is a South African artist born in the province of Gauteng in 2001. \\nRooi's work centres around the artist's personal connection to the township and interrogates the emotional landscape of Soweto, where he currently lives and works. \\n \\nRooi's interest in the arts was first initiated through 'arts and crafts', classes where he was introduced to Nelson Makamo, Wonder Buhle Mbambo and Jean Michel Basquiat, who became significant influences. \\n \\nWorking primarily in Acrylic on Canvas, Rooi has established his style through a series titled; 'Kasiflavour' which translates to 'Location Flavour', highlighting his deep affection for the township. Rooi paints stills, culled from both his own photobook collection and personal experiences to capture Soweto's nocturnal allure through his use of bright colours and flat brush strokes. \\n \\nThe moments captured in Rooi's paintings are the result of a delicate balance between recollection and interpretation. Whether it's an intimate moment between friends or figures staged against the Sowetan landscape - Rooi's reverence for his richly diverse home and its inhabitants is paramount."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014085157085 gid://shopify/Product/9014085189853 gid://shopify/Product/9014085222621 gid://shopify/Product/9014085320925 gid://shopify/Product/9014085353693 gid://shopify/Product/9014085386461 gid://shopify/Product/9014085419229 gid://shopify/Product/9014085451997 gid://shopify/Product/9014085550301 gid://shopify/Product/9014085583069 gid://shopify/Product/9014103245021

item.title: Karabo Johannes Phaho
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641586020573 Karabo Johannes Phaho gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640672350429 [] Discover the work of Karabo Johannes Phaho, a South African artist blending acrylics, charcoal, and pastels to express themes of spirituality, emotion, and lived experience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karabo Johannes Phaho (b.2001, Mokopane, Limpopo), is a multidisciplinary artist whose work explore spirituality, emotion, and identity through mixed media. After earning a BCOm in Marketing and Management in 2022, he completed a Postgraduate Diploma in Business Administration at Wits Business School in 2023, before committing fully to his art practice. \\nPhaho's creative journey began in childhood, where drawing became a tool for self-expression. Since 2020, he has developed a distinct style using acrylics, charcoal, oil pastels, and pencil on surfaces such as paper, cardboard, and canvas. His work is deeply personal, shaped by life experiences and a search for meaning within broader social and spiritual contexts. \\n \\nThe primary school years were a vital period in the artist's career because it was at this point that he would be introduced to pencils and drawing. Creating visual representations gradually became an important part of expressing the feelings and thoughts of Phago. It had always been a hobby but became a profession in 2020 which was his first year of tertiary education. During this time he would explore his craft by painting or drawing on unrelated surfaces such as paper, wood, clothes and even cement walls. Over the years his style would mature into using mixed media (primarily acrylic paint, charcoal, oil pastels, pencils) on paper, cardboard and canvas. He draws the majority of his inspiration from life experiences in aspects relating to spirituality, relationships, emotions, mentality, invocations and his position in the world and society."}]}]}

item.title: Karabo Maine
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641586643165 Karabo Maine 2561 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640673038557 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013975580893","gid://shopify/Product/9013976989917","gid://shopify/Product/9013977088221","gid://shopify/Product/9013977186525","gid://shopify/Product/9013977284829"] [20950,20943,20944,20945,20929,20949,20952] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karabo Maine (b. 1986, Gaborone, Botswana) is a visual artist currently residing and practicing in his hometown. He holds a BA Fine Art (Photography) from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. He has exhibited his artwork in several exhibitions in Gaborone, as well as at the FNB Art Joburg Art Fair in 2022. \\n \\nKarabo Maine's artistic practice not only celebrates the aesthetic richness of his subjects but also invites contemplation on societal narratives and personal introspection through his own lens. Importantly, Maine's artistic practice is deeply personal, informed by his own experiences as a recovering individual. This perspective adds a layer of authenticity and empathy to his work."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013975580893 gid://shopify/Product/9013976989917 gid://shopify/Product/9013977088221 gid://shopify/Product/9013977186525 gid://shopify/Product/9013977284829

item.title: Karin Basel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641587265757 Karin Basel gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640673399005 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karin Basel is an artist and lecturer based in Johannesburg. She currently teaches theory and history for the Visual Art and Design Theory a the University of Johannesburg. She has a masters in Visual Art, obtained from the University of the Johannesburg. She also runs coaching sessions for aspiring artists. Her art education was initially focused on painting and drawing but she is currently making artists books. She is interested in working with a variety of materials, such as thread, wire, paper and found objects, these are incorporated into the books which focus on how we record and engage with time and place."}]}]}

item.title: Karin Daymond
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641591689437 Karin Daymond 301 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640673628381 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013293514973"] [4276,4275] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karin Daymond’s work is strongly rooted in the South African landscape. \\n \\n“Although a work starts from a geographical point, it quickly becomes my inner space. I live within this space even during more mundane activities. I become involved with the possibilities of paint and design; how they can be used to describe an environment, but also how the marks, textures, patterns can capture the energy and rhythm of both the external and internal landscapes that I associate with a place”. \\n \\nShe speaks of landscapes as having an emotional identity, for instance the vegetation in the Karoo is restrained and cautious, while the natural growth in the Lowveld of Mpumalanga is flamboyant. Intensive mark-making, patterning and colour create a world within a world. “Sometimes a landscape enhances my sense of self and how I belong, and sometimes it’s the other way around”. The exploration of belonging is central to much of her work, most recently explored in the context of migrancy and refugeedom. \\n \\nDaymond works from her studio in Mpumalanga, a province known for its sub-tropical beauty. She committed to her full–time art practice in 2008, following many years of teaching. Her primary medium is large-scale oil painting. Drawing and printmaking, particularly lithography, form an integral part of her work. \\n \\nDaymond was born in 1967 in Durban, South Africa and has a BA Fine Art from The University of KwaZulu-Natal. She lives in Nelspruit, Mpumalanga. Her work is included in many public and private collections, both in South Africa and internationally. Amongst these are the UNISA collection and the University of the North-West."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013293514973 gid://shopify/Product/9013293547741

item.title: Karin Miller
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641596080349 Karin Miller 682 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640673923293 [2602,2603,2600,2604,2597,2599,2601,2598] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karin Miller is a truly South African artist, focusing on digital collage and the new media. To generate images of outstanding quality, Miller combines traditional artwork skills and photography with modern technology. In creating a fusion of past and present, personal and public, Miller has developed a unique style that exudes a rich eclecticism, playfulness, quirky humour and the post-modern element of neo-baroque. Each facet of the image is carefully chosen and placed to form unexpected combinations and compositions. She explains that sometimes ‘I spend days looking for a haunting face in an old photograph, or a beautiful pattern in an antique print’. Her tactic is to transform the everyday into something captivating. With meticulous attention to detail, she can convey theatrical flamboyance, splashes of parody or just about any mood or setting. Nonetheless, her work often subtly suggests a uniquely South African ambience. Miller has been exclusively signed with the ManZArt gallery, based in Franschhoek, South Africa, since the beginning of her fine art career where she has been given numerous solo shows at our Cape Town and Franschhoek spaces. In addition, she has showcased special commissions, group shows and interim presentations in other locations, including France and Germany. \\n \\nMiller’s works are in many important national and international collections and have an ever increasing following throughout the world – a truly South African artist whose longing for beauty in the world often hides the intrinsic agenda of each work – an artist who never judges, but instigates – who never instructs, but offers, inspires and allows for a long lasting connection between art and its viewer."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013279981789 gid://shopify/Product/9013280047325 gid://shopify/Product/9013280112861 gid://shopify/Product/9013280145629 gid://shopify/Product/9013280178397 gid://shopify/Product/9013280211165 gid://shopify/Product/9013280276701 gid://shopify/Product/9013280309469

[24672,24668,24666,24664,24671,24669,24670,24665,24673,24667] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karin Preller is a Johannesburg-based artist and academic. After a brief career in law, she pursued her passion for art, earning a BA(FA) (cum laude) from Unisa and an MA(FA) (cum laude) from the University of the Witwatersrand. She completed her PhD in Art and Design at the University of Johannesburg in June 2024. \\nPreller's paintings are known for capturing the haunting and strange within the mundane, through snapshots and still lives. Her distinctive style references moments frozen in time, revealing layers of memory and forgetfulness. Her work chronicles ordinary, paused stories—interrupted narratives and lost tales. \\nHer solo exhibitions include: \\n \\n Family Albumat ABSA gallery in 2001 \\n Snapshots at GordartGallery in 2007 \\n Aperture at Fried Contemporary in 2008 \\n Stills at Artspace (now Lizamore and Associates) in 2009 \\n City and Suburban at the Standard Bank Gallery in 2010 \\n Just above the mantelpiece at Artspace in 2013 \\n Stilled lives at Lizamore and Associates in 2015 \\n Stilled lives II at the Association of Arts in 2018 \\n Almost no memory at Lizamore and Associates in 2020 \\n Beyond memory at the 2022 KKNK \\n Alles in foto’s at Woordfees, Stellenbosch, 2024 \\n \\nPreller has received several accolades, including the 2022 KKNK KANNA award and a nomination for a KykNET Fi?sta for her exhibition Beyond Memory. Her work is part of prestigious collections such as The Johannesburg Art Gallery, Sasol, ABSA, Unisa, Oliewenhuis Art Museum, The Public Protector, ATKV, the Pretoria Art Museum, and the Standard Bank."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014083977437 gid://shopify/Product/9014098821341 gid://shopify/Product/9014098854109 gid://shopify/Product/9014098886877 gid://shopify/Product/9014098919645 gid://shopify/Product/9014098952413 gid://shopify/Product/9014098985181 gid://shopify/Product/9014099017949 gid://shopify/Product/9014099050717 gid://shopify/Product/9014099083485 gid://shopify/Product/9014099116253 gid://shopify/Product/9133230784733 gid://shopify/Product/9133230817501 gid://shopify/Product/9133233799389 gid://shopify/Product/9133234127069 gid://shopify/Product/9134146617565

item.title: Karla Nixon
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641598013661 Karla Nixon gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640674480349 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Karla Nixon, born in 1990, spent her early childhood on a sugarcane estate in Swaziland before relocating to Durban, South Africa. She is a Durban based artist who predominantly works with paper. She hand-cuts, tears and sculpts intricate images and objects, drawn from her surrounding environments. More recently her work has used this medium to explore themes around colour, texture, textiles and land. Nixon completed her Master’s degree in Fine Art in 2017 at the Durban University of Technology, South Africa. Her degree focused on transience in the work of paper artists, which she completed with Cum Laude. Nixon was awarded and completed an artist residency in Bremen, Germany, in 2017-18. She has been selected as a finalist in both the Sasol and ABSA art competitions. Nixon has participated in a number of group shows in Durban, Cape Town and Johannesburg, and has had a few solo shows the most recent being, Crease, in 2021 at State of the Art Gallery, Cape Town. Her work is in private collections in South Africa, Lebanon, Australia, Spain and Holland to name a few. As well as in public collections including the Durban Art Gallery and The National Art Bank. Nixon is currently lecturing 2D and 3D studies in the Arts Extended Curriculum Program at The Durban University of Technology."}]}]}

item.title: Kate Gottgens
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641598275805 Kate Gottgens gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640674545885 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kate Gottgens was born in 1965 in Durban, South Africa, and currently lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. Gottgens graduated from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town, in 1987. She was the recipient of the Ampersand Fellowship Award, resulting in a residency in New York City, USA, in 2019, and was selected for the prestigious Thames & Hudson publication, 100 Painters of Tomorrow in 2014. \\n \\nGottgens presented a solo exhibition titled Whispering of Ghosts at the Boschendal Norval Art Gallery, in Stellenbosch South Africa. In 2020, Gottgens presented her critically-acclaimed solo exhibition, Skyglow on Mars Black, at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town. Earlier solo exhibitions include: Tired from Smiling at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town (2017); Famine at SMAC Gallery in Johannesburg (2016); Infinite Loop at SMAC Gallery in Stellenbosch; and Savage Nature at Espacio Liquido in Gijon, Spain (both in 2014); and MALICE Aforethought at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town (2013). \\n \\nFurther selected group exhibitions include: A Show of Solidarity, a group exhibition in support of the South African Solidarity Fund during a nationwide enforced lockdown, at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town (2020); the Ampersand Foundation Award 21 years celebration exhibition curated by Gordon Froud at the University of Johannesburg Art Gallery in Johannesburg; and Suitcase Show, at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town, as part of the group show in collaboration with Galleria Massimo Minin, both in 2019; Bathing, curated by Brian Shure at Planthouse Gallery in New York City, USA (2018); Summer Show ’16 at SMAC Gallery in Stellenbosch, South Africa (2016); Imago Mundi, a travelling exhibition held at Museo Carlo Bilotti, Rome and Ca’ dei Carraresi in Treviso, Italy, both in 2014; the 8th New Delhi Triennale in India in 1994 and Scurvy at the Castle of Good Hope in Cape Town in 1995. \\n \\nGottgens’ art fair participation includes a solo booth at Untitled, Art in Miami Beach, USA in 2019, as well as group presentations at artmonte-carlo in Monaco, Artissima in Turin, Italy, and Miart in Milan, among others."}]}]}

item.title: Kate Otten
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641601650909 Kate Otten 2469 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640678478045 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013934817501"] [19483] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kate Otten is a South African architect, who has won numerous awards for her South African traditional work. After working for a number of other practices, Otten established her own firm in 1989 in Johannesburg. \\nShe has designed community libraries, the waterfront development at Tzaneen, an art therapy centre in Soweto and the museum exhibition space at the former Women's Jail at Constitution Hill which received a commendation from the South African Institute of Architects (SAIA). \\nKate has won many awards including the SAIA Award of Merit House Staude in 1998 to the Mbokodo Awards Architecture and Creative Design in 2013."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013934817501

item.title: Kate Schärf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641602175197 Kate Schärf gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640681591005 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kate Schärf (b.1993, Pietermaritzburg, KZN) is a full-time artist, living and working in Cape Town. She holds a Master’s degree in Visual Art from the University of Stellenbosch, graduating in 2021. She obtained her BA Fine Art degree from the same university in 2018. \\n \\nKate focuses exclusively on creating two-dimensional artworks in a variety of media, from printmaking to drawing and painting. She is mostly known for her immersive charcoal drawings, which were a sell-out at her graduate exhibition in 2018 (also known as Grad’EX). She soon began exhibiting in various galleries within the Western Cape. \\n \\nPlants and gardens are the inspiration behind Kate’s work, in the construction of what she calls ‘foliagescapes’. Her work is an expression of the uplifting, calming and reassuring qualities inherent in nature, therefore attempting to bring contentment and tranquillity to the viewer. By utilising soothing colours in her paintings and constructing harmonious, balanced compositions, Kate endeavours to create art that invites the audience inward in quiet contemplation. Through the constant process of layering and erasure, her work is a manifestation of the love of complexity, a fascination with the intricate, the intertwined, and the interconnectedness of organic structures. \\n \\nKate’s artworks have been obtained by various private collectors, and are also in the permanent collection of Ebony Curated. She has exhibited at a number of Western Cape Galleries, such as RK Contemporary (Riebeek Kasteel), Rust-en-Vrede (Durbanville), Art on Avenues (Somerset West), and Mullers Gallery (Cape Town). \\n \\nShe is the guest curator of Entangled at RK Contemporary, a group exhibition on show for the month of April, 2023."}]}]}

item.title: Katharien de Villiers
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641602961629 Katharien de Villiers gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640683393245 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Through tactile manipulations involving the juxtaposition and de-contextualisation of material, Katharien de Villiers calls on the sensorial, mental and physical capacities of her audience. Her paintings, sculptures and site-specific installations consider the spatial and relational dynamics of space and the relationship between the work and the viewer. Katharien de Villiers is based in Cape Town."}]}]}

item.title: Kathy Robins
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641605615837 Kathy Robins gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640686080221 [] Discover the work of Kathy Robins is a multidisciplinary artist and community activist, whose work engages with themes of displacement, ecological issues, and social connection through sustainable development projects and exhibitions. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kathy Robins is a seasoned professional with a career that spans community development, art, design, and social activism. In 1999, she founded a Corporate Social Responsibility Programme and has since contributed to sustainable development projects, such as community gardens and entrepreneurship initiatives. She holds a BA in Social Science from the University of Cape Town (UCT), a degree in Textile and Product Design from Parsons School of Design in New York, and an MA in Fine Art from UCT's Michaelis School of Fine Art. \\n \\nAs an artist, Robins has participated in numerous exhibitions both locally and internationally. Her work explores themes of displacement, home, and the intersection of contemporary ecological and socio-political issues. Using natural materials and organic forms, she reflects on humanity's connection to nature and the current global challenges of physical and social displacement."}]}]}

item.title: Katherine Spindler
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641604174045 Katherine Spindler gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640685129949 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The unlikely marriage of movement and stillness, of tumult and quietude, is a defining characteristic of Katherine Spindler’s oeuvre, eliciting a similar mix of emotion in the viewer. In examining Spindler’s paintings, one has the sense that things are moving just beneath and beyond the surface, too vast to fully perceive or understand. With a quiet immensity and arresting gravitas, Spindler’s work sees light and shadow flicker and evade, swirl in eddies, swell and recede. The surface of the canvas, like water, is unstable, constantly shifting and undulating while maintaining a meditative stillness that both captivates and mystifies. Often blurring, veiling, or erasing the images she works with, Spindler’s intention is to evoke rather than explicate, to suggest more than to prescribe."}]}]}

item.title: Katja Abbott
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641605746909 Katja Abbott gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640686211293 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"After completing a National Diploma in Graphic Design at the Cape Technikon, I worked for many years in the publishing industry as a book designer, illustrator, editor and project manager. To fulfill my desire to engage in hands-on art-making, as opposed to computer-based design, I embarked on a Bachelors Degree in Visual Arts through UNISA in 2015. \\n \\nArtist’s statement \\nMy art is a silver rabbit \\nfoolishness trying to understand \\nIt’s an ache for real, for life’s bitter ecstasy \\nfor this is how it is \\n \\nMy art is a storm that \\nthrows things around \\nBecause it can \\nBecause things want to be moved \\n \\nMy art is incomplete, \\nunwilling \\na poem, a lament \\nIt’s a hundred songs sung at the same time \\nluminous, discordant \\n \\nMy art is salvation \\na temple \\na balm for passion and confusion \\na possession, an affliction \\na cat that won’t be told or tamed \\nIt is never good enough \\nor has time enough \\nIt is impatient \\nlike the flight of a thousand swallows \\nto the sun"}]}]}

item.title: Katlego Love Sithole
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641606140125 Katlego Love Sithole [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Initially embarking on a journey in the world of accounting, I quickly realized that its confines stifled my creative spirit. In 2019, I broke free from those limitations and wholeheartedly embraced graphic design as a self-taught discipline. Art flowed through me effortlessly, and in my creative process, I see myself as an architect constructing a visual language that transcends conventional boundaries. \\nThrough my artwork, I venture into diverse subjects, delving deep into the intricate layers of the black body and its perception of self. I confront the false narratives perpetuated by external influences, revealing how society has veered the black body away from its natural origins. This detachment has led to a resentful disconnection from our own inherent connection with nature. Tragically, this internal struggle manifests in our relationship with ourselves, as we unconsciously inflict harm upon our bodies, manipulated by the ignorance propagated by those who seek to exploit and control our very essence. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Katlego Tlabela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641608499421 Katlego Tlabela 2004 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640687849693 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013403123933"] [14441] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Multidisciplinary artist Katlego Tlabela creates work that examines social and political crises in post-apartheid South Africa. He employs painting, sound, photography, and sculptural installations to spark important dialogues surrounding race and representation. \\n \\nAfter graduating from the University of Cape Town’s Michaelis School of Fine Art, where he majored in printmaking, Tlabela began showing work in group exhibitions throughout South Africa. Though at first reluctant to call himself a painter due to his formal training as a printmaker, Tlabela has received attention for his paintings depicting Black subjects in positions of leisure and luxurious domestic settings. These works—often composed of acrylic, ink, and collage on canvas—feature sprawling interiors, high-end furniture, and walls adorned with colorful artwork."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013403123933

item.title: Kato BC
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641608827101 Kato BC gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640687915229 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013982003421","gid://shopify/Product/9013982036189"] Kato BC {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kato BC, born in 1997 in Masaka, Uganda, is a painter whose work explores the delicate balance between constraints and freedoms experienced by religious leaders in Africa. He sheds light on the complex challenges and opportunities these leaders face as they navigate societal expectations, internal religious hierarchies, and political landscapes within diverse cultural and social contexts. His artistic vision is deeply influenced by the shadows of his childhood, especially the impact of his twin sister’s blindness. These personal experiences have heightened his sensitivity to light, shape, and form. His artworks reflect both his introspective journey and keen observations of the world around him. He offers a nuanced perspective on the intersections of faith, culture, and power, capturing the subtle tensions and harmonies that define the lives of religious leaders. He explores the human condition, inviting viewers to engage with the intricate dynamics of belief and authority. Through his evocative use of color, patterns, and texture, Kato BC’s paintings provide a window into the multifaceted experiences of those who lead and serve within religious communities. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013982003421 gid://shopify/Product/9013982036189

item.title: Kay-Leigh Fisher & Nadia Myburgh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641609187549 Kay-Leigh Fisher & Nadia Myburgh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640690634973 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kay-Leigh Fisher is a visual artist, curator and publisher based in Johannesburg. She holds an Honours in Curatorship degree from Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (2020) and a Bachelor’s Degree in Fine Arts from the University of Witwatersrand (2019). Her research and practice focuses on themes and narratives of becoming, thinking through familiar relationships with objects and how they reinforce ideals around racial and gendered identity. \\n \\nHer portraits speak to a multiplicity of identities that exist within an individual. The artist as part of her practice creates publications as curatorial interventions which speak to the ambiguity of being and the unlearning that occurs in counter-cultural spaces. Fisher holds an Honours in Curatorship degree from Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (2020) and a Bachelor’s Degree in Fine Arts from the University of Witwatersrand (2019). Currently she is a Programme Associate at The Johannesburg Contemporary Art Foundation (JCAF) and held the post of Assistant Curator at the Constitutional Court‘s Art Collection, Constitutional Court of South Africa. \\nFisher is a co-recipient of the Bag Factory Artist Studios Young Womxn Studio Bursary (2023). \\n \\nNadia Laila Myburgh, is a Johannesburg based artist and energy healer. She completed her BA (Fine Art) Degree at the University of the Witwatersrand in 2016 and went on to complete the Advanced Programme in Photography at the Market Photo Workshop in 2017. She works in and outside of liminal spaces, especially the spaces of the unseen in all of its configurations. Both her artistic and energy healing practices navigate these spaces, to find ways in which to re-member “lost” or “forgotten” aspects of being-ness. Within her artistic practice she is interested in navigating and understanding the ways in which cultural and ancestral knowledges, practices and legacies are preserved and the ways in which they are accessed through story-telling, re-memory work and dreaming. She has had work included in exhibitions such as the VI New Media Arts Festival - IVAHM ’17 (International Video Art House Madrid) (2017), FNB Joburg Art Fair 2017 [Cartier booth] – Collaboration between Market Photo Workshop and international jewellery company Cartier, was part of the group exhibition ‘No Other Country: The Gospel According to Chris Hani’ (2015) and was a finalist for Sasol New Signatures (2014 and 2015)."}]}]}

item.title: Kayode Ejioye
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641609679069 Kayode Ejioye gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640690766045 [] Kayode Ejioye (b. 1985, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist renowned for his emotive figurative portraits that explore themes of black identity, cultural narratives, and personal introspection. His work merges bold color palettes with layered symbolism, offering a nuanced perspective on the human experience. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Ikole-Ekiti in 1985, Kayode Ejioye hails from Ekiti State, southwest Nigeria. While still in secondary school as an early teenager with a sprouting passion for creativity, he signed up for apprenticeship at Momsam Publicity in Lagos, where he learned publicity graphics – (sign-writing, screen printing et al) – after normal school hours. The young Kayode later on proceeded to study Drawing and Painting at the Ultimate Art Gallery & ArtPoint Studio, also in Lagos. \\nHe obtained an OND certificate in General Art from the department of Art and Industrial Design, Lagos State Polytechnic, Ikorodu. In his quest to attain higher artistic erudition and professionalism, he further reapplied in the same institution and bagged HND. He approaches his works: depicting the black body, especially the male in a position of power , force, hope, beauty and elegance with a modern day fashion trends. \\nHis preferred medium is acrylic on canvass. He has partaken in many group art exhibitions and his works can be found in galleries and private collections in Nigeria and beyond. Kayode is a full time studio artist in his Lagos base. Artist statement: My art this time must be self inclusion. the black body must take a center-stage, prominence so that it has the equall opportunity with the rest of other colours in the world. The black body must be glorified now and forever! This is why I paint black body. selected exhibitions/ auctions 1:\" collagist\" : focus on kayode\" online art exhibition, Taag gallery. Chelsea art district, new York. \\n \\n2022 2: \"Broken shackles\" an online group art exhibition, Taag gallery. Chelsea art district, new York 3:\"Genesis\" a group exhibition, okomoko art gallery, Lagos Nigeria. 2022. 4:\"the affordable art exhibition\" mydrim gallery, 2018. Lagos Nigeria 5:\"Signature and sogal art auction\", signature art gallery. lagos Nigeria. 2016. 6:\"Signature and sogal art auction\" signature art gallery, lagos Nigeria. 2015 7:\"Oreze\" --the kings crown, The cultural center, onisha, 2014 8:\"young shall grow\" Heritage bank PLC , Lagos Nigeria,2013 ‘Figureblox’ online solo show , 2024 @ taag gallery. \\n"}]}]}

Seema exploring themes of culture, spirituality, and personal reflection. Her work explores the politics of the black female body and identity, using various art forms such as monotypes, photography, and mixed media. Seema is currently the 2024 recipient of the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize. \\nSeema has been a part of various group exhibitions including : TAF Paper Exhibition (2023); University of Pretoria, Group Exhibition (2023); Among The Lilies (2023); Son of Langa presents: Brown Flesh Tales (2023); Turbine Art Fair, Unearthed (2023); Sasol New Signatures (2021); Alter Ego Sculpture Exhibition (2020); First Rand x Mmarthouse (2019); Emergence and Thou Art Women at Mmarthouse (2018)"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013983051997 gid://shopify/Product/9013983150301 gid://shopify/Product/9013983215837 gid://shopify/Product/9013983346909 gid://shopify/Product/9133223248093 gid://shopify/Product/9133223280861 gid://shopify/Product/9133225279709

Through her yarn paintings, she weaves stories of Black joy and fantasy, drawing inspiration from her own experiences and the cultural milieu of Tembisa \\nMaake’s work is characterized by its deep engagement with themes of Black childhood joy, fantasies, and African identity, reflecting a rich cultural heritage and personal narrative. A sense of playfulness and wonder, reflecting the exuberance of youth. Simultaneously, she addresses broader themes of African identity, often using her art to question and celebrate the complexities of her heritage."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013845623005 gid://shopify/Product/9013962113245 gid://shopify/Product/9013962211549 gid://shopify/Product/9013962309853 gid://shopify/Product/9013962375389 gid://shopify/Product/9013962473693

item.title: Keabetsoe Makgoane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641613349085 Keabetsoe Makgoane gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640700793053 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Keabetsoe Makgoane (b. 11 January 2000) is a multidisciplinary artist living and working in Johannesburg, South Africa. Makgoane began drawing and painting in preschool as most children did, and since then has used art to explore new worlds of perception. After completing their matriculation in 2017, a journey of self-discovery became apparent - a year later, they received their first camera and began paying tender attention to the people and spaces they were photographing during that period. \\nMakgoane acquired their photographic education at the prominent school of photography in the southern hemisphere, The Market Photo Workshop in 2019 - where they were trained and mentored by Tshepo Gumbi, recipient of the 2015 Tierney Fellowship photography mentorship programme. The Market Photo Workshop prepares students for the creative, conceptual, \\ntechnical, and professional needs of photography. Makgoane showcased a selection of their photographs at The Market Photo Workshop group exhibition(2019) later that year. \\nMakgoane honed their art and narrative using modern media, capturing their attention. They had their first opportunity to exhibit their painting in 2023 with Latitudes.Online - REVERB 23(abstract resonance) was a group exhibition including the work of over fifty modern African artists that use abstract art to create a sensory map of sight, sound, and texture. The show \\nbrought together 70 pieces by 51 artists from Africa and the Diaspora. \\nTheir art embraces imperfections and adversity, encapsulating the essence of their journey within the context of the black collective and experience . This piqued the interest of Sara Hallatt, the director and creator of META Foundation, who invited Makgoane to exhibit at META's 76 project (2024) and Contra. Joburg, the largest open studios event in South Africa. \\nMakgoane's work delves into black sociology, black identity, the communal black experience, and the queer experience, dissecting the intricacies of the numerous repressive regimes in South Africa through various mediums; these include: drawing, painting, photography, film and beat-making. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Kealeboga Tlalang
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641619280093 Kealeboga Tlalang gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640705085661 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kealeboga Tlalang is South African artist specializing in cutting-edge collage portraitures, figures and sculptures. Analytical by nature, Tlalang uses collage which he links to puzzle play as a way of synthesizing his love for solving problems. \\nTlalang's self-professed focus is on social and economic issues back in his village. Art is a universal language and by creating is more like sharing stories affecting youth with intend to build a better future for the next generation. The colourful portraits and figures speak to the vibrancy of people, with all their fascinating colour and movement, and are more eye-catching than their textual fragmented background (perhaps representative of the world and all its background noise?). \\n \\nTlalang's artworks look digitally produced because each larger-than-life human he depicts is made up of tiny squares and rectangles of colour, their hair matte black and their expressions brimming with realism. In real life, however, it`s striking to discover that each artwork is actually mostly made up of small pieces of paper, layered with a striking precision that creates a subtle effect. When looking at them close up, each work is a rainbow, full of texture. Take several steps back and each work is glossy with rich shadows and highlights, smooth contours. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Keiskamma Art Project
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641625735389 Keiskamma Art Project 1627 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640717865181 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013350432989","gid://shopify/Product/9013350564061","gid://shopify/Product/9013350629597","gid://shopify/Product/9013350695133","gid://shopify/Product/9014073884893","gid://shopify/Product/9014073950429","gid://shopify/Product/9014074015965"] [24136,24138,24139] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Founded in 2000, the Keiskamma Art Project in Hamburg, Eastern Cape, produces major textile artworks, all of which aid in the archiving of the Eastern Cape rural collective memory and preservation of oral history. The Project has won numerous awards, including the Business and Arts South Africa (BASA) Award and the Chairman’s Premier Award (2011), which recognises sustained and extraordinary commitment to the arts in South Africa. \\nMarking twenty years since the launch of the Keiskamma Art Project, Umaf’ evuka, nje ngenyanga / Dying and Rising as the Moon Does, a retrospective exhibition at Constitution Hill, Johannesburg, aims to bring together iconic pieces into one immersive experience. An inquiry, through embroidery and storytelling, into the fabric of society, the meaning of humanity and the stark realities of illness, this retrospective brings into view the conversations of a community using art as a medium of expression and healing. \\n \\nIn 2022 Constitution Hill, a living museum that tells the story of South Africa’s journey to democracy, is observing the founding principles of our transformative Constitution. Steeped in history, Constitution Hill is a profoundly symbolic site. Against this backdrop, the Keiskamma artists have made three prototypes towards a beautiful, limited edition tapestry series to raise funds for the retrospective. \\nIn these extraordinary artworks they reveal what they value most about our democracy and what the pillars of our Constitution – EQUALITY, FREEDOM and HUMAN DIGNITY – mean in their daily lives as women from an impoverished area of the Eastern Cape. The finished artworks, richly coloured, intricate and thought-provoking, make up a symbolic narrative of possibility for a resilient community. Individually, the tapestries represent an intimate expression of personal hopes and dreams, manifested stitch by stitch."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013350432989 gid://shopify/Product/9013350564061 gid://shopify/Product/9013350629597 gid://shopify/Product/9013350695133 gid://shopify/Product/9014073884893 gid://shopify/Product/9014073950429 gid://shopify/Product/9014074015965

[24972,24974] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Keith Henning (b.1982, South Africa), currently lives and works in Cape Town. Originally developing a practice in design, founding the well-known AKJP design store and clothing label, Henning has expanded his material interests into sculpture, working primarily in steel and ceramic. \\nMost recently, the artist presented WATERSPORTS — Not for public consumption, at RESERVOIR in Cape Town. This marked Henning’s third solo exhibition, expanding on the body of work which was exhibited at the Michaelis Gallery upon conclusion of his studies in 2024. In 2023 the artist presented PUMPED at The Fourth Gallery in Cape Town, South Africa. In 2023 his work was included in the group exhibition, Hello Stranger at Bhalla Munro, New York, USA. In 2019 Bad Paper Editions presented Henning’s work at AKAA Art and Design fair, Paris, France, and the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, South Africa. \\nKeith Henning’s contribution to material and design discourse has been recognised by TWYG, who in 2021 awarded him the Sustainability Prize in 2021, and Cape Wools as the Designer Competition Winner in 2018. In 2021 Zeitz MOCAA exhibited his work in 21 Years of South African Fashion. His work is included in the Zeitz MOCAA Permanent Collection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014109405405 gid://shopify/Product/9014109470941

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641630519517 Kelechi Charles Nwaneri gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640718520541 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kelechi Charles Nwaneri (b.1994, Nigerian) is a self-taught mixed-media artist. He currently lives and works in Lagos state, Nigeria. Nwaneri obtained his Bachelor's degree in Agricultural Extension from the University of Nigeria in 2015. Kelechi Nwaneri focuses on discussing issues around mental health, psychology and social values with his work. \\nInspired by the events happening in his environment, he creates art with surrealistic imagery that is often allegorical, but is based on real experiences. The use of indigenous symbols (including mainly Adinkra, Uli, Nsibidi) and sometimes foreign symbols, mystical, metaphysical and allegorical imagery are major characteristics of his style of work."}]}]}

item.title: Kelly van Graan
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641631437021 Kelly van Graan gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640718684381 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born and based in Cape Town, Kelly Van Graan (b. 1997) is a mixed media artist who spent four years at Stellenbosch University under the BA Fine Art programme. Van Graan’s practice involves multiple processes within photography, collage and painting that traverses themes of identity in relation to inhabited spaces. Her art-making process rotates through various moments of her past to create a layered and overlapping history of herself. Within this, she constantly performs the act of photographing her environment and uses images as a tool for reflection and making sense of her being. She describes this process as a necessary, imperative act towards self-exploration through which she is able to piece together fragments of the past and form a better understanding of her being. Van Graan’s works thus become an attempt to reconcile the discrepancies between her unrecognisable past selves and her present self. Van Graan has exhibited in both local and international exhibitions such as the Incheon Asia Maritime Media Festival (2018) in South Korea. Her work is also a part of the Stellenbosch University private art collection (2017)."}]}]}

item.title: Kelvin Trautman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641632190685 Kelvin Trautman 2637 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640718749917 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014012608733","gid://shopify/Product/9014014542045"] [22337] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kelvin Trautman is a self-taught photographer and filmmaker based in Cape Town and London, specializing in narrative-driven content that explores the intersection of human experience and environmental conditions. Known for his creative direction, unique perspectives, and athletic ability behind the camera, Kelvin has made a significant mark in the outdoor industry. \\n \\nHis work spans all seven continents, with high-profile clients such as Patagonia, the United Nations, Reuters, and Red Bull. His images have been featured in prominent publications like The New York Times, National Geographic, Red Bulletin, and Outside Magazine. \\n \\nKelvin is passionate about using photography and film-making to connect, educate, and inspire, believing that all you need to tell a good story is a camera, courage, and empathy. He strives to challenge perceptions and push creative boundaries, seeking to go beyond the stereotypical perfect moment to capture authentic, immersive experiences."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014012608733 gid://shopify/Product/9014014542045

item.title: Kemang Wa Lehulere
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641633468637 Kemang Wa Lehulere gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640718880989 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kemang Wa Lehulere was born in Cape Town, South Africa. He has a BA Fine Arts degree from the University of the Witwatersrand (2011). \\nWa Lehulere’s artistic practice reacts to the historical legacy of South Africa, using performative acts with objects and materials familiar to South African society, to carve, dig, break, erase or reconstitute. Objects like wooden school desks, ceramic sculptures of Alsatian dogs and blackboards are incorporated into various installations and used as symbols of both an educational system within the apartheid regime and its performance within a contemporary democratic society. \\nThe objects transmute between a familiar object from childhood into more pointed questions or concerns that challenge our assumptions about the histories and social structures that shape the world around us. \\nSolo exhibitions include Art Institute of Chicago, Chicago (2016); Gasworks, London (2015); Lombard Freid Projects, New York (2013); the Goethe-Institut, Johannesburg (2011), and the Association of Visual Arts in Cape Town (2009). Notable group exhibitions include the 8th Berlin Biennale (2014); Yerba Buena Center for the Arts, San Francisco (2014); The Ungovernables, the second triennial exhibition of the New Museum in New York (2012); the 11th Lyon Biennale at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Lyon, France (2011) and at the Kunsthalle Bern and Zentrum Paul Klee in Bern, Switzerland (2010). \\nWa Lehulere was a co-founder of the Gugulective (2006), an artist-led collective based in Cape Town, and is a founding member of the Center for Historical Reenactments in Johannesburg. He was the winner of the inaugural Spier Contemporary Award in 2007, the MTN New Contemporaries Award in 2010, and the Tollman Award for the Visual Arts in 2012; he was one of two young artists awarded the 15th Baloise Art Prize at Art Basel in 2013, won the first International Tiberius Art Award Dresden in 2014 and was the Standard Bank Young Artist for Visual Arts in 2015. Wa Lehulere was also the recipient of an Ampersand Foundation residency in New York in 2012. \\n"}]}]}

I was \\nchosen as a top10 finalist for ‘Continuing Conversations UJ portrait award 2018. \\nA recent project I managed, ‘NUMBERS’ exhibition curated by myself a \\ncollaborative multi disciplinary exhibition featuring an interactive multimedia \\ninstallation and a group show of selected female artists showed at Hazard Gallery, \\nJohannesburg. I was recently in an artist residency programme at Southern \\nAfrican Foundation for Contemporary Art (SAFFCA) in Knysna , end of 2018. I’m \\nwas recently in the ‘Artists in Schools’ education programme with Sibikwa Arts \\nCentre, working as an art facilitator at Mogale primary school in 2019. I’m \\ncurrently the director of The Project Space organisation since September 2019 till \\n2021."}]}]}

item.title: Kenneth Shandu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641634418909 Kenneth Shandu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640719044829 [] Kenneth Shandu is a renowned contemporary artist known for his thought-provoking works that explore themes of identity, culture, and societal norms. His art incorporates rich symbolism and evocative imagery, inviting audiences to engage in deep reflection on the human experience through a dynamic fusion of traditional and modern techniques. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kenneth Shandu is a contemporary artist whose multifaceted practice encompasses drawing, printmaking, sculpture, and installation. Born in KwaMbonambi, KwaZulu-Natal, Shandu now resides in Durban, where he continues to explore the socio-economic issues affecting marginalized communities in post-apartheid South Africa. \\n \\nHe graduated with a Diploma in Fine Art from the Durban University of Technology (DUT) in 2018 and is currently pursuing his Master’s degree in Fine Arts at the same institution. Shandu’s work is deeply rooted in the lived experiences of marginalized farmers and informal traders, reflecting his commitment to highlighting their struggles and contributions to society. As a finalist for the Sasol New Signatures Art Awards in 2018 and 2021, he has gained recognition for his powerful commentary on identity and displacement. His accolades include awards from the PPC Imaginarium Art & Design Competition and participation in the NSA Members Exhibition. An active member of the art community, Shandu has served as an assistant curator and participated in the Thupelo Art Workshops, while also working as a teaching assistant at DUT. He has showcased his work in numerous group exhibitions, notably in the 2019 “Land” exhibition at the KZNSA Gallery, and his recent solo show, “Azilime Ziyetsheni,” at the Bag Factory in 2022. Through his artistic endeavors, Shandu aims to challenge perceptions and elevate the narratives of those often overlooked in society."}]}]}

Featured on Latitudes Online. [25498,25499,25497] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kerri Liebovitz, born in 2002, is an emerging contemporary South African fine artist whose \\nwork is marked by a deep exploration of themes surrounding the self, the representation of the nude in art, vulnerability, sexual violence, and having a room of one’s own. \\nDrawing inspiration from her own experiences, Liebovitz utilises the image of her own body as her subject for her portrait paintings to explore these complex concepts. Based in Johannesburg, Liebovitz has just completed her studies at The University of the Witwatersrand, with a Bachelor's in Fine Arts. Her more recent works comprise of a series of nude, self-portrait, oil paintings, serving as a form of empowerment and reclamation of her body and the representation of the female form. \\nIn her artistic methodology, she references her exploration and research into the portrayal of women and the nude and challenges historical representations shaped by the male gaze. This holds great personal importance for her as she advocates for women to assert their presence in the art world and to reclaim agency over their own bodies and narratives, transcending the \\nconstraints of patriarchal historical frameworks."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9133213155549 gid://shopify/Product/9133231177949 gid://shopify/Product/9133231374557

From oil paintings to unique ceramics, Collins’ art spans a range of media, with exhibitions across South Africa. [24409,24411,24389,24398,24394,24391,24390,24415,24421,24424,24423,24425,24420,24406,24427,24422,24419,24388,24404,24393,24418,24413,24426,24405,24397,24407,24428,24402,24417] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kevin Collins studied under Stanley Pinker, Helmut Starke and Cecil Skotnes at Michaelis, UCT in the late seventies with painting as his specialisation. These men provided him with the basis of how he use colour, composition and actually lay the paint down: all of these learnings he has now ‘translated’ into his new medium of ceramics. \\nHis subject matter is collected from years of travelling (many miles from the age of three) and making small sketches and picking up little bits of visual imagery from packaging, transport tickets, and sweet wrappers - from Mandalay to Dharamsala. Some imagery emerges from his childhood and early and continued love of illustrated story books. \\nAfter graduating, he worked in brand communications and stopped painting for close on twenty years. Then an unfortunate health trauma made him seriously consider what he really wanted to do, and he started painting again. He started painting small works mostly of animals which formed the basis of his first solo show in 2003 titled 'The Taxonomy of non endangered Species' at Gallery Moja in Johannesburg. Following this, he has contributed to numerous group shows in Johannesburg and Cape Town. Large solo in 2021 and during Covid perfected his understanding of ceramics now his chosen medium. He has works in public and private collections in Australia, America, Argentina, Holland, Germany and UK as well as South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014085943517 gid://shopify/Product/9014085976285 gid://shopify/Product/9014086107357 gid://shopify/Product/9014086140125 gid://shopify/Product/9014086238429 gid://shopify/Product/9014086303965 gid://shopify/Product/9014086500573 gid://shopify/Product/9014086566109 gid://shopify/Product/9014086697181 gid://shopify/Product/9014086729949 gid://shopify/Product/9014086828253 gid://shopify/Product/9014086893789 gid://shopify/Product/9014086959325 gid://shopify/Product/9014087024861 gid://shopify/Product/9014087123165 gid://shopify/Product/9014087221469 gid://shopify/Product/9014087319773 gid://shopify/Product/9014087418077 gid://shopify/Product/9014087549149 gid://shopify/Product/9014087614685 gid://shopify/Product/9014087712989 gid://shopify/Product/9014087778525 gid://shopify/Product/9014087844061 gid://shopify/Product/9014087876829 gid://shopify/Product/9014087975133 gid://shopify/Product/9014088040669 gid://shopify/Product/9014088138973 gid://shopify/Product/9014088171741 gid://shopify/Product/9014088237277 gid://shopify/Product/9014088302813 gid://shopify/Product/9133212238045 gid://shopify/Product/9133230850269 gid://shopify/Product/9134146388189 gid://shopify/Product/9134146715869 gid://shopify/Product/9134149042397

item.title: Kevin Roberts
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641641824477 Kevin Roberts gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640719995101 [] Discover the compelling work of Kevin Roberts, a South African artist exploring themes of identity, memory, and cultural narrative through striking visual forms. View his artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kevin Roberts was born in Rustenburg, in the North West province of South Africa. He received a National Diploma in Fine Arts in 1988, followed by a National Higher Diploma in Fine Arts, both from Pretoria Technikon. He won several awards during his career, including the 1995 Volkskas Bank L’Atelier Competition and the 1996 Kempton Park/Tembisa Fine Art Award. Women are the subject of his calm surrealist works, which often include animals along with recurring symbolic motifs. He regularly exhibited with Everard Read, and his artworks form part of the collections of the Pretoria Art Museum, Absa Bank, Sanlam, Unisa, and the Department of Foreign Affairs."}]}]}

item.title: KG'AKG'AM TSHABU
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641641857245 KG'AKG'AM TSHABU gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640667730141 [] Discover the dynamic and multimedia-rich work of KG’Akg’am Tshabu, a South African artist whose practice spans painting, installation, and cultural storytelling. Explore their artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kg’akg’am was born in Ghanzi, Botswana in 1954, and moved to D’kar with her father and children later in her life. She joined the Kuru Art Project in 2005. Her vibrant paintings of bold contrasting colours evoke a cheerful feel amongst viewers. Her subjects vary between her people's traditional life and the Kalahari's natural environment. \\nWhile working on her art she often remembers the stories about the hunter-gatherer lifestyle from her ancestors. She enjoys the creative process and proclaims that it gives her confidence, and that art has made a great change to her life. \\nKg’akg’am works in various mediums but focuses mainly on painting and linocuts."}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641641922781 Kgotlelelo Sekiti 480 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640720257245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013388706013","gid://shopify/Product/9013388738781","gid://shopify/Product/9013388771549"] [13629,13631,13630] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kgotlelelo Bradley Sekiti is a 21-year-old performance artist from Alex. \\n \\nSekiti explains that his work is inextricably linked to his experience of being a black queer body – one that is, undeniably, not been the easiest. His work speaks to that fact that the journey of being a black, queer body seems to be designed with the challenge of navigating “safe” spaces of existence which - along the way - prove that the notion of a safe space is one that is almost non-existent. This work looks into what he has deemed as a “safer” space. “As recently discovered by NASA —the possibility of an alternate/parallel universe — m practice forms into the exploration of parallel universes that queer bodies create in order to enable the co-existence of split realities that they identify with into a single frame\". \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013388706013 gid://shopify/Product/9013388738781 gid://shopify/Product/9013388771549

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641642021085 Khanyisa Agnes Brancon 2911 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650724163805 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014103441629","gid://shopify/Product/9014103474397","gid://shopify/Product/9014103507165"] Khanyisa Agnes Brancon (b.?2002, Polokwane) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work spans printmaking, photography, and installation. [24803,24804,24805] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"KHANYISA AGNES BRANCON| b. 2002 Tzaneen, Limpopo is a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist hailing from Polokwane. Brancon explores mediums of expression namely Printmaking, Photography, and Installation through an interdisciplinary approach that consists of the use of textiles, thus prioritising materiality throughout her work. The manifestation of labour and leisure, maternal lineage, and the black experience are grand themes addressed throughout her work. \\nHer work explores the contemporary feminist approach that calls to attention the intersection of representation needed for the kind of \\nblack women who reflect on personal and family-related histories. The existence of Spirituality as an additional layer of which life is experienced and explored in the work. Brancon plans to actively participate within the art ecosystem by creating platforms of representation for black bodies envisioning her story as a reflection to theirs. \\nShe is currently pursuing a degree in Fine Arts with the University of the Witwatersrand. In addition to her ventures, Brancon forms part of a collective bonded by the practice of printmaking with three black women artists from Limpopo. The printmaking collective called Boteng, explores themes of materiality and the black experience within its art practice. Due to their meticulous organisation and continuous dedication to the practice of art; their direction leans towards curation and establishing a presence within the art ecosystem. \\nKhanyisa is the recipient of the 2025 Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014103441629 gid://shopify/Product/9014103474397 gid://shopify/Product/9014103507165

Through abstraction and the use of various media, Mawhayi examines personal and collective histories, engaging with the complexities of belonging and memory. [23867,23883,24822,18393,18402,25331,17885,24823] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Khanyi Mawhayi (b. 1998) is an artist and curator based in Cape Town, South Africa. She is developing a formal language across media, tackling themes such as decoloniality and world-building. Mawhayi’s work is concerned with self-location and identity formation, exploring how abstraction can be used to achieve the right to opacity. \\nThrough her artistic and curatorial practice, Mawhayi looks for ways in which society can reimagine normalized structures and systems by acknowledging individual and shared desires and encouraging fabulation and imagination. \\nShe makes drawings, paintings, non-narrative videos, and tapestries and considers materiality and form, especially colour, not only on an aesthetic level but also on a conceptual basis. Drawing from art history, popular culture, and personal experience, she sees her wider practice as a reflection on her mission to comfortably exist within multiplicities. Mawhayi holds a BFA from Wits University (‘20) and has held three solo exhibition's in Cape Town, most recently Black and White Paradise at Vela Projects. Her work has been shown in the Kampala Biennale (‘20), the Zozimo Bulbul Black Film Festival (‘22) and What We Know at Keys Art Mile (‘22). She is currently a curatorial assistant at Zeitz MOCAA."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014061334749 gid://shopify/Product/9014104031453 gid://shopify/Product/9014104064221 gid://shopify/Product/9133223510237

item.title: Khaya Sineyile

Most recently he turned his attention to the effects of social inequality, specifically relating to the South African family structure. His confident brush marks and considered palette convey a rawness which he contrasts with cartoon-like outlines - a device which removes the figures from their ground and introduces elements of playfulness, wit and humour to the often-loaded subject matter. \\n \\nSineyile is a mostly self-taught artist from Nyanga, Cape Town. From an early age, he has had a love for drawing and painting and trained at the Arts and Media Access Centre (AMAC) in 2005. In 2009, he was selected as a resident artist at Greatmore Studios and later that year at the Souq Waqif Art Center in Doha, Qatar. Sineyile has participated in several solo exhibitions and more than 30 group exhibitions, locally and abroad. Artworks of his are included in private collections overseas and the corporate collections of Spier, Nando’s UK, Truworths, Groote Schuur Hospital and Hollard. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013301477597 gid://shopify/Product/9013958410461 gid://shopify/Product/9013958541533 gid://shopify/Product/9013958672605

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641643069661 Kholofelo Simon Moshapo jnr gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650725834973 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014058483933"] Discover the impactful artworks of Kholofelo Simon Moshapo Jnr, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Moshapo’s work explores themes of identity, heritage, and the human experience, blending traditional and contemporary techniques to create visually engaging pieces. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simon Moshapo Junior (b. 1991) is a South African multi-disciplinary artist. His artistic practice is deeply personal and serves as a form of healing and self-expression, reflecting his journey with epilepsy and the exploration of identity. Living with this condition has shaped his worldview, inspiring a body of work that speaks to the sense of \"otherness\" he experiences, and confronting the realities of mortality and resilience. \\nMoshapo's art is characterized by its layered exploration of human existence, often drawing on themes of self-preservation, identity, and cultural heritage. His sculptural work, paintings, and drawings serve not only as expressions of his personal journey but also as reflections on broader societal issues. Through intricate compositions, Moshapo tackles political and social challenges, using his art to provoke thought and foster dialogue about life’s complexities. \\nMoshapo’s art is characterized by its layered exploration of human existence, often drawing on themes of self-preservation, identity, and cultural heritage. His sculptural work, paintings, and drawings serve not only as expressions of his personal journey but also as reflections on broader societal issues. Through intricate compositions, Moshapo tackles political and social challenges, using his art to provoke thought and foster dialogue about life’s complexities. \\nHis practice integrates a strong connection to the material world, with wood sculptures and tactile mediums playing a significant role in his exploration of form and texture. Each piece is a testament to his belief in the transformative power of art—his work seeks to communicate not just emotion but also a deeper understanding of the human condition. \\n \\nInformed by his lived experience, Simon Moshapo Junior’s artistic vision is one of resilience and reclamation, rooted in a profound sense of identity and a drive to create art that transcends personal and political boundaries."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014058483933

item.title: Khaya Witbooi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641642905821 Khaya Witbooi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650725736669 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Khaya Witbooi (b. 1977) grew up in Uitenhage in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. After matriculating in 1995 he did a college course in draughtsmanship and started working as an illustrator for an architectural firm while doing freelance work for The Argus newspaper in Cape Town (court sketches, cartoons etc.). He also specialised in the painting of portraits. \\n \\nIn June 2010 he was selected to join the Good Hope Artist’s Studio programme where he was given a studio and the opportunity to paint full-time. In December 2011 he was awarded an artist’s residency at the more prestigious Greatmore Studios in Woodstock, Cape Town. Witbooi uses a combination of stencilling and oil painting to express his observations, usually of socio-political nature. The result is a surreal and gritty feel layered with pop art iconography and distinctly African subject matter. Topics like democracy in post-apartheid South Africa, human behaviour in this context and the effects of globalisation are dealt with regularly. It provides valuable insight into a world the viewer seldom had the opportunity to experience firsthand. \\n \\nARTIST STATEMENT \\n“I’ve taken it upon myself to make a statement of a concerned citizen. I’m not expecting people from around the world to do it before I do. If there’s any person to make the first comment, it is the person \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Khulekani Mayisa

She obtained a BA degree in Film& Television Studies from The University of Johannesburg, and, since graduating in 2018, has created several experimental short films, with a style that has been described in the Mail & Guardian as, “blending polemicism with a unique, sensuous visual sensibility”. \\nHer last film, “Okumhlophe” (2021) won two international awards: Best Short Film at the B3 Biennale of the Moving Image in Frankfurt, Germany; and Best Cinematography at the Mom Film Fest in New York, USA. She was one of 25 participants invited to attend Frankfurt’s B3 Hessenlab in 2022 for a new screenplay in development. \\nHer work has been showcased in local film festivals such as the Africa Rising International Film Festival, as well as film festivals in Nigeria, The United Kingdom, and Poland. This work earned her a spot as a finalist for the 2021 Africa Photo Awards, which doubled as an exhibition at The Gallery in Keyes Art Mile. So far, her photography has been featured on Adidas ZA, Photo Vogue, and Morning Live. \\nShe has freelanced in the industry as a film director, editor, videographer, photographer, and stylist. Raised in a family of artist, Khwezi was immersed in painting from a young age, with his mother's passion for art nurturing his creative spirit. His artistic journey began with drawing and painting, evolving into graffiti during his adolescence. \\nAfter initially pursuing a degree in astrophysics, Khwezi transitioned to become a craftsman glass blower at the Cristallerie Saint Louis, where he refined his skills over five years. However, his innate need to create led him back to painting, and in 2012, he dedicated himself fully to the art form. Khwezi now lives and works in Drôme, France, where he continues to develop his dynamic, colorful, and enthusiastic pieces. \\nKhwezi's work is a fusion of modern and traditional ethnic cultures, inspired by his travels to the United States and South Africa, and the diverse cultures he has inherited. His paintings often pose questions about the possibility of harmonious cohabitation between globalized culture and rich traditions of different territories, ethnic groups, and families. Through his art, Khwezi builds a world of respect, cultural richness, openness, and solidarity, characterized by hope and optimism. \\n \\nHis style incorporates a range of techniques, from engraving to aerosol painting, creating a visual language that captures the essence of his cultural fusion. Tribal and ancestral motifs play a significant role in his work, adding depth and meaning. Khwezi's art has been exhibited in Lyon, Tokyo, and other international venues, showcasing his unique approach to storytelling through visual art."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013382381789 gid://shopify/Product/9013382414557 gid://shopify/Product/9013388411101 gid://shopify/Product/9013395685597 gid://shopify/Product/9013395718365 gid://shopify/Product/9013395751133 gid://shopify/Product/9013395816669 gid://shopify/Product/9013395849437 gid://shopify/Product/9013397848285 gid://shopify/Product/9013398012125 gid://shopify/Product/9013398208733 gid://shopify/Product/9013398929629 gid://shopify/Product/9013401157853 gid://shopify/Product/9013401223389 gid://shopify/Product/9013401256157 gid://shopify/Product/9013417050333 gid://shopify/Product/9013417410781 gid://shopify/Product/9013417443549 gid://shopify/Product/9013417509085 gid://shopify/Product/9013417574621 gid://shopify/Product/9013417705693 gid://shopify/Product/9013417771229 gid://shopify/Product/9013417869533 gid://shopify/Product/9013417902301 gid://shopify/Product/9013418000605 gid://shopify/Product/9013835759837 gid://shopify/Product/9013840642269 gid://shopify/Product/9013840707805 gid://shopify/Product/9013840740573 gid://shopify/Product/9013845197021 gid://shopify/Product/9013845295325 gid://shopify/Product/9013845328093 gid://shopify/Product/9013845360861 gid://shopify/Product/9013845393629 gid://shopify/Product/9013845426397 gid://shopify/Product/9013974728925 gid://shopify/Product/9013974827229 gid://shopify/Product/9013974925533 gid://shopify/Product/9014011658461 gid://shopify/Product/9014011691229 gid://shopify/Product/9014011756765 gid://shopify/Product/9014011789533 gid://shopify/Product/9014011822301 gid://shopify/Product/9014011855069 gid://shopify/Product/9014011887837 gid://shopify/Product/9014011920605 gid://shopify/Product/9014036889821 gid://shopify/Product/9014037512413 gid://shopify/Product/9014047637725

Through his art, Getaw seeks to unravel the intricate interplay between reality and illusion, revealing how our innermost musings, desires, and fears shape our perceptions and actions. \\n \\nGetaw captures the complex web of human emotions and subconscious influences. His art invites viewers to navigate the blurred boundaries between lived experience and dreamlike reverie, offering a space where the dualities of reality and illusion coexist and interact. By exploring these themes, Getaw encourages deeper reflection on the ways in which our dreams and waking lives are intertwined.
