[23501,23502,23503,23504,23505] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mandisa Buthelezi, a photographer and filmmaker born in Empangeni, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, grew up in the township of Umlazi, Durban. Her deep connection to the rural landscapes of KwaZulu-Natal led her to embark on a self-taught journey in photography, where she began documenting the social and cultural dynamics of the province's rural and peri-urban areas. \\nWith a rich portfolio that highlights the rural experience, Buthelezi's work reflects a profound respect for culture and traditions that shape her world. Her photography delves into themes of culture, identity, and spirituality, capturing the essence of life through her lens. Buthelezi's commitment to preserving African culture through visual storytelling has become a cornerstone of her practice, particularly in her assignments that focus on documenting and sustaining the traditions surrounding her. \\nCurrently, Buthelezi splits her time between Johannesburg and Durban, where she continues to create and share her unique perspective on African culture."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014048293085 gid://shopify/Product/9014048325853 gid://shopify/Product/9014048391389 gid://shopify/Product/9014048424157 gid://shopify/Product/9014048489693

item.title: Mandisi Mncela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641761755357 Mandisi Mncela gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640792183005 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mandisi Mncela is a full time artist that specialises in mosaic art, painting and mixed media. Mncela studied visual arts at Community Arts Projects in 2000. Thereafter he worked at Nyanga Arts Development Center where he found platforms in painting and facilitating at schools and after school community programmes. In 2015, Mncela obtained a three-year certificate in professional mosaic art at Spier arts academy in Cape Town. His work is focused on portraiture and figures - where his personal expression reflects his inspiration from African history, spirituality and religion. \\n \\nMncela uses natural stone, bricks, ceramics, mali tiles and man made industrial material for mosaic artworks. He has been involved in group exhibitions at Art B, AVA, Cape gallery and Greatmore studios. In 2015, he participated in an residency, ”RITES and DUTIES”, at Constitution Hill in Johannesburg, produced by COOP COFFE company sculpture. During his time at Spier arts in 2016, Mncela's confidence grew and allowed him to become one of the mosaic facilitators in Sports ground produkte mark hall at Vredendal under Greatmore art studios in 2017. \\n \\nMncela is currently working with Thomarts Gallery and his works have sold in the United States, France and Germany."}]}]}

item.title: Mandla Mahlangu (1989-)
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641762443485 Mandla Mahlangu (1989-) gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640792412381 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mandla Mahlangu, a painter and muralist artist who is proudly carrying on the artistic legacy of his grandmother, Ester Mahlangu. Born and raised in South Africa, Mandla has been immersed in the vibrant world of Ndebele art from an early age, thanks to the guidance and mentorship of his esteemed grandmother. Mandla's artistic journey has been shaped by the rich traditions and captivating geometric patterns of Ndebele art. He draws inspiration from the deep-rooted symbolism and storytelling elements that have been passed down through generations. Embracing the vibrant colors and meticulous details, Mandla's work reflects his deep connection to the Ndebele culture and his desire to preserve its artistic heritage. \\n \\nArtistic Experience \\n \\nServing under Ester Mahlangu from 2005 – Current \\nAssisting as a muralist and studio assistant \\n \\nPrevious Contributing Projects \\n \\nMurals: \\n• Oprah Winfrey School for \\nGirls(Johannesburg, South Africa) \\n• South Gate Mall \\n• Phola Mall \\n• Mandela Forum (Florence Italy) \\n• Khulisile Palace \\n• Dr Esther Mahlangu House \\n• Botshabelo Museum \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Mandy Johnston
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641764442333 Mandy Johnston gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640793067741 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mandy Johnston is a practicing visual artist based in Cape Town, South Africa. She earned a Master’s degree from the University of the Witwatersrand in 2003. Since then, Johnston has collaborated on various inner-city art projects and initiatives, including Assemblage (an arts facilitation organization) and the Artist Career Development Program. She has presented six solo exhibitions and participated in numerous group exhibitions. \\nJohnston's works are part of multiple corporate and private collections. Notably, her pieces for the \"Negotiate\" group show at the Johannesburg Art Gallery were commissioned by the \"Makeshift\" project, initiated by the Joubert Park Project and the Canadian National Art Gallery. Johnston is currently working on a new body of work while mentoring young artists. \\nArtist Statement: \\n \\nI am interested in the notion that things are often defined by their antithesis and that often the formation of a value is around the threat of absence. There is pain and fear associated with absence with a thing that once filled space literally or figuratively, now open and vulnerable to be absorbed, used, ignored or quoted. In this, there is also opportunity for reflection, renewal and rebirth. My work almost always refers to a specific historical and cultural context. I use materials for the contextual values, definitions and symbolisms they bring. I am currently interested in the experiential, visceral responses to works of art and am in search of its recipe.\""}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641765916893 Manuela Holzer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794312925 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Manuela Holzer was born into a creative Austrian family. Her late Viennese grandmother, Grete Zimmer, was a famous actress in Austria and was also well known in many parts of Germany and Switzerland. Manuela matriculated from the Deutsche Internationale Schule Johannesburg, South Africa, in 2008 and thereafter decided to pursue her passion for art. She initially studied at the University of Witwatersrand where she completed her Bachelor in Fine Art in 2012. In 2013 she completed a Postgraduate Certificate in Education cum laude at the University of Johannesburg. Thereafter Manuela moved to the Western Cape to study further and received a Master’s degree in Visual Art from the University of Stellenbosch in 2016. She currently resides in Cape Town and furthers her artistic practice by creating sculptures of the female figure in various media exploring the notion of the internal shadow."}]}]}

item.title: Many Libuta
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641768407261 Many Libuta gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794411229 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Many Libuta, born in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, graduated with a BA degree in Fine Art from the Académie des Beaux-Arts of Kinshasa in 2007. Currently residing and working in Cape Town, he has facilitated workshops at institutions such as the Alliance Française and the Iziko (the South African National Gallery). Alongside his participation in various exhibitions, Many founded the performance group SangisArt/ Sangisa Sangisa, aiming to support his artistic practice and delve deeper into his creative abilities. \\n \\nMotivated by a dedicated commitment to initiating conversations and raising awareness, Libuta’s primary focus revolves around environmental conservation. He explores theintricate relationship between humans and nature, emphasizing the crucial role of awareness and action in preserving the environment for future generations. His devotion to sparking change is evident in his acrylic works, characterized by a strong, bold surrealist style that seamlessly blends familiar elements with natural motifs, particularly butterflies. This incorporation serves as a metaphor for transformation, highlighting the essential nature of growth and flourishing. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Manuela Pimentel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641768210653 Manuela Pimentel 2408 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794378461 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013852242141","gid://shopify/Product/9013852274909","gid://shopify/Product/9013852307677"] [19054,19056,19055] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Manuela Pimentel (b. 1979, Portugal) ingeniously fuses together references to the traditional handicraft art of painted mural tiles with the aesthetics of street billboards and their cumulative layers of ripped and lacerated advertising posters. Bearing in mind post-war artists of the New Realism movement such as Mimmo Rotella, Raymond Hains or Jacques Villeglé, Pimentel incorporates fragments of street posters she takes off herself or uses them as supports for her painted interventions. \\n \\nUsing acrylic colours, the artist accurately reproduces traditional figures and scenes taken from the visual culture of the Portuguese tiles (azulejos). By integrating the tiles’ conventional chromaticism, iconography and naif-style rendering into specific wall-mounted artworks, and by merging all of it with torn street posters, adding resins, rough mortar and neon lights, the artist reconfigures the place of the tile as a popular and decorative expression that used to belong to local collective memory to inscribe it in the space of global artistic creation."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013852242141 gid://shopify/Product/9013852274909 gid://shopify/Product/9013852307677

item.title: Manyaku Mashilo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641768276189 Manyaku Mashilo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794706141 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Manyaku Mashilo was born in 1991 in Limpopo, South Africa and is currently based in Cape Town, South Africa. Mashilo is a self-taught multidisciplinary artist who creates mixed media paintings. Dedicated to the act of cherishing lineage, Manyaku Mashilo creates otherworldly re-imaginings with precise linework. The portraits capture the self, representing a black, queer community cloaked, clothed and bathed in celestial cartographies. The enmeshed figures perform a multiplication of mappings piecing together dimensions of time, place and space, offering the land and the body as the source of a complex question of spiritual identity. Mashilo will present a solo presentation at the ART X Lagos 2021 at Victoria Island in Lagos Nigeria as well as at Bonne Esperance Gallery in Paris, France in 2021. Mashilo’s work will also be included in 99 Loop Gallery’s group presentation at the \\n2022 Investec Cape Town Art Fair. \\n \\nIn 2020 Mashilo’s work was included in notable group shows “The Medium is the Message” curated by Azu Nwagbogu at Unit London in London, UK, as well as “Liminality in Infinite Space” at the African Artists Foundation in Lagos, Nigeria. Both the exhibitions spotlighting artists that form part of the new vanguard in the field of contemporary African figuration. Mashilo’s work was also included in the 2020 Prizm Art Fair titled “NOIR, NOIR: Meditations on African Cinema and its influence on Visual Art” curated by Mikhaile Solomon and William Cordova in Miami, USA. \\n \\nIn the same year she presented her solo exhibition “There are other worlds they have not told you Of” ,at 99 Loop Gallery in Cape Town, South Africa, and The Possibility of a Journey, curated by Tammy Langtry as part of the Klein Karoo National Arts Festival, South Africa, both in 2020. \\n \\nEarlier solo exhibitions include: “There’s an Exhibition in My Kitchen at Breaking Bread” in 2019 and “Beauty | Skin |Beholder” at The New Heritage Gallery in 2017, both in Cape Town. Her past group exhibitions include: “She Impressions” at the Project Space in Johannesburg in 2019; “Sunday Service” at GUS in Stellenbosch and “The Numbers Exhibition” at Hazard Gallery in Johannesburg in 2018; “La Gravitas” at La Provence Gallery in Franshoek in 2017. Mashilo’s work forms part of the Tiroche Deleon Collection and The Suzie Wong Collection."}]}]}

item.title: Marc Shoul
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641774698717 Marc Shoul gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640794968285 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marc Shoul lives and works in Johannesburg. He works largely in portraiture and documentary photography that observes complex social issues. Shoul graduated from the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University with a BTech in Photography in 1999. \\n \\n \\n \\nHe has had solo exhibitions at: The South African Jewish Museum, Cape Town (2018); Musée Pierre Noël, Saint-Dié-des-Vosges, France (2017); Blue Sky Gallery, Portland, USA (2015); Extraspaszio Gallery, Rome, Italy (2013); Pretoria Art Museum (2012); Quai 1, Vevey, Switzerland (2010); and Atelier de Visu, Marseille, France (2013), where he also completed an artists’ residency. Shoul’s work has been featured at the screenings of Visa Pour L’Image, Perpignan, France and the Ankor Photographic Festival, Siem Reap, Cambodia. His series Landsman featured at Addis Foto Fest 2018, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Shoul won the WinePhoto photographic competition with Brakpan and received an honourable mention for Flatlands in 2011. \\n \\n \\n \\nHis work is included in the collections of the Iziko South African National Gallery, Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Museum, as well as The Memmo Foundation in Rome, Italy. He is represented by Panos Pictures in London, UK."}]}]}

item.title: Marcel Herholdt
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641772536029 Marcel Herholdt gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640796246237 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marcel Herholdt (b. 1980) lives and works in Greyton, a small town near Cape Town. He works with paint on canvas and his narrative deals with his dislike of control and authority. His latest body of work will be featured in his first gallery exhibition and is titled Welcome to Club Cocomo. \\n \\nHis Afro-pop protest art paintings shoot from the hip and hits the heart. His style is colourful and solid, his iconography laden with metaphors for hope, peace and love. \\n \\nThe message is simple; resist power and control. Fight war, don’t make war. \\n \\nThe irony is that we’ll all end up in Club Cocomo, a fictional world created by Herholdt that symbolises a paradise park, a place of lost dreams, lost hopes and broken promises. \\n \\n“For me these paintings are like tickets or stamps that get you entry to Club Cocomo.”"}]}]}

item.title: Marcel Tchopwe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641772732637 Marcel Tchopwe 2256 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640796311773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013460304093"] [17115] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"To develop his potential, he regularly visits the workshop of the main young artists of the contemporary Cameroonian scene such as Jean Jacques Kanté, Herve Youmbi, Salifou Lindou and Jean-David Nkot.\" \\n \\nBorn in the Far North region of Cameroon, Marcel TCHOPWE is a young artist passionate about drawing and painting. In 2014, he interrupted his studies in geoscience and environmental studies at the University of Ngaoundéré to enroll in the Institute of Fine Arts at the University of Douala in Nkongsamba (IBA). Five years later, he graduated with a degree in fine arts. In order to further his education and immerse himself in the art scene, he worked with artists such as Hervé YOUMBI, Jean Jacques Kanté, SALIFOU LINDOU, and Jean David Nkot. Today, he is still mentored by Hervé YOUMBI, who was his teacher at IBA and is now considered his mentor. \\n \\nMarcel's work revolves around psychological portraiture in relation to social unease, where he explores emotions and human complexity. Whether through painting, drawing, or installations, social discomfort serves as a pretext for him to journey through the inner world of his subjects. He highlights the latent social discontent that accompanies our pursuit of profit in an era where capitalism increasingly defines us. Influenced by artists such as Lucien Freud, Cristina Troufa, Kevin Peterson, and Mich Griffitchs, who serve as models for him in exploring human emotions and their capacity to be human, Marcel's artistic production portrays the psychological profile of Cameroonian and African youth navigating a landscape marked by a significant gap between their university education and the job market. Through a realistic approach, he provides insight into the daily lives of a youth educated for unemployment. Marcel's works depict young people with the tools of their dream professions, engaged in menial jobs that have become their sole escape for survival. Against flat backgrounds, this abandoned youth is seen in burning solitude, facing their situation. Through this work, he sparks a discussion about the role of youth in a society undergoing transformation. He also questions the functionality of social mobility and equal opportunities in a political landscape marred by poor governance. \\n \\n \\n \\nThe question of emotion is a constant concern in Marcel's work as he explores the inner world of his characters, leading to introspection of himself and humanity as a whole. He delves into the mindset of his subjects through facial expressions, body language, gestures, clothing styles, and the objects that surround them because they reflect our inner selves. In his paintings and drawings of recent years, sadness, anxiety, and solitude occupy a central place in his creation, reflecting the economic situation of African youth on the cusp of entering the job market after their university and professional training. \\n \\n \\n \\nExhibitions and Training \\n \\n• Master class for strengthening artists' skills led by Simon Njami from December 5, 2022, at the \\n \\n MAM Foundation in Souza. \\n \\n• 2020-2022 Post-Master program created and led by Hervé Youmbi. Artwork Workshop, MAM \\n \\n Gallery, organized by the Moleskine Foundation and led by Simon Ndjami, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• 2014 - 2019 INSTITUTE OF FINE ARTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF DOUALA IN NKONGSAMBA \\n \\n \\n \\n \\n \\nExhibitions \\n \\n• 2023 - The Art of Equality: A journey to justice; United Nations Office in Geneva. \\n \\n• 2023 - Summershow, group exhibition, 193gallery, Paris, France. \\n \\n• 2023 - Arco Lisbao, Artfair, Lisbon, Portugal. \\n \\n• 2023 - MOMO SA Exhibition of Pan African Contemporary, The Melrose Gallery. \\n \\n• 2022 - AKAA (ALSO KNOW AS AFRICA), 7th edition at Le Carreau du Temple, Paris, France. \\n \\n• 2022 - DICOKAM, group exhibition, 193 gallery, Paris, France. \\n \\n• 2021 - POP, group exhibition, The Melrose Gallery, Sandton City, South Africa. \\n \\n• 2021 - REFLET, French Institute of Cameroon (IFC), Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• 2020 - After work, Carré Gallery, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• 2019 - The kai exhibition, Annie Kadji Gallery, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• 2017 - Off du \"SUD\" Exhibition (Urban Salon Douala), Jean David Nkot's studio, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• Exhibition at the LABA (Libre Académie des Beaux-Arts) as part of the \"Young Hopes\" competition \\n \\n initiated by the Doual'art Contemporary Art Center, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• Exhibition at Doual'art for the final of the Young Hopes competition, as part of SUD at Doual'art, \\n \\n Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• Artwork Workshop, MAM Gallery, organized by the Moleskine Foundation and led by Simon \\n \\n Ndjami, Douala, Cameroon. \\n \\n• Exhibition of the results of the Artwork Workshop, MAM Gallery, Cameroon."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013460304093

item.title: Marco Cianfanelli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641774272733 Marco Cianfanelli gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640796475613 [] Marco Cianfanelli, South African Artist, Contemporary Art, Sculpture, Public Art, Art for Sale, Buy Art Online {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marco Cianfanelli was born in Johannesburg in 1970 and graduated, with a distinction in Fine Art, from the University of the Witwatersrand in 1992. He has had seven solo exhibitions – the most recent being data: process – and has won numerous awards, including the ABSA L’Atelier and Ampersand Fellowship. \\nWell-known for his bold public art pieces and large-scale sculptural works, he was a member of the design team for The Freedom Park, South Africa’s national monument to freedom, situated in Pretoria. And his monumental fragmented portrait sculpture, Release, was inaugurated to symbolically mark the 50th anniversary of Nelson Mandela’s capture at the site in the KwaZulu Natal Midlands. Cianfanelli’s latest public works, of unprecedented scale, have been realized in Abu Dhabi, UAE and he is currently working on projects in Texas, USA and Ede in the Netherlands. \\nCianfanelli’s work embodies a vast variety of media and materials. Marrying the application of data to more expressive gestural acts, he aims to set up a tension or dialogue between the controlled accuracies of the digital realm and the uncontrollable realities of being human. \\nKey to his practice is an attempt to give shape to the convergence of multiple kinds of data, knowledge and experience, asserting the interrelatedness of all things. His work explores social hierarchies and channels of consumption as they relate to aspects of human desire, value, beauty and material relationships. \\n"}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641776599261 Margaret Njeri Ngigi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640796541149 {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Margaret Njeri Ngigi was born in 1996 in Kenya and currently lives and works in Nairobi. \\n \\nShe’s a passionate emerging photographer, filmmaker, and film production student at the United States International University-Africa. \\n \\nWhile Margaret has been an artist in many forms since she was young, she has started her journey with the camera over the last four years and with filmmaking two years ago. \\n \\nWomen have been and continue to be the center of most of her projects and by taking those images she makes an image of herself and tries to bring these issues affecting women to the limelight. Another topic she holds dearly is mental illness, represented by using bandages, flower-crowns, and cages to convey the message. \\n \\nHer work has been shown in local and international galleries. \\n \\nRepresented by AKKA Project"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013312979165 gid://shopify/Product/9013313044701 gid://shopify/Product/9013313110237 gid://shopify/Product/9013313143005

She grew up in Wellington in the Cape Winelands and matriculated from La Rochelle Girls’ High School in Paarl. Marguerite Roux is a three time top 100 finalist in the Sasol New Signatures Award competition. \\n \\nSince graduating in 2014 Roux has taken part in a number of group exhibitions, including Greatest Hits: The Domestic Odyssey presented by the AVA Gallery in 2015 and Hinterlands: The Keith Dietrich Award Exhibition at GUS in the same year. Most notably Roux’s work has been shown at the 4th Istanbul Design Biennial, in Turkey as part of Emelie Röndahl’s project Google Weaving Stop-Time in 2018 and at the Also Known as Africa (AKAA) Art Fair in Paris, France with Dyman Gallery in 2019."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013284143325 gid://shopify/Product/9013284176093 gid://shopify/Product/9013284208861 gid://shopify/Product/9013284241629

item.description: Mari Vermeulen Breedt gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640797163741 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Imperfectly Perfect is a collection of works in ceramics by Pretoria based artist Mari V. Breedt. A combination of the artist's own \\nexperiences, knowledge, interest and interpretations illustrates her preoccupation with illness, ceramic and the works of the \\nDella Robbia family of the 15th and 16th centuries. \\n \\n\"The natural world of ferns, foliage and cacti are reminders of the perfect ratio of the Golden Section and is a prime example of \\nthat which is glorious - as opposed to the brokenness of that which surrounds us.\" \\n \\nMari V. Breedt is a multidisciplinary artist with an impressive resumé that include: \\n \\nSOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n1974 Saambou National Building Society,Pretoria. \\n1981 Galerie Duncan, Saint Germaine,Paris \\n1988 Schweickerdt Gallery, Pretoria \\n1993 Sculptura Gallery ,Brasschaat, Belgium. \\n1996 The High Banks Gallery, Saugatuck, MI.,USA \\n1998 ‘’PORTRAITS BY OMISSION” Karen Mc Kerron Gallery,Johannesburg. \\n1999 ‘’INTERIORS’ South African Association of Arts. \\n2002 ‘’VESTIGES OF GRANDEUR’’ Dorpstraat Gallery, Stellenbosch RSA \\n2004 ‘’HIGHVELD - the lives of...’’ University of Pretoria. \\n \\nGROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n1967-NEW SIGNATURES \\n2003,4,6,7 -WH PATTERSON , BOND STREET, LONDON, UK. \\n2007,8.9 --AZALI GALLERY , LAGUNA BEACH, CALIFORNIA, USA \\n2008-‘100 JARIGE BESTAAN’VAN UNIVERSITEIT VAN PRETORIA \\n2013-PENTIMENTI -EXHIBITION Sasol Museum. \\n2013-BP PORTRAIT AWARDS LONDON UK. \\n2014-‘ODYSSEE MET ALEXIS PRELLER’-KKNK \\n2013 SANLAM PORTRET KOMPETISIE TOP 100 \\n2015 SANLAM PORTRET KOMPETISIE- TOP 5 \\n2016 –‘’BREAKING THE SPELL’’WOORDFEES \\n2016-‘’100 GEOGRAPHIES’’WOORDFEES, SASOL MUSEUM."}]}]}

item.title: Maria Caley
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641778008285 Maria Caley gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640797262045 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maria Caley (b. 1982, Rundu, Kavango, north eastern Namibia) was exposed to traditional forms of making indigenous art during her childhood, such as basketry, which has remained part of her unique design identity and inspiration. Caley is a lecturer at the University of Namibia in the department of Humanities and Art. She specializes in textiles and fashion design, and holds a Bachelor of Arts (Textiles and Fashion Studies), and a Masters degree (Visual Arts) from the University of Namibia. Her textile work is informed by Kavango traditional baskets, extracting natural dyes, and creating motifs based on the patterns worked into the baskets, and other indigenous crafts. Caley has exhibited and showcased her work in numerous local and international shows."}]}]}

item.title: Maria Mbereshu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641779581149 Maria Mbereshu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640797425885 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maria Mbereshu (b. 1984 Uvhungu-Vhungu in Rundu, Kavango Region), earned a Higher Diploma in Visual Arts from the University of Namibia in 2013, including Fashion and Textile Studies, and Visual Culture. Mbereshu recently attended the Bakers Bay artist retreat, held in Oranjemund, Namibia in 2022. \\n \\nWorking with symbols drawn from her Sambyu culture as well as the banal everyday, Mbereshu works with repetition creating new forms in fields of abstract shapes. She is constantly experimenting with different materials to express ideas around domesticity and the home. \\n \\nMbereshu’s work has been included in various exhibitions locally and internationally, including: Education, arts, and culture conference exhibition NAGN, 2022; To the Land ll, Percil Forest Munich (group exhibition) 2022; Cross-Cultural Collaboration, Germany/Namibia (virtual residency) ~dotlab, 2021; #WhatsYourStory, COVID-19 Project, NAGN, 2020; Bank Windhoek Triennial, NAGN, 2020; Reflect: Namibia 30 years of independence, NAGN, 2018; Piece of Heaven exhibition, Gallery Hamara, University of Lapland and fringe festival, Australia, 2017; Werah Cafe and Gallery, Rundu, 2017; Textures and Textiles on fabric, NAGN, 2017; Booth Exhibition, NAGN, 2013; Land Matters in Art, Namibian art project, NAGN, 2010; UNAM annual student exhibition, NAGN and FNCC."}]}]}

Working with the Omba Arts Trust and drawing on San cultural resources to develop products, the San artisans are reviving the 72 000-year-old ostrich eggshell bead-making skills. These beads are incorporated by artists into some of their artworks, together with embroidery."}]}]}

item.title: Mariapaola McGurk
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641777287389 Mariapaola McGurk gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640798114013 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mariapaola (or fondly known as MP) has been a practising visual artist for over 20 years. She has her honours, cum laude, in visual arts and an Executive MBA. Her speciality was painting until, in 2010, she started exploring papercutting as an artform and has been working in this artform ever since. This artform is not common and there are only a handful of contemporary papercutting artists globally with even fewer within South Africa. MP has been exploring this medium for many years trying to find an approach that both technically and conceptually aligns to her style and intention. \\n \\nThe process of making these artworks is core to its appeal: \\n \\n‘This artform challenges my very nature and has been critical to my daily life. I am a fast paced, passionate, and volatile person who sometimes does not stop long enough to catch my own breath – but this artform forces me to stop, to consider, and to breathe a little slower. I cannot speed up the process, I cannot ‘run’ as I usually do – this has been a huge blessing to me. The simplicity of the material really captivates something that I am continually in search of – peace, truth, the purpose of our lives. The final artworks are all only one piece of paper that have been cut delicately to reveal the artwork, they are fragile and very detailed. The process of this artform is as important as the concept in the works.’ \\n \\nMP works as a lecturer, researcher, and consultant alongside being a visual artist. Her interest lies in creative entrepreneurship and its potential impact on youth unemployment within South Africa. Mariapaola McGurk (D’Andrea) is first generation South African born with Italian/Irish heritage. Her father immigrated to South Africa from a small village in Abruzzi, Italy at 17 years old; and her mother from Dublin, Ireland at 5 years old."}]}]}

item.title: Marie Aimée Fattouche
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641785872605 Marie Aimée Fattouche gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640798605533 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013977383133","gid://shopify/Product/9013977579741","gid://shopify/Product/9013979283677","gid://shopify/Product/9013979349213","gid://shopify/Product/9013979447517"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1991,Marie Aimée Fattouche lives and works in Seine-Saint-Denis, France. Marie draws inspiration from her fascination with mechanics, whether mental, bodily, or environmental. From simple disruptions to breakdowns, from initial impulses to the ultimate fluidity of movement, her art navigates the space between repair and sublimation, exploring areas of uncertainty where contradictory possibilities converge. For her, each fracture, whether tangible or abstract, serves as a catalyst for profound transformation. \\nImbued with her Egyptian roots, her perspective on the organization of bodies reflects Eastern perceptions of space. Through her work, she actively interrogates collective narratives and femininity while scrutinizing mechanisms of power and belief systems. Her artistic compositions offer a multitude of perspectives, both spatial and temporal, inviting the viewer to immerse themselves in a construction perpetually in motion, transcending mere representation. \\nFollowing her final MA Fine Art exhibition in 2016 (Chelsea College of Arts, London), M.A Fattouche was awarded the Mercers’ Arts Award. In 2017, as the winner of the Red Mansion Art Prize, she was invited to spend a month of residency in Beijing. In 2019, she had the honor of being among the eight artists shortlisted for the Mark Tanner Sculpture Award at Standpoint Gallery in London (the UK’s most prestigious prize for emerging artists working in sculpture). Her work has been exhibited in various institutions, including the Hock-ney Gallery (2018), and more recently at the Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MAMC+) in Saint-Étienne as part of the GLOBALISTO exhibition (June to October 2022). In January 2024, she has presented her solo exhibition NOUS INFINIR MON AMOUR at Galerie du Haut-Pavé in Paris."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013977383133 gid://shopify/Product/9013977579741 gid://shopify/Product/9013979283677 gid://shopify/Product/9013979349213 gid://shopify/Product/9013979447517

item.title: Marie Kenny
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641786724573 Marie Kenny 2750 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640798867677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014034366685"] Discover Marie Kenny, a self-taught lens-based artist from Lyon, France, who uses photography to explore identity, cultural heritage, and neurodivergence. Her work merges documentary style with painterly qualities, inviting viewers into a contemplative space. [23005] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marie Kenny (b. 1984), a self-taught contemporary lens-based artist from Lyon, France, has been passionate about art from a young age. After studying the cello at the Conservatoire de Lyon, she moved to the UK and Ireland in her early twenties to further her studies in music, language, art history, and literature. \\nMotherhood, particularly raising neurodivergent children, deepened her commitment to photography, which she uses as a tool to navigate and understand the world, and explore her own neurodivergence. Radical acceptance and mindfulness are central to her practice. \\nMarie’s work merges documentary style with painterly qualities, using light, movement, and framing to create images that feel both immediate and timeless. Her art explores themes such as identity, cultural and familial heritage, and neurodivergence, inviting viewers into a contemplative space where fleeting, nuanced moments are celebrated. \\nMarie draws inspiration from her experiences and has been a mentee of the Through the Lens Collective."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014034366685

item.title: Marie-Lorraine Kalassa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641783644381 Marie-Lorraine Kalassa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640799260893 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013927051485","gid://shopify/Product/9013927117021","gid://shopify/Product/9013927149789","gid://shopify/Product/9013944713437"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Through an autoethnographic practice; that is the primary use of personal reflexive writing to craft narratives related to wider social and cultural experiences, Lorraine Kalassa explores themes revolving around her experiences of ‘otherness’. \\nHer main focus lies in trying to make sense of notions of home as a person born in South Africa with ancestry rooted in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Lorraine is fascinated with her family photo archive as well as the archive existing within her mother’s mind. She is also intrigued by how relationship with land and place influences the development of identity and culture. Returning to her ancestral archives have become important sites of exploration and excavation for her work as this act becomes a form of pilgrimage and time travel to her place of origin. By using a range of media and thinking through cracks in identity, landscape and policies, Lorraine ultimately tethers ancestral fragments as a means to remember and heal. \\nLorraine’s obtained a degree in Fine Arts from the Michaelis School of Fine Arts and an Honours degree in Landscape Architecture from the University of Cape Town. Lorraine is a member of The Photographic Collective(TPC) and has been featured in the following exhibitions and publications: \\nUnder Projects, Cape Town: JIVE Exhibition, 2023 ,Goethe-Institut, Johannesburg: JIVE Exhibition, 2023, Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg: We are Culture Exhibition, Sept-Oct 2022 ArtThrob: Family Albums, September 2021, 99 Loop Gallery, Cape Town: 12 Hours of Breathing (group show), July 2021 Group exhibition with TPC, London: 1-54, Contemporary African Art Fair, 2021 In conversation with The Photographic Collective (TPC): In Conversation with Lorraine Kalassa, May 2020"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013927051485 gid://shopify/Product/9013927117021 gid://shopify/Product/9013927149789 gid://shopify/Product/9013944713437

item.title: Marieke Kruger
item.description: Marieke Kruger 666 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640799424733 [2777,2778,2779,2780,2781,22915,2782] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"I currently work as a visual artist and lecturer of drawing and printmaking at the Jack Meyer Art Centre in Paarl, South Africa. I was brought up on a farm called “Rainbow’s End” in the Banhoek valley. Being surrounded by the beauty of nature since childhood, I developed a growing desire to study art and completed my B.A. Fine Art Degree at the University of Stellenbosch in 1994 (majoring in Painting). I moved to Johannesburg in 1996 and completed my M. Tech degree studies (cum laude) in Visual Art specialising in drawing and stone lithography at the University of Johannesburg. After completing a 4-month student exchange, specialising in printmaking, at the Karel de Groote Hogeschool in Antwerp, Belgium, I returned to South Africa to finish my M.Tech studies with a solo exhibition entitled “A HOLY WAR” at the Civic Gallery, Johannesburg in 1998. \\n \\nShortly after the birth of my first daughter, I moved back to Cape Town and worked as a Visual art and Design lecturer in various institutions. Currently, I am employed as a Visual art educator at the Jack Meyer Art Centre in Paarl, which focuses on secondary Visual art and Design education. Furthermore, I have been involved in various community art projects (through VANSA), presenting different drawing workshops for the Stellenbosch Art Society as well as my involvement in drawing rehabilitation workshops, product development, job creation for ex-convicts in the visual arts and research (focused on identity transformation, healing and rehabilitation through drawing and printmaking) in various prisons in South Africa. Most recently we have extended our prison project to other prisons in the Paarl vicinity such as Allandale prison and currently Anne-Ghrett Erasmus and I have curated our first Virtual prison art printmaking and drawing exhibition entitled “INMATES VS OUTMATES” at the Breytenbach Art Gallery in Wellington. (https://www.facebook.com/breytenbachgalery/). (June/July 2020) \\n \\nI participated in various art projects and group shows as well as several solo exhibitions. My first solo exhibition entitled “A HOLY WAR” took place at the Civic Gallery (1998, Johannesburg, partial requirement for Masters studies) and was followed with several other solo shows – such as “TO A PROMISED LAND…” at the Bell-Roberts gallery, (August 2006) and a collaborative exhibition with the ceramicist, Dr Ralph Johnson entitled “JOURNEYS” at the Grande Provence Gallery in Franschhoek (March 2007). These solo shows were followed with another solo exhibition at the ABSA Gallery in Johannesburg, entitled “ABOUT FACE I” (February 2009) and a follow up solo show entitled “ABOUT FACE II” (was held at the Art-b Gallery in Bellville during August 2009). Most recent solo exhibitions include “Carceral spaces - Anticipating the Sublime” (Oliewenhuis Museum, Reservoir Gallery, 2017) and the “Hidden” solo exhibition hosted at the Everard Read Gallery in 2018. Currently working on upcoming two person exhibition with artist Henk Serfontein entitled “CONFESSIONALE” (Italian for “Confessional”) at the DeepestDarkest Gallery, Cape Town (October/November 2020). \" \\n \\n \\n \\nIn November 2009, one of my daughters, Bethany, was diagnosed with cancer. For the duration of her illness, I only took part in various group exhibitions during 2010. In 2011, I was accepted to study for a second Master’s Degree in Visual art, specializing in drawing, at the University of Stellenbosch. I recently successfully completed this degree with a solo exhibition entitled “REFLECTING SELF” of my drawings as partial requirement towards obtaining the degree, at the Equus Gallery, Cavalli Estate in October/November 2014. \\n \\n \\n \\nIn 2015 I started becoming involved with the Art Programme at Drakenstein Correctional Services and specifically focussed my drawing and printing rehabilitation workshops towards skill training, job creation for the inmates when they leave prison in the field of visual arts and my personal research (on the transformative potential of the experience of the sublime through the visual arts in carceral spaces). During 2015 and 2016 I was nominated as finalist to obtain second prize in the painting and drawing categories of the CELESTE ART PRIZE as well as the TABOO International Art prize competitions in Italy. I was also an invited artist to represent my country in the ArtRooms 2016 Art Fair in London, UK in 2016."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013280637149 gid://shopify/Product/9013280669917 gid://shopify/Product/9013280702685 gid://shopify/Product/9013280735453 gid://shopify/Product/9013280768221

item.title: Mariette Momberg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641784103133 Mariette Momberg 1709 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640799752413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013358919901","gid://shopify/Product/9013360001245","gid://shopify/Product/9013361311965","gid://shopify/Product/9013369635037"] [11406,11446,12381] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I work predominantly on paper to create colourful and emotive works. My works are in private collections, both international and local. My current art practice centres predominantly around printmaking, which I often use in conjunction with other mediums such as embroidery, acrylic and watercolour. I am passionate about the environment and strongly feel that creative efforts should make a conscious effort to minimise environmental impact. For this reason I use water-based mediums in my art making and strive to maintain a low-toxic and environmentally considerate studio. \\n \\nI am a self-taught artist and printmaker and have been practicing full-time since 2018. Prior to pursuing a career in art, I worked in Academia and as an Osteopath. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013358919901 gid://shopify/Product/9013360001245 gid://shopify/Product/9013361311965 gid://shopify/Product/9013369635037

item.title: Marilú Mapengo Námoda
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641792917725 Marilú Mapengo Námoda gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640800407773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013389361373","gid://shopify/Product/9013389394141","gid://shopify/Product/9013389426909","gid://shopify/Product/9013389492445","gid://shopify/Product/9013389590749","gid://shopify/Product/9013389623517"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marilú Mapengo Námoda is an artist that engages with the politics of giving birth to the futureS. Her research explores the possibility of a love politics for healing colonial wounds in its multiple expressions of racism, machismo, classism, etc. Through hybrid formats, their practice weaves languages from performance art, animist astrology, storytelling, Bantu writing symbols, healing rituals, and post-activist provocateur prompts. Her work has been exhibited at the Santarcangelo Festival (Italy, 2022), Spielart Festival (Germany, 2021), Kaserne Basel (Switzerland, 2021), and Entretodos Human Rights Festival, ( Brazil, 2019), among others. \\nNámoda holds a MA degree in Art Praxis from the Dutch Art Institute, Arnhem 2022; A BA in Sociology from the Eduardo Mondlane University - Maputo, 2013; and a Post-Graduation Degree in Gender Studies from the University of Iceland /UNU GEST Program – Reykjavik, 2016. In 2022 the Artist was nominated for two international awards: The Berry Koedam Award by Kunstinstituut Melly, Netherlands, and The Paulo Cunha e Silva award by the Municipality of Porto, Portugal."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013389361373 gid://shopify/Product/9013389394141 gid://shopify/Product/9013389426909 gid://shopify/Product/9013389492445 gid://shopify/Product/9013389590749 gid://shopify/Product/9013389623517

item.title: Marina Walsh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641794785501 Marina Walsh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640800800989 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born and raised in Johannesburg, South Africa, Marina Matriculated from the Deutsche Schule zu Johannesburg before obtaining her Diploma in Ceramic Design from the Technikon of the Witwatersrand. \\n \\nEarly on in her professional career, she established her own company that focused on ceramic design. This branch of her work continues to thrive today and has provided her with one of many creative channels. \\n \\nFor a decade she worked as a freelance Art Director for some of the top-rated photographers in Johannesburg; including art directing and producing magazine and billboard advertisements"}]}]}

item.title: Mário Macilau
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848590557 Mário Macilau gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640895762653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013404664029", "gid://shopify/Product/9013404729565", "gid://shopify/Product/9013404860637"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mário Macilau is a multidisciplinary artist and activist, best known for his work as a photographer. He was born in 1984 in the Mozambican capital and currently lives between Lisbon and Maputo. \\nIn 2003, Macilau began his photographic activity, spending his early career learning and developing his techniques. \\nIn 2007, he launched himself as a professional photographer, swapping his mother's mobile phone, without her knowledge, for an excellent Nikon FM2. A few years later his talent crossed borders and he has won several major international awards, travelled widely and seen his work published in some of the most prestigious galleries, art fairs and exhibitions around the world. \\nHis photography highlights identity, political issues and environmental conditions, sometimes working with socially isolated groups to make his audience aware not only of the many social injustices and inequalities in the world but also to show stories of humanity, brotherhood, victory, love and hope. Often the portrait is his starting point, his approach being instrumental in revealing a broader perspective. \\nMacilau's work has been a regular presence in solo and group exhibitions, both in his home country and abroad. \\nExamples include the Art Fair 1: 54 in London, UK (2018); Art Madrid in Madrid, Spain (2018 and 2019); Art Marbella,Spain (2018); Third Beijing Biennale of Photography, Beijing, China (2018); Unseen, Amsterdam, Netherlands (2018); FNB Art Fair Johannesburg, South Africa (2018); the World Climate Summit, San Francisco, USA (2018); the High Museum of Art in Atlanta, Georgia, USA (2018); IPhoton Festival, Valencia, Spain (2017); Photomonth Festival Krakow, Krakow, Poland (2017); the Indian Festival of Photography - IPF (2017); Hyderabad, India (2017); Berlin Art Week at Kehrer Gallery, Berlin, Germany (2017); Sicily Photobook Festival, Sicily, Italy (2017); Porto Photography Festival, Porto, Portugal (2017); \"I don't like Black People but I do like you\", Paulo Nunes Gallery, Portugal (2017); Tbilisi Photography Festival, Tbilisi, Georgia (2017); AKAA Art Fair,Paris, France (2016). Macilau was also selected by Fotofestiwal of ?ód?, Poland,to present his first monograph, \"Growing in Darkness\", in a monumental self-name exhibition as part of the festival entitled \"Discovery Show\" (2015). Other noteworthy exhibitions in his own name include: the photographer's participation in the56th. the Venice Biennale, Italy (2015), \"The Road Not Taken\" at The Auction Room, London (2015); \"Nothing Like Time\", curated by Berry Bickle, at Kulungwana Gallery in Maputo(2015); ENTRY PROHIBITED TO FOREIGNERS, Havremagasinet - Boden Art Centre, Sweden (2015); The Pangaea: New Art from Africa and Latin America, Saatchi Gallery,London, UK (2014); Fotofest Biennial, Houston, Texas, USA (2014); among many others. His work is present in many private and public collections around the world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013404664029 gid://shopify/Product/9013404729565 gid://shopify/Product/9013404827869 gid://shopify/Product/9013404860637

He moved from Mozambique to South Africa in 2008. Soares initially worked as an artist/embroiderer for Boitumelo in Hillbrow, however in 2010 he began his studies at Artist Proof Studio. Soares graduated in 2013 and proceeded to develop his skill in etching. Soares’ medium is printmaking, and he works primarily in etching on steel plates. In his body of work he divulges into the metaphor of the road to explore concepts concerning the processes of growing up, travel and migration. As an immigrant himself, Soares chooses to use faceless and generalised ‘identity-less’ subjects as he feels it gives a voice to the ways in which immigrants seek to make themselves invisible in their new home country, fearful of entrenched xenophobia. In 2014, he became an intern at APS at the Pro-Shop. Soares now works as an independent artist full time fro his studio on Johannesburg. \\n \\nHe has been part of numerous group shows and art fairs both in Johannesburg and in Cape Town. \\n \\nSOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2017 \\n \\nEvolution - Being engaged in a private community project in Kliptown, she began her artistic career in Johannesburg creating her unique, magnificent collages. The artist addresses and examines the interfaces and relationships between African and Western cultures in history until nowadays. Her themes relate to personal experiences and are reflected in her different series focusing on socio-economic and cultural matters. Her work is an impressive combination of artistic integrity, conceptual vision and aesthetic beauty. \\n \\n2020 \\n- Solo Show - OOA Gallery - Barcelona, Spain \\n- Art X Lagos Art Fair - OOA Gallery - Lagos, Nigeria \\n- 1-54 New York Online Art Fair - OOA Gallery - New York, USA \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n2019 \\n- “On paper” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n- Cape Town Art fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- Expo Chicago – ARTCO Gallery – Chicago, USA \\n- “Filam(a)nt Exhibition – Fondation Blachère – Apt, France \\n- “Spaces in Between” Exhibition – This is Not a White Cube Gallery - Lisbon, Portugal \\n- AKAA ART Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- Paper Positions Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Berlin, Germany \\n- Latitudes Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Gallery Michel Giraud – Paris, France - Luxembourg Art Week – Gallery Michel Giraud – Luxembourg, Grand-Dûché de Luxembourg \\n2018 \\n- “Background Africa” - SOART Gallery – Casablanca, Morocco \\n- AKAA Art Fair - ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- 1-54 London Art Fair (solo show) – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Black Paris” (solo show) – Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- “Unfolding fibre” - Pretoria Art Museum – Pretoria, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- London Art Fair (solo show) – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n2017 \\n- “Hairitage” - AKAA Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- “Stitched” (solo show) – Art Paris Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- “Rituale” - Afrikahaus Aachen – Aachen, Germany \\n2016 \\n- “Maskerade” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n- AKAA Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Paris, France \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- That Art Fair – ARTCO Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- “Targets” - ARTCO Gallery – Aachen, Germany \\n2015 \\n- Start Art Fair Saatchi Gallery – ARTCO Gallery – London, UK \\n- Art Vilnius – ARTCO Gallery – Vilnius, Lithuania \\n- “Swenkas” (solo show) – In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Ubuntu Reflections” (solo show) – Alliance Française – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Cape Town Art Fair – Cape Town, South Africa \\n2014 \\n- Group exhibition – Youngblood Gallery – Cape Town, South Africa \\n- FNB Joburg Art Fair – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Silent beauty” (solo show) – Saxon Hotel – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Silent beauty” (solo show) – Alliance Française – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Gold rush” - In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2013 \\n- Joburg Fringe Art Fair – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- Group Exhibition - The German Weeks – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n- “Patched” (solo show) – In Toto Gallery – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2012 \\n- Grand Hyatt Hotel Rosebank – Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\nHer newest series “Legacy” interprets a new African identity based on traditional roots facing the confusion of a globalized world. “In my series„ Legacy, I want to point out that the African continent has a rich cultural background to build on” says Marion. Her mixed media collages with traditional African masks, beads, cawrie shells and fabrics highlight the beauty, loyalty and positive energy of the African women. \\n \\nThe traditional African masks that Marion Boehm integrates in her artworks were used in traditional and social events to represent the spirits of ancestors or to control the good and evil forces in the community. They come to life, possessed by their spirit in the performance of the dance and are enhanced by the music and atmosphere of the occasion. Some masks combine human and animal features to unite man with his natural environment. This bond with nature is of great importance to the African and, through the ages, masks have always been used to express this relationship. \\n \\n“I use African masks in my work to relate to the beauty and spiritual power of them in the context of a culturally impoverished and spiritually distressed modern world. But do they still have their original meaning? What do they represent to the generation of today? Can they be a point of reference and still offer a kind of orientation? What do the traditions mean for today’s life and what do they teach us for the future?” In order to underline her message, Marion’s statement is always printed in the faces of her characters. \\n \\nMarion Boehm ?s work has been collected internationally. Her artwork was presented during shows and art fairs in South Africa, Germany, France, UK, Lithuania, Morocco, Portugal, Luxemburg, Switzerland, USA. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013448671453 gid://shopify/Product/9013448704221 gid://shopify/Product/9013448736989 gid://shopify/Product/9013448769757 gid://shopify/Product/9013448835293 gid://shopify/Product/9013448868061 gid://shopify/Product/9013448900829 gid://shopify/Product/9013448966365 gid://shopify/Product/9013449031901 gid://shopify/Product/9013842968797 gid://shopify/Product/9013843001565 gid://shopify/Product/9014039544029 gid://shopify/Product/9014039576797

item.title: Marisa Maré
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798193373 Marisa Maré gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640802603229 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013926822109","gid://shopify/Product/9013926887645","gid://shopify/Product/9013927018717"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marisa Maré is an artist and educator from the Western Cape who investigates the pressing issues related to climate change. \\nAs a leader in the arts education space she has actively developed her students' awareness of climate change issues through various educational initiatives. This included participation in the Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Programme, collaboration with the WWF, and planning and presenting a webinar titled Drought in South Africa: Resilience in the Face of Climate Change. Marisa has won the Bow Seat global Educator Innovation Award for two years. \\nMore recently, she has turned her focus to her visual arts practice completing a Master's degree in Visual Arts at the University of Johannesburg with distinction. Her dissertation and exhibition titled Making and Unmaking: Plastic Matters explored themes such as grieving ecological loss, and developing empathy with nonhumans. In her exploration of the creative and destructive potential of plastic, Maré has developed bioplastic from natural and agricultural waste materials, utilising them as art materials for her experimental works. She documents the degradation of these bioplastic sculptures through photographic and microscopic imaging to raise questions about the possibility of 'touching the Earth lightly'. Through her creative process, she aims to uncover how her choice of medium is entangled with an extensive web of environmental factors. To some extent, her sculptures and the microbesaiding in their decay are ‘performers’ with agency beyond the artist’s control that render the entangled materiality visible. \\nIn earlier bodies of work, she has been concerned with the impermanence and transience of her art materials. In an exhibition titled Symptoms, she created an installation that included sculptural works with hand-made paper, gauze, rust and salt which pointed to 'symptoms' that are indexical of broader societal concerns."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013926822109 gid://shopify/Product/9013926887645 gid://shopify/Product/9013927018717

item.title: Mark Modimola
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798258909 Mark Modimola 1593 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640803127517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013342109917","gid://shopify/Product/9013352399069","gid://shopify/Product/9013371961565","gid://shopify/Product/9013371994333","gid://shopify/Product/9013372813533","gid://shopify/Product/9014000156893","gid://shopify/Product/9014000189661"] [21597,21599,12510,12511,9606] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I am an African Visual Artist, born in Pretoria. Originally a graphic designer, I consider myself a versatile creator, with a portfolio that explores the cadences of African identity and spirituality, often through the cultural aesthetics of portraiture and surrealism. I aim to emphasize the experience of blackness through my work. I believe in sharing positive representation to and for the black community while translating the complexity we bring to the world through vivid imagery. I am highly inspired by nature, it’s authenticity, unending originality and innovation. As such, my passions are tied in with Africa; its land and its people, this can be seen in my work. \\nOver recent years, I have been involved in a range of international projects. My work features on several articles by The Kraal who have published: The Guide to African Spirituality. Volume 0, in which my artwork of Ma’at is featured. I worked on a South African history graphic novel called “All Rise ; Resistance and Rebellion “. My work will appear in an upcoming American book called Black Joy Project. In 2021, I worked on a campaign for #Giveheracrown, an initiative raising funds for young female Africa designers in association with Jaguar, in which my work was donated and exhibited. \\nMy work has been exhibited in Art it is Gallery as well as Stargazer gallery among other. group shows in Johannesburg. Having participated in an Online art Residency known as BLVCK BLOCK I have explored natural themes and materials in a search for a deeper connection between contemporary Africans and nature. Recently I showcased my new clay and acrylic paintings at Solo restaurant in Sandton, as well as Troyeville house in Johannesburg with The Culture Review."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013342109917 gid://shopify/Product/9013352399069 gid://shopify/Product/9013371961565 gid://shopify/Product/9013371994333 gid://shopify/Product/9013372813533 gid://shopify/Product/9014000156893 gid://shopify/Product/9014000189661

item.title: Marius Jansen van Vuuren
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798226141 Marius Jansen van Vuuren gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640802930909 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marius Jansen van Vuuren born in 1981 in South Africa is a multidisciplinary artist working in various materials. Part of his process is collaborating with other artists when creating large scale artworks in public spaces. His interests speak to establishing relationships with the spaces that we inhabit, both physical as well as social. Consequently, his works aim to engage the public as part of his art creation process. \\nBorn in 1981, Jansen van Vuuren received his BTech: Fine Arts degree from the Central University of Technology in Bloemfontein in 2009, and has since worked as an art artist, facilitator, educator, and art coordinator. In 2016 he built a giant sculpture as part of the flagship project of the Free State Art Festival. This led to collaborations with international artists on a variety of large-scale works, including the world’s largest straw squirrel in Kazakhstan, as well as works in China and the UK. Recently he coordinated the Presidential Public Arts Program (PPAP) which enabled 100 artists to create mural paintings as part of the Presidential Employment Stimulus Plan (PESP)."}]}]}

item.title: Mark Rautenbach

Mark has worked as Mark Rautenbach, Mark Splendid, Mark Maria and Splendid Miriam. He works in a variety of mediums; often with material which is considered waste matter, thread and paper. Mark uses many techniques; development of yarns, knitting, public performances and craft-like studio work. \\n \\nMark has also lectured Design for a number of years at Cape Peninsular University of Technology [CPUT], and education recurs as a theme in his work along with identities born out of narratives [yarns]. \\n \\nRautenbach has shown at The south African National Gallery, Everard Read, Open 24 Hrs, Spier, David Krut Projects, and Ebony/curated."}]}]}

item.title: Mark Swart
item.description: Mark Swart 2939 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640804045021 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014142140637","gid://shopify/Product/9014142206173","gid://shopify/Product/9014142238941","gid://shopify/Product/9014142304477","gid://shopify/Product/9014142337245","gid://shopify/Product/9014142370013"] Explore the art of Mark Swart, a renowned South African sculptor. Discover how he challenges perceptions of steel, creating expressive forms that unite imagination with tangible matter, sought after by collectors worldwide. [25276,25275,25279,25278,25277,25274] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mark Swart (born in 1966) is a renowned artist who has became a full-time designer and sculptor in 1992. His artistic journey is a pursuit of beauty through form, whether in design, sculpture, architecture, or functional pieces. \\nSwart's design philosophy is elegantly simple: form follows function, utilizing only essential lines to define an object. He believes in how form presents itself, the message conveys, and the emotions it evokes. \"By giving my sculptures titles, I am giving them life, opening channels to communicate their story to the observer,\"Swart explains. He challenges the perception of steel as merely hard and cold, instead stretching its physical plasticity to enhance the image and convey the sculpture's emotional message. \\n \\nUltimately, Swart's work strives to create balance between the spiritual and physical worlds, uniting imagination and sensation with tangible matter. His art is highly sought after by collectors both locally and internationally."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014142140637 gid://shopify/Product/9014142206173 gid://shopify/Product/9014142238941 gid://shopify/Product/9014142304477 gid://shopify/Product/9014142337245 gid://shopify/Product/9014142370013

item.title: Marlene Steyn
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641800716509 Marlene Steyn gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640804339933 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marlene Steyn was born in 1989 in Cape Town, South Africa, where she currently lives and works. Steyn obtained her Master of Fine Art degree in 2014 from the Royal College of Art in London, UK. \\nHer work is included in Phaidon’s prestigious Vitamin C: Clay and Ceramic in Contemporary Art publication in 2017. Artist-in-residence programmes include a collaborative residency with Kay 16 and Artport Residency in Tel Aviv, Israel (2017) and an upcoming residency Sundaymorning@ekwc and centre-of-excellence for ceramics in Oisterwijk, Netherlands in 2022. \\nSteyn has participated in numerous art fairs including a solo presentation at Miart in Milan in 2018, as well as group presentations at 1:54 Contemporary African Art Fair, London, UK; the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, Cape Town, South Africa; (2020) and FNB Art Joburg, Johannesburg, South Africa (2019)"}]}]}

item.title: Marlene de Beer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641798455517 Marlene de Beer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640804733149 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marlene de BeerPhD Visual Arts (US)Marlene is a PhD graduate in Visual Arts (US) and a qualified goldsmith. Apart from her participation in the genre of contemporary jewellery, her artistic interest includes sculptural objects in a selection of materials such as porcelain, resin, and bronze. Her research interests include an exploration of female subjectivity and agency, and the notion of a feminine Imaginary and Divine. From a phenomenological perspective, meaning making and sublimation as an active agent is directly dependant on the subjective lifeworld of the subject. Contemporary jewellery can serve as coded messages with which to challenge and comment on prescriptive norms."}]}]}

item.title: Marlise Keith
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641800782045 Marlise Keith gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640805093597 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marlise Keith (b. 1972) is known for her mixed media collages; large-scale drawings in pencil, ink and acrylics; and most recently, for her small sculptures of fabric, embroidery and found objects. \\n \\nHer subject matter is vast, drawing inspiration from a mental medley of horrific news headlines, colonial history, friends’ pets, psychopathology, girlhood memories, dreams, her persistent migraines, and roadside memorials. Subjects too daunting, too confused, or too subliminal to articulate in neat words and sentences, are processed through mark-making; offering an alternative “understanding” of a world that often does not make sense in traditional, logical language. This violence emerges in plentiful paint; sometimes it is suggested by the very act of mark-making itself – paper is gouged, scratched, sanded, torn, folded, and nailed."}]}]}

item.title: Marna Hattingh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641801076957 Marna Hattingh gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640805454045 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The densely patterned, colourful work of Marna Hattingh (b.1977) occupies a hybrid, ambiguous space in both form and meaning. She describes her artworks as “interrogations of the complexity and the contradictions of human nature and also the absurdity of life”, with her background in children’s book illustration lending her practice a playfulness and humour that belie the darker, satirical and more serious thematic undercurrents. Drawing inspiration from sources as diverse as Asian fashion, the media, history and novels, she creates a kind of parallel universe, where grotesque-cute , busy characters are layered over dizzying backgrounds in an intensive and intricate creative process. Depth is flattened, non-existent or even used to introduce additional “parallel worlds”, with shadow planes further populated by lyrical imagery that collides with and complicates the layers of narrative. The result is an idiosyncratic graphic style that has been described as a “hyper-textual visual language”."}]}]}

item.title: Marnus Strydom
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641801797853 Marnus Strydom gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640805847261 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marnus Strydom is a self-taught fine art photographer based in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\nKnown for his portraiture and experimental landscape work, Strydom uses analogue photography and cross-process development techniques, to distort reality and create an alternate universe in which he explores themes such as the current climate crisis, human nature and nostalgia \\nStrydom cut his teeth in rural South Africa before relocating to Johannesburg in 2018. His Rural Gothic series caught the attention of the public with regular features in online publications such as Klyntji and Between 10 and 5, allowing the artist to make a move from the Eastern Cape Highlands to Johannesburg. He is currently working in the contemporary art industry."}]}]}

item.title: Marolize Southwood
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641803272413 Marolize Southwood gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640806011101 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marolize Southwood is an artist based in Cape Town. She completed her BAFA at the Michaelis School of Fine Art in 2017. She was born in Potchefstroom and grew up in Viljoenskroon, a small town in the Free State. At Michaelis, Marolize majored in photography but has since expanded her practice to include painting. \\n \\nSouthwood’s work stems from a fascination with the constructed reality we humans have created for ourselves. The artist explores this notion through the use of spaces and objects. In her work, new realities and narratives are created through unusual pairings of the two. The resulting images invite viewers to explore potential meanings and links between the depicted objects. \\n \\nBy using familiar objects in unusual pairings, the artist aims to create a subtle absurdity in her work. This reflects her views upon modern human life, that if you look at it closely you notice the absurdity. In constructing a reality that is slightly absurd but also familiar, the objects and their connotations reflect the very real issues we face as a species due to our technological devices. \\n \\nFor the most part, the artist’s compositions are devoid of natural elements, except for the inclusion of flowers. These flowers represent the role that nature plays in this constructed human life, the amusement we gain from it, the strain we put on it and also our distance from it. Southwood believes that there is humour and beauty in the absurdity that is the human race, the things we do to pass the time and the stuff we make."}]}]}

item.title: Maroula Lambis
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641803305181 Maroula Lambis gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640806240477 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maroula is a self-taught South African artist currently residing in Cape Town. \\nHer contemplative aesthetic draws deeply from within the realms of womanhood, melancholy and isolation. \\nWorking with photography, she incorporates found still lifes, collage and embroidery into her practise. \\nShe has been recognised as an Artist to Follow by Latitudes, and was long-listed in the photography and printmaking category of the Woman United Art Prize 2022. \\n \\nMaroula is mentored by Through the Lens Collective and has participated in group exhibitions in the UK, South Africa, and online."}]}]}

item.title: Marsi van de Heuvel
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641804681437 Marsi van de Heuvel gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640807256285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013928591581","gid://shopify/Product/9133226000605"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Marsi van de Heuvel is a Cape Town-based artist. \\nHer current work deals with visibly, using paint to explore the act of fading as part of the artist’s broader interest in what it means to belong to a place, to a family and to a particular culture. \\nThe artist deals with this erasure through family photographs that record their experiences before forced removals in Upington and Graaff Reinet during this period in South Africa’s history: I use the mediation of these photographs to bridge past to present, to feel out what resonates, what I connect with, what’s worth keeping and to preserve what needs to be re-imagined, reframed, restored, and repaired – van de Heuvel"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013928591581 gid://shopify/Product/9133226000605
