item.title: Martina Gruber
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641806188765 Martina Gruber 1665 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640807518429 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013353185501"] [10780] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Austria, b. 1968 \\n \\nIn the tradition of American writer Joan Didion, Gruber photographs solely to find out what she is thinking, what she is looking at, what she is seeing and what that means. Gruber is a photographer, social anthropologist, a wanderer, a gatherer of inspiration from journeys. As an artist Martina explores the medium of still and moving images, printmaking and is drawn to the seemingly unremarkable, peoples' stories, reflections and the wide view. Her works are observations of her changing surroundings in the social landscapes and tell narratives around the beauty and challenges of everyday life. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013353185501

item.title: Martina Jjunju
item.description: Martina Jjunju 2585 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640807649501 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013982068957"] Martina Jjunju [21053] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Martin Jjunju was born in 1979 in Masak, Uganda. He is a painter and sculptor whose artistic journey is deeply rooted in the vibrant cultural tapestry of his hometown, Masaka. His work reflects an introspection into the parallels between his childhood experiences and those of his children, exploring themes of memory, growth, and the passage of time. Jjunju’s practice is characterized by a bold and dynamic use of color and texture. With a keen eye for detail, he employs a rich and layered color palette, using thick, expressive hues to evoke the emotional depth of his memories. His artworks vividly capture the essence of his experiences, creating a visual dialogue between past and present. He offers a poignant commentary on the evolution of familial and societal dynamics in the contemporary world. His work delves into the cyclical nature of time, exploring how personal histories shape and are reshaped across generations. It is a reflective exploration of how memories, both joyous and challenging, influence our understanding of ourselves and our relationships with others. Martin Jjunju invites viewers to engage with the intimate connections between past and present, offering a window into how our experiences shape our identities and communities."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013982068957

item.title: Martie Bitzer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641805730013 Martie Bitzer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640807485661 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Martie Bitzer (1968) born in Soth Africa, is an architect and artist. She obtained an M.Arch Degree in Architecture in 1998 from the University of the Free State. She has 28 years' experience as lecturer at different tertiary institutions in the Free State as well as Gauteng. \\nMartie is currently enrolled for a PhD by Design at the Department of Architecture, UFS, and works interdisciplinary on the theme Ecdysis: Shedding Skin as Performative Agent in Negotiating New Transitions for Architecture. Her work investigates new applications for ‘skin’ [walls also seen as the ‘skin’ of buildings] and she shows ecdysis as the driving force when dealing with the transient and stratified nature of the skin metaphor in architecture and art. These temporal and layered qualities together with the ‘surface-ness’ of the architectural skin appeal to the concept of shedding and renewal which she also explores through photography and digital drawing. \\nExperimental work is found in activities at the ‘edge’, and in her search towards new edge conditions she explores fragments of skin as found in several shedding phenomenon: roadside waste, decay and integumentary evidence [feathers, skin, nails and containers]. She has been a finalist in the Phatshoane Henney Attorneys New Breed Art Competition in 2016 as well as in 2018 at Oliewenhuis Art Museum and has taken part in several exhibitions through the years. \\nMartie is currently a Senior Lecturer in Architecture at the University of the Free State. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Mary Holland
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641807401181 Mary Holland gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640808501469 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mary Holland graduated with a BA Fine Arts Degree from the University of the Witwatersrand in 1993 (with Distinction) She exhibited on various group exhibitions like Taking Stock, at the Old Stock Trading floor doing a performance art piece with Brian Webber, under the auspices of the French Institute, at the time of the 2nd Johannesburg Biennale curated by Marco Cianfinelli, Andrea Burgener and Luan Nel. She has exhibited in mainly in the United Kingdom, where she lived for eight years and in South Africa, after she returned to the country. She has held multiple solo exhibitions, mainly through Dawid Ras Gallery in Sandton, South Africa. She was given a posthumous exhibition of her last body of work (Highveld winter landscapes) at Nel Gallery in Cape Town in 2020."}]}]}

item.title: Mary Sibande
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641807728861 Mary Sibande gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640808829149 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013943795933","gid://shopify/Product/9013991276765","gid://shopify/Product/9013991309533","gid://shopify/Product/9013991342301","gid://shopify/Product/9013991440605","gid://shopify/Product/9013991473373","gid://shopify/Product/9013991571677","gid://shopify/Product/9014016737501","gid://shopify/Product/9014052389085","gid://shopify/Product/9014067822813","gid://shopify/Product/9014067855581","gid://shopify/Product/9014067921117","gid://shopify/Product/9014088433885","gid://shopify/Product/9014115369181"] Mary Sibande, a South African sculptor and visual artist, explores identity and the black female body through her alter-ego, Sophie. Her innovative work blends sculpture, photography, and installation, and has earned her numerous awards, including the Smithsonian African Artist Award. Sibande's art is exhibited globally, reflecting post-colonial and post-apartheid themes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mary Sibande (b. 1982, Barberton, South Africa) is a multidisciplinary artist renowned for her compelling explorations of identity, the black female body, and the socio-political landscape of post-colonial and post apartheid South Africa. She received her Diploma in Fine Arts from the Witwaterand Technical College and her Honours degree from the University of Johannesburg in 2007. \\nSibande's practice combines sculpture, photography, and installation, often centered around her alter-ego, Sophie. This sculptural figure, modeled after herself and inspired by the women in her family, serves as a powerful symbol of femininity, labour, and the intersection of personal and collective histories. Sophie's attire, blending domestic worker uniforms with extravagant Victorian dress, subverts traditional power structures and challenges historical narratives. \\nHer work addresses sensitive topics such as gender-based violence, ensuring dignity and respect for the women she represents. Sibande's art has evolved through phases marked by distinct colors—Blue, Purple, and currently Red—each reflecting a shift in focus and narrative depth. \\nSibande's notable achievements include the Helgaard Steyn Prize for Sculpture (2021), the Smithsonian African Artist Award (2017), and the Standard Bank Young Artist Award for Visual Arts (2013). She has exhibited widely, including at the 54th Venice Biennale (2011), the 12th Biennale of Contemporary Art in Lyon (2013), and recent solo shows such as \"Unhand Me, Demon!\" at Kavi Gupta Gallery in Chicago (2021) and \"The Red Ventriloquist\" at Musée d’art Contemporain de Lyon (2022). \\nAs co-founder of Occupying the Gallery, Sibande transforms gallery spaces into open studios for mentorship and artistic development. Her work continues to evolve, now focusing on future-oriented themes and the transformative power of imagination and storytelling. \\nSibande resides in Johannesburg, where she remains deeply connected to the society and culture that inspire her art."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013943795933 gid://shopify/Product/9013991276765 gid://shopify/Product/9013991309533 gid://shopify/Product/9013991342301 gid://shopify/Product/9013991440605 gid://shopify/Product/9013991473373 gid://shopify/Product/9013991571677 gid://shopify/Product/9014016737501 gid://shopify/Product/9014052389085 gid://shopify/Product/9014067822813 gid://shopify/Product/9014067855581 gid://shopify/Product/9014067921117 gid://shopify/Product/9014088433885 gid://shopify/Product/9014115369181

item.title: Mashir Kresenshun
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641808679133 Mashir Kresenshun 1237 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640809976029 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014058811613","gid://shopify/Product/9014092103901"] Discover the art of Mashir Kresenshun, a South African artist based in Johannesburg. His work explores human identity through cardboard, combining drawing, painting, printmaking, and sculpture. [23796,24502,24504,24501] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mashir Kresenshun (b. 1999, South Africa) is a dynamic and evolving artist based in Johannesburg. From a young age, he developed a deep connection with creativity, and upon graduating high school, he made a conscious decision to pursue a career that combined both passion and purpose. His artistic journey led him to explore various mediums, ultimately finding a distinctive voice in the world of visual arts. \\n \\nKresenshun works across multiple discipline, with a particular focus on drawing, printmaking, and sculpture. Central to his practice is the use of cardboard, which he has chosen not only as a medium but also a metaphor. Through this, Kresenshun questions the essence of humanity, exploring ideas of fragility, impermanence, and identity. The cardboard itself—an often discarded material—becomes a powerful tool for reflection on the value and significance of life, challenging the traditional understanding of what makes us human. \\nHis approach to printmaking on cardboard sets him apart. This innovative method allows him to create unique textures and surfaces, while his sculptural additions add a dimensional quality to the works, inviting viewers to engage with the art on multiple levels. The layered use of materials and techniques within his practice reflects his ongoing exploration of the boundaries between two-dimensional and three-dimensional art. \\nKresenshun's formal education began at the University of Johannesburg, where he hone his skills and deepened his understanding of art theory and practice. He is currently studying at Artist Proof Studios, further refining his techniques. His artistic endeavors are centered at his studio in August House. \\nKresenshun's work has earned him significant recognition. In 2019, he was selected as one of the Top 20 artists in Thami Mnyele and was also named among the Top 100 artists in Sasol New Signatures. Looking ahead, Kresenshun is preparing for a highly anticipated exhibition in London later this year. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014058811613 gid://shopify/Product/9014092103901

item.title: Mashudu Nevhutalu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641809465565 Mashudu Nevhutalu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640810238173 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mashudu Nevhutalu was born in Auckland Park, Johannesburg in 1992. Although he did not receive much art training at a primary or high school level, he has always had a keen interest in art. Mashudu’s first artistic influence was the graffiti and street murals he saw that decorated dilapidated buildings, almost bringing them to life with their colours. This love for graffiti urged Mashudu to pursue art at a tertiary level where he received an Honours in Fine and Applied Arts in 2014 at the Tshwane University of Technology. As an artist that year, Mashudu felt as if his foot was in the door and that he had found his voice as he was selected to participate in the Sasol New Signatures Competition. As his work developed each year, he went on to take part in a number of small group shows and other competitions such as the SA Taxi Foundation Art Award in which he participated in both 2016 and 2017. \\n \\nMashudu seeks to bring about feelings of nostalgia in the viewer looking at his work. He believes these feelings occur from anything such as a dress worn by one’s mother, or a bumper sticker that reminds one of their parents', or their own, first car. Mashudu is interested in photography and works from old family photographs in his paintings. Though these images are personal to him, he believes that we have all had similar experiences and moments captured in photographs. In his works, Mashudu’s figures are simplified and often made to look hazy and blurry, this depiction emphasizes the notion of memory being a vague and elusive thing. This effect also removes the identity of the person from the original photograph, making the work universal and the figure representative of anyone the viewer wishes them to be from their own memories. Mashudu’s use of bright, vivid colours is his way of reliving those memories and creating them anew."}]}]}

item.title: Masonwabe Ntloko
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641810415837 Masonwabe Ntloko 2622 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640810598621 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014056976605", "gid://shopify/Product/9014057107677", "gid://shopify/Product/9133228163293", "gid://shopify/Product/9133230489821"] [21568,21567,21565,25688,21564,25690,23745,24190,24192,24193,24195,25691,21566,25689,21563,23746] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Masonwabe Ntloko (b. 1996) is a South African visual artist, illustrator, and textile design graduate known for his modern heritage style that blends cultural richness with contemporary expression. Originally from Engwane, a village that greatly influences his work, Masonwabe grew up in a small town of Dutywa. His art is deeply rooted in Xhosa culture, South African heritage, and personal experiences, which he intricately weaves into his visual narratives. Ntloko's art serves as a storyteller, offering a bridge between past traditions and modern life, with particular focus on the everyday experiences of ordinary Black people. \\n \\nHis work is characterized by its simplicity and cultural influence, often exploring themes of spirituality, rites of passage, and the role of matriarchs within the Xhosa community. Through these stories, Masonwabe celebrates not just the Xhosa people but the diversity of South African culture as a whole. His pieces, which include illustration, painting, textile, and rug design, have been featured in museums and exhibitions across South Africa, allowing him to showcase his unique interpretation of South African heritage."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014056976605 gid://shopify/Product/9014057107677 gid://shopify/Product/9133211812061 gid://shopify/Product/9133227835613 gid://shopify/Product/9133228163293 gid://shopify/Product/9133230489821

item.title: Matthew Eguavoen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641810546909 Matthew Eguavoen 2239 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640812826845 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013450997981","gid://shopify/Product/9013451030749","gid://shopify/Product/9013451096285"] [16736,16735] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Matthew Eguavoen (born 1988), is a rising contemporary artist from Edo State, currently living in the city of Lagos, Nigeria. He attended the University of Port Harcourt , where he attained a Bachelors in Engineering for Civil Engineering and Structures. In his final year at the university of Port Harcourt, Matthew decided to pursue his passion for creating art through self-study, where he continued his artistic development. \\n \\nMatthew is a full-time contemporary painter, he depicts his figurative and portrait subjects using a combination of oil paint, acrylic paint, charcoal, and graphite pencils to document stories that encompass the emotions and demeanor of his muse to the viewer of his work. \\n \\nMatthew uses his work to address the societal, economic, and political views across the complex intersectionality that Nigerians face in different facets of life. The constraint of societal ideology about life, on human existence and survival. \\n \\nHis work addresses the impact of Slavery on the Africa and its people, the extinction of African traditional values and the growing sensation of religion in Africa, importation of western moral and cultural values to Africa and exiling Africa’s own cultural values as a people, with Africans abandoning Africa for relative greener pastures in western countries. \\n \\nMatthews works are featured in collections across West Africa, USA, Europe, and North America. \\n \\nArtist statement \\n\"As an artist I am deeply concerned about the impact of my work on my immediate environment and the world at large and that is why themes of my art centers around the societal, political and economic imbalance taking over humanity happiness, swamping over the essence of society. \\n \\nI am fascinated by people’s reaction to their immediate environment, and how it affects their demeanor and in turn affects their reaction to life. That is what I find really interesting. I see people trying to re-write their past, I see violence, I see the effect of corruption and slavery on the lives of nations citizens, I see people trying to find a way to have fun and survive. \\n \\nFrom my work you can notice a strong striking focus from each of my models, this bold unwavering stare is my way of using my works to project identity formation, mental health, gender construct, societies and government’s impact on both the common man and the affluent. I have a need for facial representation and I am fascinated by its power to evoke an emotional response from my viewers. \\n \\nIf you look at my work from a distance, it looks realistic but when you come close you start to notice my brush strokes, the strokes are a representation of the subjects’ experience, and how they are affected by it. \\n \\nI want people to see the good and the bad times I see. I want to make the unseen other-self tangible, to feel a connection to something larger and feel the magic of transformation, in so doing, inviting my viewers to look in. I appreciate mystery in a painting; uncertainty about what you are seeing is desirable for me, why and how the subject(s) has been affected.\""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013450997981 gid://shopify/Product/9013451030749 gid://shopify/Product/9013451096285

Kay studied at the Market Photo Workshop in Johannesburg and is currently completing a fine arts master’s program through the University of the Witwatersrand. \\n \\nHe was the recipient of the Ithuba Arts Trust and the Tierney Fellowship in 2014, during which he was mentored by David Goldblatt. item.title: Matty Monethi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641812381917 Matty Monethi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640813678813 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Matty Monethi (b. 1996) was born in Maseru, Lesotho and grew up in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Monethi completed her Diploma in Fine Art at the Ruth Prowse School of Art in Cape Town in 2016. In 2017 she went on a semester abroad in the United Kingdom where she specialized in Printmaking at the University of Hertfordshire. In 2020 Monethi completed a BA Fine Arts at the Wits School of Arts, University of the Witwatersrand, in Johannesburg, where she is currently based. Monethi uses painting, printmaking and text to explore the personal dimensions of migration and memory. Through the use of family and personal photographic archives she scrutinises her connections with her adopted countries, cultures and close relationships. Monethi has participated in group exhibitions at the Julie Miller Art Institute, Bag Factory Artist Studios, Gallery MOMO, The Joyce Gordon Gallery and Forms Gallery."}]}]}

item.title: Maurice Mbikayi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641813889245 Maurice Mbikayi 1875 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640813875421 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013384052957"] [13550] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maurice Mbikayi interrogates the proliferation of technological commerce in our geopolitical system. Technology’s reliance on mining for resources, for instance, has made African countries and their people vulnerable to resource extraction and low-wage labour abuse. Mbikayi collects remnants of this rapidly developing technology and incorporates them in his work, resulting in sculptures, photographs and performances that link the materials back to their political contexts. \\n \\nMaurice Mbikayi was born in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo in 1974. He graduated with a BA in Graphic Design (Advertising and Visual Communication), from the Academies des Beaux-Arts in Kinshasa. He completed his Master of Fine Arts degree (with distinction) in 2015 at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013384052957

item.title: Maurizio Donzelli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641813922013 Maurizio Donzelli gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640814104797 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Maurizio Donzelli produces drawings, paintings, textiles, sculptures, and installations through which he seeks the meeting point of the real world, our perception of it, and its artistic representations. His approach to making art is rooted in philosophical considerations of the nature of perception, and how visual phenomena such as color, images, and art itself affect the way we see and understand reality. He considers drawing both an intellectual and technical pursuit, and it is central to his practice. Donzelli’s work also features mirrors, which he sees as symbols of the process of perception. With their simultaneous ability to reflect and distort, they also mirror our own variable and inevitably inexact comprehension of the surrounding world. In one series, Donzelli layered sheets of lenticular glass over watercolor drawings; the works appear to shift and distort as viewers pass by them."}]}]}

item.title: Mave Rick
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641813954781 Mave Rick gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640814498013 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mave Rick was born in 2020 to an affluent imagination as an alias and alter ego to a “Real Artist”. The ever enigmatic Mave Rick is a brain child selected from submissions by a covert group of emerging, mid-career and famous, practicing contemporary artists. This Alias, Mave Rick, is an early representative of the newly launched Incognito Art House Project. This experimental artist-run initiative playfully prods at ideas around the commodification of identity, market accessibility, artist sustainability and the effect of market and/or investor expectation on the artist’s creative autonomy. \\n \\nThe purpose of this invented persona is to grant the artist from whence it came complete autonomy in the creative process. Removing the artist’s identity (arguably the fetish of the art world) creates a buffer between artist and marketplace. “Real Artists” are thus offered a reprieve from the responsibility of maintaining a career trajectory and preserving their “brand”. This allows them to be playful and experimental, producing work far removed from their usual repertoire without fear of reproach by the unwritten rules of the system. \\n \\nThe works produced for the Incognito project are sold at a standardised price point, levelling the playing field among artists and offering the public a rare opportunity to affordably own quality, curated, contemporary art. Artists, in turn, can give back generously to art admirers during this challenging time. \\n \\nFor more information and updates about the Incognito Project please follow the yellow brick road to the project profile, under curators, where you can also link through to our social media pages."}]}]}

Her work in print and mixed media moves one to mediation and reflection of one’s inner self, in the same way as Tauzeni herself reflects on her inner world. Speaking unapologetically from a woman’s perspective, she constantly reflects on the mutable relationship between a woman, her potential and her actual in daily life, and through the life cycle. \\n \\n“I feel that women in particular relate the physical with the spiritual and emotional in a uniquely powerful way, being the givers of life and the nurtures of others. The physical strength is integral to the spiritual importance.” With quiet confidence and gentle poetry, Tauzeni asserts the right of the new generation of women in Zimbabwe to claim a place in their society on their own terms. \\n \\nTauzeni represented First Floor Gallery Harare at 1-54 contemporary African art fair in London, 2013 and at Berliner Liste 2013. item.title: Mbaka Wainana Kenyanjui
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641814446301 Mbaka Wainana Kenyanjui gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640819019997 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As a Neurodivergent individual, Mbaka Kenyanjui’s entire life has been an artistic journey -- her mind racing with stories, and eyes framing each shot of her life. Her latest series reflects this. The rich colors seen in the world and the feelings within her they represent. Each scene carries an emotion words can’t quite capture, and each color a piece of nature her eyes can’t move on from. The angles, blurs, and scenery are each deliberate -- a chance to see the world from the view of her heart."}]}]}

item.title: Mbali Nqobile Mdikane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641814479069 Mbali Nqobile Mdikane gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640819151069 [] Mbali Nqobile Mdikane {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mbali Nqobile Mdikane (b. 2001) is a visual artist based in Johannesburg. Hailing from Mthatha/East London in the Eastern Cape, Mdikane has been actively involved in the art world since a young age. Her works concentrate on the development of fantastical characters that seemingly transcend human anatomy. These characters serve the purpose of presenting solutions to human problems and highlight the simplicity of life, diverging from its complexities. embracing afrofuturism/africanism, Mdikane intriguingly explores how black individuals can be perceived. By challenging the conventional depictions of the black body through the use of organic shapes and unconventional approaches to color, materiality, and form, Mdikane aims to shift the narrative surrounding black people and ensure their representation in the forefront of ideas."}]}]}

item.title: Mbali Shabane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641817755869 Mbali Shabane 2393 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640820625629 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013848277213","gid://shopify/Product/9013959688413","gid://shopify/Product/9013959786717"] [20629,18879,20630] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mbali, Mbalenhle Shabane, is a 34-year-old multifaceted South African artist and emerging curator Based in Durban. Her work is the observation and the aim to reflect the female; journey, transmutation, experience and the relationship it has with itself. Touching on concepts of spirituality, identity, physical, psychological and emotional trauma, displacement and healing. \\n \\nMbali completed her N.D in Fine Arts at the Durban University of Technology in 2012, majoring in sculpture and printmaking. After featuring in the 2013 Sasol New Signatures, she primarily participated in group exhibitions and in 2017 ventured to the administrative and curatorial side of the arts thereafter launched her first independent curatorial project in 2019, Change Room, which is a collaborative visual arts conversation through an interactive discourse aimed at bringing womxn together through an engagement of shared experiences. \\n \\nMost recently her work is part of the Durban: A Curatorial Journey (2024) exhibition at The Pencil Club, Durban."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013848277213 gid://shopify/Product/9013959688413 gid://shopify/Product/9013959786717

item.title: Mbali Tshabalala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641818607837 Mbali Tshabalala 523 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640820920541 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013372027101","gid://shopify/Product/9013372092637","gid://shopify/Product/9013403091165","gid://shopify/Product/9013436940509","gid://shopify/Product/9013438513373","gid://shopify/Product/9013850374365","gid://shopify/Product/9014034661597","gid://shopify/Product/9014034759901","gid://shopify/Product/9014034890973","gid://shopify/Product/9014035022045"] [14407,23012,23015,23018,23020,23939,14415,12591,18953,12592,16082,16144] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mbali Tshabalala is a South African multidisciplinary artist, curator, and creative entrepreneur. She was born in East London, in the Eastern Cape. She holds a Bachelor's Degree in Fine and Applied Arts from Tshwane University of Technology. Tshabalala honed her skills with studies in printmaking at the Artist Proof Studio, complementing her background in Graphic Design and Darkroom photography. \\nHer artistic journey began in 2019, transitioning from a career in curatorial and art administration spanning over seven years. This background enriches her artwork, often described as embracing a \"curator as artist\" approach. \\nPrior to focusing entirely on her art, Tshabalala held prominent roles including assistant curator at the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (Zeitz MOCAA). Her curatorial credits include leading initiatives like The Joburg Fringe under the Young Capital banner. Driven by an entrepreneurial spirit, Tshabalala founded Collective UNTITLD and Anecdotes Gallery, contributing to South Africa's art scene. Her talent has garnered recognition, with features in prestigious collections such as Rand Merchants Bank, JP Morgan Chase, William Humphreys Gallery, Art Bank South Africa, and Spier Art Trust. Her work has also been showcased at esteemed institutions like Pretoria Art Association, Constitution Hill, Johannesburg Art Gallery, and prominent auction houses including Strauss & Co. and Aspire Art Auction. \\nTshabalala's practice encompasses collage, painting, printmaking, drawing, and photography, exploring the intersectionality of black women's experiences. Mbali's work challenges dominant narratives around mental health, femininity, and African spirituality. \\nCentral to her artistic expression is her own identity, particularly within the context of a post-colonial African city. I critique the collision between indigenous culture and a Eurocentric urban landscape, highlighting the neglect and its impact on mental health. Tshabalala's artwork intertwines ancient African knowledge systems with contemporary lived experiences through storytelling that reflects this cultural collision and its consequences."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013372027101 gid://shopify/Product/9013372092637 gid://shopify/Product/9013403091165 gid://shopify/Product/9013436940509 gid://shopify/Product/9013438513373 gid://shopify/Product/9013850374365 gid://shopify/Product/9014034661597 gid://shopify/Product/9014034759901 gid://shopify/Product/9014034890973 gid://shopify/Product/9014035022045

item.title: Mbongeni Mhlongo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641819951325 Mbongeni Mhlongo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640821280989 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naphtal Mbongeni Mhlongo was born and bred in Durban, and now lives and works in Johannesburg. He started practising art at an informal art school where he first learned how to paint. He enrolled for a full course in art and design shortly after. His subject matter is diverse, ranging from people to buildings. His body of work depicts recognisable shapes blended with abstract elements. Most of these are complex compositions with distinct elements of colour. \\n \\nHe believes in the existence of the unknown and the unseen. Which is the reason why he works from abstract (unknown) to realism (recognizable. He starts his painting with elements and shapes from his imagination and develops them into recognizable objects. Through that process, he manages to keep his work purely original with minimal references, if any, which he usually uses for the final finishing touches. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Médéric Turay
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848525021 Médéric Turay gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640896155869 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013341290717","gid://shopify/Product/9013439496413","gid://shopify/Product/9013439529181","gid://shopify/Product/9013439594717","gid://shopify/Product/9013439627485","gid://shopify/Product/9013439660253","gid://shopify/Product/9013439758557","gid://shopify/Product/9013444968669","gid://shopify/Product/9013456535773"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Visionary, thoughtful as much as intuitive, Mederic Turay uses his talents to participate in raising awareness by telling the most beautiful as well as the hardest stories. This multidisciplinary storyteller lives his art as a privilege and uses a plurality of techniques to create entities, sometimes figurative, sometimes abstract, which become the protagonists of his graphic stories. \\n \\nHis style and the themes he deals with reflect his cosmopolitan life journey and his West African origins. Descendent of a royal family of the Akan people in present-day Côte d'Ivoire, Mederic only got to know his country of origin as a teenager when he returned from the United States where he grew up. \\n \\nHis cultural mix which explains his constant quest for balance in duality, influences the way he builds his works. Trained in Fine Arts, he easily got rid of stylistic constraints by drawing from the material and the process which \\nallow him to best express his point. This is how he combines his talent for music and writing with his passion for painting and sculpture, multiplying albums and first artistic prizes. \\n \\nThe maturity and humility he acquired through travel and meetings with other recognized artists of his generation and the previous one allowed him to focus on the visual arts and to assert his unique style. \\n \\nExcerpt from Melrose Gallery"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013341290717 gid://shopify/Product/9013439496413 gid://shopify/Product/9013439529181 gid://shopify/Product/9013439594717 gid://shopify/Product/9013439627485 gid://shopify/Product/9013439660253 gid://shopify/Product/9013439758557 gid://shopify/Product/9013444968669 gid://shopify/Product/9013456535773

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641820475613 Megan Gabrielle Harris 2086 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640825180381 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013423800541", "gid://shopify/Product/9013423833309", "gid://shopify/Product/9013423898845", "gid://shopify/Product/9013424357597", "gid://shopify/Product/9013424455901", "gid://shopify/Product/9014000779485", "gid://shopify/Product/9014000845021", "gid://shopify/Product/9014000910557"] [15410,15452,15451,21614,14541,15403,21616,21618,15405] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Megan Gabrielle Harris is a multi-disciplinary artist from Sacramento, California. \\n \\nHer work is mostly comprised of drawings, paintings and photography. M.G.H.’s desire to paint began at an early age, ignited by her father Thomas Harris whose paintings covered every wall in their home and continues to be heavily influenced by her father’s work and his Escapism style. \\n \\nThe inspiration for her work comes from fashion photography, surreal landscapes and natural forms, stemming from her experiences working as a model for over ten years. Women of color are the primary focus in her work. She uses vibrant and rich color palettes in an attempt to create a light and airy atmosphere for her subjects, while depicting these female figures as independent and powerful which is the perception she has of the women in her community. \\n \\nM.G.H.’s goal as an artist is to create dreamy and sublime escapes, not only as a form of self-therapy but also to inspire anyone who views her artwork. \\n \\nShe received her B.A. in Art History from California State University, Sacramento in 2014 and is currently based in New York City."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013404303581 gid://shopify/Product/9013423800541 gid://shopify/Product/9013423833309 gid://shopify/Product/9013423898845 gid://shopify/Product/9013424357597 gid://shopify/Product/9013424455901 gid://shopify/Product/9014000779485 gid://shopify/Product/9014000845021 gid://shopify/Product/9014000910557

item.title: Mel Madiba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822605533 Mel Madiba 1926 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640829571293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014001041629","gid://shopify/Product/9014001074397","gid://shopify/Product/9014001107165"] [21623,21624] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phenyo Melody Madiba, better known as 'Mel Madiba', born in October 1993, in Mafikeng and grew up in Pretoria. She now lives and works intermittently between Pretoria and Johannesburg. When she finished High School, having taken Design as a subject, she went to study Interior Design at The Design School of Southern Africa. It was there where she fell in love with wood and discovered pyrography, which is the art of drawing on wood, leather, or other materials using a soldering iron. It is through this art form that she began creating works that seek to explore various aspects of who she is. \\nMadiba taps into the inner workings of her mind to conceive work that is rooted in femininity, consciousness and the full expression of oneself. She portrays an array of emotions from a black woman's lens. Her chosen subject matter is predominantly black women at different stages of their growth. She envisions a world where black beauty can be fully expressed and appreciated without the need for it to be substantiated. The artist uses expressive markings by fire, gold, and African bronze blue to illustrate that black women are naturally divine. Her career officially launched in 2019 after being dubbed a Design Indaba Emerging Creative, appearing on the TV show Hashtags Africa, and winning the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize. Madiba's work has evolved through personal experiences and she strives to improve her craft even further."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014001041629 gid://shopify/Product/9014001074397 gid://shopify/Product/9014001107165

item.title: Megan Shipman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641820639453 Megan Shipman gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640827277533 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here’s the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang. In 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University which has always had a strong history of printmaking. During a class reunion exhibition in 2016 they inspired each other to create in print again and began to exhibit as The Printing Girls. The following year they decided to invite new female printmakers to join up, and TPG in its current incarnation began to materialise. But the main focus has never changed - to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network and exhibit together."}]}]}

item.title: Melinda Matyas
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641820934365 Melinda Matyas 577 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640831307997 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013284438237","gid://shopify/Product/9013284503773","gid://shopify/Product/9013284536541"] Melinda Matyas is a London-based artist whose figurative paintings explore the complexities of the human condition, psychological aspiration, and societal pressures. Her work blends abstraction and figuration to create dynamic compositions that delve into the internal world. [3243,3244,3242] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Melinda Matyas is a London-based artist originally from Romania, was born as an ethnic Hungarian in 1976 during the communist regime. Her formative years were shaped by witnessing the violent uprising that led to the fall of the regime. The mass transition from silent acceptance to a powerful desire for freedom intrigued her deeply. This experience ignited her interest in psychological mechanisms driving human aspirations, a theme that continues to influence her artistic practice. \\nIn 2009, she graduated from the University of Art and Design in Cluj-Napoca with a BA in Fine Art, Painting, before relocating to England in 2013. Her work centers on the human condition, focusing on the internal world one navigates within the context of societal expectations. She explores the tension between individual desires and the pressures of society, using color, texture, and the deconstruction of forms to achieve a balance between figuration and abstraction. Although Melinda considers herself a figurative painter, her innovative use of dynamic form-breaking often results in works that can appear abstract upon closer inspection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013284438237 gid://shopify/Product/9013284503773 gid://shopify/Product/9013284536541

Despite his international success, he remains humble and unassuming. \\nMéné's art is characterized by its focus on human beings, both individually and in groups, often accompanied by elements like a red animal, a beast with horns, the sun, or a hut. His work examines human nature in all its facets, presented in deceptively simple, child-like silhouettes that convey both the freshness of youth and the depth of adult experience. His subjects often smile or show subtle emotions, depicted affectionately in pairs or groups, highlighting the effervescence of youth and the pursuit of life's meaning."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013426421981 gid://shopify/Product/9013426487517 gid://shopify/Product/9013426520285 gid://shopify/Product/9013426553053 gid://shopify/Product/9013426684125 gid://shopify/Product/9013452701917 gid://shopify/Product/9013452734685 gid://shopify/Product/9013452832989 gid://shopify/Product/9013452865757 gid://shopify/Product/9013452964061 gid://shopify/Product/9013452996829 gid://shopify/Product/9013453029597 gid://shopify/Product/9013453095133

item.title: Mercy Moyo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822703837 Mercy Moyo 2197 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640831996125 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013435695325","gid://shopify/Product/9013435728093","gid://shopify/Product/9013435793629","gid://shopify/Product/9014043410653","gid://shopify/Product/9014043508957","gid://shopify/Product/9014043541725"] Discover the vibrant and evocative artworks of Mercy Moyo, a Zimbabwean-born visual artist known for her collages and paintings depicting the beauty and realities of African women. Explore her exhibitions in South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and the USA. [16056,23388,23389,23390,16054,16055] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zimbabwean-born visual artist and collagist Mercy Moyo shares, “Art and creativity have always been part of my life. As a child, I would observe my grandmother weaving baskets that were the main source of livelihood for the family. Fascinated by the techniques involved in patterns, designs and her skill of making each basket unique despite similar materials and colors. Through my observation, I realized that the more she made, the more creativity emerged from the process.” \\nFrom this experience, Mercy began to draw at a very young age. Her drawings describe the world around her and tell the story of life in contemporary Africa, specifically through women figures. This narrative is prominent in her artistic practice, where her images are primarily collages, incorporating objects that complement and reinforce the depicted images. She uses various mediums, including oil, acrylics, charcoal, pencil, and recently, smoke from candles. These diverse mediums help create vibrant images of contemporary women in Zimbabwe today, expressing their lived realities, aspirations, and dreams. \\nUltimately, Mercy uses art as a fundamental element in depicting the beauty of African women, whether they come from rural or urban contexts. She emphasizes that she does not consider herself a feminist but wants to portray the real African woman—comfortable in her self-identity, wearing long skirts, with a fuller figure, and head nicely covered. \\nMercy has participated in group and solo exhibitions in South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and the United States of America. These experiences have significantly influenced her work through encounters with the lived realities of different societies. For example, the young men working in the mines of South Africa, who live underground and surface only to socialize and sleep at night, inspired her experimentation with male figures. She captures the lives of these miners using charcoals and working in hues of black and brown, reflecting the loneliness and individualism associated with their daily lives, unlike most of her works, which depict people in community dialogues and deep conversations."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013435695325 gid://shopify/Product/9013435728093 gid://shopify/Product/9013435793629 gid://shopify/Product/9014043410653 gid://shopify/Product/9014043508957 gid://shopify/Product/9014043541725

Their work exists across various mediums; literary, audio-visual, theatrical and visual. Mercy has had minimal formal training for their creative explorations, however being an artist has been an organic part of their life since early childhood. They learned the rigor of rehearsal and performing by participating in plays, poetry, and song performances at church from as young as age 3. Mercy’s distinctly vibrant depictions of intimacy between Black, gender and sexually self-determined peoples have been featured and exhibited across an array of platforms, including the Paris Review and Superrare’s Black*Rare showcase (curated by Linda Dounia Rebeiz)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013459386589 gid://shopify/Product/9013459452125 gid://shopify/Product/9133222691037 gid://shopify/Product/9133223149789 gid://shopify/Product/9133223543005

item.title: Meriel May
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822802141 Meriel May gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640832389341 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Meriel May is a professional artist based in Gauteng, South Africa. \\n \\nMeriel works in a multitude of mediums. After many years of working in water colour, she has now moved into pen-and-wash and more recently into oils. An accomplished artist, she sells her work at annual exhibitions, to interior decorators and by private commission. \\n \\nA dedicated artist, Meriel began her art career as a textile designer working with Cyril Lord. It is worth noting that Meriel is a master craftsman in the ceramics field, originally tutored by Digby Hoets. Her design experience and her craftsman like approach to mastering the various techniques she enjoys are clearly evident in her works. She has also drawn her inspiration from the likes of Klimt, Whistler, Walter Battiss and Judith Mason. \\n \\nMeriel bases her approach to her art on premise that “you don’t have to be different to be good, but you do have to be good to be different”-anon."}]}]}

item.title: Mfundo Mthiyane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823031517 Mfundo Mthiyane 1297 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640833667293 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013332967645","gid://shopify/Product/9013333033181"] [9067,9068] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"B. 1991, Durban, lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\n \\nAfter graduating with a Diploma in Multimedia Studies at the Centre for Fine Art, Ani- mation and Design College, Mthiyane earned his stripes in design at a number of studios and advertising agencies in Johannesburg. \\n \\nHis love for paintings saw Mthiyane pursue an artistic practice that is founded on explor- ing and critiquing social and spiritual norms through figurativism and portraiture. Mthi- yane’s most recent body of work titled “In search of the miraculous” (inspired by Russian philosopher P.D Ouspensky, allegories, metaphors and mythologies to name a few) ex- plores miracles as an extension of God. This body of work explores the use of doves that denote peace, love and harmonious energy that surrounds and guards us throughout our existence. Throughout his work, Mthiyane probes self-awareness and the idea of reality. \\n \\nMthiyane has participated in a number of group exhibitions including “Emerge” at The Station House DSTP in Florida, USA and the “Portrait Show” at Everard Read in Johan- nesburg. Mthiyane was awarded the SAFFCA Artist of The Month in September 2020, which resulted in a two man exhibition titled “In Search” alongside emerging artist Lindo Zwane, Mfundo is currently featured in a group show titled In Your Shadow – Masking Realities at SMAC gallery in Cape Town. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013332967645 gid://shopify/Product/9013333033181

item.title: Mfundo Mbali Joseph
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641822965981 Mfundo Mbali Joseph 2285 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640833503453 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013465022685"] [17406] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I create art to express myself, about how i see life during my everyday life of people come across within my community, \\n \\nComing from a poverty stricken background my work depict everyday scenes from my Surroundings, I paint traditional scenes, I sometimes ask people to pose for me to Create scene. \\n \\nI had a second love and is photography in the day I hunts the streets for intresting composition and reference materials,that I then takes home to my Studio space to portray in a realism style using oil medium on canvas, \\n \\n\"Where there is Community the is art Where there is Community the is a Story\""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013465022685

item.title: Mia Chaplin
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823097053 Mia Chaplin 920 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640833896669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013346500829","gid://shopify/Product/9013346533597","gid://shopify/Product/9013433434333","gid://shopify/Product/9013433499869","gid://shopify/Product/9013433532637","gid://shopify/Product/9013433598173","gid://shopify/Product/9013433696477"] [16006,16008,9990,16009,16011,16010,9988] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mia Chaplin (b.1990 South Africa) is a painter who lives and works in Cape Town. Working in oil on canvas and paper, her highly expressive works are characterised by their rich impasto surfaces and visible brushstrokes. Chaplin’s most recent works emphasize a muted colour palette of pink fleshy tones and golden highlights. Consisting of still lifes, figure studies and landscapes, her work seems to meditate on the familiar. Her loose, erratic style of painting – synonymous with that of the impressionists – is intuitive, heightening the emotionality of her pieces. They communicate a sense of estrangement; reflecting a detachment between the self and her surroundings. Her works sway between voyeurism and intimate interaction, while remaining consistently self-referential. \\n \\nSince completing her BFA at the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town in 2011, Chaplin has hosted four solo exhibitions, Mouth (2018), Under a Boiling River (2017) and Binding Forms (2016), with WHATIFTHEWORLD and most recently, Underbelly (2019), with No Man’s Art Gallery in Amsterdam. She has furthermore extended her painting practice into printmaking, hosting a mini-exhibition of monotypes from the series, The Making of a Sharp Blade (2017), in collaboration with Warren Editions, Cape Town. Chaplin has completed artist residency programmes at Cité Internationale Des Artes in the Marais district, Paris (2018), Nirox Arts Foundation in Johannesburg, South Africa (2016) and at OBRAS Foundation in Alentejo, Portugal (2015). \\n \\nSELECTED SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n2019\\tUnderbelly, No Man's Art Gallery, Amsterdam \\n2018\\tMouth - WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town \\n2017\\tUnder a Boiling River - WHATIFTHEWORLD, Johannesburg \\n2016\\tBinding Forms - WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town \\n2014\\tMia Chaplin: Ceremony, Salon 91, Cape Town \\n2011\\tMia Chaplin: No Place, Michaelis School of Fine Art, Cape Town \\n \\nSELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n \\n2020\\tMatereality, Iziko National Gallery, Cape Town \\nProxies, Gallery, Gallery, Johannesburg \\n2019\\tMeasures of Poetry, GoGo Collective, Bogardenkapel Brugge, Belgium \\nOutside, RBK Contemporary \\n2018\\tShowroom, Galerie extérieure at Cité internationale des arts, Paris \\nA letter to my 22 year-old self, BKHZ, Johannesburg \\n2017\\tNano, Barnard Gallery, Cape Town \\nThe Making of a Sharp Blade, Warren Editions, Cape Town \\nYou Leave Me with This?, No End Contemporary, Johannesburg \\nCape Town Art Fair, Cape Town International Convention Centre, Cape Town \\nLady Garden, Cavalli Wine Estate, Cape Town \\n2016\\tNo Man’s Art Gallery, Tehran \\nNo Man’s Art Gallery, Shanghai \\nSouth African Art Exhibition, Galerie Pat ries van Dorst, Netherlands \\nCape Flower Show, The Castle, Cape Town \\nFor What its Worth, No End Contemporary, Johannesburg \\nFUGLY, Die Voorkamer, Cape Town \\nSewing Paradise: a Sisterhood through Suzani, Irma Stern Museum, Cape Town \\nNano, Barnard Gallery, Cape Town \\n2015\\tWet Paint, Die Voorkamer, Cape Town \\nCape Town Art Fair, The Avenue, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town \\nThat Art Fair , The Palms, Cape Town \\nNew Voices 01 - WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town \\nSurface: Emerging South African Painters, Barnard Gallery, Cape Town \\nOut of Context, UJ Art Gallery, Johannesburg \\nPink, Chandler House, Cape Town \\nPaint it Black, Salon91, Cape Town \\n2014\\tCape Town Art Fair, The Pavillion, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town \\nCubicle, Infecting the City Public Arts Festival, Cape Town \\nTurbine Art Fair, Johannesburg \\nArt in Red Light #10, Art Fair, Amsterdam \\nSA Art Now, No Man’s Art Gallery, Amsterdam \\nFlorabunda, Die Voorkamer, Cape Town \\n2013\\tCape Town Art Fair, The Look Out, V&A Waterfront, Cape Town \\nIn Good Company, Irma Stern Museum, Cape Town \\nCollections and Archives, Salon 91, Cape Town \\nOne in a Million, Salon 91, Cape Town \\nI’d Rather Be Swimming, Salon 91, Cape Town \\n2012\\tImpression: Sunset, Salon 91, Cape Town \\n2010\\tFirst Edition, These Four Walls Gallery, Cape Town"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013346500829 gid://shopify/Product/9013346533597 gid://shopify/Product/9013433434333 gid://shopify/Product/9013433499869 gid://shopify/Product/9013433532637 gid://shopify/Product/9013433598173 gid://shopify/Product/9013433696477

item.title: Michael Amery
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823621341 Michael Amery 1482 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640834814173 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013333557469","gid://shopify/Product/9013333623005"] [9079] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Cape Town based artist Michael Amery, showcased his first solo show of drawings, Tress by Man at David Krut Projects Cape Town in 2016. As a freelancer in the advertising industry, he tackles the effect of consumer culture on the natural world via a collection of accomplished drawings in charcoal and India ink. \\nAmery is interested in themes pertaining to how man shapes the land: the spaces that we create, manipulate and destroy. He sees a world where land and resources are divided up into geometric shapes and rows, often with mathematical precision, and no space is left unaccounted for. His drawings mimic the techniques and systems of industry imposed on the natural world. Symmetry, repetition, calculation: the carving up of the landscape. Amery comments that through his work we “glimpse the disquieting commodification of the natural world required to sustain our consumer culture.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013333557469 gid://shopify/Product/9013333623005

item.title: Micha Serraf
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641826373853 Micha Serraf 1893 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640834191581 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013380415709","gid://shopify/Product/9013380481245","gid://shopify/Product/9013380546781","gid://shopify/Product/9013380612317","gid://shopify/Product/9013380645085","gid://shopify/Product/9013380677853","gid://shopify/Product/9013380776157","gid://shopify/Product/9013380808925","gid://shopify/Product/9013401288925","gid://shopify/Product/9013401354461"] [13278,14148,14147,13276,13279,13277,13275,13281,13274] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"b. 1994 in Zimbabwe \\nBAFA from Michaelis School of Fine Art, UCT \\n \\nMy practice is centred around rewriting the trauma of displacement with the imagined memory of celebration, homage and childlike wonder. In pursuit of memory, identity and a place to call home, my work is grounded in a nostalgia of personal and ancestral experience, of what never was, and of what could have been. Caught in an entanglement between ancestral history and utopic optimism. My work is often informed by memories I have from when I was a child in Zimbabwe and my endeavour to understand the deep nostalgia I feel toward the seemingly unfamiliar. To push a more celebratory narrative that is fuelled by the unshakable belief in an abundance, where the often-imposed political narrative takes second seat to that of our lived experience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013380415709 gid://shopify/Product/9013380481245 gid://shopify/Product/9013380546781 gid://shopify/Product/9013380612317 gid://shopify/Product/9013380645085 gid://shopify/Product/9013380677853 gid://shopify/Product/9013380776157 gid://shopify/Product/9013380808925 gid://shopify/Product/9013401288925 gid://shopify/Product/9013401354461

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823686877 Michael Badger 2547 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640835043549 [] [20588,20589,20590] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Badger (b. 1992, Accra, Ghana) is an artist proficient in traditional and digital mediums, crafting surrealistic pieces. Michael’s art delves into the realms of suppressed inner worlds, fears, and dreams, navigating the challenges of growing up and seeking direction in a society marked by increasingly rigid conservative ideals and gender norms. Michael Badger’s works have been exhibited at a group exhibition with Immerse Ghana, Accra (2023), In Relation To Light, Accra (2023), Celebrate Her: A Tribute To Women And Nonbinary Artists, Accra (2023). Michael has had work featured on products from renowned makeup artist Pat Mcgrath (2017-2018) and won a competition for an eco-friendly red carpet dress in collaboration with Vivienne Westwood and Red Carpet Green Dress, worn at the Oscars in 2013. They have a Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Fashion Design from SCAD Atlanta."}]}]}

item.title: Michael Beckurts
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823752413 Michael Beckurts gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640835633373 [] Michael Beckurts {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Beckurts (b.2000) lives and works in Cape Town. Since graduating in 2021 from the Cape Town Creative Academy, he has been a full-time visual artist working in oils, charcoal, watercolour, and digitally. Drawing from memory to create luminous, vivid scenes, Beckurts’ oils on canvas are characterised by rapid mark-making and considered compositions. From family gatherings, to farm road walks, and nights out with friends, central to all these scenes is the connection to nature and connection to people. Ever curious to explore new media, Michael can be seen at evening jazz sessions where he combines his love of music with his observational skills. Here he live-draws in sketches projected onto a wall. \\n \\nBeckurts has had 4 solo exhibitions: Archives held at the Test Kitchen in Woodstock (2021), Portraits of Nature, Portraits of Places at MOK Gallery, Muratie wine estate, Stellenbosch (2022), Remember to Play at Openwine, Wale Street (2023), and Vivacity at the AVA Gallery, Church Street (2024). He participated in the Baz Art International Public Arts Festival in Cape Town in 2019 and 2023 and has also displayed his artworks in several group exhibitions. Beckurts was a participant in the 2023 Sessions Programme for Visual Artists led by Dominique Edwards which culminated in a group exhibition, Pomegranate in Woodstock, Cape Town. \\n \\nIn the words of critic Ashraf Jamal, “Beckurts’ art draws us towards what we long for most – stillness, with all its tremulous \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Michael Gah
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823883485 Michael Gah 1811 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640836059357 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013375926493","gid://shopify/Product/9013375992029","gid://shopify/Product/9013466038493","gid://shopify/Product/9013466136797","gid://shopify/Product/9013466169565","gid://shopify/Product/9014068445405","gid://shopify/Product/9014068478173","gid://shopify/Product/9014068609245"] [17477,17476,24062,24063,24064,17472,12931] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Accra born-and-based, contemporary artist Michael Gah is one of Ghana’s most exciting contemporary portraitists. His medium is equally intriguing – fashioning larger-than-life and hyper coloured figurative works using strips of endemic fabrics, the hugely colourful and patterned textiles that are intertwined with the very heart of womanhood in the modern African context. His pieces are a challenge – to social norms for women in Africa and indeed to contemporary art and figurative work; working with fabric and collaging has long been the realm of crafters and his potent portraits are frank in their delivery. \\n \\nGah cites not only his mother, but all modern African women, as his inspiration – his faceless (though no less personality-laden) subjects defy traditional ‘African expectations’. They are represented as thoroughly modern muses engaged in social and even romantic activities, that answer only to their own whims and certainly not to the stifling belief systems thrust upon them for eons. The poses are provocative in that they are a far cry from the head and shoulders ‘African Woman’ figurative work, so commonplace on the continent in 20th century art. Gah’s work also references social media and the modern day importance of Instagram reality and camera facing messaging. \\n \\nThe power in Gah’s portraits lies in the intentional tension between past and present and a suggestion that eradication of repressive expectations is inevitable and crucial. The use of traditional fabrics insists on the viewer's mindfulness about outdated norms, while still appreciating the gifts and weight of the past. \\n \\nCOUNTRY • GHANA"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013375926493 gid://shopify/Product/9013375992029 gid://shopify/Product/9013466038493 gid://shopify/Product/9013466136797 gid://shopify/Product/9013466169565 gid://shopify/Product/9014068445405 gid://shopify/Product/9014068478173 gid://shopify/Product/9014068609245

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641823850717 Michael Enejison gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640835862749 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Enejison is an artist and an independent curator based in Lagos, Nigeria. \\nAs an artist Michael’s work contemplates the intersection of culture, civilisation and the environment. His recent works focus on orthographies, native scripts and text originating from West Africa as a device to contemplate current realities. \\nMichael was a part of the curatorial team of the inaugural Lagos Biennial and his works have been featured in exhibitions and auctions in Lagos. His project was listed as finalist in the National Art Competition (2015) and the Sterling banks/British Council Recycle Art competition (2017)."}]}]}

item.title: Michael Jackson Blebo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641824047325 Michael Jackson Blebo 1930 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640836681949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013386313949", "gid://shopify/Product/9013386412253", "gid://shopify/Product/9013386641629"] [13599,13600,13601,13598] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Jackson Blebo also known as MJ (b.1993) is a Ghanaian artist who resides and works in Ada-Accra and currently works as an artist (sculptor) and a griot at Nkyinkyim Museum. MJ got his Bachelor in Fine Arts (Sculpture) in 2018 from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Kumasi- Ghana. He has participated in local and international residencies such as Critlab and Rele Arts Foundation Bootcamp in 2020 and 2021 respectively. \\nMJ is fascinated by his environment as he draws inspiration wherever he finds himself from cities, urban centres, villages, markets, lorry stations etc. MJ has also participated in various local and international group exhibitions, including ‘‘Middle grounds’’ curated by MJ at Nuhalenya-Ada. In 2021, his works were featured in the group show ‘‘Young Contemporaries’’ curated by Adéoluwa Olúwajoba, at National Museum in Onikan-Lagos, Nigeria.’ He is also the 2021, Absa L’atelier Ambassador. \\nMJ’s approach to his art practice has been experimental as he makes colours from plants, charcoal, earth and other materials found in his environment, allowing him space to determine the materiality of his practice. He investigates nature, material memory, natural architecture and humankind’s relationship with the environment. Primarily working with drawing, painting, sculpture and installation as a point of entry, his exploration of geological formation and architecture raise important questions on how his artworks are viewed. The elements used in his works are usually welded or constructed together to create installations that reference kinetic sculpture and the aethetics of minimalist abstraction. \\nMJ’s works employ materials such as charcoal, phyto (natural pigment), red ochre, steel and mirrors, while also utilising indigenous working techniques, methodologies and aesthetics which allow him to place his works in direct connection to historical context and tradition. The questions that guide MJ’s practice and process relate to the longevity of the materials used and the display or form of the artwork. This has led MJ to adopt techniques like encaustic and egg tempera which are ancient and contemporary techniques."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013386313949 gid://shopify/Product/9013386412253 gid://shopify/Product/9013386576093 gid://shopify/Product/9013386641629

item.title: Michael MacGarry
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641824145629 Michael MacGarry gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640837697757 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355512029","gid://shopify/Product/9013355577565","gid://shopify/Product/9013355610333","gid://shopify/Product/9013355643101","gid://shopify/Product/9014056124637","gid://shopify/Product/9014056190173","gid://shopify/Product/9014058582237"] Michael MacGarry is a multi-award-winning South African artist and filmmaker whose diverse practice spans sculpture, photography, installation, and film. With exhibitions at Tate Modern, Guggenheim Bilbao, and Kiasma Museum, his work delves into the intersections of politics, identity, and contemporary life. A recipient of the Standard Bank Young Artist Award, MacGarry is known for his exploration of marginalized narratives and the political landscapes of Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael MacGarry is a distinguished South African artist and filmmaker, celebrated for his political and poetic exploration of contemporary life. His work spans a diverse range of media, including sculpture, photography, installation, and film, addressing the complex tensions between marginalized and dominant narratives. MacGarry's art reflect the ever-evolving landscapes of identity, power, and history, particularly in the context of post-colonial Africa. \\n \\nWith a Master's Degree in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand, MacGarry is currently a Ph.D. candidate in the History of Art. MacGarry is a fellow of the Gordon Institute of Performing and Creative Arts (GIPCA) at the University of Cape Town and a recipient of the Standard Bank Young Artist Award 2010. \\n \\n \\nHis extensive body of work has earned him international recognition, with exhibitions at renowned institutions such as Tate Modern, Guggenheim Bilbao, and the Kiasma Museum. His diverse artistic practice has also extended to film, with several award-winning short films that have been featured in over 30 international film festivals. He is a recipient of an El Ray Award - Excellence in Narrative Short Filmmaking (Barcelona Film Festival 2015), a finalist for the Huysmans Young African Filmmaker Award 2015 (Belgium) as well as Jury Awards from 19th VideoBrasil (Sao Paulo), K3 Internationales Film Festival (Austria) and 13th International Festival Signes de Nuit (Paris). \\n \\nSELECTED SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n 2017: Show No Pain, Wits Art Museum, Johannesburg. \\n 2015: There’s an Animal Inside. \\n 2013: As Above, So Below, Centre for Democracy, Cape Town. \\n 2012: The Other Half, Stevenson, Cape Town. \\n 2011: Entertainment, Stevenson, Johannesburg. \\n 2010: END GAME, Standard Bank Young Artist Award 2010 (Visual Arts) Monument Gallery, Grahamstown. \\n 2010: This is your world in which we grow, and we will grow to hate you, Stevenson, Johannesburg. \\n 2008: When enough people start saying the same thing, Art Extra, Johannesburg \\n 2004: Or Until the World Improves, The Premises Gallery, Johannesburg \\n \\n \\nSELECTED GROUP EXHIBITIONS \\n \\n 2017: Utopia/Dystopia, MAAT, Lisbon, Portugal \\n 2015: Bronze, Steel & Stone, Everard Read, Johannesburg \\n 2015: The Film Will Always Be You, TATE Modern, London \\n 2015: FNB Joburg Art Fair \\n 2015: Making Africa. A Continent of Contemporary Design, curated by Okwui Enwezor and Amelie Klein Vitra Design Museum, Weil am Rhein, Germany Guggenheim Bilbao, Spain \\n 2015: Africa: Architecture, Culture, Identity, curated by Mathias Ussing Seeberg Louisiana Museum of Modern Art, Humlebaek, Denmark \\n 2015: The Johannesburg Pavilion, During the 56th la Biennale di Venezia,Venice, Italy \\n 2015: Africa Salon, Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, USA \\n 2014: Half-­Devil Half-­Child, Blank Projects, Cape Town \\n 2014: Pop Goes the Revolution,The New Church, Cape Town \\n 2013: 'MINE' – MC2a – MIGRATIONS CULTURELLES \\n 2013: Aquitaine Afriques, Bordeaux, France \\n 2012: Impakt Festival 2012 \\n 2012: CBKU, Utrecht, The Netherlands \\n 2012: Making Way: Contemporary Art from South Africa and China, Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg \\n 2011: Johannesburg Contested Terrains, Tate Modern, London \\n 2011: ARS 11, Kiasma Museum of Contemporary Art Helsinki, Finland \\n 2010: Ampersand, Damiler Art Collection, Berlin \\n 2010: Life Less Ordinary: Performance and display in South African art, Ffotogallery, Cardiff, U.K. \\n 2009: Life Less Ordinary: Performance and display in South African art, Djanogly Gallery, Nottingham \\n 2009: Why Not?, Kuckei + Kuckei, Berlin, Germany \\n \\nAWARDS: \\n \\nEl Ray Award -­? item.title: Michael Mansfield
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641824407773 Michael Mansfield gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640837501149 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Mansfield was born in the 20th century and will die in the 21st. Born in 1964 Windhoek, Namibia, he worked as a journalist in Windhoek in the 80s and 90s. After a period in Cape Town, the artist returned to Swakopmund in 2000, where he resides till today. The multidisciplinary artist illustrated the Go For English for Gamsberg Macmillan for more years than he cares to remember, and remained consistent to his practice for many years before he had the opportunity to start exhibiting. The artist has mainly exhibited locally, the most notable being at the National gallery of Namibia with a show titled Who Killed Mr Art? Over the last couple of years Mansfield has hosted multiple solo exhibitions in Swakopmund and in Windhoek. The most recent of these was Still Life Stories, hosted at local gallery The Project Room. The artist remains committed to raising eyebrows and shifting perspectives, with his tongue-in-cheek approach for years to come."}]}]}

item.title: Michael Meyersfeld
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641824800989 Michael Meyersfeld gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640838156509 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"In a career stretching over many decades Michael Meyersfeld has garnered many successes, as commercial photographer and as artist. His entire working life has embraced photography in various forms. He has an extensive local and international portfolio of exhibitions and campaigns. The long list of awards he obtained in London and New York is evidence of his aptitude, as is the list of exhibitions since 1975 and his remarkable ability to view the world afresh. As he indicates, “What is important for me in my work is that it is constantly evolving.” \\nMeyersfeld lives and works in Johannesburg and he is currently completing his Master’s degree in History of Art at the University of the Witwatersrand where he explores the role of the Camera Club of Johannesburg in South African histories of photography. \\nHis experimental photographic gallery Backlight continued for five years. This initiative included interactive photographic workshops and discussion groups fostering innovation at the intersections of photography and art. These lively gatherings, mainly attended by young black photographers, provided an opportunity for exposure and networking, supporting and enhancing the work and career development of black artists and thinkers. Special friendships were forged through the showing and discussion of each other’s work and sharing of critical perspectives, technical and professional experience. \\nMeyersfeld’s work has recently shifted to a contemplation of the inherent qualities in objects. Presented as social commentary, it is notable for its stark, sometimes sombre, lonely and edgy imagery that has separateness from reality. The volume of the external world has been turned down in order that both the artist and the viewer can hear and feel the silence. These images could be rendered as abstractions, as less representational, less reliant on meaning and understanding. They are images drawing on texture and dramatic tension more than a linear narrative, pictures more inclined to be felt, to be experienced, than to be understood. \\nHis recent photographs require a different type of eye, not an eye programmed to understand, to fathom or to find a narrative, but one that is alerted to a deeper sense of awareness. With an eye liberated from the dominant quest to find and attach meaning, more faculties, other than just the cognitive, are employed to sense and experience form, shape, texture, play of light, distance and fragmentation, as well as connections and conversations between the photographs. Inner dialogue seems to have taken over the role that commentary was playing in his previous work. \\nMeyersfeld’s recent exhibitions include Discordance (2013 at the University of Johannesburg Gallery), Dark City Dreams (2014 at the Jewish Museum, Cape Town; In Toto, Johannesburg and Puthaditjaba Community Centre, Alexandra), Adaptation (2017 at In Toto, Johannesburg, and in 2018 at Fried Contemporary, Pretoria), and Notional(2019 at the George Henry Gallery, Johannesburg). \\nBooks published by Meyersfeld include Gaze (2003) and Life Staged (2010). \\nLink to website here"}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641825128669 Michael Nyoni 2788 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640838484189 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014062842077"] Michael Nyoni is a talented Zimbabwean artist whose work blends traditional African influences with contemporary artistic expressions. His dynamic creations explore themes of identity, heritage, and the complexities of modern life, offering a deep and introspective look at the cultural landscape of Africa. [23902,23898,23908] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Michael Nyoni is a Zimbabwean-born wood sculpting visual artist currently residing in Knysna, South Africa. His artistic journey is deeply rooted in his profound connection with nature, which inspires him to craft intricate and thought-provoking pieces from various types of wood, including driftwood. \\nNyoni's work is characterized by its organic and earthy essence, reflecting his reverence for the natural world. Through his art, he seeks to convey the beauty, simplicity, and complexity of the African landscape and its inhabitants. \\n \\nWith driftwood as one of his primary mediums, Nyoni breathes new life into discarded fragments, transforming them into stunning sculptures that evoke emotions and spark imagination. His creative process is intuitive and spontaneous, allowing the natural textures and forms of the wood to guide his artistic vision. \\n \\nNyoni's artwork has been influenced by his Zimbabwean heritage, as well as his experiences living in South Africa. His unique blend of traditional and contemporary styles has captivated audiences and collectors alike. \\n \\nThrough his art, Michael Nyoni invites viewers to contemplate their relationship with the natural world and the beauty that can be found in unexpected places."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014062842077
