Her background in Information Sciences has guided her process in photography by the systematic creation and preservation of her own stories. Nadia’s work is an introspective exploration of social issues, personal identity, and domesticity in South Africa. Through her works, she authors and witnesses the individuality and diversity of womanhood. \\nRecently named a CAP (Contemporary African Photography Award) 2023 winner, her work has been exhibited as part of the group exhibition 'Shutterland' by Lizamore and Associates in Johannesburg as well as a collective exhibition, ‘(IM)Materiality’ by Notamuseum in Lisbon. She was featured in a group exhibition ‘Everything, Everyone, Always’ by Through The Lens Collective. She resonates with the complexities of the human experience, reflecting on her own identity and abuse. Nadia continues to work on projects in analogue, digital and printed mediums. item.title: Nadine Mathenjwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848852701 Nadine Mathenjwa 1686 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640902578397 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013983477981","gid://shopify/Product/9013983576285","gid://shopify/Product/9013983674589"] [21080] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nadine Noluthando Mathenjwa is a young woman born and raised in Gauteng South Africa. In 2021 Nadine graduated at Artistproof studio where she practiced printmaking working in different mediums such as Cyanotyp, Screenprint, Linocut and etching. With the help of Artistproof studio. Nadine’s work has been exhibited at Turbine Artfair 2022, Investec Capetown Art Fair 2022, ABSA virtual space in 2021 and her grad show “A version of us” in 2021. Nadine aspires to further her study’s in fashion She currently resides in Johannesburg producing work and entering competitions \\nin the hopes of getting her works seen worldwide. \\n \\n“My body of work focuses on the hybrid cultures that western society introduced my ancestors to, I am a young black woman navigating for an identity in a society where information on native cultures has been washed down, as most young people I find solace in fashion it has become a great part of my evolved culture, my self expression, identity and individuality. As much as my work is about paying homage to the lifestyle that my ancestors and family chose to make out of colonisation my work is also about the subcultures that the millennials and genZ have created, particularly those of fashion and luxury or ghetto fabulous lifestyle. These subcultures have become part of the movement towards changing the narrative about what it is to be young, African and cultured. \\n \\nI often use tribal patterns on the figures which are a representation of the information on ancient African beliefs and history that I unravel through watching documentaries and finding books on African spirituality, with the patterns I aim to shift the demonised notions on African spirituality and rituals.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013983477981 gid://shopify/Product/9013983576285 gid://shopify/Product/9013983674589

item.title: Naki Narh
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641848951005 Naki Narh 1600 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640903954653 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013346599133","gid://shopify/Product/9013346631901"] [10044,10045] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naki Narh (b.1993) is an artist of Ghanaian descent from two homes- Accra and London. Her work currently draws inspiration from a plethora of tropes and concerns which are quintessentially Ghanaian and African countries alike. Specifically, these revolve around explorations of self and identity social and personal conscience as well as social issues affecting her and many other developing countries in over sixty years of what should have been the post-independence honeymoon after British colonialists departed from Ghana’s shores. The abstract works depict the expressions of self and thoughts of responsibility to the country, Ghana. Explored through a symbolic, language, the works present metaphors of chaos and anxiety in images that are essentially transpositions of an individual’s sense of responsibility and culpability in a country that struggles to find stability. These ideas are expressed through the mediums of ink and acrylic on paper, digital painting and canvas - with explosions of colour and patterns as distinctive features that mark a rapidly evolving signature style. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013346599133 gid://shopify/Product/9013346631901

[25214,24225,23603,15172,15181,24230,23604,23752,15177,23601,25261,23753,15175,24226,15173,23602,24228,24229,15174,24227] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naledi Maifala is a Botswana-based contemporary expressionist painter exploring themes of stillness and contentment. Her journey with painting began in 2007 during her junior years, and in 2022, she transitioned into professional art. She has participated in several group exhibitions in Botswana, including Dikgosigadi Exhibition, Women Create Love Exhibition, and Heart Scape in Nigeria, among others. \\n \\nHer work is guided by the theme “Just as Petals Fall, Life Too Fades”—a metaphor for presence, impermanence, and the fleeting nature of life. She focuses on mind-soothing surroundings, painting domestic animals, garden flowers, sentimental objects, and serene individuals. Fascinated by the journey of inner contentment, she believes that external surroundings can also nurture this experience. With her keen photography skills, she captures moments of solitude, later translating them onto canvas with acrylic paints. Her brushstrokes balance intuition and intention, using light, texture, and colour to shape mood and storytelling. Through her work, she hopes to inspire appreciation for life’s simplicity, offering a space of meditation that alleviates the pressures of constant striving. She envisions her art as a sanctuary for spiritual, psychological, and emotional well-being."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013418655965 gid://shopify/Product/9013418688733 gid://shopify/Product/9013418721501 gid://shopify/Product/9013418787037 gid://shopify/Product/9013418819805 gid://shopify/Product/9013418852573 gid://shopify/Product/9014051635421 gid://shopify/Product/9014051668189 gid://shopify/Product/9014051733725 gid://shopify/Product/9014051799261 gid://shopify/Product/9014057402589 gid://shopify/Product/9014057435357 gid://shopify/Product/9014078308573 gid://shopify/Product/9014078341341 gid://shopify/Product/9014078406877 gid://shopify/Product/9014078472413 gid://shopify/Product/9014078537949 gid://shopify/Product/9014078603485 gid://shopify/Product/9014126346461 gid://shopify/Product/9014138306781

item.title: Nandipha Jantjies
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641849147613 Nandipha Jantjies 2130 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640906412253 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013437006045","gid://shopify/Product/9013437038813","gid://shopify/Product/9013438185693","gid://shopify/Product/9014025158877","gid://shopify/Product/9014025191645","gid://shopify/Product/9014025322717","gid://shopify/Product/9014025355485"] [22774,22775,16133,16083,22773,16084] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Artist Nandipha Jantjies (b.1998) is a painter and multi-media digital artist and creator. The prolific artist is also know by the name 'Neferuda' which is a character that inspires and features prominently in her digital artworks. Jantjies was born in Bloemfontein, South Africa and later relocated to Welkom. She currently resides in the Free State where she has set up her artist studio and practice. Nandipha graduated in Studio Art and Design at CUT, South Africa. Her works symbolically traverse space and time, and mediate culture and ancestry in the contemporary. \\n'My work can also involve culture, spirituality, nature and the philosophy of what a soul is. Challenging topics like \"how one should carry themselves in terms of society, or how one's culture/traditions are constantly appropriated\" are one of the things I love putting out there, but mostly I embrace the woman's body. My signature style is inspired from the complexity (overlapping lines) of this beautiful Earth, from the traffic to marching ants to different faces you meet on a daily. All of those are complexities, in all their shades of beauty. \\nThe horns I include in my paintings represent strength, a sense of boldness, royalty and yet I create them in a way that the feeling you get once glancing on them is serene. Horns are protective. I mostly use a Nguni cow, a mountain goat or a buffalo. A bit of my culture is included within the Nguni horns, which is isiXhosa. The baSotho tradition or culture is one that I include too, I tend to play around with \" Nkgo\" an African beer pot, nonetheless my love for animals is important in my practice. My medium is, ink, acrylic paint, wool and beads on a canvas. I've recently started playing around with wool and beads on my artworks'. item.title: Naledi Modupi

As the founder and CEO of King Nandi & Co., she leads a dynamic multimedia production collective specializing in commercial, corporate, and fashion photography. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nandipha Khemese, 33, is a photographer and the creative director and founder of multimedia production company King Nandi & Co. She creates space for others – emerging artists, voices at the margins – to rise, to be seen and to belong. \\nWhether behind the lens or beside a team, Khemese builds bridges between passion and purpose. Her work has reached global platforms, but her heart remains grounded in local soil, nurturing transformation from the inside out. Her journey is not just her own – it is one shared with collaboration, courage and care. Through every frame and every initiative, she carries community forward – one powerful story at a time."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014094823645 gid://shopify/Product/9014094856413

item.title: Nandipha Mntambo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641849442525 Nandipha Mntambo 514 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640907886813 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013436678365","gid://shopify/Product/9013436743901","gid://shopify/Product/9013436776669"] [16076,16075,16077] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nandipha Mntambo was born in Mbabane, Swaziland. In 2007, she completed a Master’s in Fine Art from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. Mntambo currently lives in Johannesburg. Mntambo is best known for her figurative cowhide sculptures which allude to the symbiotic relationship between humans and nature. \\n \\nHer work addresses ongoing debates around traditional gender roles, body politics, and identity. She works in photography, sculpture, video, and mixed media to explore the liminal boundaries between human and animal, femininity and masculinity, attraction and repulsion, life and death. \\n \\nNotable solo exhibitions include Transience at Stevenson (Johannesburg: 2014); Nandipha Mntambo at Andréhn-Schiptjenko (Stockholm, Sweden: 2013) and Faena, a travelling exhibition showcased at the Grahamstown National Arts Festival, the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Art Museum in Port Elizabeth, and at Iziko South African National Gallery in Cape Town (2011). \\n \\nMntambo’s participation in group shows include Regarding Africa: Contemporary Art and Afro-Futurism at Tel Aviv Museum of Art (2017); the 12th Edition of Dak’Art, the African Art Biennale in (Dakar, Senegal: 2016); Disguise: Masks and Global African Art at Seattle Art Museum (Seattle, USA: 2015); What Remains is Tomorrow for the South African Pavilion (56th Venice Biennale: 2015); The Divine Comedy: Heaven, Purgatory and Hell Revisited by Contemporary African Artists (Museum für Moderne Kunst (MMK), Frankfurt/Main, Germany: 2014), Nandipha Mntambo at the FNB Joburg Art Fair (Johannesburg: 2013) and the 3rd Moscow International Biennale for Young Art (Moscow, Russia: 2012). \\n \\nShe has been shortlisted for the AIMIA | AGO Photography Prize in Canada (2014), was a Civitella Ranieri Fellow (2013), received the Standard Bank Young Artist Award for Visual Art (2011) and the Wits/BHP Billiton Fellowship (2010)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013436678365 gid://shopify/Product/9013436743901 gid://shopify/Product/9013436776669

She holds a MA in Media Studies and a PhD in ICT4D from the University of Cape Town, she recently completed her post-doctoral tenure at the department of Applied Design at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology. \\nShe has created design and illustration work for Apple Music, Nike, Microsoft, Speedo, Square Enix and Mr Price, among many others."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013928362205

item.title: Naomi Loabile
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641851146461 Naomi Loabile gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640911622365 [] Discover the work of Naomi Lilian Loabile, a Botswana-born interdisciplinary designer exploring the intersection of space, function, and human experience. Learn about her innovative approach to design, blending cultural heritage with diverse artistic mediums. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Naomi Lilian Loabile (b. 1993, Botswana) is an interdisciplinary designer whose work explores the intricate relationship between space, function, and human experience. With a Bachelor's degree in Interior Architecture from the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point (2015) and a Master's in Design from Listaháskóli Íslands in Iceland, Loabile's practice transcends traditional design boundaries. \\n \\nHer creative process is characterized by a hands-on approach, where she meticulously crafts and shapes materials, allowing the project to evolve through each stage. Loabile's work encompasses a wide range of disciplines, including speculative design, furniture and product design, material research, cultural and heritage studies, storytelling and writing, textiles, and printmaking. She skillfully merges these diverse fields to create cohesive and thought-provoking works. \\n \\nLoabile is particularly interested in how interior environments influence an individual's state of being, and this fascination drives her exploration of spatial use and function. Her work is deeply rooted in her cultural heritage and identity, which she weaves into her designs through storytelling and material choices. \\n \\nHer exhibitions include \"Flæði\" in Reykjavik (2020), live readings from her fictional writings at the Reykjavik Museum, and participation in Design March 2021 in Reykjavik, Iceland. She is also actively involved in the art community, currently serving as the vice-secretary on the ARC Executive board."}]}]}

item.title: Nano Le Face
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641851080925 Nano Le Face 1835 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640908673245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013463384285","gid://shopify/Product/9013463679197","gid://shopify/Product/9013463711965","gid://shopify/Product/9013839200477","gid://shopify/Product/9013843362013","gid://shopify/Product/9014011953373","gid://shopify/Product/9014011986141","gid://shopify/Product/9014012051677","gid://shopify/Product/9014012084445","gid://shopify/Product/9014012117213","gid://shopify/Product/9014013591773","gid://shopify/Product/9014013624541","gid://shopify/Product/9014013690077","gid://shopify/Product/9014044491997","gid://shopify/Product/9014044524765"] Discover the satirical and visually striking works of South African artist Nano Le Face. His vibrant, mixed-media art pieces critique consumerism and pop culture. Explore and purchase unique, original artworks online, reflecting the beauty, humor, and complexity of contemporary life. [22273,17223,22270,22309,22269,22311,22308,22271,17267,17266,18526,23412,23413,22272,22310,18248,22312] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ntwanano Shilubana (b. 1999), better known as Nano Le Face or simply Nano, is a self-taught visual artist based in Pretoria, South Africa. Nano studied Film Arts at the Open Window Institute in Pretoria and at AFDA in Johannesburg before committing entirely to fine art. Through a suite of Post-Pop drawings, Nano Le Face employs humour and satire to mock and critique our obsession with consumerism, fame, and self-image. \\nNano work is distinguished by sharp-witted prose and acerbic characterization offering a biting critique of contemporary culture. Nano began his artistic practice during the COVID-19 pandemic, a period that prompted individuals to observe one another through screens, turning their attention inward. Initially gaining traction on Instagram, Nano developed a dedicated base of collectors. His works quickly attracted attention from prominent figures in the art world, leading to numerous exhibitions and fairs, including the Turbine Art Fair and RMB Latitudes Art Fair. \\nWorking primarily in mixed media on paper, Nano's creations borrow freely from popular culture, editorial photography, and luxury brand advertisements. His imagery is flattened into vivid lines and striking colours palettes, presenting scenes that seem like bite-sized snippets from a satirical cartoon. Through a combination of coloured pencils and wax crayons, Nano crafts playful yet deeply critical works that draw viewers into a world of glamour and melodrama. \\nNano’s art often features enigmatic characters and scenes, allowing viewers to interpret and imagine their own narratives. His characters, such as the recurring \"Bettys and Veronicas,\" embody a mixture of distant glamour and relatable human traits, reinforcing the satirical nature of his work. \\nNano’s recent works continue to delve into themes of pop culture, hyper-consumerism, and social media vanity. He remains fascinated by the glamorized yet surreal nature of celebrity culture, capturing its essence in his satirical and often provocative drawings. Through his evolving artistic practice, Nano Le Face offers a mirror to society’s obsessions and invites viewers to engage with his biting critiques. \\nNano’s distinctive voice and artistic style ensure that his works are not only visually captivating but also intellectually stimulating, providing a fresh perspective on the complexities of modern life."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013463384285 gid://shopify/Product/9013463679197 gid://shopify/Product/9013463711965 gid://shopify/Product/9013839200477 gid://shopify/Product/9013843362013 gid://shopify/Product/9014011953373 gid://shopify/Product/9014011986141 gid://shopify/Product/9014012051677 gid://shopify/Product/9014012084445 gid://shopify/Product/9014012117213 gid://shopify/Product/9014013591773 gid://shopify/Product/9014013624541 gid://shopify/Product/9014013690077 gid://shopify/Product/9014044491997 gid://shopify/Product/9014044524765

item.title: Narina Trogon
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641851474141 Narina Trogon gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640912081117 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Narina Trogon was born in 2020 to an affluent imagination as an alias and alter ego to a “Real Artist”. The ever enigmatic Trogon is a brainchild selected from submissions by a covert group of emerging, mid-career and famous, practising contemporary artists. This Alias, Narina Trogon, is an early representative of the newly launched Incognito Art House Project. This experimental artist-run initiative playfully prods at ideas around the commodification of identity, market accessibility, artist sustainability and the effect of market and/or investor expectation on the artist’s creative autonomy. \\n \\nThe purpose of this invented persona is to grant the artist from whence it came complete autonomy in the creative process. Removing the artist’s identity (arguably the fetish of the art world) creates a buffer between artist and marketplace. “Real Artists” are thus offered a reprieve from the responsibility of maintaining a career trajectory and preserving their “brand”. This allows them to be playful and experimental, producing work far removed from their usual repertoire without fear of reproach by the unwritten rules of the system. \\n \\nThe works produced for the Incognito project are sold at a standardised price point, levelling the playing field among artists and offering the public a rare opportunity to affordably own quality, curated, contemporary art. Artists, in turn, can give back generously to art admirers during this challenging time."}]}]}

item.title: Natalie Paneng
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641852391645 Natalie Paneng gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640912408797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013968404701","gid://shopify/Product/9013968503005","gid://shopify/Product/9013968634077","gid://shopify/Product/9013968732381","gid://shopify/Product/9013968863453","gid://shopify/Product/9013968961757","gid://shopify/Product/9013969092829","gid://shopify/Product/9013969322205","gid://shopify/Product/9014057173213"] Natalie Paneng, a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist, combines her theatre background and digital skills to create imaginative digital art and new media. She has exhibited widely, including at Galerie EIGEN + ART in Leipzig, and has participated in several artist residencies and digital art festivals. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natalie Paneng (b. 1996) is a Johannesburg-based multidisciplinary artist whose innovative work spans digital art, new media, and performance. She earned her BA in Dramatic Arts from the University of Witwatersrand in 2018, winning Leon Gluckman Prize. Combining her theatre background with self-taught digital skills, Paneng describes herself as a world-builder, creating and archiving imagined realities through digital art. \\nPaneng has exhibited her work with esteemed institutions such as TMRW Gallery, The National Arts Festival, Blank Projects, Michaelis School of Fine Art, BKHz, Javett UP, Galerie Eigen Art Leipzig, and Mutek. Her first solo exhibition, 'Maze,' was presented internationally at Galerie EIGEN + ART in Leipzig, Germany. She has also participated in prominent artist residencies, including Bubblegum Future 76 Residency, Floating Reverie, Fak’ugesi Digital Innovation Artist Residency, and The Centre of A Less Good Idea’s So Academy’s ‘Thinking in Cardboard’ scenographers mentorship. \\nIn addition to her exhibitions, Paneng has published creative research through Ellipses Journal and Artist Research Africa and was a 202 Fellow with the Institute of Creative Arts and UCT. Recent exhibitions include Galerie Eigen + Art in Leipzig (2023), Stevenson Gallery in Johannesburg (2023), FCA Ghana (2023), Standard Bank Gallery in Johannesburg (2022), Galerie Konerpark in Berlin (2023), and The Centre For A Less Good Idea in Johannesburg (2023). She has also participated in digital art festivals such as MUTEK Montreal, KIKK Festival, Fak’ugesi Festival, and IDFA. In 2023, Paneng was awarded the Special Jury Prize for her use of creative technology at the International Documentary Festival of Amsterdam."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013968404701 gid://shopify/Product/9013968503005 gid://shopify/Product/9013968634077 gid://shopify/Product/9013968732381 gid://shopify/Product/9013968863453 gid://shopify/Product/9013968961757 gid://shopify/Product/9013969092829 gid://shopify/Product/9013969322205 gid://shopify/Product/9014057173213

item.title: Natalie van Wyk
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641853309149 Natalie van Wyk gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650752639197 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natalie van Wyk is a practising artist living on the Indian Ocean in the Eastern Cape of South Africa. She has an Honours Degree in Fine Art from Rhodes University. \\n \\nHer work explores both her environment and an intrapsychic terrain. It is figurative and tends towards the narrative, drawing on personal experience, Jungian psychology, archetypes and mythology. Nature is ever present and recurring motifs are the artist’s shadow, animals and birds. \\nHer work hangs in private collections in New York, Johannesburg, Cape Town and the Eastern Cape. \\nSolo Exhibitions \\n2022: \\nStories that Float on the Wind’ \\nAn Exhibition of inner and outer landscapes \\nCVD Art Gallery, East London \\n2020: \\n‘Reveal Conceal’ \\nAn Exhibition of inner and outer landscapes \\nNational Arts Festival \\nMakhanda"}]}]}

item.title: Natasha Evans
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855045853 Natasha Evans 351 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640914211037 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013999042781","gid://shopify/Product/9013999075549","gid://shopify/Product/9013999108317","gid://shopify/Product/9013999141085"] [21540,21543,21542,21541] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natasha (b. 1978) in Zimbabwe in and raised from a young age in Zambia, the birthplace of both her parents. In her early twenties Natasha studied at The Arts Institute at Bournemouth where she earned a bachelor's degree with honors in Illustration. Natasha works as a full time artist from her home studio in Lusaka, Zambia. Natasha has taken part in multiple group exhibitions and last year November she showed a collection of work in her fifth solo exhibition. Internationally Natasha travelled to Paris to exhibit a calabash vessel body of work, representing Zambia. \\nNatasha prepares new work for an upcoming show at the end of this year. Natasha creates contemporary mixed media works that see fluid shifts and overlaps in abstraction and figuration. Her work is realized on traditional media using paper and canvas and has editions in print. Her use of less traditional media includes the organic vessel the calabash, cement, earth, textile and found materials that are sculptural in nature. She makes use of tangible and non- tangible elements like, transferred photographic image, light, shadow, sculpted paper, automatic drawing, building, stacking, repetition, concealing, revealing and mark making. Natasha extracts resources from the physical (earth), cultural and social environments she (we) connect to in both the past and present. \\nShe goes deeper by often fragmenting texts and uses metaphor and symbolism to tell stories that she finds being Africa. Exploring selfhood, womanhood, dark and light, strength and fragility, presence and absence. In her work, Natasha quests to understand our edges, our deep cavities as well as our dreams and our lightness; the duality of being inside and outside simultaneously."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013999042781 gid://shopify/Product/9013999075549 gid://shopify/Product/9013999108317 gid://shopify/Product/9013999141085

item.title: Natasha Norman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855078621 Natasha Norman 1711 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640914276573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013424718045"] [15467,15465] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natasha completed her Honours (2005) and Masters (2011) degree in Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. She currently works as a part-time lecturer, arts writer and practicing artist. Throughout her art training and career she has consistently been inspired by the medium and technical challenges of print. She trained in traditional Western print methods at the University of Cape Town and subsequently attended residencies in Japan to study the Japanese relief print method, Mokuhanga. \\n \\nNatasha’s mastery of printmaking enables her to work across various print techniques. Her work is deeply inspired by her experiences of the natural world. Her practice is about remembering time and place. In her optically shifting colour layers and planes of marks and tone is an elementary, sensory memory. \\nIn recent works, Natasha has taken much inspiration from the Japanese cultural aesthetic wabi sabi. Her study of this term that defies translation has fostered an appreciation for the beauty in transient natural moments and a sense of spiritual well-being centred on imperfection and simplicity. The theme of her work tends toward expressing the momentary and experiential in a pared-down language of mark and form that seeks to evoke a resonant response in the viewer rather than portray a particular event."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013424685277 gid://shopify/Product/9013424718045

item.title: Nathan Vuuren
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855439069 Nathan Vuuren gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640914473181 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As an artist, I am interested in exploring the complex and often \\ntumultuous nature of the South African landscape, both physical and \\nsocial. Through my paintings, I seek to capture the visceral experienc\u0002es of violence, excess, politics, and personal struggle that are so deeply \\nembedded in this context. \\nMy work is a reflection of my own personal experiences, as well as an \\nattempt to grapple with the larger societal issues that impact us all. \\nWhether I am exploring the religious roots that underlie some of \\nSouth African culture or delving into the entropy that seems to per\u0002vade every corner of the urban landscape, my goal is always to create a \\nsense of raw emotive power that resonates with viewers. \\nIn my paintings, I employ a range of techniques and approaches, \\ndrawing on a rich visual vocabulary that includes everything from \\nbold brushstrokes and vivid colors to subtle and intricate rendering. \\nEach piece is a unique expression of my own vision and perspective, \\nand I strive to create works that are both deeply personal and broadly \\nrelevant."}]}]}

item.title: Natnael Ashebir
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855602909 Natnael Ashebir 1597 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915161309 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013346730205","gid://shopify/Product/9013349318877","gid://shopify/Product/9013349417181","gid://shopify/Product/9013349974237"] [10071,10072] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Natnael Ashebir (b. 1995) is one of the most exciting young artists to emerge from the Ethiopian visual arts scene in recent years. Now based in Addis Ababa, Natnael received BFA from Alle school of fine art and design 2021, Diploma from Entoto Polytechnic College 2016 and Abyssinia Fine Art School (2013). Throughout his latest body of work, Natnael merges form in a meditative exploration of layers of life and inwardness. His artworks are not only about urbanization and social structure; rather, they are immersive experience of time and space. He works across a variety media including painting, digital art, drawing and photography. His work has been exhibited in Ethiopia, Kenya and Nigeria. Natnael was a second prize winner of the Emerging Painting Invitational Prize (EPI2022) organized by African Art Galleries Association (AAGA). He currently live and work in Ethiopia."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013346730205 gid://shopify/Product/9013349318877 gid://shopify/Product/9013349417181 gid://shopify/Product/9013349974237

item.title: Nathi Ndlandla
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855537373 Nathi Ndlandla gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915128541 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nathi Ndlandla was born in the Alexandra Township in 1979. He was raised by a single parent and completed his matric at East Bank high school. He lived with his mother, aunt, five cousins and two uncles under one shelter. He survived through the support of the community, friends and teachers who mentored him. As his school did not have art as a subject, he created his own art projects, most often wire cars and clay sculptures. \\n \\nAfter a year at home with no financial support to study further, he was introduced to Artist Proof Studio. Here he was introduced to printmaking and after a year he was sponsored by Pin Point One Solutions. He graduated after three years as a professional printmaker. Soon after graduating his mother passed away. \\n \\nHe later worked at Phumani Paper, a research development unit of the University Of Johannesburg researching and developing Archival Hand-Made Paper for printmaking as well as training and development in the community. He worked as an apprentice for Tim Foulds and currently works as a master printmaker in the Artist Proof Studio Pro-Shop. He was awarded an Ampersand Fellowship to New York in 2018."}]}]}

item.title: Navel Seakamela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855635677 Navel Seakamela gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915226845 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Navel Seakamela was born in Soshanguve, Pretoria, in 1991 and raised in Tembisa, Johannesburg. Seakamela went to public school where he studied engineering graphics and design and practiced art as his hobby. From 2007-2010 he practiced fine art full time at the Tembisa art Centre before studying Fine and Applied Art at the Tshwane University of Technology (TUT). His work consists of themes such as isolation, alienation and depression amongst our generation and captures the raw scenes which are mostly ignored and hidden within our society."}]}]}

item.title: Ncaoto Thama (Kuru Art Project)
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855668445 Ncaoto Thama (Kuru Art Project) gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915259613 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014079062237"] Discover the vibrant work of Ncaoto Thama, a member of the Kuru Art Project Collective, showcasing cultural heritage and creative storytelling through immersive visual art. View artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Kuru Art Project is located in the village of D'kar, Western Botswana. The project was established in 1991 as part of the larger Kuru Development Trust. The artists are Naro and Dcui San, who have lived in and around D'kar since the early 1960's. Formally a nomadic people, hunting and food gathering from the veld remain significant cultural activities, but increasing westernisation means that this is not a sustainable lifestyle anymore. \\nMyths, legends and events of a bygone era are readily told by elders, but the less fortunate can only try to imagine life as it once was. Yet they all converge on a theme characterised by a mythical connection with animals and objects of their ancient past, while continuing their lives in a world that demands completely different skills to survive. \\nToday, there are 18 artists actively participating in the project. The artists work in a variety of media and techniques, which include oil on canvas, different printmaking techniques, and embroidery. \\nThey draw inspiration from stories told by their ancestors, and their expansive knowledge about the plants and animals from the Kalahari. For them, their art is a way to convey their identity and unique ways of life to the rest of the world. The Kuru artists’ work is known for its spontaneity. Often, the process is preferred over the product—their love for making and creating forms an intricate part of their culture. Bright colours and naive animal and plant forms signify the work of these artists. Their body of work is internationally acclaimed and has been exhibited in over fifteen countries abroad and in Africa over the years. \\nIn her own words, Ncaotoe says, “I do not really know what art is”, says Ncaotoe. “I just do it and I find I like it.” Ncaotoe joined the Kuru Art Project in the beginning of 2010. She loves the Kalahari bush passionately. She lived previously in the settlement of Rooibrak on the very edge of the Central Kalahari Game Reserve. Since Ncaotoe joined the project, she has made beautiful paintings and linocuts that tell of her love and knowledge of the Kalahari. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014079062237

item.title: Ncg'abe (Nxabe) Tase
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855701213 Ncg'abe (Nxabe) Tase gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915357917 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014053863645"] Explore the evocative oil paintings of Ncg’abe Tãse, a Botswana-born artist and founding member of the Kuru Art Project. Her work blends traditional San motifs with contemporary expressions, preserving and celebrating indigenous heritage. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1955, Botswana artist Ncg’abe is one of the last remaining original Kuru artists in the Kuru Art Project today. \\nShe joined the Kuru Art Project in 1992 together with her close friend Cg’ose Ntcox’o. Apart from visual art, Ncg’abe is a keen traditional dancer and musician, and she and Xgaiga, her husband, are founder members of the Nharo Giraffe Dance Group. \\n \\nAlthough she also makes beautiful linoleum prints, etchings and lithographs, Ncg’abe prefers to work with oil paint on canvas. The large-scale canvasses give her more freedom and directness, which is difficult to get with printmaking techniques. \\nShe loves to portray strange combinations of plants, birds, and other creatures like snakes and insects. The leaves, twigs, and creatures in her art sometimes form abstract patterns with great appeal. \\nShe also depicts beadwork patterns and the patterns on the shaved skin aprons that form part of the traditional attire of her San people, which she remembers her grandmothers having made many years ago."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014053863645

item.title: Ndabuko Ntuli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855733981 Ndabuko Ntuli gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915652829 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ndabuko Ntuli (b.1975) in KwaZulu Natal, South Africa. Ntuli is a Multidisciplinary artist,producer, sangoma, musician and spiritualist. Being born and raised in the Zulu heartland of Kwa-Zulu Natal and moving to Johannesburg at a young age, Ntuli has already enjoyed a storied and diverse career. His proud Zulu heritage informs his art, each piece never quite being the same as the last whether it is painted, sculpted, made from discarded materials or drawn."}]}]}

item.title: Ndako Nghipandulwa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855799517 Ndako Nghipandulwa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640915947741 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ndako Nghipandulwa (b. 1988 in Kwanza Sul, Angola) is a self-taught artist. His parents were in exile during the liberation struggle, returning to Namibia post-independence in 1990. He studied Civil Engineering & Project Management, and worked in the construction industry before becoming a fulltime artist. Recent exhibitions include his solo exhibition ‘Just Because’, at the Project Room in 2022, the Beijing Biennale, 2022 and the group exhibition ‘In the Meantime’ in 2021. Working predominantly with nails and string, Nghipandulwa is highly sought-after for his craft, creating numerous commissioned works for clients in Namibia as well as hosting workshops for children, most recently for ‘UNICEF World Children’s Day’."}]}]}

item.title: Ndidi Dike
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855930589 Ndidi Dike gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916111581 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in London, Ndidi Dike studied painting at UNN. Since graduation, Dike taught herself to sculpt and has established herself as one of Nigeria’s leading contemporary artists. She returned to painting in 2004 after a brief hiatus in well over a decade of transgressive sculptural practice. And is stimulated by Nigerian visual culture, urbanism, globalisation, consumerism, post-colonial studies, slavery, cross border/country migration, multiculturalism, art history, and contemporary politics. Having had numerous solo exhibitions till date, and group exhibitions in Nigeria and abroad. Including, Seven Stories About Modern Art in Africa: Whitechapel Art Gallery, London, England (1995. ), Solo exhibits include Waka-Into-Bondage: The Last 3/4 Mile, Centre for Contemporary Art, Lagos (2008) Unknown Pleasures and Competing Tendencies, National Museum Onikan, Lagos,(2012), State Of The Nation, new works and installations, National Museum Onikan ,Lagos (2016) Biennale Jogja XIII “Hacking Conflict Indonesia meets Nigeria”( 2015) . She currently runs her own studio in Lagos."}]}]}

item.title: Ndaya Ilunga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641855832285 Ndaya Ilunga 2885 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916013277 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014094758109"] Discover the powerful and expressive work of Ndaya Ilunga, a contemporary African artist featured on Latitudes Online. Explore original artworks and collect now. [24549] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Johannesburg to Congolese parents, Ndaya Ilunga, 29, began her artistic journey in her mother’s studio at the Bag Factory. She explored painting, sculpture and storytelling from a young age, later studying Fine Arts at the University of Johannesburg. In her third year, she was awarded a German Archdiocese exposure trip to Stuttgart, where she deepened her interest in surrealist and Renaissance art. \\nIlunga’s work is rooted in her exploration of a displaced refugee identity, merging Afrofuturist and surrealist elements into a unique visual language. She completed an Ampersand Foundation residency in Manhattan, New York, and interned at the Goodman Gallery, where her interest in the collective consciousness, blackness and the human condition evolved. \\nShe has exhibited at the UJ Art Gallery, The Viewing Room Art Gallery and Art & About. She was a finalist for the 2024 Nando’s Vusa Awards and participated in the RMB Talent Unlocked programme. She was awarded the 2024/2025 Bag Factory Young Womxn Studio Bursary supported by South African artist Sam Nlengethwa and has a studio at the Bag Factory in Fordsburg. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014094758109

item.title: Ndumiso Verity Bhengu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641856454877 Ndumiso Verity Bhengu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916439261 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ndumiso Verity Bhengu is a Johannesburg-based artist born on the 7th of May 1998 in Soweto, where he started his photography practice. He developed an eye for photographing landscapes through cellphone photography in 2016, prompting him to pursue his photography practice at the Market Photo Workshop where he rediscovered his unique style of fusing Documentary and Street photography during 2019. Since then, his work has been exhibited at the RMB Turbine Art Fair, a Covid-19 project relief fund (2020). He has participated in a collaborative exhibition named Enlightened 20(2020) and also is a verified member of the Viewbug community where he shares his creativity with the rest of the world. After completing his studies at the Market Photo Workshop he then when on to nurture his skills particularly in African Contemporary Photography at Through The Lens Collective (2021) and is currently doing an Advanced Course (2022)."}]}]}

item.title: Ndlovukazi Ngilande
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641856225501 Ndlovukazi Ngilande 2630 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640916144349 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014001926365"] [21644] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ndlovukazi Ngilande's work is a celebration of women, honoring their beauty, strength, and vital roles within society. Her art is driven by a deep desire to pay tribute to the significance of the isicholo—a traditional Zulu hat worn by married women—and to ensure its appreciation endures for future generations \\nRooted in her heritage and inspired by the rich cultural history around her, Ngilande's pieces reflect a deep fascination with African art. She strives to honour her ancestors by blending traditional techniques with modern elements, creating works that bridge the gap between the past and the present. Her art serves as a homage to the artistic legacy that came before her, while also bringing it into the contemporary sphere. \\nNgilande's vision is for every married woman to own an isicholo sculpture, not only as a beautiful piece of art but also as a symbol of her marital status, proudly displayed in her home. Through her work, she seeks to preserve and celebrate this powerful cultural icon, ensuring it remains a meaningful part of African tradition for generations to come."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014001926365

item.title: Neil Badenhorst
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857208541 Neil Badenhorst 1049 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917160157 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013466300637","gid://shopify/Product/9013896446173","gid://shopify/Product/9013897101533","gid://shopify/Product/9013897855197","gid://shopify/Product/9014024011997","gid://shopify/Product/9014024143069","gid://shopify/Product/9014024634589","gid://shopify/Product/9014024667357"] [22693,22710,19245,22711,19246,19247,22689] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neil Badenhorst (b. 1995) is an artist and illustrator based in Pretoria. He completed his Undergraduate and Honours degrees in Visual Communication with a major in Illustration at the Open Window, graduating in 2017 and 2018 respectively. Badenhorst began his Masters in Illustration in 2019, exploring ritual spaces and crisis heterotopias in illustrated fantasy books. Badenhorst has been pursuing a career as an independent artist since his early days at University and has also worked as a freelance illustrator and designer, as well as a lecturer, since then. Badenhorst’s ultimate goal as a creative is to be a ‘jack of all trades, master of none’. Through formally taught in digital design and illustration, Badenhorst’s artistic practice extends into painting, collage, and more recently digital and traditional installation art. His practice is largely concerned with themes such as liminality, multi-layered space and experience, queer themes, ritual process and imaginary worlds. Badenhorst’s creative process relies heavily on intuition, and his dreamscapes are a desperate attempt to map out the eternally expanding internal landscape, and recollection of memories from other worlds and universes. Badenhorst's master's exhibition, between worlds, explores these themes in practice. The exhibition centers around fragments of a narrative I have been piecing together for most of my life, from recorded dreams and daydreams. The exhibition consists of illustrated pieces that tell stories about things I ‘remember’ in the otherworld. The gallery space ultimately becomes both a ritual space (a liminal space between this world and our own), but also becomes the book of sorts; as one must move through the space to follow and piece together the narrative. The narrative, and world, the pieces centre around were never exactly an intentional creation on my part. It developed naturally from dreams and my imagination, piecing itself together. Thus artmaking, here, became a deeply personal ritual process where I am almost desperately clinging to the memories of my life in the otherworld I encounter when asleep or daydreaming; and it is these stories and spaces that allow me to reflect and make better sense of my experiences within the ‘real’ world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013466300637 gid://shopify/Product/9013896446173 gid://shopify/Product/9013897101533 gid://shopify/Product/9013897855197 gid://shopify/Product/9014024011997 gid://shopify/Product/9014024143069 gid://shopify/Product/9014024634589 gid://shopify/Product/9014024667357

item.title: Neil Nieuwoudt
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857306845 Neil Nieuwoudt gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917291229 [] Neil Nieuwoudt {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"NEIL NIEUWOUDT \\n(b 1979. South Africa. Lives and works in Johannesburg) \\nNeil is a self-taught artist who is one of the founding members of the Dead Bunny Society, which was founded in March 2015. Neil has studied the use of symbols and imagery as language for over two decades and found it bizarre and surreal, so he chose to create his own language to decode it all. Inspired by the process of alchemy The Long Dark Tea Time of the Soul, delves into sub-conscious imagery and recurrent symbols presented as altered, hand-bound artist books and screen prints. \\nNeil Nieuwoudt works in a free-flow manner. His artworks take shape naturally from his subconscious mind. His energetic artworks combine colour, symbol, and form to create a language beyond categorization where the meaning is left to interpretation. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Neil Wright
item.description: Neil Wright gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917422301 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neill Wright is a multidisciplinary artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. His satirical work braves the world of social commentary in a bold, colourful and humorous manner. Wright explores various mediums, such as sculpture, printmaking and painting as modes of expression, drawing inspiration from the interconnected worlds \\n \\n \\n \\nof media, popular culture, politics and societal interactions in an attempt to create panoramic views of current issues, hardships, complexities and paradoxes present within South African and to some extent African society as a whole. Through highlighting the absurdities of a collectively experienced ‘everyday’, his work subverts the tragic, placing the viewer in a space where they are confronted by opposing feelings: the melancholic reality and the ironic hilarity of his compositions. \\n \\n \\n \\nBIOGRAPHY \\n \\n \\n \\nIn 2007, Neill graduated with distinction for the degree of Bachelor of Arts in Fine Art (Honours), at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town, where he was co-awarded the Simon Gerson Prize for an outstanding body of work. In 2009, he graduated with a Postgraduate Diploma in Fine Art, majoring in printmaking. In 2013, Wright was named one of the ten emerging South African artists to watch by The Times, and he has exhibited in a number of group and solo shows as well as at numerous South African and International Art fairs. His works are housed in private collections in Europe, the United States, Australia and South Africa. \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Nel Erasmus
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857994973 Nel Erasmus 1019 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640917848285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013302034653","gid://shopify/Product/9133235011805"] [4981,25534] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nel Erasmus (born 1928 in Bethal, Transvaal Province, South Africa) is a South African artist. Erasmus obtained a BA in Fine Art at Wits and a NATC at The Witwatersrand Technical College in the early 1950’s. After teaching in art in Johannesburg and London, she settled in France in 1953, studying at the Academie Ranson, Ecole des Beaux Arts and the Sorbonne. Her first solo exhibition was in South Africa in 1957 and she is one of the earliest abstract artists of South Africa. Erasmus has produced thirty solo exhibitions, taken part in more than seventy group exhibitions and her writing has been widely published. Although Erasmus was never a ‘popular’ painter, her work received much critical acclaim and she was the only South African artist to be included in Michel Seuphor’s 1964 survey of abstraction, Abstract Painting: 50 Years of Accomplishment. \\n \\nNel Erasmus was an early proponent of Abstract Art in South Africa – both as a practice and a principle. Erasmus also influenced the South African art scene as director of the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG) (1966–1977). \\n \\nNel Erasmus worked at the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG) from 1957 as Professional Officer until her retirement as Director in 1977. She has contributed to the acquisition of artworks to public and corporate (especially Sanlam and Sasol) collections in South Africa, in particular the international modern and contemporary collection at the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG). \\n \\nErasmus’ notorious acquisition in 1973, the year Picasso died, of Pablo Picasso’s Tête d’Arlequin (1971) was made possible by funding from The Friends of the Museum organization. The acquisition of this painting of a clown met with resistance from conservative, censored, isolated, apartheid South Africa, “No normal person would like this painting”, and provoked Erasmus to write a paper about why the acquisition was made. \\n \\nNel Erasmus is in her 80s and still paints daily. The most recent exhibitions she has participated in were solo exhibitions in 2009 in the Dawid Ras Art Gallery (Johannesburg) and in 2015 in the Dawid Ras Gallery (Cape Town), and since then various group exhibitions. \\n \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013302034653 gid://shopify/Product/9133235011805

Her work explores themes of nature, emotion, and abstraction, using delicate textures and intricate details to create visually captivating and thought-provoking pieces. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Growing up on a farm in the Free State, born in 1972, was a life filled with freedom, adventure, and creativity. Being surrounded by such a dynamic community has fueled my own creativity Living in Stellenbosch, with its stunning natural scenery and vibrant creative community, has been a source of constant inspiration and joy. \\nIt’s a place where the beauty of the environment and the creativity of its people come together to create a truly unique and enriching lifestyle. Part of the Voice Collective group. Group exhibit together at Kamers, Blaauklippen (October 2023 and March 2024), Garden Town, Stellenbosch 2023, Welgemeend in Cape Town (July 2024). Was part of the Woordfees exhibition in 2023 \\nLife in Creative Blocks As I reflect on my journey through the last fifty years, I see my life not as a linear narrative, but as a mosaic of creative blocks, each representing different stages, experiences, and transformations. Each block tells a unique story, yet together they form a cohesive tapestry of my existence, infused with the richness of lived moments."}]}]}

item.title: Nelo Teixeira
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857601757 Nelo Teixeira gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640918995165 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Angolan born Nelo Teixeira (b. 1975) creates collages, paintings, performances and installations out of mixed media, predominantly waste products collected among the rubble of Chicala. This Luandan neighbourhood where Teixeira once lived and worked has been largely demolished to make way for modern development, the remaining debris fundamental to the artist’s practice – in both subject and medium. Scraps of fabric, paper and hessian; wood and concrete detritus; as well as consumer waste from gentrified areas are torn, cut, juxtaposed and further worked with layers of acrylic paint, these repurposed found objects highlighting parallel narratives that challenge the powers that be. His subject matter speaks of the politics of space, of displacement and fragmentation, of personal and collective memories, of boundaries both physical and socio-political, with the dynamic vertical and horizontal dimensions of his installations suggesting the widespread cost to (razed) communities caused by so-called (sky-scraping) progress. \\n \\nNow based in Lisbon, Portugal, Teixeira has exhibited extensively in group shows and art fairs across South Africa and in Luanda, Lisbon, Paris, Milan, London as well as the 2015 Venice Biennale. He also participated in a residency at South Africa’s AVA Gallery."}]}]}

item.title: Nelson Makamo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641857831133 Nelson Makamo 557 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640919650525 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013316813021","gid://shopify/Product/9013940912349","gid://shopify/Product/9013940977885","gid://shopify/Product/9013941010653","gid://shopify/Product/9013941043421","gid://shopify/Product/9013941076189","gid://shopify/Product/9013941141725","gid://shopify/Product/9013941174493","gid://shopify/Product/9013941207261","gid://shopify/Product/9013941272797","gid://shopify/Product/9013941371101","gid://shopify/Product/9013941436637","gid://shopify/Product/9013941502173"] [19981,7389,24040,24044,24047,24048,24049,19957,19958,19959,19979,19963,19967,19971,19976,19982,19984] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nelson Makamo is a Johannesburg-based artist born in Limpopo, South Africa, where he dedicates his art to amplifying the voices of African children. Over a career spanning sixteen years, Makamo has risen as one of the world's most sought-after, young visual artists. His diverse portfolio includes, but is not limited to acrylic, print, watercolor, and charcoal drawings, with a keen focus on storytelling through candid portraits of children, capturing the resilience and beauty inherent in the human spirit. \\nTrained at the Artist Proof Studios in Johannesburg, Makamo's artistic journey began with three years of studying printmaking, providing a solid foundation. Continuing to evolve, he experimented with various materials, eventually finding his signature medium in charcoal. Makamo's unconventional work ethic embraces creative spontaneity, steering clear of detailed plans in his artistic process. Influenced by artists like Dumile Feni, Picasso, and Van Gogh, Makamo's globally acclaimed collections have graced exhibitions in South Africa, the USA, France, Italy, the Netherlands, England, and Scotland. His artwork challenges stereotypes in depicting African children, finding a place in prestigious collections worldwide. \\nBeyond the canvas, Makamo's impact extends to mainstream recognition, including an appearance on 'The Daily Show with Trevor Noah' and gracing the cover of Time magazine. Celebrated for creating a platform for young African artists to communicate through their art, Makamo's portraits exude strong emotions, reflecting the conviction, prowess, and determination of young Africans. His mixed-media style and unique mark-making technique distinguish him as a trailblazer in contemporary visual art, reshaping global perceptions of what it means to be an African child."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013316813021 gid://shopify/Product/9013940912349 gid://shopify/Product/9013940977885 gid://shopify/Product/9013941010653 gid://shopify/Product/9013941043421 gid://shopify/Product/9013941076189 gid://shopify/Product/9013941141725 gid://shopify/Product/9013941174493 gid://shopify/Product/9013941207261 gid://shopify/Product/9013941272797 gid://shopify/Product/9013941371101 gid://shopify/Product/9013941436637 gid://shopify/Product/9013941502173

item.title: Neo Matloga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858027741 Neo Matloga gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640919879901 [] Discover the powerful and expressive mixed media collages of Neo Matloga, a celebrated South African artist on Latitudes Online. Explore original artworks that blend painting, photography, and storytelling. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neo Matloga was born in 1993 in Mamaila, Limpopo, South Africa, and is currently based between Mamaila and Amsterdam. He studied Visual Art at the University of Johannesburg, and completed a residency at De Ateliers with a focus on painting. Matloga won the 2021 ABN AMRO Art award and the 2018 Koninklijke Prijs voor Vrije Schilderkunst. \\nSolo exhibitions include Mokete, MOU Projects, Hong Kong, China (2024); along came my eyes, Hermitage Amsterdam (2022), my hero is always next to me, Stroom Den Haag, the Hague (2021); Neo Matloga, S.M.A.K, Ghent (2021); Neo to Love, Fries Museum, Leeuwarden (2019) and Good Morning Midnight, De Ateliers, Amsterdam (2018) in addition to Stevenson (2020 – 23). \\nGroup exhibitions include Circulate: Photography Beyond Frames, Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam, the Netherlands (2024); Insistent Presence: Contemporary African Art from the Chazen Collection at Chazen Museum of Art, Wisconsin, USA (2023); Africa Supernova at Kunsthal KAde, Amersfoort, the Netherlands (2023); CODA Paper Art 2023 at CODA Museum, Apeldoorn, the Netherlands (2023); Brave New World: 16 painters for the 21st Century at Museum Fundatie, Zwolle (2023); When We See Us: A Century of Black Figuration in Painting, Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art, Cape Town, South Africa (2022), Kunstmuseum Basel, Switzerland (2023), BOZAR, Belgium (2025); We just want to be closer at Marta Herford Museum for Art and Galerie der Stadt Backnang, Germany (2022); HI-STORYTELLING at Sfeir-Semler, Hamburg, Germany (2021); ofte vojagantoj at Wilford X, Belgium (2019); Still Here Tomorrow To High Five You Yesterday at Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2019); Winter Sun at Stevenson, Amsterdam (2019); De Volkskrant Beeldende Kunst Prijs at Stedelijk Museum, Schiedam (2019); BIG AND PLENTY at Foundation AVL Mundo, Rotterdam (2019); About Face at Stevenson, Cape Town (2018); Koninklijke Prijs voor Vrije Schilderkunst at Koninklijk Paleis, Amsterdam (2018); Tell Freedom, 15 South African artists at Kunsthal KAdE, Amersfoort (2018); LET'S SEE, WHERE WERE WE, IN THE PIT OF DESPAIR at De Ateliers, Amsterdam (2017); Post It’s at South African Constitutional Court, Johannesburg (2016);Time Line at The Bag Factory, Johannesburg (2015); South African and Chinese exchange at Workers Museum, Johannesburg (2015) and South African New Voices at Washington Printmakers Gallery, Washington DC. \\n \\nHe has taken up residencies at Foundation AVL Mundo, Rotterdam (2019); Thami Mnyele Foundation, Amsterdam (2018); Zeitz MOCAA, Segera, Laikipia, Kenya (2018) and The Bag Factory, Johannesburg (2015).Matloga was nominated for De Volkskrant Beeldende Kunstprijs in 2019, and was among the artists shortlisted for the 2015 Taxi Art Award."}]}]}

item.title: Neo Matome
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858060509 Neo Matome 2870 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640919945437 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014079127773","gid://shopify/Product/9014079193309","gid://shopify/Product/9014079258845"] [24242,24243,24241] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neo Matome is a Motswana artist (b.1967, Johannesburg, South Africa). Neo works in various media, which include drawing, painting, installation and photography. She also incorporates the use of textiles in her practice. \\nGender, culture and socio?political issues inform her expression. Identity, belonging, parity and issues of equity – be it to land, education, health, economic or social opportunity are issues she addresses in her artworks but mainly from a gender perspective. She is interested in the intersection between culture, perception and power relations. \\nNeo has won prizes, with the most recent one being the prestigious 2024 National Arts Festival Best in Mentorship Award (Visual Arts) at the Gaborone International Conference Centre, awarded by the His Excellency the President Dr Mokgweetsi Masisi. Neo has participated in national, regional and international exhibitions including art workshops in Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia and Mozambique and a residency at the Vermont Studio Centre, Johnson, Vermont, USA, with her artworks represented in private and public collections locally and abroad. She is also an arts activist who has served in various roles to promote the visual arts in Botswana. \\nMs. Matome is one of Botswana’s key proponents in the official establishment of a formal Creative Industry economic segment of government, and a key contributor to the emerging contemporary art scene in Botswana since the mid-90’s. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014079127773 gid://shopify/Product/9014079193309 gid://shopify/Product/9014079258845

item.title: Neo Nene Mahlangu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858126045 Neo Nene Mahlangu 610 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920043741 [3143,3148,3141,3145,3142,3149,3150,3146,3151,3147,3144] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neo Mahlangu is (b. 1992) is a Johannesburg-based artist working primarily with charcoal and digital illustrations. Human connection grounds the practice of her work – her most recent work reasserts rhetoric of authority of the female voice in the everyday world and in the art world. The work normalizes vulnerability again, brining elegance and grace to the spaces that we occupy, it helps theorize the meaning of vulnerability in our lives, pushing you to day dream, and move into a space that allows spending uninterrupted time with thoughts, and dreams. Reminding you that in the midst of solitude is where we sometimes experience sharp insight and clarity. The process of creating work for the artists has proven to be more than a practical extension but also time spent in contemplation and preparation. \\n \\nThe body of work is one by a woman who is well absorbed in her politics, affirming other women in their own efforts to construct worlds of undisturbed space, where we can work with passion and abandon."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013282767069 gid://shopify/Product/9013282799837 gid://shopify/Product/9013282832605 gid://shopify/Product/9013282865373 gid://shopify/Product/9013282898141 gid://shopify/Product/9013282963677 gid://shopify/Product/9013282996445 gid://shopify/Product/9013283029213 gid://shopify/Product/9013283094749 gid://shopify/Product/9013283127517 gid://shopify/Product/9013283160285
