Neo currently resides and creates in Bloemfontein, where his work continues to evolve and make an impact."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014026272989 gid://shopify/Product/9014026698973 gid://shopify/Product/9014026731741 gid://shopify/Product/9014026797277

item.title: Nessi Penman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858191581 Nessi Penman 2558 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920273117 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013971878109","gid://shopify/Product/9013974597853","gid://shopify/Product/9013992161501","gid://shopify/Product/9014065823965","gid://shopify/Product/9132522963165","gid://shopify/Product/9133213548765","gid://shopify/Product/9133215875293","gid://shopify/Product/9133230260445","gid://shopify/Product/9133232160989","gid://shopify/Product/9133233733853"] [20866,25578,25575,25577,25579,20904,21304] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nessi Penman is a contemporary impressionist impasto painter creating works which invite the viewer into the natural world of flowers and lush landscapes. \\n \\n'My desire when I paint is to create works which instill within the viewer a deeper sense of calm and appreciation for nature and the paradise we live in. My objective is to draw people into my artworks so that they can find the creative spirit within themselves. I believe that we are all artists - may not be in paint or clay or charcoal, but we have the power to create beauty in our own environments and share that with others. \\n \\nI cannot say for sure where my love for oil painting came from, but one of my earliest memories were when my mother would take me to the art store once a month on her payday and she would buy me 'paint-by-numbers' and I would fall in love with the smell of those little tubs of paint and the distinct smell of the linseed oil contained therein - every time. \\n \\n Growing up in South Africa, the African landscape and its rich colours embedded themselves within my spirit. Irma Stern, Vincent van Gogh and Claude Monet are the three artists whose work I resonate with the most. I love their use of texture, emotion and dominant brush strokes. \\n \\nIt makes you feel like you are observing a painting - not a photograph. Your eyes dance across the canvas trying to understand what the artist did and what they were seeing and feeling. As a self-taught artist, I have been guided by my intuition, the medium and the artwork itself. It is my personal experience that I am only a conduit - the artwork creates itself through me. \\n \\n I had the privilege of meeting Pino Daeni and Howard Behrens - contemporary masters who have inspired me in both genre and technique. \\n \\nI have a passionate love for nature and animals. My deepest desire is that I use my talent to bring the viewer closer to experiencing flora and fauna within their own homes - a relief from the concrete jungle we live in. \\n \\n Since the digital economy has afforded artists an opportunity to communicate directly with collectors, I revel in hearing from you and love building relationships with every single person who has one of my works.’ \\n \\n \\n \\nEXHIBITIONS \\n \\nGroup exhibition – Young Blood, Cape Town, South Africa, 2024 \\n \\nGroup exhibition - Flagstaff Gallery, Devonport Auckland, New Zealand 2022"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013971878109 gid://shopify/Product/9013974597853 gid://shopify/Product/9013992161501 gid://shopify/Product/9014065823965 gid://shopify/Product/9132522963165 gid://shopify/Product/9133213548765 gid://shopify/Product/9133215875293 gid://shopify/Product/9133230260445 gid://shopify/Product/9133232160989 gid://shopify/Product/9133233733853

item.title: Neville Starling
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858224349 Neville Starling gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920371421 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Neville Starling is a self-taught, interdisciplinary artist. Starling was born in 1988 in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe where he maintains a secondary darkroom and studio for larger works. His primary workspace is held at The Bag Factory Artist’s Studios in Johannesburg, South Africa. \\nMotivated by his father’s windows of changed personality due to Alzheimer’s disease, Starling deconstructs time’s relationship with memory. He examines courses of normalisation and change, the processes of forced and chosen memories, modes of individuation and collectivism, as well as the connection between future being and the cultural archive. These are examined within the interplay of reality and perception with memory, and how these are interwoven within the continuum of identity. \\nAlthough Starling amalgamates various mediums and disciplines into his works, he has reached an in-depth understanding of the photograph as object. Beyond the artist's use of found films, slides, plates and negatives from either personal, collective or institutional archives, Starling also practices various analogue photographic techniques from wet-plate collodion to the silver gelatin negative/positive process, to handcrafted printing papers as well as digital video. Starling often removes photography from its two-dimensional realm into sculptural forms. These forms, which move between individual pieces and installation, are often light-based and kinetic. From this redefinition, Starling utilises photography as an immersive tool of mnemonic, temporal and spatial enquiry. \\nStarling represented Zimbabwe at the 58th Venice Biennale, May You Live In Interesting Times, 2019. He has also been selected to participate in the postponed 14th Dak’Art Biennial I? 'Ndaffa / Forging / Out of the Fire, 2020. The artist’s solo exhibition, Rest Until, traveled to The National Gallery of Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in 2016. Starling has an upcoming solo exhibition at Njelele Art Station in Harare, curated by Dana Whabira. Notable recent group exhibitions include: Another Kind of Blue, curated by Amé Bell at David Krut Projects as part of the Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees in 2020; I had a dream, 2019, conducted by Simon Njami and Andrew Tshabangu, held at the Africa Center, New York City, U.S.A.; Lost and Found: Expectations, Uncertainty, Excitement and Hope, 2018 curated by Raphael Chikukwa at The National Gallery of Zimbabwe; the 51st edition of the Zimbabwe Annual Art Exhibition, Blood Relatives, 2018, curated by Raphael Chikukwa at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe. Starling finished runner-up in the first Zimbabwean PPC Imaginarium Awards in 2018."}]}]}

item.title: Ngoma KaMphahlele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858257117 Ngoma KaMphahlele gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920436957 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014017687773","gid://shopify/Product/9014017720541","gid://shopify/Product/9014017786077"] Explore the profound works of Ngoma KaMphahlele, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through vibrant compositions and rich cultural narratives, KaMphahlele’s art explores themes of heritage, identity, and social commentary, creating visually captivating and thought-provoking pieces. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ngoma KaMphahlele is a visual artist who uses photography to explore various themes, such as fashion, jazz, and the architecture of Johannesburg, migration, and home (the sense of belonging). \\nNgoma's artistic journey has been deeply influenced by the diverse cultural landscapes of South Africa. In 2018, KaMphahlele graduated from the Market Photo Workshop with an Advanced Certificate in the advanced photography program. \\nInspired by the vibrant fashion scene and the timeless art form of jazz, Ngoma started capturing the essence of both through his lens. His visionary photography not only showcased the beauty and intricacies of fashion but also captured the soulful essence of the jazz appropriators in their gatherings. This unique combination of fashion and jazz became a prominent feature in Ngoma's work, offering a mesmerizing blend of visual aesthetics and musical narratives. In 2023, he developed and exhibited a body of work titled \"JazzLand,\" which further solidified his reputation as a remarkable artist. \\nFurthermore, KaMphahlele has always been fascinated by the architecture of Johannesburg, a city that reflects the history, growth, and transformation of South Africa. By capturing the city's iconic buildings and structures, KaMphahlele aimed to shed light on the intersecting stories of urban development, cultural heritage, and personal experiences. Migration, home, and a sense of belonging are recurring themes in KaMphahlele’s body of work. Drawing on his own experiences and the stories of others, he examines the complex feelings and challenges faced by individuals who have left their familiar homes in search of new beginnings. Through his photography, KaMphahlele invites viewers to contemplate the notions of identity, roots, and the profound yearning for a place to call home. \\nThroughout the years, Ngoma KaMphahlele has participated in various exhibitions, showcasing his exceptional talent and thought-provoking work. Additionally, KaMphahlele received the prestigious Thami Mnyele Award in 2018, winning the Ekurhuleni prize. \\nCurrently, KaMphahlele is part of artists under the banner of occupying the gallery under the guidance and mentorship of esteemed artists Mary Sibande and Lawrence Lemaoana. This influential and nurturing artistic environment allows KaMphahlele to further refine his craft, experiment with new techniques, and continue to push the boundaries of his artistic vision."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014017687773 gid://shopify/Product/9014017720541 gid://shopify/Product/9014017786077

item.title: Ngozi Lebogang Chukura
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858289885 Ngozi Lebogang Chukura 2343 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640920994013 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013841494237","gid://shopify/Product/9013949071581"] [20358,18375] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ngozi Lebogang Chukura is a multidisciplinary Nigerian/Motswana artist based in Botswana. She holds a BAFA from the Michaelis School of Fine Art and has participated in several group shows, including Surprize Surprize, the Joburg Fringe and the FNB Art Joburg fair. Her solo exhibition, 'The Shadow Journals' was held at the Alliance Francais in Gaborone in 2012. Chukura is an ardent feminist, and her poetry, short stories and op-eds have been published in Botswana Women Write, New African Woman Magazine, Galdem.com and the Stanford Journal of African Studies. \\n“I have been interested in the intersection between femme identities, nature and spirituality. I am also an avid consumer of contemporary popular media and culture.” The result has been a series of hybrid, pop-femme-flora subjects on paper and canvas, that document her exploration of contemporary feminisms and evidence her process of ‘writing’ contemporary mythologies. \\nHer fascination with nature-based religions and indigenous spiritualities has also allowed her explore the idea of contemporary myth-making that centers femme figures and imbues them with power. Her newer work does this quite literally by playing with scale and multiple mediums including thread and beads. \\n“With my work, I am investigating symbols and energies that come from ‘Where the Stories Live’, a nameless, ageless place that speaks directly to our imaginations when we hear, look, create meaning. We are in an ephemeral continuum. What is ancient and sacred was once contemporary and secular.” \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013841494237 gid://shopify/Product/9013949071581

item.title: Nhlanhla Nhlapho
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858322653 Nhlanhla Nhlapho 638 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640922042589 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014068183261", "gid://shopify/Product/9014068216029", "gid://shopify/Product/9014068248797", "gid://shopify/Product/9014068281565"] [3064,3062,3060,3061,24057,24060,24059,3063] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nhlanhla Nhlapo (b. 1988, Frankfurt, Free State, South Africa) studied fine arts degree four years programme at Tshwane University of Technology specializing in painting and has been teaching painting there since 2013. Nhlapo’s practice takes Dutch masters’ techniques and 17th century Dutch landscape painting as a point of departure, situating it in the South African landscape and his hometown of Frankfurt in particular and populating it with images from his family albums. The works engage both with the nature and cultural context of depiction in art history as well as the unspoken and unacknowledged politics of trauma within carried through landscape and implicit trauma of colonization, loss and confrontation between modernity and tradition in family photographs. Through many personal and day to day conflicts growing up in rural Free State and later moving to Gauteng and City Life, Nhlapo endeavors to create a personal narrative with this body of work, a symbolic longing to re-connect to the Land of his Ancestors; His reference to the Dutch Baroque Interior paintings reflects the firsthand experience of both his late grandmother and mother being Domestic workers and the hardship he experienced with their absence in his formative years during Apartheid. Nhalapo was awarded the 2018 Unisa Academic Portrait Commission of Chairperson Mr Simelane and the 2018 Artist residency at Lacreusette in France Boussac with Louis Jansen van Vurren. His first solo exhibition was with Lizamore Associates in 2019."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013281652957 gid://shopify/Product/9013281685725 gid://shopify/Product/9013281718493 gid://shopify/Product/9013281751261 gid://shopify/Product/9013281784029 gid://shopify/Product/9014068183261 gid://shopify/Product/9014068216029 gid://shopify/Product/9014068248797 gid://shopify/Product/9014068281565

item.title: Nic Bladen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862090973 Nic Bladen 659 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640922697949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014071525597","gid://shopify/Product/9014071591133","gid://shopify/Product/9014071754973"] [24103,24104,24106] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South African artist Nic Bladen has become known for his extraordinary botanical sculptures, which demonstrate the technique he pioneered of casting entire plants in bronze and sterling silver. Born in 1974 in Pretoria, Bladen trained in the field of dental technology, a discipline that requires incredible precision and attention to detail. After working for eight years making gold and porcelain crowns in various dental laboratories in South Africa and the UK, Bladen developed an interest in sculpture and began working at the Bronze Age Foundry, learning large-scale bronze casting as well as all aspects of metalwork. Knowledge of the two seemingly different fields of dental technology and bronze casting precipitated Bladen's experimentations in 2001: casting flowers and leaves. In marrying the micro and macro disciplines, he pioneered a way of developing perfect castings of organic matter. His way of preserving/fossilizing plants and flowers involves a method known as 'lost wax casting' (or cire perdue) and it involves creating moulds from actual organic material, and then transforming these into once-off sculptures of entire plants. \\n \\nNic's first solo exhibition, Peninsula, held at Everard Read, Cape Town in 2013, focused on the richness of botanical diversity that surrounds the artist's Simon’s Town studio, which is situated within the heart of the Cape Floral Kingdom, the smallest yet richest of the world's six floral kingdoms. For this show, concessions from landowners on the peninsula enabled Bladen to harvest such rarities as a Blue disa and the endemic Serruria villosa, amongst others. \\n \\nIn 2015, Nic worked as an Artist in Residence at Tswalu Kalahari, a private game reserve in South Africa's Northern Cape Province. The sculptures that he created during this time, a depiction of iconic, beautiful and strange Kalahari desert plants and trees, formed his second solo exhibition: Kalahari: A season at Tswalu, held at Everard Read, Johannesburg, in October 2015. \\n \\nThe title of Nic’s third exhibition ‘even in this unfavourable dry season’ is attributed to William J. Burchell, an early Cape botanist, in about 1810. Referencing the floral abundance and diversity encountered even during severe drought, this body of work depicts the tenacity of Cape Flora to tolerate this dryness, and the splendour with which it does so. \\n \\nNic’s fourth solo exhibition ‘Botanical Studies in Bronze and Silver’ was held at Everard Read London in May 2018 and introduced his unique cast botanicals to a while new audience. In January 2020, Nic’s fifth solo exhibition ‘Proteaceae’, was held at Everard Read Cape Town and focused on this spectacular and diverse plant family. \\nNic is currently preparing for his next solo exhibition, scheduled for February 2021, at Everard Read London. \\nNic's unique works can be found in the Standard Bank Art Collection, Ellerman House Cape Town, BMW and Oppenheimer Collections, as well as in many other prestigious private collections, both locally and abroad. \\n \\nSolo Exhibitions \\n2021 Upcoming solo, Everard Read, London, UK \\n2020 Arid, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2020 Proteaceae, Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2018 Botanical Studies in Bronze and Silver, Everard Read, London, UK \\n2017 Even at this unfavourable dry season, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2016 New Works, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2015 Kalahari: A season at Tswalu, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2013 Peninsula, Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\nSelected Group Exhibitions \\n2019 Masterpiece Art Fair London, Everard Read booth, London, UK \\n2018 FNB Joburg Art Fair, Everard Read CIRCA booth, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2017 Off the wall: A group sculpture exhibition, Everard Read Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2014 Exact Imagination: 300 years of botanically inspired art in South Africa. Curated by Cyril Coetzee. The Standard Bank Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nDesign Miami/Basel 2014, Southern Guild Collection, Basel, Switzerland \\n2012 Conversation Series, with Astrid Dahl, Jane Eppel and Katherine Glenday, Amaridian Gallery, New York, USA \\nSOFA (International Exposition of Sculpture Objects and Functional Art), with Amaridian Gallery, New York, USA \\n2011 Rare, joint show with Lisa Strachan at Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\nNatural Selection, joint show with Jane Eppel at Rust en Vrede Gallery, Durbanville, South Africa \\n2010 SOFA (International Exposition of Sculpture Objects and Functional Art), Amaridian Gallery, Chicago, USA \\n2009 Realisme, Art Fair, Amsterdam, Netherlands \\n2008 Group Exhibition at KZNSA Gallery, Durban, South Africa \\n2007 Greenhouse, group exhibition at Bell-Roberts Gallery, Lourensford, South Africa"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014071525597 gid://shopify/Product/9014071591133 gid://shopify/Product/9014071754973

item.title: Nicholas Hales
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858420957 Nicholas Hales gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640929317085 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013470658781"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicholas Hales is a contemporary artist living in Cape Town, South Africa. He works across a number of disciplines, including painting, drawing and video/film. He has an Advanced Diploma in Fine Art from the University of Cape Town (1992) and a Diploma in Graphic Design (1991) also from the University of Cape Town. To date, he has held six solo exhibitions. He has participated in numerous group shows in South Africa and a number of exhibitions internationally. \\n \\nHe has won a number of awards for his work, including a Scholarship award for an art residence, at L’Air Arts, Paris, France in 2019, and a Merit winner, ‘What is life exhibition?’ at the South African National Museum, Cape Town, 2002. His work is included in the permanent collections of L’Air Arts, Paris, France, Detroit Museum of New Art(MONA), U.S.A., Spier Arts Trust, South Africa and Nandos, South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013470658781

item.title: Nick Muzik
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641859895517 Nick Muzik 2636 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640929349853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014014083293","gid://shopify/Product/9014014410973"] [22324] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nick Mužík is a seasoned commercial and editorial photographer with over 15 years of experience, specializing in sports, fitness, and adventure lifestyle imagery. His background in sports and calm approach allow him to capture authentic, powerful images, even in high-pressure situations. \\n \\nNick’s passion for photography began at age eight, inspired by his father. After university, he pursued photography full-time in 2008, combining his love for the outdoors with his work. While running and cycling are his main focus, he also shoots alternative sports like surfing, sailing, and motorsports. \\n \\nMemorable assignments include the 400km Ultra Gobi in China and the Cape Epic, where he captured the action while riding on the back of a motorbike. Nick’s aspirations include covering events like the Dakar Rally and South Africa's Skyrun. Inspired by photographers such as Kelvin Trautman and Simon Bruty, he continually pushes himself to create impactful work."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014014083293 gid://shopify/Product/9014014410973

item.title: Nicki Friedlein
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641858519261 Nicki Friedlein 2786 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640929382621 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014062219485"] Discover Nicki Friedlein, a Knysna-based textile artist who transforms recycled denim into emotive embroidered artworks. Explore intuitive mixed-media creations and small-scale gallery shows on Latitudes Online. [23891] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicki Friedlein is a textile and thread artist who has worked with fabric and thread for as long as she can remember. Growing up in a family of makers, she was surrounded by sewing, lace-making, knitting, and crocheting—skills passed down from her mother and grandmothers. Embroidery became her own creative expression, and she inherited a deep appreciation for the meditative process of making and the versatility of woven and spun materials. \\nAfter completing a foundation year in fine art and design, she chose to specialize in fashion and textiles, earning a BA (Hons) from Kingston University in London. This led to a fulfilling creative career that spanned both Europe and Asia. Her artwork has since evolved from this experience. She creates portraits and landscapes from previously loved denim clothing—a fabric known for its durability and universal presence across cultures. Using her own photographs as a foundation, she experiments with positive and negative imagery, translating digital captures into tactile, analogue forms. Her abstract works incorporate \"knips,\" the small thread offcuts she diligently saves from sewing and embroidery projects, creating a connection between each piece. More recently, she has been exploring the sculptural possibilities of thread. Each artwork is stitched by hand and on the same trusted sewing machine she has used since she was 18 years old."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014062219485

item.title: Nicky Liebenberg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641859272925 Nicky Liebenberg gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930037981 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here’s the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang. In 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University which has always had a strong history of printmaking. The main focus has never changed - to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network and exhibit together. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Nicky Marais
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641859371229 Nicky Marais gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930136285 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicky Marais (b. 1962) is a Namibian artist, educator and activist. Marais is well-known for her abstract artworks created using a personal vocabulary of abstract forms and colour relationships derived from everyday life as well as the socio-political history of Namibia and icons from around the continent. These forms are often layered using a mixture of stencils and traditional painting techniques. Marais describes her practice as a “constant hunt for significant shapes”, which are subjected to a process of near-obsessive repetition, appearing multiple times in different combinations. \\n \\nMuch of her work explores the relationship between physical and spiritual worlds, which extends into an investigation of the relationship between the tangible and the intangible, the signifier and the signified. Speaking about Marais’ work, Rosa Namises said “Sometimes we are trapped between the gates and the snakes. We have to choose to go through the path of knowledge, to learn what the snakes have to teach us, and not allow ourselves to be trapped by the gates” (2017). \\n \\nMarais is recently retired from an eleven year posting as the Head of Department of Visual Arts at the College of the Arts in Windhoek. As an artist, she has exhibited extensively in Namibia and abroad. In 2017, The National Art Gallery of Namibia hosted a solo exhibition by Marais, titled ‘Presence in Absence’. Her next solo ‘Connections‘ was held at Guns & Rain Gallery in Johannesburg in 2020. Most recently in 2022, the artist participated in the Baker’s Bay Artists’ Retreat Exhibition in Oranjemund, and served as a judge for the Emerging Painters Invitational. \\n \\nCollections: National Art Gallery of Namibia, British Council (Namibia), Goethe-Institut (Namibia), Standard Bank (Namibia), University of Namibia, Omuntu Gardens (Namibia), Museum Würth (Germany), Arts Association Heritage Trust (Namibia), Tulipamwe International Artists Workshop Collection (Namibia), Collection of the government of the Republic of Namibia, Private Collections: UK, Namibia, USA, Germany, South Africa, Kenya, Australia, Austria, France, Italy, Denmark, Finland"}]}]}

[24648,24650,24651,24649,24647,24646] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicky Newman, 57, completed a Journalism and Media degree at Rhodes University as well as an honours in Psychology in the 1980s. She has had the privilege of attending the Maurits Binger Film Institute in Amsterdam and the Berlinale Talent Campus and, more recently, participating in the RMB Talent Unlocked mentorship programme in 2021. \\n Newman started making documentary films and has had a long and fertile career in this medium on camera and as an editor, producer and director. She also lectured at numerous educational institutions. \\nLooking for a quieter medium, Newman revived her love for stills photography and after being placed in various competitions and having her images published, she now sells fine art prints of her photography from galleries and shops in Cape Town. \\nShe is currently working on a book on her series A Place of Water, featuring images from the Sea Point Pavilion public swimming pool. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014098362589 gid://shopify/Product/9014098395357 gid://shopify/Product/9014098428125 gid://shopify/Product/9014098460893 gid://shopify/Product/9014098493661 gid://shopify/Product/9014098526429

item.title: Nico Ras
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861796061 Nico Ras 2806 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930365661 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052454621","gid://shopify/Product/9014052487389"] Explore the innovative printmaking of Nico Ras, a Johannesburg-based artist specializing in silkscreen and etching. Discover his works and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [23620,23621] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nico Ras, born in South Africa and based in Johannesburg, is a bookmaker and printmaker working in a wide range of printmaking techniques and exploring and experimenting with unconventional printing techniques such as dry medium printing. The artist mainly specializes in silkscreen printing and etching. Ras obtained his master’s degree with distinction in Fine Art (2022) at the University of Johannesburg, FADA. The artist explores themes of racial politics, heritage as a young white Afrikaner in South Africa, religious dogmatism, masculinity, and gender expression. Ras works at Artist Proof Studio as an educator and the second-year coordinator."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014052454621 gid://shopify/Product/9014052487389

item.title: Nicola Bailey
item.description: Nicola Bailey 2288 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930431197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014072574173"] [24122] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"b.1965 Durban, South Africa \\n \\n‘My practice engages with ideas of interspecies relationships in the domestic environment, exploring the intimacy and tender nature of companion species and making visible our entangled existence. ‘ \\n \\n- Nicola Bailey 2022 \\n \\n \\nA multi-media interdisciplinary artist, Bailey began her art tuition in 1997 at Ruth Prowse Art College in Cape Town South Africa. Since 2008 she has been part of an art collective founded by Rose Shakinovsky and Claire Gavronsky, collectively known as Rosenclaire, which is based in both Italy and South Africa. \\n \\n'At first blush', Bailey’s first solo, was held in 2014 at The Culture Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa. In 2020 she presented a solo 'And the Animal Responded' for the Cubicle Series at Everard Read in Cape Town, followed in May 2022 by 'The tenderness of ghosts' at Everard Read in Johannesburg. 'A Gentle Entanglement' followed in 2023 at Everard Read Cape Town. \\n \\nLiving and working in Cape Town, Bailey’s artworks are collected both locally and internationally. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014072574173

item.title: Nicola Holgate
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641860550877 Nicola Holgate gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930660573 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicola Holgate is a contemporary figurative painter and a sculptor. Her current practice is focused on medium and process. Nicola relocated to South Africa in 2016 after living in Botswana for 16 years. She spent three years in residencies at Greatmore Studios in Cape town in 2018, August House in Johannesburg in 2019 and 2020, and currently practices from her home studio in Hartbeespoort in the North West Province. \\n \\nShe participated in the RMB Talent Unlocked 2021 program, culminating in a group show at Everard Read \\nCirca Gallery, followed by an online Auction of the works made during the program with Strauss and Co. \\nNicola also placed in the top 20 of the Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards in September 2021. \\n \\nIn her words, “I tell stories as both a painter and a sculptor, currently working with paper as the common element in both forms. Paper has a versatility that allows for wide expression, whether it's a full body paper clay or a delicate hand made sheet. This medium, in all its textures and grain, makes the descriptions possible that telling a good story requires. My recent work has focused on exploring metaphors to describe a state of mind or mood, seeking to spark recognition and extend an invitation to dream into the story the work is telling the viewer.”"}]}]}

item.title: Nicola Roos
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641860813021 Nicola Roos 615 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640930922717 [3169,3170] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicola Roos works in life-size figurative sculptural installations constructed out of recycled rubber tyre tubing. She investigates the origins of civilization and society, as well as the ever-changing politics of national identity, collective memory and cultural belonging in the postcolonial world. The point of reference for her 2015 debut installation, No Man’s Land, was the only black Samurai in recorded history: a Mozambican slave named Yasuke, who was taken from his homeland to serve under an influential shogun in 16th century Japan. His legacy of cross-cultural exchange shifted the focus to this new world state of ethnographic modernity and the transient fixity of culture and tradition. Roos’s interest in colonial history and the commemoration of abstruse individuals was sparked by Yasuke and the myriad of socio-cultural implications that ripple outwards from this remarkable man in Africa and abroad. Her work suggests that this shifting state of culture (and the resulting sense of rootlessness) is much more apparent at the dawn of post-Westernism – a possibly threatening, unstable no man’s land that we find ourselves in today. However, her characters are no longer individuals, but rather elements of an imagined realm beyond official history. They are the embodiment of a local cultural breakdown and a communal future where beliefs, assumptions and knowledge about place and culture can be deconstructed and re-negotiated. Roos has not exhibited in 2019 as she set aside the year for the preparation and creation of artworks for her upcoming Solo exhibition and for Art Fairs. \\n \\nGroup Exhibitions \\n \\n2018 Defying the Narrative: Contemporary Art from Southern and West Africa , Evergold Projects, San \\nFrancisco, USA. \\nRight at the Equator , Depart Foundation, Malibu Village, California, USA. \\n2017 Recent Acquisitions , UNISA Art Gallery, Kgorong Building, Tshwane, South Africa \\nBlack and White , Absolut Art Gallery, Stellenbosch, South Africa \\nTurbine Art Fair , Turbine Hall, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nCape Town Art Fair , Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa \\n2016 Cape Town Art Fair , Cape Town International Convention Centre, South Africa \\nOn Photography, Painting, and Sculpture, Erdmann Contemporary, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2015 Form and Substance, Erdmann Contemporary, Cape Town, South Africa \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013283553501 gid://shopify/Product/9013283619037

item.title: Nicola Taylor
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861075165 Nicola Taylor 1335 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640931086557 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013317861597","gid://shopify/Product/9013318123741","gid://shopify/Product/9013318254813","gid://shopify/Product/9013318353117","gid://shopify/Product/9013318418653","gid://shopify/Product/9014065758429"] [7428,7429] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicola Taylor (b.1984) is a visual artist from South Africa. In the context of belonging and connection, Nicola investigates natural laws and matter taking form. Using paint, animation, light installations and sculpture, she explores the human experience from a quantum perspective, looking at unity and identity at a level where manifestation is still physically undecided. \\n \\nNicola studied in the UK, Italy and South Africa, she has presented five solo exhibitions since 2010, taken part in group shows and collaborations, attended residencies in South Africa and abroad and her work is part of private and public collections."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013317861597 gid://shopify/Product/9013318123741 gid://shopify/Product/9013318254813 gid://shopify/Product/9013318353117 gid://shopify/Product/9013318418653 gid://shopify/Product/9014065758429

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641860026589 Nicolaas Maritz 2756 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640931152093 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014036431069"] Discover the vibrant world of Nicholaas Maritz, an artist born in Pretoria in 1959, known for his expressive works in enamel on board and other mediums. Explore his journey and see his artworks in top South African collections. [23069] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicolaas Maritz (b. 1959, Pretoria), was surrounded by art from a young age due to his artistic family background. He held his first solo show at the Eastern Province of Fine Arts in Port Elizabeth in 1976 and began his fine art studies at the University of Cape Town in 1978. Maritz's works are known for their vibrant colours and expressive quality, ranging from still lifes and landscapes of cats. \\nMaritz is a multi-media artist, with a particular reputation for his works in enamel on board. Maritz lives in Darling, on the West Coast, where he showcases his art at the Maritz Museum, his former home and studio. His works are also featured in esteemed collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, the University of Cape Town, Stellenbosch University, the Pretoria Art Museum, and the Johannesburg Art Gallery."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014036431069

item.title: Nicolas Lambelet Coleman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641860485341 Nicolas Lambelet Coleman 2416 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640931840221 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013855453405"] [19150] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1998 in North Carolina, in the United States to a Swiss mother and African American father, Nicolas Lambelet Coleman is a painter currently based in New York. \\nHis work focuses on portraiture, with a particular emphasis on self-portraiture, a journey to self-discovery, he is reimagining his image and path through his art. \\nHis work has been featured in several exhibitions across the US, recent shows include 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair in New York in 2022 and 33rd September, the Alexandria Museum of Art in Louisiana, 2020 and the Duke University Visual Arts Exhibition in 2020. \\nHis art embodies a subversion of the boundaries that we have constructed around identity and what it means to be human. Much of his identity has been constructed through a process of self-invention to which his art is central. Through vibrant colours, meaningful imagery and the distinctive visual language that he has developed, he projects himself and those around him into a world of his own making. Using clothing, facial features, hairstyles, and other objects, he confuses traditional depictions and understandings of culture and social class. \\nThe artist observes then creates from his daily existence, his surroundings and also explores Black history such as in his ongoing series of portraits named “Reconstruction & Redemption” centred around 19th century African American leaders from the South. Placing humankind at the centre of his oeuvre, his work is an invitation to reflect on different facets of identity, community and humanity."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013855453405

item.title: Nicole Clare Fraser
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861271773 Nicole Clare Fraser 2457 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640932069597 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014014836957"] Discover the work of Nicole Clare Fraser, a Cape Town-based artist specializing in photography that captures built structures, interior spaces, and the nuances of human presence and absence. Explore her exhibitions and teaching expertise in darkroom techniques. [22364] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicole Clare Fraser (b. 1989) is a Cape Town-based image maker and artist whose work focuses on built structures, interior spaces, and objects that evoke human presence, absence, loneliness, and tenderness. Her passion for photography ignited in high school, where she developed a deep appreciation for silver gelatin hand prints through darkroom work. This foundational interest led her to further her studies at Michaelis School of Fine Art, where she earned hr BAFA in 2012 and MFA in 2022. \\nIn addition to her personal artistic practice, Nicole is a photography lecturer specializing in darkroom techniques and printing. She has taught at various secondary and tertiary institutions in Cape Town and has enhanced her expertise through workshops with master printer Dennis Da Silva in Johannesburg. \\nNicole's solo exhibitions include \"Making Space: Traces of Absence, Stillness and the In-Between in Public Spaces\" (2021), which was re-exhibited at Daor Contemporary in 2023, \"untitled (façade)\" (2020), \"a quiet place | a collection of hand-printed silver gelatin prints\" (2018), and \"Garrisons\" (2012)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014014836957

item.title: Nicole Jean McComb
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861337309 Nicole Jean McComb gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640932626653 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"mccomb \\nNicole Jean McComb uses a chaotic collage style subject matter \\nto hide the subtle semiotic clues of the groups of people hidden \\nin her 'full busy life paintings'. McComb paints what she sees in \\nold print media, social media and pictures of scenes from her \\neveryday life living in the Eastern Cape. These images all come \\ntogether in a new collage repainted in oil paint. \\nMcComb's underlying theme under the decorative elements is \\nLeisure Culture. Who is resting and tanning vs working? Often \\nthe white woman is relaxing, while other cultural groups are \\nworking around her. McComb has started to add more animal \\nelements into her work getting closer to Safari Culture. To watch, \\nto rest or to work how does one get to govern their time. Who is \\nallowed to have leisure time? \\nThese subtle cultural stereotypes hidden under highly colourful \\ndecorative elements confuse the viewer into a happy or joyful \\nfeeling when looking at the painting similar to the busyness and \\nbombardment of images that people look at everyday on social \\nmedia. So much imagery that no one can focus on what they \\nare really seeing and experience what they are seeing. \\nMcComb hopes that by creating these new realities as paintings \\nviewers will linger longer on the images and question or piece \\nsome of the new and old relationships placed together in a new \\nway."}]}]}

item.title: Nicole Rafiki
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861599453 Nicole Rafiki gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640932692189 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicole Rafiki, a Norway-based Congolese visual artist who uses symbolism to challenge stereotypes in a critical way. She uses symbolism to re-imagine and challenge the stereotypical depiction of spaces, contexts and the people who are affected by global migration. \\n \\nAccording to the prolific artist, she views her work as a platform for dialogues about identity, fluidity, place, and belonging, adding that, as an artist with a diverse cultural, historic and artistic background, she uses art to inform, engage and heal, because it is too easy to fall into the trap of promoting idealism or clichés, and she makes it a point to be critical and analytical in her work."}]}]}

item.title: Nicolette Geldenhuys
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861173469 Nicolette Geldenhuys gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640932856029 [] Discover the captivating work of Nicolette Geldenhuys, a contemporary artist known for her expressive and thought-provoking creations. Her art explores themes of identity, nature, and emotion through intricate textures and compelling compositions. Explore and collect her unique pieces on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicolette’s art practice is a rich tapestry woven from diverse media, including printmaking, painting, drawing, and collage. Her printmaking focuses on dry point, monotype, and low-toxic etching techniques, reflecting a deep commitment to both craftsmanship and environmental consciousness. \\nThough she learned the printmaking basics from artist Mimi van der Merwe, Nicolette’s journey has been largely self-directed, marked by a continuous exploration of materials and methods. Her current work integrates botanical and sea algae monoprints, water colour, oil and charcoal monotypes, dry point engraving, collagraphs, painting and drawing, revealing a dynamic interplay between technique and emotion. \\nTransitioning from representational to abstract expression, Nicolette now also employs mixed media to convey a profound emotional landscape. Her art seeks to evoke the mystical and divine found within trauma, hope, resilience, and the ordinary. This exploration is deeply personal, rooted in her experiences, particularly the loss of her son, and the ongoing journey of healing and faith. Nicolette’s work draws inspiration from her surroundings, transforming the everyday into a “mystical landscape” where healing, joy, and freedom emerge. Through her art, she aspires to offer viewers a sense of connection and solace in a world often marked by loneliness, inviting them to find belonging and transcendence in her evocative creations."}]}]}

item.title: Nicolette von Wiese
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641861239005 Nicolette von Wiese gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640933183709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013376024797","gid://shopify/Product/9013468823773","gid://shopify/Product/9013468889309","gid://shopify/Product/9013468922077","gid://shopify/Product/9013468954845","gid://shopify/Product/9014116188381","gid://shopify/Product/9014116253917","gid://shopify/Product/9014116286685","gid://shopify/Product/9014116483293","gid://shopify/Product/9014121627869","gid://shopify/Product/9014121890013"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nicolette von Wiese is a mixed media artist working with, inter alia, paper, cloth and thread. Her creative process is primarily centred on a dialogue with materials - both fortuitously found and deliberately sought. Nicolette celebrates and embraces the irregular, carefully giving space for imperfections to simply be. Her tactile, slow, rhythmic and repetitive process is revealed in the final outcome of the work of her hands, with a special ode to her matrilineal lineage through stitching that transcends different generations."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013376024797 gid://shopify/Product/9013468823773 gid://shopify/Product/9013468889309 gid://shopify/Product/9013468922077 gid://shopify/Product/9013468954845 gid://shopify/Product/9014116188381 gid://shopify/Product/9014116253917 gid://shopify/Product/9014116286685 gid://shopify/Product/9014116483293 gid://shopify/Product/9014121627869 gid://shopify/Product/9014121890013

item.title: Nidaa Hussain
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862189277 Nidaa Hussain gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640934232285 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“After dedicating years to theatre performance, I pursued photography, a lifelong passion, at Market Photo Workshop in Newtown, JHB, where I \\ncompleted the Photojournalism and Documentary Photography Programme in 2012. \\n \\nI am particularly interested in social documentary and street photography. Awed by the resilience of the human spirit, I am driven a nd inspired by my \\npassion for people and the undeniable, sometimes complicated beauty of our daily existence, often in seemingly unlikely places. I am drawn to stories of social upliftment, lived experiences of women and the marginalised, and issues of identity. I am currently working as a freelance photographer and videographer.”"}]}]}

item.title: Nina Holmes
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862287581 Nina Holmes gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640934625501 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013324218589", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324316893", "gid://shopify/Product/9013324415197"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The process of altering or intervening to create work is a significant quality of Nina Holmes’ practice and she often includes pieces of material or repurposed upholstery. She likens this process-based approach to “surrealist automatism”, while also allowing for the inevitable influence of found images, photographs and the borrowing of techniques and inspirations from other paintings. Working loosely and around expectations Holme’s paintings are never limited to canvas and oil. Instead they push the formal, rigid canon of painting. \\n \\nShe enjoys working on multiple paintings at the same time, with work spread out across her studio in Woodstock. The working process is occasionally accompanied by a grand symphonic soundtrack and sometimes with silence. There is careful thinking and intense working through various influences and concepts. \\n \\nHolmes is a Cape Town-based artist who completed her Post Graduate Diploma (2017) with distinction at the Michaelis School of Fine Art. She has had two solo exhibitions with Eclectica Contemporary and was featured in the 2020 Investec Cape Town Art Fair solo section. \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013324120285 gid://shopify/Product/9013324218589 gid://shopify/Product/9013324316893 gid://shopify/Product/9013324415197

item.title: Nikhil Tricam
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862254813 Nikhil Tricam gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640934428893 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nikhil Tricam is a South African artist based between Johannesburg and Durban. Tricam trained as an architect and his work focuses on the human relationships and experiences formed within, and against, the back-drop of the urban realm - with a focus on large scale ink and acrylic gestural works. Tricam draws on his experience in the realm of design to inform his narratives, while absorbing elements of contemporary art, street art and abstract expressionism to root his compositions in time.This body of work investigates the experience of our bodies within the physical spatial realm we inhabit. The figures, objects and marks are memories of elements inherent to our understanding of habitat. Geometric forms become caves, mountains or buildings. Bold, dark strokes are vines, branches or electrical infrastructure in the urban wilderness.Through the complex geometric and spatial interplay of these elements, we are invited to contemplate our experience within our habitat."}]}]}

item.title: Nina Jacobson
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641862320349 Nina Jacobson gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640934822109 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nina Jacobson currently lives and works in Johannesburg, completing her 4th year of studying Fine Arts at Wits. In her own practice, she is primarily interested in the techniques of printmaking and painting. Her experience of life is largely in colours and sounds which she relay in her artwork. Her work has been very influenced by how one can experience physical space and is characterised by distortions because of her own experience with dissociation. \\n \\nIn 2019, Nina was featured in Turbine’s PAPER exhibition, and apprenticed under Tracey Rose for the Kampala Biennale. \\nIn 2021, Nina was awarded the merit prize for the Wits Young Artist Award, and shortlisted for the Arts Thread x Gucci Global Design Graduate Show."}]}]}

[23712] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Njabulo Hlophe (b. 1996 in Johannesburg, South Africa) is an illustrator and visual artist based in Johannesburg operating under the pseudonym Dirty Native Chief. Njabulo completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in visual communication at the Stellenbosch Academy of Design and Photography in the Western Cape, where he conceptualized and created Studio Dirty Native. \\n \\nNjabulo’s work is can be seen as a response to observations about human life, and not only as a means to scrutinize and critique the human experience but rather a means to explore it and how he exists in relation to that particular experience as a young black cultural hybrid walking the contemporary landscape."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013413314781 gid://shopify/Product/9014055698653

item.title: Nkabinde Mpendulo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863041245 Nkabinde Mpendulo 2864 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640935477469 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014115533021","gid://shopify/Product/9014115598557","gid://shopify/Product/9014115631325"] Discover the captivating work of Nkabinde Mpendulo, a South African artist exploring themes of identity, memory, and cultural expression through evocative visual forms. Explore available artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [25144,25145,25146,25147,25143] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Kwa-Zulu Natal, in March 2003, Nkabinde Mpendulo is a Johannesburg-based artist working across various mediums to explore systemic and epistemic violence in contemporary civilization. Nkabinde approaches this concept by looking at how institutionalized education and industrialization undermine relationships between humans, land, and language in the form of urbanization. In this way, Nkabinde comments on the remnants of Western oppressive powers over the “primitive nations” or the “Other”. \\nNkabinde completed his primary and secondary education in rural Kwa-Zulu Natal and began his tertiary education at BAT Center. He holds a bachelor’s degree in visual arts from the University of Johannesburg, obtained in 2024. Nkabinde participated in various group shows, including a painting exhibition in Fox Wood House in JHB in 2022; a printmaking show with the Pretoria Association of Art in 2023; the UJ Visual Art 3rd year grad show, and the UJ FADA show at the University of Johannesburg in 2024."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014115533021 gid://shopify/Product/9014115598557 gid://shopify/Product/9014115631325

They describe their work as a queer meditation on transience, aesthetic sociology, and redemptive futurologies to explores what individuality is, what collectivity is, and what it means to share space. \\nNkhensani continues to expand in their praxis, synthesizing mediums to evoke new passages of materiality rooted in counteractive ways of seeing and modes of hearing."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014048030941 gid://shopify/Product/9014048063709 gid://shopify/Product/9014048162013 gid://shopify/Product/9014048194781 gid://shopify/Product/9014048227549

item.title: Nkhensani Rinhlampfu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863499997 Nkhensani Rinhlampfu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640935575773 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1988 in Limpopo, Nkhensani Rihlampfu matriculated at Nylstroom Hoerskool in a town called Modimolle. He then went to study Fine and Applied Arts at the Tshwane University of Technology in Pretoria, where he obtained a B-Tech in Fine and Applied Arts, majoring in printmaking and sculpture. \\n \\nThroughout his career, Nkhensani has been involved in several art programs, a number of exhibitions and produced many commissioned pieces. One of the commissions was a painting that he made for Constitutional Hill in Johannesburg. \\n \\nNkhensani works in multidisciplinary materials, which include sculpture, painting, and drawing. Nkhensani has exhibited in The Absa L’Atelier, Grahamstown Arts Festival, Pretoria Art Museum, Turbine Art Fair, NeoEmergence Centurion Art Gallery, Arts Alive, The Jo’burg-Jo’burg Show, and the FNB Joburg Art Fair. \\n \\nIn addition, Nkhensani has had solo exhibitions at mmArtHouse and was a Turbine feature artist. Nkhensani has worked at Workhorse Bronze Foundry, where they were involved in casting multiple Artists' culptures including William Kentridge’s bronze pieces. He has also worked with other prominent South African artists such as Nandipha Mntambo, Nelson Makamo, and Louis Olivier. (Source: https://mssimone.co.za/artists/nkhensani-rihlampfu)"}]}]}

item.title: Nkoali Nawa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863532765 Nkoali Nawa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640935936221 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Initially a mineworker, Nawa is understandably passionate about the daily struggles that face impoverished South Africans. He depicts the harsh existence that mineworkers have to adapt to, as well as the plights of rural women whose husbands have relocated to the urban areas in search of work. Nawa depicts the daily tasks and responsibilities that fill the lives of these individuals - their daily tasks almost becoming sacred rituals. Everyday scenes are represented in a personal, intimate manner, revealing the artist’s deep understanding of the challenges facing these communities. To document the moment, Nawa takes photographs and works from the image telling their stories through his art. \\n \\nNawa completed a B-Tech Fine Art, Free State Technikon, in 2001. He was a visiting artist at the Bag Factory, Thupelo International and Greatmore Studios and a national finalist in the 2003 Brett Kebble Awards, Cape Town. A large mural of his dominates a building in the inner city of Johannesburg. His solo exhibition held at the AVA Gallery Cape Town in 2008. Nawa has partaken in numerous group exhibitions locally and abroad. In 2018 he was part of the Nando’s Creative Exchange culminating in Rituals, at AVA Gallery, Cape Town and the Bashu Uhuru Freedom Festival. His work is held in corporate collections globally."}]}]}

item.title: Nkosinathi Thomas Ngulube
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863794909 Nkosinathi Thomas Ngulube gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640936067293 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nkosinathii Thomas Ngulube considers himself a sculptor before a painter, and a poet before a writer. \\n \\nArtist's Statement \\n \\n\"The reduction of visual fact to the surface of my work, that lies over various layers and textures, which represent, on a larger scale, my life’s journey, socially, politically and spiritually. I use found objects to convey my stories through their sentimental value that resonates to my spirituality, in sculpture as a medium yet in my paintings as a metaphor for texture, being and feel. I am encapsulated in interesting life stories of a withered object lying in it and over it. The mystery of a found object resonates with my emotions, feelings are thus executed as a synonym to these layers. l choose to use paper to paint on for its tenderness which pars the same in me, hessian which allows me to bring both softness and hardness, and sculpture which allows me to express the raw hardness of my nature and these objects that have outlived their weaker subordinates. The equality status that l par with my materials personifies us as one body, inseparable kinship that asserts our invaluable connection in speaking the same language. The relativity negates religiousness but confirms the individuals’ invaluable spirituality. The height of my creative depth’s passion insinuates, through symbolic metaphors, representational of male and female, a consummation-type of relationship with every piece l ecstatically create, in the formation of each complex individualism. The uncontrolled trashy messiness of my materials evokes/invokes beauty as my signature that l compliment with a personal thumbprint as a seal.\" \\n \\nNKOSINATHI THOMAS NGULUBE \\n \\nContemporary Sculptor, Painter + Writer. \\n \\n2020 \\n \\nTHE SOLOTIST: A solo show, Thomarts Gallery, Sandton \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR: Illovo, Johannesburg \\n \\nLATITUDES ART FAIR: Sandton, Johannesburg \\n \\nTHE OTHER ART FAIR: Barker Hangar, Los Angeles 2019 \\n \\nIntimations: TURBINE Art Fair, Illovo, Johannesburg \\n \\nTHE OTHER ART FAIR: Barker Hangar, Los Angeles \\n \\nUNIQUE: A group show. Thomarts Gallery, Sandton \\n \\n2018 \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR: Turbine Hall, Johannesburg \\n \\nSTART FAIR: Saatchi Gallery, London 2017 \\n \\nABSTRACTIONS, Thomarts Gallery, Cape Town \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR, Turbine Hall, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\nKKNK ARTS FESTIVAL, Oudtshoorn, South Africa \\n \\nSILENT CONVERSATIONS, Thomarts Gallery, Cape Town. \\n \\nCOMMEMORATIVES, Group project \\n \\n THOMARTS GALLERY 2016 \\n \\nCAPE TOWN ART FAIR, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\nRESURRECTION, THOMARTS GALLERY, Cape Town, South Africa \\n \\nSTART FAIR, London \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR, Turbine Hall, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n \\nTHAT ART FAIR, Woodstock, South Africa \\n \\nKKNK ARTS FESTIVAL, Oudtshoorn, South Africa \\n \\n2015 \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR, Turbine Hall, South Africa \\n \\n2014 \\n \\nTURBINE ART FAIR, Turbine Hall,South Africa \\n \\n2013 \\n \\nBLACK LIKE US, Watercolour Society, South Africa \\n \\nTRANSLATIONS, Thomarts Gallery, Johannesburg ,South Africa \\n \\n2012 \\n \\nBLACK LIKE US, Watercolour Society, South Africa \\n \\nDUO EXHIBITION(with Samson Mnisi),Thomarts Gallery, Johannesbur g, South Africa 2011 \\n \\nBLACK LIKE US, Watercolour Society, South Africa \\n \\nMUSEUMSQUARTIER, Vienna, Austria \\n \\nUNITY GALLERY, Newtown, South Africa \\n \\nWHITEHOUSE GALLERY, Oaklands, South Africa \\n \\nCOMMISSIONS \\n \\n2018 \\n \\nSTANDARD BANK BRONZE SCULPTURE (https://youtu.be/2ZxfXvxRU R4) 2012 ANC SENTENNIAL CELEBRATION, South africa \\n \\nINVESTEC GOLF TROPHY (Collaboration with Marko Cianfanelli) \\n \\nWELDING DESIGN COURSE, (teaching corporate clients diys though w elding / an after hours hobby ) Tool Share Studio, South Africa \\n \\n2010 \\n \\nCASCOLAND PUBLIC ART , Drill Hall, South Africa \\n \\nSYSPRO SCULPTURE, South Africa \\n \\n2009 \\n \\nPUBLIC FUNCTIONAL ART, Hillbrow, Berea and Parktown municipality public parks, Johannesburg, South Africa"}]}]}

item.title: Nkosinathi Quwe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863696605 Nkosinathi Quwe 536 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640936001757 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013302657245","gid://shopify/Product/9013303443677","gid://shopify/Product/9013470822621"] [5132,5325,17916] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nkosinathi “Nathi” Quwe sees his art as a calling. He is a visual messenger - telling stories in his work that have been told before but by bringing in new elements and layers, he connects differently with his viewer. His inspiration comes from religious rituals, listening to jazz and from South Africa’s troubled past where he feels it is his duty to address these ills and injustices through his work. Quwe paints on different mediums, working primarily on canvas but also on fabric where he works with a fashion label. He is a spiritual person and to him, it is important that we embrace who we are. \\n \\nQuwe was born in a township in Butterworth (Eastern Cape) but now lives and works in a studio at Victoria Yards, Johannesburg. He obtained a B-Tech in Fine Art (Visual Art) and then went on to complete an additional year at the University of Johannesburg in 2005 where he majored in painting. In 2006 he received the Ekurhuleni Art Award in Printmaking and was one of 30 Top Finalists in the SA Taxi Award Competition (2016). Humanity Revisited was a solo exhibition of his held at Eyethu Gallery in Soweto in 2015. Quwe has participated in a number of group exhibitions. In 2018 he was part of the Nando’s Creative Exchange culminating in exhibitions at AVA Gallery, Cape Town and the Bashu Uhuru Freedom Festival. His work appears in several corporate collections globally."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013302657245 gid://shopify/Product/9013303443677 gid://shopify/Product/9013470822621

item.title: Nkuli Mlangeni
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641863958749 Nkuli Mlangeni gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640936427741 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nkuli Mlangeni, is a creative entrepreneur, dreamer, traveler and maker of things. She is the founder of the The Ninevites a collaborative platform and design studio, most well-known for the handcrafted Sankara Rug, which won Design Indaba’s Most Beautiful Object in South Africa in 2017. \\n \\nThe Ninevites seeks to explore under-told narratives of life from Southern Africa using creativity, design and imagery. It is a celebration of black aesthetics. And, keeps pushing to tell African stories in ways that reflect their vast beauty and invention. \\n \\nNkuli studied social innovation and creative leadership at the Kaospilots school of innovation and design in Switzerland. And, she has participated in numerous local and international arts exhibitions and artist residencies. \\n \\nShe is passionate about black culture, youth development and documenting textiles from the continent."}]}]}

item.title: Noa Hall
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864024285 Noa Hall 2822 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640936624349 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014055633117"] Discover the work of Noa Hall, a South African visual artist exploring the relationship between images and the human body through multimedia, photography, and performance. Featured graduate from the University of the Witwatersrand. [23710] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Noa Hall is a South African artist, she was born in 2000 in the city of Johannesburg. After graduating with an honours degree in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand in 2023 she, along with some fellow graduates, founded the artist colllective and studio space House of Special Things where she continues to practice and collaborate. \\nHer work employs a range of mediums and techniques, traversing between video art, painting, some printmaking and installation building. Hall enjoys creating large-scale experiential artworks. Her painting practice consists of a curiosity around the graphic mark. \\nShe draws inspiration from the versatility of image within social media, cartoons, the internet, manga, comic books, posters and images confronted in everyday life. She conceives of her work as claustrophobic mind-maps or orientation devices. Surfaces \\nonto which she can measures different objects and representations against one another externally from herself. \\nShe is interested in the predicament of inhabiting a body that is bound within space, located amongst many other objects and beings - embedded within varying systems, biological, interpersonal, social, technological, cybernetic and environmental. She uses her \\nwork as a way to investigate and study this experience. Her work therefore often deals with space, proximity, intimacy and suffering."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014055633117

item.title: Nobukho Nqaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864057053 Nobukho Nqaba 587 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640937050333 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013435367645","gid://shopify/Product/9013435400413","gid://shopify/Product/9013435465949"] [16045,16046,16047] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nobukho Nqaba was born in Butterworth located in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. At the age six, she and her family moved to Grabouw in the Western Cape and later attended Luhlaza High School in Cape Town. She is a graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town(UCT) where she majored in photography and was mentored by Svea Josephy and Jean Brundrit (2012). In 2012, she was awarded the Tierney Fellowship and was the recipient of reGeneration3, a photography focused initiative by the Musee de l’Elysee. Nqaba holds a Post Graduate Certificate in Education Visual Art and Theory from the UCT (2013). \\n \\nShe has embarked on several teaching endeavours through her role as Visual Art and Digital Photography Educator at the Peter Clarke Art Centre. Nqaba is currently a Lecturer of Photography at the Red & Yellow Creative School of Business. \\n \\nNobukho Nqaba graduated from the Michaelis school of Fine Art (Cape Town, South Africa) and was the 2012 Tierney Fellowship recipient. In 2015 she was one of only two photographers from Africa selected for reGeneration3 – a travelling exhibition and publication. Nqaba has exhibited in a number of international exhibitions, including Photo Lagos (2015) and Duro Olowu’s Making and Unmaking exhibition at Camden Arts Centre, London (2016). \\n \\nNqaba has exhibited widely including at the SOLAR Festival (Brazil: 2018); FITE Festival of Textiles: Clermont Ferrand (France: 2018); Africa Africa (Milan, Italy: 2018); GETOXOPHOTO (Spain: 2017); China Afrika (Germany: 2017); Also Known As Africa: Contemporary Art and Design Fair (France: 2016); Making & Unmaking: An exhibition at the Camden Art Centre (U.K.: 2016); reGeneration3 (UK, USA, Mexico and Switzerland: 2015-16); Designing Africa 3.0 (Spain: 2016), LagosPhoto Festival (Nigeria: 2015) and Against Time, Bamako Encounters (Bamako, Mali: 2015)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013435367645 gid://shopify/Product/9013435400413 gid://shopify/Product/9013435465949

item.title: Nola Ayoola
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864515805 Nola Ayoola 2510 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640937214173 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013941600477","gid://shopify/Product/9013941633245"] [19991,19990,19992] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nola Ayoola (b. 1992) is a multidisciplinary artist whose works are her visual journal. \\n \\nThrough sculptures, portraiture, woven and cut out abstract compositions they encapsulate the philosophy that ‘you cannot understand what you cannot pull apart’. Her works are an observation of her heritage and its profound impact on her identity by storytelling through varying lenses in which she sees and imagines, while connecting to and interpreting objects. \\n \\nNola’s work is both theoretically and physically layered as a core voice, it's a study of dismantling and assembling, while telling stories of interconnection and the synchronisation between the past, present and what is to come. She describes her work as reticulations of the state of dreams and experiences. \\nHighlighting the varying complexities of identity, she is heavily triggered by hyper- sensory processing of sensitivity and synesthesia - naturally connecting sounds, colours and emotions to each other, it allows her to capture essence. \\n \\nNola’s visual languages pay homage to traditional African craftsmanship practices, - hand dyed indigo to carved block printing and weaving. The process of hand printing layers (an ode to Yoruba carving techniques and traditional Adire textiles) holds equal importance to the subjects. \\n \\nWhilst constructing/ deconstructing; her works celebrate representation and shared narratives. She is nurturing recurring themes of her interpretations of womanhood, social constructs of gender, human interaction with communities and environments, Yoruba tradition, spirituality, individualism, auras and the seen/ unseen."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013941600477 gid://shopify/Product/9013941633245

item.title: Nolan Oswald Dennis
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641864089821 Nolan Oswald Dennis gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640937312477 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nolan Oswald Dennis (b. 1988, Zambia) is a para-disciplinary artist from Johannesburg, South Africa. Their practice explores what they call ‘a black consciousness of space’: the material and metaphysical conditions of decolonization. \\nDennis’ work questions the politics of space (and time) through a system-specific, rather than site-specific approach. They are concerned with the hidden structures that pre-determine the limits of our social and political imagination. Through a language of diagrams, drawings and models they explore a hidden landscape of systematic and structural conditions that organise our political sub-terrain. This sub-space is framed by systems which transverse multiple realms (technical, spiritual economic, psychological, etc) and therefore Dennis’ work can be seen as an attempt to stitch these, sometime opposed, sometimes complimentary, systems together. To read technological systems alongside spiritual systems, to combine political fictions with science fiction."}]}]}

item.title: Norman Catherine
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641867170013 Norman Catherine 300 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640940949725 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013293351133", "gid://shopify/Product/9013293416669", "gid://shopify/Product/9013293482205", "gid://shopify/Product/9013850341597", "gid://shopify/Product/9013943369949", "gid://shopify/Product/9013943435485", "gid://shopify/Product/9014018769117", "gid://shopify/Product/9014068969693", "gid://shopify/Product/9014069067997", "gid://shopify/Product/9014069100765", "gid://shopify/Product/9014069166301", "gid://shopify/Product/9014076309725"] [4273,20113,18950,4274,4272,24182,20114,24073,24074,24075,24076,24077,4271] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Norman Catherine was born in 1949 in East London, South Africa. \\n \\nHe works in various media including painting, sculpture, mixed media, printmaking, wall hangings and bronze and has been an influence on many younger artists. \\n \\nHis prodigious output has been engaging art enthusiasts since 1969 when he held his first solo exhibition in Johannesburg. He has exhibited extensively in South Africa and internationally. His work is included in most South African Art Museums and Corporate collections as well as in MOMA (Museum of Modern Art) and the Brooklyn Museum, both in NYC, USA. \\n \\n \\n \\nCatherine’s art imbibes a dystopian vision of the socio-political landscape that informs his psyche. History, horror, crime, conflict, psychoses, politics & pathologies serve as stimuli for his creative output that vacillates between the macabre and the comic, between a gasp and a giggle. He conveys his cynical vision through a juxtaposition of dark and light sensibilities veering between an internal hallucinatory realm and literal commentary on the material world. There are no easy classifications for the genre of his work suffice to say that he rebels against any dogma or rigid definition."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013293351133 gid://shopify/Product/9013293383901 gid://shopify/Product/9013293416669 gid://shopify/Product/9013293482205 gid://shopify/Product/9013850341597 gid://shopify/Product/9013943369949 gid://shopify/Product/9013943435485 gid://shopify/Product/9014018769117 gid://shopify/Product/9014068969693 gid://shopify/Product/9014069067997 gid://shopify/Product/9014069100765 gid://shopify/Product/9014069166301 gid://shopify/Product/9014076309725

item.title: Nothando Chiwanga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641867890909 Nothando Chiwanga 1539 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640941113565 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013385986269", "gid://shopify/Product/9013386019037", "gid://shopify/Product/9013386182877", "gid://shopify/Product/9013435531485", "gid://shopify/Product/9013435597021", "gid://shopify/Product/9013435629789"] [13594,16053,13596,13593,13595,16052,16051,13597] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nothando Chiwanga, born on May 6, 1997, in Harare, Zimbabwe, is a multidisciplinary artist known for her work in performance art, photography, and collage. She attended the National Gallery of Zimbabwe's School of Visual Arts and Design, from which she graduated in 2019. Chiwanga's work is deeply influenced by her personal experiences and reflections on womanhood, tradition, and change. \\nShe uses her body as a medium to explore themes of education, food, bereavement, and domestic life, highlighting the complexities of young womanhood in a society where traditional values are evolving. Her art incorporates an expressionist and performative style, with vivid use of light, pose, and environment in her portraiture, giving her work a distinct sense of realism. \\nChiwanga has exhibited in several prominent group shows, including New Signatures and Green Shoots exhibitions, the Notes for Tomorrow traveling exhibition, and Young Contemporary 2022 at the National Museum in Lagos. Her international experience extends to the Madzimbawe Group Show at Akka Project in Dubai. She has completed artist residencies at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe in 2020 and Releartsfoundation in Lagos in 2022. In addition to her exhibitions and residencies, Chiwanga has participated in various workshops, including realism with John Kotze, performance art with Sithembile Msezane, and art ethics with Julius Mushambadope. \\nHer work documents the changing perceptions of women and positions womanhood as a political subject, examining its transformation within the context of modern society."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013385986269 gid://shopify/Product/9013386019037 gid://shopify/Product/9013386051805 gid://shopify/Product/9013386084573 gid://shopify/Product/9013386182877 gid://shopify/Product/9013435531485 gid://shopify/Product/9013435597021 gid://shopify/Product/9013435629789

Originally a filmmaker, Ntate blended his storytelling skills with his ever-growing love for African digital and fine art, bringing out the perfect marriage of his two passions. \\nNtate’s evolution as a storyteller has allowed him to introduce some of the most forsaken, and ordinary stories of African people as beautiful and unforgettable works of art. His use of digital and fine art mediums to tell these stories has allowed Ntate to challenge the norms of African storytelling. He pays homage to the traditional tone of African storytelling of the past, and to how African history, culture and tradition was passed on through story. Having worked with some of South Africa’s leading creatives, Ntate continues to etch himself as one of Africa’s greatest prospects. \\n“Art and storytelling are cousins. They are at grandmother’s house. Her name is Africa.” - Ntate Phakela"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013400305885 gid://shopify/Product/9013400502493 gid://shopify/Product/9014003368157 gid://shopify/Product/9133221773533
