item.title: Phindile Mamba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641889583325 Phindile Mamba gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640977322205 [] Phindile Mamba {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phindile Mamba is a self-taught artist from Mbabane, who has been painting full time since 2104 after participating in the Livi laBomake - Women's Voices project run by Yebo ArtReach. Her work is in private art collections around the world. She exhibited at Art Joburg in 2019. Her work is also in the US Embassy in Eswatini, featured in a book ; On Balance- A woman from each African country and she was recently selected by The World Bank Art program to feature in an online exhibition, We are Afrika: the Power of Women and Youth. \\n \\n“Most of my paintings are about women, I see them struggling and living a very painful life. Women are abused because they don’t have the power to fight and this touches me deeply and shows in many of my paintings. I also explore happier topics as some women do live a happy life with their families. I also explore the ideas that women can do everything a man does and have the power. People in Eswatini must start trusting women and giving them respect and power. But women must also make themselves powerful!” \\n \\nDespite tackling difficult subjects relating to women’s oppression, Phindile uses charming and colourful images to illustrate her strong point of view. Animals feature often; good people are symbolised as cats, doves or sheep and dangerous ones as hyenas or snakes. Flowers, butterflies, and nature bring Phindile much joy in her life and are in most paintings. The husband in the one painting is featured as a leopard, but not a threatening one, now docile and content being carried around by a strong wife. Even in The Leader, the woman has her fist raised demanding power, but the cute sheep soften the message. Phindile is softly spoken and humble but one should not underestimate her power and strength as like many women in a patriarchal culture like Eswatini, she holds the society together and speaks out through her art and community work."}]}]}

item.title: Phillipe Koudjina
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641889059037 Phillipe Koudjina gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640977256669 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"In the 1960s, he was the photographer of the Independence of Republic of Niger, capturing the spirit of freedom, hope and carelessness of an entire generation. Philippe has acquired a great reputation which has largely crossed the borders of Niger. Numerous exhibitions and publications have been dedicated to him. Highlighted by French publication Revue Noire and by French-Nigerien organisation Contrechamps, his work has been the subject of numerous exhibitions and continues to influence African photographers. \\nHe was born in Togo, moved to Benin and at 17 years of age he migrated to Niger until his time of death. Philippe Koudjina passed away on May 29, 2014. \\nTo continue to promote his work, it was decided by the Koudjina family, to explore the multitude of his unpublished photographs, to restore them in the respect of the hard conditions they have been through and to offer them to institutional and private collectors. \\nIt is the choice of the Koudjina family that new photographs will be “Fine Art” quality prints, in inkjet printing on Hahnemühle paper, done by the Fotodart workshop of David Attal and Hervé Pain in Paris, France."}]}]}

item.title: Phumulani Ntuli
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641890599133 Phumulani Ntuli 393 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640978993373 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013310980317", "gid://shopify/Product/9013355348189", "gid://shopify/Product/9013397323997", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008119517", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008152285", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008185053", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008217821", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008250589", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008283357", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008316125", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008348893", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008381661", "gid://shopify/Product/9014008414429"] Phumulani Ntuli (b. 1986, Soweto) is an acclaimed multidisciplinary artist whose work spans artistic research, sculpture, video installations, and performative practices. His art critically engages with archives, surveillance, and historical narratives, striving to illuminate history's gaps and silences. Ntuli's practice invites viewers to reconsider historical and contemporary narratives, drawing connections between personal heritage and sociopolitical issues. [22037,11001,22044,22040,22038,22039,22041,22042,22043,22034,22035,22036,14030] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phumulani Ntuli (b. 1986, Soweto) is an acclaimed multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans artistic research, sculpture, video installations, and performative practices. His work critically engages with notions of archives, surveillance, and historical narratives, striving to illuminate history's gaps, silences, and remnants. Ntuli holds a Masters in Fine Arts - Art Public Sphere from ECAV in Switzerland, where he was awarded the Prix-excellence for his ongoing research project Permutations of an Event \\nNtuli's artistic process is characterized by a convergence of documentation, image, and visual engagement, creating spaces that challenge viewers to reconsider historical and contemporary narratives. He consistently engages diverse audiences, drawing connections between personal heritage and broader sociopolitical issues, particularly within the context of decoloniality. \\nHis career includes notable exhibitions and performances, such as the 2016 Kampala Biennale in Uganda curated by Elise Atangana, the Bone Performance Festival in Bern, Switzerland, and the Act Festival in Geneva, Basel, Sierra, and Zurich. Ntuli has also participated in residencies at the Fondazione Pisteletto in Italy and the Alps Art Academy in Switzerland. \\n \\nIn his own words, Ntuli explores the collision between reality and fantasy, using this intersection to investigate memory and its fragmented, unreliable nature. His recent solo work, \"Kunanela iphuzu emafini / Echoes of the Point Cloud,\" debuted at the FNB Art Joburg Fair in 2023, incorporating mixed media collages and unique works on paper. The project delves into South African motion picture history, merging it with contemporary data and artificial intelligence to re-contextualize past narratives within a changing socio-political landscape. \\nNtuli's practice often employs collage techniques, both digital and manual, to create 'pseudo-reality' that challenges preconceptions and invites alternative perspectives. His work, deeply rooted in his South African experience, is both personal and powerfully political, aiming to observe, analyze, reflect, and bring people together. \\nImage credit: Sublime Photography and Design"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013310914781 gid://shopify/Product/9013310980317 gid://shopify/Product/9013355348189 gid://shopify/Product/9013397323997 gid://shopify/Product/9014008119517 gid://shopify/Product/9014008152285 gid://shopify/Product/9014008185053 gid://shopify/Product/9014008217821 gid://shopify/Product/9014008250589 gid://shopify/Product/9014008283357 gid://shopify/Product/9014008316125 gid://shopify/Product/9014008348893 gid://shopify/Product/9014008381661 gid://shopify/Product/9014008414429 gid://shopify/Product/9014008447197

item.title: Phumzile Buthelezi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641892237533 Phumzile Buthelezi 611 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640979091677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014072475869", "gid://shopify/Product/9014072508637"] [25418,3152,25419,24120,25420,24121] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phumzile Buthelezi (b. 1976) is a fine artist that graduated at Artist Proof Studio with print making. She always had an affinity with art, starting from an age as young as 13 years old where she won third prize in a drawing competition. She has always been crafty and was mostly occupied with embroidery, crocheting, knitting, bead-work and fabric painting in her teenage years. Her style is easily distinguishable, with organic forms and shapes and a colourful palette. Her work extends the qualities of nature; as beautiful, life-giving, and a formidable force which also examples female energy of strength, beauty and nurturing qualities – exhibiting the feminine not as an idolization and mystical far-fetched concept but as a real force that shapes us and our and understanding of the world and ourselves related to the world. The works are templates of wisdom, that offer a reflection with the maternal relationships in our lives. \\nShe is currently working on multiple projects, including a sculpture/illustration exhibition with Candice Berman and exhibited work in the 2020 Turbine Art Fair amongst many others. Her most recent exhibition is Ambiguous with MMArthouse which opened on the 15th of August 2020."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013283193053 gid://shopify/Product/9014072475869 gid://shopify/Product/9014072508637

item.title: Phuong Hoang
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641894498525 Phuong Hoang gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640979747037 [] Discover the creative world of Phuong Hoang, a Vietnamese painter and visual storyteller. Her work, rich in emotions and bright geometrical forms, focuses on the underprivileged and has been exhibited at major European photo festivals. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Phuong Hoang is a Vietnamese painter, photographer, educator, and visual storyteller. From a young age, she has expressed her perception of the world through art. Emotions are crucial in her work, often featuring geometrical forms and bright colors. Growing up in 1990s Hanoi, Hoang developed an interest in using photography and multimedia to tell stories, particularly about the underprivileged. \\nWith over 15 years of journalism experience, Phuong Hoang employs various techniques such as interviews, research, and data analysis to explore her subjects conceptually, critically, and humorously. \\nPhuong Hoang believes in humanity, self-awareness, and self-reflection. Since 2022, she has been teaching photography, visual narratology, and experimental media at the University of Europe for Applied Sciences. In the same year, she joined the collective Unbinding Histories. \\nHer work has been exhibited at various photo festivals in Europe, including the European Month of Photography Berlin, Lange Nacht im Museum Hamburg, Backlight Photo Festival in Finland, and OFF Bratislava for Academy in Slovakia."}]}]}

item.title: Pierre Le Riche
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641894531293 Pierre Le Riche gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640979943645 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Pierre le Riche (b.1986, Port Elizabeth) is a conceptual artist with a practice spanning many mediums and techniques, and widely recognised for his dynamic use of string and textiles. He uses thread as structural element – both a connection point, an unravelling, and a space demarcation – and evokes a complex set of ready-made associations through material and colour use: exploring permeable gender roles and liminal identities. Weaving a complex set of associations, the threads running through his practice tap into a rich seam of metaphor and ambiguity. \\nHe has participated in many projects and exhibitions in South Africa and abroad, and has worked with the likes of Power Play, Trenery, Cartier and Daimler. He has recently showed adaptations of his Rainbow Room installation in the United States of America and the People's Republic of China; both being part of traveling exhibitions. Le Riche holds a Master of Fine Arts degree from the University of Cape Town's Michaelis School of Fine Art."}]}]}

item.title: Pieter Hugo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641895940317 Pieter Hugo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640980369629 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Pieter Hugo (born 1976 in Johannesburg) is a photographic artist living in Cape Town. \\nMajor museum solo exhibitions have taken place at The Hague Museum of Photography, Musée de l’Elysée in Lausanne, Ludwig Museum in Budapest, Fotografiska in Stockholm, MAXXI in Rome and the Institute of Modern Art Brisbane, among others. \\nHugo has participated in numerous group exhibitions at institutions including Tate Modern, the Folkwang Museum, Fundação Calouste Gulbenkian, and the São Paulo Bienal. His work is represented in prominent public and private collections, among them the Museum of Modern Art, V&A Museum, San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, Metropolitan Museum of Modern Art, J Paul Getty Museum, Walther Collection, Deutsche Börse Group, Folkwang Museum and Huis Marseille. Hugo received the Discovery Award at the Rencontres d’Arles Festival and the KLM Paul Huf Award in 2008, the Seydou Keita Award at the Rencontres de Bamako African Photography Biennial in 2011, and was shortlisted for the Deutsche Börse Photography Prize 2012."}]}]}

item.title: Piloya Irene
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641896071389 Piloya Irene 1931 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640980697309 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013387231453", "gid://shopify/Product/9013387362525", "gid://shopify/Product/9013388509405", "gid://shopify/Product/9013393850589", "gid://shopify/Product/9013393883357", "gid://shopify/Product/9013393948893", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394112733", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394145501", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394178269", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394211037", "gid://shopify/Product/9013394309341"] [13831,13829,13833,13827,13826,13825,13824,13820,13819,13611,13610,13624] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Piloya Irene is a multi-form conceptual artist currently based in Kumasi, Ghana. Piloya uses sculpture, painting and film to explore personal experience of displacement and its effects, memory and history in relation to place, identity and belonging. She has a Post Graduate Diploma in Art Education from Kyambogo University 2019, Bachelor's Degree in Industrial Fine Art and Design from Uganda Christian University 2016 and is currently pursuing a Master’s program in Painting and Sculpture at Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Kumasi-Ghana. \\nPiloya participated in documenta fifteen as part of the blaxTERLINES collective that collaborated with Gudskul collective in Kassel, Germany. She was part of the GASTHOFF 2022 in Frankfurt Germany, where blaxTERLINES worked with Staedelschule and various international artists. In 2021, she worked with CAI, a USA based organization that empowers the girl child in various parts of the world as an art consultant. In 2020, Piloya exhibited her painting “Fearless” at the UWONET annual celebrations of women’s day in Uganda. Piloya is now part of UNDER GROUND, Kampala, an art space run by Nantume Violet, the organizer of the international arts exchange programme “Travel somewhere nice” that visited Ghana last year for an exchange program, where Piloya was among the artists that time. In 2018, her paintings featured the Okuki-women rising collectively through art reflecting on gender related struggles and successes. Piloya has worked with Wajuku artists collective on a research project for the Research Centre Society of Groningen in Nairobi, Kenya in 2017. She was part of the History in Progress Uganda collective art project that depicted the \"Ekifananyi Kya Muteesa\". In Ebifananyi 8 \"The king pictured by many '' curated by Andrea Stultiens and exhibited at FotoMuseum Antwerp, Belgium and Makerere art gallery in 2017. Piloya participated in the \"Surfaces,\" a conceptual Drawing workshop and exhibition at Afriart gallery, Kampala 2017. She participated in the Parallel Portraits Project of course 2016 under the theme \"we, people in transition,\" exhibited at Academie Minerva Praediniussingel in Groningen, Netherlands. She exhibited her work \"Rebirth\" during the first Annual member's exhibition of 32° East; Ugandan Arts Trust in 2016 at Humurah Hotel, Kampala. She has showcased her work at Bayimba International festival of the Arts 2016 and Milege World music festival in 2016 and 2017. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013387231453 gid://shopify/Product/9013387362525 gid://shopify/Product/9013388509405 gid://shopify/Product/9013393850589 gid://shopify/Product/9013393883357 gid://shopify/Product/9013393948893 gid://shopify/Product/9013394112733 gid://shopify/Product/9013394145501 gid://shopify/Product/9013394178269 gid://shopify/Product/9013394211037 gid://shopify/Product/9013394309341 gid://shopify/Product/9013394374877

item.title: Plácido 'Pocho' Guimaraes
item.description: Plácido 'Pocho' Guimaraes ["gid://shopify/Product/9013936062685","gid://shopify/Product/9013936095453","gid://shopify/Product/9013936128221"] Plácido 'Pocho' Guimaraes {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Plácido “Pocho” Guimaraes (b. Malabo, Equatorial Guinea) carries on the tradition of Equatorial Guinean textile craft practice, which has been passed down from generation to generation in local communities and Bubi culture. Using dance, symbols, and experiences to enrich his current works, he contemporizes these traditions, reconnecting with his cultural and family roots. Guimaraes is a disciple of Josep Grau-Garriga and uses the high heddle technique rather than traditional looms. The unusual materials he incorporates into his work are fabrics of African origin; old newspapers and waste materials, as well as objects found in the cities and natural environments around Malabo and Madrid. These found residual elements carry personal or family meanings, with each of the works he produces referring to a specific theme and reality of his immediate environment: his political dissent, family customs, and rituals. Touch and the tactile nature of his work are highly important elements to help narrate the personal stories of Bubi culture, so relevant to his history. \\n \\nEquatorial Guinea achieved independence from Spain in 1968 when Guimaraes was 17 years old. His grandfather, Francisco Malabo, recognised as the last Bubi king, was in charge of his education until he was 10 when he was admitted to the La Salle school in Malabo. There, he was tutored by Teodoro Obiang Nguema (now President of Equatorial Guinea). The events and the political figures involved in the independence and the dictatorship of Macías Nguema (former President of Equatorial Guinea), marked his life politically. The persecution by Nguema directly implicated Guimaraes, whose Father was imprisoned, tortured, and killed by the regime in 1971. Guimaraes sees his country submerged under the current dictatorship of President Obiang, whose rule is considered one of the most repressive in the world. Wanting to escape from these inequalities encountered in his home country, he has been largely self-exiled in Spain since he was 19 years old. \\n \\nHis political and cultural concerns led him to Kyiv in 1975, where he studied Urban Planning. Upon returning to Spain, he studied Fine Arts in Valencia, exploring many visual languages and collaborations in the world of dance, theatre, and cinema. Pocho Guimaraes has been participating in exhibitions since 1984 and currently resides in Spain, though had returned to Equatorial Guinea in 2005, where he lived on the island of Bioko until 2019, undergoing the traditional ceremonies that he was unable to perform due to his early departure."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013936062685 gid://shopify/Product/9013936095453 gid://shopify/Product/9013936128221

item.title: Prince Galla Gnohité
item.description: Prince Galla Gnohité gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640981156061 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013454733533","gid://shopify/Product/9013454766301","gid://shopify/Product/9013454864605","gid://shopify/Product/9013454930141","gid://shopify/Product/9013454962909","gid://shopify/Product/9013455093981","gid://shopify/Product/9013455192285","gid://shopify/Product/9013455323357"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1989 in Ivory Coast. \\nLives and works in Abidjan, Ivory Coast. \\n \\nThe theme of “street children” — a phenomenon that is both common and often scandalous — can be found in the artistic creation of visual artists from a number of countries. \\n \\nIn the Ivory Coast, this was crystallized in the political and institutional crisis which destabilized the social structures of this country for several years and swarms of children and adolescents into the streets, condemned to live and to “play” at war, but with real weapons. We call these children “microbes” or “grazers”. \\n \\nFortunately, peace has returned, weapons are now toys and the children of poor neighborhoods are, like all children in the world, in search of age appropriate pleasures and diversions, their ingenuity making up for their lack of resources. How the faces and attitudes of these children have changed! \\nWe no longer see hunger or fear, but simply the innocence of children playing, sometimes marked by solemnity. Children whose favorite playground is the street, for want of another. \\n \\nIt is possible to trace commonalities as to the variations on this theme, which goes from ABOUDIA to Armand BOUA, via YEANZI, but beyond the theme, the treatment reserved by each differs significantly…it is not possible to confuse their works. \\n \\nThe children of GNOHITE are no longer afraid, they have fun and delight in the joys of their youth with all the spontaneity of this blessed time of life, carefree and cheerful, despite the ugliness of the world around them. \\n \\nThe artist insists on capturing and preserving this happiness, this fullness, by referring to education, to the preparation of the adults of tomorrow, who had the chance, like him, thanks to his family environment, to enjoy a balanced education, who put his personal development first and did not interfere with his artistic aspirations. \\n \\nIn a swirl of large flat areas of primary and saturated colors (blue and yellow, mainly) whose playful character is reinforced by a myriad of dots and small circles of color, the main characters are sketched, suggested, schematized and perfectly recognizable for those who have seen children playing in the African sun and dust. \\n \\nPrince Galla GNOHITE considers Grobli ZIRIGNON his teacher and from him he borrowed the technique of scraping and washing out paint that was projected onto the canvas using a pipette, an instrument familiar to children. \\n \\nThe bicycle and its inevitable accidents and flat tires, the worn tires that we push, hoops for adults, to give the impression of driving a car, football, of course, but also struggle, or for the more relaxed, reading; a list of the daytime activities, themes of GNOHITE’s work, which sometimes may be disrupted by the attack of a stray dog! \\n \\nThis work is distinguished from that of its predecessors by that happy vitality that we perceive from the start and which makes you want to dance in the dust and lead children from all over the world in the farandole. \\n \\nBecause, beyond the technical mastery, the chosen subject and its treatment, there emerges an infinite tenderness in Prince Galla GNOHITE’s works, a form of nostalgia for the artist from a carefree and happy time in his life seen through the prism of transpositions. \\n \\nHaving trained from 2000 to 2004 at the Regional Center of Arts and Crafts of Abengourou (CRAMA) in the Ivory Coast, Prince Galla GNOHITE, who is barely thirty years old, has acquired an indisputable technical mastery of his subjects, of the desired and obtained effects and of the composition of his works. He completed his training with the artist Youssouf De Kimbirila dit Le Quetzal, who believes GNOHITE shows great promise and a brilliant future. \\n \\nGNOHITE also displays his talents in sculpture, design and decoration, and works in abstract, figurative and surrealist styles. \\n \\nThe curators were not mistaken in selecting Prince Galla GNOHITE for important artistic events in the Ivory Coast, even though he was not yet twenty years old. His success has continued, receiving extensive attention for his exhibitions in Europe as well as other African countries. \\n \\nThis very sunny exhibition, in the grayness of our days, gives us color, light and comfort that we so badly need. \\n \\nSylvain Sankale \\nArt Critic \\nDakar, Senegal \\nFebruary 28, 2021"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013454733533 gid://shopify/Product/9013454766301 gid://shopify/Product/9013454864605 gid://shopify/Product/9013454930141 gid://shopify/Product/9013454962909 gid://shopify/Product/9013455093981 gid://shopify/Product/9013455192285 gid://shopify/Product/9013455323357

item.title: Prince Timi Kakandar
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641896300765 Prince Timi Kakandar 679 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640981221597 [2591] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\\nTimi Kakandar is one of Nigeria's renowned contemporary artists and painters, he began his creative career soon after graduating from the University of Port Harcourt, Rivers State, Nigeria in 1999. Kakandar uses painting, drawing and collage to explore his fascination with the human form in relationship to the challenges, joy, and social political issues that emanate from living and working within the African space. His recent work exudes a profound intensity of bright raw colours and gestural lines that infuse a presence which powerfully engage the viewer. He reveals an ability in the composition of human forms with dramatic colours reminiscent of Fauvism. \\n \\nTimi Kakandar is one of Nigeria's prolific contemporary artist with a keen following internationally and in his native country and has had four Solo Exhibitions and over 30 group Exhibitions worldwide. He lives and works in Lagos, where he is a member of the Society Of Nigerian Artists (SNA) Lagos Chapter."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013279949021

item.title: Princia Matungulu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641896333533 Princia Matungulu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640981287133 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013846704349"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Princia \\nMatungulu was born in 1999 in Lubumbashi, DR Congo She lives and works in Johannesburg, South Africa \\nPrincia recently graduated from the University of the Witwatersrand with a Bachelor of Fine Arts ( degree Being a \\nCongolese born immigrant navigating through the South African landscape, she draws from her background and identity by \\nmeans of constant shared processes and conversations with her mother Princia practice is a combination of weaving, \\nsculpture and storytelling whereby the approach towards the materiality, the intricacy of the weaving process and the \\nresulting sculpture bears record of a personal, inferred or imagined history She employs weaving processes as a form of \\nsilent protest a means of understanding Congolese traditions, norms and values of ‘ womanhood, which sometimes \\noverlap and intersect with those of women from the African diaspora thus exploring themes such as intimacy, sacredness, \\ndress and work in her artistic practice \\nPrincia \\nparticipated and was a finalist for the Wits Young Artist Award 2021 exhibited at The Point of Order in a joint \\nexhibition in part fulfillment of her degree 2021 She has also exhibited work at the Holy Art Gallery in London, UK 2020 \\nand her series of work Nouveaux Mémoire Vieux Pagne (New Memory Old Cloth) was part of Archive of Forgetfulness’ \\nGroup exhibition with the Goethe Institut South Africa 2020"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013846704349

item.title: Prisca Akua Kwaning
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641897382109 Prisca Akua Kwaning gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640981418205 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013404336349"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Prisca Akua Kwaning (1989) was lucky enough to find her very own creative studio in her hometown of Amsterdam. Prisca is a abstract expressionist and gestural artist of Ghanaian-Dutch heritage. \\n \\nThe act of painting can be liberating, it can be healing, a way to shed old layers and carve your own path. After going through a difficult time, Claiming her space was exactly what she needed and painting the rooms she was about to inhabit, turned out to be addictive. Once she was done with the walls, Prisca moved on to large canvases: spaces in their own right. \\n \\nShe used the same paint buckets, poured some of the pigment onto the frame and let loose to create her immersive, gestural works. To her, painting represents freedom. To be by herself, no need to analyze her feelings, right there; in her very own space."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013404336349

item.title: Prudence Chimutuwah
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641897808093 Prudence Chimutuwah gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640983843037 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Prudence Chimutuwah is a Zimbabwean contemporary visual artist whose work highlights the everyday lives and socio-economic struggles of women in patriarchal societies. Raised in Chitungwiza, she was inspired by local sculptors and female artists like Seminar Mpofu and Colleen Madamombe. Prudence studied painting and sculpture at the National Gallery Visual Arts School from 2009 to 2011. \\nWhile initially interested in sculpture, Prudence found the field to be male-dominated, which presented challenges for her. In 2015, she discovered a passion for collage, which allowed her to creatively incorporate recycled materials, including decommissioned Zimbabwean banknotes, magazines, old novels, and newspapers. Her work also integrates elements of contemporary African fashion, text, and symbols, adding depth to her artistic narratives. \\nPrudence's art primarily centers on women's roles in society, exploring themes of economic ambition, spirituality, and resilience. She is particularly interested in the struggles of young female graduates who face uncertain futures. Through her art, Prudence hopes to inspire and empower women, narrating their evolving roles in the world. \\nPrudence has participated in numerous major group exhibitions, including at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe and international art fairs such as AKKA in France. She has also completed residencies at Greatmore Studios in Cape Town and participated in the Young Contemporary Artist residency in Nigeria. Her solo exhibition, Purple Rhythm, was nominated for Best Exhibition at the National Arts Merit Awards (NAMA) in 2020. Additionally, she was shortlisted as a finalist in the ILO Green Enterprise competition for her mixed media artwork and received an Award of Merit for Originality from Gallery Delta in 2020. Her works can be found in embassies, diplomats' homes, and private collections both in Zimbabwe and around the world."}]}]}

Purchase his dynamic pieces online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Pule Ratsoma (b. 1990) is a South African printmaker and artist who divides his time between Johannesburg, where he trained and worked at Artist Proof Studio, and Limpopo. His artistic journey began in 2013, and he has since developed a distinctive style characterised by gestural and expressive marks that resemble code or tangled language. This unique approach to visual storytelling enables him to communicate complex themes and narratives through his art. \\nRatsoma's artistic practice is heavily influenced by his personal experiences and the vibrant artistic community at Artist Proof Studio. He combines traditional printmaking techniques with contemporary themes, resulting in dynamic compositions that are both visually striking and thought-provoking. His work delves deeply into themes of human conditions and societal issues, often drawing inspiration from his observations and life experiences. \\nRatsoma has exhibited widely in South Africa, participating in notable shows such as the Turbine Art Fair. His commitment to art extends beyond creation; he is passionate about transferring art skills to younger artists in rural areas, townships, and communities. By doing so, he aims to ensure the growth and accessibility of art education, fostering creative expression in areas where it is most needed."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014013427933 gid://shopify/Product/9014013460701 gid://shopify/Product/9014013493469 gid://shopify/Product/9014064054493

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641897906397 Puleng Mongale 364 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640984465629 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013290598621", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290631389", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290664157", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290762461", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290795229", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290860765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013290893533", "gid://shopify/Product/9013327790301", "gid://shopify/Product/9013361115357", "gid://shopify/Product/9013997732061", "gid://shopify/Product/9013997797597"] [8145,4065,4073,4074,21492,4064,4063,21493,21495,4071,4070,4069] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Puleng Mongale (b. 1991) is a contemporary visual artist based in Durban, South Africa, specialising in photography and digital media. Since the inception of her art practice, Mongale has used her creative expression to probe into her subconscious to process and articulate her lived experiences. \\nOver the years, her artistic journey has evolved into a reflective exploration of themes that resonate with her as a young African woman in South Africa. Mongale’s work explores themes related to spirituality, belonging, identity, and womanhood. \\nMongale’s work has been shown in multiple group exhibitions including Africa Foto Fair, Abidjan (2023); Abadali Group Show, Johannesburg (2022); The Fold Group Show, London (2021); Beyond Group Show, Cologne (2021); Terrains of Possibility at the Rele Gallery in Lagos (2021); Heaven on Earth, an online solo exhibition with Doyle Wham x Latitudes (2021); and Ambiguous, a group exhibition with mmArthouse (2020). \\nIn an ever-evolving society, art serves as Mongale's resistance, a tool to define her narrative on her terms."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013290565853 gid://shopify/Product/9013290598621 gid://shopify/Product/9013290631389 gid://shopify/Product/9013290664157 gid://shopify/Product/9013290762461 gid://shopify/Product/9013290795229 gid://shopify/Product/9013290860765 gid://shopify/Product/9013290893533 gid://shopify/Product/9013327790301 gid://shopify/Product/9013361115357 gid://shopify/Product/9013997732061 gid://shopify/Product/9013997797597

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641898627293 Purnaa Deb gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640984662237 [] Explore the evocative artwork of Purnaa Deb, a contemporary artist known for her deeply introspective and culturally rich pieces. Discover and collect her original creations on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Purnaa Deb grew up in Kolkata, India, and completed her academic art education (under- and post-graduate degrees) in Printmaking from the faculty of Visual Art, Rabindra Bharati University, India. \\nPurnaa has been awarded Gold Medal for her BFA in 2010; and a Certificate of Merit at the annual exhibition of MFA in 2012. Purnaa also received a Fellowship in Printmaking Department at the National Lalit Kala Academy of the Government of India for the year 2014-2015. \\nBesides participating in several group exhibitions and community-based art activities, Purnaa has been working as an art educator and engaged in different schools and institutions, teaching different methods of arts and creative practice using interactive communicating tools. The artist moved to Johannesburg, South Africa in 2015 and worked as an intern at David Krut Projects, Johannesburg, where she received the professional printmaking studio experience that elevated her overall technical knowledge. Purnaa also worked as a printmaking teacher at Artist Proof Studios, Johannesburg from 2017, providing basic understanding and training in different printmaking technics to the students. \\nPurnaa is committed to her printmaking practice and has participated in several group shows and art fairs as a fellow member of The Printing girls since 2018. Her artworks have been acquired for international collections and one of her pieces featured in the comic magazine published by the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany in 2015. In 2021 Purnaa was awarded the Printmaking Residency with the National Arts Festival in Grahamstown/ Makhanda."}]}]}

item.title: QAQAMBILE Beading Collective
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641899348189 QAQAMBILE Beading Collective gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985120989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013435826397","gid://shopify/Product/9013435859165"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Cape Town-based beading, art and crafts collective Qaqambile and run by women crafters, artists and maker are the masterminds informing premiere artworks that feature beading by leading artists from across South Africa. \\nFor the exhibition 'Embodying Her, 2023' the women have for first time in their history as a collective the women feature artworks made by themselves and that brings to life their own life stories through beading. \\nThe master-beaders of Cape Town partnered with iconic artist and visual activist Zanele Muholi to collborate on the production of several works in the series, and produced beautiful beaded-paintings of their own - works that powerfully convey their journey of economic striving towards independence as women."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013435826397 gid://shopify/Product/9013435859165

item.title: Qeren Creates
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641899610333 Qeren Creates gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985186525 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"(b. 1995) is a multidisciplinary artist from Nelson Mandela Bay who now lives and works in Cape Town.Town. \\nHis work explores the externalizing of the inner worlds of feeling and thought. Qeren employs a range of characters to denote different parts of the mind and how they interact with each other. \\nQuern’s best-known character is Imaginary Friend, a protagonist who represents relentless hope and child-like ambition. \\nGrowing up in various cities, towns and villages in Southern Africa, Qeren embraced art from a young age, not only as a solitary pastime but also as a way to connect with new friends in every new place. Punk-rock, skate culture, hip-hop and street art dominated Qeren’s early exploration of the arts, with a deep love for painting, digital artwork and animation developing later on. \\nQeren’s work spans virtual and digital mediums, bringing together fine art, prints and collectables and have found form in painting and sculpture, as well as animated, 3D, virtual- and augmented reality works. \\nIntentional meaning is paramount to Qeren’s art practice. Every piece has an intended but incomplete message, inviting the viewer to interpret, project, and ultimately complete the shared pool of meaning. \\nQeren has exhibited locally and his first online international solo exhibition was held in October 2022 in collaboration with award winning virtual reality company, ROOOM AG, in Jena, Germany."}]}]}

item.title: Queezy Babaz
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641900200157 Queezy Babaz 2633 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985448669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014003400925","gid://shopify/Product/9014003466461","gid://shopify/Product/9014003564765","gid://shopify/Product/9014003597533","gid://shopify/Product/9014003630301","gid://shopify/Product/9014003695837","gid://shopify/Product/9014003728605","gid://shopify/Product/9014003761373","gid://shopify/Product/9014003826909","gid://shopify/Product/9014003859677","gid://shopify/Product/9014003925213"] [21709,21700,21712,21703,21698,21702,21707,21708,21711,21710,21704] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Queezy Babaz (b. 1992) is a multidisciplinary artist whose practice spans fine art, fashion, and performance. Through mediums such as printmaking, videography, drag performances, and DJ sets, Queezy constructs immersive worlds that blend fantasy with radical social commentary. Their work challenges and redefines the experiences of being queer and coloured in South Africa, deconstructing notions of masculinity, sexuality, and the body. Themes of gender norms and identity politics are central to their practice, where artistic craftsmanship meets authenticity to create pieces that are visually captivating and socially provocative. \\n \\nQueezy's interactive artworks foster spaces of protest, empowerment, and celebration, disrupting normative narrative. Trained in pottery, painting, sculpture, and graphic design at Belgravia Art School, Queezy later earned a BTech in Fashion Design with a distinction in specialized clothing technology from Cape Peninsula University of Technology. Their performances have been featured at institutions such a Gallery MOMO, Zeitz MOCAA, AVA Gallery, World Art Gallery, and Norval Foundation, while her work has gained international recognition in publications including I-D Magazine, New York Times, NATAAL, Paper Magazine, and Vogue Italia. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014003400925 gid://shopify/Product/9014003466461 gid://shopify/Product/9014003564765 gid://shopify/Product/9014003597533 gid://shopify/Product/9014003630301 gid://shopify/Product/9014003695837 gid://shopify/Product/9014003728605 gid://shopify/Product/9014003761373 gid://shopify/Product/9014003826909 gid://shopify/Product/9014003859677 gid://shopify/Product/9014003925213

item.title: Qhamanande Maswana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641899741405 Qhamanande Maswana gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985383133 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"“I work intently to produce work that successfully conveys issues around beauty and other struggles witnessed on the continent, drawing inspiration from my surroundings and people I interact with – I focus on articulating the beauty and the strength they possess. The people depicted in my work often come from economically depressed communities, so I paint their skin with purple hues, because purple is often associated with royalty, luxury, and power - it also represents meanings of wealth, creativity, wisdom, dignity, and magic. I see it as my duty as an artist who grew up in those spaces to recreate the image of these bodies in a new light, one that portrays the royalty I see inside of them.” \\n \\nQhamanande is a young artist whose painted portraits speak to the beauty, life challenges and spirituality in Africa. \\nBorn in King William’s Town, Eastern Cape, Qhama studied art at Lovedale College and then obtained a Diploma in Fine Art from the University of Fort Hare, Alice, in 2015. He was commissioned to produce work for the university’s centenary celebration, and worked at the Steve Biko Foundation as volunteer. With detailed brushwork, he combines acrylic and oil paints and creates striking imagery, imparting hidden folklore and culture religion on viewers, but with a modern and colourful aspect. As an African, he wants his work to show the strength of his people and their descendancy from royalty. Maswana draws from his rural upbringing and respect shown to culture, customs and nature and describes his aim with art is to ‘breathe life into a long-forgotten past’. \\n \\nHe has showcased his artworks at group exhibitions at The Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Art Museum in Port Elizabeth, Ann Bryant Art Gallery in East London, Galerie NOKO in Port Elizabeth, The National Arts Festival in Grahamstown, Eclectica Design Art in Cape Town and MMart House in Johannesburg, to name a few. \\n \\n“Qhama Maswana draws inspiration from his surroundings and people articulating the beauty and strength they possess and often show people caught in a particular moment.” \\n- Hanneke Benade, Artist Mentor"}]}]}

item.title: Quinten E Williams
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641900331229 Quinten E Williams gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640985546973 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Quinten Edward Williams attended the University of the Witwatersrand, from which he holds a Bachelors of Art in Fine Arts (2010) and a Masters Degree in Fine Arts (2014). \\nHe lives and works in Johannesburg and experiments with various media, including painting and print."}]}]}

item.title: r1
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641901773021 r1 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641020543197 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"r1 is one of South Africa's leading street artists and is based in Johannesburg He is a multi-layered artist that over the years has used various materials and combined them through inventive ways to create site­specific works in an attempt to find a: visual conversation. His visual language is the re-combination of his environment, documenting it and then giving the viewer a different perspective on how we see our day-to-day surroundings. His work has developed not just as mere conceptual street art pieces, but hos transformed into permanent public artworks and exhibited works. \\n \\nAlthough his work has developed into multi-facets, he is renowned for his signature geometric style which reverts to the chevron design. This design is commonly found in rood-safety signs and equipment (ie: chevron street signs and barrier tape). r1 takes these simple and recognisable geometric symbols and re-appropriates them into a new narrative. He's particularly inspired by the chevron designs and finds ways to manipulate and develop its design to reveal a unique visual aesthetic His use of these materials and designs ore directly linked to his exploration and relationship of how a city like Johannesburg is structured with its seen and unseen boundaries. \\n \\nEffortlessly blending these designs, his current practice seeks to combine elements with contemporary visual referents into new forms that reveal on impressive complexity attention to detail. Creating balance and harmony from symmetrical repetitions, a build-up of layers and techniques of visual illusion, his multi-layered patterned compositions produce a poetic rhythm (vibration) that plays with the viewer's perception and the (multiple) possibilities of interpretation. \\n \\nBesides the numerous public art interventions he hos accomplished in South Africa, he has also been creating in various countries and also been showcasing his work internationally as port of the street art community including Le Voyage à Nantes Festival, Fronce (20 16), Urban Art l'>iennole, Germany (20 17), Nosimi Art Festival, Azerbaijan, 2018."}]}]}

item.title: Ra-ees Saiet

He graduated from the Michealis School of fine art in 2014 and has exhibited and sold work internationally since then, despite not practicing art consistently over this time. \\n \\nHis work looks at themes of presentation, authenticity and reproduction in a digital and cultural space. How these spaces and modes of production intersect and who validates them are points of interest in worlds and objects built from reference, duplication, repetition and personal context."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013398536413 gid://shopify/Product/9013398569181

item.title: Rachel Seidu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641901871325 Rachel Seidu 2747 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986464477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014033613021"] Discover the powerful visual storytelling of Rachel Seidu, a contemporary photographer and artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through striking imagery, Seidu explores themes of identity, culture, and social narratives, capturing moments that challenge and inspire. [22993] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rachel Seidu (b.1997) is a Lagos-based photographer and filmmaker whose work delves into the intimate and emotional aspects of human experience. \\n With a focus on capturing personal narratives, Seidu uses both conceptual and documentary techniques to create portraits that resonate with simplicity and depth. Her images invite viewers into the interior lives of her subjects, emphasizing authenticity and raw emotion, often exploring themes of identity, freedom, renewal, and self-expression. \\nHer photography serves as a meditation on identity, healing, and connection. Seidu’s work is marked by its quiet, affective power, engaging deeply with the emotions and stories of her subjects. \\nIn 2021, Seidu photographed the cover of the Booker Prize-shortlisted novel We Need New Names by NoViolet Bulawayo. She was shortlisted for the James Barnor Prize and Yaa Asantewaa Prize. In 2023, she collaborated with Yves Saint Laurent for a fanzine and exhibition at the Saint Laurent Rive Droite stores in Paris and Los Angeles. Additionally, she was selected for the Tremplin Jeunes Talents at the Planches Contact Photography Festival and residency in Deauville, France \\nHer exhibitions include Festival Planches contact (2024, Deauville), Freedom Multitudes (2024, Houston), YSL Rive Droite (2023, Paris/LA), Awa nibi (2023, Lagos/Hamburg), and Let’s Take a Moment (2022, Lagos). Seidu is a member of Black Women Photographers and the African Photojournalism Database."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014033613021

item.title: Rahma Naili
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641901936861 Rahma Naili gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986530013 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rahma Naili is a visual artist born in 1991 in Bizerte. Graduated from the Higher Institute of Fine Arts of Tunis (master of research in plastic arts in 2016), she chose engraving as her main discipline but she also practices drawing and painting. \\n \\nHer artistic approach is based on an aesthetic of fragility where she seeks to reach what remains hidden behind appearances, the soul of objects, and the people around her. She uses paper to convey the ephemeral part that inhabits each of us. She makes it undergo all sorts of experiences (collage, painting, embossing, engraving, printing, ...) in the image of those that each person goes through in life. \\n \\nShe participated in a one-year artistic residency at the Cité International des Arts in Paris (2018-2019). Young international artist, she has taken part in numerous exhibitions in Tunisia: at the Contemporary Art Days of Carthage, at the El Birou Gallery, at the Alain Nadaud Gallery, at the International Feminist Art Festival of Tunis. More recently, her work was presented at the second edition of the 21x21 fair held in Barcelona."}]}]}

item.title: Rai Gandra
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902035165 Rai Gandra 314 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986595549 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013292466397"] [4240] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rai Gandra is a Brazilian artist based in Rio de Janeiro. He graduated in Cinema and Audiovisual from the Federal University of Recôncavo da Bahia (UFRB). Gandra has been the creator, organizer and curator of the \"Mostra Universitária de curtas LGBT\" – a short film festival – that in two editions circulates 8 Brazilian states and 1 exhibition in Germany. He was a producer in Janela LGBTQI + - Diversity festival with various artistic languages (music, theater, dance, visual arts and cinema), which had Marielle Franco as a jury member. Gandra is one of the authors of the book Bixinho in partnership with the German/South African publisher Iwalewabooks. The book portrays themes of love, desire and sex in Rio de Janeiro through photographs."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013292466397

item.title: Ralph Ndawo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902297309 Ralph Ndawo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986661085 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South African photographer Ralph Ndawo (1932 – 1980) began his career as a darkroom assistant, also freelancing for the Golden City Post and Drum magazine. He rose to become Chief Photographer of the Post after joining the paper in 1966 and, when it closed in 1971, was transferred to Drum. In 1972, he joined the Rand Daily Mail – working for the publication from 1978 until his untimely death. Ndawo covered important events in South African history during this period, including the 1976 protests, Steve Biko’s funeral, and the Mandela family. His legacy also reflects feature and social documentary work, some which was published in Staffrider magazine. Ndawo’s work has recently been archived by the PLP."}]}]}

item.title: Raja Oshi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902100701 Raja Oshi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986628317 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Raja Oshi is a Sudanese artist now living in South Africa. Graduated from the College of Fine and Applied Art at the Sudanese University of Science and Technology in Khartoum in 1994, her journey of diaspora, and that of her family, has taken her through Norway, Wales, France and Egypt. From 2004 to present, she has settled in Pietermaritzburg where she completed a postgraduate diploma in Fine Art from the Centre for Visual Arts at the University of KwaZulu-Natal in 2006, raised a family and has continued to paint.Raja’s work is inspired by her life context and what is happening in the world. Living in Sudan, her early work depicts the situation of Sudanese women and things going on in their lives. Being part of this moved her and this came out in her paintings. Her work from that period carries the pain and the desire to change things. \\n \\n?Her recent, depicts a new moment. Emerging from the desert literally and figuratively, as an artist, she wants to find something different in her art and in the process of making it - to get out of that world of pain, to experience, enjoy and find happiness in the painting and colour at this time in her life. Her work explores colour, texture, shape and design, drawing from the rich profusion of colour in her South African environment. Her workweaves and overlaps different materials and layers of paint to reveal the colours coming up from underneath. As she finds her own signature, this body of work radiates a stilled centeredness, a vibrant visual record of this time in her life. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Ramotoana Mokgomme
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902690525 Ramotoana Mokgomme gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986824925 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ramotoana was born in a small village called Indemaker, located in the Limpopo province. Having been exposed to art since the age of 5, his interest grew when he started primary school at Kgobokang Primary School. Ramotoana's art career was properly nurtured under his former teacher and mentor, Simon Moshapo. \\nAfter moving to Johannesburg in 2009, he established his career as a full-time artist. In 2012, he enrolled at Johannesburg Art Gallery for printmaking lessons. \\nIn 2019, he worked at Artist Proof Studio and Constitution Hill (South Africa) at Chepape Makgato Studio as an assistant. He then went on to graduate from Artist Proof in 2019. \\nHe is currently a co-founder of So & Mo Basement Art Studio based in Parkhurst Recreation Centre, where he has been working with Mario Soares to specialise in printmaking, painting and collage. \\n\""}]}]}

item.title: Ramarutha Makoba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902657757 Ramarutha Makoba 329 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640986693853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052552925","gid://shopify/Product/9014052585693"] Explore the impactful artwork of Ramarutha Makoba, a South African artist known for using trees as metaphors for growth, knowledge, and community. His prints explore themes of personal and societal development. Makoba’s work has been exhibited internationally, and he plays an active role in art education and outreach through various community projects. [23623,23624] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ramarutha Makoba (b. 1984, Soweto, Johannesburg) is a talented artist who began his artistic journey at the age of 13 when he began attending art classes at a local community center. He refined his skills through workshops at the Johannesburg Art Gallery and completed a two-year course at FUBA (Federated Union of Black Artists). Makoba joined Artist Proof Studio in 2004, earning certificates of excellence in his first twp years, and completed his third year of professional printmaking in 2007. \\nMakoba’s artwork often uses trees as a metaphor for family and community life. He believes trees symbolize growth, knowledge, and productivity. The roots represent one's origins, while the stem and branches signify growth and success. His art reflects how communities come together for shade, support, and problem-solving under the tree, with the goal of inspiring individuals to relate to his work and bring about positive change in the world. \\nMakoba’s works have been displayed in numerous exhibitions, including the District Six 50th Commemoration Print Exchange (2016), solo exhibitions like “Change The World” (2016) at Art Room, and group shows at David Krut Art Gallery and Lizamore & Associates. Besides his practice as a full-time artist, Makoba is deeply involved in education and community outreach, facilitating art programs through the Artist Proof Studio’s ‘Artist in Arks’ and the Little Artists School Project in Berea."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014052552925 gid://shopify/Product/9014052585693

item.title: Rana Kadry
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902756061 Rana Kadry gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987218141 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rana Kadry is an Egyptian/Canadian illustrator based in Stockholm. Her practice involves illustration, moving images and poetry. She is interested in questions related to women’s empowerment, sexuality, migration and representation. Her working method is mostly based on experimental and intuitive processes. She graduated with a master’s degree in visual communication from Konstfack in Stockholm and holds a bachelor degree in scenography from The Faculty of Fine Arts in Cairo. She is currently studying a research based course about black feminism at The Royal Institute of Arts in Stockholm."}]}]}

item.title: Ranji Mangcu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902788829 Ranji Mangcu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987283677 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I am a South African artist and creative director, specializing in photography. In December 2020, I completed my Bachelor of Fine Art degree at the University of Cape Town’s Michaelis School of Fine Art. In my work, I use portraiture to engage with questions of identity and the role of art history and photographic archives in defining humanity’s current relationship with imagery. In my existing bodies of work, \"NOMDAKAZANA\" (2019), \"Ulwalamano/Kinship\" (2020) and \"IQHINA\" (2020), I have and continue to foreground the importance of documenting and archiving Black experience, reflexivity, kinship and connection. My 4th Year body of work \"IQHINA\" (2020), was awarded the highly prestigious Michaelis Prize for the \"Most Outstanding Body of Work by a Student in the Year\", as well as the Simon Gerson Prize. This project formed a process of re-tracing and retrieving my lineages and identity, which required me to contend with a South African post-memory that is defined by the consequences of colonial disruption. In its essence, IQHINA is a body of work about two South African families from Ginsberg Township in the Eastern Cape, and how they have formed and performed identity and kept their own histories intact in the face of the grand narratives of colonial erasure and Apartheid."}]}]}

item.title: Raphaela Cocotos
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641902952669 Raphaela Cocotos gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987447517 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Raphaela Cocotos (b.1999) is a multimedia artist who is currently enrolled in her final year of Fine Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand. Cocotos’ artworks employ frameworks centred around healing, the body and mental illness. She draws inspiration from personal experiences and utilizes the act of repetition as part of her process in order to furtherinvestigate the concept of healing. \\nCocotos’ work can be understood as an in-depth exploration into the relationship between repetitive behaviours and aspects of abjection that are present within mental illness through the use of food, weaving, and list-making. Her explorative process makes use of these mediums in order to conceptualise and materialise the aforementioned concepts in relation to the ritualization of repetitive behaviours linked to religion, the body, fear, food, nudity, and mental distortion of the physical body (body dysmorphia)."}]}]}

item.title: Ras Silas Motse
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903149277 Ras Silas Motse gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987611357 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ras Silas Motse (b.1989), bred in Motlatla, Thabanchu, Free State, South Africa. When he completed high school, he went to study Fine Arts and a PGCE at the Central University of Technology, Bloemfontein. Motse became a high school educator and now is a full-time artist. \\nRas Silas is a interdisciplinary artist who works with the concept of capturing feelings to narrate contemporary concepts using different African people. His practice is stylistically and structurally experimental, stemming from a desire to invoke the spirits deep within, those of our forefathers, as a means to seek peace and ask for guidance rooted in African knowledge systems. “I have discovered that in order to move forward one needs to engage the past, to deal with it if you’re going to shape a future that reflects you”."}]}]}

She obtained a BA in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand in 2015. Her \\nwork will be shown in several group and solo exhibitions in 2021."}]}]}

item.title: Razia Myers
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903280349 Razia Myers gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987939037 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Razia Myers was born in Johannesburg and lives in Cape Town. She studied under the tutelage of Paul Birchall who is an Art Teacher at Ruth Prowse School of Art and later on with Jill Trappler. She was awarded a Masterclass and Arts Residency Scholarship at the Jerusalem School of Arts in Italy. An intensive studio program for the highly motivated and gifted student under the tutelage of Israel Hershberg. She has recently included Sculpture and Photography into her Art Practice. Myers has participated in numerous group shows nationally. \\n \\nOf her expressive work, deeply spiritual but playful, she attests much of her inspiration to elements found in nature but also the composition and forms found in design and aesthetics. She finds that they are inextricably linked. Myers' colourful and vibrant works are done mostly on large scale as she feels she is able to better express factors such as balance, color, movement, pattern, scale, shape and visual weight. Myers' current body of work concentrates on metamorphosis and human agility . She explores the anchors we seek, the evolution, adaptation and change for survival that is taking place in the midst of a pandemic. Through her painting she presents this time as one of opportunity, to morph into a metaphorical chrysalis state, reassessing, adopting agility and changing approach."}]}]}

item.title: Raymond Fuyana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903247581 Raymond Fuyana 332 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640987775197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014052716765","gid://shopify/Product/9014052749533","gid://shopify/Product/9014052847837"] [23626,23629,23627] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Raymond Fuyana was born in 1995 in Zimbabwe. He moved to South Africa, Johannesburg in 2009 seeking a good deaf school, where he attended St Vincent School for the Deaf in Rosebank. Fuyana joined the Saturday Youth Portfolio Development at Artist Proof Studio in 2015 as he was still in school. While at St Vincent he worked with artists at the Bag Factory for a year. \\nFuyana participated in the Strauss and Co. commission called Pierneef Interpreted in 2017. He made beautiful watercolour monoprints which were exhibited alongside Strauss and Co.’s collection of Pierneef original works at Turbine Art Fair. In 2018 he won the 1st prize in the printmaking category for the Strauss and Co. Irma Stern still life competition. The work was exhibited and sold out the Turbine Art Fair. This was followed by a wonderful article in the Sowetan on his journey as an artist. He plans to enroll for the 4th Year internship programme in 2019 to further his studies at Artist Proof Studio. \\n“My work is influenced by the Surrealism. I create a world of different perspectives. As a deaf person, my experience of the world and the hearing community can be seen in the work I make. I create dreamlike landscapes to express my feelings and mood. The spaces I creates can be viewed upside down and right up. In this body of work, I have used elements of classical architecture fused with African landscapes. The emoticon adds a contemporary element of how we communicate emotions using technology. I focus on capturing the confusion and communication breakdown I experiences daily. The crow plays an important role in my work because it represents me in these spaces. I am able to interpret noise and emotions by creating busy and strange spaces.” \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014052716765 gid://shopify/Product/9014052749533 gid://shopify/Product/9014052847837

item.title: Rebaone Finger
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903345885 Rebaone Finger 2941 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640988004573 ["gid://shopify/Product/9133223379165","gid://shopify/Product/9133225476317"] Rebaone Finger (b. 2001) is a South African multimedia sculptor. Her art dissects black identity, feminism, and consumerism, using the 'Cheese Girl' concept to explore opulence and contrasting realities. [25332,25623] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Rebaone Finger (b. 2001) is a multimedia sculpture artist born in Bloemfontein and raised in Pretoria and Johannesburg. A graduate of Michaelis, her incisive practice is deeply engaged with the multifaceted politics or being, exploring themes such as silent rage, rest, freedom, luxury, black consumerism, social media, food, politics, naming cultures, blackness, and black feminism. \\nFinger's work critiques societal dynamics by adopting the South African use of food as a naming culture, reflecting the experience of living between worlds of access and lack. Central to her artistic commentary is the concept of 'Cheese Girl', a distinctively South African term denoting class privilege and social distinction. Finger re-imagines \"Cheese Girl\" as an articulation of blackness as opulence, wealth, and luxury. Her sculptures actualize this notion by merging Instagram-inspired tropes and symbols of perceived opulence with images and objects that embody contrasting realities, capturing the term's fluid and inherently complex nature."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9133223379165 gid://shopify/Product/9133225476317

item.title: Reef Sithole
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903444189 Reef Sithole 1899 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640988365021 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013400273117"] [14113] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I’m a fine artist from Johannesburg. My style of work is contemporary neo-expressionism infused with pop art and surrealism, pulling strong references from my rough-yet-unique upbringing in Soweto. The dichotomy of what Soweto is, is largely what inspires my work till today. I also produce a wide scope of multimedia visual art, exploring nuanced digital design themes, techniques and usage of soundscapes. Eventually enrolled at the prestigious National School of The Arts, by the tender age of 8, I was already engaged in art classes by my parents. With the inherent ability for draughtsmanship, art was always encouraged as an avenue away from the hotbed for drugs and violence which exists in Soweto. My accumulating gallery experience includes Artist Residency with The Fourth (2021), Death Row Dinner (2021), Fede group exhibition (2022) and Cape Town Art Fair (2022) My work is essentially an amalgamation of niche techniques, such as stitching, infused to create a completely new style. It feels extremely inspired; like a proposition for a new way of painting. And within this work, you can see the influence of legendary artists such as Basquiat, Bacon, Matisse & Warhol, and more. I’m a punk at heart, and that’s what resonates through my paintings. I experiment in digital design and soundscapes, unlocking two alternative career paths as a reputable graphic designer."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013400273117

item.title: Reem Aljeally

item.title: Regina Bardavid
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641903706333 Regina Bardavid 436 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36640989544669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013289025757","gid://shopify/Product/9013460041949","gid://shopify/Product/9013460074717","gid://shopify/Product/9013853651165","gid://shopify/Product/9013853716701","gid://shopify/Product/9013853749469"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Regi Bardavid was born in Alexandria Egypt and has travelled extensively, living in Italy, Zimbabwe, Zaire and South Africa. She has remained firmly rooted in the ‘abstract’ throughout her career which spans more than four decades. Her inspiration comes from the act of play, “releasing the Self of all obligations and constrictions of upbringing.” \\n \\nMy artistic journey can be best described as a voyage through imaginary landscapes, where vibrant hues and non-figurative forms converge to evoke emotions and stir the imagination. Each painting is a spontaneous exploration, a dance of intuition, and a dialogue between myself and the canvas. Inspiration also emerges from the patterns left by coffee remnants, a ritual I adopted from my time in Egypt. These diverse stimuli ignite my creativity, leading me to seek surprise and discovery in my work. \\n \\nMeditation plays a crucial role in my practice, helping me enter a state of flow where paintings unfold organically. I embrace the notion of the Zone, where the act of creation feels effortless, allowing the artwork to manifest itself. \\n \\nDespite studying art history extensively, I ultimately returned to my roots in abstract expressionism, finding solace in its freedom of expression."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013289025757 gid://shopify/Product/9013460041949 gid://shopify/Product/9013460074717 gid://shopify/Product/9013853651165 gid://shopify/Product/9013853716701 gid://shopify/Product/9013853749469
