[23414,23415,24414,24410,23188,24412,24416] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sichumile Adam (b. 2001) is an emerging visual artist based in Johannesburg, South Africa. She recently graduated with an honours degree in Fine Arts from the University of Witwatersrand. As a multi-disciplinary artist, Sichumile works primarily with acrylic paint, fabric, and glass beads. Her work uniquely combines contemporary African American and South African imagery to create a landscape that resonates with women across the Black diaspora. \\nThrough curated posing, Sichumile uses the figures in her painting to celebrate and explore womanhood, drawing from both personal and collective experiences as a Black woman. The use of beads and fabric in artwork further celebrates her cultural heritage, adding texture and dimensions to her creations. \\nThis approach also enhances the viewing experience, encouraging viewers to engage with her painting up close and explore the intricate beading styles and techniques. “I enjoy using my art to explore the dynamic social cultures that women share globally, but from a South African context, ” says Sichumile."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014039871709 gid://shopify/Product/9014044557533 gid://shopify/Product/9014044623069 gid://shopify/Product/9014087188701 gid://shopify/Product/9014087287005 gid://shopify/Product/9014087385309 gid://shopify/Product/9014087483613

His recent installations or \"collection projects\" include the display of multiple historical artifacts in which he explores issues of identity and branding. His most current collection project is an extensive web-based archive documenting South African audio history. Records, an installation that developed out of this archive, was shown in South Africa in 2009 and in the United States in 2010. \\n \\nIn addition to collection projects and woven panel installations, Allen also employs cut-up collage techniques using comics. item.title: Sifiso Mkhabela
item.description: Sifiso Mkhabela 2208 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641060585693 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014059663581"] Discover Pretoria-based sculptor Sifiso Makhabel, who creates large-scale geometric/organic metal works exploring abstract objects, Platonism, and childhood memory. [23827] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sifiso Mkhabela (b. 1991, Mbombela) is a sculptor based in Pretoria, where he moved in 2013 to complete his B-Tech degree in Fine and Applied Arts. His engagement with metal began early, inspired by his father, a boilermaker, whose tireless work ethic deeply influenced him. This foundational experience was further developed when Mkhabela worked as a studio assistant for sculptor Angus Taylor after graduating. \\n \\nMkhabela's practice involves creating sculptures that often blend geometric forms with organic structures, employing hybrid techniques to transform existing concepts into new forms. He frequently stars his process with models made from shoe sole rubber or wire, which are later scaled up into life-sized or ever larger metal sculptures. The surfaces often retain a raw, translucent quality that highlights the texture and inherent properties of the medium. \\n \\nConceptually, Mkhabela draws inspiration from childhood memories integrated with mathematical and scientific ideas, particularly Platonism – the philosophical view of abstract objects existing beyond time and space. He describes his sculptures as attempts to represent these abstract objects filtered through his personal experiences, calling them \"hybrids of my thoughts.\" For Mkhabela, metal is a potent medium, resonating with its fundamental role in everyday life and infrastructure, connecting back to his father's craft and his own artistic explorations."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014059663581

item.title: Sihle Inensiko
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641925988573 Sihle Inensiko gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641060880605 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Alvin Sihle Inensiko is a Multi-disciplinary artists based in Durban, who’s process of creating art is influenced by the lived experience, meaning my work is based off my informative reflection about the world gained through direct, first-hand involvement in everyday events rather than through representations constructed by other people. Within this notion Sihle’s work is often explored from the peripheries of society in an attempt to capture moments that challenge the viewer to ‘re-imagine spaces or moments he or she would have otherwise neglected. In most cases this is achieved through the use of painting as an interpretive rendering of the artist own experience within these spaces. \\nThroughout His practice, Sihle has always been fascinated by images and how they have the power to impact other people’s emotions and persecution of things and the world at large. The interest was cultivated during his teenage years and has further developed since He opted to take his post-grad Diploma in Fine Art, at the Durban University of Technology. After completing his post-grad diploma. Sihle aims to delve even more into his Artistic practice, which requires, that he constantly be in the center of the experiences he opts to capture. Since to perceive a world and be shaped by it, one must be in and of its flesh. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Silas Adelanke Adeoye
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641926217949 Silas Adelanke Adeoye 336 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641061208285 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013290926301","gid://shopify/Product/9013290959069"] [4130,4131] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Silas Adelanke Adeoye was born in Osun State, the South-Western part of Nigeria, in 1962. He took to fine art early, experimenting with various ideas and coming up with innovative techniques before even starting his primary education. He largely developed as an artist by himself, later joining a group of young, prominent artists at the National Museum, Lagos. His works represent a continuation in the tradition of Yoruba Art, recognizable by his choice of pigment to suit each motif. Visual art, in the historic Yoruba setting, was generally restricted to the courts of the kings and chiefs, and to religious houses. Silas believes that it is the responsibility of the modern artist to extend the enjoyment of this very unique form of expression to a far broader audience in a manner that music and poetry, are today. Adeoye uses the technique of pointillism exclusively in his work, a technique that is utilized by few contemporary artists. \\n \\nHe has participated in numerous exhibitions and fine art auctions in Nigeria and internationally, his work can be found in selected collections worldwide."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013290926301 gid://shopify/Product/9013290959069

item.title: Simon Attwood

He is currently studying at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago, USA where he has been awarded a Presidential Scholarship. \\n\"As an artist, I am interested in the relationship between the individual and their environment (namely the sociopolitical structures they interact within and the natural environment that they eke sustenance from). In my work, I aim to make the viewer reflect on their own interactions in these fields and the impact that they have on the world. I do this by criticizing the shortfalls of the politically powerful and addressing the devastating impacts of human greed on the environment.\""}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013287354589 gid://shopify/Product/9014015230173

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928544477 Simon Venter 1407 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641063567581 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014041084125","gid://shopify/Product/9014041116893","gid://shopify/Product/9014041182429","gid://shopify/Product/9014041215197","gid://shopify/Product/9014041247965","gid://shopify/Product/9014041313501","gid://shopify/Product/9014050455773","gid://shopify/Product/9014050521309","gid://shopify/Product/9014053961949","gid://shopify/Product/9014054027485","gid://shopify/Product/9014054060253","gid://shopify/Product/9014054093021","gid://shopify/Product/9014054125789","gid://shopify/Product/9014054158557","gid://shopify/Product/9014054191325","gid://shopify/Product/9014054256861","gid://shopify/Product/9014054289629","gid://shopify/Product/9014054322397","gid://shopify/Product/9014054355165","gid://shopify/Product/9014054420701","gid://shopify/Product/9014057730269","gid://shopify/Product/9014115467485"] Discover Simon Venter, a multidisciplinary artist who integrates traditional fine arts with emerging technologies like AI. His work explores creativity's evolving dynamics, engaging with themes of history, identity, and the meaning of life. [23665,23669,23661,23659,23304,23673,23300,23299,23658,23579,23670,23671,23760,23578,23580,23672,23662,23664] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simon Venteris a multidisciplinary artist who bridges traditional fine arts with emerging technologies to explore creativity in the digital age. With a foundation in classical oil painting, Venter incorporates artificial intelligence into his work, creating a dialogue between human ingenuity and machine-driven processes. This interplay critically examines how technology redefines creative boundaries, focusing on the tension between human agency and AI’s transformative presence in artistic production. \\nCentral to Venter's work is an engagement with archetypal themes and existential questions. Drawing from global traditions and cultural memory, his art weaves together symbols and narratives that speak to the timeless human pursuit of meaning and individuality. By juxtaposing traditional techniques with AI-generated elements, Venter addresses fundamental questions about the essence of creativity and the ways technology mediates our connection to history, identity, and the meaning of life. \\nVenter's projects often highlight critical themes, such as the myths surrounding AI’s perceived autonomy and intelligence, while challenging its status as a colonizing force in contemporary culture. His recent works include explorations of still life, existential symbolism, and architectural motifs, serving as metaphors for humanity’s complex relationship with technology. \\nA graduate of a Master’s program in Creative Media and Production, and a 'self-taught' artist, Venter has exhibited work both locally and internationally. His practice is deeply influenced by his South African heritage, rich in oral storytelling and visual traditions, which he combines with European art historical references to create a globally resonant dialogue. Venter’s art is a testament to the enduring relevance of traditional artistic techniques as a critical lens for understanding the rapid technological shifts shaping the 21st century, making him a compelling voice in contemporary art."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014041084125 gid://shopify/Product/9014041116893 gid://shopify/Product/9014041182429 gid://shopify/Product/9014041215197 gid://shopify/Product/9014041247965 gid://shopify/Product/9014041313501 gid://shopify/Product/9014050455773 gid://shopify/Product/9014050521309 gid://shopify/Product/9014053961949 gid://shopify/Product/9014054027485 gid://shopify/Product/9014054060253 gid://shopify/Product/9014054093021 gid://shopify/Product/9014054125789 gid://shopify/Product/9014054158557 gid://shopify/Product/9014054191325 gid://shopify/Product/9014054256861 gid://shopify/Product/9014054289629 gid://shopify/Product/9014054322397 gid://shopify/Product/9014054355165 gid://shopify/Product/9014054420701 gid://shopify/Product/9014057730269 gid://shopify/Product/9014115467485

item.title: Simone Brewster
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641926742237 Simone Brewster 2760 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641064288477 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014038823133","gid://shopify/Product/9014038855901","gid://shopify/Product/9014038921437","gid://shopify/Product/9014038954205","gid://shopify/Product/9014039019741"] Discover the art and fashion of Simone Brewster, a London-based artist and designer blending Caribbean roots with contemporary aesthetics. Her vibrant works celebrate Black female narratives, exploring identity through abstraction, rhythmic forms, and the fusion of ethnic and Western influences. [23164,23162,23161,23160] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Art and Fashion Experience \\nSimone Brewster (born 1983, London) is an artist, designer, and educator. A Bartlett School of Architecture graduate (2003) with a Masters in Design Products from the Royal College of Art (2007), Brewster boldly infuses her Caribbean roots into her work, celebrating Black female narratives through vibrant colors and rhythmic forms. Based in London, she explores craft, balancing beauty, functionality, and a fusion of “ethnic” and “western” influences. \\nIn painting, Brewster uses abstraction to delve into identity, expressing the hidden complexities of our internal landscapes. Her works transcend figurative art, inviting viewers to interpret layered shapes that reflect multifaceted identities. \\nIn fashion, she frames design as a reflection of emotion and self-discovery. Through colors and forms, she highlights the power of fashion to celebrate individuality and the \"beautiful messiness\" of identity, merging art and self-expression beyond aesthetics."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014038823133 gid://shopify/Product/9014038855901 gid://shopify/Product/9014038921437 gid://shopify/Product/9014038954205 gid://shopify/Product/9014039019741

item.title: Simone Verfaille
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641927233757 Simone Verfaille 2250 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641065435357 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013457387741","gid://shopify/Product/9013988950237","gid://shopify/Product/9014004744413","gid://shopify/Product/9014004809949","gid://shopify/Product/9014004842717","gid://shopify/Product/9014004875485","gid://shopify/Product/9014004908253","gid://shopify/Product/9014004941021","gid://shopify/Product/9014005006557"] [21800,21798,21803,21804,21799,21801,21208] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simone Verfaille (b. 1995, Cape Town, South Africa) creates through the folds and layers of her life. After earning her BA(Hons) Fine Art from Stellenbosch University in 2018, she had a break from the art world, before returning in 2023 with renewed passion and perspective. \\n \\nTo Simone, art is not merely a product but a process that extends beyond the canvas. It mirrors the way we experience, navigate, and embrace life's ever-evolving nature. She believes that life, in all its facets, is best captured through the intricate layers that compose it. In all her work, she strives to capture the depth and richness of life, whether it be the present moment or memories. Each layer of paint represents a distinct memory, a fragment of time, or a moment of existence. To Simone, layers hold the power to create depth and dimensionality. Through layering, she’s able to process the multitude of narratives that shape our and her existence, both weaving together the personal and the universal. \\n \\nHer works become a captivating interplay of colors, forms, and textures, where she hopes to capture the folds and layers of her own sense of self, life and expression. Simone uses her artistic expression not only as a medium for self-discovery but also as a means to find her voice and articulate the profound beauty and complexity of the world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013457387741 gid://shopify/Product/9013988950237 gid://shopify/Product/9014004744413 gid://shopify/Product/9014004809949 gid://shopify/Product/9014004842717 gid://shopify/Product/9014004875485 gid://shopify/Product/9014004908253 gid://shopify/Product/9014004941021 gid://shopify/Product/9014005006557

item.title: Simphiwe Buthelezi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928577245 Simphiwe Buthelezi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641065468125 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Simphiwe Buthelezi was born in 1996 in Benoni, South Africa, and currently lives and works in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nIn 2016, Simphiwe Buthelezi participated in a peer mentoring programme hosted by Assemblage Studios, which launched her development as a young artist. She received her National Diploma in Fine Art at the University of Johannesburg in 2017, and she is the recipient of the 2018 Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize, culminating in a residency at The Bag Factory Artist Studios. \\nButhelezi presented her first solo exhibition, ‘Lala La’, curated by Chumisa Ndakisa, at The Bag Factory Studios in Johannesburg in 2019, as well as a solo exhibition at SMAC in Stellenbosch, South Africa, titled Imvuselelo Yenkululeko / Freedom’s Domain, in 2020. \\nIn 2020, Buthelezi participated in two group exhibitions: Shaping Things: An exploration of clay and ceramics in contemporary South African art practice, at SMAC Gallery in Stellenbosch; and A Show of Solidarity, at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town. Group exhibitions in 2019 include: Young Congo Biennale in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC); The Female Line at SMAC Gallery in Cape Town; Preview#3 in Milan, Italy; tête-à-tête, curated by Candice Allison and Tiina Liebenberg at the Absa Gallery in Johannesburg; Self at Glen Carlou Gallery in Stellenbosch; Art Market Budapest with Johannesburg Art Gallery in Budapest, Hungary; and What is South Africa, Even? Vol.2, curated by Carlyn Strydom at the Bag Factory Artist Studios in Johannesburg. Further group exhibitions include NOW, curated by Aysha Waja at St Teresa’s Art Festival at the Keyes Art Mile, Johannesburg; a flood in my hands at Fried Gallery in Pretoria, South Africa and Ukuma, The Weight of the Wait, curated by Phumzile Twala and Marguerite Visser at Assemblage Project Space in Johannesburg (all in 2018); Atomic Peace, curated by Chumisa Ndakisa, at The Bag Factory Artist Studios in Johannesburg, and Capturing State, at the Klein Karoo Nasionale Kunstefees (KKNK) in Oudtshoorn, South Africa, both in 2017."}]}]}

item.title: Sinalo Ngcaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928872157 Sinalo Ngcaba 1685 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641067630813 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013362000093", "gid://shopify/Product/9013363343581", "gid://shopify/Product/9013365342429"] [11873,11617] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"My name is Sinalo Ngcaba, I'm a 27 year old visual artist from East London and Bizana but now based in Johannesburg. I'm always updating my style and trying new things with different mediums such as oil pastels, ink, digital and paint. \\n \\nI am a creative. I am a storyteller. I am an artist. In my art I explore the intersections of black joy, black pop culture, womanhood and human rights issues in a contemporary world. As creatives it's our duty to evoke emotions that can change the world for the better, to record and document stories of the current world we live in. I believe There's more to life than just breathing. \\n \\nI am grateful to have worked with brands and people such as Piano People UK, Nike, Aperol Spritz, Gauteng Dept. of Sports, Arts & Culture, Amref International, Comedy Central Africa and NATIVE Mag, Sindiso Khumalo and Bam Marley."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013362000093 gid://shopify/Product/9013363343581 gid://shopify/Product/9013363376349 gid://shopify/Product/9013365342429

item.title: Sinenkosi Msomi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641928937693 Sinenkosi Msomi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641068155101 [] Discover Sinenkosi Msomi, a photographer from Eswatini known for his staged and conceptual photography addressing themes of mental health, self-expression, and childhood memories. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sinenkosi Msomi (b. 1995, Eswatini) is a male photographer currently residing in Mbabane. Mpolonjeni. His work comprises staged and conceptual photography, addressing themes such as mental health, self-expression, and childhood memories. Msomi was awarded the social justice prize at the African Union and Afrochampions Nefertiti art prize in 2020 for his work on social change, justice, inclusion, equity, equality, struggle, and anti-oppression. \\nIntroduced to photography by his best friend Clifford Dludlu, Msomi began to view the world differently. His major life challenge has been overcoming the pain of losing loved ones, which taught him to cherish moments with those he loves. He is currently in his final year of a Bachelor of Commerce in Marketing at the University of Eswatini and holds an Associate degree in Business Management. \\nMsomi believes photography is a medium of self-expression that educates, tells stories, and unites. His first solo exhibition, titled All that glitters is not gold, held at Yebo Art Gallery, explored youth mental health issues and encouraged peers to seek psychological help. His upbringing in an African extended family profoundly influences his work, helping him to articulate feelings and experiences that words often fail to convey. Msomi uniquely employs natural light in his photography and uses Lightroom mobile for post-production. He aspires to collaborate with other African artists in the future."}]}]}

item.title: Siphamandla Oscar Mngwango
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929232605 Siphamandla Oscar Mngwango 713 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641068646621 [] [4684] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Siphamandla \"Ex\" Oscar Mngwango was born in Vryheid in July 1987. He went to school at Kanye Kanye High School, where he matriculated in 2007. Since he was a child he loved to draw. From an early age, he chose to use art as an outlet to share his perspective and ideas. His intimate closeness to his grandmother has influenced his lyrics and art, as 'Ex' is his pseudonym adopted from years of passionately devoting himself to producing hip hop underground music. He draws his inspiration from the beauty he finds in women, which resonates with the beauty he sees in his grandmother. \\n \\nHe paints women, mostly. He finds them to be the most interesting subject, like a \"Blue Rose\". They are a mystery. His medium consists of colourful acrylics, oil paint and charcoal on canvas. Because of his background, it was easy for him to become part of the community of artists at August House, and learn from them. This has aided him in terms of developing his own style. \\n \\nSiphamandla has participated in various group shows such as the 2018 Thami Mnyele Fine Art Award group show, the MTN UJ Top 10 emerging artists group show and recently, the launch of \"Riboville Boutique Hotel\" group show."}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929724125 Sipho Mpongo 374 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641069891805 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013290041565","gid://shopify/Product/9014014804189"] Sipho Mpongo, a South African photographer born in Nqamakwe, Eastern Cape, and raised in Langa, Cape Town, is known for his powerful visual stories documenting the "Born Free Generation" and advancing human rights. Currently studying at the Michaelis School of Fine Art. [3950,22360] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sipho Mpongo's (b. 1993, Eastern Cape) photographic journey began with IIiso Labantu, a local mentorship program, which propelled him into his career. Mpongo completed a full-time course at The Cape Town School of Photography. In 2014, he embarked on a four-month tour around South Africa with photographers Wikus de Wet and Sean Meterlerkamp, as part of the Twenty Journey project, documenting the \"Born Free Generation\" 20 years after apartheid. \\n \\nA member of the lliso Labantu photography collective, Mpongo is currently studying at the Michaelis School of Fine Art in Cape Town. In 2015, the Magnum Foundation recognized Mpongo as one of their Human Rights Fellows, providing scholarships and training for photographers from the Global South. Through this fellowship, he attended NYU’s Tisch School of the Arts in New York City, where he developed strategies for creating powerful visual stories to advance human rights."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013290041565 gid://shopify/Product/9014014804189

item.title: Siphesihle Ntsungwana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929265373 Siphesihle Ntsungwana gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641069564125 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Siphesihle Ntsungwana is an Eastern Cape-born artist whose work explores his identity. Through painting, he explores the transition from the rural area of Bizana, Eastern Cape, to the urbanity of Durban and the transformation of his identity and art-making. Since moving to the city, his work references mass media and pop culture in an exploration of the youthful imaginings of a millennial, filtering contemporary imagery and social culture and opposing this to reality. These are filtered as in-depth studies of individuals seen in social culture and rendered in paintings of, at times, single color gradations of primary colours. Ntsungwana is a recent graduate of the Durban University of Technology and offers a fresh perspective on popular culture as it relates to the social diaspora of South African youth. His work has recently been featured at PRIZM Art Fair with the KZNSA Gallery (2021) and is enjoying rising favour with local and international collectors."}]}]}

item.title: Siphokazi Mlangeni
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929461981 Siphokazi Mlangeni 2602 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641070088413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013987606749","gid://shopify/Product/9013987737821","gid://shopify/Product/9013987803357","gid://shopify/Product/9013987868893","gid://shopify/Product/9013995274461"] Siphokazi Mlangeni [21186,21190,21188,21415,21191,21189] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"I Siphokazi Mlangeni was born on June 12, 2001, in Bergville KwaZulu \\nNatal. I later moved with my family to Johannesburg, Gauteng where I \\nattended primary school and later interchanged high schools between \\nKwaZulu-Natal and Gauteng. \\nThe passion I have for art developed during my early years of high school \\nwhen I taught myself how to draw. Upon studying BA Visual Arts at the \\nUniversity of KwaZulu-Natal I was introduced to the ceramics medium \\nwhich I felt more drawn to as I continuously worked with it. I realised that I \\nenjoyed working with the medium as it allows me to feel the clay, and to \\nmanipulate it into any form I may desire. \\nThe inspiration behind my work is the feminine body, particularly the vulva, and the positive and negative notions that society associates with it. As a young woman my experiences with my body and where I stand in society are also inspirational to my work. The series titled Ukuzihlola (2023) which is a part of the Decurex Exhibition was created for the purpose of my honours research at UKZN titled; State of the Vulva: Themes of virginity and female sexuality in the works of Suzanne Santoro, Lady Skollie, and Siphokazi Mlangeni. This body of work was informed by the themes of virginity and female sexuality, where I translated collected information into visual depictions to be consumed as art. \\nThese art pieces reflect on the descriptions extracted from my sources describing the changes that occur on a woman’s body upon losing her virginity. These changes include sagging breasts, stretchmarks on the waist and behind the legs, and any signs of cellulitis or loosening of the skin on the lower parts of the body. I took some of these descriptions and added them as textures on my vases with an attempt to embrace these changes as normal. The titles of the art works derive from the word intombi, describing a virgin girl in Zulu. \\nMy research and my works do not pose as a challenge, an agreement, or disagreement to the cultural practice of virginity testing. It is more of an inquiry on the practice, its notions, and the value that society holds against women through their bodies. \\nIn the process of creating these pieces as an artist, I felt more like an examiner looking into the vulvas and choosing which ones I viewed as “virgins” and “non-virgins” as I gave them characteristics that forced me to question how I feel about the practice as a woman who has never been exposed to it. I hold dear the idea of an individual examining her own virginity, both literally and metaphorically, something like self-reflecting, seeking to perceive yourself from your perception. This idea creates a feeling of acceptance and comfort in one’s skin, shadowing feelings of shame, hate, and other negative self-imagery that stem from women viewing themselves through the lens of society. \\nI appreciate how clay allows me to feel the work as I make it. Like my interpretation of Ukuzihlola, I feel and see parts of myself through the process of making art and from that I choose how to respond to the negative views of society associated with female sexuality."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013987606749 gid://shopify/Product/9013987737821 gid://shopify/Product/9013987803357 gid://shopify/Product/9013987868893 gid://shopify/Product/9013995274461

item.title: SIPHOSETHU MTSHALI
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929527517 SIPHOSETHU MTSHALI gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641021919453 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Johannesburg, Raised in Nqutu, KwaZulu-Natal Siphosethu Mtshali, a rising star in the world of visual art, was born in the vibrant city of Johannesburg, but her artistic journey truly began amidst the serene landscapes of Nqutu in KwaZulu-Natal, where she spent her formative years. Born with an innate artistic streak, Siphosethu only embraced her true calling as an artist in the transformative year of 2022. Siphosethu's artistic odyssey is a testament to the power of inspiration and the latent creative potential within each of us. Her early years in the picturesque rural surroundings of Ngutu instilled in her a deep appreciation for the natural world and a unique perspective on life, which now permeates her artistry. At the core of Siphosethu's captivating body of work are her enchanting paintings, which predominantly feature children. Her muse is the innocence and wonder of youth, which she elegantly captures through her distinctive style and use of mixed media- acrylic and watercolour to soft pastels and charcoal-Her paintings are a heartfelt celebration of the unbridled joy, curiosity, and resilience that define childhood. Each piece tells a story, inviting viewers to reconnect with the purity of their own early experiences and rediscover the enchantment of the world through the eyes of a child. Siphosethu's choice of mixed media adds depth and complexity to her artwork, reflecting the multifaceted nature of life itself. Her skillful blending of various materials and techniques creates a rich tapestry of textures, color's, and emotions that draw observers into her vibrant world. Whether it's the interplay of watercolors and acrylics, the juxtaposition of pastels and charcoal, or the incorporation of found objects, each element in her work contributes to a captivating narrative."}]}]}

item.title: Sisanda Nxumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641929756893 Sisanda Nxumalo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641070252253 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sisanda Nxumalo (b.1998) is an illustrator, creative and mixed-media designer currently based in Cape Town. Nxumalo draws from her immediate environment and also utilises her experiences from the location she finds herself in towards her creative practice in photography. She describes her passion for illustration as the best medium through which she is able to articulate her thoughts and depictions that are informed by intrusive and often random thoughts. Nxumalo was previously enrolled in the Fine Arts programme at the University of Cape Town in 2016 before making the decision to move to follow her passion and transfer to the Durban University of Technology to study Graphic Design where she graduated in 2019. At present, Nxumalo wishes to expand her passion in illustration into the arts."}]}]}

[22290,22292,19249,19250,19251,22293,19253,19248,19254,25518,25519] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sitaara Stodel (b.1991) is a Cape Town-based contemporary artist whose practice spans photography, collage, video, and printmaking. Her unique artistic perspective is deeply influenced by a lifetime of frequent relocations, having moved house forty times. This transient lifestyle profoundly shapes her work, where she often reconstructs personal and collective memories through found family photographs sourced from antique stores and markets. \\nStodel's pieces are marked by her meticulous process of tearing, cutting, and reassembling these photographs, often using gold thread to symbolize the preciousness of memory. Her collages depict domestic scenes, integrating her ideals of home—complete with fresh flowers, framed artworks, houses with sea views, and shiny cars. \\nAfter graduating from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2014, Stodel received the prestigious Tierney Fellowship. She has since exhibited her work in numerous Cape Town galleries, including Zeitz MOCAA, SMAC Gallery, Smith Gallery, Gallery MOMO, and Everard Read. Stodel also contributes to the Michaelis photographic department as the technical officer of photography, utilizing her extensive knowledge of analogue photographic methods to influence her varied approaches to image-making"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013898608861 gid://shopify/Product/9013899329757 gid://shopify/Product/9013900181725 gid://shopify/Product/9013900935389 gid://shopify/Product/9013901787357 gid://shopify/Product/9013902573789 gid://shopify/Product/9014012641501 gid://shopify/Product/9014012707037 gid://shopify/Product/9014012739805 gid://shopify/Product/9133212074205 gid://shopify/Product/9133213188317 gid://shopify/Product/9133231636701 gid://shopify/Product/9133233930461 gid://shopify/Product/9133233963229 gid://shopify/Product/9133234028765 gid://shopify/Product/9134146355421

After his primary and secondary studies, his taste for drawing led him to integrate the Academy of Fine Arts of Kinshasa to train in the know-how of arts in order to \\nperfect his look and his practice where, after several years of learning, Ndombe obtained his diploma of graduation in Plastic Arts. Touching several fields of creation, Sisqo Ndombe then decided to devote himself full time to his passion: painting. \\n\"I paint everything that affects human\" he says. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Siyabonga Fani
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641930412253 Siyabonga Fani gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641072185565 [] Siyabonga Fani {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Cape Town in 1981, Siyabonga Fani is one of South Africa's terracotta sculptural masters. Raised in the township of Gugulethu, and now working in a studio in Woodstock, Fani has been working in clay since the late 1990s. \\n \\nThere is a duality to Fani’s work: the artist’s ceramics, pit-fired with a smoky scent, reflect the memory of his late father, a self-taught artist, as they draw inspiration from natural elements such as trees, rivers, and the earth. \\n \\nYet his work likewise resonates with the joy and estrangement of life in the township, capturing the vibrant energy of urban life. This duality creates a poignant tension, as his art embodies both a longing for idyllic landscapes and an appreciation for the lively sounds and cultures of his upbringing. \\n \\nFani's work is unique in its emotional depth, expressing love and nostalgia through a diverse and multilingual lens. His pieces are showcased in private and public collections in South Africa and the United States, where they continue to evoke a sense of connection and yearning."}]}]}

item.title: Siyabonga Mlambi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931264221 Siyabonga Mlambi 469 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641072611549 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013288206557","gid://shopify/Product/9013288239325"] [3593,3595] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Siyabonga Mlambi was born in the small town of Bizana located in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. This area is famous for sharing the birthplace of Winnie Madikizela Mandela and anti-apartheid politician Oliver Tambo. Built with mixture of warm hospitality, cultural sites, and breath-taking landscapes mixed with the click language of Xhosa tribal traditions make this location like no other in the world. \\n \\nAlmost love at first sight, Siyabonga became smitten with art as a child and by the time he finished High School it was full-blown love affair. While in college he studied art and design and focused his attention on nature and various colour palettes. Upon graduating his mediums of choice became acrylic, fabric, stones, grass, ink and graphite. As his artistic skill-set matured, he began experimenting with various styles and technique, which ultimately lead his to discover a style that would later become his signature. Identified as Superblur African Synthetic Cubism/Circlelism the style aim is to entertain the viewer with beauty and desire that the eye cannot see but only the heart can feel. Similarly to the way we interpret music subconsciously that has touched our lives in ways that became forever memorable. \\n \\nIn his own words “My work stems from observation while problem solving. I look to do it in a way that is honest and from a distance. My influences explore the idea of changing lives in the world through meaningful massages and stories of everyday happening. I am also a poet, therefore no matter if I'm being artistic through mixed media or words; I hope to convey a message of love that hits the heart and spirit of all that I encounter\". \\n \\nSolo & Group Exhibitions \\n \\n2019 – LAE Group exhibition –– “Contemporary African Art meets European Design” - European Light & Design Centre \\n \\n2019 – Group Exhibition – “Africa’s Art Collective Seasons Spring 2019” - The Mall of Africa \\n \\n2019 – Turbine Art Fair \\n \\n2019 - Group Exhibition – “Africa’s Art Collective Seasons Autumn 2019” - The Mall of Africa \\n \\n2019 – LAE Group Exhibition –– “African Influences” - The Hyatt Regency Hotel Rosebank \\n \\n2019 – Group Exhibition – Curated by Leigh Rein – Werksmans Sandton \\n \\n2018 – LAE Group Exhibition – “Thebe Ya Mosadi - She is Power” – Urban Tree Sandton \\n \\n2018 – LAE Group Exhibition – “FNB Early Childhood Development Fundraiser” – FNB Private Wealth Sandton \\n \\n2016 – Group Exhibition – Margate Art Museum – South Coast KZN"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013288206557 gid://shopify/Product/9013288239325

item.title: Sizwe Khoza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931755741 Sizwe Khoza 327 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073332445 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013292073181", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330182365", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330247901", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330346205", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330411741", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330477277", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330542813", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330575581", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330608349", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330641117", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330706653", "gid://shopify/Product/9013330739421", "gid://shopify/Product/9013937832157", "gid://shopify/Product/9014015951069", "gid://shopify/Product/9014052978909"] [4211,4210,8706,8707,22400,19706,8709,8708,8705,4214,8715,4212,4213] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Khoza was born in Mozambique towards the end of the Civil War and moved to South Africa with his family in 1995. He matriculated in 2010 from Nkumbulo Comprehensive School and during his matric year he attended Saturday classes at Artist Proof Studio. Thereafter, he studied printmaking for three years and graduated in 2012. In 2013 he was awarded a residency through Artist Proof Studio at William Humphrey Art Gallery (WHAG) in Kimberley under the mentorship of the late Dumisani Mabaso. Khoza was then offered an internship at Artist Proof Studio in 2014 as a facilitator in Printmaking for first and second year students attending full time and chose to be a full-time artist from 2016. Twice a year Khoza travels to Mozambique to take photographs and sketch people and upon return creates new works inspired by his visit home. Khoza specializes in painting, monotype and combined printmaking techniques. In 2017 he was commissioned by Rand Merchant Bank Holdings to create an artwork for their boardroom. He donates two artworks a year to auction initiatives that raise money for education and continues to have exhibitions and shows around the country. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013292073181 gid://shopify/Product/9013292105949 gid://shopify/Product/9013292138717 gid://shopify/Product/9013292171485 gid://shopify/Product/9013292237021 gid://shopify/Product/9013330182365 gid://shopify/Product/9013330247901 gid://shopify/Product/9013330346205 gid://shopify/Product/9013330411741 gid://shopify/Product/9013330477277 gid://shopify/Product/9013330542813 gid://shopify/Product/9013330575581 gid://shopify/Product/9013330608349 gid://shopify/Product/9013330641117 gid://shopify/Product/9013330706653 gid://shopify/Product/9013330739421 gid://shopify/Product/9013937832157 gid://shopify/Product/9014015951069 gid://shopify/Product/9014052978909

item.title: Siyabulela Ndodana
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931329757 Siyabulela Ndodana gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073004765 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013303509213"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"A quote from a book, a verse from a poem, a lyric of a song, or a simple chat with a friend becomes a medium to motivate and inspire. Siyabulela Ndodana sees himself as not only as a motivational sculptor. Working in clay he translates the words of the Wiseman into figures to inspire and motivate his audience. Everybody needs something that can pick them up when they are down. He believes that art can heal a broken soul. \\n \\nNdodana was born and bred in the Eastern Cape and he worked for a couple of art foundries, in Western Cape and Gauteng, before he became an artist himself. He lives and works in Johannesburg."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013303509213

item.title: Sizwe Nyanga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931821277 Sizwe Nyanga 2253 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073463517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013845459165","gid://shopify/Product/9013845491933","gid://shopify/Product/9013845524701","gid://shopify/Product/9013845557469"] [18716,18717,18714,18715] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Nyanga, an artist and community activist, merges creativity and social impact. Hailing from Vosloorus (South Africa), he sees art as a transformative force, blending research, education, and culture to reshape society's outlook through his photographs, paintings, drawings and multi-medium installations. \\nEducated at Umuzi.org in Multimedia, he has delved into the digital art space for over a decade, crafting a unique artistic voice. In 2018, his daring expedition backpacking from Johannesburg to Malawi with only R1300 a tent and a camera, captured in \"Mayendo Abwino\" (Photo-Essay), revealed his narrative through powerful imagery. This year, Sizwe exhibited twice in Bonn, Germany, leaving an indelible mark. \\nFirstly, with \"the holy trinity,\" presenting \"Please Don't Pinch\", at Alanus Hochschule für Kunst und Gesellschaft and later, an artist-in-residency project called \"Homeless in The Global Village\" at the Kunst Museum Bonn. \\nSizwe's art transcends borders, reflecting his dedication to preserving culture, fostering creativity, and creating conversation through his stories and photographs. His journey showcases art's transformative potential and its ability to shape a better tomorrow. Now, he expands his artistic horizon into music, film, and performing arts as mediums to convey his evolving ideas."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013845459165 gid://shopify/Product/9013845491933 gid://shopify/Product/9013845524701 gid://shopify/Product/9013845557469

item.title: Sizwe Sama
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641931952349 Sizwe Sama 2223 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641073758429 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013449785565","gid://shopify/Product/9013449818333","gid://shopify/Product/9013449883869","gid://shopify/Product/9013449916637","gid://shopify/Product/9013450375389","gid://shopify/Product/9013839757533","gid://shopify/Product/9013839790301","gid://shopify/Product/9013839855837","gid://shopify/Product/9013839888605","gid://shopify/Product/9013839954141","gid://shopify/Product/9013839986909","gid://shopify/Product/9013840019677","gid://shopify/Product/9013840183517"] [16719,18312,16685,18303,16690,18304,18305,18310,16686,16687,18311,18308,18318] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Sama (b.1986) is a self-taught visual artist from Kwa-Zulu Natal, who learnt about art from his local library in Pietermaritzburg and from visiting the Tatham Art Gallery. The fabrics he uses in his tapestries are sometimes recycled from his own closet, or acquired for their specific visual impact and cultural references. The imitation tartans and Kente cloths used in these works draw attention to the intercultural translation of visual languages, and the ease with which cultural forms are appropriated and cross-pollinated in a globalised world. \\n \\nFor Sama, this plurality is always proudly celebrated. He sees his work as a tribute to the LGBTQI+ community, as calls to freedom and self-expression, just as art-making has allowed him to express his own queer identity. \\n \\nAs much as his work is a highly visible outward celebration of queer personhood, it is also deeply rooted in his personal experiences and memories. Sama learned sewing by hand from his mother, a seamstress who raised him and his brother alone, and who mended their clothes in particular ways. \\n \\nSama has exhibited in multiple group shows with Guns & Rain and had his first solo with the gallery in 2022. He has also recently shown work at Galerie Christophe Person in Paris, and at the KZNSA Gallery in Durban, as well as at Duende Art Projects in Antwerp, Belgium, MOV’ART in \\n \\nLisbon, Portugal, and by Africa First/Gordon Gallery in Tel Aviv, Israel. His work already sits in multiple international and local collections, including the AMAWAL (Spain), ARAK (Qatar) and Africa First (Israel) Collections."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013449785565 gid://shopify/Product/9013449818333 gid://shopify/Product/9013449883869 gid://shopify/Product/9013449916637 gid://shopify/Product/9013450375389 gid://shopify/Product/9013839757533 gid://shopify/Product/9013839790301 gid://shopify/Product/9013839855837 gid://shopify/Product/9013839888605 gid://shopify/Product/9013839954141 gid://shopify/Product/9013839986909 gid://shopify/Product/9013840019677 gid://shopify/Product/9013840183517

item.title: Sizwe Sibisi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932116189 Sizwe Sibisi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641074151645 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sizwe Sibisi (b.1986) is a visual artist from Kwa-Zulu Natal who taught himself about art thanks to his local library in Pietermaritzburg and the Tatham Art Gallery. He originally trained as a nurse but has recently become a full-time artist. \\n \\n“My work celebrates and honours the LGBTQI+ community and Single Mothers. The colourfulness and layering calls to mind ‘confetti’ which signifies celebration and festivity at PRIDE marches and events. The various colours is me sprinkling some confetti onto the downtrodden members of our society. The consistent D shape signifies the profile of a pregnant woman’s stomach. Oftentimes a woman is left to raise her young alone, which is a huge struggle, yet they manage beautifully.” \\n \\n“Non binary groups and women are subjected to wide lack of acceptance, ridicule and violence. I reflect on this in the intricate patterns of my artworks. Hand-stitching is a part of my art making process, as it reminds me of my mother doing mending for my brother and I growing up. She’s worked as a seamstress most of her life. She’s been taking care of my brother and I by using her hands to stitch. The way I look at it is, women do a good job stitching society together.” \\n \\n“South Africa as society has a long way to go in terms of normalising and accepting the non-binary. I hope through my work I will shift paradigms and inspire change”."}]}]}

item.title: Skubalisto
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932280029 Skubalisto gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641074970845 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Skumbuzo Vabaza, known as ‘Skubalisto’, is a visual artist based in Cape Town, South Africa. Skubalisto was born in Harare, Zimbabwe (1987), where his parents had spent their twenties in political exile. Stemming from a background in street art, Skubalisto primarily creates portraits in a contemporary expressionist style, both as murals and canvas paintings. His mediums range from spray paint, acrylic, oil pastel, charcoal to ink. His works, punctuated with social consciousness, are a collection of ideas and stories, serving as visual diaries for the state of the world at the time of their creation. \\n \\n“I am not a writer; painting is my weapon of choice. The makings of a true artist lie in the fact that an individual can create no matter what medium they use.” - Skubalisto"}]}]}

item.title: Slovo Mamphaga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932378333 Slovo Mamphaga gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641075134685 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013357707485","gid://shopify/Product/9013357805789","gid://shopify/Product/9013357838557","gid://shopify/Product/9013357904093"] Discover the art of Slovo Mamphaga, a South African artist who uses drawing, painting, and print-making to explore identity and societal issues. His surrealistic works aim to redefine the Afrocentric narrative. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Slovo Mamphaga is a South African artist specializing in drawing, painting, and print-making. Mamphaga recreates everyday scenes in South Africa to explore his identity and his place in the world, while addressing societal issues ranging from the spiritual to the political. Mamphaga delves into how our internal and external worlds collide and examines how unchallenged external factors can shape our sense of self. \\nMamphaga reflects on how individuals can influence their surroundings to effect change. His surrealistic work, influenced by elements of design due to his background, is experimental and guided by the creation process. \"In an effort to create art that is utilitarian and memorable, my work seeks to find new ways to redefine the Afrocentric narrative.\" - Slovo Mamphaga"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013357707485 gid://shopify/Product/9013357805789 gid://shopify/Product/9013357838557 gid://shopify/Product/9013357904093

item.title: Sma Rajoale Kumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932443869 Sma Rajoale Kumalo 599 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641075396829 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013282472157","gid://shopify/Product/9013282504925"] Sma Rajoale Kumalo, based in uMlazi, KZN, creates ritualistic video, installation, and photographic art that challenges cultural and religious norms, focusing on post-colonial trauma and queer identity in the context of African heritage. [3094,3095] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sma Rajoale Kumalo is a multidisciplinary artist based in uMlazi, KwaZulu-Natal, who uses video, installation, and photography to document his ritual performances. Raised in a strict Christian household by his paternal grandmother, who rejected Zulu traditions, Kumalo was also influenced by his grandfather, who embraced his African Zulu/Sotho heritage and playfully called him \"Bussman\" due to his lighter skin. \\nAs a queer Black man, Kumalo’s work is deeply rooted in exploring the tension between societal expectations, such as religion and culture, which uphold heteronormative sexualities. \\nIn this 2017 exhibition, The Monkey on My Shoulder, Kumalo examines post/colonialism and psychological trauma, particularly in the context of being considered the Other. His research into historical figures like Sara Baartman and Frans Taaibosch, who were displayed as “freaks” in European colonial freak shows, alongside the work of artists like Tracey Rose and Nandipha Mntambo, informs his artistic exploration. Kumalo’s work engages with the concept of cultural contestation and resistance, focusing on how these artists challenge European colonialism by inserting their bodies into their works, as seen in pieces like Venus Baartman (2001) and The Rape of Europa (2009). \\nDrawing from their legacy, Kumalo presents his own counter-gaze, performing his identity at historical colonial sites in Durban, such as Francis Farewell Square, the Natural Science Museum at City Hall, and his former school, George Campbell School of Technology. His art challenges oppressive narratives, reflecting on the complexities of cultural identity and the effects of colonialism."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013282472157 gid://shopify/Product/9013282504925

item.title: Smiso Cele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932574941 Smiso Cele 2352 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641075560669 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014091251933"] [24490] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Smiso Cele (b. 11/02/2002) in KwaZulu Natal, Port Shepstone. Cele is currently living in Johannesburg, practicing as an artist and completing his third year of his BA in Visual Arts at the University of Johannesburg. In his latest works he’s been exploring his interest in printmaking and drawing, trying to merge the two. \\n \\nAs per Cele's prolonged desire to be an artist, he chose Visual Arts as a subject in high school (Olwandle High School). During his high school days, Cele attended numerous workshops (Woodblock workshop with Ben Ntsusha at Margate Art Museum, in 2020) and painted murals by means of elevating his artistic abilities in terms of mediums and skills. In exploring different mediums as per his interest to break through the conventions of drawing, Cele curated a show/drawing invention at Stokvel Gallery. The Exhibition functioned as a drawing in a sense that the gallery space worked as substrate to which he placed/made marks by placing selected artworks on the walls, feeding into his understanding of what drawing is. \"Drawing is a continuous process of placing/making marks on a surface\". \\n \\nHe has participated in a few exhibitions, namely UJ's Best of the Best exhibition at Art and Collect Gallery in 2020, Margate Art Museum in 2022 and Best of the Best exhibition at Art and Collect Gallery in 2023. As he is in completion of his undergraduate degree, he's also been working as a studio assistant at Subotzky studio. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014091251933

item.title: Snelihle Maphumulo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932640477 Snelihle Maphumulo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641075953885 [] Explore the work of Snelihle Maphumulo, a contemporary South African artist featured on Latitudes Online. Through a bold and expressive style, Maphumulo’s art delves into themes of identity, culture, and personal storytelling, offering a powerful visual narrative. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Snelihle Maphumulo is South African artist, born and raised in Durban KZN. She is a 2024 Sasol New Signatures finalist and Merit Award winner. Maphumulo has exhibited her works at the 2023 and 2024 National Arts Festival where she also worked as a Gallery Custodian. \\nShe is a practicing artist whose work delves deep into the intersection of gender, tradition, material, and societal critique. Maphumulo decided to pursue art as a way to explore personal and cultural narratives, particularly how traditions evolve and maintain relevance over time. Her artistic journey became an avenue to express complex ideas about her identity, faith and history, all of which resonate deeply within Maphumulo's practice. \\nSculpture, as a medium, has long been a space for three-dimensional exploration, allowing Maphumulo to manipulate and transform materials into tangible expressions of form, meaning, and metaphor. The tradition of working with found materials brings a unique dimension to her practice, as it involves recontextualizing objects that carry their own history. \\nMaphumulo's choice to work in sculpture stems from a fascination with form, texture, and the physicality of materials. The use of found materials, especially sheep hide and cow hide, draws from both personal and cultural experiences. These materials evoke ideas of heritage, religion, and the relationship between the natural world and human culture. Their organic qualities create a visceral connection to the past, while their manipulation within Maphumulo's sculptures speaks to contemporary narratives of adaptation, and transformation. \\nMaphumulo's work is a conversation between material, tradition, and society, constantly negotiating the boundaries of freedom and control. Through sculpture, Maphumulo invites viewers to question what is hidden, what is erased, and what continues to persist despite efforts to silence it. \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Sol
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641932902621 Sol gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076150493 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013355282653","gid://shopify/Product/9013355774173","gid://shopify/Product/9013355872477"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sol is a first-generation Eritrean South African. Having experienced life through various lenses, she's learnt to develop a strong sense of story. \\n \\n'Understanding that despite all our differences, we're all fundamentally the same. We all want peace, love, and to feel valued and heard. Wherever you go on this planet, you will always meet people with dreams and stories they want to share. That's the secret to great storytelling. Understanding.' \\n \\nSol has worked as a producer and scriptwriter in the South African Film and Television industry for the past few years. She aspires to create co-production across the African continent and bring our uniquely African stories to the rest of the world with an emphasis on showing the beautiful capabilities and strengths that lie in African stories."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013355282653 gid://shopify/Product/9013355774173 gid://shopify/Product/9013355872477

item.title: Solomon Geleta
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641933754589 Solomon Geleta gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076281565 [] Solomon Geleta Urgessa is an Ethiopian visual artist known for his evocative figurative paintings that delve into human emotions, identity, and societal dynamics. His work has been showcased at Post Gallery in Addis Ababa and featured in the 2024 FNB Art Joburg Fair. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Solomon Geleta Urgessa (b. 1990) is a full-time studio artist based in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in painting from the Addis Ababa University Alle School of Fine Arts and Design in 2018. Following in the footsteps of his brother Asrat Urgessa and Tesfaye Urgessa (60th Venice Biennial - Ethiopia Pavilion) who graduated from the same school in 2004 and 2006, respectively Solomon also studied under the influential Ethiopian modernist artist Tadesse Mesfin. \\nSolomon focuses on capturing the essence of daily urban life within the broader community. His artwork serves as a critical commentary on the constantly evolving social and political structures. As an emerging artist, Solomon is actively developing his unique visual language, drawing inspiration from the works of his former mentor, Tadesse Mesfin, and his older brother, Tesfaye Urgessa. Solomon, who prefers oil painting because he believes it enables him to capture the nuances of the flesh effectively, portrays figures that make direct eye contact with the viewer. In his most recent collection titled \"Connections,\" the artist delves into the political and social implications of engaging with and consuming information in the realm of social media. \\nSolomon Urgessa is currently represented by Post Gallery Ethiopia, which showcased his works at the FnB Joburg 2024 Art Fair. Moreover, he has been involved in numerous exhibitions hosted by the Addis Ababa Museum, Alliance Ethio-Française, Addis Ababa City Hall, and the Sheraton Addis. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Solomon Omogboye
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641933787357 Solomon Omogboye gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076412637 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Solomon Omogboye was born in 1982 in Lagos. He had his early education in Lagos before proceeding to \\nLagos State Polytechnic with HND in ART AND INDUSTRIAL DESIGN (PAINTING) in 2007. He was awarded AADS best Artist of the Year in 2007. \\n \\nHe is a prolific painter. Encouraged by his mother, a teacher, Omogboye was introduced to drawing as a child. He has worked extensively as an art instructor in secondary schools in Lagos after his graduation and also \\npractice art from his home studio. His paintings are a reflection of his thoughts, inspiration and ideas. The \\n artists mainly uses charcoal, pastel, acrylic and oil on canvas. \\n \\nOmogboye relocated to South Africa in 2014 where he worked as full time artist from his home studio and the Living Artists Emporium, Johannesburg. He is currently based at August House studios in Johannesburg, South Africa. Omogboye's works has attracted local and international attention over the years. He ranks among the young leading Nigerian artists."}]}]}

item.title: Sonia Martins Mateus
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641933852893 Sonia Martins Mateus 2948 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641076969693 [] Explore the poetic, material-rich works of Sonia Martins Mateus, a French–Portuguese artist whose installations using site-specific ash, soot, wood, and mythic creature sculptures navigate memory, displacement, and vernacular culture. Exhibited in Cape Town, Bern, and Caen. [25381,25382,25380] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"As a result of her Portuguese family’s complex heritage of displacement and movement, Sonia Martins Mateus travels through remote, rural, arid and desert territories to inform her practise. Collecting materials, documents and testimonies, her work unfolds in different forms; sculptures, drawings, photographs or ‘landscape-sculptures’ (installations) - all of which are traces of a personal and collective history, of a culture that is popular as it is universal. Mateus’ work has a poetic quality that is both gentle and brutal, a strange in-between where our relationship with our origins lies,familial geographical or social. In 2019 Martins Mateus graduated from ESAM Caen with honours in History and Fine Arts. After a number of exhibitions, she was awarded a residency at the Cité Internationnale des Arts in 2022, resulting in a visual and sound performance at the Musée des Beaux Arts in Caen. After her first international exhibition in 2023, The Invisble Thread, at the AVA Gallery in Cape Town, South Africa, she went on to perform in Bern during the summer season while being based in Normandy with a studio at the art factory Le Bazarnaom. In 2025, Martins Marteus returnedto South Africa for a creative and research residency in the Klein Karoo, at GO Residency in Oudtshoorn."}]}]}

item.title: Sophia Oshodin

Inspired by African arts and contemporary culture, her work examines mental health and uses art as healing. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sophia Oshodin is a self-taught figurative painter from London. Her captivating paintings depict candid moments of everyday domestic life, often placing her figures in their comfort zones. Sophia challenges stereotypes and delves into metaphysics, exploring how culture and perception influence life. Her imaginary subjects, inspired by scenes from memory and popular culture, executed in oil and acrylic. \\nSophia places her subjects in ordinary settings to understand the complexities of human experience in society, examining the impact of mental health and using art as a form of healing. \\nHer practice documents the human experience, focusing on the interaction between body and space, and overlaying the past with the present through shared memory. Sophia's work communicates the fundamental nature of reality through a colorful emotional dialogue that engages viewers in their own interpretations. \\nShe draws inspiration from African arts, art history, the Old Masters, contemporary arts, fashion, politics, and colors. Sophia's work has been exhibited nationally and internationally at various fairs, including the Affordable Art Fair Hampstead, 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair - Marrakech, and The Other Art Fair Exhibition."}]}]}

item.title: Sophie Mahlangu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641934934237 Sophie Mahlangu 2438 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641077625053 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013975089373", "gid://shopify/Product/9133229408477", "gid://shopify/Product/9133229441245"] [20914] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nguni beadwork is a vibrant form of communication among Zulu and Ndebele peoples, evolving from traditional materials like bone and shells to colorful plastic beads. Renowned Zulu beadworks express intricate societal themes through their shapes and patterns. \\n \\nSouth African musician Sophie Msoziswa Mahlangu gained international recognition for her exceptional beadwork, winning the 2020 Innibos National Craft Awards in the Beading Category. Her winning entry, a pair of intricately beaded bicycles, showcased her originality and skill, inspired by her mother's craftsmanship. \\n \\nBased in Gamorwa, Mpumalanga, Mahlangu sells her beadwork through Nomhlekhabo Craft Africa, catering to both local ceremonial needs and tourist interests. She advocates for women's empowerment through craft and educates others in traditional Ndebele arts alongside Dr. Esther Mahlangu. \\n \\nMahlangu emphasizes the importance of perseverance and originality, both in her own work and in mentoring her children and students. Through her efforts, she continues to inspire and preserve the rich cultural heritage of Southern African beadwork. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013975089373 gid://shopify/Product/9133229408477 gid://shopify/Product/9133229441245 gid://shopify/Product/9133231014109

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935032541 Sophie Peters gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078051037 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. item.title: Sophie Smith
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935098077 Sophie Smith 2542 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078149341 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014018212061","gid://shopify/Product/9014018277597","gid://shopify/Product/9014018310365"] Discover the evocative work of Sophie Smith, a lifestyle photographer based in Kenton on Sea, South Africa. Her images blend documentary photography with fine art, capturing the intimate dynamics between women, children, and nature, and evoking deep emotions through the magic of everyday moments. [22462,22463,22464] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sophie Smith (b. 1988) is a lifestyle photographer based in Kenton-on-Sea in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. Her creative journey is a mirror of her personal evolution, embarking on a path of introspection and healing while documenting tender moments of motherhood and her children's lives. This journey has fueled her fascination with the intimate dynamics between women, children, and nature, particularly the healing properties of water. \\nTrained as a photojournalist, Sophie practiced documentary-style photography for many years. However, it was only after having children that she began to blend documentary photography with fine art, creating images that evoke emotion rather than just capturing moments. Sophie's work is an artistic documentation of life, capturing both the big moments and the small, seemingly mundane ones, in a way that allows viewers to relive the depth and soul of those experiences. \\nSophie's philosophy revolves around the collaboration between the photographer and the subject, capturing authentic and intimate moments in the most beautiful way when the subjects feel relaxed and confident. She believes in creating a sweet spot between storytelling and art, capturing the magic that already exists within her subjects. \\nDeeply inspired by life, nature, and her children, Sophie is obsessed with light and shadow and how they dance together. Her ability to blend storytelling with art has been nurtured over the years, allowing her to see what others might not notice and turn it into magical photographs. Living near the ocean in Kenton on Sea, Sophie finds daily inspiration and a sense of freedom, but she also loves the feeling of being on the road in search of new adventures."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014018212061 gid://shopify/Product/9014018277597 gid://shopify/Product/9014018310365

item.title: Sotiris Moldovanos
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935196381 Sotiris Moldovanos gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078477021 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sotiris Moldovanos (b.1977) was born in Johannesburg and obtained a B.Tech degree in Fine Arts from the Pretoria Technikon (now known as the Tshwane University of Pretoria) in 1999. \\n \\nMoldovanos focuses on painting, with a preference for portraiture and figurative work as subject matter. These figures, while anatomically accurate, are simplified and flattened to become outlines and silhouettes. He would often hide the figures, providing clues of its existence through the use of vibrant patterns reminiscent of op art and hard-edge abstraction. \\n \\nIn his recent work, Moldovanos incorporates bold flat colours with geometric patterns to create a sense of optical illusion. He plays with positive and negative spaces and blurs the lines between subject and background. The result is a surreal illusion where the viewer experiences uncertainty. This is extended with the use of realistically painted elements that are juxtaposed with the abstract patterns, offering clues to possible varied meanings. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Souad Abdel Rassoul

Her works have been on display since 1998, mainly in exhibitions in Egypt. \\n \\nBesides designing book covers and children’s books, she conducts art workshops for children in and outside Egypt. \\n \\nSouad Abdel Rassoul lives and works in Cairo."}]}]}

item.title: Souad Mardam Bey
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935360221 Souad Mardam Bey gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641078903005 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Mardam Bey's oversized canvases are brimming with undercurrents of emotion; layers of color and intricate details which adorn her subjects, yet it is their eyes that leave you spellbound. Trapped behind hauntingly beautiful irises are tales derived from life. \\n \\nHer palette alternates from one painting to another; through scarlet backgrounds, violet turbans, and orange cloaks - the artist professes her passion for color. Still, she grants each of her subjects a colorful, melancholic persona. Their plush lips are sealed, fencing in their deepest secrets, while their eyes ratify an ethereal disposition. \\n \\nThe artist has seen her subjects a million times before, either lurking around or speeding past her on the streets - and all around her head. It is humankind, which drives this artists paint brush. Yet Mardam Bey does not simply produce snapshots of your everyday man and woman - she creates a community of otherworldly creatures, held captive to her use of overpowering colors and entrancing techniques. \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Sphatho Mzantsi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641935392989 Sphatho Mzantsi ["gid://shopify/Product/9013943730397"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Sphatho Mzantsi is a South African artist. He was born in 1995 in Mthatha, South Africa. He completed his BA in Fine Arts Degree at the University of the Free State, South Africa. Mzantsi’s interests include the exploration of the idea of living across multiple cultures that intersect at the periods of post- \\napartheid, the post-colonial, and an increasingly globalized world. He explores 'indawo elalini ne engekhoyoe Dolophini (Rural Place and City Displacement)', a concept that ruminates on the displacement of African/indigenous people in Western culture within intra-African migrations. His preferred mediums include pit, charcoal, ballpoint pen, video, photography and painting. \\nMzantsi is a member of the Free State Art Collective (FAC) and has been included in group exhibitions at the Johannes Stegmann Art Gallery, the 2019 Vryfees Festival and at Gallery 2 in Johannesburg. In 2020 he was part of the Turbine Art Fair, another group exhibition at Gallery 2 and was part of the Sasol New Signatures at the Pretoria Art Museum in 2021. He is a resident of Occupying the Gallery; the project aims to transform gallery spaces into makeshift open studios for mentorship and artistic development. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013943730397
