[23126,23127,23128,23129,16766,20610,10913,23124,23130,23131,15546] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tessa Teixeira (b. 1969, Ermelo, South Africa) is a visual artist who completed a Bachelor's in Primary Education, majoring in Art, in 1991 through the University of the Witwatersrand. Her self-portrait from that time was preserved by the JCE Arts Department. \\nIn her twenties and thirties, Tessa was deeply involved in projects addressing housing access in lower-income sectors. She founded an NGO, raised funds to build two primary schools for children who were receiving tuition under trees, and worked with The Mineworkers Development Agency, the development wing of The National Union of Mineworkers, addressing rural development and economic needs in South Africa. \\nIn 2006, Tessa began to actively focus on her art practice, participating in various short art development programs in San Francisco and London in 2010 and 2011. She returned to Johannesburg at the end of 2011 and has since been developing her practice, focusing on Existential Philosophy and Ecology—Climate narratives, aligned with materiality exploration in Mixed Media, Painting, Installation, and Printmaking. \\nSince 2012, Tessa has exhibited, auctioned, and sold work for private collections in local and international group shows. Some recent exhibitions include: ‘1.5 Degrees’ in Berlin, Germany (2021), ‘What’s next for earth? - Depletion’ – MAHB, Stanford University, USA (2021), ‘Enviro Art gallery 2021’ – Dukes University, USA (2021), ‘Amref Artball Auction – pre-featured on Artsy – New York (2019), ‘Optimism’ Endless Editions Biennial in New York (2018), ‘Art of Lithography’ - The University of the Witwatersrand Museum (WAM), and a solo show - ‘Nothing stands still’ - Johannesburg Holocaust & Genocide Centre (2018)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013354430685 gid://shopify/Product/9013425635549 gid://shopify/Product/9013443526877 gid://shopify/Product/9013452275933 gid://shopify/Product/9013959164125 gid://shopify/Product/9014036922589 gid://shopify/Product/9014036955357 gid://shopify/Product/9014036988125 gid://shopify/Product/9014037086429 gid://shopify/Product/9014037119197 gid://shopify/Product/9014037250269 gid://shopify/Product/9014037283037

item.title: Teresa Kutala Firmino
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954070749 Teresa Kutala Firmino 670 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109311709 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013436219613","gid://shopify/Product/9013436285149","gid://shopify/Product/9013438546141","gid://shopify/Product/9014058647773","gid://shopify/Product/9014072443101","gid://shopify/Product/9014102819037","gid://shopify/Product/9014102851805"] Teresa Kutala Firmino is a multimedia artist based in Johannesburg, exploring trauma, collective history, and the resilience of women in post-colonial Africa. Her work delves into themes of identity preservation, personal and collective trauma, and the complexities of living with past and present struggles. Firmino’s art uses vibrant, surreal scenes to rebuild African history and challenge the legacy of colonialism and civil conflict. [24119,24777,24778,16069,16148,16070,23791] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"We heal by retelling our stories. \\nTeresa Kutala Firmino’s work negotiates trauma both personal and collective in her everyday life. Her paintings are constructed scenes of the past and present, which are sometimes intertwined. Firmino carefully collects images from magazines, newspapers, historical documents and social media, and places them in colourful, box-like stages. This creates surreally baroque scenes which take place in tightly confined interiors, where the characters have the opportunity to re-enact their stories or construct new ones. This process allows Firmino to create alternative past, present and future narratives of Africa, thus rebuilding her own archive of African history. \\nFirmino seeks to investigate the trauma that African people in her community and beyond have experienced and continue to experience due to colonisation, civil wars and present day obstacles. Her own stories begin with the collective trauma of Pomfret. Located in the North West Province of South Africa, and the place where she was born, Pomfret is a community of former 32 Battalion soldiers and their families, many of whom settled there after the end of the South African Border War. \\nColonial rule and the trauma it induced forced many African people to cling to one another in a common cause, which was to create free and independent countries. Africans, though constantly reminded that they were seen as less than human, held on to what reminded them of their humanity: their communities and their struggles for freedom. Once they achieved a form of independence, though, many civil wars erupted, where the people who fought for the same freedom were caught in a new, raw struggle for power. These civil wars caused a second wave of trauma; suddenly the people one depended on for a sense of community and humanity now turned against each other. \\nBoth the women and men in the Pomfret community experienced these traumas – but it is the women who were subjected to further pain. Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is not only experienced by people who have been through a war. Firmino affirms that the women in the community experienced a second wave of trauma: rape, abuse, accidents and torture. The women clung to what gave them a sense of security and humanity, which were their husbands and the community. Many of them experienced abuse, and some were even killed by their partners. Those who survived could not trust the community for support, because society had normalised abuse against women. \\nKutala Firmino looks at how, despite the trauma they experienced, many of these women had to continue living with their abusers. The artist interrogates what it is about the black female body and mind which, despite trauma, continues to thrive. Is she truly living, or is she in constant melancholy as she exists in the aftermath of colonialism, civil war and betrayal? Is negotiating trauma realising that your abuser is possibly part the bigger of cycle of abuse? \\nTeresa Kutala Firmino is a multimedia artist, now based in Johannesburg, working with paint, photography and performance. She is part of a collective called Kutala Chopeto, which started as an investigation into their shared history which is linked to the 32 Battalion, the soldiers who were settled in Pomfret after the Border War. \\nCV \\nCOLLECTIVE EXHIBITIONS \\n2018 \\nKutala Chopeto, The Point of Order, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2017 \\nSilences in Between, Goodman Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa \\nNirox Sculpture Winter Fair, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThe Centre for the Less Good Idea Season 1, Arts on Main, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n [South-South] Let me begin again, Goodman Gallery, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2016 \\nBoda Boda Lounge Project, South Africa \\nHybrid Culture, MB Studio, Pretoria, South Africa \\nSELECTED GROUP & SOLO EXHIBITIONS \\n2021 \\nARCOLisboa, Everard Read, Lisbon, Portugal. \\n2020 \\nBlack Melancholy, solo booth, Investec Cape Town Art Fair, with Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\nStaring Straight to the Future, digital group exhibition, Everard Read, South Africa \\n2019 \\nTaxidermy of the Future, group show, Luanda Museum of Natural History, Angola \\nPseudo Restitution, solo, World Art, Cape Town, South Africa \\nThe War at Home, solo, Everard Read, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nTurbine Art Fair, with World Art, Johannesburg , South Africa \\nInvestec Cape Town Art Fair, with Everard Read, Cape Town, South Africa \\n2018 \\nEmergence, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nMasters solo show: Pomfret Community Stories, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThou Art Women, Mmarthouse, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nThe People’s Exchange, IDC Gallery, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nNow and Then, Trent Gallery, Pretoria, South Africa \\nProtagonist: Artists in Response to Sexual Violence, Studio Fracture, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2015 \\n14/15 exhibition, The Point of Order, Johannesburg, South Africa \\n2014 \\nThe African Utopia Lecture Series, University of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa \\nRESIDENCIES \\n2020 \\nFynbosch Residency, Franschhoek, South Africa"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013436219613 gid://shopify/Product/9013436285149 gid://shopify/Product/9013438546141 item.title: Thabang Molefe
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954267357 Thabang Molefe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109737693 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thabang Molefe was born in 1996 in Soweto, Johannesburg, where he currently resides. In 2015, he matriculated from Northcliff High School. \\nMolefe was a part of an NPO called Izinkhanyezi di Naledi community development in 2015-2017. The NPO aimed to educate High School children in Soweto about career choices. Molefe is also a vocalist, lyricist, music producer and photographer. Through Artist Proof Studio, he has participated in community-based projects such as revamping a primary school library. \\nIn 2018 Molefe completed his is third year at Artist Proof Studio mastering the print medium of Intaglio and relief printing. \\nArtist Statement: \\nIn my body of work, I explore the vulnerability of the masculine figure. I have used my own body as a source of reference in order to interrogate my own identity. The male figure in my works can be found in different foetal positions. This passive position challenges the stereotypical patriarchal role of the masculinity I experience in society. \\nI explore a range of atmospheric surfaces that interact with the passive figure. These emotive surfaces create a dialogue with the figure that at times create a contrast between the two. It is this relationship that creates a dream-like world and allows an escape from reality and from conforming to the social construct of masculinity."}]}]}

item.title: Thabo Motseki
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954365661 Thabo Motseki gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641109835997 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thabo Motseki's body of work explores a visual account as an attempt to record the rhythms and patterns of several periods in his life through lines and mark making. For him, the action of carving a lino plate is an act of removal and re-looking. The marks in/on the plate represent his interpretation of time and life as a rhythm, pulse, negotiation and pattern. He records the consistencies and inconsistencies in these concepts, represented as abstract, and open for negotiation and conversation. \\n \\nHis work is visually grounded on the African continent, yet it unpacks and negotiates urban themes and motifs such as healing, scarification and vibrations offered by his immediate environment, yet global in influence. \\n \\nThabo has had multiple solo exhibitions with notable studios and institutions such as Artist Proof Studio, 13th Floor Gallery, the Workers' Museum as well as Museum Africa. He has also worked as a printing technician at the Wits School of Arts, specializing in relief and printing process and silk-screening and Llithography Planographic printing processes. \\n \\nThabo is the co-founder and current CFO of the The Arts Company Soweto Pty Ltd (TACS)."}]}]}

item.title: Thalente Khomo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954595037 Thalente Khomo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111310557 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thalente Khomo, born 25 September 1995 at Gcilima in Margate, is a member of the Amasosha art Movement, a collective of young Durban-based artists that promotes hard work and solidarity among its members. \\n \\nIn her work, Khomo questions the exploitation of young adults, which leads to the exposing of their body as an object in adult life. She uses photographs as her preferred medium of expression. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Thamba Tabvuma
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954627805 Thamba Tabvuma gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111376093 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in Zimbabwe, Tabvuma showed great interest in his surrounding environment which he found expression in. Encouraged to find ways to portray how he interpreted his environment, he found his expression in art. \\nThamba studied art all his schooling days. In primary school he attended all the classes that were on offer. He remembers going to partake in pottery classes his mother was enrolled in. His desire for art was insatiable. Graduating from high school he again took all the art classes that were available. This resulted in him receiving his O’Levels in art and thereafter his A’Levels, in which he obtained a Distinction in Art. During this time he partook in several national competitions culminating in a First Prize in portrait. \\nHe has continued to follow his passion, participating in numerous exhibitions in his native Zimbabwe and South Africa. His work has found homes in many parts of the world. Over the years he has been a member of various Art groups, including being a member of the AVA gallery in 2009 and Work in Progress in 2013. \\nThamba has been drawing since he can remember, evolving from the use of pencil to ink. Currently, his medium of choice is oil. He continues on his journey. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Thami Jali
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954726109 Thami Jali gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111441629 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thami Jali was born Lamontville, Durban in 1955. He matriculated at Dlangezwa in KwaZulu Natal and started to study for a Law degree at the then University of Zululand when he met students from Rorke's Drift. This meeting was a pivotal moment for him as he decided to drop out of law to study at the Rorke's Drift Art Centre. \\n \\nThami Jali went on to study ceramics at the Natal Technikon. Later he moved to Johannesburg where he taught pottery and sculpture at Mofolo Art Centre in Soweto and also worked at the Kim Sacks Studio. \\n \\nThami Jali is said by Lionel Davis to have felt that many of his peers at the Rorke's Drift Art Centre were not sufficiently politicised, Jali has since commented that it was not only his peers that he tried to alert to the demands of the Struggle but also the wider community. This was made possible for him through the medium of prints, the democratic multiple. \\n \\nJali's work continued to deal with social and political issues and he was part of the movement focusing on mural art which emerged in each of the country's three major cities shortly after 1990. In Durban, Community Mural Projects was formally constituted by Terry-Anne Stevenson and Thami Jali (later joined by Ilse Mikula) in 1991. One of their first murals dealt with AIDS awareness. Whilst in Durban he coordinated The BAT Visual Arts Studio which provided a space and facilities for artists who would otherwise not have been able to produce work. \\n \\nIn the mid-1990's he moved to Nelspruit in Mpumalanga. At The Matsulu Centre, Jali was involved in training youth in ceramics with the support of the Department of Arts and Culture. It was here that he became aware of the work of outsider artist Nukain Mabuza. \\n \\nIn 2004 he returned to Rorkes Drift, to assist in re-establishing the ceramics studio there with the support of Khumbulani Afrika. Since then he has established his studio in Durban. \\n \\nHis work is represented in the collections of the Durban Art Gallery, Tatham Art Gallery, The Constitutional Court and the University of KwaZulu Natal as well as in numerous private collections."}]}]}

item.title: Thamsanqa Kiti
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954791645 Thamsanqa Kiti 2555 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111638237 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013964210397"] Thamsanqa Kiti [20776] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thamsanqa 'Thami' Eddie Kiti was born in 1968 in Machabini, a village near Queenstown in the Eastern Cape. He has lived in Khayelitsha since his early youth. \\nIn the late 1980s and 90s, Thamsanqa Kiti attended Community Arts Project (CAP) at St Philips in Woodstock, and took classes in carving, drawing, painting and print making under Mario Sickle, Lucy Alexander, Lionel Davis, Lovell Friedman and Sipho Hlati. \\nWorking mainly as a carver, Thamsanqa Kiti has had his work included on various exhibitions including: ‘Thami Kiti and Wanini Hill’ at the UCT Irma Stern Museum in 1995; ‘Engaging the Shadows’, Robben Island, 1997; ‘Homecoming’, Gug’Sthebe, Langa, 2001; ‘Against the Grain’, 2013, Iziko South African National Gallery curated by Mario Pissarra; ‘my whole body changed into something else’, Stevenson gallery, 2021 curated by Sisipho Ngodwana and Sinazo Chiya; and ‘Seeds of the Fig’ an exhibition curated by RESERVOIR in collaboration with Whatiftheworld for Krone in Tulbagh, 2023. He participated in the Thapong International Artists Workshop in Gaborone in 1996 as well as a number of workshops in Cape Town and Pretoria. Thamsanqa Kiti worked for the Handspring Puppet Company from 2008-2011, and has produced a number of his own unique articulated and puppet animals. In 2017, he was the winner of the Craft Award for his carved initiation staffs for the Innibos Laeveld Nasionale Kunstefees in Mbombela. He was commissioned to create a large temporary public sculpture, a mosaic hybrid figure of a bride, Umakhoti, for an outdoor exhibition, ‘Reflections’, in Stellenbosch in 2015; a staff with a leopard, Ingwe Izidla Ngamabala, for the UCT Vice-Chancellor’s annual Award for Transformation in 2019; and a carved broom with a bird as part of Jane Alexander’s installation Infirmary, 2014, 2019. He has artwork in the Robben Island Collection, the collection of William Humphreys Art Gallery in Kimberley, the Community Arts Project Collection at the University of the Western Cape, and numerous private collections. \\nThamsanqa Kiti’s works make direct reference to Xhosa culture, particularly birth, initiation, marriage and death in relation to the earth. They sometimes combine hybrid forms, particularly human and goat features, and other animals that hold cultural significance such as Inqaqa (civet) and Inganda (serval). His most recent work includes carved and decorated staffs with mounted animal figures that often refer to initiation, and individual animals composed of multiple types of wood, some with elaborate inlay."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013964210397

item.title: Thami Nonceba Dwanya
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641954758877 Thami Nonceba Dwanya 2913 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111539933 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014103638237","gid://shopify/Product/9014103671005","gid://shopify/Product/9014103703773","gid://shopify/Product/9014103736541"] Discover the vibrant and thought-provoking work of Thami Nonceba Dwanya, a South African artist exploring identity, culture, and social narratives. Explore their artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [24812,24811,24809] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Nonceba Thami Dwanya (b. 2000, Pretoria). Nonceba is a young, black female artist who explores and utilises art to understand unconfronted parts of herself. Excelling in fine arts/ multidisciplinary portraiture she unpacks layers of understanding using paint and drawing mediums, charcoal and ink. \\nMotho ke motho ka batho. \\nAlthough one’s experience is personal to themselves it is not singular, as it is shared in a space with and amongst equal and opposite singular experiences. \\nSelf understanding is “the awareness of and ability to elaborate/explain that which is considered a being which distinguishes from others, especially considered as the object of introspection or reflexive action”. This abstract idea has been the topic of my work, expressed in the form of portraiture which looks at others and self for and from both others and self. Life is an experience that is personal to both the experience, but is just as personal to the those \\naround the experience as it is to the experience. In simple terms, self doesn’t and can’t exist without others. \\nLooking beyond the simplicities of the face, my practice uses colour, and texture to unpack reflection of myself in others and the perspective of others through the subject. Through layers of paint, drawing mediums, collaging, texture and colour this is a complex relationship which I unpack in my work. Silhouettes play a vital role in the visual respesenstion of presence and absence simultaneously, thus using silhouettes of existing objects or co-subjects allow me to highlight the absence and presence of others in the understanding of self, prioritising and emphasising balance/coexistence as the basis for one’s relationship with themselves. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014103638237 gid://shopify/Product/9014103671005 gid://shopify/Product/9014103703773 gid://shopify/Product/9014103736541

item.title: Thandazani Ndlovu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955021021 Thandazani Ndlovu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641111834845 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thandazani was born in the city of Bulawayo (Zimbabwe) – known to many as the gateway to Matobo National Park, but within the township of Nkulumane it was known for other reasons. Branded as the “City of Kings” due to the number of Kingdoms in the region – including close proximity to the Zulu Kingdom where King Shaka Zulu’s prowess reigned supreme. Today the city stands tall with monuments that reflect its royal past and ruins that date back as early as the 15th century. \\n \\nSpirited by a passion for the arts that began while in elementary school, where he would draw caricatures of his teachers and classmates, the self-taught figurative and impressionist artist’s career almost didn’t get off the ground. He went from this joyous experience to working in a shoe factory where he worked for almost 5 years before deciding to follow his dreams. He received his first big break after creating a series that featured the dying cultures of Africa. The works were revered by many, mostly due to the light they shone on African cultures and traditions, acting as a reminder to the elite and those that worked in places like the factory where he worked that we are all bonded by the same African roots. \\n \\nAfter several well-received series, Thandazani began exhibiting, and his works have showcased and featured at art festivals and galleries throughout Africa. This led to several commissioned works, one of which sits in the Newtown Workers Museum Cottages and the National Gallery of Zimbabwe. The full-time artist also finds time to give back to his community through his support of local orphanages and fundraising initiatives. He wishes to create awareness of social issues and making a difference for disadvantaged children all over the world. Today, his works are in gallery collections and art networks throughout the world."}]}]}

View their artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thando Phenyane (b. 1997, Johannesburg) is a figurative painter with a wide pool of influences. Trained as an architect, his process draws heavily on art history and pop culture, employing a unique painterly language that presents Black figures as dark, whimsical characters, at once comical and menacing. He took part in the 2021 Design Indaba Emerging Creatives programme and the 2021 V&A Waterfront Artist Alliance Programme."}]}]}

item.title: Thanduxolo Nombali Phakathi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955348701 Thanduxolo Nombali Phakathi 2456 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641113080029 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013928034525","gid://shopify/Product/9014012510429","gid://shopify/Product/9014012543197"] Explore the vibrant and evocative art of Thanduxolo Nombali Phakathi, a self-taught artist from KwaZulu Natal. Her mixed media works delve into themes of identity, womanhood, and human experience. Buy original art online and discover her unique visual storytelling. [22283,19352,22282] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thanduxolo Nombali Phakati (b. 1994, Greytown, KwaZulu Natal) is a self-taught artist who has developed a distinctive voice in the world of contemporary art. Raised in Dundee, where she currently resides, Thanduxolo began her artistic journey in 2019 as a means of escaping the demands of her academic studies at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology, from which she graduated with an undergraduate degree. \\nThanduxolo's art is characterized by a rich exploration of color, texture, and composition, drawing inspiration from her upbringing and the diverse environments she has encountered. Her work delves deeply into themes of identity, womanhood, and the human experience, often reflecting the nuanced interplay between belonging and otherness, familiarity, and the unknown. \\nHer artistic process involves a mix of traditional and contemporary drawing mediums, creating a visual language that is both vibrant and evocative. Thanduxolo's use of bold colors and intricate patterns brings a dynamic energy to her pieces, inviting viewers to engage with her personal narratives and the stories of the women who have influenced her life. \\nCurrently a featured artist in the upcoming exhibition 'Embodied Narratives,' Thanduxolo continues to captivate audiences with her innovative approach to visual storytelling. Her work not only serves as a reflection of her personal journey but also as an invitation for others to explore and appreciate the complexities of cultural identity and human connection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013928034525 gid://shopify/Product/9014012510429 gid://shopify/Product/9014012543197

item.title: Thania Petersen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955676381 Thania Petersen 2348 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641114063069 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013842739421","gid://shopify/Product/9013855387869","gid://shopify/Product/9013929476317","gid://shopify/Product/9013929574621"] [18441,19148,19373,19374] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thania Petersen (b. 1980, Cape Town) is a multi-disciplinary artist who uses photography, performance and installation to address the intricacies and complexities of her identity in contemporary South Africa. \\nPetersen’s reference points sit largely in Islam and in creating awareness about its religious, cultural and traditional practices. She attempts to unpack contemporary trends of Islamophobia through her analysis of the continuing impact of colonialism, European and American imperialism, and the increasing influence of right-wing ideologies. Threads in her work include the history of colonialist imperialism in Africa, Asia and the Middle East, as well as the social and cultural impact of westernised consumer culture. Her work is also informed by her Cape Malay heritage, and the practice of Sufi Islamic religious ceremonies. Petersen studied at Central Saint Martin’s College of Art in London. \\nShe has held solo exhibitions at WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town, the AVA, Cape Town and at the Everard Read Gallery, Cape Town. She has participated in numerous group exhibitions both locally and abroad. Recent exhibitions include ZAMUNDA FOREVER?????, Nicodim, Los Angeles (2023, solo); ??Galeria Nicodim, Bucharest: 10 Years, Galeria Nicodim, Bucharest (2023); 18th Venice Architecture Biennale (2023); Indigo Waves and other Stories, SAAVY Contemporary, Berlin (2023); Indigo Waves and other Stories, Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2022–2023); Artists’ Film International (traveling), Whitechapel, London, Istanbul Modern, Istanbul, Ballroom Marfa, Marfa, and others (2022); Can We Sing Together, Old Friend?, 32 Bis, Tunis (2022, solo); Triennale Kleinplastic Fellbach: The Vibration of Things, Alte Kelter Fellbach, Fellbach (2022); Where Do I Begin, Stevenson, Cape Town (2022); KASSARAM, Zeitz MOCAA, Cape Town (2021, solo); Indian Ocean Craft Triennial: Curiosity and the Rituals of the Everyday, Fremantle, Australia (2021); Self-Addressed, curated by Kehinde Wiley, Jeffrey Deitch, Los Angeles (2021); Un.e Air.e de Famille, Musée d’art et d’histoire Paul Eluard, Saint-Denis (2021); Between Land and a Raised Foot, National Arts Festival, Grahamstown, South Africa (2019, solo); Radical Love, Ford Foundation, New York (2019); and IQRA, WHATIFTHEWORLD, Cape Town (2019, solo). Her work is collected by the Smithsonian National Museum of African Art, Washington, D.C.; Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA), Cape Town; IZIKO South African Museum, Cape Town; Pérez Art Museum, Miami; and many others."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013842739421 gid://shopify/Product/9013855387869 gid://shopify/Product/9013929476317 gid://shopify/Product/9013929574621

item.title: Tharien Smith
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955709149 Tharien Smith gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641114357981 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THARIEN SMITH (1973 - ) \\n \\nTharien Smith was born in the Free State, schooled in Johannesburg and studied and lived in Pretoria for the past 23 years. She graduated with a National Textile Diploma from Tshwane University of Pretoria (1995) and has spent most of her career working in various different creative, corporate environments designing anything from furnishing fabrics/fashion, graphics and ceramic tiles. She has recently moved to Cape Town, South Africa, in order to focus more on her art and design work.?Tharien’s first solo exhibition Indians vs Nature (2007) was held at the Gallery on the Corner, Johannesburg, and most recently she took part in the Flow Group Art Exhibition (2016), 196 Victoria Road, Cape Town. Fascinated with nature, archeology, human anatomy, perspective and chiaroscuro, Tharien loves to experiment and explore new techniques. \\n \\nShe lives by the words of Ronny Garcia Moton, which she freely interprets: '' Living life changed the perspective I had about life and also showed me that I can create whatever I wanted without limits, that I could make my own worlds and that I was the owner of my own story and that I was allowed to create them as I imagined them.”"}]}]}

item.title: Thato Mabaso
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641955774685 Thato Mabaso gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650759553245 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thato Mabaso, artistically known as Director P, is a self-taught photographer and aspiring Director of Photography. Born and bred in Kagiso, Johannesburg, Mabaso discovered his natural mode of expression through his photography and videography practice, which has only enhanced his true passion for art. \\n \\nHis current focus is portraiture, videography and fashion photography. He has worked in the commercial industry since 2018, but remains rooted in the township scene as co-founder of Kasi Vogue - a platform for township-groomed creatives to empower themselves by expressing the core of their everyday existence. Recently, he has been working on collaborative projects which combine various disciplines such as photography, illustration, music and movement, while focusing specifically on developing his videography practice. Mabaso believes that, through his representation of characters and spaces, he can potentially provide alternative portrayals of South African narratives and culture."}]}]}

Explore their practice on Latitudes Online. [23861,24839,24840,23882] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thato Makatu (b. 2000 Oslo) is a South African artist/cultural producer in training and printmaker from Boksburg. Makatu completed their Honours in Curatorship at the Michaelis School of Fine Art, University of Cape Town (UCT). Born in Norway and having moved across the world several times during their childhood, their artistic work is concerned with working through notions of home and stability through the physical aspects of domestic spaces. \\nThey Engage with questions of how these spaces interact with evocations of memory and formation of identity.Because of their dislocated upbringing, Thato has used their art to work through howthe home is constructed both physically and socially. Focusing on how the domestic space interacts with our memories, and how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time, the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people. Through their Hons in Curatorship, they have become increasingly interested inhow homemaking practices exist culturally, and how the family can be a way to navigate research and access cultural identity in the home. \\nThato's work thinks through how the domestic space interacts with our memories, how objects in the home are activated in our memories through time and the many interactions we have with these objects and with other people."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014060843229 gid://shopify/Product/9014061301981 gid://shopify/Product/9014104522973 gid://shopify/Product/9014104555741

item.title: Thato Toeba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641956823261 Thato Toeba 1170 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641124843741 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013318516957"] [7498] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thato Toeba is a Lesotho artist and legal scholar currently called flattendacurve (b.1990, Maseru). She shares visuals of continuing thoughts on personhood, politics, propaganda, nationality, globalisation, law and culture. Her work is influenced by her suspicion of formal things (culture law, politics, institutions,) as sober, objective, neutral tools in resolving growing crises of being here in the world today. She speculates on the intrusion of formal things in the emancipated joy of life, womb to tomb and fantasises about some kind of sweet chaos to be master in a less theorised life. \\nShe is a LLD candidate at UWC."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013318516957

item.title: The Strategic Radicals
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641965736157 The Strategic Radicals gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641124974813 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"The Strategic Radicals’ Manifesto was formulated in Windhoek in January of 2020. Stemming from the collaborative exhibition and discussion group FAVT – Future Africa Visions in Time – engaged with conversations around knowledge production in the context of institutions and African futures. The project initially launched in Germany in 2015 resulting in a traveling exhibition spanning Nairobi, Johannesburg, Salvador da Bahia, Windhoek, Harare and Ouagadougou thus far. Further editions will travel to Kigali, Kampala and Santiago/Cuba. The design presents a glimmering yellow cover paper held together by a bright green rubber band. The heraldic animal is designed by Emeka Alams. It embodies the manifesto in a visual form, and also appears in the silk-screen artist edition you find on the next pages."}]}]}

[24191,24210,24199,23597,23598] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thebe Phetogo (b. 1993, Botswana) is an artist whose work blends figurative and abstract landscapes painting to explore themes of race, Setswana geography, and indigenous knowledge. Drawing inspiration from sacred caves and African mythology, his art reflects on the concept of origins and personal identity, offering a unique perspective on how individual experiences shape our understanding of the world. \\nThrough his work, Phetogo seeks to make visible the distinct “world-version” he carries. As the artist himself states, “Each of us ‘makes’ the world. In other words, it is our positionality that allows us to imagine each of our own immediate worlds. In my work, I endeavour to make visible the specific ‘world-version’ I carry.”"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014051406045 gid://shopify/Product/9014051504349 gid://shopify/Product/9014076834013 gid://shopify/Product/9014077227229 gid://shopify/Product/9014077718749

item.title: Thelma van Rensburg
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641956987101 Thelma van Rensburg gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641125269725 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013338505437","gid://shopify/Product/9134149107933"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thelma van Rensburg was born in Pretoria, South Africa in 1969. In 2004 she decided to study art full time and received her B.Tech degree in Fine Arts at Tshwane University of Technology in 2007. She completed a further Honours degree in Fine arts at the University of Pretoria in 2013 and completed a Masters of Arts degree in Fine Arts at the University of Pretoria in 2016. She has participated in nine solo exhibitions and numerous group exhibitions throughout South Africa. Her work has featured in prestigious competitions such as Sasol New Signatures, Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Awards and the Sanlam Vuleka Arts competition."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013338505437 gid://shopify/Product/9134149107933

item.title: Themba Given Msiza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963180253 Themba Given Msiza gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641126056157 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Given Msiza (b. 1986) creates artworks that may evoke a sense of déjà vu for those familiar with his previous exhibitions, particularly his 2019 show titled Asia (As So Is Africa) at the Pretoria Art Museum. The current body of work continues to explore themes of immigration, inequality, hard labor, and xenophobia in South Africa. \\nWhile inspired by his surroundings, Msiza's artwork delves into the emotions of regret, nostalgia, grief, and occasional joy that African immigrants in South Africa experience. He is also deeply influenced by the music of Motlapele Morule (Molemi), whose themes align with Msiza's focus on immigration and labor. As an ardent follower of Molemi's music, Msiza draws inspiration from the themes addressed in the music alongside his own personal themes \\n \\n \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Themba Khumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963278557 Themba Khumalo 330 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641126547677 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013937733853","gid://shopify/Product/9013937799389"] [19691,19692] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Benedict Khumalo was born on 16 February 1987 in Soweto, Johannesburg, South Africa. He graduated from Artist Proof Studio in printmaking, where he obtained a Design Foundation Certificate. He went on to do a professional printmaking development course under the sponsorship of Pinpoint One, at Artist Proof Studio in 2009 where he was an intern in the silkscreen unit and special project team. Khumalo is interested in exploring different mediums, such as charcoal drawings and painting. \\nKhumalo’ work is inspired by everyday day life. His visuals are stimulated by events he witnesses daily in the city such as everyday struggles, prospects and desires. He documents his interaction with the city as both an outsider and a city dweller. This dual tension is evident in his work; as he takes note of people who have come to the city in seek of the unknown. This is reflective in his work through his intense dark mark-marking and subtle texture of clouds, which evoke specific moods and emotions. \\nKhumalo’s work explores the dangers of Johannesburg while reflecting its beauty through its architecture and cityscape. Khumalo identifies in his work the importance of family and how they play an important role in one’s life. Although he hardly depicts human figures in his work, he uses pylons, cranes, and electric wires to represent movement, energy, and unity: portraying how electricity connects us all. Thus, informing his audience of his relationship with people, exploring feelings of connectivity and isolation within the city. \\nHe has been involved in number of group exhibitions, commissions and special projects; such as painting murals in the Eastern Cape and being invited to exhibit in a group show at Isolate del Cinema festival in Rome, Italy. He has exhibited widely and been on various residencies internationally since 2016. Khumalo works as an independent artist."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013937733853 gid://shopify/Product/9013937799389

item.title: Themba Mathenjwe
item.description: Themba Mathenjwe gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641126744285 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Under the shade of an indigenous Mpengende Tree, deep in rural Zululand, sits an artist of epic proportion. This is the home of Themba Mathenjwe. Born in 1967, Mathenjwe worked as a labourer and during his time off, whittled away at wooden sticks creating carved wooden animals. His natural talent was recognised by the late artist, Peter Engblom, who mentored him and Mathenjwe went on to study at the then Natal Technikon. \\n \\nMathenjwe gets inspiration from nature and his imagination. The branches of the tree, movement of clouds, and things all around him. He loves the use of bold and bright colours. His creatures are joyful and whimsical, many sporting a naughty attitude. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Themba Msiza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963376861 Themba Msiza gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641126777053 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in South Africa in 1987, Themba Given Msiza \\nis a self-taught artist who learned a lot of his trade through his work at The Pretoria Art Museum. \\n \\n\"In my abstract art, I simply try to achieve beauty through the combination of different colours. I have decided to work with a number of different colours, though which I try to convey a certain message, like the artworks I produced for the exhibition at the St'lorient art gallery in Pretoria titled \"The Gray Landscape.\" \\n \\nThese older artworks of a similar style were exhibited at the Pretoria art museum in 2013. I titled the artwork \"Nations Amalgamation\", that artwork, also using the multiple colours was observing or representing the coming of different African nationals into South Africa. Since my artworks try to comment on the issues of the foreign nationals that have come to our country and the treatment they receive from locals, despite this decision to remain in South Africa. \\n \\nMy artworks reflects or holds up a mirror on how detached we are as South Africans from the rest of the Continent.\""}]}]}

item.title: Themba Shabalala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963442397 Themba Shabalala 1349 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641127497949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014063988957"] [23937] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Themba Shabalala is a contemporary South African artist born in 1994. A totem award winner in 2015 and currently based in Johannesburg in an art community called August House, Themba Shabalala’s formal discipline lies in printmaking. He is predominantly engaged with fire and wood as a medium. He is currently exploring the concept of self-image, which is a reflection of his upbringing and his battle with an absent father figure. His work shows how he chooses to carry traits his mother has given him instead and how he learns to overlook his father’s physical absence. His work has been featured in several group exhibitions and has also been auctioned. Shabalala was one of 9 artists selected in Africa for the prestigious World Art Print in France."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014063988957

She completed her Bachelors of Technology in photography at the Durban University of Technology in 2017. \\n \\nThembi has participated in a number of notable local and international group exhibitions. Thembi is also a member of visual arts collectives in Durban, Amasosha Art Movement. Thembi’s artistic practice spans a variety of different disciplines and mediums. \\n \\nHer work explores the notions and politics surrounding ‘the body’, with her often using her own body as a site for her artistic exploration of these themes. item.title: Thembeka Heidi Sincuba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641963802845 Thembeka Heidi Sincuba gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641131626717 [] Explore the work of Thembeka Heidi Sincuba, a South African multidisciplinary artist and writer whose practice engages African spirituality, abstraction, and cultural discourse. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thembeka Heidi Sincuba is a multidisciplinary artist, writer, and educator born in Maphumulo, rural Kwa-Zulu Natal, with the German Christian Mission called Kwasizabantu. Sincuba began their arts education at Michaelis School of Fine Art in 2005 and earned a BFA from Artez Academy of Art in Arnhem, Netherlands in 2010 and an MFA from Goldsmiths University of London in 2014. \\n \\nObsessed with art and art history, Sincuba has served as an art and culture writer, contributor and/or editor at various publications including Art in Context, Mail &Guardian, Chimurenga, Bubblegum Club, ARAK Collection and ZAM Magazine. They were the Head of Painting at Rhodes University from 2017 to 2019 and during this time, they also taught a course on spirituality in art as a Guest Lecturer at the University of Cape Town. Sincuba is vice chair on the board of SWEAT (Sex Workers Education and Advocacy Taskforce), serving since January 2019. In 2021, they were the Artist in Residence at the Nordic Arts Association in Stockholm where they collaborated with renowned South African painter Lefifi Tladi, exploring Afro Abstraction and its connection to African spirituality. Sincuba’s most recent solo exhibition was at Galerie 23 in Amsterdam in October 2023, with a recent group show at Berman Contemporary in April 2024."}]}]}

His work has appeared in NICE Magazine 3rd Edition and group exhibitions at Fotomuseum Winterthur, IAF Basel Festival, and Johannesburg’s Turbine Art Fair. Thembinkosi Hlatshwayo is the Gisèle Wulfsohn Mentorship in Photography Recipient for 2019 and Slaghuis II is his first solo exhibition. \\nMoments in solitude allow Hlatshwayo quietness to process the noise, and the trauma, allowing for healing through the images he makes."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013389066461 gid://shopify/Product/9013389099229 gid://shopify/Product/9013389131997 gid://shopify/Product/9013397356765 gid://shopify/Product/9013397389533

Some time after her arrived in Johannesburg, he joined Artist Proof Studio to study printmaking part-time until 2002. \\n \\nSinalo's work lies in the interest expressing his culture and heritage - particularly the Zulu culture and its customs. He depicts the ceremonial rituals that members of his culture go through. Seeing the importance of ones roots and their lineage, he is best known for his works which depict the Reed Dance. [25600,25601,24539,24540,24541,25598,25599] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Born in 1980 in New York, Thenjiwe Niki Nkosi currently lives and works in Johannesburg. \\nNkosi obtained her BA from Harvard University (2004) and her MFA from the School of Visual Arts in New York (2008). She divides her time between studio work, performance, and navigating the field of art as social practice. Her work investigates the lived consequences of imperial histories and the personal dimensions of political identities, collectivity, and futurity, among other concepts. \\nArena V by the artist was exhibited as a site-specific mural and installation in the lobby of the Hammer Museum (2024). Nkosi presented, in collaboration with East Side Projects, the multimedia work Equations for a Body at Rest, across public spaces in Birmingham as part of the 2022 Commonwealth Games. Her solo exhibitions include Stadium, Stevenson, Amsterdam (2023); Landings, Stevenson, Cape Town (2022); Gymnasium, Stevenson, Johannesburg (2020); Gymnasium, The Africa Center, New York (2019); and The Beginning of Stories (Part 1 of Many), Seed Space/ Tri-Star Arts, Nashville, Tennessee (2017). \\nNotable group exhibitions include Movements, Museum Hilversum, the Netherlands (2024); In Terms of Sports, New Taipei City Art Museum, Taiwan (2024); Power Plays, Carnegie Museum of Art, Pittsburg, USA (2024);Thinking Historically in the Present, the 15th Sharjah Biennial, UAE (2023); Resistance Training: Arts, Sports, and Civil Rights, the Broad Museum of Art, Michigan State University (2023); Fix Your Pony, Naughton Gallery at Queen’s University, Belfast (2023); CHAMPS, Granville Centre Art Gallery, Cumberland (2023); Don’t Ask Me Where I’m From, Orlando Museum of Art, Florida (2023); THE GYM, Soho Studios, Vienna (2022); When We See Us: A Century of Black Figuration in Painting, Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa, Cape Town (2022) and Kunstmuseum Basel, Switzerland (2024); New Formations, deCordova Sculpture Park and Museum, Massachusetts, USA (2022); How to Make a Country, FRAC Poitou-Charentes, Angoulême, France (2021); Mixed Company, Norval Foundation, Cape Town (2021); Don’t Ask Me Where I’m From, Aga Khan Museum, Toronto (2020); NIEPODLEG?E, Women, Independence and National Discourse, Museum of Modern Art, Warsaw (2018); and Art Afrique, Le Nouvel Atelier, Fondation Louis Vuitton, Paris (2017), among others. \\nShe has participated in residencies including the Pala Lab (2018); XXVIIes Ateliers Internationaux, FRAC des Pays de la Loire, France (2013); VAIVEM, Sao Paulo, Brazil (2013); Vanilla Facts, Berlin (2012); Cruces International, Montevideo, Uruguay (2011); and the Bag Factory Artist Residency (2009). \\nShe has received grants from Pro-Helvetia (2019); Goethe-Institut (2018, 2010); National Arts Council of South Africa (2015, 2009); Virginia Wellington Cabot Foundation (2008); and fellowships, including the School of Visual Arts Alumni Award Fellowship (2006); Pforzheimer Foundation Public Service Fellowship (2006); and Mellon Mays Undergraduate Fellowship (2002). \\nNkosi is the recipient of the Helgaard Steyn Prize in Painting (2023); the Tollman Award for the Visual Arts (2019) and Philippe Wamba Prize in African Studies (2004) \\n \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014094168285 gid://shopify/Product/9014094233821 gid://shopify/Product/9014094299357 gid://shopify/Product/9132523061469 gid://shopify/Product/9133211910365 gid://shopify/Product/9133231800541 gid://shopify/Product/9133231898845

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641965670621 Thero Makepe 554 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641137721565 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013442674909", "gid://shopify/Product/9013442707677", "gid://shopify/Product/9013442773213", "gid://shopify/Product/9013442838749", "gid://shopify/Product/9013442871517", "gid://shopify/Product/9013442969821", "gid://shopify/Product/9013443002589", "gid://shopify/Product/9013443035357", "gid://shopify/Product/9013457682653", "gid://shopify/Product/9013468266717", "gid://shopify/Product/9013928886493", "gid://shopify/Product/9013928919261", "gid://shopify/Product/9013929050333", "gid://shopify/Product/9013929345245", "gid://shopify/Product/9013942124765", "gid://shopify/Product/9013942190301", "gid://shopify/Product/9013942354141", "gid://shopify/Product/9013942419677", "gid://shopify/Product/9013986722013", "gid://shopify/Product/9013986787549", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038036701", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038102237", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038135005", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038167773", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038233309", "gid://shopify/Product/9014038266077", "gid://shopify/Product/9014040199389", "gid://shopify/Product/9014040232157", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042493149", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042558685", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042591453", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042624221", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042689757", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042755293", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042788061", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042820829", "gid://shopify/Product/9014042886365", "gid://shopify/Product/9014078046429", "gid://shopify/Product/9014078210269", "gid://shopify/Product/9014078243037"] Discover the captivating multimedia art of Thero Makepe, a Botswana-born artist based in Gaborone, Cape Town, and Johannesburg. His photography, video, and installation works explore memory, history, and identity. Purchase original art that intertwines spirituality and regional histories, reflecting personal and collective narratives. [16440,16439,16438,16437,16436,21165,23148,21166,16973,23371,19369,23268,23145,20053,23365,24219,19366,24223,19365,24224,23367,19370,23359,21167,23369,20060,23146,20071,23147,23368,23358,23149,23357,20074,23144,17774,19372,23362,23269,19371] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thero Makepe (b. 1996, Botswana) is a multimedia artist whose practice spans photography, video, and installation, rooted deeply in the exploration of memory, history, and identity. Based between Gaborone, Cape Town, and Johannesburg, Makepe's work delves into the nuanced spaces between collective and personal memory, exploring how historical and cultural narratives shape contemporary identity. \\n \\nHis imagery often weaves together elements of spirituality and regional histories, focusing on the liminal spaces of social and familial relationships. Makepe reflects on his experiences and heritage in Botswana and South Africa, using visual storytelling to navigate themes of spirituality, diaspora, and transformation. His project have received international attention; he was awarded the prestigious MEP residency in Paris (2023), participated in the Invisible Borders Trans-African Road Trip (2022), and received the Diane and Charles Frankel Fellowship (2020). item.title: Thuli Lubisi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966031069 Thuli Lubisi 852 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641139654877 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013296496861", "gid://shopify/Product/9013296595165", "gid://shopify/Product/9014015819997", "gid://shopify/Product/9014056059101"] [22396,4349,4347,23721,4348] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Thuli Lubisi, a Johannesburg based visual artist and printmaker, was born in 1993 in Atteridgeville, Pretoria. In 2011 Lubisi completed her matric at P.J Simelane Secondary School and in 2013 she obtained a Computer Literacy certificate at Birnam Business College. Thuli then went on to study Visual art at Funda Art Centre in Diepkloof, Soweto during 2015. \\n \\nDuring 2016, Lubisi enrolled at Artist Proof Studio for a printmaking programme and, upon graduating, she began an internship at the Studios Education unit, assisting as a printmaking facilitator. \\n \\nSince 2017, Lubisi has been involved in various printmaking and mural projects as well as being part of group exhibitions such as the Joburg and Turbine Art fairs with Artist Proof Studio, in collaboration with Cartier and Strauss & Co respectively. In 2019 Lubisi was one of the artists commissioned by The Trinity Session to make artworks to be installed at the Leonardo Building; in addition Lubisi’s artworks have also been commissioned by the Bidvest bank SA and the HSBC bank. \\n \\nArtist Statement \\n \\nMy work is a celebration of African heritage and embraces our diversity. I combine patterns that derive from fabrics/textiles that are associated with different cultural groups, to make them hybrids. No pattern dominates or overpowers the other (suggesting cohesion); they create shapes that are a metaphor for a new landscape that is free from its historical, political and cultural constraints. \\n \\n‘Segregated’ and ‘Apart’ represent the new norm which has been created by this pandemic. The lives that we were accustomed to have been interrupted; because we’re separated from each other and there is now a void. As we slowly resume more normality I’m hoping that, with our differences, we can and will be able to form stronger and cohesive relations and keep the bonds that we have formed ‘intact’. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013296496861 gid://shopify/Product/9013296595165 gid://shopify/Product/9013296693469 gid://shopify/Product/9014015819997 gid://shopify/Product/9014056059101

He was represented by Art Eye Gallery and had his solo show titled “Soul Songs: The shape of my head.” \\nWhenever Mthiyane paints he plays a lot of jazz in the background and that also fuels his thought process. item.title: Tiaan van Deventer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966063837 Tiaan van Deventer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641139785949 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013847818461","gid://shopify/Product/9014030631133"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tiaan van Deventer is a multidisciplinary visual artist with analog photography being his primary medium of expression. His work also comprises a mixture of video, painting, sculpture, and assemblage. His art is first and foremost an investigation into the subconscious dystopian state of the human mind. He explores this and other darker Surrealist themes by means of framing paradoxical symbols onto the photographic emulsion. Images are made in-camera without any digital manipulations taking place. Male angst is a primary driver in his work, which can be seen with countless contorted male nude figures which are a recurring symbol in his work. His creative approach is grounded in reality with a documentary approach to his imagery. His latest project “Die Uitgewerptes” focuses on homeless Afrikaner men caught up in the battle of drug addiction."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013847818461 gid://shopify/Product/9014030631133

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966358749 Tilly de Harde gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641140637917 [] Meet Tilly de Harde, a South African fibre artist, educator, and Bernina quilting ambassador. Discover her innovative approach to contemporary quilting and textile art. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"With a career spanning three decades, Tilly de Harde is a contemporary South African fibre artist renowned for her innovative approach to quilting and textile manipulation. Her creative journey is driven by a passion for breaking traditional rules and reimagining the possibilities of fabric. In recognition of her significant contributions to the craft, she was chosen by Bernina to serve as an ambassador for quilting in South Africa. \\n \\nAs a fibre artist, de Harde is known for her experimental use of bright colours and diverse textures. Her work is the result of continuous study and invention, as she finds deep fulfillment in discovering and developing new techniques. This dedication to innovation allows her to transform conventional textiles into contemporary art. \\n \\nDe Harde is also a passionate and dedicated educator. She shares her extensive knowledge through a teaching practice designed to empower students with the confidence and skills to create their own unique artworks. Her enthusiasm for fabric manipulation inspires a new generation of textile artists and quilters. \\n \\nHer expertise has been recognized with numerous prizes for her quilts, both locally and internationally. In addition to her own artistic practice, de Harde offers a professional longarm quilting service, using her innovative skills to turn her clients' quilt tops into masterpieces."}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966457053 Timi Kakandar gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641140703453 [] Discover the work of Timi Kakandar, a leading Nigerian artist. Explore his large-scale abstract figurative paintings, known for their bold colours and Fauvist influences. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Timi Kakandar (b. 1979) is a leading Nigerian contemporary artist, celebrated for his imaginative and bold use of colour. A consummate painter and mixed-media artist, he is renowned for his striking, often large-scale abstract figurative paintings that have established him as a significant figure in the West African art sector. \\n \\nKakandar’s signature style is characterized by a deep fascination with the human form and spirit. His rich, expressive colour palette, reminiscent of both Fauvism and the vibrant spirit of Africa, captures the full range of human emotion with quiet intimacy and depth. He is unafraid to experiment with form and depiction, solidifying his reputation as a \"visual adventurer.\" \\n \\nThrough his evocative portraits, the artist explores themes of cultural identity, hope, and resilience. His recent body of work, in particular, is a powerful celebration of women and their essence. \\n \\nOne of Nigeria's most prolific artists, Kakandar has garnered a substantial international following. With four solo exhibitions and over thirty group shows to his name, his work has been exhibited extensively and is held in prominent private and museum collections worldwide."}]}]}

[24003] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tinsae Mesfin (b. 1998) is an emerging contemporary artist from Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. He is a 2022 graduate of the renowned Ale School of Fine Art and Design at Addis Ababa University, where he specialized in sculpture. Since graduating, he has dedicated himself to a rigorous studio practice, developing a distinctive and expressive artistic voice. \\n \\nMesfin's work is deeply influenced by key modern art movements, skillfully blending the structural innovations of Cubism and the bold colours of Fauvism with an overarching love for expressionism and figurative art. He draws inspiration from a wide range of sources—including photographs, friends, and his immediate surroundings—channeling the legacies of masters like Picasso and Matisse into a visual language that is uniquely his own. \\n \\nHis work has been actively exhibited in the Addis Ababa art scene. In 2024, he held his solo exhibition, “Beyond the Surface,” at Atmosphere and participated in the “New Voices” group exhibition at the Hayatt Regency. His work was also featured in the “Addis Art Exhibition” and his graduate show in 2022, marking a dynamic start to his professional career."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014066118877

[23870,24824,23875,21099,21097,23871,25463,25461,25464,25462] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tinyiko Makwakwa (b. 1984) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose process-driven studio practice is a deep investigation into African indigenous science and realities. Working primarily with textiles, she creates layered compositions of vibrant colour using ochre, glass beads, and stitch embroidery on umbaco, a fabric used in traditional Xhosa attire. \\n \\nAt the heart of Makwakwa’s work is the exploration of cultural materiality as a form of language. Her practice is centered on what she terms \"Matrilineal Methodologies\"—rituals and spiritual practices that promote circularity and link generations. She champions ancestral knowledge systems as a valid science in and of itself, examining how these indigenous perspectives and lived experiences build and sustain cultures over time. \\n \\nThrough a visual language of curvilinear abstract shapes and forms, Makwakwa explores the interwoven narratives between her materials, the landscape, and her artistic process. Her work seeks to create a seamless blend between the physical and the spiritual, functioning as a continued, natural synthesis of tradition and contemporary expression."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013984526557 gid://shopify/Product/9013984755933 gid://shopify/Product/9014061138141 gid://shopify/Product/9014104129757 gid://shopify/Product/9133224132829 gid://shopify/Product/9133224165597 gid://shopify/Product/9133224755421

item.title: Tinyiko Maluleke
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966686429 Tinyiko Maluleke gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641141293277 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013341028573"] Discover the work of Tinyiko Maluleke, a South African artist. Through powerful portraiture, he explores his journey of healing and recovery from a life-altering trauma. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tinyiko Maluleke is a South African artist and Master Printer originally from Bungeni, Limpopo. A graduate of the prestigious Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, where he also taught drawing, Maluleke’s practice is a profound testament to the restorative power of art. \\n \\nHis life and artistic direction were irrevocably altered by a severe car accident that left him with significant language and memory impairments. In the aftermath of this trauma, Maluleke’s ability to create art returned to him even before he could read or write again, becoming his primary tool for processing and healing. This experience is now the central force behind his work. \\n \\nMany of Maluleke’s portraits are a direct reflection of his journey of overcoming isolation, fear, and alienation. The creative process itself serves as a form of mental therapy. As he states, “My desire for my artwork is to connect and share with other victims who found themselves trapped in difficult life-changing positions and feel like they won't make it out and succeed.” Through his work, he offers a message of hope and resilience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013340963037 gid://shopify/Product/9013341028573

item.title: Titus Shitaatala
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966817501 Titus Shitaatala gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641142374621 [] Meet Titus Shitaatala, a Namibian digital artist and architect. Explore his Afro-Futurist digital collages that address social issues in Namibia and beyond. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Titus Shitaatala (b. 1998) is a Namibian digital artist and architectural designer from Windhoek whose socially motivated creations have made a notable impact. True to his family name, which means “what they look at,” Shitaatala commands attention for his work, using digital platforms to engage a new generation of audiences. \\n \\nWorking in a style he describes as locally inspired Afro-Futurism, Shitaatala creates intricate digital collages that address pressing social and historical issues, from economic inequality to cultural division. His process involves meticulously sourcing and piecing together images to build a narrative before digitally manipulating colour, scale, and dimension to provoke emotion. His works range from nostalgic reflections to radical calls for societal change, positioning him as an artistic activist for the digital age. \\n \\nShitaatala's creative practice is uniquely informed by his academic background. He holds an Honours degree in Architecture from the Namibia University of Science and Technology (2020), and his interests in sustainable design, local materials, and cultural heritage are central to both his art and his architecture. This dual focus allows him to seek holistic solutions for community matters through both built environments and visual commentary."}]}]}

item.title: Tj Lemon
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966915805 Tj Lemon gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641142997213 [] Explore the career of TJ Lemon, a key figure in South African photography. Learn about his foundational role at the Market Photo Workshop and his work with the Afrapix collective. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"TJ Lemon is a significant figure in the history of South African photography, recognized for his contributions as a photographer, educator, and institutional director during the pivotal years of the late 1980s and early 1990s. \\n \\nHis career began in the 1980s as a student photographer in the university town of Makhanda (formerly Grahamstown). He quickly established himself in the local scene with three exhibitions and held a position as a lecturer in Photojournalism at Rhodes University from 1988 to 1989. \\n \\nIn 1990, Lemon moved to Johannesburg and took on a formative leadership role as the director and trainer at the newly established Market Photo Workshop. His work there was instrumental in shaping one of the country's most important institutions for photographic education, renowned for developing new generations of South African photographers. \\n \\nDuring this period, Lemon was also an active contributor to Afrapix, the influential photographic collective known for its critical documentation of South Africa during the final years of apartheid. This dual role as an institutional builder and an engaged photographer cemented his legacy within the national photographic community."}]}]}

[25283,17808,17809,25061,17807,25062] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tom Cullberg is a Swedish-born South African artist whose captivating paintings blend the familiar with the foreign, and the pensive with the playful. He delves into the space between tangible and intangible worlds, using collections of objects that appear like symbols from dreams. These elements float above abstract backgrounds, reminiscent of the ever-shifting nature of memory. \\nWith a keen sense of humour and wit, Cullberg's work explores how we associate and recognize meaning in both personal and public stories. item.title: Tolulope Ami-Williams
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641966981341 Tolulope Ami-Williams gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641143029981 [] Meet Tolulope Ami-Williams, a Nigerian multidisciplinary artist and Prince Claus Fund awardee. Discover her powerful performance and installation work. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tolulope Ami-Williams (b. 1997) is a Lagos-based multidisciplinary artist who has rapidly gained international recognition for her powerful work in performance and installation. Her rising prominence is underscored by prestigious accolades, including being named a 2023-2024 Chevening Scholar and receiving the 2023 Prince Claus Fund Seed Award, where she was one of only 100 awardees selected globally. \\n \\nHer artistic practice is built on a strong foundation of formal training. She graduated from the Yaba College of Technology in 2018, where she was mentored by seminal performance artist Jelili Atiku, and subsequently completed her Master’s degree in Contemporary Performance at the Manchester School of Theatre in the UK. \\n \\nAmi-Williams has had a prolific series of exhibitions and performances. In 2022, she was a finalist for the prestigious Access Art X Prize, participated in the Rele Art Foundation’s Young Contemporaries residency, and held a solo exhibition, Harmony in Discord, at the Alliance Française in Lagos. In 2023, her work on decolonizing restitution was featured at Yinka Shonibare's G.A.S. Foundation, and she performed works from her major project, Knit My Broken Bones Together, at various Lagos venues. \\n \\nSince 2016, she has been an active participant in the Lagos art scene, contributing to numerous community festivals and biennials, and continues to explore critical contemporary themes with growing impact."}]}]}

item.title: Tommaso Fiscaletti
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967079645 Tommaso Fiscaletti gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641143193821 [] Tommaso Fiscaletti is an Italian-born visual artist and photographer based in Cape Town, South Africa. His work explores human consciousness, memory, and the universe through photography and installations. Notable projects include Hemelliggaam or The Attempt To Be Here Now and The Skin Underneath. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tommaso Fiscaletti (b. 1981) is a photographic artist based in Cape Town. His work explores the connection between humans, memory, and the universe, moving between reality and imagination. In 2016, his project Between Home and Wisdom was presented in a wide exhibition at the Santa Maria Della Scala Museum in Siena, accompanied by a monograph. \\nThe same year, he began working with Nic Grobler on Hemelliggaam or The Attempt To Be Here Now (Hemelliggaam, in Afrikaans: heavenly body), a visual archive of photographs, videos, and installations that brings together images of astronomical observatories, remote landscapes, and inspirations from old local (Afrikaans) science fiction novels. \\nThe project, which took six years to complete, has been exhibited in various South African museums, including the Iziko South African Museum in Cape Town and the Pretoria Art Museum. Today, this exploration is evolving into a book. In 2021, he began collaborating with anthropologist Nicola Perugini on The Skin Underneath. Through photography and public installations, the project examines how citizens perceive the Villa Marina Colony, a Fascist-era building on the Pesaro waterfront (the author's hometown), shedding light on individual and collective stories. His works are part of public and private collections and have been showcased internationally. Fiscaletti has taught photography at IED Milan and currently teaches at the Creative Academy in Cape Town."}]}]}

item.title: Toni Bico
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967276253 Toni Bico gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641144045789 [] Discover the work of Toni Bico, a Mozambican artist. Explore his vibrant, layered paintings that blend abstraction and figuration, inspired by his rural African roots. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Toni Bico (b. 1963) is a Mozambican artist whose work is deeply informed by his early life experiences. Born in Quelimane, his childhood on a remote cattle farm left a lasting impression of rural Africa, while his first forays into drawing began in primary school in South Africa as a fundamental means of communication and self-expression. These formative influences have become an enduring and recurring theme throughout his artistic career. \\n \\nBico’s paintings are a vibrant exploration of colour, texture, and form. He employs a multilayered approach, combining layered brushstrokes, appliqué, and original patterns to create a visual kaleidoscope that fluidly interplays between abstraction and figuration. This intentional and bold use of colour and shape is a reflection of his adaptation of traditional methods of representation and composition. \\n \\nHis creative process is highly intuitive. The distinct patterns and visual rhythms in his work are not predetermined but emerge from his own aesthetic sensibility and state of mind on any given day. The paintings remain in a state of visual fluctuation, only finding their resolution when Bico feels they are complete. His works are held in private collections both in Southern Africa and abroad."}]}]}

item.title: Toni-Ann Ballenden
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967243485 Toni-Ann Ballenden gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641144307933 [] Discover South African artist Toni-Ann Ballenden. She creates abstract art by cathartically cutting up and reconstructing past works, a process born from her personal history. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Toni-Ann Ballenden is a South African artist whose work is born from a unique and deeply personal process of deconstruction and reconstruction. Her abstract compositions are meticulously reassembled from older, unresolved works that she has obsessively cut up—a cathartic act that transforms destruction into a positive creative journey. \\n \\nThis method is rooted in her personal history and a long-standing impulse to destroy figurative drawings she deemed \"not good enough.\" This process, influenced by feelings of being undervalued in childhood, has become a way to cope with life's challenges. Guided by the principle articulated by Louise Bourgeois that “art, no less than wisdom, waits on life,” Ballenden allows her lived experience to be physically and metaphorically remade in the studio. \\n \\nA pivotal moment in her career came in 2015 with a residency at The Bag Factory in Johannesburg, which catalyzed her shift from figurative work into abstraction. It was here that she fully embraced her process, finding a way to use the cut-up pieces of her past to build a new, abstract visual language. \\n \\nBallenden’s work is held in high esteem, evidenced by numerous accolades and significant collections. She holds a National Higher Diploma cum laude from Wits Technikon (1993) and was the winner of the prestigious Thami Mnyele Fine Arts Award in 1992. With nine solo exhibitions to her name, her work is included in major collections such as The Astrup Fearnley Art Museum in Oslo, the Sasol Collection, the Anglo American Collection, and the SAFFCA Collection."}]}]}

[15471,13155,15476,15473,15477,15483,15485,15482,15480] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tony Gum is a highly acclaimed, award-winning South African artist whose multidisciplinary work operates at the intersection of performance, portraiture, and visual storytelling. In her practice, Gum’s own body and persona serve as the primary canvas, creating a profound and self-reflective universe where the artist and the artwork are inextricably linked. \\n \\nDrawing deep inspiration from her Xhosa heritage, Gum creates rich visual narratives that are both deeply personal and universally resonant. Her work transcends singular stories, skillfully breaking down barriers of culture, race, and gender to explore the poignant and subtle realities of the shared human experience. \\n \\nAs the creative director of her own imagery, Gum orchestrates every element of the visual narrative. Her process seamlessly combines photography and digital film with elements of graphic design, painting, and still-life composition.
