item.title: Tony Figueira
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967374557 Tony Figueira gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641144406237 [] Explore the legacy of Tony Figueira (1959-2017), a prominent Namibian photographer. Discover his work documenting Namibian independence, landscapes, and people. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tony Figueira (1959-2017) was a prominent and influential Namibian photographer of Angolan birth, celebrated for his powerful documentation of Namibian life, its landscape, and its path to independence. \\n \\nBorn in Huambo, Angola, Figueira moved to Windhoek, Namibia with his family at the age of seven. His passion for the camera was ignited as a teenager, a pursuit he formalized by studying journalism at Rhodes University in South Africa, graduating in 1984. This journalistic foundation would become a cornerstone of his narrative-driven photographic style. \\n \\nFigueira’s extensive body of work captured the soul of his adopted nation through three distinct but interconnected lenses: the profound beauty and intricacy of the human experience; the critical pre- and post-independence struggle for freedom and justice in Namibia and its neighbours; and the vast, contrasting beauty of the Namibian landscape and its wildlife. \\n \\nA key figure in Namibia’s photographic community, Figueira held his first solo exhibition, Minha Terra, at the National Art Gallery of Namibia in 1989. In 2004, he co-founded the influential Studio 77, which he ran until 2017. His award-winning work gained significant international acclaim, with exhibitions travelling from Namibia and South Africa to Angola, Portugal, and across Scandinavia."}]}]}

item.title: Tony Nkotsi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967440093 Tony Nkotsi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641145487581 [] Discover the work of Tony Nkotsi, a major South African artist and master printmaker. Explore a career shaped by the Rorkes Drift Art Centre and social commentary. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tony Nkotsi (b. 1955) is a highly respected South African artist whose life and work are deeply entwined with the country’s history of struggle and artistic resistance. Born in Johannesburg’s Western Township, his early passion for art was shaped by informal classes in Soweto and a profound admiration for artists like Dumile Feni. His involvement in the 1976 student uprisings and subsequent detention was a pivotal experience, cementing his belief in art as a vehicle for social and political expression. \\n \\nThis path led him to the legendary Rorkes Drift Art Centre, where he studied from 1980 until its closure in 1982. At Rorke's Drift, Nkotsi was immersed in the world of printmaking, or \"democratic multiples,\" a medium that resonated with his political sentiments. The Centre’s extensive curriculum—covering intaglio, woodcuts, and screenprinting—provided him with a technical mastery that remains a hallmark of his practice. This period solidified his commitment to socially conscious work, exemplified by early pieces like his 1982 Portrait of a Man (Biko). \\n \\nA dedicated community builder, Nkotsi played an instrumental role in developing Johannesburg's art infrastructure. Alongside his lifelong friend Dumisani Mabaso, he helped establish the Squzu Studio for printmaking and assisted with the Hammanskraal Art Project. He became a key educator, teaching printmaking at institutions like the Federated Union of Black Artists (FUBA), the Open School, and the Johannesburg Art Foundation. \\n \\nOver the years, Nkotsi’s visual language evolved to embrace abstract expressionist forms, while retaining its political undertones. His significant contributions have been recognized both locally and internationally. In 1988, he was awarded a British Council scholarship to work in Scotland, and he held a solo exhibition at the prestigious Goodman Gallery in 1987, alongside participating in numerous group shows worldwide."}]}]}

They create black and white images using only in-camera effects to explore themes of psychology and emotion. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"ToscaNeena is a Cape Town-based photography couple, a collaborative entity formed by artists Tosca Marthinus and Neena Borrill in 2019. (They/them). Working in unison, they develop and execute singular creative concepts that challenge the boundaries of their medium. \\n \\nTheir practice is defined by a rigorous and purist approach to photography. Working exclusively in black and white, they create simplified compositions of objects or people which are then manipulated or distorted using manual, in-camera techniques. Crucially, their final images are achieved without any digital post-production, a commitment that underscores the integrity of their process. \\n \\nThis distinct visual language serves their exploration of psychology and social conditioning. By bending the rules of commercial photography and aesthetic conventions, ToscaNeena creates images that mirror human emotions and complex states of the psyche, often using blur and other distortions to evoke a feeling rather than document a reality. While photography is their primary focus, they also extend their conceptual inquiries into other mediums, including mixed media, video, and sound installation."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013353644253 gid://shopify/Product/9013472297181 gid://shopify/Product/9013975679197 gid://shopify/Product/9013975777501 gid://shopify/Product/9013975875805 gid://shopify/Product/9013975974109 gid://shopify/Product/9013976072413 gid://shopify/Product/9013976170717 gid://shopify/Product/9013976269021 gid://shopify/Product/9013976367325

His artistic journey began in early childhood with a keen interest in drawing portraits, a foundation that continues to inform his professional practice today. \\nKalejaye uses his art as a powerful instrument to explore and comment on modern society and the everyday Black experience. His work is deeply ingrained in storytelling, representation, and historical documentation, seeking to capture and preserve nuanced narratives of Black identity. \\n \\nWorking primarily with charcoal, acrylic, and oil on both canvas and archival paper, Kalejaye aims to incite emotion in his viewers. He sees this emotional response as a necessary catalyst for initiating everything from vital social conversations to practical, real-world action and the liberation of consciousness. \\nHis compelling narratives have reached international audiences, with his work being displayed in a range of exhibitions globally. A notable example includes his participation in the group exhibition “Stop, listen!” in Sweden."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014002450653 gid://shopify/Product/9014002483421 gid://shopify/Product/9014002516189

item.title: Tracey Rose
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641967800541 Tracey Rose gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641148010717 [] Discover the work of Tracey Rose, a major South African artist. Through radical performance, video, and photography, she confronts the politics of race, gender, and identity. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tracey Rose is one of South Africa’s most influential contemporary artists, renowned for her radical performance, video, and photographic work. Based in Johannesburg, her practice is a bold and unflinching confrontation with the politics of identity. \\n \\nAt the core of her work is a critical response to the limitations of dogma and institutionalised cultural discourse. Rose relentlessly interrogates themes of race, gender, and sexuality, often using her own body as a site for protest, parody, and radical self-expression. While performance is central to her practice, it extends into photography and video installations. Her potent artistic language often references art historical precedents, with critic Jan Avgikos noting that \"part of Rose's appeal is her fluid referencing of '60s and '70s performance art.\" \\n \\nRose holds a B.A. in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (1996) and has taught at several South African institutions. A pivotal moment in her career came in 2001 when, as artist-in-residence at the South African National Gallery, she developed work for the prestigious Venice Biennale, curated by the legendary Harald Szeemann."}]}]}

item.title: Tracy Keza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641968029917 Tracy Keza gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641149288669 [] Meet Tracy Keza, a Kigali-based filmmaker and photographer exploring identity, culture, and conservation. Her work has been featured by the Smithsonian. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Kenyan-born and raised across South Africa and Rwanda, Tracy Keza is a Kigali-based documentary photographer and filmmaker whose work explores complex notions of identity, culture, and conservation. Her multinational upbringing informs a perspective dedicated to using visual storytelling as a powerful tool in the fight for justice and equity. \\n \\nKeza holds an academic background in Environmental Science from Trinity College (USA), a foundation that underpins her thematic interests. She currently works as a filmmaker at the acclaimed MASS Design Group, applying her narrative skills to impactful projects. As a multimedia artist, Keza employs a hybrid style that merges fine art with documentary photography, allowing her to challenge existing stereotypes of the “other” and create nuanced, human-centered narratives. \\n \\nHer work has gained significant recognition. As a former creative resident at 72andSunny, she co-created a storytelling platform addressing the challenges of mass incarceration. In 2016, she was selected as an artist-in-residence at Studio Revolt, where she developed her project “Hijabs and Hoodies.” This important work was later activated at the Smithsonian Asian Pacific American Center’s “CROSSLINES: A Culture Lab on Intersectionality” in Washington D.C."}]}]}

item.title: Tracy Payne
item.description: Tracy Payne gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641150140637 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013416034525", "gid://shopify/Product/9013416067293"] Explore the work of Tracy Payne, a Cape Town-based artist and Michaelis graduate. Discover a career shaped by international residencies and eight solo exhibitions. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tracy Payne (b.1965) is a Cape Town-based South African artist and a 1987 graduate of the acclaimed the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town. \\nA significant influence on her artistic development has been a series of self-directed international residencies. These periods of focused work and travel have taken her to diverse global cities, including Berlin and Barcelona (1988/89), New York (1995), Tokyo (2002), and the Indian locales of Dharamkot and Khajuraho (2012). \\n \\nWhile maintaining a primary base in Cape Town, Payne has also worked from studios in Johannesburg and abroad. In 2014, she established a studio in a renovated Victorian building in Woodstock, Cape Town, where for four years she balanced her painting practice with teaching art. Payne is now dedicated full-time to her studio practice, focused on developing her next body of work and continuing a prolific career that already includes eight solo exhibitions to date."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013313994973 gid://shopify/Product/9013416034525 gid://shopify/Product/9013416067293

Using digital manipulation, wood carving, and painting, Mlima's ethereal works reflect his journey of self-discovery and new identities from an African perspective. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Treasure Mlima (b. 1999, Durban, South Africa) is a self-taught mixed media artist exploring themes of identity, space, and the African experience through his distinctive art. Raised between visual arts education in high school and self-driven learning via the internet, Mlima's journey of self-discovery is rooted in both trial and error and spiritual exploration. His ethereal work features untypical spaces against blank backgrounds, symbolizing a quest for answers and new identities. \\nMlima's creative process includes the digital manipulation of found images, which he then carves into wood and paints with oil-based and acrylic inks. This technique results in 2D prints that deal with space and identity from an African perspective. \\nMlima plans to work on a lifelong series titled \"Honing,\" which will explore various mediums in a non-linear fashion. His art reflects his journey of rebellion against traditional art principles, using unorthodox techniques to capture the essence of his thoughts and emotions. Mlima considers himself a cultural practitioner with the duty to reveal hidden realities and suggest alternative ones using neutral symbolism. \\nHis art is for anyone who sees value in it, and private collectors hold pieces of his work, continuing his legacy. Mlima's commitment to sharing a part of himself through his art ensures that his creations will make sense and be treasured long after he is gone"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013946024157 gid://shopify/Product/9013946056925 gid://shopify/Product/9013963784413 gid://shopify/Product/9013963882717

Discover his professional journey and community work. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Treatwell Mnisi is a Johannesburg-based artist whose career is built on a foundation of formal training and dedicated professional development. Originally from the rural developments of Mpumalanga, his artistic journey led him to the Tshwane University of Technology (TUT), where he earned a National Diploma in Fine & Applied Arts in 2008. \\n \\nFollowing his studies, Mnisi dedicated himself to building a multifaceted career in the arts. In 2011, he shared his skills by facilitating art classes at the Tshwane Leadership Foundation in Pretoria. Eager to understand the commercial landscape of his craft, he participated in entrepreneurial business workshops with the Craft and Design Institute (CDI) between 2015 and 2016 to deepen his knowledge of the art and craft market. \\n \\nMnisi’s engagement with the arts community also includes his participation in philanthropic efforts. In 2020, he was an invited artist at a fundraiser auction hosted by Smile Artist Africa (SAA), a successful campaign that raised money to support women with breast cancer."}]}]}

[9230,9231] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"With a distinguished career spanning over six decades, Trevor Coleman (b. 1940) is a veteran South African artist whose life has been an unwavering dedication to his craft. His formative years were spent in London, a five-year period he describes as his “university of life.” There, he attended the Central School of Art, immersed himself in the gallery scene, and met influential figures such as Henry Moore, experiences that profoundly shaped his artistic trajectory. \\n \\nColeman’s practice is driven by the principle that “an artist should be an explorer.” This philosophy is evident both in his creative process—marked by a constant evolution of new ideas and techniques that shift between abstraction and figuration—and in his extensive global travels. Drawing inspiration from his journeys to India, Morocco, Mali, Zanzibar, and beyond, his work captures a rich tapestry of international influence. \\nFor Coleman, art is not merely a profession but a “full-time experience,” an endless medium for expressing feeling. His enduring legacy is marked by numerous successful exhibitions from South Africa to London and a consistent presence at auction."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013338538205 gid://shopify/Product/9013338570973

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641968652509 Trianus Nakale gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641151844573 [] Discover the work of Namibian artist Trianus Nakale. Through provocative illustrations and text, he confronts societal ills like corruption and gender-based violence. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Trianus Nakale (b. 1986) is a Namibian artist whose work serves as a powerful and provocative critique of contemporary social challenges. Through a distinctive combination of illustration and text on paper, Nakale uses his creative calling not for aesthetics, but as a dedicated tool for social commentary and activism. \\n \\nOften working with his preferred medium of pen ink in blue, black, and red, his pieces directly confront societal ills such as gender-based violence, corruption, greed, and other irresponsible actions he observes within his community. While he also experiments with materials like coffee, watercolours, and occasionally clay sculpture, his primary focus remains on visual protest. As Nakale states, “Art is a visual language, which we should use as artists to change the world... I'm speaking out for the victims so they can get justice, and visualise their experiences in the hope for these sickening activities to come to an end.” \\n \\nBorn into a family of educators and creatives in the village of Ekoka in northern Namibia, Nakale’s artistic path was fostered from a young age. He later relocated to Windhoek, graduating with a Diploma in Visual Arts from the College of the Arts in 2013."}]}]}

Their work draws on personal experiences of their identity, specifically themes of gender dysphoria, assigned sex, sociopolitical trauma and healing, while simultaneously engaging in themes of catharsis and disruption. They work primarily in two methodologies – glitch art and textile art – and enjoy understanding and navigating the queer energy that these mediums evoke, and their infinite potentiality for catharsis and disruption."}]}]}

item.title: Troy Makaza
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641968816349 Troy Makaza gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641153089757 [] Explore the work of Zimbabwean artist Troy Makaza. Discover his unique woven silicone sculptures that address politics, history, and contemporary African identity. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zimbabwean artist Troy Makaza is renowned for his innovative use of a signature hybrid medium: painted and woven silicone. Originally a painter, Makaza’s deep interest in form and texture led him to develop this unique practice, which allows him to cast, paint, weave, and tie the material, creating complex, tapestry-like works that defy traditional categorization. \\nOver the past eight years, his art has evolved into a powerful commentary on the contemporary Zimbabwean experience. Makaza viscerally and philosophically addresses compelling issues of politics, history, and power, exploring their impact on the daily lives of ordinary people from the perspective of a globally-engaged artist. His creations resonate with traditional crafts like weaving yet are unequivocally contemporary, articulating a new paradigm for what modern Zimbabwean and African art can be—both internationally engaging and locally compelling. \\nMakaza has received significant early-career acclaim from critics and collectors. He was featured in the 2018 survey of Zimbabwean contemporary art at the Zeitz MOCAA and won the prestigious Tomorrows/Today prize at the 2019 Investec Cape Town Art Fair. His work is held in major institutional collections, including the Museum of African Contemporary Art Al Maaden (MACAAL) in Marrakech and the Rollins College Museum of Art, as well as in esteemed private collections like that of Jorge Pérez in Miami."}]}]}

Featured in “Where You Are” at Constitution Hill. Explore his work on Latitudes Online. [23639,23641] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tsako Manuel Hobyani (b. 2000) is a multi-disciplinary artist who grew up In Freedom Park, Johannesburg, South Africa. His artistic journey began with an innate love for illustration, painting and printmaking, which has now become his primary mediums of expression. Tsako thrives on conceptualizing his art by infusing a re-imagination of a future flush with art, culture and technology through a black lens. Through his work he aspire to reinvent the past and the future using traditional patterns in a digital manner incorporating elements of black history and culture. \\nTsako’s artistic journey reached a turning point during his time at Artist Proof Studio. This pivotal experience allowed him to embraced his interests in various printmaking processes like Linocut and silkscreen and this uplifted him as a well determined and vigorous artist and also improving his skills to being a professional printmaking artist and hones his artistic voice. \\nHis talent and dedication have earned him recognition and numerous exhibition opportunities, including being a featured artist in the Investec Cape town Art Fair 2025 .Tsako’s work has been celebrated in the art community, earning him a spot in the nationally recognized “Art Times” magazine. Notable group exhibitions, such as the Bon A Tier (BAT) and “Where you are” graduate exhibition in Constitution Hill, and FNB Art Fair have further showcased his compelling creations."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014053175517 gid://shopify/Product/9014053241053

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969012957 Tshepiso Mazibuko 346 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641156497629 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014014771421"] Discover the evocative photography of Tshepiso Mazibuko, a Johannesburg-based artist known for her sensitive and poetic storytelling. Explore her works capturing the essence of Thokoza and beyond. [22354] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tshepiso Mazibuko (b. 1995, Thokoza, South Africa) is a talented photographer based in Johannesburg. Initially interested in journalism, she was introduced to photography through the Of Soul and Joy initiative at Buhlebuzile Secondary School. Her work tells the stories of her community, blending documentary realism with artistic expression. Notably, her photogravure series \"Gone and Here\" captures the essence of Thokoza with a dynamic interplay of light, focus, and composition. \\n \\nMazibuko's approach has earned her comparisons to renowned photographers like Santu Mofokeng and David Goldblatt. Her work has been showcased in numerous exhibitions, including \"Free from my Happiness\" at the Johannesburg Art Gallery and \"80 Days of Summer: Stories of Identity\" at the Ghent International Photography Festival. She was selected for the Addis Foto Fest 2016 and awarded a Tierney Fellowship in 2017. Mazibuko continues to inspire with her powerful visual narratives."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014014771421

item.title: Tshepo Moloi
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969209565 Tshepo Moloi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641158267101 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013389197533","gid://shopify/Product/9013389230301","gid://shopify/Product/9013389263069","gid://shopify/Product/9014031384797"] Discover the work of South African photographer Tshepo Moloi, who explores themes of migration, community, and identity, using his art to reconnect with his rural roots in Daggakraal. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tshepo Moloi is a contemporary photographer and filmmaker whose work is deeply rooted in his upbringing in the rural community of Daggakraal, Mpumalanga. Since becoming interested in the lens in 2015, Moloi has developed a practice that critically unpacks complex social themes, including migration, belonging, identity, consumerism, and community. His art serves as a powerful medium to navigate and understand the world around him. \\nFeeling a sense of isolation from his own community, Moloi uses his photography and filmmaking as a deliberate means to reconnect and foster dialogue. This personal mission infuses his work with a poignant sense of searching and engagement. \\nMoloi has built an impressive exhibition record, participating in numerous group shows both in South Africa and internationally. His work has been shown in diverse locations, from Johannesburg (\"Fluxus Now,\" 2016; \"The Portrait Show,\" 2020) and Amsterdam (\"URBAN MYTHS\") to Switzerland, Pakistan, and New York. He was also a participant in the 2021 Kampala Art Biennale. His photography has been featured in notable publications such as the Mail & Guardian and Amsterdam-based Africanah.org, underscoring his growing international recognition."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013389197533 gid://shopify/Product/9013389230301 gid://shopify/Product/9013389263069 gid://shopify/Product/9014031384797

[5568,5567,5564,329,332,5769,5563,5569,5570,333,330,331,5566,5565,5576] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tshepiso Seleke, professionally known as The DarkRoom Artist, is a visual artist from Orlando East, Soweto, whose work is a powerful act of decolonization and reclamation. He consciously rebels against photographic practices that perpetuate colonial ways of seeing. For him, the camera is a tool to construct an oppositional Black aesthetic, moving beyond stereotypes to present multifaceted and radical identities. \\n \\nHis work focuses on the beauty and reality of everyday life, aiming to fill the historical void where stories of Black culture, spirituality, and existence have been hidden or erased. By documenting the social and economic positionality of Black lives, he gives a platform to marginalized voices. Through both documentary and staged imaginative spaces, Seleke's photography seeks to empower, reaffirm, and celebrate the richness of Black history and identity after a long history of oppression."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013274050781 gid://shopify/Product/9013274083549 gid://shopify/Product/9013274116317 gid://shopify/Product/9013274149085 gid://shopify/Product/9013274181853 gid://shopify/Product/9013305966813 gid://shopify/Product/9013306032349 gid://shopify/Product/9013306097885 gid://shopify/Product/9013306196189 gid://shopify/Product/9013306261725 gid://shopify/Product/9013306360029 gid://shopify/Product/9013306392797 gid://shopify/Product/9013306458333 gid://shopify/Product/9013306523869 gid://shopify/Product/9013307375837 gid://shopify/Product/9014017884381 gid://shopify/Product/9014106980573

Her practice is deeply inspired by themes of identity and storytelling, which she explores through a unique contemporary lens influenced by the historical Baroque art form. Moropa channels the drama, complexity, and elaborate detail characteristic of the Baroque to evoke powerful human emotions. \\nHer collage work, in particular, is defined by its intricate forms, bold ornamentation, and the skillful juxtaposition of archival imagery with contrasting materials. item.title: Tsoku Maela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969373405 Tsoku Maela 1828 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641159839965 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013368160477", "gid://shopify/Product/9013368193245", "gid://shopify/Product/9014002876637"] Discover the work of Tsoku Maela, a South African artist who uses photography and storytelling to explore dreams as an archive, healing historical trauma and forging new African perspectives. [12343] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South Africa artist Tsoku Maela uses the powerful concept of \"dreams as an archive\" to explore human behaviour and well-being within socio-economic and pyschospiritual frameworks, particularly in African contexts. Born in Limpopo and now working between Johannesburg and Cape Town, Maela's path to art was unconventional. \\nAfter studying at The South African School of Motion Picture Medium and working as a copywriter and scriptwriter, he discovered his true voice in experimental photography. It became his medium for finding clarity on issues of the mind, body, and spirit, using storytelling to tap into dreams as an archive of both past and future realities. \\nGrowing up in a nation scarred by colonial history, Maela is part of a generation navigating identity within a young democracy. His work consciously utilizes these collective memories and histories not to perpetuate suffering, but to construct new, empowered African and global perspectives. His approach is one of healing and empowerment, using storytelling to move beyond historical trauma and envision new futures. \\nMaela's impactful work was recognized in 2016 when he received the Standard Bank Rising Star Award for Media & Marketing. He has exhibited internationally in cities like Lagos, Zürich, and at Art Basel in Miami, and his art is held in prestigious private collections, including M&C SAATCHI, the Amawal collection, and the JP Morgan Abadali art collection."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013368160477 gid://shopify/Product/9013368193245 gid://shopify/Product/9014002876637 gid://shopify/Product/9133223903453

item.title: Tuli Mekondjo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969438941 Tuli Mekondjo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641159971037 [] Discover the work of Namibian artist Tuli Mekondjo, who uses embroidery, photo transfer, and symbolic materials to explore colonial histories, trauma, and identity. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tuli Mekondjo (b. 1982, Angola) is a self-taught Namibian artist whose powerful mixed-media works explore the complex tapestries of Namibian history, identity, and memory. Working with a unique combination of embroidery, photo transfers, paint, resin, and the symbolic mahangu (millet) grain—a Namibian food staple—Mekondjo delves into colonial and war-time photographic archives to confront and reinterpret the past. \\nMekondjo's practice is a poignant act of stitching together past and present, giving voice to histories of change, loss, and the submission experienced by women. In her art, she pays homage to her forebears, celebrating fertility and continuity while simultaneously commenting on gendered struggle, displacement, and the haunting realities of intergenerational trauma. Spirituality has become an increasingly vital element in her practice; she often positions herself in direct dialogue with her ancestors, acknowledging their pain while referencing diverse African folklore. This spiritual and historical exploration extends beyond the canvas, as Mekondjo incorporates performance into her textured and layered artistic language. \\nA recipient of the prestigious DAAD Artists-in-Berlin Program fellowship in 2022, Mekondjo has gained significant international acclaim. Her work has been exhibited in museums and galleries across Namibia, South Africa, Côte d’Ivoire, Europe, and the UK, and is held in multiple international collections. She is represented by Hales Gallery (New York) and Guns & Rain (Johannesburg)."}]}]}

Now based in Johannesburg, Mphela is an alumnus of Tshwane University of Technology where he refined his crafts in Fine Arts. \\n \\nInitially captivated by the nuanced textures and tones achievable with charcoal, Mphela has since expanded his practice to embrace a diverse range of artistic mediums, including sculpture. His compelling artworks frequently delve into pertinent social issues, aiming to evoke profound emotional responses from the viewer."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014142042333

item.title: Tshogofatso Nkhumeleng
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969340637 Tshogofatso Nkhumeleng gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641159512285 [] Discover the work of Tshogofatso Nkhumeleng (I.N.I), a Soweto-born printmaker whose journey from the Room13 art studio to Artist Proof Studio showcases resilience and emerging talent. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tshogofatso Nkhumeleng, fondly known as I.N.I, is a visual artist born and raised in the vibrant community of Soweto, Johannesburg. His artistic journey began after overcoming early academic challenges, finding his true calling at the Sapebuso Primary School's Room13 art studio. Here, under the mentorship of resident artist John Vusi Mfupi, his passion for art was ignited. This early guidance proved fruitful when, in 2009, he won his first major art competition hosted by Webber Wentzel and participated in the Joburg Art Fair. In 2010, he contributed to a significant mural project for the FIFA World Cup held in South Africa. \\nThroughout his time at Emadwaleni High School, I.N.I continued his artistic development at the Room13 studio at Saint Martin's Catholic School, where he was mentored by Nkosana Ngobese, who taught him both the creative and business aspects of the art world. \\nFollowing his passion, I.N.I pursued a three-year course in Printmaking at the prestigious Artist Proof Studio (APS). His dedication culminated in several group shows in 2019 with his peers, exhibiting at Artist Proof Studio, in Cape Town, and with Strauss & Co. In 2020, his potential was further recognized when he was selected for a special projects internship at APS, where he currently works as a gallery assistant, continuing to build his career from within the heart of Johannesburg's art community."}]}]}

item.title: Tuomo Manninen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969570013 Tuomo Manninen gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641160495325 [] Explore the work of Finnish photographer Tuomo Manninen and his renowned "Me/We" series, a global collection of group portraits that dissect the balance between individual and group identity. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tuomo Manninen (b. 1962, Helsinki) is a Finnish photographer renowned for his extensive series of group portraits, \"Me/We,\" which he began in 1995. His work masterfully blends documentary photography with a sense of dramatization, creating meticulously structured compositions where subjects actively participate in the perpetuation of a moment. By having them pose, often within their professional environments, Manninen captures a sense of shared identity, pride, and purpose, from Helsinki to Havana, and right here in Johannesburg. \\nManninen’s portraits delve into the complex tension between the individual and the collective—the \"Me\" versus the \"We.\" While the group shapes and defines each person's identity, it can also erase distinct individual characteristics. Manninen emphasizes this dynamic through his artistic method, carefully choreographing his subjects and using specific lighting techniques to transform their everyday surroundings into what feel like theatrical stage sets. These settings highlight that an individual's membership in any single group is just one fragment of a much larger, untold personal story. \\nThis ongoing project, spanning cities from Kathmandu to Ramallah and Tehran, serves as a cross-section of modern life, cutting through the surface of global communities to reveal the pride and dignity within them. Manninen's celebrated work has been featured in over 80 solo and group exhibitions worldwide, including the 49th Venice Biennale and the Rencontres d’Arles photo festival, and is the subject of numerous publications."}]}]}

item.title: Turiya Magadlela
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969602781 Turiya Magadlela 1037 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641160626397 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013835825373","gid://shopify/Product/9014025126109","gid://shopify/Product/9133222494429","gid://shopify/Product/9133222822109"] Discover the work of Turiya Magadlela, the FNB Art Prize-winning artist who uses pantyhose and textiles to create abstract art exploring gender, politics, and South African history. [22778] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Turiya Magadlela is a highly acclaimed South African artist whose work skillfully balances politically charged narratives with a refined and powerful aesthetic sensibility. Using unconventional materials such as pantyhose, correctional service uniforms, and textiles, she creates abstract compositions that explore themes of gender, sexuality, and the complex social and political histories of South Africa, particularly those relating to women's bodies and incarceration. \\nAs acclaimed artist Sue Williamson once observed in ArtReview, Magadlela's \"blocks of fabric in brilliant scarlet, pinks and oranges suggest an exuberant celebration of womanhood, a refusal to allow oneself to be downtrodden.\" This potent combination of material and meaning earned her the prestigious FNB Art Prize in 2015, an award judged by influential curators Bisi Silva and Koyo Kouoh. \\nA graduate of the renowned Rijksakademie in Amsterdam (2003–2004), Magadlela has a significant exhibition history. She held a major solo exhibition at the Johannesburg Art Gallery in 2015 and has participated in numerous high-profile international group shows, including Blue Black, curated by Glenn Ligon at the Pulitzer Arts Foundation (2017), Blackness in Abstraction at Pace Gallery (2016), and The Past is Present at Jack Shainman Gallery (2017)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013835825373 gid://shopify/Product/9014025126109 gid://shopify/Product/9133222494429 gid://shopify/Product/9133222822109

item.title: Tusevo Landu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969766621 Tusevo Landu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641161478365 [] Discover the Afrofuturist art of Tusevo Landu. The Congolese, Cape Town-based painter uses cultural symbols to explore identity, challenge injustice, and restore pride in Black bodies. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tusevo Landu (b.1997, Kinshasa, DRC) is a self-taught painter whose powerful work confronts injustice through the lens of Afrofuturism. Though he briefly studied at the prestigious Artist Proof Studio in Johannesburg, Landu has forged his own path, developing a multifaceted practice that includes acrylic painting, printmaking, drawing, and mixed media. \\nNow based in Cape Town, his art is a direct response to the daily realities of discrimination, choosing cultural expression over traditional politics as his tool for advocacy. \\nIn alignment with the Afrofuturist movement, Landu’s work is a social and political act. His mission is to restore a profound sense of pride to Black bodies and to breathe life into the narratives of Black existence, challenging perceptions and economic voids. Drawing from his experience as a Congolese artist in South Africa, he incorporates traditional Congolese masks—symbols used in coming-of-age ceremonies—to explore the enigmatic nature of his subjects and bridge ancestral heritage with contemporary life. \\nLandu has gained significant international recognition with solo exhibitions such as “Now or Never” (2022) at Simchowitz Gallery in California and “An Introduction” (2023) at Latitudes Centre for the Arts in Johannesburg. He has also participated in numerous group shows, including at Everard Read gallery. For Landu, art is not a mere commodity; it is a political statement, a method of storytelling, and a therapeutic medium to inspire change and testify to the resilience of the human spirit. \\nmany of his Black contemporaries, faces the daily reality of injustice and discrimination. Instead of following a traditional political route to combat these injustices, he has turned to culture and the power of artistic expression to envision and advocate for an alternative to an oppressive reality. In alignment with the Afro-futurist movement, Landu sees his art as a significant social event in the contemporary world. His mission is to breathe life and fullness into the void that often characterises the construction, perception, and economy of Black life, with the ultimate aim of restoring a profound sense of pride to Black bodies. Landu's experiences as a Congolese artist living in South Africa have been a driving force in shaping his artistic practice. He employs traditional African masks, typically used in Congolese coming-of-age ceremonies, as symbols of the enigmatic nature of his chosen subjects. Through his work, Landu explores how such cultural events can profoundly affect one's life, based on their appearance, bridging the gap between the ancestral and the contemporary. In Landu's view, art transcends its role as a mere commodity; it becomes a political statement, an allegory, a form of demonstration, a method of storytelling, and even a therapeutic medium. Through his multifaceted practice, Tusevo Landu invites viewers to delve into the intricate layers of human existence, where culture, history, and identity intertwine to shape our understanding of the world and the narratives that define it. Landu's work not only provokes thought but also speaks to the soul, striving to be a catalyst for change and a testament to the resilience of the human spirit. Born in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic Of Congo, Landu lives work in Cape Town, ZA Education 2018: Artists Proof Studio, Johannesburg, ZA Solo Exhibitions 2023: “An Introduction”, Latitudes Centre for the Arts, Johannesburg, ZA 2022: “Now or Never”, Simchowitz Gallery, Pasadena, California, USA Group Exhibitions 2023: “Winter group show”, Everard Read, Cape Town, ZA 2020: (un)Masked, Artists Proof Studio, Johannesburg, ZA 2020: The Lockdown collection, Artists Proof Studio and the University Of Johannesburg, Johannesburg, ZA 2019: Louis Khela Maqhubela and Douglas Portway, Artists Proof Studio and Straus & Co, Turbine Art Fair, Johannesburg, ZA 2019: Fundamentalist Rationalism, Eclectica Print Gallery, Cape Town, ZA Residency 2022: Cape Town Residency, Cape Town, ZA Accolades 2022: Simchowitz Collection, Los Angeles, USA 2019: Finalists of Fundamentalist Rationalism Print Competition, Eclectica Gallery, Cape Town, ZA"}]}]}

In 2001, he transitioned his focus to a successful career in tattooing and professional sign writing, mastering the precision and design principles of both disciplines. \\nIn recent years, Tyler has embarked on a new chapter in his fine art career, developing a unique and dynamic style that fuses his diverse expertise. His current work masterfully blends the energy and aesthetics of urban culture and street art with the craftsmanship of traditional sign writing and the intricate artistry of tattooing. This powerful combination results in pieces that are both visually complex and deeply rooted in the authentic language of street-level creativity."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013945336029 gid://shopify/Product/9013945434333

item.title: Tyrrel Thaysen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970421981 Tyrrel Thaysen 1146 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641161969885 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013309341917","gid://shopify/Product/9013310161117","gid://shopify/Product/9013375336669","gid://shopify/Product/9013470920925"] Discover the work of South African artist Tyrrel Thaysen. His mixed-media assemblages and portraits explore heritage, self, and spirituality, with work featured at the Zeitz MOCAA. [6012,6095,12869,17918] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tyrrel Thaysen (b. 1969) is a mixed-media, multidisciplinary artist from Belvedere, Knysna, whose work is deeply rooted in his heritage as a descendant of farmworkers in apartheid South Africa. Now based in Cape Town, Thaysen's art is a profound exploration of the self, examining the cyclical patterns of thought and behavior that arise from personal history and coping mechanisms. He frequently represents his family in his work, finding solace and a foundational peace in spirituality. \\n \\nThaysen creates complex assemblages, layering materials with an inspiration drawn from Hollywood fashion and celebrity lifestyles. This unexpected juxtaposition stems from an upbringing where a pristine physical appearance was emphasized as a key to success. His portraiture reflects this internal narrative; the figures appear to have weathered numerous life events, emerging wiser and more capable. \\n \\nA graduate of the Michaelis School of Fine Art with a diploma in Fine Art and a major in sculpture, Thaysen's talent was recognized early when he won a national drawing competition at the AVA Gallery. His career is marked by prestigious awards, including the Montague White bursary and the Vermont Studio Center Triangle Arts Residency fellowship. He has been a frequent participant in Thupelo workshops worldwide, a three-time finalist at the Brett Kebble Art Awards, and an artist-in-residence at Greatmore Studios. \\n \\nThaysen has held two solo exhibitions at the AVA Gallery and currently has work on loan at the Zeitz MOCAA Museum. He is represented in corporate and private collections both in South Africa and internationally and has worked as a freelance visual artist for the Spier Arts Trust for over seventeen years."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013309341917 gid://shopify/Product/9013310161117 gid://shopify/Product/9013375336669 gid://shopify/Product/9013470920925

Through a balance of fragility and aggression, her work challenges preconceptions, creating nuanced, thought-provoking visual narratives."}]}]}

item.title: Tyler Durban
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641969930461 Tyler Durban gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641161674973 [] Discover the work of Tyler Durban, a versatile artist exploring the human mind through painting, digital art, and film. Learn about his mission to make art accessible for healing and self-expression. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tyler Durban is a versatile, multidisciplinary artist dedicated to exploring the intricate workings of the human mind and our interpretation of the world. His work is centered on a keen interest in how we perceive patterns and derive meaning from the everyday, delving into complex themes such as pareidolia, love, religion, depression, and the broader human condition. \\nWorking fluidly across a range of mediums—including painting, digital art, film, music, collage, and photography—he investigates the myriad ways we process our experiences. A core tenet of Durban's practice is the passionate belief that art should be a universal tool for healing and self-expression. He is committed to breaking down the monetary and mental barriers that often prevent people from engaging with their own creativity. This mission has led him to collaborate with initiatives like Durban Draws, where he facilitates workshops teaching participants how to create art using accessible, everyday items. Tyler Durban's artistic journey is a testament to his dual dedication: to profoundly explore the human experience and to ensure that the transformative power of art is accessible to all."}]}]}

item.title: Tzung Hui Lauren Lee
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970454749 Tzung Hui Lauren Lee gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641162264797 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013358428381","gid://shopify/Product/9013363540189","gid://shopify/Product/9013363572957","gid://shopify/Product/9013363638493","gid://shopify/Product/9013438906589"] Discover Tzung Hui Lauren Lee, a South African Chinese artist whose installation work, blending calligraphy and sculpture, explores diaspora, identity, and decolonizing the self. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Tzung Hui Lauren Lee (b. 1998) is a multimedia South African Chinese artist based in Johannesburg. A recent graduate of the Wits School of Arts at the University of the Witwatersrand with a BA in Fine Arts, Lee has quickly established a unique and compelling artistic voice. Her practice is primarily installation-based, emerging from a multi-layered process that incorporates digital spaces, hand-made paper, sculpture, and calligraphy. \\nA core element of Lee's work is the translation of two-dimensional markings, such as her personal writings and calligraphic forms, into three-dimensional, immersive environments. She draws profound inspiration from Chinese philosophy and culture, particularly customary folk art, using it as a lens to investigate complex themes of personal diaspora, the decolonization of the self, identity, and the intricate relationships that span past and present. \\nIn a significant recognition of her early career, Lee's work was acquired for the BMW Group's Private Art Collection in 2021, and is situated at the BMW Midrand Campus in Johannesburg."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013358428381 gid://shopify/Product/9013363540189 gid://shopify/Product/9013363572957 gid://shopify/Product/9013363638493 gid://shopify/Product/9013438906589

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970487517 Ugo Woatzi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641162330333 [] Discover the work of Ugo Woatzi, a queer visual artist exploring identity and community. His photography navigates worlds of freedom and restriction, confronting heteronormative structures. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ugo Woatzi (b. 1991) is a queer visual artist based in Brussels whose work navigates the spaces between the real and the imagined, freedom and restriction. His background is uniquely interdisciplinary, with a BA Sociology from Toulouse and Galatasaray (2013). His connection to the South African art scene was solidified in 2016 when he completed the Intermediate Course at the renowned Market Photo Workshop in Johannesburg. \\nWoatzi’s art functions as a form of camouflage and adaptation, much like a chameleon blending into its surroundings as a means of survival and self-preservation. Through a deeply collaborative process, he channels the desires and struggles of his community. Together, they work to create a more sensitive and accepting world, simultaneously escaping and confronting the harsh realities of divisive heteronormative structures. \\nHis acclaimed series \"chameleon\" has been featured in multiple publications and has won several international awards. Since 2019, Woatzi has been developing his work under the mentorship of the South Africa-based Through The Lens Collective. In 2021, he was selected to join FUTURES, a prominent Europe-based photography platform that supports emerging talent."}]}]}

His work draws deep inspiration from his roots and the natural beauty of Namaqualand, encompassing the environment, culture, and legends of the Nama people. Primarily working with oil paint, Ulric is based in Concordia and identifies as a visual storyteller, dedicated to portraying the stories of his community. \\nUlric's notable achievements include participating in the 2005 Soul of Africa SADC Arts Exhibition, exhibiting internationally with SANAVA in 2007, and having his work included in the permanent collection of the William Humphrey’s Art Gallery in 2019."}]}]}

[7255,7254,7256,7257,7260,7261,7264,7265,7268,7269,7270,7271,7266,7267,7262,7263,7258,7259,7253] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"\"Umseme Uyakhuluma: A celestial conversation” is a collaborative and experimental body of work that delves into the profound connectivity and duality between the physical and spiritual realms. The project explores the multifaceted nature of communication across these different planes of existence. The title, which translates to “The Straw Mat Speaks,” pays homage to one of Africa's most ancient and sustainable methods of recording information on grass mats. \\n \\nAt its core, the project reinterprets Bantu symbol writing—an ideographic system that evolved into a form of steganography, or coded language, used to convey sacred messages. This tradition is preserved today in cultures like the Ndebele, where it is known as “Umgwalo.” The artists draw a parallel between this coded script and the historical and divine significance of cowry shells in African spirituality, treating them as sacred messengers from the unseen world. \\n \\n“Umseme Uyakhuluma” serves as a powerful metaphor, urging viewers to contemplate the evolution of communication—what it has been, what it is today, and what it might become. By weaving together the spiritual symbolism of cowry shells and “umgwalo,” the work gives form to previously overlooked methods of dialogue. Ultimately, the project acts as a modern-day letter exchanged between African artists, recorded in digital mediums yet transcending space and time, much like the enduring legacies of the artifacts it honors."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013270937821 gid://shopify/Product/9013270970589 gid://shopify/Product/9013271003357 gid://shopify/Product/9013271036125 gid://shopify/Product/9132521062621 gid://shopify/Product/9132521095389 gid://shopify/Product/9132521128157 gid://shopify/Product/9132521160925 gid://shopify/Product/9132521193693 gid://shopify/Product/9132521226461 gid://shopify/Product/9132521259229 gid://shopify/Product/9132521291997 gid://shopify/Product/9132521324765 gid://shopify/Product/9132521357533 gid://shopify/Product/9132521390301 gid://shopify/Product/9132521423069 gid://shopify/Product/9132521455837 gid://shopify/Product/9132521488605 gid://shopify/Product/9132521521373 gid://shopify/Product/9132521717981 gid://shopify/Product/9132525945053 gid://shopify/Product/9132526010589 gid://shopify/Product/9133210665181 gid://shopify/Product/9133210697949 gid://shopify/Product/9133210730717 gid://shopify/Product/9133210763485 gid://shopify/Product/9133210796253

[24833] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Unathi Mkonto (b. 1982 Peddie, South Africa) is a Cape Town based artist working with drawing, sculpture and installation. Mkonto is a self-taught artist and pursued a Bachelor in Architecture at Nelson Mandela University. He was also a design fellow at Architecture for Humanity in Johannesburg. Stevenson Amsterdam gallery and Alma Martha, both in Cape Town, South Africa. \\nMkonto has also experimented with performance art, most notably in the 7th season of mentorships at the Center For The Less Good Idea. With a practice that sits at the juncture between art, design and architecture, Mkonto says, “I am always studying and looking at processes to humanize this historically apartheid-inspired built environment.” Solo exhibitions include flat (2018) at Blank Gallery in Cape Town; Juxtapositions at Stevenson gallery (2023), Enclosed Camp (2022) at Open 24 hours Gallery in Cape Town as well as Mkonto l Mazwana (2021) at Spaceby in Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014104391901

item.title: Usen Obot
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970651357 Usen Obot gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641163444445 [] Explore the work of Nigerian artist Usen Obot, who uses mixed-media sculpture and installation to interrogate social issues by re-contextualizing the ancient 'Ekpo' society. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Usen Obot (b. 1973, Port Harcourt, Nigeria) is a contemporary artist whose work interrogate our inner consciousness and its power to shape society. With a formal education in Art and Design (HND/BA), Obot's artistic practice has evolved from traditional two-dimensional mediums like ink, watercolour, and acrylics toward a dynamic, experimental use of common materials. \\nHis current work incorporates wood, fabric, metal, stainless steel, and biodegradable elements into compelling sculptures, installations, and site-specific pieces that reflect our present-day society and provoke critical thought. \\nIn his recent and significant \"Mkpese\" series, Obot explores and reimagines the ancient traditions of the 'Ekpo' society, a pre-colonial institution in which initiated men integrated spirituality, governance, and religion to maintain community harmony. By contrasting the Ekpo's principles of family custodianship and unity with contemporary governance, the series highlights the crucial role of social cohesion, empathy, and a strong family construct in building a better community. \\nThis body of work also serves to communicate the profound significance of the spirit world in African culture and reaffirms the value of African spirituality in creating and maintaining social order. For Obot, the diverse range of materials merged in his art is symbolic, representing the unification of people from all backgrounds coming together to forge a single, cohesive society."}]}]}

[9099,16150] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"South African artist Usha Seejarim (b. 1974) is widely recognized for her thoughtful and inventive transformation of everyday domestic items into compelling works of art. Drawing inspiration from the Dadaist tradition, Seejarim skillfully reinterprets common objects such as safety pins, wooden pegs, irons, and brooms. \\nThrough repetitive and meticulous acts of mark-making and composition, she explores profound themes of time, chance, space, and displacement. She holds a B-Tech Degree in Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg (1999) and a Master’s Degree in Fine Art from the University of the Witwatersrand (2008). \\nSeejarim has an extensive history of solo exhibitions, both locally and internationally. Her notable presentations include \"Transgressing Power\" at SMAC Gallery in Johannesburg, \"Nestings\" at The Center for the Less Good Idea, and \"Un balai pour un balai\" in France. Her work has been showcased at major art fairs such as the Investec Cape Town Art Fair and featured in prominent institutions including the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG), the Durban Art Gallery, and NWU Gallery."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013334442205 gid://shopify/Product/9013438709981

item.title: Usyay Mei-sooksul Yaymaykray
item.description: Usyay Mei-sooksul Yaymaykray gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641165279453 [] Discover the Incognito Art House Project and its enigmatic artist, Usyay Mei-sooksul Yaymaykray. An experiment in creative freedom and market accessibility, offering unique contemporary art at a standardized price. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"An intriguing new art-world experiment is challenging the conventional notions of identity and value in the contemporary art market. The Incognito Art House Project, an artist-run initiative, has introduced its first enigmatic creator: Usyay Mei-sooksul Yaymaykray. This alias, born in 2020 from a collective of emerging, mid-career, and established artists, serves as a shield, allowing for unbridled creative exploration. \\nThe core mission of the Incognito Art House Project is to liberate artists from the constraints of their established reputations and market expectations. By divorcing the artwork from the artist's name—often a focal point of the art world—the project provides a space for genuine experimentation and playfulness. This allows the \"Real Artists\" behind the persona to create works that may be a significant departure from their usual styles, without the pressure of maintaining a specific brand or career trajectory. \\nA key feature of this initiative is its democratic approach to pricing. All works produced under the Incognito project are sold at a standardized price, making high-quality, curated contemporary art more accessible to a broader audience. This model not only benefits art admirers but also offers artists a sustainable way to give back to the community. \\nFor those interested in following this innovative project, the organizers encourage a journey \"down the yellow brick road\" to the project's profile under the \"curators\" section, where links to their social media pages can also be found. \\n"}]}]}

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641970913501 Vanessa Majoro 2385 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641167376605 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013848539357"] Vanessa Majoro is an emerging South African abstract artist who uses recycled materials to explore themes of perception, the subconscious, and the myth of identity. [18890] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vanessa Majoro is an emerging South African abstract artist whose work explores themes of perception, the subconscious, and the influence we have on one another. With a unique background in law, Majoro turned to art as a form of expression and spiritual freedom, influenced by her experiences during the #FeesMustFall movement. \\n \\nHer practice is characterized by a deep engagement with process and materiality. She often incorporates recycled materials, such as plastic, alongside marker and fine liner to create intricate patterns and mappings that emerge from her subconscious. Through her work, Majoro seeks to move beyond the \"myth of individuality and identity,\" delving into the complex ways our thoughts and behaviors are shaped by our connections to others. \\n \\nMajoro has begun to establish her presence in the contemporary art scene, having participated in group exhibitions such as \"What is this place? Notions on site\" at the Bag Factory in Johannesburg (2024). Her work has also been featured at the Turbine Art Fair (TAF) and is available through platforms like Latitudes Online."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013848539357

item.title: Vanessa Tembane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971077341 Vanessa Tembane 473 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641167409373 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014097379549", "gid://shopify/Product/9014097412317"] Vanessa Tembane is a South African artist of Mozambican heritage who explores identity and belonging through intricate collage using family photos and traditional fabrics. [24620,25412,24618,3612,25414,25413,25411,24619] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vanessa Tembane is a South African artist of Mozambican heritage, currently based in Johannesburg. She holds a master’s degree in Fine Arts and is an acclaimed artist, having received the prestigious Ampersand Fellowship in 2018, among other awards. \\n \\nWorking primarily in collage and digital print media, Tembane’s art is a deep exploration of how her mother's narratives have influenced her own identity and sense of belonging. She creates strange and beautiful hybridized composites by merging her photographs taken in South Africa with those of her Mozambican relatives. These collages are further enriched with photographic cut-outs of capulanas—vibrant fabrics given to her by her grandmother and aunts during visits to Mozambique. \\n \\nThrough this process, Tembane’s work becomes a powerful means of telling stories about her origins and what is, for her, an alternative “home” culture. Her art enables her to identify with her mother’s country by constructing new, imagined memories, ultimately forging a unique and personal sense of belonging."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013288370397 gid://shopify/Product/9014097379549 gid://shopify/Product/9014097412317

His work has been exhibited internationally and is held in the collection of the National Museum of Art in Mozambique. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vasco Manhiça (b. 1978) is a Mozambican artist who was born in Nampula and grew up in one of the peripheral areas of Maputo City. His practice is informed by his extensive training in design, holding degrees in Communication Design from Medien College in Essen, Germany (2010), and in Graphic Design from the National School of Visual Arts in Maputo (1998). \\n \\nAn award-winning artist in his home country, Manhiça received first and second prizes from the prestigious Bienal TDM and MUSART early in his career. He has since built a significant international presence, participating in numerous workshops, artistic residencies, and exhibitions in South Africa, Germany, France, Holland, Nigeria, Portugal, and Senegal. \\n \\nManhiça has held several solo exhibitions in both Mozambique and Germany, including «Ponto de Vista» (2015) at the Centro Cultural Portugues in Maputo and «Pim-Pam-Pum» (2009) at Galeria Stadthaus Lechanich in Germany. His work is held in major public and private collections, including the National Museum of Art in Mozambique and the Telecommunications Museum of Mozambique (TDM)."}]}]}

item.title: VAS
item.description: VAS gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641166196957 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013349712093", "gid://shopify/Product/9013349875933"] VAS is a Ghanaian/Russian artist who uses vaporwave aesthetics and vintage imagery to critique consumerism and politics in contemporary Ghanaian society. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"VAS (b. 2003) is a Ghanaian/Russian artist from Accra, currently based in Moscow. His work centers on critical themes of female objectivity, consumerism, and politics, drawing unique inspiration from late 1980s Ghanaian magazines and the aesthetics of the ‘vaporwave’ genre. \\n \\nVAS employs elements of vaporwave art, such as grid lines and futuristic colour schemes, to deconstruct and comment on the emergence of hyper-consumerist culture in contemporary Ghanaian society. He connects this to the pivotal era of the late 80s and 90s, a time of large-scale privatization and the introduction of foreign companies in Ghana. \\nBy using vintage images and subject matter in a contemporary style, his work illustrates the paradox of how that period's economic shifts continue to have prevalent effects today. Through this lens, VAS highlights the complex relationship between history, media, and modern consumer life."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013349712093 gid://shopify/Product/9013349843165 gid://shopify/Product/9013349875933

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971142877 Velile Soha gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641168556253 [] Velile is a South African realist artist and a graduate of Rorke's Drift Art School. His work documents and expresses the everyday lives of people in township and homeland scenes. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Velile Soha is a Cape Town-born artist whose work serves as a realistic and vital document of South African life. His formal training took place at the acclaimed Rorke's Drift Art School in KwaZulu-Natal from 1981 to 1983. Following his studies, he became deeply involved in community arts, working and lecturing at both the Nyanga Art Centre and the Community Art Project in Cape Town. \\n \\nAs a full-time artist, Velile has built an extensive international career, with his work featuring in solo and group exhibitions across South Africa, Namibia, Germany, the USA, England, and many other countries. His artistic mission is clear and focused. In his own words, “I am a realistic artist. I express myself mostly through black location and homeland scenes. My aim is to show outside communities how my own people live their lives.” \\n \\nThis dedication to depicting the everyday realities of his community with honesty and clarity remains the cornerstone of his impactful practice."}]}]}

item.title: Veronica Losantos
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971208413 Veronica Losantos gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641169342685 [] Discover the evocative photography of Verónica Losantos, a Spanish artist whose work explores memory and identity through innovative visual narratives. Her award-winning projects blend documentary and fictional approaches, inviting viewers to reflect on their own experiences. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Verónica Losantos is a Spanish artist whose work is deeply rooted in personal life histories, focusing on the mechanisms of memory and past processing. Lasantos uses photography as a medium to create metaphors rather than merely documenting situations, often blending documentary and fictional approaches. She combines various visual styles and technical elements to present her subjects in unique ways. \\nIn her artistic practice, Verónica explores the intersections between photography, memory, and identity. Her work navigates the tension between personal experiences and collective memory, using photographic archives, material traces, and everyday objects to tell stories. She is particularly interested in how stories and meanings are passed down, transformed, or lost over generations. \\nPhotography serves as a medium of reflection for Losantos, allowing her to penetrate and make visible both inner and outer worlds. She questions how we construct visual narratives and their influence on our understanding of identity. Verónica approaches photographic techniques playfully and experimentally, combining analog and digital methods to create new layers of meaning. \\nHer work is strongly rooted in research and theoretical approaches from history, philosophy, and art history. These reflections flow into her projects, which often have a dialogical character, inviting the audience to question their own experiences and memories. Verónica also engages with participatory art, creating spaces where viewers are actively involved in interpreting and transforming stories. \\nAchievements and Exhibitions \\nVerónica Losantos' work has been exhibited internationally, earning her several awards such as Talents 36 by C/O Berlin, the Young Art Prize La Rioja 2020, the Kunstpreis Fotografie Berlin Brandenburg Lotto 2016, and the Foro PHOTOESPAÑA - Comunidad de Madrid \"Hacer\". She has also been a finalist in the Kassel Photobook Dummy Award and the European Photography Award, among others. In early 2020, she completed a Master's Degree in Photography & Design at FH Bielefeld and now lives and works in Berlin."}]}]}

item.title: Veryan Edwards
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971241181 Veryan Edwards 2397 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641169440989 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013850833117","gid://shopify/Product/9013851291869","gid://shopify/Product/9013851554013"] Veryan Edwards is a Botswana-based artist and the founder of the Thapong Visual Art Centre. Her work, inspired by the Kalahari, explores ambiguous space and reality. [19001,19008,18999,19000,18984,19007] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Veryan Edwards (b. 1949, Hong Kong) is a pivotal figure in the development of contemporary art in Botswana, recognized both for her artistic practice and her foundational work as an arts organizer. Based in Gaborone, she holds a Master’s Degree in Fine Art from Rhodes University, South Africa, and has exhibited her own work extensively across Africa, the USA, and Europe since 1979, including numerous Triangle Network workshops. \\n \\nA visionary organizer, Edwards initiated and coordinated the first international artists' workshop in Botswana in 1989, based on the Triangle model from New York. Her efforts were instrumental in creating a vibrant, international artistic dialogue within the country. In 1995, she initiated the idea for a visual arts centre in Gaborone, which led to the establishment of the highly influential Thapong Visual Art Centre in 1999. Edwards served as its founding Director and as Chairperson of its Trust until 2003. \\n \\nEdwards' own artwork spans various genres and mediums, from abstract to semi-figurative. She describes her practice as a continual investigation of reality, informed by her readings in lay-person's quantum physics, spiritual texts, and the vast beauty of the Kalahari. Her work often features an ambiguity of space, inviting viewers to bring their own perceptions to complete the meaning."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013850833117 gid://shopify/Product/9013851291869 gid://shopify/Product/9013851554013

item.title: Virginia Mackenny
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971765469 Virginia Mackenny gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641170653405 [] Virginia MacKenny is a South African artist, curator, and critic whose work focuses on gender and environmental issues through painting, video, and performance art. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Virginia MacKenny is a distinguished South African artist, independent critic, and curator with a significant focus on gender and environmental issues. She holds a BAFA from the University of Natal (1980) and an MA in Gender Studies from UKZN (2001). Her acclaimed career is marked by numerous awards, including the Volkskas Atelier Award (1991), an Ampersand Fellowship in New York (2004), and a Donald Gordon Creative Fellow Award (2010). \\n \\nA pivotal voice in contemporary South African art discourse, MacKenny has contributed essays to numerous catalogues and publications like Art South Africa and was a KZN editor for the pioneering website Artthrob. She has presented papers on South African art at international forums, including the Tate Modern in London. As a curator, she co-curated the seminal 2006 exhibition ‘Second to None’ at the Iziko South African National Gallery, celebrating the 50th Anniversary of the 1956 Women’s March. \\n \\nMacKenny’s own artistic practice, which emphasizes painting, video, and performance art, is deeply engaged with environmental concerns. She was a co-founding member of the artists' initiative COPART, which raised awareness for climate change at COP17. This commitment was profoundly expressed in her solo exhibition ‘Waymarker’ (2012), the culmination of a 700km walk across France dedicated \"to the Earth and all living beings on her.\" Her work continues to explore the vital intersection of art, gender, and ecology."}]}]}
