Explore and collect her original creations on Latitudes Online. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Viviane Herzog (b. 1990) has always been intrigued by the complexities of human relationships. Her journey began during her studies in Art Conveyance (Kunstvermittlung) in Basel, Switzerland. Drawing on her previous experience as a writer and editor, where she delved into the lives of individuals, Herzog has been translating this fascination into her artistic practice since 2021. \\n \\nHerzog’s work, mostly paintings and installations, celebrates the inherent ambiguity of life. By highlighting the beauty within this uncertainty, her art hopes to provide comfort and hope to the viewer. She has exhibited her work in several group shows in Cape Town, South Africa (2023) and is currently preparing for her first solo show in Basel, Switzerland in May 2025."}]}]}

item.title: Vivien Kohler
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971896541 Vivien Kohler 391 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641172783325 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013296759005","gid://shopify/Product/9013296824541","gid://shopify/Product/9013296955613"] Vivien Kohler is a South African artist who explores themes of urban identity, decay, and transcendence. Discover his work inspired by the liminality of the South African city. [4351,4353,4352] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vivien Kohler (b. 1976) is a Johannesburg-based artist, originally from Cape Town. He holds a National Diploma in Fine Art from the Ruth Prowse School of Art and Design and is an acclaimed, award-winning artist, having received the Thami Mnyele Sculpture Merit Award, among others. His work is housed in prominent private and public collections throughout South Africa. \\n \\nKohler's work is a profound investigation into the unique liminality of the South African city and the ability of the human spirit to transcend what he terms ‘conceptual decay’. He is fascinated by how individuals and communities flourish and bloom from circumstances of enormous complexity. His practice is driven by a need to restructure the \"residue\" of this urban chaos, finding meaning, positivity, and history in the cracks of the city. \\n \\nThrough his art, Kohler explores the perpetual process of change and the striving to move from deficiency to authenticity. Using the metaphor of a chrysalis, he views his works as representations of the traces we leave behind as we change form. Each piece is a vital aspect of a shifting persona, collectively redefining the identity of people in this complex place called home."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013296759005, gid://shopify/Product/9013296824541, gid://shopify/Product/9013296955613,

item.title: VIVIERS
item.description: VIVIERS gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641166491869 [] VIVIERS is a sustainable luxury clothing brand from Johannesburg, offering limited edition, made-to-measure pieces crafted by local artisans to celebrate individuality. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"VIVIERS is a Johannesburg-based concept clothing brand founded by Lezanne Viviers, which launched in 2019. Operating from its by-appointment atelier and concept store, Lotus House, VIVIERS offers a unique experience in building a wardrobe, centered on limited edition, numbered pieces that can be made to measure. \\n \\nThe brand celebrates the senses and individuality, creating clothing from a place of passion that allows the wearer to be their radical self. Made by local artisans in the VIVIERS Studio, the collections breathe the spirit of Johannesburg while attempting to redefine luxury through integrity, quality, and longevity. \\n \\nAt the core of VIVIERS is a deep commitment to sustainable practice. The brand minimizes textile waste by hand-cutting garments, re-using off-cuts to innovate new Edition 1/1 items, and sourcing 'Dead Stock' fabrics. By producing limited edition runs and focusing on trans-seasonal, versatile pieces, VIVIERS actively avoids creating waste and discards fleeting trends in favour of timeless quality."}]}]}

item.title: Vladimir Tretchikoff
item.description: Vladimir Tretchikoff gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641172848861 [] Discover the life and work of Vladimir Tretchikoff, the "King of Kitsch," one of the 20th century's most commercially successful and iconic artists, known for his mass-produced prints. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vladimir Tretchikoff (1913-2006) was one of the 20th century's most commercially successful, yet critically debated, artists. His peripatetic early life began in Petropavlovsk, Russia, from which his family fled the Russian Revolution to Harbin, China. As a young man, he lived in Shanghai and Singapore before being captured by the Japanese during World War II. He spent the war as a prisoner in Java, where he was allowed to continue painting, before finally reuniting with his family and settling in South Africa, which would remain his home. \\n \\nTretchikoff held his first solo exhibition in Cape Town in 1948 to immense public acclaim. Following successful shows in the United States, Canada, and England, he made the pivotal decision to mass-reproduce his works as affordable prints, making his art accessible to a global audience. This move brought him unprecedented popularity but also led to him being derided as ‘kitsch’ by the art establishment. \\n \\nDespite this critical reception, Tretchikoff's work, characterized by its exotic subjects and hyper-realistic style, has maintained a powerful and enduring presence in popular culture. His life ended in 2006 after a stroke in 2002 left him unable to paint, but he remains one of the most recognized and admired artists of his time."}]}]}

item.title: Vonani Hlungwani
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971929309 Vonani Hlungwani gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641173536989 [] Vonani Hlungwani is a Johannesburg-based South African artist and a graduate of Artist Proof Studio. Working in charcoal, paint, and watercolour, he has exhibited at the FNB Art Fair. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vonani Hlungwani is an emerging artist originally from the small village of Dzingidzingi in Limpopo, South Africa, now living and working in Johannesburg. A graduate of the renowned Artist Proof Studio, Hlungwani has developed a strong practice working across various mediums, including charcoal, watercolour, paint, and ink. \\n \\nSince matriculating in 2018, Hlungwani has quickly made his mark on the art scene. He exhibited his work at the prestigious FNB Art Fair in 2019 and participated in a heritage competition at GCR FM, demonstrating his early career momentum. \\n \\nDeeply committed to his community, Hlungwani actively contributes by painting public murals, bringing art into the everyday lives of those around him and underscoring his belief in the social role of the artist."}]}]}

item.title: Vusi Beauchamp
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641971962077 Vusi Beauchamp 1476 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013334540509","gid://shopify/Product/9013334606045"] Vusi Beauchamp is a South African artist creating satirical paintings and mixed-media works that critique the country's social and political landscape. [9103,9104] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vusi Beauchamp is a Johannesburg-born artist, multimedia designer, and art director whose work serves as a sharp and satirical critique of the contemporary South African social and political landscape. A graduate of Tshwane University of Technology in printmaking and painting, with further studies in graphic design at Damelin, Beauchamp employs a dynamic, mixed-media approach to his canvases. \\n \\nHis paintings are created using a variety of methods, including spray painting and stencilling, and incorporate a range of materials such as crayons, charcoal, oil sticks, and acrylic paints. Through this vibrant and layered technique, Beauchamp comments on pressing social issues and political events. \\n \\nOften considered the artistic version of satirical journalism, his work leverages humour and media-driven stereotypes of local politics and politicians to create a dialogue that is both provocative and insightful. This approach positions him as a crucial voice of social critique in the South African art scene."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013334540509, gid://shopify/Product/9013334606045,

item.title: Vusi Khumalo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972027613 Vusi Khumalo 555 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641199915229 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013361737949","gid://shopify/Product/9013361770717","gid://shopify/Product/9013361803485","gid://shopify/Product/9013361836253","gid://shopify/Product/9013361901789","gid://shopify/Product/9013361967325","gid://shopify/Product/9013378449629"] Vusi Khumalo is a South African artist who creates startlingly realistic collages of landscapes and informal settlements, shaped by his history in political exile. Discover his unique work. [11607,11610,11613,11615,11614] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vusi Khumalo (b. 1951) is a celebrated South African artist whose life and work are deeply intertwined with the country's political history. A long-standing member of the African National Congress, Khumalo left apartheid South Africa in 1986 for ANC camps in Zambia and Tanzania. It was in the Dakawa Camp, Tanzania, that he first had the opportunity to fully explore his artistic talents, initially training and later teaching textile printing, art, and design. \\n \\nAfter being repatriated in 1992, Khumalo continued his work as an educator at the re-established Dakawa Art and Craft Community Centre in Grahamstown. His efforts earned him a scholarship to the Konstfack National Art College in Stockholm, Sweden. In 1996, he dedicated himself full-time to his own art, seeking a medium that could powerfully render the South African landscape and its burgeoning squatter communities. \\n \\nFinding oil painting insufficient for the intense realism he wanted to evoke, Khumalo developed his signature collage technique. By meticulously reconstructing these informal settlements, his startlingly real works challenge viewers to look beyond media facades of squalor and crime, humanising the residents and environments of these complex communities. Now working as a full-time artist in the Eastern Cape, Khumalo has exhibited extensively in South Africa and internationally, with a long history of solo and group shows at Everard Read Gallery and in London, China, and Sweden."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013361737949, gid://shopify/Product/9013361770717, gid://shopify/Product/9013361803485, gid://shopify/Product/9013361836253, gid://shopify/Product/9013361901789, gid://shopify/Product/9013361967325, gid://shopify/Product/9013378449629,

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972125917 Vusi Mbulali 392 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641199980765 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013289353437", "gid://shopify/Product/9013289386205", "gid://shopify/Product/9013289418973", "gid://shopify/Product/9013289451741"] Vusi Mbulali is a South African artist known for his abstract portraits of iconic figures like Nelson Mandela, Oliver Tambo, and Steve Biko. [3811,3810,3809,3812,3808] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vusi Mbulali is a South African painter celebrated for his unique and expressive portraits. While highly sought after for both family and individual commissions, his most notable work focuses on iconic South African heroes, including Nelson Mandela, Oliver Tambo, and Steve Biko. Mbulali employs abstract techniques to offer a unique interpretation of these famous faces, creating a powerful dialogue between representation and abstraction. \\n \\nDiscovered at the age of 12, Mbulali honed his skills throughout his schooling and early career, exploring everything from book illustration to mural painting. His first solo exhibition was held at the Springs Art Gallery in 2009, where he introduced his innovative abstract portraiture style to overwhelmingly positive reviews. His work gained further acclaim at the 30 30 Contemporary Group Art Exhibition in 2014, receiving praise from esteemed artists like David Koloane. \\n \\nMbulali’s work has been featured in numerous high-profile exhibitions, including the OR Tambo Centenary Celebrations in 2017 and shows at the Absa Art Gallery in 2018. A dedicated mentor, he has taught art to students at various schools and libraries and also studied professional printmaking at the renowned Artist Proof Studio. His art is featured in publications such as Lindiwe Mabuza's book Tambo Lenyoka, alongside other prominent artists."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013289353437, gid://shopify/Product/9013289386205, gid://shopify/Product/9013289418973, gid://shopify/Product/9013289451741, gid://shopify/Product/9013289484509,

item.title: Vusumzi Nkomo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972158685 Vusumzi Nkomo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641200341213 [] Vusumzi Nkomo is a Cape Town-based multidisciplinary artist whose work interrogates racial violence, memory, and the afterlives of colonialism through installation, sculpture, and sound. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vusumzi Nkomo (b. 1993) is a Cape Town-based artist, musician, writer, cultural theorist, and educator whose work is situated at the intersection of art and politics. His multidisciplinary practice—spanning installation, sculpture, video, drawing, performance, and sound—investigates how systems and structures persist long after they are declared obsolete. \\n \\n \\nNkomo’s work probes and critiques hegemonic systems, interrogating themes of racial violence, knowledge production, language, power, history, and memory. Using a range of materials such as concrete, glass, shoe polish, salt, soil, and found objects, he stages speculative encounters that expose the operations of structural violence in the long history of South Africa’s colonialism and its afterlives. Drawing from conceptualist and minimalist strategies like seriality and repetition, his practice seeks to unveil and demystify the pervasiveness of anti-blackness as a structuring modality of Black life. \\n \\nNkomo has presented work in numerous significant group exhibitions, including SENSES (2024) at Michaelis Gallery and Occupation (2022) at the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG). He is also an active musician and sound artist, performing with his collective DEAD SYMBOLS and producing work with the sound collective Blackness and Dance. His sonic lecture, Sagrili and The Coming of Western Schools, was presented in dialogue with Grada Kilomba’s work at the Norval Foundation in 2022."}]}]}

item.title: vuyo mabheka
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972224221 vuyo mabheka gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641201914077 [] Vuyo Mabheka is a Johannesburg-based photographer exploring memory and township life. Discover the work of this Images Vevey Special Jury Prize winner. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Vuyo Mabheka (b. 1999) is a visual artist and photographer based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Introduced to photography in 2017 through the Of Soul and Joy Photo Project, his work has since garnered international acclaim for its originality and emotional depth. \\n \\nDrawing from his personal childhood experiences in the township of Thokoza, Mabheka’s art explores themes of memory, fantasy, and community. Growing up with instability and the absence of a father figure, he uses collage and photography to weave together family snapshots with elements of his community. This practice captures the essence of township life, highlighting the resourcefulness and resilience of its inhabitants. His key series, Popihuise—named after the Xhosa adaptation of the Afrikaans word for 'dollhouse'—symbolizes the imaginative power of childhood play and creativity. \\n \\nMabheka's innovative, autobiographical approach to storytelling earned him the prestigious 2023/2024 Images Vevey Special Jury Prize, cementing his position as a significant emerging voice in contemporary photography."}]}]}

item.title: Wallen Mapondera
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641972289757 Wallen Mapondera gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203454173 [] Wallen Mapondera is a celebrated Zimbabwean artist who represented his country at the 59th Venice Biennale. Discover the work of this National Arts Merit Award winner. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wallen Mapondera (b. 1985) is a highly acclaimed contemporary artist from Harare, Zimbabwe, where he continues to live and work. He holds a Masters Degree in Fine Art from Rhodes University in Makhanda, South Africa (2019). \\n \\nMapondera’s international prominence was solidified in 2022 when he represented Zimbabwe at the 59th Venice Biennale with the exhibition I did not leave a sign, curated by Fadzai Muchemwa. That same year, he presented a solo exhibition, Chikokoko (Little Pleasures That Count), at Galerie Mitterrand in Paris. His work was also featured in a solo booth with SMAC Gallery at Art Basel OVR: Miami Beach in 2020. \\n \\nHe is the recipient of Zimbabwe’s prestigious National Arts Merit Award (2015) and has completed residencies at the National Gallery of Zimbabwe (2007) and the Vermont Studio Center in the USA (2012), underscoring his significant contribution to the contemporary art landscape."}]}]}

item.title: Walter Battiss
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641973436637 Walter Battiss 302 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203585245 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013293580509", "gid://shopify/Product/9013947236573", "gid://shopify/Product/9014062088413", "gid://shopify/Product/9133213253853"] Discover the work of Walter Battiss, a pioneering South African modern artist. His dynamic style was influenced by Picasso, Ndebele art, and more. Founder of the Walter Battiss Museum. [23892,20282,4280,4277,25529] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Walter Battiss (1906-1982) was one of South Africa's most significant and innovative modern artists, known for his lifelong dedication to art education and his dynamic evolution of style. A founding member of the New Group, Battiss was a revered art educator for over 30 years. His early realistic painting style transformed following travels in Europe and pivotal meetings with figures like Abbé Henri Breuil, Pablo Picasso, and Gino Severini, leading to a more symbolic and hieratic approach. \\n \\nThroughout his career, Battiss seamlessly absorbed and reinterpreted a wide range of influences. His work saw the introduction of calligraphic forms, the abstract influence of Ndebele bead work, experiments with coloured woodcuts, and later, the use of palette-knife techniques with graffito. His extensive travels to the Middle East and Greece further expanded his visual language, introducing Pre-Islamic and island-inspired motifs into his creative thinking. \\n \\nA pioneer in South African printmaking, Battiss championed the medium of serigraphy (silkscreen), culminating in his organisation of the country's first exhibition of serigraphs in 1970. His immense contribution to South African art is immortalized in the Walter Battiss Museum in his hometown of Somerset East. His work continues to be celebrated for its intellectual curiosity, vibrant energy, and unique synthesis of global and local influences."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013293580509 gid://shopify/Product/9013293646045 gid://shopify/Product/9013947236573 gid://shopify/Product/9014062088413 gid://shopify/Product/9133213253853

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641973731549 Walter Oltmann 280 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203912925 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013843394781", "gid://shopify/Product/9013843427549", "gid://shopify/Product/9013843460317", "gid://shopify/Product/9013843525853", "gid://shopify/Product/9013843558621", "gid://shopify/Product/9013850243293", "gid://shopify/Product/9013943992541", "gid://shopify/Product/9013944025309", "gid://shopify/Product/9013944123613", "gid://shopify/Product/9013944189149", "gid://shopify/Product/9013944254685", "gid://shopify/Product/9013944320221", "gid://shopify/Product/9014015918301", "gid://shopify/Product/9014016377053"] Walter Oltmann is a South African artist celebrated for his intricate wire sculptures and drawings. Influenced by rural craft traditions, his work masterfully explores the translation of line from 2D to 3D. [20128,20129,20131,18571,18572,18573,18574,18948,22399,20127,368,18575,20132,20133,369,22413] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Walter Oltmann (b. 1960) is a celebrated South African artist renowned for his mastery of line in both two and three dimensions. He holds a BA in Fine Arts from the University of Natal (1981) and an MA in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (1985). His unique aesthetic is deeply influenced by his migratory childhood across remote areas of KwaZulu-Natal, which exposed him to the region's rich craft traditions. \\n \\nOltmann’s practice is primarily divided into intricate drawings (using pencil, ink, and bleach) and delicate wire sculptures. A conceptual and visual thread runs through all of his work, seamlessly connecting the drawn line to the sculpted wire form. This exploration extends into his printmaking, as seen in his work with The Artists’ Press. Reflecting on this process, Oltmann notes how \"the thread of the pencil line moves into wire which moves into polymer plate.\" He successfully found a way to translate the \"delicacy of lace and wire work\" into print media, a discovery he describes as both unexpected and welcome. \\n \\nThrough his meticulous and innovative approach, Oltmann continues to explore the boundaries between drawing, sculpture, and printmaking."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013274673373 gid://shopify/Product/9013274738909 gid://shopify/Product/9013843394781 gid://shopify/Product/9013843427549 gid://shopify/Product/9013843460317 gid://shopify/Product/9013843525853 gid://shopify/Product/9013843558621 gid://shopify/Product/9013850243293 gid://shopify/Product/9013943992541 gid://shopify/Product/9013944025309 gid://shopify/Product/9013944123613 gid://shopify/Product/9013944189149 gid://shopify/Product/9013944254685 gid://shopify/Product/9013944320221 gid://shopify/Product/9014015918301 gid://shopify/Product/9014016377053

item.title: Walter Meyer
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641973502173 Walter Meyer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641203650781 [] Discover the work of Carl Walter Meyer, one of South Africa's foremost landscape painters, known for his evocative and poetic depictions of remote places. His art is held in major collections. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Celebrated for his compelling and evocative paintings, Carl Walter Meyer was one of South Africa's most significant landscape painters. His work, both melancholic and poetic, masterfully captures the softness of morning or evening light and the stark heat of the desert. Inspired by the beauty of remote places, he rendered the landscape as he observed it, creating a powerful body of work that also included portraits, still lifes, and sculpture. \\n \\nBorn in Aliwal North, Meyer studied at the University of Pretoria, graduating in 1984, before continuing his studies in Düsseldorf, Germany. Throughout his career, he won numerous prestigious awards, including first prizes from New Signatures and the South African Association of Artists (SAAA). \\n \\nMeyer participated in solo and group exhibitions across South Africa, Europe, and the United States. A memorial exhibition, Tuisveld, was held at the William Humphreys Art Gallery in 2018 to honour his legacy. His work is represented in major private and public collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery in Cape Town. Walter Meyer passed away at his home in Upington in 2017."}]}]}

item.title: Wana Udobang
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641973829853 Wana Udobang gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641204043997 [] Wana Udobang is a storyteller and artist working across film, poetry, and performance. Her work explores memory, re-imagination, and the female body politic, as seen in her acclaimed film *Shrink*. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wana Udobang is a multidisciplinary storyteller and artist working at the intersection of writing, poetry, performance, and film. Her poetic work, which includes three studio albums—Dirty Laundry, In Memory of Forgetting, and Transcendence—interrogates themes of memory and re-imagination. In film, Udobang has created powerful works such as Nylon and Warriors, alongside the important archival project Culture Diaries, which documents the work of African artists. \\n \\nA central interrogation in Udobang’s practice is the body politic, particularly as it relates to the female body, its value, and societal pressures. Her acclaimed 2014 film, Shrink, is a powerful tribute to women that courageously addresses the destructive impact of body shaming. Through her highly relatable and resonant focus, Udobang gives voice to the conflict many women experience with their bodies, creating work that is both a poignant social commentary and a catalyst for conversation and healing."}]}]}

She utilizes the medium of photography as a courageous tool to confront and express these universal, yet intensely personal, subjects which are often considered taboo, particularly within her community. \\n \\nHer artwork delves into the everydayness of things and their seemingly innocent associations, subtly breaking through stereotypical notions. Focusing on the challenges faced by young African-born millennials in a rapidly globalizing world, Kirika's art skillfully turns portraits and images of his immediate community, friends, and family into visual narratives that reflect contemporary life. \\nKirka's personal tone and the immediacy of his subjects create a balanced interplay between imaginative interpretation and the genuine story of the individuals portrayed. item.title: Water Dixon
item.description: Water Dixon gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641206894813 [] Water Dixon (Caitlin Warther & Wendy Dixon) is a Johannesburg-based artist duo creating immersive light and mirror installation sculptures that explore themes of time, identity, and spirit. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Water Dixon is a collaborative artist duo comprised of Caitlin Warther and Wendy Dixon. Working together from their base in Johannesburg, South Africa, they create mirror and light-based installation sculptures that produce subtle yet complex perceptual effects. \\n \\nTheir work delves into themes of time, identity, and spirit. By transforming architectural spaces, their installations often provoke a phenomenological experience, encouraging an internal dialogue between mind and body in the viewer. Through this interaction, they hope to foster an embodied learning of self and soul. \\n \\nThe duo's practice is a synthesis of its members' distinct but complementary skills. Caitlin Warther (b. 1990) is an interdisciplinary light artist with an MFA in Lighting Design from The Parsons School in NYC, bringing a deep investigation into what it means to inhabit space. Wendy Dixon (b. 1990) is a creative director and designer whose background in bridging rich graphic narratives with rigorous spatial design allows the duo to build powerful, immersive experiences."}]}]}

item.title: Wayne Barker
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641975304413 Wayne Barker 2843 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641207025885 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014063038685"] Wayne Barker is a renowned South African contemporary artist known for his bold use of color, mixed media, and powerful social commentary. [23913] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wayne Barker, born in Pretoria, South Africa, in 1963, is a fine artist based in Komatipoort. He rose to prominence in the late ‘80s, at the height of the political unrest during apartheid. He remains one of the most prolific and influential artists to have emerged from the country. \\nHe works in various mediums, including but not limited to painting, printmaking, sculpture, video, performance and installation. In addition to collaborations with other artists, Barker has collaborated with the Qubeka Beadwork Studio based in Cape Town, South Africa, to realize large-scale glass beadworks. Major concerns have included the legacy of colonialism in South Africa, issues of land and contestation – as evidenced in works referencing the paintings of JH Pierneef – issues around race, reconciliation and accountability as well as a sensitivity to humanist concerns that border on the poetic. \\nHis works have influenced contemporary art practice in South Africa, with several of his contemporaries and younger artists citing his work as turning points in perspective and practice."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014063038685

item.title: Wayne Matthews
item.description: Wayne Matthews gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641207156957 [] Wayne Matthews is a Gqeberha-based multidisciplinary artist working in collage, drawing, and assemblage. He explores the interplay of meaning through symbolic language, mythology, and literature. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Exploring the intimate and generative interplay of meaning in a context without fixed interpretations, Wayne Matthews (b. 1982) is a multidisciplinary artist living and working in Gqeberha, South Africa. His work draws from contemporary visual culture, literature, and cosmogonic myth, presenting an emergent iconography that embraces shifting styles and materials as part of its subject matter. \\n \\nWorking primarily in collage, drawing, and assemblage, Matthews incorporates a range of materials such as graphite, dust, foodstuffs, torn paper, palindromes, and phonemes. These fragments of word, object, and image are freely integrated into abstract, semi-figurative, and figurative forms. \\n \\nA graduate of Nelson Mandela University (2006), Matthews was awarded a fellowship from the Ampersand Foundation in New York (2019) and the ABSA L'Atelier Merit Award (2007). He has served as a lecturer, curator, and gallery director and is a founding member of the experimental Labyrinth Project. His work has been featured in numerous group exhibitions, both locally and internationally, and can be found in private and public collections worldwide."}]}]}

Mentored by Sibusiso Duma and influenced by the late legendary artist Trevor Makhoba, Danca has forged a distinct path in the visual arts. \\n \\nHis work is a conceptual exploration of everyday life, delving into personal memories to navigate the profound contrast between his rural upbringing and his current urban lifestyle. [19506,19510,19496,19529,19497,19511,19495,19508,19513,19522,19526] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wendy Vincent is a celebrated South African master painter and printmaker, distinguished as a pioneer in the field of stone and lithography within the country. Her artistic journey began in her childhood on a farm, where she developed a profound connection with nature, drawing and planting from the age of ten. This lifelong passion is the central theme of her paintings. \\n \\nEducated between 1958 and 1971 at the Durban and Witwatersrand Technikons, Vincent later continued her training in the international art hubs of New York and Paris. Her work has achieved global recognition, with exhibitions across South Africa, Europe, Australia, and the UK. In the United States, her art is part of significant public collections, including the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the New York Public Library, and the South African Embassy Collection in Washington, D.C. Her importance in the national canon is cemented by her inclusion in seminal publications like Esmé Berman’s Art and the Artists of South Africa. \\n \\nFor the past two and a half decades, Vincent has largely retreated from the public art scene. In a creative partnership with her life partner, artist Geoffrey Armstrong, she has dedicated herself to another form of artmaking: the creation of a sprawling indigenous rock garden, continuing to work with the natural world that has always inspired her."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013413478621 gid://shopify/Product/9013420064989 gid://shopify/Product/9013420097757 gid://shopify/Product/9013934948573 gid://shopify/Product/9013934981341 gid://shopify/Product/9013935014109 gid://shopify/Product/9013935145181 gid://shopify/Product/9013935210717 gid://shopify/Product/9013935309021 gid://shopify/Product/9013935341789 gid://shopify/Product/9013935374557 gid://shopify/Product/9013935538397 gid://shopify/Product/9013935603933 gid://shopify/Product/9013935669469 gid://shopify/Product/9014031810781 gid://shopify/Product/9014031843549 gid://shopify/Product/9014032040157 gid://shopify/Product/9014032105693 gid://shopify/Product/9014045016285 gid://shopify/Product/9014083911901 gid://shopify/Product/9014115696861 gid://shopify/Product/9014115729629

[5326,18466,18522,18523,18524,5346,18467,18520,18521,18465] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wessel Hamman is a South African painter living and working in Pretoria. A designer by trade, Hamman brings the principles of deliberate visual communication to his artistic practice, creating works that signal with clarity while rejecting what he calls the \"cheap mystery of over-abstraction.\" This background has profoundly influenced his unique aesthetic. \\n \\nHamman employs a distinctive masking technique to produce figurative works that are visually reminiscent of the stained-glass depictions of saints. In a nod to Andy Warhol’s hero worship, he portrays contemporary cultural heroes alongside anonymous faces, drawing inspiration from social media's blurring of the lines between icons and ordinary people. He then juxtaposes these \"holy\" figures against screen prints of real-world graffiti. This contrast between a revered, high-art style and the accessible, often discarded form of street art allows him to grapple with complex questions of relevance, accessibility, and the nature of \"fast fame\" in a world dominated by fleeting digital celebrity."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013303476445 gid://shopify/Product/9013304131805 gid://shopify/Product/9013842903261 gid://shopify/Product/9013842936029 gid://shopify/Product/9013843132637 gid://shopify/Product/9013843165405 gid://shopify/Product/9013843198173 gid://shopify/Product/9013843230941 gid://shopify/Product/9013843263709 gid://shopify/Product/9133221839069

item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641977434333 Wezile Harmans gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641212301533 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013842411741"] Discover the work of Wezile Mgibe, an award-winning South African interdisciplinary artist using performance, film, and installation to foster social change. Explore his powerful, site-specific projects that confront prejudice and explore themes of exile, memory, and healing. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wezile Mgibe is an acclaimed South African art practitioner whose interdisciplinary work encompasses performance, film, and installation to drive social change. His practice is centered on confronting societal prejudices and advocating against inequality, creating platforms for critical self-reflection in often unwelcoming spaces. In recognition of his impactful work, Mgibe is a recipient of the prestigious 2019 David Koloane Award and a 2020 Arts & Culture Trust Award. \\nA core element of Mgibe's practice involves developing continuous, site-specific series that interrogate the dynamics of place and culture. He powerfully uses his own body as a primary tool to reveal forgotten ways of existence and to facilitate a process of internal healing. A recurring visual motif is his body covered in bandages, a striking image that evokes the dual sensation of remembering home while simultaneously carrying a profound sense of exile. \\nMgibe's work has been exhibited at prominent institutions both locally and internationally, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, Norval Foundation, FNB Art Joburg, the Centre for Applied Human Rights (UK), and Hangar Online (Portugal). He has an extensive history of residencies and workshops, and is currently a permanent artist at the Bag Factory studios in Johannesburg."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013842411741

Explore his career spanning over three decades, from his early video art acquired by the Iziko National Gallery to his drawings held at the Johannesburg Art Gallery. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Willie Saayman, born in Robertson, Western Cape, in 1962, is an established contemporary South African artist. Since his first solo exhibition at the Association for Visual Arts in Cape Town in 1990, Saayman has built a significant career with numerous solo shows in both Johannesburg and Cape Town. \\nFrom the outset of his career, his work garnered institutional recognition. A video piece from his debut 1990 exhibition, titled Channel Zero – An Evening’s Viewing, was acquired by the Iziko South African National Gallery, highlighting his early engagement with new media. Over the years, he has continued to evolve his practice, gaining acclaim for his work in other mediums. He was a featured artist in the seminal 2010 group drawing exhibition, Draw Links, at GALLERY AOP, from which several of his drawings were acquired by the prestigious Johannesburg Art Gallery. Willie Saayman currently lives and works in Cape Town."}]}]}

item.title: Wessel van Huyssteen
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641977237725 Wessel van Huyssteen gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641212268765 [] Discover the work of Wessel van Huyssteen, a Free State-based artist whose paintings and drawings explore the human impact on the landscape. Learn about his concept of "diaphanous barriers" and how he critiques political orders versus natural ecosystems. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wessel van Huyssteen is a full-time practising artist based in the Free State, holding multiple degrees including a Master of Arts in Fine Arts with distinction from Wits University (2017). His artistic practice is a deep investigation into the landscape and the complex ways humans impact our perception and reading of place. \\n \\nCentral to his work is the concept of \"diaphanous barriers\"—translucent veils like the frost cloths covering fruit trees, safety fences at construction sites, or coverings on buildings under restoration. For van Huyssteen, these grids or coverings are conceptually rich, speaking to the dualities of protection and peril. They visually alter the shape of what they conceal, prompting an intuitive and rational inquiry into the marks left upon a location. \\n \\nInfluenced by Peter Wohlleben's book, The Hidden Life of Trees, van Huyssteen's art laments the destruction of natural ecosystems and their \"memories.\" He creates a powerful dialogue by contrasting what he terms the \"irrational order of a fascist state,\" representing destructive neo-liberal policies, with the \"rational chaos of conservation.\" Through this lens, his work becomes a literal and metaphorical exploration of the conflict between human control and the resilience of nature."}]}]}

[376,377,378,24061] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Willem Boshoff stands as one of South Africa's most important and intellectually rigorous contemporary artists, with a career marked by national and international exhibitions. Born in Vanderbijlpark, his early exposure to his father's carpentry work instilled a deep appreciation and technical expertise for working with wood, a skill that has influenced his artistic practice profoundly. \\nWhile renowned for his mastery of various materials including stone, paper, and sand, Boshoff is most celebrated for his conceptual installations. These large-scale works are frequently based on a deep exploration of language, dictionaries, and the boundaries of knowledge. His art often challenges viewers to reconsider established power structures and the ways in which information is organized and withheld. \\nBoshoff's practice is supported by a distinguished academic career spanning over two decades. After training as a teacher, he earned a diploma in fine art and a master's degree in sculpture. His commitment to research is evident in his study trips across Europe and his extensive work in academia. In recognition of his immense contribution to the arts, he was awarded an honorary doctorate from the University of Johannesburg in 2008."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013275164893 gid://shopify/Product/9013275197661 gid://shopify/Product/9013275328733 gid://shopify/Product/9014068379869

[19745,19746,19747,4575,19744,19718,14623,19298,19299,14624,25286,25285,25287,25284,25288,19300,19301,19302,19303,14645,14627,14637,14625,14626,25530,25527] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"William Kentridge (b. 1995, Johannesburg) is a multidisciplinary artist known for his work in print-making, animation, theatre, and opera. His art blends traditional and modern techniques, exploring themes of historical trauma, social justice, and the legacies of apartheid and colonialism in South Africa. Working mainly in charcoal and ink, his animated films are created through drawing, erasure, and reworking, giving his work a haunting, layered quality. \\nKentridge's pieces often intertwine various media, with film, print, and theatre projects influencing one another in a seamless narrative flow. This approach is exemplified in the The Nose series, which draws inspiration from his adaptation of Shostakovich’s opera for the Metropolitan Opera, New York, and carries traces of The Magic Flute and other past projects. \\nHis film series 9 Drawings for Projection (1989-2003), set against Johannesburg's industrial landscapes, established Kentridge as a master of politically charged, autobiographical storytelling through expression gesture and rich symbolism."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013298790621 gid://shopify/Product/9013406630109 gid://shopify/Product/9013924462813 gid://shopify/Product/9013924528349 gid://shopify/Product/9013924561117 gid://shopify/Product/9013924659421 gid://shopify/Product/9013924724957 gid://shopify/Product/9013924757725 gid://shopify/Product/9013937963229 gid://shopify/Product/9013938061533 gid://shopify/Product/9013938258141 gid://shopify/Product/9013938290909 gid://shopify/Product/9013938356445 gid://shopify/Product/9013938389213 gid://shopify/Product/9014143090909 gid://shopify/Product/9014143647965 gid://shopify/Product/9014144205021 gid://shopify/Product/9014144729309 gid://shopify/Product/9014145253597 gid://shopify/Product/9133231538397 gid://shopify/Product/9133231702237

item.title: William Bakaimo
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641977827549 William Bakaimo gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641213579485 [] Discover the work of Cameroonian artist William Bakaimo. Explore his unique artistic process that uses the metaphor of molting lizards to represent humanity's resilience, life cycles, and the beauty of life despite its challenges. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"William Bakaimo (b. 1988) is a Cameroonian contemporary visual artist with a unique philosophical approach. After studying private law, he pursued his passion for art, earning a design engineer diploma in Fine Arts from the Higher Institute of the Sahel. His training was further enriched through various workshops and academic internships, notably at the In and Off Art Centre with artist Hako Hankson. \\nAt the core of Bakaimo's art is a singular artistic process that challenges Man and his society. He employs a vibrant mix of warm colours to tell stories where humans and lizards are presented metaphorically. In his artist's statement, he explains this central theme: \"When lizards molt to grow, their process is similar to man trying to cope with the incongruous situations of his existence.\" The lizard, with its ability to shed its old skin to grow a new one, becomes a powerful symbol for the cycles of life, death, and rebirth. This molting process represents the beauty of life and the possibility of renewal, even amidst pitfalls and inconveniences. Through a style he describes as \"doodling,\" his characters emerge as hybrid forms, neither fully human nor animal, occupying a symbolic space that speaks to universal struggles and triumphs."}]}]}

item.title: Willemien de Villiers
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641977499869 Willemien de Villiers gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641213317341 [] Discover the work of Willemien de Villiers, a South African artist who uses textiles, thread, and staining to explore themes of restoration, connection, and female experience. Explore her unique process of transforming fragmented, everyday fabrics into whole, meaningful artworks. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Willemien de Villiers (b. 1957, Pretoria) is a Cape Town-based artist whose work spans writing, painting, ceramics, and, most notably, textile art. A graduate of Fine Art from the University of Pretoria, her practice is deeply influenced by Louise Bourgeois's idea of art as \"restoration\" — a way to repair life's damages and make something whole from that which is fragmented. \\n \\nDe Villiers uses soft, mutable cloth, often sourced from domestic settings via thrift shops and friends, as the foundation of her work. She subverts the traditionally female task of stain removal by deliberately using substances like red wine, turmeric, and coffee, embedding personal and collective histories into the fabric. Her primary medium, cotton thread, acts as both a physical and figurative tool for connection. Using colours inspired by the body—pinks, reds, browns, and off-whites—she stitches through and over the stained fabric, tying together the visible and invisible. This intricate process speaks to the lived experiences of women, acknowledging the traumas enacted upon them while simultaneously performing an act of healing and restoration. The interwoven warp and weft of the cloth, combined with the running stitch, serve as powerful metaphors for connection and repair."}]}]}

item.title: William Matlala
item.description: William Matlala gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641214562525 [] Discover the work of William Matlala, a key South African documentary photographer who captured the heart of the anti-apartheid labour movement. Explore his journey from a union shop steward to a full-time photographer for COSATU, documenting a pivotal era in South African history. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"William Matlala began his remarkable journey in photography not as an artist, but as a worker and a shop steward for the Food and Allied Workers Union (FAWU). Between 1980 and 1986, he started taking pictures for his union, initially focusing on portraiture. As the trade union movement became a formidable force on South Africa's political and economic front, Matlala’s work evolved into powerful documentary photography, capturing the raw energy and activities of the labour struggle. \\nTo hone his skills, Matlala attended several workshops with influential photographic institutions, including Photo Teach, the renowned Market Photo Workshop, and the Afrapix photographers’ collective, which was central to the anti-apartheid \"struggle photography\" movement. In 1989, his dedication and talent led him to become a full-time photographer for the Congress of South African Trade Unions (COSATU). He later worked for the South African Labour Bulletin from 1992 to 1993 before establishing himself as a freelance photographer. His archive remains a vital visual record of the role of organised labour in the fight for democracy in South Africa."}]}]}

[23045,22049,22048,22051,22120,22052,22053,22054,22055,20339] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Dr. Willie Bester is globally recognized as one of South Africa's most significant resistance artists. Viewing his art as a \"nasty tasting medicine for awakening consciences,\" Bester creates powerful works that confront political, social, and economic injustice. He is renowned for his innovative use of recycled materials, scouring scrap yards for objects that he incorporates into his compelling assemblages, sculptures, and paintings. \\nFrom massive, multi-ton steel sculptures to realistic paintings framed in hand-beaten metal, his art demands attention. Bester embeds potent symbols within his work—such as the shoes of missing children, representations of apartheid-era laws, and scenes of informal settlements—to bear witness to societal ills. His unwavering belief that the personal is political has driven his practice for decades. \\nA recipient of numerous awards, including the Order of the Disa and an honorary doctorate from the University of KwaZulu-Natal, Willie Bester's work is a vital part of the South African school curriculum. His art is held in prestigious collections worldwide, including the Iziko South African National Gallery, the Smithsonian Institute, and the former David Bowie Collection, cementing his status as a crucial voice in our history and our present."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013285257437 gid://shopify/Product/9013327593693 gid://shopify/Product/9013949038813 gid://shopify/Product/9014008479965 gid://shopify/Product/9014008512733 gid://shopify/Product/9014008545501 gid://shopify/Product/9014008578269 gid://shopify/Product/9014008611037 gid://shopify/Product/9014008643805 gid://shopify/Product/9014008676573 gid://shopify/Product/9014010740957 gid://shopify/Product/9014035316957 gid://shopify/Product/9133222756573

Learn about her major exhibitions and significant public monuments. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wilma Cruise is a prominent South African sculptor and visual artist renowned for her evocative, life-sized human and animal figures crafted mainly from fired clay. Her extensive body of work also includes works on paper and print editions that complement her sculptural installations, and many of her key ceramic pieces have been translated into bronze. \\nCentral to Cruise's art are themes exploring the complex interface between humans and animals, with a particular focus on communication and the nature of being. Her doctoral thesis, \"Thinking with Animals,\" delves into conditions of muteness and the search for meaning across the species divide. This intellectual inquiry finds potent expression in her art. Her exhibitions are often structured around literary allegories, such as \"The Alice Sequence,\" a seven-exhibition series that used Lewis Carroll's Wonderland to challenge human exceptionalism. Her more recent suite of exhibitions, \"1984: Fight or Flight? Recycle, Re-use, Re-con(figure),\" draws from George Orwell's dystopian novels to comment on contemporary society. \\nCruise has created several major public works, including the \"National Monument to the Women of South Africa\" at the Union Buildings in Pretoria (with Marcus Holmes), the Memorial to the Slaves in Cape Town (with Gavin Younge), and \"The Right to Life\" sculpture at the Constitutional Court in Johannesburg. \\nHer work is held in numerous public, corporate, and private collections and has been exhibited globally, including at the Havana Biennale, the Florence Biennale, and the 7th Gyeonggi International Ceramic Biennale in Korea. Cruise is also a respected writer in her field and a fellow of Ceramics South Africa."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013285585117 gid://shopify/Product/9013285650653 gid://shopify/Product/9013285716189 gid://shopify/Product/9013285748957 gid://shopify/Product/9013285814493 gid://shopify/Product/9013285847261 gid://shopify/Product/9013285880029 gid://shopify/Product/9013285912797 gid://shopify/Product/9013285945565 gid://shopify/Product/9013286011101 gid://shopify/Product/9013286043869 gid://shopify/Product/9013286076637 gid://shopify/Product/9013286109405 gid://shopify/Product/9013286142173 gid://shopify/Product/9013286174941 gid://shopify/Product/9013286568157

item.title: Wim Botha
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641980514525 Wim Botha gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215381725 [] Explore the striking works of Wim Botha, a renowned South African artist featured on Latitudes Online. Known for his sculptures and mixed media works, Botha's art engages with themes of memory, identity, and the complexities of post-apartheid South Africa, offering a deep reflection on contemporary issues. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wim Botha (b.1974) is a leading South African contemporary artist best-known for his sculptural works. He graduated with a degree in visual art from the University of Pretoria in 1996. \\nA defining feature of Botha’s practice is the diverse and often unconventional media he employs – from carved books, marble, bronze and wood, to oil paint and ink. Famously, in 2004, Botha created a replica of Michelangelo’s Pietà out of maize meal. \\nThe mediums Botha uses are very much intertwined with his objective to explore history, religion, status and power through an art historical lens. Botha’s reinterpretations of baroque and renaissance figures in his unique armoury of materials sees them transformed, blurred and reconstructed, subverting their original meaning. \\nBotha has been recognised with a number of honours and awards including, in 2013 the Helgaard Steyn Prize for sculpture, in 2005 the Standard Bank Young Artist Award, and in 2003 he was the first recipient of the prestigious Tollman Award. In 2013 his work was included in the South African pavilion at the 55th Venice Biennale, and in 2018 a major solo exhibition of the artist’s work, Heliostat, was shown at Norval Foundation, Cape Town. His work is included in a number of important collections, including the Iziko South African National Gallery as well as the Spier Art Collection."}]}]}

item.title: Wim Legrand
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641981268189 Wim Legrand gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215447261 [] Discover the playful and paradoxical art of Wim Legrand (b. 1978). Explore his unique blend of painting, cartoons, and pop culture with art historical references, creating peculiar allegorical narratives that comment on our postmodern world. See his exhibition history, including numerous solo shows at 99 Loop Gallery in Cape Town. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wim Legrand (b. 1978) is a contemporary artist who offers a playful yet poignant take on the paradoxical strangeness of everyday reality. His work serves as a commentary on the postmodern condition, where individuals are often victims of a relentless barrage of information and news feeds. Legrand has a unique ability to transform mundane and forgettable objects into central figures within peculiar allegorical narratives. \\nIn his art, the past blurs with the present and fact intertwines with fiction, creating scenes set in a liminal zone that resembles the unfettered \"now\" of a dream. Meanings remain tantalizingly out of reach, continually open to the viewer's interpretation. Legrand masterfully combines painting with drawing, infusing his work with elements of cartoons and pop culture. These contemporary references are overlaid onto an art historical atmosphere, drawing from North European history painting and Surrealist traditions. \\nWim Legrand has established a significant presence in both Europe and South Africa, with solo shows in Belgium and numerous exhibitions in Cape Town, particularly at the 99 Loop Gallery, which has hosted several of his solo shows including 'The Parafix' (2020) and 'Twilight of the Vanities' (2019). He has also participated in major art fairs such as the RMB Turbine Art Fair and the Cape Town Art Fair."}]}]}

item.title: Winifrid Luena
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641982185693 Winifrid Luena gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215742173 [] Discover the work of Tanzanian artist Winifrid Luena, the 2019 Absa L'Atelier award winner. Based in Johannesburg, Luena explores themes of history, identity, and cultural adaptation through photography, printmaking, and video art, using vibrant colours to tell powerful stories of transformation and healing. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Winifrid Luena is a multidisciplinary artist born in 1992 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, and currently based in Johannesburg, South Africa. Working across photography, printmaking, and video art, Luena's work delves into profound themes of history, identity, and individuality. Since beginning his exhibition career in 2016, he has gained significant recognition both in Tanzania and internationally, highlighted by winning the prestigious Absa L'Atelier award in 2019. \\n \\nLuena's recent work is a deeply personal reflection on his experience of migrating from Tanzania to South Africa. This body of work, including projects like Parsing the Juncture: 110 Billion Praxis, explores the continuous shifts in perception, culture, and self-identity that accompany living between two countries. He seamlessly blends conceptual art, photojournalism, and documentary-style storytelling to reconcile his past and present realities. By documenting the socio-political climate of his home country, particularly during the COVID-19 pandemic, he gives voice to the stories of its people. \\n \\nCharacterised by vibrant colours and expressive, minimal compositions, Luena's art evokes a sense of healing, transformation, and harmony. He fluidly shifts between the roles of artist, photojournalist, and documentarian, choosing the medium that best communicates the stories he feels compelled to tell, with the ultimate goal of shedding light on important narratives and inspiring tangible change."}]}]}

His notable series of lithographs produced with The Artists' Press has garnered significant attention, including a feature in Art Africa magazine's 'Bright Young Things', His piece 'Silence' was the cover of Thabo Jijana's book, 'Failing Maths and my other Crimes'. Thekiso's first solo exhibition, 'Timeless Moments', was hosted by the White River Gallery in 2019. His art is part of the High Court collection in Mbombela."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013937570013 gid://shopify/Product/9013937602781 gid://shopify/Product/9013937635549 gid://shopify/Product/9014015131869

His distinctive artistic practice involves a wide array of unconventional materials, including plastics, textiles, used credit cards, research articles, and newspapers, which he combines with acrylic on canvas. \\n \\nThrough this unique fusion of media, Amoah delves into complex themes of personal identity and community belonging, with a particular focus on their expression within the contemporary Ghanaian context. item.title: Wonder Marthinus
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641983594717 Wonder Marthinus gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641215971549 [] Discover the inspiring story of Cape Town artist Wonder Marthinus. Learn how he transitioned from a dancer to a celebrated painter after a life-altering accident, developing a unique style that balances representation and abstraction. Explore his journey, exhibitions, and notable collections. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wonder Marthinus is a Cape Town-based artist whose career was born from immense personal adversity. Formerly a dancer, his life was irrevocably changed by a tragic accident that left him severely injured and unable to continue his passion. This led to a period of isolation, living as a hermit on the slopes of Table Mountain. \\nA pivotal moment occurred in 1995 when a chance encounter at a soup kitchen led to his introduction to the Greatmore Street Studios, marking the beginning of his journey as a visual artist. Marthinus's paintings navigate the fine line between representation and abstraction. He often uses photographic sources as a starting point, but manipulates the images to such an extent that they transform into new, independent works, frequently allowing viewers the freedom for their own interpretation. \\nBorn in Cape Town, where he continues to live and work, Marthinus completed an artist residency at Greatmore Studios in 2001. He has since participated in numerous group exhibitions both in South Africa and internationally, including \"The Artist’s Prism\" (2015) at Eclectica Modern Gallery in Cape Town. His artwork is featured in several prestigious collections, such as those of Spier, Hollard, SAB, and Nando’s UK."}]}]}

His accolades include the Phillip Ravenhill Fellowship awarded by UCLA in 2006 and the Pollock-Krasner Foundation award in 2009. \\nLagunju’s artistic inspiration draws from traditional Yoruba women textile designers, particularly those involved in the indigenous indigo tie and dye industry (Adire), which is a significant part of Nigerian heritage. item.title: Wopko Jensma
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641983791325 Wopko Jensma 890 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641217446109 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013298823389","gid://shopify/Product/9013300691165"] Explore the life and work of Wopko Jensma (1939-1993), a white South African artist and poet who used his craft to challenge the injustices of apartheid. Discover his powerful poetry, including "Once and Now," his significant contributions to the art world, and the mystery surrounding his disappearance. [4577,4809] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Wopko Jensma born in Middelburg, Cape Town, on July 26, 1939, was a prominent white South African artist and poet who became a vocal critic of the apartheid regime. Educated at the University of Potchefstroom and the University of Pretoria, where he majored in sculpture, Jensma's creative endeavors were deeply intertwined with his political convictions. His work, which includes the poignant poem Once and Now, openly addressed the systemic racism experienced by Black South Africans, particularly the exploitation of young domestic workers. \\n \\nJensma's artistic expression was not confined to a single medium; he was also an editor for Gerwe Magazine and a translator. His extensive travels and work experience in Swaziland, Botswana, and Mozambique, including a teaching position at the Serowe Art School in Botswana, broadened his perspective and influenced his work. As a privileged white artist, he used his platform to give voice to the oppressed, and his poetry is often interpreted as a reflection of his personal struggles with the South African government's discriminatory policies. In a tragic and enigmatic end to a life of creative resistance, Wopko Jensma disappeared without a trace after August 1993."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013298823389 gid://shopify/Product/9013300691165

Her recent projects include curating Offcuts at the Association for Visual Arts and being selected as a finalist for the 2024 ANNA Award. \\nLardner-Burke continues to push the boundaries of her practice, using her work as a platform to investigate deeper conversations about structures, value, and language we use to describe them."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014065430749

Born and raised in Harare, Somers graduated from the Michaelis School of Fine Art at the University of Cape Town in 2015. Through her work, Somers reimagines everyday life and explores what she terms the \"subtle treason of objects.\" Employing a distinct visual language characterized by a sense of play, bright colours, a mocking tone, and exaggerated shapes, she actively challenges prevailing ideas of normalcy, beauty, and refinement. \\nHer sculptures serve as a powerful critique of the Christian-Colonial gaze that remains fixed upon southern Africa. Somers' work is held in numerous private and public collections, including the prestigious Victoria and Albert Museum in London."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014104981725 gid://shopify/Product/9014105145565 gid://shopify/Product/9014105309405 gid://shopify/Product/9014105342173 gid://shopify/Product/9014105473245

[22329] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xavier Briel, born and raised in Pretoria, moved to Cape Town in 2010, inspired by its stunning landscapes. Initially a draughtsman and IT professional, he discovered his passion for photography while exploring South Africa’s outdoors. Known for his ability to run long distances with a camera, Xavier’s work is defined by his belief that great stories come from pushing beyond comfort zones. \\n \\nWith dreams of shooting in Africa’s most remote locations, Xavier aims to link adventure photography with conservation, showcasing the continent’s beauty and challenges through his lens. Inspired by local talents like Kelvin Trautman and Craig Kolesky, he continues to push his creative and physical boundaries."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014014214365 gid://shopify/Product/9014014247133

item.title: Xavier Clarisse
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641988903133 Xavier Clarisse gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641223737565 [] Discover the work of Xavier Clarisse, a Durban-based artist and designer creating theatrical sculptures, lighting, and wearable art inspired by nature and materials. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xavier Clarisse is a Durban-based artist and designer whose work is celebrated for its theatricality, interactivity, and masterful use of materials. Born in Lyon, France, he cultivated a passion for design from a young age, leading him to study at L’Ecole Nationale des Beaux Arts with a specialization in sculpture and product design. After working in France and the UK, he established his practice in South Africa. \\n \\nDrawing inspiration from his local surroundings, Clarisse incorporates the lush, subtropical vegetation of Durban into his designs, particularly evident in his lighting where leaf motifs cast atmospheric shadows. His creative process is driven by hands-on material exploration and experimentation. A running theme throughout his work is a sense of playfulness and movement, inviting interaction with the object. While his primary focus is sculptural lighting—with notable pieces like the Delicious Light and Blade Light—his interest in fashion has led him to translate his leatherworking techniques into a range of wearable designs. \\n \\nClarisse's artwork is held in significant public and corporate collections. His sculptures are part of the Durban Art Gallery and the Moses Mabhida Stadium's permanent public art collection, where his interactive 'King Protea' is housed in the Presidential suite. His 'Cabinet of Curiosities,' commissioned by UCLA's Art and Global Health Centre, is now in the permanent collection of the Wits Adler Museum. \\n \\nA regular contributor to exhibitions with Southern Guild, his work has been shown internationally, including at the prestigious Salon Art + Design in New York."}]}]}

item.title: Xhanti Zwelendaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641990246621 Xhanti Zwelendaba 1891 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225015517 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013394669789","gid://shopify/Product/9013397979357","gid://shopify/Product/9013842346205","gid://shopify/Product/9013962604765","gid://shopify/Product/9013962703069","gid://shopify/Product/9013962866909","gid://shopify/Product/9013962997981"] Explore the work of Xhanti Zwelendaba, a South African artist interrogating Xhosa culture, colonialism, and identity through sculpture, printmaking, and performance. [20764,20761,20762,18426,20763,13860,14051] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xhanti Zwelendaba is a South African multi-disciplinary artist whose practice spans sculpting, printmaking, installation, performance, and video art. His work confronts the complex tensions between traditional Xhosa culture and the contemporary forces of capitalism and nationalism, all while interrogating the enduring legacies of colonialism and apartheid. This exploration is deeply informed by his own experience of navigating and balancing these often-conflicting cultural paradigms. \\nEach of Zwelendaba's works is a testament to his commitment to questioning both his personal identity and the collective identities of Black people in South Africa. By employing diverse materials and collaborative processes, he allows each idea to unfold with unique nuance. His practice is overtly situated within a decolonial framework, constantly pushing the boundaries of art-making from the African continent within a contemporary art sphere that remains largely dominated by Western European traditions. \\nZwelendaba's career has been marked by numerous significant achievements. He was featured as the Artist of the Year at the Turbine Art Fair in 2021 and has participated in major art fairs, including Investec Cape Town Art Fair and FNB Art Johannesburg. His work has been shown in solo and group exhibitions such as Chamber of Mines (2016), Familial Threads (2019), and Tongues (2021). He has completed prestigious residencies at NIROX (2017) and the Leipzig International Art Programme in Germany (2022)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013394669789 gid://shopify/Product/9013397979357 gid://shopify/Product/9013842346205 gid://shopify/Product/9013962604765 gid://shopify/Product/9013962703069 gid://shopify/Product/9013962866909 gid://shopify/Product/9013962997981

item.title: Xolela Bithia Madlanga
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641990410461 Xolela Bithia Madlanga gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225048285 [] Discover the work of Xolela Bithia Madlanga, an abstract artist creating emotive, African-inspired prints and patterns that explore human emotion through design. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xolela Bithia Madlanga is an abstract visual artist who specializes in creating evocative, African-inspired prints, patterns, textiles, and art. Her work is a unique form of storytelling, drawing profound inspiration from the complexities of human emotion and expression, which she interprets through the rich visual language of South African pattern-making styles. \\n \\nWhile her signature style is a striking black and white, Madlanga also incorporates colour palettes that reflect the natural environment around her. Her patterns are meticulously constructed using a combination of lines, curves, and geometric shapes. Among these, the triangle is a favoured and recurring motif, chosen for its powerful symbolism representing partnership, power, and balance. \\n \\nThrough her distinct aesthetic, Madlanga translates deep emotional concepts into compelling abstract visuals, offering a modern interpretation of traditional African design."}]}]}

item.title: Xolile Mtakatya
item.description: Xolile Mtakatya 1408 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225343197 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013470626013"] Discover the work of South African artist Xolile Mtakatya, whose vibrant paintings of everyday life belie deeper messages about history, politics, and memory. [17906] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xolile Mtakatya (b. 1968) is a Cape Town-based artist whose vibrant work is born from a history of political activism and resistance. A former youth activist and political detainee, Mtakatya first began drawing on his prison cell walls as an outlet for frustration. Following his release, he pursued a formal arts education, completing a Diploma at the Foundation School of Art in 1993 after attending lessons at the Community Arts Project. \\n \\nMtakatya's art is a compelling record of everyday life in all its variety. His work is characterized by dynamic colour combinations, skilled draftsmanship, and a strong sense of line, often depicting engaging characters in familiar local scenes. However, the bright colours and seemingly naive perspective frequently belie deeper, more melancholic or even disturbing messages that are revealed upon closer inspection. Through his art, he processes personal experiences and engages with critical themes of history, poetry, African legends, rituals, and the politics of gender. \\n \\nA veteran of numerous workshops and residencies as both a participant and a teacher, Mtakatya has taken part in over thirty group exhibitions and held several solo shows. He continues to contribute to the local art scene from his successful studio workshop in Khayelitsha."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013470626013

item.title: Xoliswa Ngwenya
item.description: Xoliswa Ngwenya 2898 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641225834717 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014098264285","gid://shopify/Product/9014098297053"] Discover the evocative work of Xoliswa Ngwenya, a South African artist exploring themes of identity, memory, and cultural narrative through vibrant visuals. View her artworks and exhibitions on Latitudes Online. [24643,24644] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Xoliswa Ngwenya is a Johannesburg-based visual artist, photographer, and archivist whose work is deeply engaged with social and historical narratives. An alumnus of the renowned Market Photo Workshop and a current BA student at Unisa, Ngwenya has built a career distinguished by prestigious accolades and significant contributions to the archival field. \\n \\nHer impactful photography has earned her numerous awards. In 2025, she was named a runner-up for the esteemed Tierney Fellowship. Her previous honours include winning first prize in the social justice photography competition from the Open Society Foundation for South Africa (2016), being shortlisted for the DemocraSEE 3 award (2018), the Magnum Foundation Fellowship (2019), and the Contemporary African Photography (CAP) Prize (2019). Most recently, she was a finalist for the Ilford Photo Community Grant (2024) and has been nominated for World Press Photo’s prestigious 2025 Joop Swart Masterclass. \\n \\nBeyond her personal practice, Ngwenya is a respected educator and archivist. She has facilitated digital curation and digitisation training at the University of Johannesburg, Wits University, and Bailey’s African History Archive. Her archival expertise has been instrumental in preserving the legacies of iconic photographers, having worked on the archives of David Goldblatt, Ruth Motau, and Ernest Cole."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014098264285 gid://shopify/Product/9014098297053

Each creation is a testament to her idealistic vision of societal development, capturing the essence of unity and strength inherent in sisterhood. Empowerment, a recurring theme, resonates through her art, advocating for the elevation of women in all facets of life. \\nThe divine feminine, a source of inspiration, lends a spiritual and transcendent dimension to her work, celebrating the inherent grace and power within every woman. Through diverse mediums, her art mirrors the dynamic interplay of surroundings, personal experiences, and an ever-evolving imagination. As I navigate this continuous learning journey as an emerging artist, her central goal remains to educate, heal, and inspire, contributing to a more inclusive and equitable world by spotlighting the beauty and resilience of women."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013385494749 gid://shopify/Product/9013842608349 gid://shopify/Product/9013979381981 gid://shopify/Product/9013979414749 gid://shopify/Product/9013979513053 gid://shopify/Product/9013981642973 gid://shopify/Product/9013985149149 gid://shopify/Product/9013989015773

[14795,14796,14797] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yannis Davy Guibinga (b.1995) is a celebrated photographer and master storyteller from Libreville, Gabon. His work is a vibrant and essential exploration of the diverse identities and cultures found across Africa and its global diaspora. \\n \\nGuibinga uses his lens not merely to document but to celebrate this rich multiplicity. His primary mission is to actively counter the singular, often reductive narratives that have historically been associated with the African continent. Through a powerful combination of narrative depth and an incisive eye for composition and colour, he creates images that are both visually stunning and conceptually profound. \\n \\nThis unique and compelling vision has enabled Guibinga to build an extensive and remarkable portfolio, leading to prestigious collaborations with world-renowned brands such as Apple and Nikon, solidifying his status as a significant voice in contemporary photography."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013411807453 gid://shopify/Product/9013411872989 gid://shopify/Product/9013412004061

[23013] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yassmin Forte (b. 1980, Quelimane) is a distinguished Mozambican artist, curator, and communication professional based in Maputo. With a degree in Communication Sciences from ISPU, Forte has cultivated an impressive 11-year career spanning Mozambique, Portugal, Cape Verde, and Brazil, working in both urban and rural contexts. \\n \\nPassionate about art and cultural diversity, Forte is an accomplished photographer who has presented several solo exhibitions, including 'On the Stage' and 'In Stage 1' at BCI Mediateca and 'Mulheres com Pinta' at Livraria Minerva. Her work has also been featured in numerous collective exhibitions over the last eight years. \\n \\nBeyond her artistic practice, Forte is a respected curator. She has curated significant projects such as the UN Women Photography Contest and a homage to Jorge Almeida (in collaboration with Filipe Branquinho) at the Franco-Mozambican Cultural Center. She is also committed to community development, leading photography workshops like \"Olhar da Rapariga\" and serving as a juror for various photo contests. \\n \\nHer global perspective has been further enriched through participation in three international artistic residencies: Catchupa Factory in Cape Verde, and Gineceu/Legado and Up Cycle in Maputo."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014034694365
