Her works delve into mental health, the female body, and cultural identity through bold colors and distorted forms. Buy original art that reflects societal pressures and emotional resilience, available online. [23812] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yolanda Mazwana (b. 1996, Eastern Cape) is a Johannesburg-based, self-taught visual artist whose paintings investigates themes surrounding mental health, the female body, and cultural identity. Mazwana synthesizes elements of abstract expressionism, neo-expressionism, and symbolism to explore the complexities of inner experience, trauma, and personal resilience. \\nThrough layered textures, bold colours and distorted forms, her figures become symbolic reflections of societal pressures, emotional vulnerabilities, probing questions of selfhood. Mazwana's recent solo exhibitions, Symptoms of Nothing at Kalashnikovv Gallery and Secret Homegirls at Daville Baillie Gallery (both in 2019), delve into subjects such as anxiety, isolation, and subconscious. Her work often portrays characters and symbols representing agoraphobia, hypochondria, and inner conflict, transforming these themes into vibrant narratives that resonate with the viewer's shared experiences. Her art has been showcased in numerous group exhibitions and major art fairs, including the Investec Cape Town Art Fair, FNB Art Joburg Fair, and RMB Turbine Art Fair. In recognition of her contributions of contemporary art, Mazwana received The Bag Factory Young Woman Studio Bursary in 2019 and secured the second prize for the Emerging Painting Invitational Prize in 2020."}]}]}

item.title: Yonela Doda
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641997127901 Yonela Doda 475 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641229635805 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014060646621", "gid://shopify/Product/9014061236445", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104195293", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104293597", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104326365", "gid://shopify/Product/9014104359133"] [23855,3616,3617,24830,24832,24828] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yonela Doda, born in 1998 is a Cape Town based collage mixed media artists. Doda work is premised on the Catharsis Theory and the deep connection she has with her physical and emotional aspect of her life as well as the things she wishes to fix within herself. Doda does this by dealing with the distortion, healing and purification of her own pain and the pain caused by others onto her. \\n \\n Doda’s interest in looking at the fragmented and distorted body (particularly the woman body) by experimenting with collage and thread has led her to her interest in extended and prosthetic bodies as well as ritualistic and transgressive body. Doda explores and confronts the violence towards women in South Africa, how and why the body comes to matter, what the body can and is able to do as a material, bodies that she comes in contact with, how sometimes these bodies are welcome and invited and how sometimes they are not. Doda also speaks of the process of going through to get through that result in Self-Knowledge which is strongly influenced by her interest in the Catharsis theory which was first used in a psychological context by Josef Breuer. \\n \\nDoda’s collage work is influenced by the creating of the hybrid body beyond the physical limitations of the human scale; extending and distorting the body to create new identity. Doda also uses stitching in her work(s), a way to communicate the process of healing and purification. \\n \\n Doda’s ways of recalling her vulnerability through herself and her own experiences, it’s heavens and hell might sometimes view as violent, which in some cases is. This helps Doda not reject self but instead visit and highlight those vulnerabilities and help herself heal. Finding a home in self is one of the important subjects that Doda highlights in her works. Doda describes “ It was when I found home within myself that I realized the importance of self-love, peace and nurturing self before others”. \\n \\nEXHIBITIONS \\nGroup exhibited at The Move Gallery, 2019. \\n \\nAnd So The Stories Ran Away Exhibition at the Zeitz MOCAA, 2019 – 2020. \\n \\nWinner of the Dreams Realities competition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography 2020. \\n \\nVirtual Group \\nExhibition at ORMS Cape Town School of Photography titled Dreams Realities, 2020. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013288501469 gid://shopify/Product/9013288534237 gid://shopify/Product/9014060646621 gid://shopify/Product/9014061236445 gid://shopify/Product/9014104195293 gid://shopify/Product/9014104293597 gid://shopify/Product/9014104326365 gid://shopify/Product/9014104359133

[24203,1135,24211,24184,24186,24206,24200,24198,1136,24189,24213,24208,14078,24196,24194,25647,25649] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Yonela Makoba is a multidisciplinary artist from Mthatha, now based in Cape Town, South Africa. Holding a BSc in Environmental and Geographic Science from the University of Cape Town, she brings a unique, analytical perspective to her creative practice, which spans photography, performance art, sculpture, mixed media, and printmaking. \\n \\nHer work is a deeply personal exploration of the self and the surrounding world, delving into themes of African spirituality, memory, body politics, loss, and even the scientific method. Drawing inspiration from everyday conversations, her plants, dreams, intshomi (Xhosa folklore), and history, Makoba creates art that serves as a space for remembering, resolving, and processing life's many intersections. \\n \\nMakoba's career has been marked by significant milestones. In February 2020, she presented her first solo exhibition, 'Kwantlandlolo; a prayer for tabula rasa,' as the culmination of her Orms Circle Residency. She has participated in numerous group exhibitions at independent spaces and established platforms like SMAC Gallery, Ebony Curated, the AVA Gallery, and the Investec Cape Town and Latitudes Art Fairs. In late 2020, she was selected for the prestigious Bodyland Residency in Hogsback. \\n \\nIn her recent work, such as the series 'iYeza neThemba Entlango,' Makoba engages in durational meditations dedicated to collective remembering and re-membering with her family, a practice that requires time, physical dedication, and intricate craftsmanship."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013275918557 gid://shopify/Product/9013275951325 gid://shopify/Product/9013399060701 gid://shopify/Product/9014076408029 gid://shopify/Product/9014076539101 gid://shopify/Product/9014076997853 gid://shopify/Product/9014077128925 gid://shopify/Product/9014077194461 gid://shopify/Product/9014077259997 gid://shopify/Product/9014077391069 gid://shopify/Product/9014077489373 gid://shopify/Product/9014077587677 gid://shopify/Product/9014077751517 gid://shopify/Product/9014077849821 gid://shopify/Product/9133225935069 gid://shopify/Product/9133226131677

Discover their writing, zines, and creative work. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Youlendree Appasamy (pronouns: Youlendree/they/she) is a multi-disciplinary artist and writer based in Johannesburg. Described as a \"feminist free radical,\" their practice spans writing, collage, jewellery-making, and DIY publishing through zines. \\n \\nTheir work, which is deeply observant of the affects and nuances of daily interactions, focuses on several key areas of interest. These include the histories of Indian indentured labour in South Africa, gender dynamics and family-making within South African Indian communities, and oceanic themes. Youlendree holds a BA (Hons) in Political and International Studies from Rhodes University and an MA in Political Studies from the University of the Witwatersrand. \\n \\nA prominent voice in contemporary discourse, their writing has been featured in numerous publications such as Roads & Kingdoms, Africa is a Country, Mail & Guardian, and Kajal Magazine. \\n \\nAs a community-builder and publisher, Youlendree co-founded the feminist zine-making collective No Sweetness Here with Wairim? Mur??thi in 2020, creating e-zines for the \"Making a Feminist Internet: Africa\" project. They also served for several years on the editorial board of Ja. Magazine, an award-winning e-zine dedicated to platforming young South African creatives."}]}]}

item.title: Yusuf Durodola
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641997979869 Yusuf Durodola 2133 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641233928413 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014031188189","gid://shopify/Product/9014031220957","gid://shopify/Product/9014031286493"] Explore the work of Nigerian artist Durodola Yusuf, a painter and performer who uses recycled materials to address environmentalism and social justice through a Yoruba cultural lens. [22939,22941,22927,22940] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Durodola Yusuf (b. 1979) is a distinguished Nigerian painter and performance artist known for his innovative use of recycled waste materials. Born in Ibadan, Oyo State, Yusuf holds an NCE from the Federal College of Education, Akoka, and a Bachelor of Arts in Fine Arts from the University of Lagos. \\n \\nHis work confronts pressing socio-cultural issues, including social justice, environmental pollution, and the complexities of the human experience. A passionate advocate for environmentalism, Yusuf often engages the public directly through thought-provoking performance art. His pieces, such as the notable ‘Global Hues’, are a powerful call for collective action, underscored by his belief that \"we are the change the world is earnestly awaiting.\" \\n \\nDeeply rooted in his heritage, Yusuf draws inspiration from traditional Yoruba idioms, proverbs, and adages, which lend sincerity and cultural authenticity to his work. This focus on his cultural identity is evident not only in the Yoruba themes of his performances but also in the distinct patterns and material choices within his paintings and experimental art. Through his dynamic practice, Yusuf skillfully merges tradition with contemporary commentary, creating work that is both culturally specific and universally resonant."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014031188189 gid://shopify/Product/9014031220957 gid://shopify/Product/9014031286493

item.title: YY
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998078173 YY gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641226391773 [] Explore the work of Leyya Matthews, a Johannesburg-based writer and editor. Her incisive essays cover race, identity, pop culture, and life in South Africa. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Leyya Matthews (also known as YY) is an acclaimed writer, editor, and cultural critic from Johannesburg, South Africa. Her work is distinguished by its incisive analysis and personal insight into the complexities of identity, race, and pop culture in a post-apartheid society. \\n \\nWith a powerful and distinctive voice, Matthews expertly navigates themes of coloured identity, feminism, mental health, and the nuances of urban life in Johannesburg. Her essays and articles are celebrated for their intellectual rigour, sharp wit, and profound vulnerability, making her a significant voice in South African letters. \\n \\nHer writing has been featured in a host of prominent local and international publications, including Mail & Guardian, New Frame, The Johannesburg Review of Books, and Africa Is a Country, among others. As an editor and critic, she has played a vital role in shaping contemporary cultural discourse. Through her deeply engaged and thought-provoking work, Matthews continues to challenge and expand conversations around identity in South Africa and beyond."}]}]}

item.title: Zacharaha Magasa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998176477 Zacharaha Magasa 2088 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641234551005 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013405188317","gid://shopify/Product/9013405221085","gid://shopify/Product/9013405253853","gid://shopify/Product/9013419049181"] Discover the work of a Harare-based artist Zacharaha Magasa who uses rubber and other non-conventional materials to explore socio-politics, resistance, and environmental themes. [15195,14560,14561,14562] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zacharaha Magasa (b. 1988) is a Zimbabwean artist who creates work driven by the direct and indirect dialogues of everyday life. Their practice is a profound investigation into socio-politics, environmental decay, and themes of territorial and cultural resistance. \\nDrawing inspiration from their immediate surroundings—from politically charged gatherings to the pervasive systems of consumerism—the artist explores how language and communication convey complex messages, whether about climate change or police brutality. The choice of materials is central to their work, with non-conventional items selected for their potent symbolism. Rubber is a prevalent medium, deliberately used for its powerful association with the histories of slavery and oppression in Africa and across the globe. \\nStylistically, the work is characterized by the use of lines to create figurative and symbolic forms. These lines suggest movement, drifting between figuration and abstraction, and referencing both contemporary political events and personal childhood memories. Techniques like weaving rubber strips speak directly to Zimbabwean traditions and the ideal of unity. By manipulating materials like rubber or telephone lines, the artist explores how meaning is constructed and carried, creating a multi-layered and critical commentary on the world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013405188317 gid://shopify/Product/9013405221085 gid://shopify/Product/9013405253853 gid://shopify/Product/9013419049181

item.title: Zama Spellman
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998700765 Zama Spellman 1751 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641234583773 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013359182045","gid://shopify/Product/9013360197853"] Discover the work of Gqeberha-based visual artist Zama Spellman, whose powerful portraits and drawings explore themes of black femininity, race, and representation. [11453,11419] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zama Spellman (b. 1999) is a visual artist based in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape, whose work is a compelling exploration of black femininity. A graduate of Nelson Mandela University with a Bachelor of Visual Arts, she is currently pursuing her Honours degree in Fine Art at the same institution. \\n \\nSpellman's practice delves into critical themes of race, representation, and displacement. She primarily works in oil painting to create rich and bold portraiture, alongside detailed charcoal drawings that place black women in their intimate spaces. Through her chosen media, she captures the nuanced experiences and powerful presence of her subjects. \\n \\nHer emerging career has already been marked by significant achievements. In 2021, she was selected as a finalist for the prestigious Sasol New Signatures art competition. Her work has been featured in notable group exhibitions, including \"Same size, Same price, No signature\" at Art on Target and \"Learning from our context: Revitalising and Decolonising the Visual and Performing Arts\" at Nelson Mandela University."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013359182045 gid://shopify/Product/9013360197853

item.title: Zamani Ngubane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998274781 Zamani Ngubane 1477 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235173597 [9101] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zamani Ngubane is a distinguished South African creative director and visual storyteller whose work is shaped by his unique upbringing between rural KwaMxhosa and the small town of KwaDukuza on the KwaZulu-Natal coast. Initially a self-taught artist, Ngubane formalised his creative education with a BTech degree in graphic design from the University of Johannesburg, which became the foundation for a dynamic and successful career. \\n \\nWith a deep-seated love for the visual arts, Ngubane has explored various creative disciplines over a career spanning more than 15 years in the advertising industry. As a creative director, he has lent his impressive portfolio and visionary thinking to major campaigns for prominent brands such as Momentum, Tiger Brands, Steers, and Nedbank. His work on the award-winning campaign for People Opposing Women Abuse (POWA) and Assupol's \"There Will Be No Monuments Here\" marks significant highlights in his career. \\n \\nNgubane's journey from a self-taught artist to a leading creative director exemplifies his passion for powerful visual storytelling and his ability to produce bold, effective creative solutions in the commercial world."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013334474973

item.title: Zamani Xaba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998667997 Zamani Xaba 1863 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235206365 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013374288093","gid://shopify/Product/9013374353629","gid://shopify/Product/9014063956189"] Discover the work of South African artist Zamani Xaba, whose 'Naked Tailor Series' uses the sewing machine to explore heritage and socio-economic inequality. [23936,12818,12819] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zamani Xaba, born in eThekwini, KwaZulu-Natal, is an artist whose work is a powerful commentary on heritage, labour, and socio-economic inequality in South Africa. His formal artistic journey began with classes at the Durban Institute of Technology and led to a diploma from Ekurhuleni East College. He further honed his skills as a printmaker, graduating from the prestigious Artist Proof Studio in 2016. \\n \\nIn his latest body of work, the ‘Naked Tailor Series’, Xaba uses the sewing machine as a profound and multi-layered symbol. This motif is deeply rooted in his personal history, representing his family's lineage of seamstresses, upholsterers, and tailors. However, the symbol transcends personal heritage to ask a critical question: when does the representation of an object become more than the object itself? \\n \\nThe series features an anonymous, silhouetted figure struggling under the immense weight of a sewing machine, reminiscent of Atlas carrying the globe. Here, the weight is the crushing pressure of unseen economic and social forces. The tailor is depicted naked because he is unable to afford the very clothes he creates—a poignant critique of the vast gap between the rich and the poor. Through these works, Xaba gives form to an unseen populace smothered under the force of systemic pressure, creating a moving personification of struggle and resilience."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013374288093 gid://shopify/Product/9013374353629 gid://shopify/Product/9014063956189

item.title: Zander Blom
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998733533 Zander Blom 1339 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235271901 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014054813917","gid://shopify/Product/9014054846685"] Discover the work of Zander Blom, a South African artist whose experimental abstract paintings challenge modernist traditions through innovative techniques and materials. [23687,23688] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zander Blom (b. 1982, Pretoria) is a prominent South African contemporary artist celebrated for his dynamic and experimental approach to painting. Initially enrolling in Information Design, Blom soon left formal studies to independently pursue his passion for art, beginning with printmaking and video before dedicating himself to painting. Now based in Cape Town, he has become a significant figure in the global art scene. \\n \\nDeeply influenced by 20th-century modernism, Blom’s work engages in a vigorous dialogue with art history, referencing masters like Mondrian and Bacon while constantly challenging the conventions of painting. His practice is characterized by a relentless drive for innovation, not only in composition but also in method. He famously repurposes everyday objects into unconventional tools, creating richly textured and gestural impasto works on unprimed Belgian linen. \\n \\nBlom’s career has moved through distinct phases, from early photographic projects documenting installations in his studio to various styles of abstraction and a recent return to monochrome palettes. This constant evolution is central to his process, which he views as a \"voyage of discovery.\" \\n \\nHe has held numerous solo exhibitions at leading galleries, including STEVENSON in Cape Town and Johannesburg, and Galerie Hans Mayer in Düsseldorf. His work has been featured in major institutions such as the Norval Foundation and the Iziko South African National Gallery. In 2014, Blom won the prestigious Jean-François Prat Prize in Paris, and his work is included in Phaidon's seminal anthology, Vitamin P3: New Perspectives in Painting."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014054813917 gid://shopify/Product/9014054846685

item.title: Zana Masombuka
item.description: Zana Masombuka gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650864869597 [] Meet Zana 'Ndebele Superhero' Masombuka, a creative director from Johannesburg exploring African identity, heritage, and globalization through a critical lens. [13565] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zana Masombuka (b. 2000), known professionally as the 'Ndebele Superhero', is a Johannesburg-based creative director whose work is a powerful exploration of modern African identity. Drawing profound inspiration from her upbringing in Siyabuswa, rural KwaNdebele, she merges her rich cultural heritage with a contemporary, global perspective. \\n \\nA graduate of International Studies from Stellenbosch University, Masombuka applies critical thinking to the complexities of globalization and its impact on the continent. Her art speaks to the urgent need for Africans to pioneer their own narratives, challenging post-colonial dynamics and preserving heritage on their own terms. \\n \\nHer projects delve into the politics of inclusion, or \"a seat at the table,\" examining how capitalism and inequality shape engagement within institutional paradigms. She explores the parallel existence of indigenous cultures within the modern world, the true price of representation, and the importance of recognizing Africa's diverse, heterogeneous nature. Ultimately, Masombuka's work acts as a bold invitation to imagine new ways of being, beyond the constraints of current schools of thought."}]}]}

item.title: Zandri Oosthuysen
item.description: Zandri Oosthuysen gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235730653 [] Discover the work of Zandri Oosthuysen, an artist exploring mortality through the lens of memento mori, using animal remains to create powerful still life art. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zandri Oosthuysen's work is a profound exploration of mortality and death, deeply rooted in the historical tradition of memento mori—the Latin reminder that 'you will die'. Drawing inspiration from the Vanitas still life genre prevalent during the Baroque period, she reinterprets its core themes for a contemporary context. \\nInstead of traditional symbols like human skulls, Oosthuysen uses animal remains—skulls, flesh, and bones—as the central subjects of her work. This fascination stems from a deeply personal place of processing her own mortality. Through the repetitive and meticulous study of these decaying forms, she creates powerful still lifes that serve as a contemplation on the transience of life. \\nThe decaying animal remains act as a direct mirror to our own human condition, reminding the viewer that we, too, are flesh and bones destined for the same fate. Through this process, Oosthuysen confronts the finality of death and the profound significance of what 'remains'—the lifeless forms that were once associated with life."}]}]}

item.title: Zanne Eiselen Steele
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998930141 Zanne Eiselen Steele gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235861725 [] Explore the innovative works of Zanne Eiselen Steele, a contemporary artist featured on Latitudes Online. Known for her thought-provoking art, Steele blends abstract forms and mixed media techniques to delve into themes of identity, memory, and personal expression. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Based in Stellenbosch, South Africa, Zanne Eiselen Steele is a fine arts photographer whose work weaves personal narratives into the broader tapestry of contemporary life. Born in Pretoria, Zanne has been captivated by the power of visual storytelling since high school, specializing in analogue photography. \\n \\nWith a Bachelor of Arts in Visual Communication, majoring in Graphic Design, and a postgraduate degree in Fashion Design, Zanne blends technical skill with a unique artistic vision. Through their lens, they explore themes of identity, experience, and cultural context, aiming to share their perspective with the world. \\n \\nZanne’s work invites viewers to engage with the stories behind each image, offering a glimpse into the complexities of personal and collective experiences within the vibrant landscape of South Africa and beyond."}]}]}

item.title: Zanele Montle
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998831837 Zanele Montle 1069 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641235796189 ["gid://shopify/Product/9014003171549","gid://shopify/Product/9014003302621","gid://shopify/Product/9014056812765","gid://shopify/Product/9014056845533"] Discover the work of South African painter Zanele, whose art explores migration, nostalgia, and identity through vibrant portraits inspired by old family photographs. [23741,23742,21688,21690,21686] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zanele Montle explores the profound anxieties of migration and the journey of creating a home away from home. Drawing from her own experience of moving from Kwa-Zulu Natal to the city, her work is a deeply personal investigation of adaptation and identity. \\nHer primary subject matter is derived from old family photographs, with a particular focus on her mother and siblings. These figures are brought to the forefront through the use of vibrant, bright backgrounds that make them prominent and immediate. In a deliberate effort to remain connected to her roots, she titles each work in isiZulu, evoking a powerful sense of nostalgia, community, and personal history. \\nZanele holds a National Diploma in Visual Art from the University of Johannesburg and a postgraduate qualification in art education. Her talent was recognized early when she became a finalist in the Thami Mnyele Fine Art Competition in 2015. After gaining industry experience as a gallery manager, she now dedicates her time to her dual practice as an arts educator and a painter. In 2021, she was honoured as the recipient of the inaugural META Foundation 'Womxn to Watch' Award."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9014003171549 gid://shopify/Product/9014003302621 gid://shopify/Product/9014056812765 gid://shopify/Product/9014056845533

item.title: Zanoxolo Sylvester Mqeku
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641998962909 Zanoxolo Sylvester Mqeku gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641236058333 [] Discover the work of Zanoxolo Mqeku, a South African artist pioneering the innovative studio practice of sand cast ceramics and exhibiting his work globally. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zanoxolo Sylvester Mqeku (b. 1987) is a South African artist celebrated for his innovative development of sand cast ceramics. Born in Mount Fletcher in the Eastern Cape, his creative journey began with foundational studies in art and architecture at Nelson Mandela University before he committed to fine art, graduating with a diploma in Ceramic Design in 2013. \\n \\nAfter a formative period working at the Oliewenhuis Art Museum in Bloemfontein, Mqeku's academic curiosity led him to the Tshwane University of Technology. There, he earned a B-Tech in Fine Art, where his research into African Philosophy and research methods laid the groundwork for his pioneering investigations into sand cast ceramics. \\n \\nMqeku's quest to develop this unique studio practice gained significant momentum in 2018 when he was commissioned by the Goethe-Institut Johannesburg. This led to the first-ever public workshop on his technique and further master's-level research into its application in public creative practice and fabrication technologies. \\n \\nHis distinct approach has garnered international acclaim, leading to a series of prestigious artist residencies, including Vallauris in the South of France (2019) and the inaugural class of the Black Rock Senegal Artist Residence in Dakar (2020). In 2021, he was invited to the Faenza Art Ceramic Centre in Italy to create a new body of work for exhibition at the renowned International Museum of Ceramics in Faenza. Through his art and teaching, Mqeku continues to explore and expand the boundaries of contemporary African ceramic practice."}]}]}

item.title: Zarah Cassim
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641999126749 Zarah Cassim 1871 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641236156637 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013849227485","gid://shopify/Product/9013849260253","gid://shopify/Product/9014065463517","gid://shopify/Product/9014065529053"] Discover the work of painter Zarah Cassim, who explores perception, memory, and spatial illusion through dream-like landscapes and evocative, textured surfaces. [23987,23986,18921,18920] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zarah Cassim (b. 1992) is a painter whose work explores the complex nature of perception. Using both painting and photography, she crafts immersive encounters with spatial illusion, reflecting the distinct creative filter through which she views the world. \\nCentral to Cassim's practice is a fascination with natural forms and landscapes, which she uses to evoke a sense of disorientation. Within these environments, she mirrors a chaotic or absurd world, probing the breaking points of the human condition. Her work shifts between surfaces that revel in the flat, textural beauty of the painted mark and dream-like, ungraspable landscapes that threaten to dissolve upon inspection. \\nEach piece is a sensitive and personal reflection—a romantic memory translated into a visual medium that invites the viewer to be seduced by both the illusion and the material used to create it. \\nCassim graduated with an Honours in Fine Art from the University of Cape Town in 2014. She currently lives and works between Paris and Cape Town."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013849227485 gid://shopify/Product/9013849260253 gid://shopify/Product/9014065463517 gid://shopify/Product/9014065529053

item.title: Zee Feels
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641999225053 Zee Feels gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641236222173 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013992816861"] Discover the vibrant world of Zee Feels (Zinhle Sithebe), a Johannesburg illustrator celebrating Zulu heritage, blackness, and self-love through bold patterns and art. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Johannesburg-based illustrator and pattern designer Zinhle Sithebe, known professionally as Zee Feels, is a creative force whose work is a vibrant celebration of her Zulu heritage, blackness, and individuality. Inspired by a love for fashion and themes of female empowerment, she creates expressive patterns and illustrations that capture the essence of modern South Africa. \\n \\nHer art, characterized by strong, bold, and unapologetic figures, serves as a powerful affirmation of self-love and diversity. This distinct vision has attracted collaborations with prominent brands including L'Occitane, Coca-Cola, Facebook Africa, and Mr Price Home, where she has skillfully integrated her unique artistic style. \\n \\nUltimately, Zee Feels' work is a celebration of individuality and empowerment, designed to inspire those who view it to embody the same strength and confidence she portrays."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013992816861

item.title: Zemba Luzamba
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641999257821 Zemba Luzamba 928 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641236549853 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013341225181"] Discover Congolese painter Zemba Luzamba, a contemporary realist based in South Africa. His work uses satire to interrogate social and political power structures in post-colonial Africa. [9516] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Congolese painter Zemba Luzamba uses the lens of contemporary realism to interrogate and satirize Africa's social and political power structures. Hovering on the border of satire, his works mimic the opulent lifestyles of post-colonial elites, simultaneously celebrating and questioning them. Is it pure observation, aspiration, or critique? \\nWhile born in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Luzamba’s career blossomed after his move to South Africa. This personal journey of migration has given him a unique and sympathetic insight into migrant communities, a theme that has profoundly informed his work for over fifteen years. \\nLuzamba masterfully situates his subjects in bold, abstract fields of colour, removing them from specific times and places. This technique elevates his scenes to universal ideas, granting viewers the freedom to find personal relevance. Combined with his sharp observation of body language, this creates a powerful sense of immediacy, drawing the viewer into an intimate dialogue with the work."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013341225181

item.title: Zenande Mketeni
item.description: Zenande Mketeni gid://shopify/MediaImage/36650865721565 [] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"THE PRINTING GIRLS (TPG) is an all-female collective of South African-based artists who work in print. Here’s the background story to our #PRINTLIKEAGIRL gang. In 2009, the six founders of TPG graduated in the Arts from Rhodes University which has always had a strong history of printmaking. The main focus has never changed - to create a platform exclusively for our country's women printmakers to share ideas, network and exhibit together. \\n"}]}]}

item.title: Zhi Zulu
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641999618269 Zhi Zulu gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641237172445 [] Zhi Zulu is an award-winning South African illustrator creating contemporary work that explores Zulu culture and aims to influence educational materials. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zhi Zulu (b. 1995) is an accomplished illustrator and designer dedicated to exploring and celebrating her cultural heritage through visual storytelling. Born in Durban and raised in Johannesburg, she holds a Bachelor of Arts (Honours) in Visual Communication from The Open Window Institute and is currently pursuing her Master's degree in the same field. \\nAs the founder and owner of the freelance illustration studio, Zuluvisual, Zhi has established a distinct and impactful artistic voice. Her talent was recognised at a national level when she won a prestigious Gold Craft Loerie Award in 2018. \\nAt the core of her work is a proud investigation of her Zulu culture. She creates contemporary visual representations that she believes are relevant to today's society. Looking forward, Zhi has a clear and ambitious goal: to make a lasting impact on the South African education sector. She aims to integrate her culturally inspired illustrations into the visual methods used for teaching literacy, hoping to entice others to discover the rich uniqueness of their own cultures while contributing to educational development."}]}]}

item.title: Zhané Warren
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641999421661 Zhané Warren gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641237074141 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013844443357","gid://shopify/Product/9013844476125","gid://shopify/Product/9013844541661","gid://shopify/Product/9014014673117","gid://shopify/Product/9014058090717","gid://shopify/Product/9014058156253"] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zhané Warren (b. 1976, Johannesburg), is the master printer and director at Warren Editions, a printmaking studio based in Cape Town. She studied Fine Art at Stellenbosch University and earned a master’s degree in Technology of Fine Art from the University of Johannesburg in 2006. Awarded a scholarship, she attended the Karel de Grote Hogeskool in Antwerp, Belgium, where she spent five years working alongside renowned artists and printmakers. \\nIn 2007, Zhané returned to South Africa as a recognized master printer and founded Warren Editions. As both a visual and performance artist, she has staged numerous exhibitions and performances in South Africa and internationally. Her solo exhibitions include \"Live with me\" (KZN Gallery, Durban, 2007), \"Recurrence\" (Art on Paper, Johannesburg, 2006), and \"In between here and there\" (with Robert van Dromme at Contemporary Wei, Antwerp, Belgium). Her work is represented in various collections in South Africa, Belgium, and the USA. \\nZhané Warren is also a respected authority in printmaking and fine art publishing, and she is a passionate educator. \\n"}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013844443357 gid://shopify/Product/9013844476125 gid://shopify/Product/9013844541661 gid://shopify/Product/9014014673117 gid://shopify/Product/9014058090717 gid://shopify/Product/9014058156253

item.title: Ziyanda Majozi
item.description: Ziyanda Majozi gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641237893341 [] Discover the powerful mosaic and mixed-media art of Ziyanda Majozi. The award-winning South African artist explores heritage, community, and social justice. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Ziyanda Majozi (b. 1985) is a full-time artist from the Eastern Cape, primarily celebrated for her intricate mosaic work. With a dedicated practice spanning over 12 years, her artistic journey began with formal studies in mosaic at the Spier Arts Academy in Cape Town, complemented by a foundation in graphic design from the Cape Peninsula University of Technology. She later expanded her versatile skill set to include painting and printmaking through various art workshops and residencies, such as the Thupelo workshops. \\nMajozi has built an impressive resume of local and international residencies, earning prestigious awards including the Thami Mnyele Award in the Netherlands and a place in the David Koloane Mentorship Programme at the Bag Factory Artist Studios. She has also held a residency at Gallery MOMO in Johannesburg. \\nA significant aspect of her career includes her powerful collaboration with renowned artist Zanele Muholi on the \"Faces and Phases\" series and the vital documentation of hate crime victims in South Africa. Majozi's own work has gained significant visibility, having been showcased at two consecutive FNB Art Joburg fairs. \\nHer art is held in high esteem by prominent collectors. Her pieces are part of the prestigious J.P. Morgan Art Collection (acquired through the Abadali artist development programme), the Arts and Culture Trust, and the Bloemfontein Oliewenhuis Art Museum (acquired through Art Bank South Africa). \\nBeyond the gallery space, Majozi is committed to large-scale public art and community engagement. She has created major murals, including one at Tshwane House in Pretoria, and has led numerous community projects in remote areas like Vredendal. Notably, she worked with the Simon's Town Museum and Greatmore Studios on the \"Waag'a Bitjie\" project, which focused on the town's displaced communities. Currently, she is participating in the ongoing project \"Whose Heritage Matters?\" hosted by the University of Cape Town (UCT)."}]}]}

item.title: Zinhle Ka Nobuhlalusa
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642002665693 Zinhle Ka Nobuhlalusa gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641237336285 [] Explore the work of Zinhle ka'Nobuhlaluse, a South African artist and scholar examining the Black female body through mixed media, philosophy, and feminism. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zinhle ka'Nobuhlalusa (b. 1993) is a South African self-taught mixed-media artist. ka'Nobuhlaluse's (legally Manzini) practice is deeply intertwined with her rigorous academic and personal pursuits. Currently based on Pennsylvania, USA, she is undertaking a dual-title PhD in Philosophy & Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies with a focus on Black existentialism, Feminist Philosophy, and Critical Philosophy of Race. \\nThis scholarly foundation, combined with experience as a certified 200hr Yoga Teach, profoundly informs her artwork. Zinhle's art centers on the naked Black femal flesh, creating a powerful dialogue between resistance and violence at the intersections of self and societal identity. Through her work—a blend of memory, illusion, and feminist joy—she offers parts of herself to the viewer. \\nHer debut collection utilizes pencil, charcoal, paint, and texture to explore and challenge conventional views of the naked body. Drawing inspiration from feminist scholars, she confronts the concept of the Black woman's body being \"pornotroped,\" a term coined by Hortense J. Spillers. Simultaneously, her art celebrates the body as a site of powerful resistance. This is explicitly referenced in works titled after chapters from Pumla Dineo Gqola's book, Female Fear Factory. For instance, her piece \"Fearing Feminist\" is a \"(re)memory\" of activist Simamkele Dlakavu during the 2016 #RUReferenceList protests, highlighting a legacy of feminist solidarity and resistance. \\nHer artwork assembles her scholarly interest and yoga; it centres on the naked Black female flesh. Zinhle plays with the representations of Blackwomen's self and societal identities at the intersections of resistance and violence. In her work, she offers parts of herself created from a place of memory, illusion, and feminist joy. \\nThis debut collection is an aesthetic representation of her body and other Blackwomen who have made their naked bodies available to the public eye. The collection plays with pencil, charcoal, paint, and texture to trouble the naked body as dainty, sexual, vulnerable, and recognises the monstrosity that is Blackwomenhood. The re-representation of the public images seeks to express how Blackwomens naked bodies no matter the form, are, have, and always-already bare the potential to be \"pornotroped\" as we are reminded by the African American literary critic and Feminist scholar Hortense J. Spillers in her icononic essay \"Mama's Baby, Papa's Maybe: An American Grammar Book\" (1987). At the same time, Blackwomen have always resisted this potentiality and have used their bodies as a resistant modality. Three of the works' titles (\"Fearing Feminists”, \"Foreign Familiars\", and \"Femicidal Intimacy\") are chapters of the South African literary critic and Feminist scholar Pumla Dineo Gqola's forthcoming book Female Fear Factory (2021). These images speak to this feminist resistance as we see in \"Fearing Feminist\", a (re)memory of the Activist and Feminist scholar Simamkele Dlakavu in protest solidarity with the 2016 #RUReferencelist protestors."}]}]}

item.title: Zizah O
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642002796765 Zizah O gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641238253789 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013857059037"] Discover the extraordinary art of Zizah O., a 15-year-old artist with autism, who blends cubism and impressionism. See his award-winning, eclectic work. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"At just 15 years old, Zizah O. has emerged as a prodigious and redefining voice in the art world. Diagnosed with autism at a young age, Zizah discovered his profound passion for creativity through sketching and colouring, transforming his unique perspective into a powerful artistic practice. \\nZizah’s art is a masterful blend of eclecticism, skilfully combining elements of cubism, impressionism, and abstraction. While his compositions often possess a striking simplicity, his subject matter is rich and diverse. In his compelling portrait work, he deconstructs and experiments with the human form, often obscuring facial expressions with innovative techniques. Every brushstroke and pencil line is a testament to his meticulous and calculated consideration. \\n \\nBeyond the canvas, Zizah’s family champions his art as a vehicle to raise awareness, foster understanding, and promote the acceptance of autism, showcasing the immense potential of differently-abled individuals when given the opportunity. \\n \\nHis career is already marked by extraordinary achievements. In 2021, he held his first solo exhibition, “Eidetic Impressions,” at Terra Kulture and was named the Youth Category Winner at the PARAART TOKYO International Exhibition. In 2023, he was a contributing artist to the \"Swing for Autism\" auction and held his second solo show, “Unknown Countenance,” at TCA Gallery, making him the first child ever to have a solo exhibition during Lagos Art Week. He concluded that remarkable year by participating in TCA Gallery’s inaugural auction in Harare, Zimbabwe. \\n \\nTCAG member artist Zizah, a 15-year-old artist and prodigy, has redefined the boundaries of art. Diagnosed with autism at a young age, he discovered his passion for creativity through sketching and colouring. \\n \\nZizah's art is a masterful blend of eclecticism, combining elements of cubism, impressionism, and abstraction. His compositions are simple in nature, while his subject matter is rich and diverse. In his portrait work, he experiments with the human form, often obscuring facial expressions with innovative techniques. His brushwork and pencil lines are a testament to calculative consideration and placement. \\n \\nHis family believes in the power of his art to raise awareness, foster understanding, and promote acceptance of autism. Zizah's work also demonstrates the immense potential of differently-abled individuals when given the opportunity. Welcome to Zizah's extraordinary world of artistry. \\n \\nHis accomplishments include “Eidetic Impressions” a solo exhibition at Terra Kulture (2021); Youth Category Winner, PARAART TOKYO International Exhibition (2021); Contributing artist for Swing for Autism Art Auction, curated by TCA Gallery (Aug 2023); “Unknown Countenance” a solo exhibition at TCA Gallery, marking Zizah as the first child to have a solo exhibition during Lagos Art Week (Nov 2023); Contributing artist in TCA Gallery’s Inaugural Art Auction in Harare, Zimbabwe (Dec 2023)."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013857059037

item.title: Zoey Trapani
item.description: Zoey Trapani gid://shopify/MediaImage/36641238417629 [] Meet Zoey Trapani, an emerging Johannesburg sculptor and Operations Manager at Lizamore & Associates, continuing the artistic legacy of her creative family. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zoey Trapani (b. 1998) is an emerging Johannesburg artist whose life and career are deeply woven into the fabric of the South African art world. The daughter of artists Sandro/Alex Trapani, a sculptor, and the late Antoinette Murdoch, former head curator of the Johannesburg Art Gallery (JAG), Trapani's upbringing was a unique immersion in creativity. She credits her early, enchanting encounters with eccentric artists and formative experiences roaming the halls of JAG as pivotal in shaping her artistic direction. \\nAfter matriculating with a distinction in Visual Arts in 2016, Trapani began her career by creating and selling functional sculptures, such as embellished vases and dolls, at local markets. This early phase allowed her to connect with a broad audience while honing her craft. \\nCurrently, Trapani serves as the Operations Manager at Lizamore & Associates, where she is mentored by veteran curator Teresa Lizamore—who notably exhibited her parents' work two decades prior. This role has provided her with invaluable industry experience, including assisting with curating the City Hall Exhibition at the 2023 SU Toyota Woordfees and helping value the extensive SA Taxi art collection. \\nWorking within the gallery has reinvigorated her passion for creating \"art for art's sake.\" She is now developing a more conceptual approach to her sculpting. Trapani made her official debut as a fine artist in the 'Season's Greetings' group exhibition at Lizamore Gallery in late 2023. Fuelled by this milestone, she is poised to expand her presence in the art market, aiming to create work that \"sparks joy and curiosity, but occasionally invokes an uneasy feeling,\" and proudly continue her family's artistic legacy."}]}]}

item.title: Zoha Zafar Malik
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642002862301 Zoha Zafar Malik 2479 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36503312400605 [] Discover the work of Zoha Zafar Malik, an award-winning visual artist and poet from Lahore, Pakistan, who has exhibited her art both locally and internationally. [19828,19838] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zoha Zafar Malik (b. 1996) is a visual artist and poet currently based in Lahore, Pakistan. A 2019 graduate of the National College of Arts, Lahore, Malik has been actively exhibiting he work since 2016, building a strong presence both within Pakistan and on the international stage. \\nHer talent has been recognised with several notable accolades. In 2019, she was honoured with the Young Artist Award by the Alhamra Arts Council in Lahore. Her work was also featured in the \"We the People, We the Arts\" competition, organised by the Embassy of Switzerland, leading to exhibitions at the embassy and the Pakistan National Council of Arts in Islamabad. \\nFurthering her global engagement, Malik was selected for an artist residency at the acclaimed Vermont Studio Center in the USA, a significant opportunity for artistic development and exchange. She made her international online debut on Artsy through a collaboration with Contempop Gallery, New York. \\nIn addition to her visual practice, Malik explores creative expression through poetry, with her work recently published in the anthology \"The New Dawn,\" showcasing her multidisciplinary approach to the arts. \\nparticipated in We the People, We the Arts, Art competition organised by the Embassy of Switzerland, Islamabad and exhibited at the same venue and also at the Pakistan National Council of Arts, Islamabad. Alongside this Zoha was privileged to have had the chance to attend an artist residency at the Vermont Studio Centre, Vermont. She was the recipient of the Young Artist Award for the year 2019 organised by the Alhamra Arts Council, Lahore. Zoha made her debut on artsy.net with Contempop Gallery, New York. She also have an interest in poetry and recently got her poems published in an anthology “The new dawn”."}]}]}

item.title: Zolile Phetshane
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642003058909 Zolile Phetshane 856 gid://shopify/MediaImage/36503362797789 ["gid://shopify/Product/9013842313437"] Discover the work of South African artist Zolile Phetshane. Explore his paintings and prints that tackle themes of politics, religion, and consumerism. [18425] {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zolile Phetshane (b. 1973) is a prominent South African artist whose work delves into complex contemporary themes such as religion, politics, consumerism, and capitalism. He holds an Advanced Diploma in Fine Arts from the University of the Witwatersrand (2006) and further honed his skills at the renowned Artist Proof Studios in Johannesburg. \\nPhetshane’s distinctive style masterfully combines abstract colour fields with figurative elements and symbols to explore the intricacies of his chosen subjects. He is a versatile artist, working across a range of mediums including printmaking, works on paper in pastel, and acrylic and oil on canvas. \\nSince 2008, he has developed a close and enduring partnership with Lizamore & Associates, leading to significant visibility and success. Through the gallery, he has participated in major art fairs like the FNB Joburg Art Fair, Investec Cape Town Art Fair, and the RMB Turbine Art Fair. He has also held several successful solo exhibitions with the gallery, including \"1 is the magic number\" (2016), \"Simplified Complexity\" (2018), and \"Neon Paradise\" (2020), the latter being a collaboration with artist Anton Burger. \\nPhetshane's work has also been exhibited at institutions like the North West University Gallery (2014) and internationally with Clifton Boulder in Europe. Highly sought after by collectors, his art is featured in numerous prominent private and public collections."}]}]} gid://shopify/Product/9013842313437

item.title: Zonia Nel Scheffer
item.description: Zonia Nel Scheffer gid://shopify/MediaImage/36547448832221 [] Explore the work of Zonia Nel Scheffer, an award-winning South African artist. Her paintings are featured in major collections like Sasol, ABSA, and Nandos. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zonia Nel Scheffer is an accomplished South African artist with a career spanning over two decades. She graduated with a B.A in Fine Arts (Honours) from the University of Pretoria in 1996 and quickly gained recognition, earning a merit award at the Sasol New Signatures competition in 1998. \\n \\nHer distinct artistic voice is evident in her success in both solo and group exhibitions. To date, Scheffer has held six solo exhibitions and participated in numerous group shows, showcasing the breadth and evolution of her work. In2009, she achieved a milestone by wining the painting category at the Sanlam \"Vuleka\" competition. \\nScheffer's work is highly sought after and is included in several prominent corporate and private art collections. These include the collections of Sasol, ABSA Private Bank, Rand Merchant Bank, Hewlett Packard, Nandos (UK), and the esteemed Leon Strydom collection. \\nShe is also an active member of 'The Voice Art Collective', collaborating and exhibiting with fellow artists."}]}]}

item.title: Zwelethu Nanise
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642003222749 Zwelethu Nanise gid://shopify/MediaImage/36506957840605 [] Discover the work of South African artist Zwelethu Nanise, who explores cultural hegemony and post-colonialism through painting, sculpture, and mixed media. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zwelethu Nanise (b. 1985) is a Johannesburg-based artist whose work critically examines the enduring impact of cultural hegemony and post-colonialism on contemporary society. A Soweto native, Nanise uses his art to deconstruct and challenge the Western values and beliefs imposed through systems like media, education, and religion. \\n \\nA 2010 visual arts graduate from the University of Johannesburg, Nanise works across a diverse range of media, including painting, drawing, sculpture, and ceramics. A core element of his practice is the juxtaposition of familiar symbols, signs, and images, creating compelling visual dialogues that urge viewers to reconsider their acquired perceptions of the world. By unsettling entrenched ideologies, he aims to spark a wider conversation about pervasive societal narratives. \\nNanise's distinct voice gained early recognition through his inclusion in the prestigious Sasol New Signatures and ABSA L’Atelier competition exhibitions in 2009. He has participated in numerous group shows, such as \"Oppitafel\" at Lizamore and Associates (2010) and, more recently, \"The Beginning\" and \"Bleed, Blossom, Bloom\" at the Touch of Genius Gallery (2019)."}]}]}

item.title: Zwelethu Machepha
item.description: gid://shopify/MediaImage/36642003157213 Zwelethu Machepha gid://shopify/MediaImage/36506963083485 [] Johannesburg artist Zwelethu Machepha creates compelling works informed by his deep expertise in printmaking. Discover his portfolio and exhibition history. {"type":"root","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Zwelethu Machepha (b. 1990) is a contemporary artist living and working in his birth city of Johannesburg, South Africa. His artistic journey began with formative classes at the Johannesburg Central Library and the Education Centre at the Joburg Art Gallery. This foundation lead him to pursue formal training in 2010 at a specialised printmaking institution. \\n \\nOver four years, Machepha honed his craft, not only completing the course but also serving as a Screen Print Technician and Facilitator. In this role, he collaborated with and printed works for some of South Africa's most prominent artists, including William Kentridge, Nelson Makamo, Faith47, and Bambo Sibiya, gaining invaluable technical experience. \\nNow a full-time artist, Machepha has built an impressive exhibition history. His work has been featured in significant showcases such as the \"Ndo-Ima-Dzi Independence Group Exhibition\" at Botho Project Space, the 2020 Ake Arts and Book Festival, the 2019 Prizm Art Fair in Miami, and a fundraising exhibition for the Blessing Ngobeni Art Prize. He has also been an invited artist at Sibisi Gallery and the Sharon Simpson annual printmaking show. \\nMachepha's growing reputation is cemented by the inclusion of his work in notable private and corporate collections, including the Arts and Culture Trust Fund and the African Arts Fund."}]}]}
